Without any warning, a <nobr>double-locked</nobr> box mysteriously appears in the middle of Semmelweis's camp. It bears no markings or messages, leaving everyone puzzled about its origin and purpose. The moonlight shines through the gaps in the branches, revealing the code entry mechanism of the lock.
Encounter a hard battle, win to obtain 100 Goldfinch Coins

Perhaps this tree shares a love of literature, as evidenced by the poster hanging from its shortest branch, drifting in from an unknown origin. Semmelweis pauses in front of the tree and studies the poster's ...

The path, agreed upon by all travelers in the area to be suitable for both feet and wheels, leads the group to discover several abandoned campfires. These remnants served as evidence of the arcane skills possessed by previous travelers.
We're not the only ones on this path. Be careful.
Weeds have taken over the field, a sign that it has been neglected for quite some time. The narrow, bumpy path causes the carriage to sway unpredictably, but the team remains in good spirits.
Don't be shy. It's a nice voice.
According to the map, we can cut at least four days off our journey by walking directly through the forest from here.

This is the road used by local hunters. It's a little out of the way and a little difficult to navigate, but it's also pretty well hidden and safe. However, the road is full of blind spots and there isn't much room for the driver to maneuver. If a Dahu were to suddenly appear in their path, the carriage would inevitably crash into a tree from swerving.
There seems to be an uninvited stalker here.

Semmelweis quietly approaches the bushes and carefully pulls apart the branches and leaves to reveal a large, drooling Critter lying on the ground. The creature thought it was hiding unnoticed, but its hair stood on end when it was startled by the team leader's sudden approach.

The bushes shake violently as a massive, drooling Critter emerges from them. It lets out a long hiss and charges toward the team. After swiping at them several times, it grabs the team's largest pack of materials.
Leave it to me. My team is more than equipped for this task, wouldn't you agree?

Hunger and zealotry have eroded the minds of these refugees for too long. As a result, they are no longer capable of making complex judgments. With a little coaxing from Semmelweis, their doubts dissipate and they laugh as they give her the information she needs. After bidding farewell to the refugees, Semmelweis sends her team members to remind that unfortunate and <nobr>kind-hearted</nobr> person.

It would be unwise to judge the situation until all the details are known. Besides, in this wild era of time reversal, it is perfectly understandable for anyone, human or otherwise, to be swept up in a wave of mass hysteria. Since Semmelweis is already struggling with her own hysteria, she has no intention of becoming anyone's savior.
It is wise to avoid these kinds of things as much as possible.
Are you in need of help?

The old man ignores Semmelweis's words, letting them fall to the ground like dead leaves. While Semmelweis's future is uncertain, the old man's purpose is clear. His arcane skill provides a comforting warmth compared to his icy touch.

When animals meet in a new environment, they are instinctively wary and cautious, a behavior that needs no explanation. The old man pulls his hand back, takes out a package from his oversized coat, and tosses it on the ground. Then he turns and walks away. Semmelweis picks up the package and inspects it to make sure it is not dangerous.
A phonograph ...? What is a phonograph doing here?

Semmelweis's heart sinks as she recognizes the tune—it was often hummed by her former teammate who had mysteriously disappeared during a "Storm". Just as the thought crosses her mind, her missing teammate appears before her, standing in the same spot where the phonograph once was. A sense of dread fills Semmelweis's thoughts as she follows the haunting song, only to realize that it is all a hallucination.

It's not a sense of guilt or an attempt to hide her guilt over the "Storm" from her team. It's not even a feeling of affection for the deceased. It is merely a delusion conjured by Semmelweis's afflicted mind. When she remembers this fact, the hallucination gradually fades.
Semmelweis gradually comes to terms with her own distorted perception. She turns around and leaves the hallucination and the melody behind.
The Critter happily takes the Goldfinch Coins, gives them a tap and a bite, and then contentedly puts them into its pouch. It then rummages around for a while before pulling out something else.
The Critter happily takes the Goldfinch Coins, gives them a tap and a bite, and then contentedly puts them into its pouch. It then rummages around for a while before pulling out a couple items.
The Critter lets out a piercing scream of anger and fear, clutching its pouch defensively as it charges at the team, brandishing its weapon in a threatening manner.
It has escaped with its pouch.
???: These are sure to be useful to you. Please choose the one you desire.
???: In terms of usefulness, that item won't compare to candy. And please take this.
???: Yes, this should better suit your physical needs. I hope you like the taste of mint and plum.
Don't resist. This will be over before you know it.

Semmelweis shatters the mask quickly and cleanly. One of the flying fragments cuts her hand, but that is the extent of the black beast's final counterattack. The young man collapses to the floor, panting like a dog. From where she stands, Semmelweis hears his muttered thanks and advice: "They're in the red house... underground..."

Semmelweis holds onto the mask, its viscous fluids forming several strands that flow over her suede gloves like contaminated blood vessels. She suddenly shakes off the thought and throws the mask to the ground. The young man collapses to the floor, panting like a dog. From where she stands, Semmelweis hears his muttered thanks and advice: "They're in the red house... underground..."

Ever agile and skillful, Semmelweis grants eternal peace to the vessel by wresting it from the clutches of the mask. She seems to hear a sigh, either from the mask or the corpse ... Regardless, she doesn't care.
We won't be returning here once we've completed our task, but it would be a shame to give up good information.
<nobr>Ten-minute</nobr> meeting, everyone—we need to come up with a plan of attack quickly.
There are gaps in the enemy's defenses. With a little planning, it should be easy enough to break through them and walk away with a fitting trophy.

There are gaps in the enemy defenses—namely, a patrol gap that occurs every 15 minutes or so on the southwest side of the house. Semmelweis leads her team through the nearby window. So far, everything seems to be going smoothly.

The guard on the southwest side of the house moves particularly slowly, so there are gaps in their patrol every 15 minutes or so. If one desired to launch a surprise attack, the southwest side would undoubtedly be the best choice.
Semmelweis leads her team through the window. So far, everything seems to be going smoothly.
Semmelweis leads her team through the nearby window. So far, everything seems to be going smoothly.
Despite barely managing to defeat the enemy, Semmelweis is nearly overcome by the hallucinations. She knows she must leave this place immediately before it's too late.

There is evidence here that various kinds of arcane skills have been used in this house. One of them may be exacerbating Semmelweis's hysteria. She picks up the item with the most noticeable residual arcane fluctuations and tucks it away.

Although Semmelweis is not afraid to take risks, moving forward blindly is not the best course of action. The hallucinations would significantly disrupt her <nobr>decision-making</nobr> abilities, so it is time for her to retreat.
This is now an empty nest. The wasps have been driven away and the nectar has been picked clean. There are no new clues to be found here—it is time to leave.

Although Semmelweis is not afraid to take risks, moving forward blindly is not the best course of action. The hallucinations would significantly weaken her combat abilities, so it was time for her to retreat.

The woman's lifeless eyes widen, her lips and hands trembling. She suddenly embraces Semmelweis, unleashing a stream of obscure prayers and tears upon her. After Semmelweis is forced to endure this experience for a while, the woman bursts into tears once more before leaving in silence.

The woman's lifeless eyes widen, her lips and hands trembling. Then tears begin to stream down her face. She clasps her fingers together and, in a manner that defies logic, gouges an object wrapped in black ink out of the painting. After Semmelweis takes the object, the woman bursts into tears again before leaving in silence.
I don't know, madam ... You should ask someone else.

The woman's lifeless eyes widen and she immediately begins to scream, frantically clawing at Semmelweis as if trying to gouge her eyes out. No one can understand her, but one thing is certain—she is in pain, and she wants everyone to feel it.
The victorious Carbuncles are overjoyed and generously share their booty with Semmelweis.
The Critters are furious and reluctantly retreat. Semmelweis successfully carves out a <nobr>wagon-sized</nobr> territory between the two Critter clans.

Experienced travelers know that the information provided by the map is far from complete. The "grassland" marked on the map is just ahead, but in reality, it is completely shrouded in fog—a gray blanket that turns the landscape into a soft, blurry haze. Perhaps there is danger in this softness, or perhaps not...
This is marked as a traversable path on the map, and the fog shouldn't last long. Perhaps a break is in order?
This is marked as a traversable path on the map, so I doubt there's any danger waiting for us in the grassland. I'll explore the path ahead—follow closely behind me.

Feeling an unusual dizziness with every breath, Semmelweis quickly realizes that the mist is not entirely harmless. Could it pose a greater danger to humans? She glances at her unconscious teammates and decides to take a detour to avoid any potential risks.
I'm sure it will come in handy on our journey.

Semmelweis blocks her companion's hand from reaching the bottle and drinks the potion in one gulp. Before her eyes appears a pack of dancing bears, which quickly transform into fluttering oak procession moths. After recounting her vision to the man, who seems lost in deep contemplation, she receives her reward.
We don't want to risk our health by trying your potion for you. But perhaps you'd be willing to accept this proposal instead—sell your... "treasure" to us for a reasonable price.
The man hesitates for a moment and nods quickly in agreement. Semmelweis is spending a considerable amount of money, but it is money well spent.

Semmelweis blocks her companion's hand from reaching the bottle and drinks the potion in one gulp. She feels a shiver run through her body and her limbs go limp. She immediately signals her team to apprehend the man, who assures her that "the sensation won't last long." He offers a reward and begs for mercy.
It looks like the team's training needs to be stepped up a notch.
According to the rules, I can take your stuff if I win, right?
That's enough of this nonsense. Let's go.
We are in desperate need of some rest. Thank you for helping us out.

The eaves offer shelter from the wind and rain, and the soft, fluffy bedding provides a comfortable place to rest. Everyone has their own reasons for choosing to build dens instead of camping in the wilderness. Even Semmelweis can't deny that she misses sleeping in a proper bed.

There is still a missing team member who has not yet returned, but fortunately, large buildings are easier to spot than a group of sleeping bags in the wilderness. With the coordinates of the accommodation provided by the associate, they should be able to find their way back soon.
Requesting temporary assistance from a Field Agent Squad member is not a complicated process, it involves just a few monotonous steps.
Was the singing I heard coming from this lake?
No, this isn't it. The song I heard was different.
But they are similar ... I should get closer.
Venturing deeper unprepared would be unwise, as only the red deer and Olitiaus dare to grace the shores of the lake. Semmelweis quickly averts her gaze from the tempting waters.

The mud and sand are soft, the lake water is cool, and the song sounds low and shallow, floating on the surface of the water and lapping against Semmelweis's calves. She picks out certain phrases that seem to be from a language she has never heard before.

The Olitiaus fly away, their wings beating in perfect harmony. A trail of silver, as bright as freshly fallen snow, flashes across Semmelweis's waist—it could be the reflection of sunlight on the lake's surface or maybe even an enormous fish tail.
Shoot. I should get out of here.
Venturing deeper would be unwise, as not even the red deer dare to grace the center of the lake. Semmelweis quickly averts her gaze from the tempting waters.

As Semmelweis and her party finally arrive at the entrance to the mountain, a breeze carrying a slightly rancid smell greets them. The abandoned Tatzelwurm lair now serves as a home for refugees, but their targets have already moved on to another exit deeper in the cave, accompanied by new followers taken from among the desperate inhabitants.
Tatzelwurms love confined and complex habitats, and this cave is no exception.
Using the excuse of an "academic investigation" and with the aid of some gold coins, Semmelweis persuades the remaining refugees to sketch a diagram detailing the layout of the cave.
It's not perfect, but it'll do the job.
Even with multiple openings, the cave is a manageable size. The team thoroughly searches every inch and discovers several useful items before finding the exit.
As I suspected, there is no danger here. The only thing that has suffered from all of this is our noses, as we now smell like a pack of Tatzelwurms.
Could there be... piles of gold down there?

There are plenty of long ropes among the team's equipment, but the coins still seem impossible to retrieve. One of the team members suggests that perhaps the gold coins can be fished out with Goldfinch Coins.
Goldfinch Coins don't like to bite as much as Sharpodonties, and their beaks aren't as strong as those sharp teeth. But where there's a will, there's a way... good luck.
Semmelweis is in charge of a team of humans, who are not typically known for their creativity. The team chuckles at the suggestion, and has no intention of implementing it.
Alright, whatever we do, we can't stay here for too long.

Semmelweis remains silent as she bends down to toss a coin into the water. Immediately, a pair of tiny hands made of flowing water reach out and grab a few coins before quickly pulling back into the water. "This is what I deserve!" A few drops of water splash onto her hands as a warning.

Semmelweis remains silent and bends down to throw a coin into the water. Suddenly, a small pair of hands formed of flowing water reach out and grab her coin purse before quickly retracting into the water. "Did you really think a few coins would be enough for a consultation? I don't think so!" A few drops of water splash onto her hands as a warning.
What Semmelweis desires cannot be obtained from this place.
A <nobr>two-wheeled</nobr> wooden cart is parked by the side of the road with a bunch of tools scattered around it ... Its owner has probably just stepped away for a moment.
A large number of unlabeled storage bags are piled here.
There's a metal box with glass beads, a whistle, and little tin soldiers. These all seem to be part of someone's childhood possessions. There's also ...
The secrets here have nothing to do with us.
An old pair of glasses, an unfinished love letter, and clippings about an arcanist. This child grew up and fell in love with someone from another race. And then ...
An article in the local news reports on an <nobr>out-of</nobr>-control arcanist who murdered a human. The photo accompanying the story shows a shockingly young victim. That about all there is here.
The owner could come back at any moment, so we should probably go.

The charred black sound of horse hooves echoes through Semmelweis's memories, as if patrolling a lush green expanse. As the horse gnaws at the grass, a crimson flame burns from its body and sears into Semmelweis's consciousness, forming the shape of a fateful omen in the ashes. It blocks out the sun, overwhelming and irresistible. Semmelweis has no choice but to accept it.

Semmelweis opens her eyes. The world around her is still a hazy, chaotic blur, but the snoring of her teammates and the rustle of the tent fabric in the wind are so very real. She thinks she can hear the sound of those hooves getting farther and farther away. After closing her eyes again, she falls into a dreamless sleep.

Semmelweis accepts her fate as she had accepted the doctor's diagnosis. The shadow envelops her, devours her, and melts her into a cocoon of darkness ... The pain is so vivid—the power infecting her is twisting her into a new species.

Semmelweis begins to flee. The road has no end, just like in her dream. She is pursued, exhausted but unable to wake up. Suddenly, a force pushes her away and she is jolted awake. Overcome by a sense of weightlessness, she feels as if she is floating on air, before realizing that it was her teammates who woke her.
Thank you ... *cough* I'm fine. It was just a nightmare.

Semmelweis finally realizes what is happening—a nightmare sprite has managed to enter her mind unopposed during her Beyond Disease outbreak, and is attempting to turn her consciousness into a delicious mental ice cream through excruciating pain. Her mind has not been completely slurped up by the sprite—she still has the strength to fight.
Sorry, there's no such thing as a free lunch. At least not in my mind.
I'm afraid the enemy has already discovered that the trap has been triggered. We need to get out of here as soon as possible.
It seems like it's time to make a decision... Should we do what needs to be done now, or save our resources for the future?

Time was against them, leaving no room for an optimal solution. As long as their hesitation didn't cost them precious time, any decision would do. Despite the minor pain from the thorns, Semmelweis and her team hurriedly gathered as many scattered supplies as they could.
Time was against them, leaving no room for an optimal solution. As long as their hesitation didn't cost them precious time, any decision would do.
We still have time. Be careful of the thorns and retreat carefully.
Just grab whatever's worth the most nearby!
Move toward the edge of the trap... Grab that package!

Semmelweis takes a step back, only to find that the ground has disappeared from beneath her feet. A shiver runs down her spine as she looks around in shock. She is now in the cabin, safe and warm. Nothing seems out of the ordinary.
Was that a just a dream, or ...?
The door closes behind her. The furniture creaks as it blocks her path in all directions. Semmelweis has awakened the cabin, and it seems to harbor evil intentions.
The truth is, we're here in search of a dangerous arcanist cult.

The hunter nods and tells Semmelweis and the others to take a break. But as he walks away, he quickly returns with a hunting knife and his trusty dog at his side. With fierce intensity in his eyes, he lunges at Semmelweis and curses: "May Perchta protect me! You treacherous human lackeys!"
Actually, we're here to study the characteristics of this region's soil and its impact on the local ecology.
The hunter nods slightly, indicating his lack of knowledge on the subject and his inability to help. "At least you'll get a good night's rest! Hang on, I'll bring you another bowl of soup!"

Semmelweis finds herself hugging nothing but thin air. The Winged Cat's true intention was to steal her backpack! The Critter uses the claws on its back to grab the goods, while the rest of its body struggles to escape, quickly eluding Semmelweis and her team's pursuit. The only consolation for the team now is that they finally found a decent place to rest during the chase...

Semmelweis realizes that her pocket has been emptied. The Winged Cat's true intention was to steal her purse! The Critter uses the claws on its back to grab the goods, while the rest of its body struggles to escape, quickly eluding Semmelweis and her team's pursuit. As it sprints away, an Artefact comes rolling out from its fur—an Artefact that clearly belongs to some other unfortunate victims of its deception.
The Winged Cat is swiftly chased away, but on the next part of their journey, Semmelweis and her team are constantly harassed by Critters.
Blood stains. Someone was injured here and fell into the river. Something shines in the dark water. Perhaps the unfortunate person lost something here?
Brr ... Gold? I can hear the river talking to me.

Semmelweis plunges into the river. It is as if she is diving into a corpse, or into death itself. She returns to shore before hypothermia sets in and discovers that one of her team members has somehow sustained a wound. She has taken some of the river with her, and so it seems the river has demanded equal compensation. A new lichen vine blooms.

This is not one of Semmelweis's hallucinations. The river is indeed speaking to her. It used to be clean and pure, but now it is murky and toxic because its gold has been taken from its sands. Now, it wants to take back what was stolen from its depths. The gift of gold comforts the river—it offers foreign objects that do not belong to it at Semmelweis's feet.

On their journey, Semmelweis's team encounters a young man surrounded by Dryads. Grateful for their rescue, the young man explains that he is a skilled craftsman with a talent for reproducing beauty of art, and hopes to create a collectible as a thank you gift for the team.

The young man asks Semmelweis to choose the collector's item she wants to "keep as a souvenir," then pulls various strange tools and materials from his pocket and becomes engrossed in his task. A few hours later, he returns to Semmelweis with a handicraft identical in appearance and function.
Thank you for your kindness, but we're in a hurry. Perhaps next time.

The young man bids a regretful farewell to Semmelweis and the others, and before they part, he hands them a pouch of money. Semmelweis accepts it for the time being, although she cannot tell whether it contains real gold coins or the young man's "reproduced artwork."

A book materializes in Semmelweis's backpack, but it is no ordinary book. A haunting voice echoes in Semmelweis's mind, but it is no ordinary voice. Its piercing gaze brushes her fingertips as it asks, "If collective ignorance stems from dictatorship, where does individual ignorance stem from?"
Seclusion is the birth of pride and decline.

This is a trick question that should not be answered logically, if at all. She is fully engrossed in the book, her physical appearance fading away as her inner thoughts and desires are revealed. Semmelweis's body begins to feel weak and numb, but her heart is racing with intense heat, as if it might burst out of her chest.
Blind obedience is the death of knowledge and progress.

This is a trick question that should not be answered logically, if at all. She is fully engrossed in the book, her physical appearance fading away as her inner thoughts and desires are revealed. Out of nowhere, a scream pierces the silence, and Semmelweis realizes that one of her team members has disappeared from the end of her group.
This is one of the strangest invitations I have ever received.

Many of these tombstones bear no names or dates of birth or death, and there is no discernible difference between the graves of arcanist and human beings. All life is equally laid to rest here. A unique atmosphere pervades this place—one that cannot be described as joyful, but one that brings a sense of calm and peace to Semmelweis.

A unique atmosphere pervades this place. The night is eerily quiet, but in comparison, the morning feels like a fresh start. Despite the team's relatively peaceful rest, upon stepping outside, Semmelweis discovers that one of their teammates on night watch has been seriously injured in a beast attack.
But I didn't hear any commotion last night ...
It's a very unique "attraction," but it's not exactly the best place for sightseeing.

In the middle of the path, a jukebox stands out like an eccentric homeless person or a wild animal that has escaped its cage. Its play button is pushed in front of Semmelweis, and it blares a short, repetitive tune: "Pick a song! Pick a song!"
Any song will do, just make this thing stop.
The rhythm beats in Semmelweis's chest, awakening memories of battle, gunfire, and the sight of enemy blood. They resurface before her, beckoning Semmelweis to join their dance.

Eventually, the excitement dies down and everyone falls into a peaceful slumber, smiles of contentment on their faces. But as with all good things in life, there is always a price to pay for such blissful dreams.
The jukebox quickly becomes a torment to the ears as it plays song after song. The machine refuses to stop, spitting out countless gold coins and swinging until dawn.
A young Carbuncle calls to Semmelweis in a pitifully hoarse voice. Semmelweis is somewhat puzzled. Has someone imprisoned it just to hear its beautiful song?
Semmelweis reaches out in an attempt to silence it, but the creature is not easily subdued. It bares its small, sharp teeth and bites down hard on Semmelweis, feeling threatened by her presence.

The workmanship of the cage is far from meticulous, and even though it is only chained, the young Carbuncle is unable to break free. The critter regains its freedom, and as it shakes its body, something rolls down from its unkempt fur.
The kin of this creature will not simply overlook its struggles. We have no reason to interfere.
Sadly, this bottle of Dr. Papper is well past its expiration date.

The glass bottle smashes into the critters hiding in the bushes, who are whispering loudly to each other. "Groo! &%#!" The critters scatter in disarray, dropping loads gold coins that must have once belonged to some unfortunate passerby.
As expected, it's the distinctive taste of Dr. Papper.

No matter where or when, Dr. Papper always satisfies and leaves a delicious taste in your mouth! Even if you are struggling financially, unemployed, single and feeling lonely without any company, there is one thing you cannot do without: Dr. Papper!—A rant from a teammate.
Great, we can resupply over there and wait for the fog to clear.

However, what lies ahead is not a lake, but a swamp. After several members of the elite team are attacked by monsters and multiple sacks of supplies are swallowed by the swamp, Semmelweis has no choice but to ask the Foundation for help.
Great, we can take a breather over there and wait for the fog to clear.

But chaos looms ahead. The fog weaves in and out of the trees, its dense green embrace enveloping the team, layer upon layer, until they are nearly suffocated like insects trapped in amber. Even when the team manages to escape the fog, the fluctuations in the artefacts they carry linger.
The timing of its appearance is too much of a coincidence.

Despite the guidance it offered, Semmelweis insists on relying solely on intuition. The team stumbles along, placing unwavering trust in their own instincts until they finally emerge from the fog and into the moonlight, dispelling the shadows that had loomed around them.
Someone must be controlling them for some purpose... Not good!

Before she can process what is happening, it is too late. The team is surrounded by hundreds of ghosts, trapped amidst strong winds and crashing waves. Cool blue flames wash over them, and as the flames recede, they are left with only their lives, much like survivors of a shipwreck who have finally reached land.
It's too late, the approaching waves are already visible. Semmelweis must face the situation directly and without hesitation.
It feels as though they are being controlled! Join forces and push through!

The words on the paper start off neatly, but gradually the handwriting and narration become blurred, illegible, and difficult to understand. Semmelweis turns to the last page, which is just as neat as the first, with a single word in German—"Redemption." Feeling through the back cover sleeve of the notebook, Semmelweis finds an Artefact.
The many sentiments in the pages of the notebook are of no concern to Semmelweis.

The team is ambushed. Semmelweis fails to gain the upper hand in the skirmish, and neither does the enemy. She snatches an artefact from the leader of these Manus followers and finds a piece of information inside: "The 'Awakening' will dawn upon this era—when the darkness fades and the light embraces us once more."
The tent is dimly lit. A thin, pale hand slowly reaches out from a corner, desperate for any ounce of compassion.
Of course, we will do our best to help you. We believe these supplies will meet your needs.

The beggar accepts Semmelweis's charity. When Semmelweis withdraws her hand, she notices that the beggar has placed an artefact and a note inside: "The 'Awakening' will dawn upon this era—when the darkness fades and the light embraces us once more."
The team is exhausted beyond belief. Semmelweis refuses to let her team continue in this state, aware of the dangers of rushing for immediate success and gratification.
The lockbox opens to reveal a neatly attached syringe in the center. The accompanying instructions indicate that it can effectively relieve the pain caused by the infection.
The lockbox opens, revealing neatly stored instant food and medical supplies—exactly what Semmelweis's team needs.
Whoever the real owner of this box is, they obviously didn't forget to put some security measures on it.
The <nobr>three-act</nobr> opera, Tosca, will be performed at the Vienna People's Opera on ... the famous opera singer ...
The names of the main actors and the time of the show are scribbled over.
It reads: "They breathe, feel, suffer, and know love."
Candlelight. Murder. A beautiful temptress in a satin gown ...
Her love and her hatred. Her sadness and her death. Her reputation.
Semmelweis does not share the same passion for opera and respectfully takes a step back, giving the tree some room to admire the masterpiece on its own.
The path expands, revealing new territories.
Character Level not limited by Real Level.
