We're in, finally. Every door leads to a new space, so what I'm trying to say is, "The Three Doors" will probably lead to ... "The Third Space"?
Well, I've heard of that before. It's a space beyond reality and imagination. You may find its traces in both the real river of time and the imaginary one.

Hope you don't mind this grandma won't stop nagging. Just take your time to organize these little ideas in your mind during the exploration. But do take these words from me: never stop where you are. Alright, I'll see you again when the time comes, darling.
Tap on the ground to walk.
Hey, what's that? It's a letter. Don't you pretend you didn't see it!

I know what's going on in your mind. But think about it: this is a special circumstance and manners are not to be considered, you understand me? How do you know if it's for you ... before you open it?
Touch it. Try to evoke a piece of the past.

C'mon, my child, c'mon. Pick it up, put it away, admire its uniqueness, and imagine the coming days with it by your side. You can read it again when you feel like it, just like how you always do with letters.
Maybe ... Oh, I'm only guessing, maybe it's all worth it.
The ice's surface is very smooth—smooth enough to make for a fun slide—but the only question is, which side is the right one?
Now watch your steps! Ooh, look at you, staggering on the ice ... Yes, that's how things work when you walk on it. You go one way and you won't stop until you are blocked.
*sighs* I had my days, when I was young and motivated, just as you are. I dashed and dashed until ... yeah, until I hit the wall and broke my head.
Knowing what choices to make is far more important than just dashing forward. Well, you are free to interpret it the way you want, because I've been there, but it does sound like a cliche.
Oh darling, the answer won't pop out by itself no matter how long you stare at the riddle. To solve it, we need something that plays the decisive role, something hiding here.
Now take a step back. That's right. Back, and look around. Sometimes you have to stay away from the showcase to see the price tag of the dress.
When encountering temporarily impassable roads, you can try exploring the surrounding area—you might just stumble upon an undiscovered secret...
Hmm, it seems to fit just well in those columns. That reminds me of diamond rings: it's not necessarily the biggest one that looks the best on your finger. Hah, I guess life just loves to joke.
Oh, but you need to know that was just the judgment of this grandma's old eyes. It's not 100% precise, I'm afraid.
The frame, nothing but another door. We've seen enough doors so far. Have you ever fallen in love with a painting because of the frame? I've seen too many cases like that ... including myself.
Where will it take us? You'll know when we are in the painting.
Feeling a bit dizzy, darling? Relax. Take a deep breath and stare into the distance. You'll be fine when you get used to it, just like how you deal with car sickness.
It's not a royal road ahead. Be careful, darling.

These steles remind me of the letters from some juniors I know. I put them under my bed and somehow one of them pops out from time to time. Those juniors arrived in this world after me, but left before I will, just like a group of movie viewers in the theatre leaving before the movie has ended ... All I could do was sit there and guess what they were in a hurry to do.
That was an amazing experience, even though I don't remember the details. Are you recalling the ones you miss because of my words? Why not take a closer look?
Touch it. Imbue it with a purpose.

You heard it, too? I thought my ears were fooling me again. It's the vibration! The vibration made by the steles, isn't it? It sounds like a kind of ... emm, rumble? Like that of a collie which just woke up.
Tap here to open your Backpack.
Tap here to use the Monolith of Solid Rock.
Place the Monolith of Solid Rock here.
Tap here to confirm the Monolith of Solid Rock's position.
Oh, this stele can conjure a pillar.
Huh? It's not falling where you want it to? Relax. Let's see what we can do. You should listen to what my grandmother always said, "Nothing is too difficult for a child with a beating pulse."
Touch the Monolith of Solid Rock. Destroy it.
See, another lesson from life. We always have the chance to make up for what we regret, well, in a way slightly different from our plan, though.
Touch the Monolith of Solid Rock again and pick it up once more.
<nobr>Mm-hmm</nobr>, you did a good job and got the hang of it. Time for some field practice.
Rewards gathered from The Three Doors will be displayed here. After accumulating a certain amount of rewards, you'll be able to claim them.
Oh ... I know you must be surprised, darling, but we are old friends. We have talked many times.
Oh let your guard down. A grandma like me won't be in your way. We can talk about me later, when we need to. For now let's seize the day and take a look at the new stuff that just came in.

As you can see, the fog has filled up this place, giving it a little bit of a mystery. If you see it as a magic show, I'm sure the answer to the mystery is close enough to us, only separated by a piece of red velvet cloth in the magician's hand ...
Now, darling, open the door and go through it. That's what it's for as well as what makes it better than a wall, don't you think?
Whether it's locked or not, the door itself is already a sign of seduction. It's waiting for someone to pry into its little secrets ... even eagerly, I suppose.
Tap here to open the door.
Looks like your nose is sensitive enough to find the right way, even in this stinky dump.
No no no, it's not yet time to blow your nose or rub your eyes. Before you take a nap, there's something you need to know ... the "good news."
What a strange sensation. I feel warm all over, full of energy, and invincible!
Perhaps... it's because I understand myself better now. I understand what it means to do what I'm doing.
Hey! I've got it! We should record the process of revival! The traces of our experiences and thoughts—
This is sure to be helpful.
A thousand... a thousand years of burning, the land turned red by passion! I danced a thousand years ago on my native soil... to pass it on!
Lady Ulu! Please calm down, the flames are rising again!
She seems to be confusing her past memories with the present. We must help her remember the era she belongs to.
The era... I belong to... hmm...
Where we came from and where we're going, the starting and ending points of the torch. Do you remember how we met?
Ezra helped with the application, and Spathodea brought the repairman... that's good.
Everything's going smoothly... Perhaps we need to find a time to talk, just to make sure everything is perfect.
You've noticed the power inside Uluru Stadium. It's the "Fire Totem," which burns brighter through understanding and spiritual connection.
Click to check characters in the Golden Thread
Oh, Malingee's Harvest has always been my forte!
This time, I'll be the one running through the land, igniting the flames, finding you in the fire... don't worry, I'll run faster than before!
Don't underestimate <nobr>grown-ups</nobr>. I still remember to avoid those "big heads" and not to pass under their watch...
A little flame can quickly grow from a shared spark. Fire shines unceasingly through sharing.
This little spark is enough to handle that bunch.
Just avoid the wandering pebbles. Find the gaps, and you can reach the finish line without stopping.
What? Blocking the way is against the rules—!
Well, these heavy and obstinate stones are such a nuisance. They always seem to be trailing behind someone.
I need to think. Should I take a detour, or just quickly solve the problem with a flame...
I... I remember this place, the red soil, the stone monsters of Malingee, and the flames... I put my hand into the fire, and then I became the fire.
I should keep running, carrying the flame I picked up with my own hands. Yes, I have to make a decision...
I will find the answer at the end.
The ground here... looks like it could crack at any moment. I need to run faster and jump over it in one go.
Maybe I can get that tall figure blocking the way to step on this thin layer of soil and fall into the pit... Yes, I need to find a way to lure it over!
I finally spotted a trap. Hey, Flammy remembers the crossbow bolts we used against Malingee!
Lucky I can't touch the ground. No need to worry about setting off traps... This makes things much easier...
We're so close now, Flammy—I know you've caught that spark from memory and are bringing me back into you.
We'll run the rest of the way together, traversing every patch of land.
I hear the voice of the flames speaking to me, rising with the beat of my heart.
Again and again. I'm getting closer to the end... Her words are becoming clearer.
Are we going to meet? Outside the dream, on the real red earth?

Please slow down, Miss! You have a paper horse stuck to your cloak ... there you go.
Just a few pieces of red paper, madam. They must have fallen from the Zhuye.
As the gentleman just said, they are probably related to the unique Eastern "prayer" custom.
It is said that by cutting these pieces of paper into shapes, you can make a wish to the gods and receive their blessing.
People who travel often say that they follow the customs of their destination. I think we should also try this custom.
But we need to be safe.
Of course, madam. They say each design corresponds to a prayer. If you figure that out before you do it, it won't be a problem.

Tatzelwurm, a highly territorial arcane creature.
Like a lizard or a snake, it has a long, slippery body, yet its grotesque head doesn't match the body at all.
Usually, it lurks under the ground and only shows up to hunt when it senses arcane fluctuation. It attacks with a disgusting, poisonous breath.
Thank goodness I brought a gas mask with me.
I can still hear that song.
Is it some kind of arcane skill? Or a symptom caused by my condition?
I know many <nobr>pure-blooded</nobr> arcanists with incredible talent also suffer from auditory hallucinations ...
... but I never thought that would happen to me.
Emil, I heard you would be promoted to Vice Director of the Belgrade branch after this mission.
Congratulations. A Vice Director in his twenties is rare to see even in the history of the Foundation.
Oh, come on, you deserve it. There's no easy job in the Field Agent Squad. Of course, the pay has to be good.
The song is still haunting me ...
I hear it more and more frequently after I arrived at this mountain.
Anyway, the clues show the Manus followers are nearby.
The critical point has been generated. I'd better complete the mission and go back to the headquarters as soon as possible.
The Manus followers are right ahead, according to the traces.
Wait, the red color, it's so beautiful ... I must reach for it ...
No. I'm seeing things this time?
So the hallucinations have invaded into the real world?
*deep breath* I need to hurry up.
Looks like the old fellas here have been waiting for new guests.
It's been so long since they had the last guest. Apparently one of them can't wait to open the door for you. Yes, the one that illuminates the column.
Alright, now try and light up the other one. There hides the key to the door, I suppose.
Redirect the light by turning the prism.

Open Sesame.
Let's go. A path has opened for you.
Sorry, darling, but don't take hospitality for granted.
You have to do it yourself and catch the light this time.
Relax. It won't be heavier than the Suitcase.
Pick up the shelf and carry it with you
Move the prism and place it under light
The light is now going where it should
It looks too worn to react to the light anymore. You need to search around to do something about it.
Like a walker with an umbrella in the rain, like a camper with firewood by the tent, you are ready. Time to bring the light back, darling.
Ooh, a hollow column ... The light can go through it to travel even further.
My my, the ceiling is so hard not even rats can make a hole in it, not to mention the formless light. This is where the little thing in your pocket comes in handy, darling.
These prisms seem different than others

Adjusts the angle, tightens the ribbon, and smooths the wrinkles.
Rolls the cuffs without drawing attention, unrolls them, and rolls them again.
She looks at herself in the mirror,
And the gentle good night.
I am ready to offer everything I have, for the new world and its <nobr>well-being</nobr>.

"I am first! I always am!"
The little winner jumped into the house of gray and white marble.
The third place?
NO! NO! NO!
That brush of orange jumped out of the chalk box, and even out of the house.
"Where is she going this time?" Murmured the little winner, "Will I ever see her again?"

Carve and polish. Water, oil, honey and sand pile.
The moonlight witnesses the transformation of the old branch and the birth of the new wand.
The branch is reborn by the craftsman.
The craftsman is reborn by the future.
Identity means nothing to the forest.

The night will blaspheme against the light,
As well as the beauty, the happiness,
The peace, the slumber,
And every lullaby in her heart.
Since then, in the future of the future,
There will be no more peace in the long night.

Through the wind and the rain, her voice grows louder and louder,
Echoing within the limited space.
Further, higher, it never ceases to spread, NEVER.
Owning the audience and the theater, the queen remains on the stage,
Still seeing herself as the lord of the infinite universe.

Paths are made by walking.
Wine and bread are achieved by working.
The new sprout stretches its leaves,
Fighting sleepiness among the mountain of potions.
More time, she needs more time,
To read the next page of the book.

Wait, dodge, escape?
Sense of security, side of caution?
No.
Record, record, and record.
Record this very moment.
Yes.

Under all the spotlights, she is like the blackhole of attention.
The most beautiful dream in that beautiful nation.
Her hair is more expensive than gold, and her lip print can be exchanged for a bundle of cash.
Yet her heart, that very heart,
Is not worth a gold coin, or a silver one, or even a glance.

Rabbit, rabbit, takes a cookie,
Hatter, hatter, pours the tea.
The Cheshire Cat lays the table,
Alice lifts her cup with glee.
So do not weep, our dear old guest,
Soon, we'll have a tea party.

On the sleepless nights,
On the painful mornings,
On the long afternoons with no one to talk to,
She opens one book after another.

When lifting the fog from the city, be careful,
Don't disturb the people hurrying home.
He travels through the city in alleys and arrives in time.
His duty will catch up with him, just as always.

The golden wattle drops to the ground. She sharpens it, polishes it till it is matte.
Half of it turns into the handy bow and arrows,
The other half turns into the streamlined surfboard.
"The tree is free as long as you are free," says the ocean.

Sitting in the small cubicle,
She typed. 41, line break, 41.
It was quiet, tranquil, and stable, 
and in the world of numbers she was safely swaddled.

Your child has never been your child.
A smart guardian is good at finding quality time to spend alone in the afternoon.
When the red fruit is fast asleep,
Will the gentleman fall from the tree?

The light is shining ahead.
It makes whatever is white whiter and whatever is shiny shinier.
Expectation, curiosity, desire, they are what the world is made of.
What I know about it is not the complete picture.

Do poems belong to parchment?
Do poems belong to walnut shell and ink?
Do poems belong to the nobles and the king?
No, said the snowy night, poems just belong to themselves.

Look around.
The edge of the stage is so far, far away.
It is beyond the islands, beyond the sea, beyond the ban and the fear.
Laugh, laugh away! There is no ending to the play!

The sailor embeds the cracks into his eyes, savoring the <nobr>bone-burning</nobr> pain.
With paeans and bleeding offered by the burning, the navigator floats high in the mist to burn down the wrong paths in the way.

Resonant and vigorous, its sound can awaken and guide the lost.
It will cleanse the people's chests when necessary.

A flash destined to disappear into craze.
The coin of greed has been tossed; it witnesses the beginning and the end of a moment.

The dark night peeks through itself, leading to a secret delight.
Along with scream and whine, the familiar death arrives as it has foretold, bringing a swamp of corpses.

The owner of those eyes which can see through everything keeps running towards the fireless night on and on.
The silent guiding horse, the Quiet Ravenheart.

Soft as breathing, itchy as allergy and hysteria.
Rubbed, grinded, twisted, tangled, the long thread connects savage and contempt.

The beating, thirsty hope of life.
The itchy longing from the bottom of the heart, the immortal new life. It grows, and grows.

An unknown fruit, both sweet and sour.
It has never existed for real, yet people eat it to savor the taste of loss.

Memory wears out in the wandering life, gaining only obscure colors and shapes.
What is the figure of the shadow in the shadow? The close friend of the close friend's strolls over in the delightful music.

The tortoise walks into the flame without hesitation.
It is devoured, soothed and drowned. It doesn't know whether it is dead or alive, nor can it feel a thing.

Unable to build its own nest, the common cuckoo is remorseful and tired.
No one affirms or denies it is a fraud.

Eight, twelve, diamonds, water drops, shining bright.
Those with levels, those with standards, those given certificates, those disqualified and discarded.
But I, I too, was once a fistful of sand.
Uncountable and uncared for.

The snake is hissing to find its way.
No one knows where it is going, but its tongue will find the scent of its prey in the air.
The desire hidden in the depths. A precious material which can be used to increase a <nobr>5-star</nobr> Psychube's Amplification level by 1.

Yesterday, today, tomorrow.
Remain silent, remain calm, remain loyal.
The precepts swim down from the glorious mountain peak.
Climb through the window, drill into the bed, deep into the skin.
And so we comply, we lower our eyes, we lock up our tongues, we abandon our thoughts.
But we still have hope.

Rolling forward, falling along the expected trajectory.
He looked around and felt at home.
Each cog has its role,
Each indispensable, each insignificant,
Each existing within a vast machine.

On the left side of the street, a stalker.
On the right side of the rear window, three fools seeking revenge.
Beneath the earth, fifteen feet away, the <nobr>thousand-legged</nobr> worm wriggles without end.
The wolf pack surrounds. Until the last of the milk, sugar, and oil mix enters their stomachs, they are all safe.

He finally came up with a new plan.
Though somewhat absurd,
Unemployment was no longer a concern.
The <nobr>so-called</nobr> new donkey life, inspiring awe and expectation.

Where does the story begin?
Little stones, red earth, distant fire.
Groping silhouettes, in the night sky, those who chase fire.
Hand in hand, heart touching heart,
surging deep in the throat, my warm fire.

Sharper than any blade, fiercer than any flame.
In the hall, in the shadows, in the busy daylight and the dark night.
In moments where no heads of the wicked need to be severed.
If you do not forsake justice, it will not forsake you.

Sails billow, swords shine, down the river.
A star twinkles in the north, chase it, chase it.
Conquer the seas, the lands, the ice rinks, and park reservoirs.
Your star twinkles in the north, Lagasa, Lagasa.

Green mountains, willows, and moonlight.
Fragrant wine in poetry and beyond.
The sky within the city and the sky beyond.
Each word and stroke, what is known and what is still unknown.
Observe and learn, the world is like a cloudy wine, its taste only discovered through trying.

Watching, always watching. Five hundred years for spring, five hundred years for autumn.
Under the shade of the trees, there is nothing new.
In bones, in jade, in stories read countless times,
Yet the puzzle remains, still existing.

Coffee, cocoa, or perhaps "dark matter coffee." The dark liquid swirls and swirls. 
On the far side or this side of the universe. 
Tasteless, acidic, completely chilled, not recommended for consumption by any life form. 
Not much different from working on official business.

Poetry is here, says the poet. 
Winter is here, says the bushtit. 
With the tip of a pen, the claw of a foot, with the soul or the silence of knowing everything. 
Write poetry on the blank earth.

Used for imprinting the psyche, providing minute experiences.

Shiva's divine bow cracked at the consort selection contest, yet Rama and Sita's love for each other was undeterred.
The queen saved the king's life on the battlefield. In return, the king promised to fulfill two of her wishes.

Envy and avarice twisted and tainted these two wishes.
On the eve of the coronation, the prince is condemned instead to a <nobr>fourteen-year</nobr> exile.

The kingdom falls into the hands of outsiders, or is lost, or cannot be protected. The heir Bharat is unwilling to ascend the throne and swears upon the boots of his elder brother Rama to wait for his return.
During his exile, Rama is beset with attacks ordered by the demon king Ravana, and must contend with danger all the time.
The witch Surpanakha falls in love with Rama, but her love is unrequited. Her plot to swallow Sita whole is thwarted, and she has her ears and nose cut off.
The demon king Ravana sends his minion in the guise of a golden deer, to lure Rama away. He then takes advantage of Rama's absence to kidnap Sita.
The headless monster convinces Rama to travel to the kingdom of monkeys. In that kingdom, the embattled Monkey King Sugriva is faced with infighting between brothers.
With Rama's aid, the Monkey King Sugriva is restored to his throne, but Sugriva gives himself over to the pleasures of the flesh and neglects his duty to the kingdom.
Betrayal and distrust soon catch fire to become the blaze that dooms the kingdom. Sugriva is persuaded by his wife Tara and eventually repents.
The divine Vanara Hanuman becomes a loyal follower of Rama. He travels south and crosses the sea to the island of Lanka, where he tracks Sita down.
Hanuman passes Rama's ring to Sita to inform her of his intent to rescue her. Sita declines to travel with Hanuman and insists on waiting for Rama to arrive in person.

The Vanara wreaks havoc in the kingdom of demons and attempts to intimidate Ravana into letting Sita go despite being captured.
The infuriated king torches the Vanara's tail, and he flies from his cage, destroying the city of the kingdom of demons with the fire before returning to Rama.
Rama uses his war machines to erect a bridge across the ocean to Lanka.
The demon king's younger brother Vibhishana is a just person who respects Rama greatly, and considers him a friend.
Disheartened by Ravana's rejection of counsel, Vibhishana decides to declare war and leave his brother's side to fight for Rama.
Rama leads his great army across the bridge into a pitched battle with the demon army. Casualties were high on both sides.
Rama's arrow pierces Ravana's head, but the demon king's head keeps regenerating. Ten heads, a hundred heads were destroyed, yet the demon king still lived until an arrow found his heart.
Wrath was the second head, for Ravana insisted on going to war with Rama out of anger, causing his sibling Vibhishana to betray him.
Pride was the fifth head. Complacency breeds blindness, which in turn brings about one's downfall. The seeds of conflict in Lanka came thus.
Envy was the sixth head. The lack of both virtue and wealth maddened Ravana, robbing him of his conscience and rationality so that he walked step by step to his doom.

"Rumors suggest 'Qi' comes from all things in the world, capable of driving other substances to undergo unexpected changes."

"'Qi' could potentially replace the operation of steam engines, and I suspect its effectiveness would be no different than manually pushing a train." Note: The phrase "to personally lead" may prove that its ruler is adept at managing Qi.

"The saying 'You must first sweep your own room before you can sweep the world' may exist, but it is clear that a broom does not hold the same importance as a sword. " We are still on the search for ancient texts regarding the "Sword Control Manual".
"Eastern wands are found in a variety of forms, often incorporating everyday items as 'magical tools,' but each serving a specific purpose."

"The 'whisk' is made of horsehair and has the power to change objects with a single command. It has an overwhelming amount of power." Note: There are strict rules against using it recklessly to swat away bugs.

"Both talisman papers and wands have the same purpose. They are commonly used in civilian households to protect against malevolent beings and creatures." Note: The intricate designs of talismans are secretly passed down among select arcanists.
"Eastern alchemy also originated from the quest for eternity. It is known as the 'Golden Elixir'".

"Their obsession centers around achieving "immortality," and they have formed a secretive group dedicated to this pursuit." Note: It's not just the potion-brewing witches who are obsessed with 'immortality'.

"Those who have mastered the art of alchemy are in high demand in the palace, while others reside among the general population." Note: It is not uncommon for them to hold positions as cooks and doctors as well.
"In general, they do not attribute it to evil spirits. The locals have a strong belief in and reverence for spirits, often worshipping them."
"Ancient Eastern beliefs say that the soul of the living can leave the body to fulfill its purpose."
"Thus, there are spirits who have died but are unaware of their demise, and they drift through the world causing disturbances to the living wherever they go."
"Using chopsticks is like balancing a unicycle on a tightrope, but somehow they do it with ease."
"The East is known for its abundance of resources and mouth-watering dishes." Note: The Eastern Travel Guide recommends that you bring your own utensils.
"Their distilleries are full of unique flavors, each with their own brewing techniques that leave a lasting impression." Note: Do not underestimate those grains of rice.
"The critters of the East have unique appearances, likely influenced by their habitats. " The concept of evolution continues to carry weight.

"There is a creature called Gluttony, shaped like a man with a sheep's body, eyes under the armpits, teeth like a tiger, human hands, and a voice like a baby's." This serves as clear proof of Satan's existence on earth!

"There is a creature called Shu Hu, with the body of a horse, the wings of a bird, the face of a man, and the tail of a serpent." Before the continents drifted apart, Medusa may have lived in several places.

"There is a creature called Qiong Qi, said to have the body of a cow and the quills of a porcupine, its howl resembling that of a dog." Cross-species reproduction between wolves and cattle is under discussion. This is a breakthrough in biology!

"There exists a being known as Bo, resembling a white horse with razor sharp teeth, that preys on tigers and leopards." We believe this is the origin of the Eastern proverb, "When a white horse is not really a horse."
"To them, racial divides are nothing but a comical act." Ladies and gentlemen, witness this allegedly accepting society!
"The Olympian gods and the thirteen Gods of Sheti are present here, though they may be known by different names."
"Legend has it that as the New Year approaches, the Gods of Sheti take turns in their duties to safeguard all living beings for the upcoming year." Their timekeeping must be immaculate.
"During the year of service, there is no place for the thirteenth God of Sheti." A secret paid vacation.
"From the sky it falls, from the earth it grows; this is the origin of the lucky coin." Obviously their gods are not economists.
"People pick up these lucky coins to gain blessings and protection." Gentlemen, a new and more effective alternative to prayer!
"During the Dushuo Festival, they beat the Peace Drum throughout the night to ward off misfortune and evil spirits." They must have incredibly resilient eardrums.

"To prevent unwanted disturbances from wandering demons, ghosts, and monsters, Eastern cultures use spring plates and wine as offerings." Overall, Eastern Critters have little interest in trivialities.
"The streets are filled with the sound of firecrackers, deafening as the cyclops's snore!" The Eastern Travel Guide recommends earplugs in case of unexpected loud noises.
"Both spirits and immortals hold a place of reverence in temples, but only those with true devotion can attain the power of divination." At least it doesn't cost any money to seek its wisdom.

Those imaginary monsters only exist in the minds of children who can't distinguish fantasy from reality...
I'm not that sort of child... right?
Fortunately, they're not dangerous. It's time to go home...
Since then, I've distanced myself from my friends.
So, even if I end up like Alma, they won't feel sad for me.
Until I was a teenager, I walked alone in silence and doubt.
Does knowledge transform us from caterpillars into butterflies? Or is it like snakes shedding their skin?
After becoming a 6, are we changed or discarded? Or is it both?
This is a long beach, and it happens to be right along the edge of the sea. I am placed here, searching for answers to my questions.
I start by opening the first book—it's so heavy that its pages seem light.
"Introductio in Analysin Infinitorum"... Hmm, no, I must have missed something before it...
"Je pense, donc je suis...?" This is a language I don't understand...
Oh! Yes, this is it; this is the optimal solution. I remember the previous book mentioned it...
Looking back, I was happy in the early stages of my retreat.
Knowledge gradually fills me. I stroll along the coast, picking up shells at my feet, putting them in my pocket, and then continuing on my way.
I start to think more about higher, loftier issues than the direction I'm heading.
It is an enlightening salvation, an immersive feeling; I'm certain that the real solution to the problem is right in front of me.
With its help, I can finally stop wandering on that dark, damp shore every day. My body feels light enough to reach the clouds in the sky.
"...Now the gods have sent me here to suffer more misfortune, my sorrows are not yet over, and the gods will send endless calamities..."
"The horse hasn't been brought yet, she stands there. Good-bye has already been said, and there is nothing more to say to each other."
"People who talk about themselves a lot are often just trying to hide their true nature."
That night, the wind was gentle. I stand on the beach, watching the night turn to dawn, the rays of golden light rising over the sea.
Waves crash forward, halting at my toes. I think of Alma, of those brief, <nobr>not-so</nobr>-lonely days that followed.
The metal on my forehead is cool to the touch - a gift from Sophia and 37, and apparently with some contribution from 210.
Sophia? Well, she stands on the shore, hesitant, perhaps looking for wood to make a small boat to follow in their wake.
They appear as graceful, gently curving lines. I understand it now; I see it. People's destinies spread out like long trails on the beach.
I don't understand their feelings, their situations, or the circumstances under which they made their choices.
I only know, but I don't understand it - just like my own fate.
Suddenly, I feel the humidity of the ocean heavy on my eyes.
My vision blurs, and the sea's horizon grows distant. It sparkles gently under the rays of the sun.
"...A peak of grey-blue waves, lifting up white foam, stirs the deep blue beneath..."
"...The tides and currents of the sea are constant..."
I stumble, my toes stepping into the waves. The icy cold washes away all knowledge and words associated with it.
Yes, this is what I'm missing.
Knowing is not understanding. Seeing is not experiencing. Nothing I thought I "knew" was more real than the cold water lapping my toes.
Until that 'revelation' truly arrives, I can never claim to have understood fate.
I close the picture book in my hands, feeling its gritty cover and solid texture.
...Then, I don't need any other books.

After a meeting discussion, the Foundation has officially named these two temporal disasters the "Storm".
Undoubtedly, the Laplace Scientific Computing Center is one of the institutes most severely affected by the "Storm".
Contact was lost with multiple research institutes, and over seventy scientists were sent back in time, including the previous and current chief officers and nearly half of the research department leaders.
Even now, many of these positions remain vacant.
The impact of the "Storm" on the Laplace Scientific Computing Center is not just material. Many of the surviving scientists have lost their faith in science and rationality, as well as their ability to conduct research.
In light of the foregoing, I have concluded that the Laplace Scientific Computing Center has completely lost its ability to perform its proper functions.

Genuineness is the key to everything. It can open up a chatterbox and a closed heart alike, and it can ultimately open the door to harmony.
Friendliness is the warm sunshine that melts the snow. It warms the rich soil, sprouting seeds and nurturing the flowers of friendship.

You meet an elderly traveler. He greets you warmly, but you cannot understand what he is saying as he appears to be speaking German.
You met a lady wearing a Foundation field uniform.

The second you hear the sound of the bowstring loose, the arrow is already flying toward you. Fortunately, the arrow lands at your feet, and you are not injured.
You look in the direction the arrow came from to see a pair of alert eyes glaring from the bushes.
You stumble upon the <nobr>half-eaten</nobr> remains of a goat. The pungent smell of blood indicates the approximate time the goat died—this tragedy occurred within the past three days.
A child's cry sounds from behind you. You recognize this figure. It's the <nobr>bow-wielding</nobr> shepherd boy who was hiding in the bushes—the one you gave some bread.
You encounter a Laplace researcher. She has been stationed on this snowy mountain for some time now. When she finds out that you are the new curator, she is overcome with excitement.
At the corner of the mountain road, you encounter a masked hunter whose entire body is swathed in ragged animal skins and strips of cloth. Fortunately, he seems to bear you no ill will.
You pass through a valley with hop trees dotted around both of its sides.
The campfire of this temporary cave camp has only just been extinguished. It appears some mountain climbers spent a relatively warm night here.

You meet four travelers journeying together—four travelers who have already achieved their climbing goals. They set off from the mountaineer's retreat this morning and began their descent down the mountain.
A masked hunter sits on the snow in a frail state. He is tightly wrapped in animal skins and cloth strips. Bloodstains mark his clothes. His left shoulder is injured and bleeding.
A masked hunter lays on his back, clutching a copper hand axe. His chest shows no signs of inhalation, and it seems clear that he has taken his last breath.
A research base established by the Foundation. With food, plants, and intelligence, it offers you many choices.
Turning the corner of the mountain road, you come across a lake formed by glacial meltwater.
You spy an abandoned mountaineer's hut which may be used as a temporary shelter.
A gas stove designed for mountaineering has been discarded on the roadside. The remaining fuel could still last for a while longer.
You discover a cave ahead, a natural shelter from the wind and snow. The sound of wild beasts can be heard coming from inside the cave, but you feel too exhausted to tempt fate.
The broken cable bridge between the cliffs blocks your way forward.
You discover a tunnel formed by the melting of ice and snow. You have no idea where it will lead.
You find animal footprints in the snow.
As you pass through a mountain pasture, your presence alerts the cattle. You have entered their living space.
A group of Eurasian lynx block your path, hungrily awaiting the perfect prey.
The wind and snow are increasing in intensity. A blizzard will soon arrive.
A stream blocks your progress. The stream is relatively wide, but the water is quite calm.
A mountaineer is resting nearby. He shares his observations with you. He tells you that a rare plant can be found on the cliff ahead.
A wolf lies on your path forward. Its fur is dark, and its hind leg is caught in an animal trap, rendering it unable to move.
You hear the sound of ice breaking. Your experience tells you that an avalanche is coming.
A mountaineer walks directly into your path. He tells you that he has found a rare and precious plant and hopes to trade it with you for supplies.
You pass by a cliff and notice that the protruding stone on its edge is perfect for standing on and taking in the view.

A snowboard lies by the side of the footpath, half buried in the snow. Although it looks somewhat old, it still looks usable.
As you move onward, you notice a small path faintly visible under the cover of bushes by the roadside. It is apparent that not many people have taken this path before.
You notice a small supply station ahead, where a group of unfamiliar climbers have gathered and are chatting and laughing.

You come to a <nobr>three-forked</nobr> junction. The slope on the left is relatively gentle but appears to be littered with countless jagged rocks, the path in the middle is steep but is closest to your destination, and the small path on the right is close to the cliff.
You find a cluster of magenta berries by the rugged mountain path. They are the same as the ones you picked from those fertile plains.
The lake ahead has frozen over. The icy surface doesn't look particularly thick—treading on it could be risky.
After the snow and wind subside, the sunlight shines through the clouds and beams upon the snow. As you look up, you can see the clear sky far above.

A Eurasian lynx appears not far from you, vigilantly watching your every move.

While walking through the snow, you stumble over something. After digging around your feet, you uncover decaying remains.
You are overcome with dizziness and begin finding it difficult to breathe. Your body sounds an alarm, demanding more oxygen.
Walking through the mountain pass, you find a sublime trekking pole in a crack in the ice sheet, but its owner is nowhere to be found.
You take a break at the large supply station. At such a high altitude, the stars seem almost within reach.
As you approach the mountaintop, the icy slopes become increasingly steeper, and the one before you now poses an extreme challenge.
A glacier topples with a deafening crash, blocking your path forward.
The closer you get to the mountaintop, the thinner the air becomes. You find it increasingly difficult to breathe.
After climbing for such a long time, your pickaxe is finally starting to wear down.
Above the snow line, the weather becomes increasingly unpredictable, and a sudden heavy downpour hinders your progress.

The mountaineer expresses his gratitude to you. "My friend, you deserve this and much more. Please accept it."

In addition to the images from his grandfather's life, he also discovered some photos of certain strange objects, which have hereby been sent to this newspaper... We speculate that the objects in these photos may have been used for cooking or to hold water.
If any of you among our faithful readership can identify these objects, please write to us with more information.

We can tentatively confirm that these objects originate from the ancient Far East. This vessel is notable for its remarkable coloring and bears evident cracks but no observable signs of infirmity. This is quite the discovery, as records speak of an ancient Eastern custom where cups would be thrown down to signal the commencement of aggressive action, like the throwing down of a gauntlet, and this vessel now provides us with incontrovertible proof of this. It is highly likely a leader or general would give orders with a dedicated "throwing cup" that would not shatter but ensure a reverberating sound.

"A poisoned wine cup used exclusively by prisoners, a cup for cultivating mandrake, an infinite spring water grail, a projectile used by the ancient peoples of the Far East to hit arcanists..."
Mysterious Ancient Artifacts of the Far East Resurface!

Yes, we'd better stay awake, stay calm, stay cautious all the time.

But then there comes the problem: how can anyone ... how can you ignore your love for those thriving plants and blooming flowers? How are you supposed to deal with the unstoppable feeling that overflows like a melody when it is stirred up by the beauty of the scenery?
Of course, you will cry the loudest cry, dance the wildest dance, drink the strongest drink, and vomit all the filth inside you.
After all, there is no need to enter the woods if the <nobr>soul-stirring</nobr> scenery is not what you are after, right?
It doesn't sound like a good way.
No, so you'd better let it slip your mind, darling.
Just let it go, and hurry forward. Remember to keep your eyes shut and hold your breath.
When you do so, the scenery will no longer mean anything to you, nor will the fragrance of the flowers. You will get out of the woods and reach where the truth lies.
Is that what you want? Don't worry. We have plenty of time. You may come back at any time and pick another way.
Come here. Place your hand on it. Feel the texture. The craft is one of a kind, not some cheapie you can get from the flea market.
I mean it. This is a kilim, and even the most traditional, delicate, and expensive kind. It has applied fiery red as the dominant color, and the stitches are perfectly neat.
From the sea, just like you, darling.
It arrived with a meerschaum pipe, a glass jar, a pack of sugar cubes, and a child in panic.
Both she and the kilim were born on the land where the craft originated. Their appearances apply the same dominant color, and the patterns in them share similar complexity.

Oh, your curiosity is aroused? But we are not done with the carpets yet. You've always gotta get a souvenir or two every time you reach a new place, so you will have something to show when you tell the stories one day, right?

Look at these handmade fabrics. How splendid ... Those incredible patterns were the only thing on the craftswomen's minds when they made the carpets. It's safe to say they have spent their whole life improving their skills at using the vertical loom, and that's how we get these carpet knots arranged in beautiful lines.
But they are just people like us. What if they get distracted? What if the carpet knots go off the right track and get tied to the wrong threads?
Then you will be in trouble, big trouble! All the problems in the universe will come at you, and the situation will be even worse than the bureaucratic system of a millennial empire.
Damn it! Damn it! DAMN IT! #Can't we do something to fix it?
Calm down. Many swear like you do when there is nothing they can do.
They always step into the same river named Mistake again and again. That's why we need THEM, those crossing the river with their rulers, spanners, tool boxes, and dusty faces.
I like the pragmatic quality in you. I'm sure it will make your life even more wonderful. The people will be impressed and line up to tackle the problems for you.
Oh, don't be mad. Some make troubles, and others deal with the troubles. That happens.
You know, every question has a questioner when they are raised. Likewise, every error has a corrector when they are corrected. That's how we get to know THEM.

Their duty is to remove the loose threads and iron out the wrinkles on the carpets. In the language of this island, that is to check the calculations on the papyri and even the holes on the punched tapes.

No one is capable of doing this job except the altruists, because it is similar to unraveling a ball of wool. Besides finding the end of the threads, you must always pay attention to the cats. Yes, the cats. They may jump on the ball and make things even worse.
And she, the <nobr>red-haired</nobr> little girl with the carpet in her arms, was overwhelmed at the beginning.

Not yet familiar with the ruler, she tried her best to find the end of the threads. So the cats took the opportunity to jump on her together and left countless scratches on that little forehead. Poor girl.
See, that's the problem every Corrector has to deal with: their job is to correct errors, but what if their own existence is also part of the errors?
Oh, it's no big deal. There is more than one loom in this world.
She left the complicated patterns behind and came to this simple kingdom featuring numbers only.

There she made the first contact with the spinning loom named geometry. She had never seen anything like that before, and it was almost impossible for her to comprehend how it worked. She could hardly convert the numbers on the books into an actual diagram in her brain.

Without a whole picture of what she was working on, she resorted to her hard work, and more hard work. Then a long time passed, leaving one wound after another on her fingers. Later, the wounds even became calluses.
In the end, her hands were no longer tender, but tough enough to resist the damage from the loom. Yes, she has won a place on this island for herself.

Yes, she's a quick learner. She learned even faster than some of the locals, but that was not enough, because she has been outmatched by her playmate, the leading one in the field of mathematics on the island.
That girl is like a perfect piece of satin born by nature. It is decorated by the beauty of mathematics and geometry, no manual work involved.
In order to reach the showcase where that perfect piece lies, and ... to stay on the right track and fit into the school ...
She has done everything she could.
But, BUT! She is still the most distinctive carpet there.
Anyone can tell that as long as they spend some time on the island.
It's not wrong to be distinctive.
Of course not. She's only a bit "different" from others.
So she will continue to weave on the loom until one day the spindle pierces her callus and the fire burns everything to the ground.
Shh, I should stop here. You know that mathematician who was thrown into the sea? He died because he said something he shouldn't have.
Cut not wood on a public road; open not an unwanted bottle.
I don't know what to say next. I guess the best line for this circumstance is, "See you later."
If you look at the ground after the "rain," you can often see a wet, long trail like this one.
At the end of the trail, there may be a snail slowly crawling forward. Yes, "forward." The snail marks the direction for us.
But, what if we don't see any snails at either end? How are we going to distinguish the direction to the future from that to the past?
We need a criterion. #Sorry, but I have no idea.
"Criterion," well said, darling. To figure something out, you always need to make deductions based on facts and logical reasoning.

What you see is not necessarily true, but what is logical is, because we haven't witnessed or experienced anything illogical so far. If something like that actually happens, it must be because we are too ignorant to understand it for the moment.
This point was firmly believed by those researchers who worked in the house like canned sardines.

It remained true to them until the first drop of rain rose. The sardines suddenly found that the knowledge they possessed couldn't support the point anymore. The can was opened, revealing a completely different thinking pattern to them.
Whatever they used to mend the can, there was still a crevice left between the inside and the outside, and it could be ripped open again at any time.
Oh, you just figured out how those researchers handled matters: face the ignorance and do everything they could to find the answers.

When the rain rose, they struggled to collect every component left, hoping to preserve the castle built by science. Unfortunately, the effort was in vain. Another wave washed away the castle and restored it to quicksand.

Even so, they still worked hard in that house like canned sardines to record what was happening, because they believed at least the can holding them was a safe place. Yet in the end, they found that the can was only another sandcastle on the beach.
Everything they were familiar with disappeared when the first drop of rain rose.
The chaos didn't last. If it really was the rain that swept away the snail and messed up time ... then, we should look at the silver lining.
Does it mean we will find out the truth of time once the secret of the rain is revealed? There has never been a shortcut like this one, since time is only an intangible concept.

So then, observation stations were built all over the globe. The staff learned how to collect and keep the valuable samples efficiently in no time. The little boxes they used to store the raindrops are still being upgraded even now.
Order and silence were brought back to the labs. Every piece of gear was placed back on the right track.
It was a grand feat, and no one could have accomplished it inside this huge, cumbersome machine except another machine. She took no sides and sought only predictable results.

That's why she made a decision as soon as she read that report and its attachment on her desk. The former was about a delicate component which flapped like a butterfly in that huge machine, and the latter was a piece of paper full of circles and dots.
Then she stored the information on her hard disk and destroyed the report.
And the paper which claimed to have recorded the locations where the "Storm" might happen—yes, the one with the <nobr>butterfly-like</nobr> drawings—was retained for data comparison.
She seems satisfied with the result.

Remembering the sweat and the shouts, it's as if the flames in the torch are still burning. During the event, arcanists and humans alike took to the field with enthusiasm, reveling in the pure joy of competition. We noticed that after the games, many spectators remained absorbed in their books, giving a silent curtain call to this historic sporting event.

Now, those returning from the mists have brought with them stories and curiosities from ancient Eastern lands—about a travel interview, a collection of observations, a local chronicle, and the birth and death of a question. Writing with a soft brush is indeed a unique experience, but words are always faithful and eternal messengers. To this end, the UTTU Flash Gathering awaits your visit amidst the fragrance of wine in the quiet alleys.

<size=40>Over</size> a thousand years ago, a traveling priestess brought back a pot of red rock powder for her tribe.
Staring down at it, she told a story.
We have bestowed the warmth of the tribe and the stalwartness of family on the "Kangaroo." It is the way home.

<size=40>A</size> woman was separated from her tribe while hunting and couldn't find her way home. She wandered in the wilderness for seven days and seven nights until she was finally brought back home to her tribe on the back of a kangaroo.
Her survival was a miracle, and from that moment on, her people firmly believed that those tall, strong beasts were guides who would always carry them home. This belief dissolved into her bloodline, lasting thousands of years and giving this place the guardians of today.

<size=40>W</size>hen the world was first created, natural disasters were a common occurrence, and thus, the Malingee was born in the forests and wilderness. Giant rocks made up its body, its hulking joints grinding with every footstep. It lingered on the edges of the tribal grounds at night, afraid of the burning campfire.
The woman prepared to set off once again. This time, she would search for the eternal flame, for the glory of the tribe, having heard the legend of the <nobr>many-colored</nobr> lizard.

<size=40>A</size>t that time, the world was devoid of color. The sun god sent a colorful lizard to the world, which cut itself open and gushed its colors upon the land, transforming the world into something entirely new. Its green blood spread into the forest, its blue eyes seeped into rivers and lakes, its yellow scales coated the mountains, and its purple bones crumbled into the valleys. As for its red heart, it landed in the center of the land, like a protruding belly button.
We bestow the dexterity of sport and the focus of perspicacity upon this colorful lizard with its joyful heart.

<size=40>T</size>he woman passed her <nobr>coming-of</nobr>-age ceremony and became a priestess.
She hunted and killed a bison, pinned its skull to her waist, and then set off on a journey.
This skull called to her so that she never forgot to look up at the night sky. In the sky, a winding band of light shone. It was a fish. Its shadow fell on the ground so that she could tread on it and never get lost in the desert.
We bestow the brightness of life and the expansiveness of memory upon this lively fish, the guide of the starry sky.

<size=40>Through</size> forests, across lakes, over hills, and upon peaks, the woman searched. She found the red heart of the earth. It was a huge red rock.
The woman removed the bison's skull, upon which it rolled around in the soil and transformed back into a bison. There, they fought again, but this time not as enemies but as friends. Seeing such a scene, the heart of the colorful lizard began to beat again.

"<size=40>"I</size> love all that you are, and so I will bestow upon you an undying fire."
He promised the woman a stunning flame and asked her to pursue it for herself. "You will find it.
Go—find it. You know its heat, its form. It will burn in the same posture as you when you run. Remember to keep its call on your knees."

<size=40>T</size>hat's it, the heart of the colorful lizard said, I love everything so very much—the running and the flying dust. The way you stand shoulder to shoulder with your friends is so mesmerizing. I used to jump like that, but then my body took on this giant stony form.
The woman replied, "I am just as happy as you are. My heart is as passionate, brave, and generous as yours. Three hundred days from now, when the sun turns around the rainbow, I will lead my friends to see you again. Please prepare some land for us to run upon freely."

"<size=40>Indeed</size>, indeed," the lizard's heart said, "I have bestowed upon you the heart of hearts, the bones of bones. Bring all of the creatures best at running and swimming before me." A red rock then rolled down from the valley.

<size=40>S</size>o the woman, with her heart and bones, rode on a red clay cow and returned to her tribe.
By that time, she had grown old. Her relatives were no longer there, and the children no longer recognized her face.
She leapt from the back of the cow, and the red stone turned to dust. She put it in a bucket and threw it into the fire, then said that this was Malingee's Harvest, and that they were going to meet a great heart.

*sighs* In the blink of an eye, my dream slips away like a deer into the deep of the forest.
Heh, what kind of question is that? You make it sound like me dreaming is the most ridiculous thing in the world!
I have to remind you, except for some <nobr>out-dated</nobr> wisdom, there is nothing different between your head and mine, dearie.
I'm as curious about that as you are.
You could always allow me to return to my soft bed to try to summon that dream again. But even then, it likely won't be the same dream.
See, we seldom remember our dreams, and even what we don't forget can be hard to understand. And that's why we need a dream interpreter.
A doctor that values Shakespeare above his patients, and cigars above his own career—a doctor like Sigmund Freud.
He lures out forgotten memories from your past, through a technique called "free association." Through this, he can reveal what makes you who you are.
All you need to do is to lie on the sofa, and spill out your thoughts like old milk.

Once you do that, your mental health will surely improve. The sleepwalkers stop falling out of their beds, the hysterical go back to their sewing, with enough time maybe Nietzsche could write a comedy.
"But what about the medical journals?" You may ask. He must have released them. Otherwise, how could we prove the effectiveness of his treatments?
And he has. You can read them in journals, in the text books, and hear them in the chattering of medical students—
Your name will be blacked out on the pages by then, but your dreams will become the latest gossip on everyone's lips.
It's not good for the patients.
Oh my dear, all medicine has side effects. The best medicine is bitter to the taste.
It must be tolerated for the sake of the treatment. How else will these patients free themselves from their mental cages of unconscious desire and delusion?
It really is the smallest of prices—a mere coffee stain on your shirt, just telling a few people about an unlucky moment or two.
Besides, the patient does not give a name. The true protagonist remains a secret between you and the doctor.
Heh. Perhaps you're right. It's not the only way ...
Come, listen ... Do you hear that? That shrill, piercing sound of metal on the skull, the <nobr>blood-cuddling</nobr> screams ... Even the strongest soul would quake in fear.
But this is the other way. However, funny enough, some people prefer the pain. It ends faster than a hard talk with the doctor.
Look at this, dearie. This kind of hand mirror has become the latest fashion. Oh, it's a trifling thing, but people like me have to stay in the loop to make a living.
Come here. Gaze into the mirror, and fix your hat. What do you see? Do you like what you see?
I feel as if I can see all of Vienna.#I, I ... I!#It's broken.
A clever answer! I can tell you will fit right in here.

But there is still much left to see beyond the mirror. Oh. The young folk step to an <nobr>ever-changing</nobr> waltz. If you want to follow their trends, you'll need perfect timing to join the swirling dance.

Some have fallen behind. They lounge by the fountains of the park, bemoaning their lives and the price of rent. Come the next banquet and exhibition, they arrive wearing a new fine coat, but underneath their linens are ragged and old.
The mirror's reflection held a silver sheen once. Now it's tarnished at the edges.
Oh, look at our little artist in the mirror.
Something of a narcissist, then? No, I'm not laughing at you. In this place, valuing one's uniqueness, one's own voice is much to be desired.
You have to be loud enough, firm enough to show no fear, nor hesitation. So that at the end of the waltz, you will have the strength to break their instruments.
Is that so? Oh, has something gone wrong? Did an old lady like me waste her money?
Or, perhaps what it reflects is the "truth."
The mirror shows reality, nothing more, nothing less. So, it may be that there is nothing to see, or it may be something that can't be seen.
But things change, darling, especially in this city. Like an avalanche taking everything in its path, changing them irrecoverably and inevitably.
So next time when you look into a mirror like this, you may just see something else. Be patient.
So, in the warmth of spring, the ice cracks deeper. One splinters into two, and each begins to splinter again.
They set up the mirror and lift the cloth exposing to light—the good, the bad, and what lies beyond them both.
Then the factions split and then split again. "Secessionists," by their nature, are not in the business of keeping things together. They won't stop the fractures—they can't.
In lifting the cloth and seeing their reflection, they scatter themselves like dandelion seeds in the wind.

Oh, I don't know where, but I do know what they're doing. Some of them still paint with gold leaf, others believe they must depict what is real, some depict the ravings of their dreams, some seek to change the streets into works of art, and others drive out all meaning from their work.
The only time they ever reach an agreement is just before they lift the cloth from the mirror.
Before the Potemkin village with all its empty facades moves somewhere else, some of them might just achieve their ends.
To be like the golden cabbage sitting atop its dome over the Ring Road—to be recognized by everyone.
Let's start our conversation with a simple exercise. First, please repeat after me: Dittarsdorf.
After all the days you've spent in Vienna, you should be familiar with the name. Tell me, how do you feel about it?
Nothing worth mentioning.#Seems like it's a word as heavy as lead.
Nothing indeed. Well, you've become numb to it after hearing it so many times, on the street corners, in the cafes, every place you go.
You can't blame them for that. Most at least speak kindly of them, so long as you don't pick up on the venom hiding in their words.
These days, to be an opera singer is more glorious than any noble title; it supersedes them all! The Dittarsdorfs are the true nobles, the ones who can create art through "channeling."
Haha, you are making light of it again. But fair enough, you're new here, not as familiar with this name as those who live here, murmuring it in their dreams.

Most of the time, it swirls invisibly through the conversations on the street; other times, it is tangible in the signatures of the exhibits, seen in the performances and the metal badges clinging to collars ... and always in the boys and girls who inherit the Dittarsdorf talents.
And just like that, they are thrust into the role of the outstanding Dittarsdorfs, the lady songbird and the artistic painter.
In truth, I don't know much at all about these "Dittarsdorf."
Oh, of course. Well, then, high time to tell you about them.

Vienna, at present, is a splendid, crumbling house. Whenever the waltz starts playing, the roof trembles along with the music. While the dancing crowd—and funny that it is a crowd—none of them dare look up at it!

The people here live in identical, pretty, little houses, the social classes smoothed out like butter on a cake. Now, works of art become their icons, and in their madness, they scramble to make these beautiful, dazzling things.

The Dittarsdorfs, nobles who can perform channeling, are made to perform like dancing animals in a circus. Businessmen and nobles clamoring to sponsor their performances in order to glorify themselves.
The noble ladies prefer to curate the finest acts, highlighting their good taste and fashionability, while the lordlings seem to prefer new and hidden talents as some example of their virtue.

How, then, could a good singer ever miss a performance? But she must, to take her chance, seizing the lovely bird in her hand—that poor, noble little bird, because people said that she was born with madness.
And it is in this act of "fighting against her madness" that she proves herself proper among the noble ladies.
She knows better than anyone why a piece of art is valuable, and how to make it worth even more.
The Danube, a river born from dewdrops grown into a mighty course. She is a mother to many children, and all are eager to be fed.
Here is the empire founded by two of her strongest children—a rich and admirable duo.
There is an alluring charm to the music of Musikverein, captivating everyone who visits this place. I can talk about its art all day, and that's just the beginning!
There are 11 children in this empire. When bond together, they are invincible.
See, the flourishing cities, the cheering citizens, even the chirping birds are singing a song of a land of freedom.
Something's not right.#Hmm ... What a promising picture.
Heh heh ho. You're familiar with the devils in the detail.
Ah. You're just buying everything I'm selling. Be smart, my dear.
You'll see, if we dive deeper, you'll see something different.
You'll see charity dances raising funds for the poor. The icing on the cake for the philanthropist, they said, though no one knows where the money goes.
You'll see mice eating the bodies of the beggars, the arcanists being ousted from their arts, and poverty spreading its misery like an illness.
Except in the great duo, Austria and Hungary, in the vast and intimidating centers of power they've built together.
The other children, however, were shut out at the door. They may have their talents, but that alone cannot buy them a place at the table.
Bohemia, Moravia ... The empire has only the slightest sympathy to these forgotten children, nothing more than articles of fine words written in the newspapers.
How funny it is. To see these poor humans now sharing in the same fate as the arcanists.
Do you think they will choose to hold together, even if left outside of the negotiation table?
Cooperation is the only way they can survive.#People are stubborn.
That's no small task. A chain is only as strong as its weakest link. An <nobr>age-old</nobr> story.
Oh. So you're a pessimist. Then, I guess, you will enjoy the drama of this broken family.
The truth is, they will fight each other like rats in the barrel, until every one of them falls.
Crack, crack. Did you hear it? It's the fracturing of a great empire, like the breaking of spring ice.
In an army that speaks twenty different languages, who can a general trust to obey his commands?
Only those who speak the language he does.
You can already imagine it—a ridiculous beast with 11 limbs, each pulling in their own direction, limping across the battlefield until it gets shot ...
Luckily, that time hasn't come yet.
The crying of the children is still being drowned out by the music playing in the theater, and the beating hearts within the dancers' chests.
The wails of suffering are silent in the newspapers, and the world sees only the silvery mirage of freedom and prosperity.
Believing all these children can live in harmony.
But my darling, we know that the ice must break. It's as inevitable as the thaw of spring.
Ah ... A lovely day to rest at an outdoor cafe, isn't it, darling? Everyone working here is a capable server and knows how to address you properly with "my lady."
I'm here for one simple thing: information. With a careful ear to the <nobr>goings-on</nobr>, a shrewd businesswoman can gather all the latest news.
Oh, there she comes, that girl in green with the bouncing feathers in her hat. Don't worry. She can't hear us from here.
Of course, you do. Isn't she our lively little cockatoo? She says she's a psychiatrist, but with all the work she does for the people, she's more like Vienna's own Robin Hood.
Look at those people around her, <nobr>tut-tut</nobr>. With their gold cufflinks and patched sleeves ... Very likely they're from Leopoldstadt.
You can hear them saying, "Our golden era is finally here! Forget all these melodramatic rumors!"
Maybe you know it by a different name? Perhaps you caught a glimpse of it under the list of exhibit sponsors?
Europe, at that time, welcomed people from all over the world; its culture and art held as their highest ideals; its institutions believed they held the keys to paradise.
They once believed that they were the lucky few. Blessed with the wisdom of a golden age, that's why they still linger here even after the smoke of war faded the glimmers of gold away.
It's not surprising to see our lady with them. See, she loves to seek these <nobr>well-hidden</nobr> things, and chirp along with the most overlooked voices.
But I feel sorry for her, because she herself overlooks some of these <nobr>teeny-tiny</nobr> things said at her own expense.
Words taken as jokes. Ignored because her wishes and anticipation outweigh their sting.

But while songs are floating in the wind, the clock keeps ticking, people in the cafe talk about the secessionists and the newest plays in the same breath ... No one cares about the rumors trafficked in the newspapers. They're only concerned with what is in front of their eyes ...
Still, the good doctor comes to share the pain of that melancholy lady, and then, next to the cafe, to encourage the lower class to persevere.
She says that every man is entitled to the same rights. She'll draw a circle around them all, like the Ring Road or the round mirrors in her clinic.
"The good times will come again," so say the coffee sippers. But you know, in the end, they'll be like the undissolved sugar at the bottom of the cup.
My dear, your coffee is getting cold.
Darling, did you hear that? The sound of a match scraping against the box, igniting in a dark, silent alley ... and then, "BOOM!"
War, like an unstoppable train, hurtles down the track with its passengers, vanishing in the thick, black smoke.
In the train, the elderly tremble in the corner, and the infants babble dreaming ...
Ah, but the only young man aboard is filling coal into the furnace. Meanwhile, another train is hurtling down the same track, puffing the same black smoke ...
Alas. The two trains are destined to collide, in "a war to end all wars."
Who are the passengers on the other train?
Pay close attention. You'll see the banner reaching out above their train, and the bloodstains on it.
Next, let's turn to where the train departed, to find the source of everything.
Rewind the clock to before the whistle blew, before the furnace ignited ...
And then, child, look somewhere far from here—in the Schönbrunn Palace, where the fine gentlemen of <nobr>Austria-Hungary</nobr> eagerly plan the extension of their national borders.
But the Habsburgs value their "honor" so much that first they must find themselves some excuse to cross that border.
Yet in another land, a humiliated people were gathering in secret. Their blood as hot as fire, ready to burn anyone and anywhere it was splattered.
Fate drove an <nobr>open-topped</nobr> car there, carrying an <nobr>ill-fated</nobr> couple. Their presence a crushing indignity that could not be endured.
An avenging bullet was sent to them as a gift from a <nobr>luck-struck</nobr> patriot.
In a moment, each party was granted their <nobr>long-sought</nobr> excuse. Boots had their excuse to kick down their doors, and guns their excuse to fire.
A yearning furnace at last had its reason to burn, to steam toward its final destination.
My dear, it's not a story of hatred or anger. The footprints were laid down before you ever stepped forward into them.
<nobr>Fresh-faced</nobr> boys traded books and toys for rifles, and poets were buried in trenches, musicians deafened by explosions and the howls of death.
But those <nobr>war-starters</nobr>? Those who doodled their ambitions on maps while supping their dessert, would lose nothing in their gamble.
The <nobr>dew-fed</nobr> river would still flow, and the facades of their great palaces would never be chipped or rocked by the guns they set off.
Nothing stains their hands, save the cream from their cakes.
Is there nothing we can do to stop all this?
Perhaps ... We wait. Wait for a pouring rain to douse the fires, a flood that might sweep the armies, wagered like betting chips, from their maps.
Then perhaps that car will turn, and the fated dead will come back to life—But you know that will not be how the story ends.
Hey, you! Yes, you, my hurried child, you rush through the street like a cyclone ... Where are you going?
I can't be late for the show!
A show, a show! So you came to Vienna for the love of stories. That's for sure.
Then this is just the right place for you. A place where the floors are decorated with gold, where music sings along with the stories ... Even a newcomer could be entranced here.
Oh, listen to me! You must not be a newcomer, but a true connoisseur! Well, before you leave, may I ask a simple question?
Which act in a show do you prefer?
Act One.#Act Three.#Act Five.#Every part of it.
Oh! Well begun is half done! You're always right to the point. We should know how a story starts and when we have stepped onto the path of fate.
Haha! The rising action! The most thrilling part, like biting into the filling of an apple strudel—you're about to have the sweetest part!

Yes, of course! The resolution, coming to its fated ending. We stand up and cheer, or stay in our seats and weep ... Our reward for not falling asleep during the intermission, worth every krone you've paid.
Haha, so greedy. It's a tough choice, isn't it? But you can't escape from making decisions.
Do you know which act I love the most? Not Act One, nor Three or Five ...
But Six. Oh! Act Six, my dear, that's the best part.

The part in which the king picks up his fallen head; the knight pulls out the sword in his chest; the bodies stand up, dust their clothes and come to the front of the stage, bow to the audience and receive their applause ...
That's not really a part of the performance ...
Yes, it is! My child, that is precisely when the real show begins.
I have a good script here. Let me put on my glasses ... Hmm ... Let's start from ... from Act Six.
The princess, a nightingale decorated with diamonds, an opera singer taking center stage, steps into a building of <nobr>gray-and</nobr>-white diamond patterns.
"And the curtain falls forever. The smile on her face seems too serene. She is still dreaming."
"Her madness keeps them all alert. But in the court, she seems so meek and mentally steady, like a docked boat on calm waters."
"Nodding elegantly to every gentleman she meets, she makes the shackle on her neck look like a piece of dazzling jewelry."
"In a transparent room, under an unyielding limelight, her dignity is stomped on, like a silk handkerchief thrown on the ground. They smash her crown, forcing her to pay for her madness."
"'Sleep, she said to me, sleep. If that's what she said, then I don't need to wake up.'"

"That's when the star falls into an <nobr>ever-lasting</nobr> dream. The blinding light becoming a spotlight on the stage; the empty room carrying the best reverberations. She has never been so calm. Everything beautiful in her is there forever, frozen in time."
I guess she went completely insane.
"Her world has become the performance. A show that never ends."
I'll say she's a great actress, isn't she?
But this is not a good story. I think it needs more context.
Hahaha, my dear. You are indeed a great connoisseur.
Only one act of a play can't tell a good story by itself.
Oh, forgive my ramblings. The golden curtain has risen.
Fix your collar, darling, and keep moving forward.

Grandma Jina received several amulets and gave them to Elena and me. Grandma Jina said that this amulet was for saying goodbye to winter and welcoming spring, but I saw some yellow powder mixed into the white hemp thread, I thought it might be daffodil powder, but Elena told me not to think too much—it couldn't have come from the cemetery.

Elena tied a knot on my amulet just like hers, so everyone would know we're sisters. She was so excited for Grandma Jina to see her handiwork that she didn't even take the time to read to me today—she just kept dragging me in front of Grandma Jina, but even now, as I write in my diary, Grandma Jina still hasn't said anything, and Elena has fallen asleep. Maybe she'll forget it tomorrow, but I'll remember it for a long time, because I want to tell her that we can't be sisters. The children in the orphanage don't have relatives. But I never said that.

There are exceptions, though, like if Elena and I are taken away by the same person, or the same couple, then we'll become sisters by law ...

The door of the orphanage is a very heavy door. I don't know how my parents managed to open it and send me inside, but maybe there are a lot of adults who can't open that door like me, so they couldn't come back to get their children. If someone knocks on the door and wants to come in, I'll run over to help them, and then I'll ask them to take me and Elena with them, and if possible, Andre as well ...

But it's okay if no one comes to knock on the door, because the three of us are together now.

As the steam engine begins to roar, resources are once again pooled and distributed accordingly.

But who would waste a glance on those who pass by on foot? The value of their labor devoured by machines—their souls forever tied to those emotionless iron things. They trade their lives for mortgages, and trade endless toil for <nobr>ever-scarcer</nobr> rewards.

Under the dark night sky, a worker stumbles down the street and sets down a baby girl on the steps of an orphanage. His right sleeve hangs empty, and he has lost a foot. His body is of no more use to the factory owner, even though it was the iron machines that made him this way.

The baby girl sleeps soundly until he walks away, until the sky in the east turns a soft white, and until the doors of the orphanage open.

Across the street, the loud footsteps of striking workers roll at a steady pace. They carry banners and shout slogans, and as they approach, the baby girl is awakened by their commotion and cries out to the dawn sky.

Inspired by the "Dance of the Seven Veils," the beloved Karlo sisters personally tailored an exquisite gown for Isolde called the "Moonlight Veil." Her headpiece, "Desires and Tears," is the crowning glory of the outfit, with pure white lace adding depth and sophistication to the piece, while the pearl necklace, representing tears, accentuates the wearer's soft beauty and elegance.

Elegant and serene, this piece embodies the pinnacle of art in jewelry, using materials that manage to be not quite prohibitively expensive. It is rumored to have once adorned a queen of the House of Bourbon. Though designed as a broach, it has been tastefully repurposed.

This genuine sapphire, weighing a staggering 326.37 carats, has internal <nobr>needle-like</nobr> inclusions that create a stunning optical effect known as asterism. Known as the "Star of Vienna," its radiant beauty speaks for itself.

Vienna, the portrait of elegance and tranquility—a pearl set upon the banks of the Danube.

Everyone knows that here, what people covet in their dreams is not merely wealth and power but something far more splendid—something that transcends class, rendering every sincere heart equal before it. It coats the barren mundanity of reality with a layer of wondrous honey, satisfying the Viennese senses to their utmost, thus giving over from taste to taste—art, and art alone.

It is an evergreen tree that grows on "desire," the world's most perfect deception. People water it with their most naked primal desires and their truest selves, sparing nothing in their devotion. "Elegance" is a golden fabric that covers wounds and makes even the most defiled shine.

Where hoarding is called "protection" and monopoly "selection." Where before a flat altar, a path paved with gold is lain, with all trying to pluck the sweetest fruit that grows beside it.

"Venus pities me," whispers an innocent voice from behind the curtain.

"Yes, yes," replies an older nobleman, leading the naive child away, while in the distance, outside the window, several plainly dressed children cling to the bars, longing for a glimpse of Venus.

Alas, they lack for much, having neither a smidgen of "talent"—a short middle name, nor the distinguished surname to follow it.
