She'll hug you, speak softly, and bake lots of apple pies. I can already imagine the workout I'll need afterwards!
But before that... we have to get Mommy to accept my profession and my choices—to accept that I've grown up.
Yes! When the time comes, I'll ride you there myself! I'll make sure you're sitting safely and comfortably on my little horse!

I think so too ... but instead of thinking about that, it's more useful to think about vacation plans.
On my next day off, maybe we can go for a walk together.
It's a subject for the sociologists and the <nobr>higher-ups</nobr> to think about, not me.
You don't give me medals, you don't make nice and useless promises, you don't pretend to agree with me ... You're my ideal boss.
Here in the wilderness, where voices are free to roam, it's much quieter than anywhere else.
People can do a lot of things, or they can do nothing at all.
In this space, anything is possible, whether it's planting seeds, or taking a nap, or writing.
No, you don't have to do anything.
If you're willing, I'd love for you to read me a poem.
For some, power is a seductive temptation. They revel in the control they have over the lives of others, ignoring the sword that hangs overhead.
And now, the responsibility to lead rests squarely on your shoulders.
I will not let my guard down because I have put my faith in others, but with you I have hope.
You are not easily influenced by power because you understand its heavy burden.
As long as you remain a righteous companion, my blade is yours as well.
I've heard that some people often bury boxes and dig them up after a period of time.
"This is a method of preserving and transcending time," according to the records I've read.
... Yes, I'm very curious about it all.
Although this technique may not be as effective in our time, it may still prove useful here on the open grassy field.
If it were you, what would you put in the box?
You still love toffee as much as ever.
The taste still lingers in my memory as if it were yesterday.
That's a good idea, Timekeeper. Do you have anything to write to the "future"?
No, please don't tell me. I look forward to reading it when the day comes.
Hey, Vertin, what do you think of shipbuilding?
No, I have all the technical skills I need. All that's left is that spark of excitement and energy, like rock 'n' roll!
Hah, of course! You think I'd forget the records and speakers?
I have just completed a state of the art audiovisual room. If you want to hear something, you know where to find it!
By the way, what do you think about me adding a tap dance aspect to it?
That's a truly rebellious concept! Let Pirate Radio take the music scene by storm across the globe!

But we can start by making small changes, like putting winged record players in the Foundation!
Which is more important for you, understanding, or experience?
Is it taking a leisurely stroll through the garden, capturing the vibrant colors of the flowers, or picking one and devoting all your time to watching it grow?
I can be of help to you, Timekeeper.
Radio waves carry stories and knowledge from every corner of the world, from the warm red lands to the frozen tundra beneath the northern lights.
And if you enjoy these stories, I hope you'll share your own with me as well.
Choosing to try new things is a wise decision, Timekeeper. It can lead to exciting experiences.
But there are times when not every piece of land is fit to be trodden.
Should you encounter any of these obstacles, my broadcasts will be your guide.
Just as apples must eventually fall from the tree, children must inevitably grow up.
Hmm ... Hello, Ms. Vertin. This APPLe is pondering some ... <nobr>sherry-induced</nobr> topics.
Yes, time, the ouroboros, the spinning wheel ... *burp* In comparison to this APPLe, you must comprehend all of this on a deeper level.
Time—"circling back on itself" in a literal sense— yet only allows those caught in its current to move forward in one direction.
Sometimes I wish kids didn't grow up so fast.
No, this APPLe is not worried ... *burp* ...
Yes, adolescence is a time of trouble for both adults and older apples. It's something we all go through.

Ferns, mosses ... animals, all kinds of animals ... D**n these classification tags, d**n these archiving processes!
Oh—I didn't notice you there, friend. Just rambling to myself.
Yes, I'm complaining, about paperwork—just a minor annoyance for any regular data collector ... These repetitive, tedious—
D**n bureaucracy ... Ah, it seems you've also dealt with the complexities of the establishment.
I knew it, we are on the same wavelength and have much to talk about, my dear friend.
Climbing trees had never been a challenge for me, so at Zeno, I struggled to find someone willing to join me in the canopy.
Have you ever climbed up a tree, Vertin?
I knew it! We could have a <nobr>tree-climbing</nobr> contest, right up the tallest tree in the wilderness!
Oh no, not having to compete is okay too.
Gently climb to the highest point of the tree and find a comfortable spot to rest, it's the perfect place for a peaceful nap.
Let me show you everything there is to know, starting with how to recognize different types of trees!
I know which tree has the best view of the wilderness, and I know which branches are the strongest!
As soon as the coin falls, of course, it's the smallest and simplest gamble, but it can still get the blood flowing.
It's in my palm, Jefe. Care to take a guess?
Absolutely correct! You've got some good luck there.
Now, would you be interested in something more exciting? Something that could make waves across the world?
Like ... doubling the viewership for Witch for a Day?
In a bet, someone always wins and someone always loses. If you want to keep practicing, I'll always be here to keep you company.

There is no need to worry, with me as your partner, we are going to amaze the house and the audience and leave them in disbelief.
Scatter some flower seeds, gift a piece of blue glass, or transcribe a classic family recipe.

Leaving a mark on the world—with pie. What a joyous thing.
If you're curious, make sure to come and give it a try.
Sir Vertin, I've discovered some fantastic discs. They're incredibly exciting and would be perfect for a movie night tonight.
If you provide the venue, I can provide the discs at ten Sharpodonties each. We'll make a fortune and have a great time together.
What do you say? Will you think about it?
Sir Vertin, I know you have a love for horror films. If you're interested, I can lend you my private collection.
As a thank you for your support, I'll even let you borrow my favorite Char Siu Bun series. Be sure to tell me what you think afterwards!
Because let's face it, even the most thrilling and <nobr>spine-chilling</nobr> movies are better enjoyed with company, don't you agree?
Ahem! I was just thinking of you—
According to my observations, even as Sonetto's superior, your arcane skills are still as poor as ever.
Therefore, I believe you need training, and the great monitor assistant, Matilda, is willing to coach you personally!
That's right! How about that? You've found yourself a great teacher!
Considering your level of expertise in the arcane arts and the challenging nature of the fieldwork ahead ...
No, I'm not worried about your safety. The Great Matilda simply cannot stand your subpar performance ranking!
Education has been compared to molding delicate porcelain. I partially agree with this comparison, as it requires patience, attention to detail, and careful observation.

Just as you lead people in your role as Timekeeper, you possess the qualities necessary to excel as a teacher, Ms. Vertin.
I'm not very familiar with this.

These souls are no longer bound to their bodies. They're a nuisance to deal with.
Hey, over there! Leave the doctor alone!
I bought this bullet with my savings! Who took it out of my body? It was you ... YOU!
Enough of your ugly fuss. What family are you from, Miss? How much property do you own?
Ugh, go away! It's not working. You'll have to try harder, Mr. Heinrich!
She took half my body! No! Father will scold me!
A nobody! A quack with the stink of a monkey! How dare you ... lay those filthy fingers upon me.
Heinrich, I'll take care of Isolde. Take this!
Erm, catching a ghost with my hands? Ugh, it's so soft and sticky?!
Move! Seal off that exit! Don't let them get away!
Got to sneak away ... Don't worry, Ms. Foundation. I won't leave you behind. I'll help you as you helped me.
Illich? I thought you were out selling wares on the street.
Is that ... the Magic Mustache? You clever boy! Quick, name your price.
You sure you can afford that, Kakania?
Triple the price? Just about what I can accept. You know my limits, old friend. Put it on, Ms. Foundation!
Don't take it off! You'll be exposed!
It smells, but bear with it. Now keep quiet and follow me. I'll get you to safety.
Lead us if you want your pay, Illich!
Deep breaths, miss. Look at the mirror.
This is a private session. Your secrets are safe with me. Now, what do you see?
I'm dizzy ... spinning ... So this is Ms. Kakania's arcane skill, a maze of mirrors.
The orphanage, the Flannan Isles ... These look like my memories, but different.
You can look at them directly, miss. They'll reveal your deepest secrets and desires.
Phew! They're only illusions, Marcus. Just break her arcane skill and get out.
I'll do the only thing I can do, "read"!
I see her. She's behind these illusions, but which one is real?
You found me? Did you see through the illusions, or was it pure luck?
Focus. She can move through mirrors. Got to keep track of her.
This can't be luck. No, I need to be sure. I'd be disappointed were it a fluke.
Everything is a book. Everything can be read.
I found it—the page of truth.
It's true. You saw through the illusions as you saw through the pistol. Alright. Enough of my tricks.
What a pleasant surprise! How does your skill work? Let me see!
Hello? Hello! Are you talking to me?
These ghosts are confusing her. I have to calm her before she hurts herself.
I'll take care of you, Ms. Dittarsdorf. Shh ... Tell me, who is here?
I'll behave, Ms. Kakania. Look at me, please ...
Who are you? Why are you in my bed?
Why do you call my father "Father," my mother "Mother," and my brother "Brother"? Hello?
I saw you beg and tremble ... Father took you away, and the servant brought you back ...
I'm sorry. I sympathize. But please give me my life back. It's not as nice as you think!
They're only memories, Isolde. What happened next?
No ... You died ... and then ... I was here?
But the story was not over. It continued with our bloodline!
The second child ... hogged all the attention.
"A genius, but a mentally unstable one! I hope the bloodline doesn't end up killing her."
She understood, and sat down. She got scared, and began to cry.
This is not a stage. It is all real!
Amid the shaking and convulsions, the second child remembered ... that she was really the third child.
A seizure. A memory related to the electroshock therapy?
At least my treatment's working. She's exploring her repressed memories.
No, no ... I don't want to hear ...
Shush. Hear that? Someone's crying fire.
Shh. What color should be used for a burning cage?
Did you hear something crack, fall, and split apart?
The fire is yelling. Something's burning in the fire ...
It's okay. I'm here. You'll be alright ...
I'm fine. They have escaped the tunnel.
Stop the chase. Let's not cause any more disturbances.
The Vienna branch ... of the Foundation?
Watch the mirrors, Ms. Marcus. I'll guide Isolde to the memory.
If only this would undo my mistakes ...
You can do this, Ms. Kakania.
I can't see you. Where did you go? Don't leave me, doctor.
Tell me what you think of ...
My eyes! Where are my eyes, sister? Where ... am I?
The acting started long before that, sister.
She's talking to her sister, who died young. Where are you now, Isolde?
Nowhere special. An ordinary party. A seance.
Admirers. Flatterers. Always there, at every gathering.
That naive little Tosca. She trusted their honeyed words.
Mmm ... Curtains in a breeze ... The sun's bathing glow ...
What's wrong with your voice? Where are you now?
A rehearsal ... the golden ball. Don't get mad at me. <nobr>I-I</nobr> know an actress should be perfect ...
Every Tosca should depict the finest dream.
They see her as a bird, praising its songs and splendor.
But does it ... does she enjoy this?
Cavaradossi opened the gilded cage, and it flew!
"Non feci mai male ad anima viva ..."
Recognize this part? I thought you would.
From a point, the brush drew a circle.
The portrait started with this silly circle. Then he drew eyes, and a mouth.

Art. A fascinating disease. Desire, repression, and madness ... are all vented through art.
It's The Salvation! We're getting closer.
No, no! He's drawing it wrong.
Please look at me, doctor! Help me? Please help me!

Welcome, welcome! You are currently reading the UTTU Spotlight Edition, a brand new feature, and I have been invited to introduce it to you all.

The content published in the Spotlight Edition comes from loyal readers like you. Legends, customs, and news of arcanum from all over are welcomed—whatever you happen to know, we value your submissions.

In every region, there are spots that have a certain allure, surrounded by stories and whispers that spread throughout the land. These are also usually the places where authorized UTTU outlets can be found.

The points of interest could be at a roadside newsstand, a hole in a wall, or even right next to a mailbox. As everyone knows, spiders have a knack for finding their way into all sorts of nooks and crannies.
If you have any interesting facts or information about this region, we'd love to hear them.

When we add up all the Exposure Rounds in an area, we will get the total amount of time that we have spent in that area.

Where, where? Is it here, or there?
In the keyhole, in the door crack, or under the covers?
The new, flowing, golden me,
The scorching, dazzling, tiny me,
In your heart, in your mind, in your bones.
Blow it out, blow him out, blow her out!
The me to be found everywhere—where am I?

Page after page. One book, then another.
Reading again and again, pondering, seeking.
From the lighthouse, toward reality.
The other side of the ending, no longer abandoned.

The beasts in the woods, or the heads under flying arrows;
The hero's song, or the souls under authority,
A thousand and three hundred years ago, or yesterday.
Round and round, three times.
<nobr>Click-clack</nobr>, <nobr>click-clack</nobr>, be it beak or tail feather.
Content doesn't matter, form is meaningless.
For the sake of humor, it's always a good time.

Rise, fall.
Tightly meshed, shining brightly.
Right now, this moment.
No need to calculate the point of landing, no need to seek balance.
Just a moment of laughter.

However, you can still live like nobility here, thanks to the neat and beautiful façade of the apartment buildings and the communal halls with their long spiral staircases. No one openly says a bad word, as the days visibly stride forward and steps quicken, kicking up a golden breeze. Almost every moment brings new tidings, new footsteps rushing to Vienna, countless new creations, useful or not so useful, all pouring into this surging stream.

    News of airship trials has plagued the papers, and porcelain and glass paintings have become essential table decorations. In years past, the Viennese created tubed toothpaste, invented the pencil, learned how to utilize cocoa beans ... Life is getting better, art shines brighter, as if making up for what was never enjoyed before. Now, Vienna won't miss any single glint on the shining crest of the age.

    People have grown accustomed to this pace. They chase novelty but always look at the city with nostalgic, expectant, trusting eyes, never believing the worst could happen here. The most astonishing news in the papers only sparks ten minutes of discussion. Even the death of the Archduke merely prompts a confused, almost embarrassed smile from the gathered crowd. It is a sudden change, and thus, they resist it.

    No matter, his successor shall shoulder the responsibility! So ... let's keep dancing.

It could be a window, a ring, an umbrella, or a noose.

    We prefer the analogy of a ring; it suits the mood better. When they first proposed building this road, there were so many voices of dissent! And now? If one takes the time to examine the jewels set into the ring's edge, our opera house, the museums of natural history, the art galleries, the gardens, and the schools—all the things that push this city forward—are meticulously adorned along the ring's side.

    Whoever it may be, wherever they come from, if they wish to understand Vienna, the best way is to lead them around this road. Even if they seek something "different," it's just a matter of stepping out one more circle—Vienna's districts have their own meticulous divisions: the nobility occupies the inner city, merchants favor the areas near the ring road, and further out, the simple, hardworking folk.

    These layered circles also have their moments of convergence. The Viennese seize any opportunity to turn their lives into a celebration. Splendor, dignity, and grandeur are unquestionable truths. Those gazing up at the parade floats have never felt so close to that select few standing atop.

    You see, anyone can stand on the stage.

"Vienna" is undoubtedly the most treasured word of the times. Those young people who shouted throughout the long struggle, eager to tear off the old labels left upon them by the elder generations, are just as keen to possess this golden beacon.

    Theophil doesn't flaunt these titles—his companions do it for him, tirelessly straightening his crown at every meeting. Rumor has it Hermann corresponded with him, the "Science Club" threw invitations his way, the Neue Freie Presse published his critiques, and a carriage belonging to Theophil once stopped at 9 Eschenbach Street. No one knows better how to play with gold, and the rumors that spread in tandem point to the <nobr>ever-changing</nobr> companions by his side. In any case, long before he reached the legal age of adulthood, he had a reputation he could toss around at will.

    But he never wrote a play for his equally popular sister, nor painted her a lavishly decorated portrait. Only a small sketch lies in a corner of a drawer. It's the only one that depicts both Isolde and their mother. Theophil's talent was already evident then; he captured their unique expressions well.

What makes this little shop so popular? Its fame even briefly surpassed that of Café Griensteidl, with its tiny storefront that fits only a handful of tables, its ordinary fried meat cutlets, and the most common, everyday coffee, it has created a small miracle.

    Running a café in Vienna is no easy task. The news racks must be filled daily with the latest papers, pressed flat with an iron. If one has connections and an eye for the popular, able to pick out newspapers that are in vogue, and displays a few publications that circulate secretly in closed circles, their wallet will surely swell. If one can advertise novel coffee recipes, recipes for secret family pastries, or perhaps encounter a rare guest—then a real opportunity has truly knocked!

    After all, the road where this shop is located is the inevitable route Kakania must take to return to her clinic. As long as she didn't intend to avoid someone by taking a detour but rather passed by as usual, with her friends for a visit. The swaying wooden sign of the café reminds her to pick up her letters and parcels. Thus, the two girls sit down at the table, and Isolde politely lifts the cup of coffee her companion has praised so highly.

    Many claim to have been there and speak of it as a conversation piece in other cafés, and so the news spread. The ordinary whipped <nobr>cream-topped</nobr> black coffee quickly earned a new nickname that consumed the streets of Vienna. The luck it allegedly carries is not important—it's the dramatic element of the story that is the key.

    No one can refuse a good play.

Artistic investment requires not only vision but also an abundance of time. Without neither of the two, one must compensate with thrice the amount of bills and coins. Fortunately, what patrons understand best and can most readily provide is money itself. A perfect match! Vienna's painters, musicians, sculptors, and actors can now stride forward on their paths with vigor. Photographers, fashion designers, jewelers, and playwrights won't be left behind either. As long as you can sell talent, ho, readers and audiences will never complain about the crowd.

    This is especially true of drama. Performances on stage are exemplary, allowing one to clearly see how that distant social stratum lives—how they converse with elegance, mind their manners, and mask any unfortunate accents in their speech. For this reason, actors are like perfect little statues, drawing attention wherever they go. Even when the play ends, they still parade around the grand stage of life.

    People chase after the name "Isolde" with such fervor because she is that flawless statue, the most transparent, the most dazzling, capable of embodying countless possibilities—those written into the script. She is the city's treasure! With this pride, even a child who has never seen her perform would not speak a word against her.

    After all, who among us has not spent a great length of time with "Isolde," witnessing her grow from a child into a fine actress? How many know the name of her household pet, or the friends of her childhood? These tales are almost indistinguishable from folklore.

Ugh, I still have the scars from shoveling snow on my legs, and we just fixed the windows at home. Who wants to leave just like that?
But what Comrade Evgeni said was reasonable, and he is always truthful ...
You're afraid he'll hear you! We may be close to the meeting room, but—
I'm not afraid, or I wouldn't have made the decision to come here. We weren't afraid in the pioneer days either. What Comrade Vila says is exactly what everyone said back then.

The town has been built, and we have been living here for a while now. Our days are not as hectic as they used to be, but it is invigorating to see the resurgence of the pioneer spirit after such a long time!
Hey, alright! That's the attitude we need! If we walk a little faster, we can still make it back to work on time!
If you're here to see Comrade Evgeni, we can wait a little. Or is there something else important you'd like to discuss?
We talked, and Ms. Windsong was there.
Comrade Evgeni is doing what's best for everyone, we all know that. But I'll tell you, I personally don't want to leave this place. Even if he ...
No, the lady turned down my proposal. And Comrade Evgeni didn't seem too invested in it either.
Isn't Zeno's help good news for all of you?
I can't comprehend the reasoning behind rejecting an abundance of food, a suitable climate, and comfortable housing.
It's not easy to leave something you've built with your own hands, comrade. I doubt you've ever experienced living in a home you built yourself, let alone living in this way!
Chances are you have never even touched freshly mined ore in your life!
That's true, gentlemen. But why do you insist on doing everything yourself?
It seems that our conversation has come to an end. I will stay here until Evgeni arrives and gives an answer, which should be soon.
Identical long tables, matching chairs, and potatoes, potatoes, and more potatoes.

In the past, we had access to tin cans and even jam and flour. It was a challenge to transport supplies, but fortunately the weather was cold enough that nothing spoiled during the trip. Time was not an issue in those days, we had an abundance of it.
The little ones used to come and ask for Alenka. While we couldn't indulge their every whim, a treat now and then was fine. Being too strict does no one any good.
Had I known the true value of Alenka, I would have been more careful about giving them away. Maybe I could have kept a few. Oh well, too late to regret now.

At first, we gathered around a single table to portion out the canned food, meticulously sopping up every last drop of broth. But now, there are more tables, but a lot less variety in our meals. And it's not like we can go hunting for critters to supplement our meals.
Why can't people live off ore like they do?
I have an urge to give a detailed account of my past and present experiences because Rayashki is exceptional; it is the most remarkable town I've encountered, although my travels have been limited.
But I'm worried that it will one day disappear.

That's for sure. If Comrade Evgeni agrees to Zeno's proposal, this place will soon be a land of snow again. The factories, the machines, everything will be covered with snow, just as it was when we first arrived ...

I have to remember to write down all the details in case the kids ask me. I want to be able to tell them about everything that disappeared. Of course, it's not going to be written down in any textbooks ...
There are countless unsung heroes in Rayashki, a place filled with ordinary people just trying to make ends meet. That's the reality of our lives here.
Comrade Windsong and Comrade Raisa helped me take the children home; it took some time.
Comrade Evgeni once mentioned that he kept some things in the cabinet in the meeting room.
He said to take them out when the time was right.
Here. This is all of it.
Comrade Vila frequents this place, always looking great in her poneva dress.
I taught her how to sew, and other comrades would bring piles of torn coats and socks for us to mend. This is something I have always done.
No matter how catchy our slogans are, we still need clothes to wear and bread to eat, right? The rest is not within my realm of concern.
Thankfully, Comrade Vila has been diligently caring for the children. My main worry was that once the teachers were gone, there would be no one to check on them and ensure they were looked after.
Leaving children to run amok on the streets will not lead to their healthy development.
I'm very grateful that she's here.
This place has become a second home to me. Despite the challenges and endless tasks, I feel content knowing that our efforts benefit our fellow comrades.

This experience is priceless to me. Anyone who has ever sat at a long table, sharing butter and conversation with people from different countries and working together to form friendships would understand the value of this way of life.
It has a powerful effect, my friend. It reminds me of dark bread - rough, but filling.
Whether it is Comrade Vila or ... Comrade Evgeni, I trust in their abilities. This town will not simply disappear.
Rayashki will always be here, steadfast and unwavering.
I've always believed it! We can dig through the frozen layers and find ways to survive here. Even when the harsh northern winds gnash their teeth, we can overcome any challenge!
Zeno will have its own specific guidelines that I doubt I'll be able to adapt to, but just like this particular component, we are already refined and capable enough!
Yes, we can live on our own without relying on other leaders.

Let me be honest, I am not much of a fighter. The only tools I know how to use are a wrench and pliers. But when push comes to shove, I will make do with whatever I can get my hands on. We need weapons to defend ourselves, and we are not afraid to use them.

It is crucial for children to explore the world. I came here at a young age, on a whim with a friend. We had no experience in shaping workpieces or handling raw materials. Now, my skills are highly valued in this community.
We did not come to Rayashki to have fun. They've got it all wrong.
I stumbled across some components. Lately, it seems like everyone is looking for them in their spare time. These little things can definitely come in handy.

The little thing was hidden just behind the base of the statue. It seemed that our resilient bear had found a new home here. The old statue had to be moved to make way for it, but its base remained. I suspected it had left some of its components behind.
Comrade Evgeni ... he did not notice the changes in Rayashki, but change is inevitable and ongoing. He was still holding onto memories of when things were tough and rough.
In those days, this square didn't even exist. We painstakingly dug it out with shovels and carried each stone ourselves.
No one expected Rayashki to end up so beautiful. We were never ones for making plans or dreaming big; we simply rolled up our sleeves and got to work.
Now, Rayashki might change once more. What will it become? Everything is changing so fast. We have a pool and a school; it all seems to have been built in the blink of an eye.
As soon as a project is completed, the difficulties and sacrifices made along the way are quickly forgotten. The immense sense of accomplishment makes us believe that all the hard work was worth it.
I don't want to leave. I'm afraid I'll change faster than this town did. Those who come back later feel like strangers themselves.
It's incredible, isn't it? How things can change in what feels like an instant ...
To me, Rayashki seems almost like another name for Runium. Perhaps it is because I am the one responsible for sifting the ore.

While most people came here with grand ideals, I simply signed my name on the list without much thought. It wasn't long before I found myself stepping off the train and into this unfamiliar land. Fortunately, aside from the wild Critters roaming about and the stubborn terrain, life here has been relatively simple.
Regardless, it's all laborious work. And I understand that even Critters have to eat and survive. I forgive them.
But back to the here and now. The factory is finally complete, and we have surpassed our wildest expectations. These accomplishments are not gifts from some higher power, but of our own making!
These are true miracles, not bestowed by any divine entity but created by our own hard work and determination. Just take a look around!

There was a time when I felt nothing, just going through the motions of everyday life. But now I finally feel like I am making a difference. It may not be extraordinary, but it's more than most people achieve in their lives.
Yes, I couldn't have done this alone. It's a rare opportunity to find others willing to work alongside you, swinging hammers and building something meaningful together.
I hope to turn our experiences here into a legend, like the stories of Comrade Evgeni. With a little exaggeration, of course. Young people need these legends to inspire them.
So let's raise a glass to the new factory and all that we have accomplished here together!
Kiril, it's time to get back to work! Please remind Bogina to come down from the forklift and stop playing Sudoku. We have to deliver the wood for reinforcing the mine roof by tonight.
Oh, Knut! What brings you here? It's not yet time for the shift change.
I'm not here for the shift change. I'm actually just dropping off some parts and a toolbox we found. Take a look, it's fully stocked.
I couldn't help but notice Comrade Kiril standing off to the side, spinning in circles. It almost made me dizzy when I first arrived.
He's been acting like this since the lunch break started, while Bogina is engrossed in her usual game. I wonder what's going on with Kiril ...
Illia, you haven't had the chance to read Comrade Evgeni's letter, so you don't know.

Looking at the stains on my hands from the coal dust, I can't help but think of his letter again. I find myself pacing back and forth, imagining how my comrades will lay me to rest when my time comes. It would be a great honor, but also ...
I can't help but feel that Comrade Evgeni deserved a different fate than this.
He did not deserve to end his journey in this place.
Comrade Knut was the first to find the letter. Later we all took turns touching it, like passing around a flag, remember?
You shouldn't talk like that to Illia, and you shouldn't think like that about comrade Evgeni.
But you said the same thing earlier, Bogina.
Yes, I said that. But I also said—
"Comrade Evgeni ended his journey here, but we must go on."
With only one square left to fill in the Sudoku, it's clear that this is the only way to go.
"Keep moving forward, to a better tomorrow."
This is not the end of our journey, Comrade Kiril.
Right ... I may not be good with words, but I wholeheartedly agree with comrade Bogina.
This must have been Comrade Evgeni's true wish.

Did you get a chance to go to see the children? They've been going on about you for so long.
It's been a while since I've been back to this town. How are the little ones doing? With you watching over them, I'm sure they're doing fine. You've always been such a caring teacher.
But there is only so much that one person can do. It would be great to have another comrade to lend a hand.

Back in Moscow, my thoughts kept returning to Rayashki. Those who have chosen to stay here are incredibly determined and tenacious. They are genuinely sincere and kind, but they are very stubborn in their beliefs. Does that make any sense?
In Moscow, you don't have to worry about cold temperatures or lack of resources. If children need pencils, they can simply go to the nearest store and buy them.
That sounds like a dream come true! We're doing everything we can to make Rayashki just that.

It was really beautiful, but when I sat next to Vasya's bed, when he was fighting his asthma, with the poplar fuzz in the air ... And then children's gravestones and coffins, so tiny and fragile, almost like toys ... I could hardly believe they were real.
I clung to the hope that life would get better in Moscow. I believed that if I just endured and persevered a little longer, things would turn around.
But that was not the way it turned out.
It's alright, I brought it up myself. When I was in the house in Moscow, I couldn't stop crying. But eventually I realized that I had to pull myself together and do something.
Is it still possible for me to reunite with everyone? Looking back, I regret leaving in such a selfish manner.
The future is unknown and unpredictable. All we can do is take one step at a time on the path that lies ahead of us.
You will always have the ability to move forward on this path, with all of us.

One morning I was floating on the surface of the water, admiring the distant shore. The horizon line seemed impossibly far away, with a soft glow radiating from it.
At that moment, I decided to go and see for myself. And so I arrived at Rayashki, my footprints leaving marks in the snow as I watched it transform into what it is today.
... It's remarkable how our dreams are gradually becoming a reality.

Miners, covered in a layer of dust and wielding their picks, hurry over as others join them after washing off their bandages. In the square, some take shelter under the statue and read books, while children are led by loving hands through rows of coats and boots. A strong sense of camaraderie unites everyone in the square; they are all part of the same <nobr>tight-knit</nobr> community.

    The conversations begin and spread like a hurricane, sweeping from one end of the square to the other as everyone tries to engage with those around them. But then another voice joins in. The town's teacher has arrived, embodying the ideals we hold dear. She is like a character from a legend who has come to our town from a faraway place. Because of our strong will, even legends can become reality here. If the teacher had not said, "See you tomorrow!" this would have gone on all night.

    As a community, we each have a voice in shaping the future of our town. It's inspiring to see so many people come together to make a difference. There is a sense of pride that radiates from within, uniting us all towards a common goal.

    Oh, how powerful it is when we come together as one!

Take another good look at the square. It hasn't changed much—a polar bear stands in the center, outlined by a faint light, while children eagerly reach out to touch its paws. The snow dusts the bear's head, giving it a serene quality that contrasts with the lively setting. Flowers bloom amidst the white snow, covering most of the stones on the ground. The bear appears to be at peace against the mustard yellow background.

    This is an important place in Rayashki, as the town kitchen cannot accommodate such a large number of people. It is often used for public discussions and will continue to serve that purpose. Recently, it was decided to allow children to venture outside and explore the world beyond. The road leading there is bathed in sunlight, decorated with red ribbons that sway in the gentle breeze from the trees.

    People find familiar images here that evoke nostalgia and memories of past lives, yet those who come here rarely speak of their homeland. This is the true essence of Rayashki—everything they hoped to see in their homeland, but never did. It's like the distant horizon that Rusalka dreams of as she braves the icy waters, or the intricate illustrations created by traveling ley hunters, or even the homes of Foundation visitors who have long since disappeared. It's what previous generations promised the next: a glimpse of their idealized homeland.

   The more impossible an ideal seems, the stronger it becomes—unbreakable in its perceived perfection.

    Despite this, there is still so much to strive for and achieve in life.

To the town, she is a familiar figure. But to herself, everything is so drastically different.

She's used to walking in the snow. The poplar fluff floating through Moscow's streets reminds her of Rayashki; it's like snow, but it doesn't make her cheeks turn red or her hands and feet cold; it doesn't melt on the skin, nor can it hide anything. Canned goods, even sausages and fresh meat, are available in stores, and one doesn't have to count the days just to exchange for everyday items ... The first time she made soup in her new home, it felt surreal. Another vivid memory was when she got off the train, holding her child's hand in fear. Outside the small town, in Moscow, there were so many people, all seemingly full of hope. 

But she boarded the train back to Rayashki anyway.

Rayashki had changed, too. There were faces in the town she didn't recognize, and the statue in the center of the square had changed. The school was still the same, and the children played games in the small playground. The townspeople's greetings were a bit awkward; no one mentioned her hasty departure as if it was not important, as if anyone could leave at any time and also return whenever they wanted.

Snow fell on her hair and collar, turning her fingers and nose red—this was real snow.

Snowmen of various sizes were arranged in a circle on the playground, and the children lovingly linked their twig arms together so that the snow friends were holding hands. Each child focused on decorating their little creation, staying close together, and when one arm brushed another's shoulder, there was a cheerful laugh. The little girl on the far left lowered her head, her braids curled up like haystacks in the sun. She carefully placed sunflower petals on her snowman's head. Nearby, two boys were trying to make their snowman's chubby body wider and sturdier so it would last longer and Ms. Vila could greet them more often. The little boy's snowman was a bear. It was only through his explanation that the head and paws of the arctic fox could be seen on its back. Foxes don't usually have long ears like rabbits, but he gave it those in order to hear his mother's footsteps, Vila's footsteps, and his friends' footsteps. Finally, he carefully placed the mined ore on the fox's chest, just as he wore the beautiful stone his father had left him. "Okay, my frosty comrades! You can all stay here and do the circle dance with Ms. Vila. Remember, no running around or making a ruckus; just listen to her instructions ..."

Among the long tables sits a group of people.

The one in the middle maintains her usual politeness and friendly smile. If you weren't looking at how her hands are resting uncertainly on the table, you'd miss the emotion beyond the politeness. Yes, this young scholar is stunned that the theory she has been focusing on is back in the spotlight. After being relegated to the pile of old papers in most places outside, it has found a place in Rayashki.

As for the people around her, most are still wearing their work clothes, with coal dust clinging to their collars and pant legs. They are aware of this and keep their distance from the scholar until she reaches out to them. This group of makeshift teachers and students shake hands, determined to spend time understanding a fading discipline. Those most dedicated to the work are also the most serious pragmatists. The study of ley lines has played such an important role in the rebuilding of the town! When the scholar first entered the research institute, this is what she had hoped for. Is the study of ley lines omnipotent? No. But it may eventually bring about change.

Perhaps it will be the moment the coal mine was discovered, or perhaps it is this moment.

The exact number shows how distinct this accessory is. "This is an essential investment, especially when you're trying to convince others of the importance of your project.

A tool often used by humans in geophysical prospecting, yet imbued with unmistakable arcane modifications. The interviewee demonstrated its paramount importance in the study of ley lines—presenting it as a symbol of the arcanum's interdisciplinarity.

These delicate papers hold the remnants of a <nobr>once-thriving</nobr> academic field. We are lucky to catch a glimpse of their forgotten knowledge by the faint glow of an oil lamp in a small, dusty chamber.

This is undoubtedly a century of creation.

Countless pioneers plunge headlong into various domains: computer science, emerging industries, Dadaism, and many others. Eager to spread their inspiration far and wide, these innovators paint every corner of the globe with their ideas. Archaeologists are no exception. Watkins, curious about these orderly, indescribable lines, called them "ley lines." Though he had few followers and faced much skepticism, his theory began its journey, albeit a rocky one.

Through "cultural transmission," this fledgling theory was spread around the world. It appeared in the newsletters of exclusive societies, was discussed in archaeological and geographical publications, and eventually found its way into university classrooms, where it was given a more formal title: the study of ley lines.

More and more young scholars, eyeing this promising field, are eager to contribute.

An ambitious girl with silver hair filled out her application form. "Excellent, this is a brand new era, and it is mine."

Tromsø, dubbed the "Paris of the North," thrives on a constant influx of energy and wealth, courtesy of its endless cruisers and passenger ships filled with curious and excited guests. Tour guides and merchants meander through the lively crowds, making sure not to miss an <nobr>aurora-seeking</nobr> tourist for fear of losing valuable income—at least according to the silver figure.

In the midst of the crowd, a young visitor is singled out and greeted by a pair of eyes as bright and eager as the aurora.

"Hey, friend, do you really want to be packed like a sardine into a tour bus, only to be dumped on a barren snowy plain to watch the aurora with a bunch of bobbing heads?"

"Uh ... of course!" The answer sounds determined. "I've never seen the aurora before!" He looks back at the advancing crowd, his voice trembling, betraying his nervous excitement.

"Oh, that's even better!" The girl's tone becomes friendlier as she lowers her voice, "I know a place where you can see any kind of aurora you want, in any shape you want!"

"Really ...?" The girl's confidence visibly sways the visitor.

"Don't you want to take full advantage of the breathtaking scenery? No need to huddle with those poor sardines. A moment like this would be all yours and yours alone!" Seeing the visitor's increasingly conflicted expression, the girl adds a persuasive nudge.

"Hurry up, friend, maybe I can introduce you to some more interesting new things, like the study of ley lines. Don't worry, my fees are quite reasonable."

"All right, I guess that wouldn't be a bad idea."

"Deal!" The girl smiles, "Tell me, friend, what else would you like to see?"

As they walk to a corner less frequented by other tourists, colorful lines flow slowly across the unnoticed snowy ground.

The design is rudimentary, lacking the elegance of skilled craftsmanship. It was made by rough, calloused hands and is now held dearly in the delicate arms of a child.

"There are many, many friends there, of all shapes and colors, with glasses and hats, singing and sleeping in <nobr>pitch-dark</nobr> caves. We all come from there, and you're welcome to visit!"
Believe me, when it comes from a child with such sincerity, it's an invitation you can't refuse.

This is the land where people gather.

The howling, biting cold winds, the high piles of bare gravel, and the endless expanses of white almost completely define the landscape here.

Yet, there is more than just white; glowing ores tumble out under the concerted efforts of picks and hoes.

More and more people arrive on roaring trains and giant ships, and crate after crate of black earth covers the barren ground.

Then come the grass, the crops, the bleating animals.

Concrete dormitories, canteens, and thriving factories follow.

It is a land of inspiration; everyone thinks so.

The pace of life here never stops.

Some gaze into the distance, while others shout aloud.

"Comrades, we still lack the most important thing."

"Yes, we need a school."

"We need hope."

Mama says, "Let's build a snowman."
It wears my clothes,
It has buttons and eyes,
It has your flower,
Combed into its branches.
A clean stream flows,
Beneath a warm belly.

I greet the snowman, "Where has mama gone?"
You have a scarf, a smiling face,
You have black buttons.
Oh!
It turns out you are Mama.

A <nobr>hand-knitted</nobr> scarf with patterns deeply inspired by the traditional cultures of the Far East. Mothers often knit these warming garments before their children embark on distant journeys, and this scarf is no exception.

A simple collection of art supplies for children, including brushes, paints, and blank sheets of paper. But the interviewee goes beyond these traditional tools. She not only teaches children to paint, but also introduces them to literature, music, and mathematics.

"My yet unmet friends, open your eyes wide. The neighbors you fear are just as curious about you!" We mutually decided to publish this statement in order to gain a deeper understanding of the interviewee.

At first they were fairies by the lake, symbols of rain and fertility. Then came the roar of machinery tearing through the marshes, the factory walls overshadowing the willow branches, and the city expanding like the gaping maw of a giant beast, indiscriminately devouring everything in sight.

As the landscape changed, so did their identities, morphing into sea nymphs and forest spirits, even embodiments of evil. The Rusalki began attacking ships and luring sailors; while humans hunted them for fish oil. Conflict and hatred inevitably became the central theme between them, seemingly perpetuating for eternity.

In the midst of these dire circumstances, there are still glimmers of hope: the singing navigator at the helm of a research vessel, the occasional glint of scales from a rescuer in the water, and the tender gaze of eyes watching from a classroom blackboard.

A wider world gradually unveils itself to a pair of pale green eyes, and the astonished girl barely has time to hide her sharp teeth. The sideways glances and the undercurrents rising from below no longer draw her attention.

Indeed, she has glimpsed the great new world described in books of fiction.

"Look, I should go there. It's a different place. No Rusalki, no humans, just 'us' and a glimmer of hope."

Dear Comrade Simonov, Today we celebrate the 60th anniversary of Rayashki's founding, and I am compelled to share this joyous occasion with you, my mentor. By the time this letter reaches you, even more time will have passed, and I am confident that our land will have seen further development. Rayashki now boasts well-developed roads, and we are eagerly preparing for a new phase of urban construction. We are upgrading various neighborhoods, and by the time you visit, our palace of culture should be complete, with a piano, balalaikas, vargan jaw harps, and, of course, guslis. We've developed a vibrant community life with people forming interest groups organically. We organize hockey games, stage plays, and occasionally screen movies. Our comrades are brimming with enthusiasm, our future is ripe with hope, and we have an endless list of things we aspire to achieve. Yet, we recognize this is just the beginning. We look forward to celebrating our 70th, 80th anniversaries, and many 100th anniversaries. I can now fully appreciate the legacy left by my parents; I see Rayashki blossoming from barrenness, and I envision it flourishing in the decades and centuries to come, becoming a center of advanced industry and agriculture with a high standard of education and living. Does that make you a little envious? How are things on your end, Comrade Simonov? Any new and positive changes? When time permits, I would very much like to hear your updates. May our aspirations prevail! P. S. If there are any new books or teaching materials available, please send them our way. The children are eagerly awaiting them. Forever your student, Vila

It belongs to you, to me, and to every hardworking, resilient person.
The lineup of tomorrow's budding astronauts eagerly awaits. This is where the dream of flight begins.
The temperature never drops in this place. The sounds of children laughing and playing fill the air with warmth and energy.
Yes, our young architects are always bold and daring—they are constantly shaping the world of tomorrow.
Wait until the seagulls flock back to their homes, wait until the quiet arrival of spring.
One step, two steps, out into the world—this is where the journey of the black diamond begins.
"Greetings, Miss Snow, a salute to you!"
Work hard, comrades, for tomorrow is a fresh start for sure.
With steel, wisdom, and firm hands, we gather here.
With steel, wisdom, and firm hands, we build a warm home on the tundra.
With morning's arrival, the snow sweeping is finished, guaranteeing safe passage for everyone.
With morning's arrival, the snow sweeping is finished, and the group of people who came together to help disperse happily to their respective homes.
In the soft morning light, the tree stands tall and straight with its branches frosted over, painting a pretty silver picture.
Do not fear the wind and snow, our home stands strong as the praises flow.
This body of water is more expansive than I imagined.
As I explore its depths, familiar memories resurface.
The water is gentle and serene, reminiscent of the water in my recollections.
It's welcoming, with various rivers coming together here just like people do.
This is the biggest difference I notice between this place and others.
I won't let myself dwell on the past, but I will remember it.
The memories of the Rusalki and the blood in the water will always be with me, but I won't allow them to consume me.
They are a part of me, but I also have a place in the present and future that is my own.
Recently, I've had a lot of academic discussions here and met a lot of fascinating people.
Talking to Ms. Yenisei as a compatriot was quite engaging.
The patterns of rivers and lines are a natural connection that can be seen by any attentive observer.
And there is plenty to talk about when it comes to rough bread and warming drinks.
Miss Tennant and I had a great conversation.
Yes, we each have our own stories to share.
Hello, Vertin. You came just in time!
I'm setting up a game of <nobr>hide-and</nobr>-seek, and there are plenty of friends here to play. Interested?
That's great! Are you hiding or seeking?
I'm really good at hiding. I remember one time I even managed to scare my own mother. She hugged me tightly and warned me never to go to the abandoned mines again.
So if you can't find me, just call my name out loud and I'll come to you.
Oh, I understand. You have more important things to do, right?
Vila thinks I should spend more time playing, but I also want to make other people happy.
If you need help with anything, just let me know!
There's Miss Floaty, and Tower Lady's big dog and little dog ...
And there's my friend, the sun! In Rayashki, he's great at this—when he hides, it can take a hundred days to find him!
Wise men warn against intertwining reality with theatrics.
But I say that if a donkey can perform and Peaseblossom can sing, then there are probably as many coincidences offstage as there are onstage.
Well said, although it's a common saying, it's true.
One never knows when the roles of performer and spectator may switch.
But I believe that you are always prepared, no matter where you are.
You have the ability to empathize and understand what is truly in the donkey's heart. When you perform on stage, the audience will undoubtedly cheer for you.
Look at the tale of a warm summer evening, the tale of a theatrical girl, the story of a playwright ...
Even the raindrops seem to fall in tune with the scene.
It's almost as if you are orchestrating it all from behind the curtain, always composed and fearless like a true actor.
One day, you will have a spectacular final act, performed for a full audience.
A smile is free, yet its value surpasses gold.
While the king has yet to make his entrance, while he is still at rest.
The ruler of the fierce army, the honorable and sagacious king... may he find eternal peace, undisturbed by our songs.
The king is dead. Long live the king! Who knows if and when the king will return?
If he does return, be ready to hop on the carriage. A spot is always reserved for you.
See, your mask bears no distinction from mine. Behind it, I can tell you are smiling as well!
The jester's eyes are always wet with tears. Yet, the jester's grin never fades.
I will keep smiling for both of us ...
In the end, we are all too familiar with wearing masks, aren't we?
Speak of the devil! We were just talking about you!
Isn't that right, Andreas? Maleficent? Did you hear these good folks calling out for you?
Tell me, how many complaint letters did you get this week? Twenty? Fifty?
We'll call it a miracle, let's give it a round of applause! We can thank the almighty heavens and your wise leadership ... but honestly, I don't give a d**n.
But, to celebrate this great, unique occasion ...
—-Yes, I'll make sure these never show up again, "boss."
So how about some ice cream? I drizzled five different syrups on top for extra flavor.
Great! Tell me, what was the count?
Ha! That's right, you were flooded with letters all about me, but you handled them with grace and elegance.
But don't think it's over yet—there may be more to come next week.
As for my thoughts ... I wonder what a combination of pine nut syrup and blueberry syrup would taste like. Want to to try it?
My friends in Wonderland are incredibly curious about you.
They have heard stories of your adventures and can't wait for you to pay them a visit.
You brave the rain and step outside, like an adventure in a mirror.
There are countless stories within you, full of courage and wit. Who wouldn't be captivated by your tales?
Just like how every Alice has their own wonderland waiting for them.
There's Mr. Cheshire's beloved tea set, Mr. Rabbit's precious syrup recipe, and we must make you the most splendid chair.
Mr. Caterpillar would turn your adventures into unforgettable songs,
ensuring that Wonderland would never forget a single tune.
A party is waiting, yes, and you are the star!
The party welcomes everyone, happy and unhappy, because eventually, everyone will be happy! Pop—pop—, everyone likes streamers and candy!
It's just like what you're good at, even if you don't bring candy, you know how to throw the biggest party!
No party is complete without a star, so wear this paper crown ... even though it's not really paper and it's not really a crown. But it looks like you already have one on. Splendid!
Here, take this stick and hit the pinata. Pop, pop! The colorful figure will burst open and its contents—candy—will fall to the ground like its insides spilling out.
Since you're always the life of the party and never fail to impress, you deserve a celebration where all the treats are yours to enjoy!
You used to read me countless stories.
Tales of a world without dangerous wolves lurking in the shadows.
Once my mission is complete and all the big bad wolves are vanquished ...
Only then will day and night feel equally comfortable and reassuring.
The thought of traveling after this is finished, I wonder if it will live up to the idyllic depictions in fairy tales?
When you have the time, do you think you could teach me some new vocabulary?
Maybe one day I'll be able to read them myself.  Also, what kind of stories do you enjoy?
Do you remember the last tale I told you? About a farmer's wish and a rich man's wish?
And the one before that, when the princess fled to the forest by my waters?
I suddenly realized—we can write these stories down! I'll tell them, and you can write them.
We can call it "Fairy Tales," just like they do in the outside world, right?
Of course, I've listened to countless wishes throughout my existence.
You could fill a book with them all. Each one is a story of the elfin's collection.
And at the end, you can write about a girl with a hat who never made a wish to me, even though she was surrounded by those who did.
I didn't expect you to be interested in that kind of thing ...
Yes, they're all yours. It's the prize for not wishing.
As long as you don't go and trade them for coins.
Thank you for bringing me to this place ... May I have permission to plant some flowers here?
Yes, in the soil—not in a pot like the ones I saw on the ward, carefully tended by the nurses.

I used to gaze at the flowers on the windowsill, unable to touch them, but grateful for their company. But this time, after coming to this wilderness ... I want to try digging the soil and planting the seeds myself.
You've taught me so much, and I want to learn even more ... Would it be a bother for me to ask?
Your response is always full of encouragement and faith, and you bring me gifts like flowers, stories, and hope.
When my flowers finally blossom, I want you to be there to see them.
Ah ... okay! Could you hold me steady while I turn the soil?
I'm looking for flowers that are easy to grow and will bloom as long as the sun shines and the rain falls.
Shh! Get over here and join me!
What are your thoughts on today? The weather is lovely, just right for us to relax and see what secrets come our way ...
The key to being a good listener is to be quiet and attentive. As long as you know how to hide, there will always be some secrets waiting for you. Here, you can come hide behind my monitor!
Look, the height is just right, isn't it? Although I can't see your pretty little face from this angle!
You're right ... I have a knack for picking up information from just sound alone.
This is how we develop a deeper understanding of each other, gradually and steadily, knowing when to ask and when to feign ignorance. Wouldn't you say so?
If you have anything you want to share with me, I'm all ears and ready to listen!
As always, you're not one to pry into other people's secrets. I can't say I'm not a little disappointed ...
In that case, do you have any secrets of your own to share? Or would you like to hear my tales about motels and other silly things?
While I am good at keeping the secrets of others, my own stories were not always given to me so freely.
In your Wilderness, each day is a journey through multiple seasons.
It's even more wondrous than the tales of the legendary underwater dragon palace.
In a single day you can see the beauty of different seasons ... If you want to enjoy the blooming flowers, I'll be happy to serve you tea and snacks.
Speaking of thanks, it is me who can't thank you enough ...
I just hope that every day in the future will be ...
So, you like things that are constant, like the moon?
The moon changes phases, but it always hangs there in the sky ...
Knowing that you, the boss, and everyone else are all looking up at the same moon... makes me think that even if this beautiful dream were to end, it wouldn't be so terrifying.
The rules of the ball game are very simple—one hand throws the ball, the other hand catches it.
You only need two hands to play.
But with four hands, when two people get together, the game becomes even more fun.
That'd be great! Now we have six hands throwing and catching the ball.
It would be even more fun if Mom and Dad joined in and we all played together!
A ball game should have many players. The more, the merrier!
That way, no one has to play with only two hands.
No matter what happens, the three of us will never stop playing together, right?
Do you want to know how to truly win someone's love and affection?
A single tear is worth a handful of diamonds, you just have to know when to use it.

And when it comes to winning hearts, it's important know when to appear strong in one moment and vulnerable in the next. A successful disguise should be balanced with moments of authenticity and vulnerability.
When I lower my head and recount the hardships of my past, the ladies may find this vulnerability more attractive than my prowess with a gun.
But it's all just a clever facade, a beautiful illusion.
For all that we should reveal to others is that polished, perfect exterior of our <nobr>diamond-like</nobr> heart.
And we all have imperfections that we need to hide, don't we?
It's a simple give and take.
Using intricate deception to uncover the truth and skillfully exposing my own vulnerability to elicit pity. Seems like a fair exchange, doesn't it?
After all, if you were to reveal your true self in this situation, what would that get you anyway?
That's not how it's supposed to go. She's supposed to grab the gun, and then ...
—Oh, you saw it, didn't you? My story, my script.
The heroine will set off on a journey ... but should she undergo a change, or remain the same?
A good choice, I'll make sure to jot down your suggestion.
Letting go of the past opens up a whole new realm of possibilities for the story.
I believe it will make for a compelling tale.
I have to agree, it takes a lot of courage to make that decision.
No matter how things may change, <nobr>"Red-haired</nobr> Bette" will always be known as <nobr>"Red-haired</nobr> Bette."
Just like how you will always be known as "Expressionless Vertin."
The topics in school change as fast as fashion trends, such as shoes, shampoos, and miniskirts ...
I struggle to keep up with them all. I've never dared to try a miniskirt. Just think, "20 centimeters above the knee," no way ...
But you ... you don't need any of those things like miniskirts or styled hair. You still stand out without any effort ...
There's definitely a word for that ... it's right on the tip of my tongue ...
Yes—yes! You're like ... one of those celebrities.
But unlike them, you wouldn't ... ditch me or ask me to fetch you a drink ... You're different ... even if you don't keep up with the latest trends.
It seems ... we have something in common after all?
Oh no, please don't say that! Isn't, isn't that a bad word?
Um ... you mean you've been told that your whole life?
Gosh ... You must be incredibly strong and resilient to have endured all that!
My desire to capture the most authentic and meaningful image feels almost instinctive.
But it is also a sense of duty.
It compels me to get closer and closer to my subject, until I can capture its true essence.
As I capture the moment through my lens, "I" fade into the background, leaving only my subject in focus.
"I" am just an observer, but my photographs will preserve these moments forever.
Please look into the camera, Miss Vertin.
Softly, yes, just like that ... brush from the roots of my hair.
Remember this moment. You've earned the praise of Darley Arabian, for you have had the honor of grooming his mane.
That's right. This is a story you can pass on to future generations.
You have a deep understanding of respect, and Darley Arabian sees something special in your eyes.
I have no doubt that you will keep pushing until you reach the finish line, am I right?
As a sneak preview, the mighty king of wooden steeds has granted you permission to gallop with him across the lush fields.
Wow, you have no idea what you just did, do you?
Not everyone gets the privilege to touch Darley Arabian's majestic mane.
For this, I think you should take on the responsibility of grooming me every day. I hereby give you this honor!
The truth is a complex mixture of flavors, both enticing and pungent, like an onion.
But peeling back its layers is no easy task, even for me.
Some people would rather turn away from it, pretending it doesn't exist. But just like the pungent smell of an onion, you can't deny the existence of the truth in the world.
Oh, sorry if that sounded offensive—I didn't mean you specifically. You're the type of person who would willingly peel back the layers and confront the truth head on.
Having a keen sense of intuition and the courage to keep digging once you've latched on.
Just what you normally do, right?
I understand, I understand. Not everyone likes the taste of onions ... and believe me, I know how hard they are to stomach.
But ultimately, everyone should have the freedom to choose whether they want to eat onions or not.
Yep, I'm getting closer and closer ... just need to save up a little more ...
Oh, hello. I'm just counting my savings, for my ... career aspirations.
Have you ever saved up for something specific, for a particular goal?
Stones are what stars are made of.
When you hold on to a stone, you are holding on to a piece of a star that once shone brightly in the past, and may do so again in the future.
Yes, for that something. We both have a goal, just like a satellite has a specific destination it is meant to reach.
Though, for me, what I'm doing now is ... breaking free from that "orbit," if you know what I mean.
Looking at your expression—or lack of it—you have some recollection of this feeling, don't you?
You, my familiar classmate ... the <nobr>"tail-end"</nobr> of arcanum, my fellow.
—One of the few who brings me a sense of stability in this world of weirdos.
... Anyway, I'm glad you gave up on those insane plans.
Please continue to do so if you don't want me to have to perform an intervention on your frontal lobe in the future.
Believe me, I don't want to have a repeat of our time in the Artificial Somnambulism room.
Actually, I don't want anyone to end up there ...
Ahoy, helmsperson! Have you been diligently practicing your understanding of the captain's instructions?
I am planning the our voyage.
It's going to be amazing! Maybe we can find someone to sing or perform for us on the ship.
What about the girl with the bright orange hair? I've seen her write hymns before, although some of her spelling is a bit questionable.
Lagasa will surely hear of our heroic deeds. Speaking of which, do you have a specific audience you want to impress with our exploits?
This will be announced at the Jarl's meeting!
First, I will conquer all the waterways in this area.
And if I am successful, I promise to grant you the equivalent output of an entire river!
I've been wanting to do this for a long time—a horror movie marathon in "the Foundation's domain."
Since this wasteland belongs to you, and we both owe our allegiance to the Foundation... that means it falls under their jurisdiction as well.
I'll provide snacks, drinks, equipment—and of course, the DVDs. What do you say? Interested?
I recommend gory horror, though psychological horror is also good.
And if <nobr>An-an</nobr> decides to join and recommend her DVDs too ...
Remember to stay by my side, Vertin. Don't forget we are both "that child" from the same place.
Our origin; clean, beautiful white squares.
They're just begging to be embellished with a touch of defiance. Maybe some blood and guts or a <nobr>zombie-esque</nobr> dance routine.
So let's have a movie night in here, sipping Bloody Marys and munching popcorn in honor of the "bad kids"!
On the road, on the road! What a fantastic word, my dear friend.
People like us are always on the move, seeking new experiences. For art is limitless and <nobr>ever-changing</nobr>.
Can you imagine a world filled only with overused expressions, deceptive words, and unoriginal ideas?
No, my friend, battling against this reality should be an artist's destiny.
We are all in this fight together, armed with flowers, love, bubbles, and honesty.
Yes! But no, when we say it like that, it sounds clichéd.
I am destined to set out on a journey for the sake of art, peace and love, even if it means going alone. After all, the muse is known for her unpredictability.
And right now, we're on the same journey together, my friend.
I'm just stretching out, with Punji and Manka.
Are you interested in Romani dances, Vertin?
They are a fluid art form, with certain elements and rhythms passed down from generation to generation, as old as the road itself.
The dance embodies all aspects of life—love and hate, laughter and tears.
But they are not kept as a guarded secret. If you wish to learn, Vertin, simply take my hand or Punji's and join in!
Yes, we travel in our caravans, spreading songs and dances wherever we go.
Because laughter and music are always better than tears and sadness, aren't they?
And one day, I will go on my own journey. Maybe not in a caravan, but maybe ... in a suitcase?
Miss Vertin, I would love to paint some pictures here, just as I did in Rayashki.
This place is a symbol of equality and beauty, a result of the hard work of all who helped build it. Your contributions have been truly remarkable as well.
As for what to paint, do you have any suggestions for me?
I agree, we should paint this landscape to preserve its beauty.
Let me think about the best way to capture it ... the terrain in this place is constantly changing, it's full of life and energy.
It is incredible ... If only more people had access to this technology, it could do so much good.
Yes, the faces of the contributors are definitely worth remembering. I want to capture the likeness of each and every one of them in my paintings.

Oh, there's no need for you to dress up for your portrait. You look fantastic just as you are now; your determined and bright eyes make it clear that you are a brave and idealistic person at first glance.
If you ever have some time to spare, I would be honored to paint you proper.
I'm watching the lines closely; they seem to be constantly changing, especially inside your suitcase.
This is a dynamic and complicated terrain, and studying it is no easy task.
Imagine, every remote island has its own ley lines, sometimes visible, sometimes not, and sometimes crossing paths with others ...
As a scholar of ley lines, your land is a goldmine of discoveries!
My current hypothesis is that the lines are connected to their owner, which in this case is you.
To confirm this theory, I will have to do some more <nobr>in-depth</nobr> research on you ...
It could also be another one of those rejection letters. Oh well, who cares?
What scholar worth their salt would pass up an opportunity to learn, especially one right in front of them?
And even if those "mainstream" researchers at the Foundation continue to reject my paper...
There's still you, the reader, isn't there? Surely you're curious about what's going on in your own territory and would be interested in reading my findings.
Vertin, take a look at this—my collection book!
There are many things in this tiny suitcase that I've never seen before. I spend my time collecting them.
When I go back to Rayashki, I can tell everyone the stories from the collection book.
Yes, they look like red brown snow in the picture book. Miss Flame said that they come from the hearts of rainbow lizards, which is amazing!
The sports field there is open to everyone, just like in Rayashki, right?
When I grow up, can I represent our city in those competitions?
Mr. Bird said this is really, really old soil. It's fed a lot of crops and people.
I tried to figure out how long "really, really" is but ended up getting dizzy.
Do you think the sunflowers will like this kind of soil?
Do you want to hear more?
Want me to play with you?
I wonder what that feels like.

—Excerpt from Travel Notes: Travelling One Hundred Forgotten Cities

The evening before yesterday, I arrived at the port following an Irish merchant ship. "Pайяшки"—the first mate taught me this word—"Rayashki," a name that is being forgotten.

This morning, a child stumbled down a snowy slope and fell into my arms. I picked up the scattered sunflower, gave him some advice, and asked why he was in such a hurry.

"Thank you, but the concert of Mr. Crocodile and the mischievous <nobr>Big-Eared</nobr> Monkey is about to start, so I have to hurry."

"Oh? A concert! Where is it being held? May I accompany you?" To a symphony enthusiast, nothing is more enticing than that.

"Yes! ... Well, that is, if you're willing to join us as a comrade. Will you make a pledge in the name of the 'Red Forest'?" A flicker of concern crossed the child's angelic, ivory complexion.

"Alright then." I had no time to ponder the child's curious metaphor, so I decided to put him at ease. To my surprise, however, I neither experienced the grandeur of the First Symphony, nor was I immersed in the folk songs of the local ensemble.

A military linen tent, an old CRT television, and a <nobr>well-known</nobr> animated film; a bunch of boys and girls crowded together, staring intently at Mr. Crocodile's accordion.

"Hey, move over a bit, make room for this <nobr>red-bearded</nobr> guest!"

"Alright, Mr. Crocodile, you can play now!"

Red beard ... Red Forest? I couldn't help but laugh: a child's world is always so wonderful.

"Believe that brighter days are on the horizon ..."

"Just like the blue carriage, keep moving forward ..."

—There was neither the grandeur of classical beauty nor the charm of folk customs in that melody, but there was something else, something truly touching.

I couldn't resist joining in with the children's clapping. Hah, at least I didn't have to say goodbye to my beloved "Red Forest"!
Index Term: "The Study of Ley Lines"

First, the study of ley lines, compared to the general geological sciences, is a <nobr>high-level</nobr> test of spatial logic and imagination. You must abandon tradition and let your imagination run wild in the palace of ideas. 

Second, you will experience a feast of colors and be allowed to give new interpretations to any unmarked hues. Countless treasures await in these bizarre and colorful scenes.

Third, whether you have a new argument or an interesting discovery, please contact us at the Review Guide. We are always open to anyone interested in the field!
                                                                                                                             —Ley Line Mapping Review Guide

In geometry, points, lines, and surfaces form the basic shapes from which countless theorems are derived.

In architecture, basic shapes are formed out of imagination, giving rise to complex structures.

In ley lineology, theorems are deconstructed, complexity is extracted, and everything is reduced to its essence.
                                                                                                                             —Tristan Lessov

Lineology has never been a discipline that can be applied with a superficial understanding, nor can it become a systematic applied science.

Lineology cannot interfere with the operating rules of the world. Even if you exhaust yourself rearranging energy lines, they will eventually return to their original state.

In short, it is understandable why lineology has been abandoned by the times.

However, for those struggling with complex problems spanning various disciplines, it may provide a unique perspective.

—Falsehood over Truth, or Decline of Talent? A Discipline Difficult to Define
