April 16th

A small skull shaped like that of a sperm whale, containing astonishing beauty and oceanic wisdom. Rostral cartilage, conical fangs, a jaw arc of more than 90 degrees ...

My intuition tells me it does not belong to a creature of nature—otherwise, the laws of biology would be a joke!

April 18th

Through the lucky discovery of a walking stick, we were able to detect high levels of hydrogen sulfide compounds. The accompanying geologist explained that this substance is typically found in rock strata thousands of meters deep.

...

The results are numerous, so I won't list them all.

April 20th

This is the last day of the Greenland expedition team's stay. After saying goodbye to the enthusiastic workers who helped us, we went to the port and waited for the last steamship to arrive.

As night fell, we could vaguely see a man's silhouette in the dock area. We recognized him by his beer belly and bushy beard. During the day, he was one of the workers who often made crude jokes; at night, he recited poetry to the sound of the waves hitting the ship's bow.

Ever since a temporary library was set up in the mining area, everything has changed, he said. During meals, he and his coworkers talked about comedies, bedtime stories for his little daughter, and even Pushkin and his Ode to Liberty.

"The feeling of reading poetry, I can't describe it ... it's like you swing a pickaxe with all your might, only to hit a piece of black diamond and make your hands bleed. But you feel immeasurable joy—because it's precious!"

Perhaps, when they no longer feel like they are being judged for a particular "identity," their secret inner desires will emerge. In the impenetrable darkness, they are more romantic, more courageous, and more poetic ...
Mermaids: The Arcanists of the Depths

Primitive mermaids inhabit the deep sea and hunt like traditional sea creatures, with a thick layer of subcutaneous fat and dark skin. Their humanoid arms are strong and powerful, with webbed fingers and sharp nails. They use arcane skills in a powerful and almost savage manner to tear apart their prey. Due to early Arcanists hunting them and the gradual development of fishing industries, primitive mermaids have all but disappeared, with no clear evidence indicating they established a transmissible civilization.

Pureblood mermaids are arcanists with at least 50% mermaid blood purity. They have a human upper body and a <nobr>fish-tail</nobr> lower body, with gills on their necks and sharp teeth, and a dorsal fin along their spines. They are adept at hiding their fish features, transforming their tails into human legs, and using their voices and gestures to lure and enchant prey, evolving into the "mermaid" image in the legends that beguile humans.

Hybrid mermaids have less than 50% mermaid blood purity. Their appearance and skin texture are almost indistinguishable from humans, but they can have some fish characteristics, such as scales, gills, fins, and webbed fingers, depending on the individual. Hybrid mermaids can use arcane skills to create a fish tail in water, but this transformation only lasts about <nobr>10-14</nobr> hours. Over time, some scholars have begun to study the race of Rusalka, which has led to a gradual reduction in the demonization of hybrid Rusalki.

Arcanists with mermaid blood (between 50%-75%) are often labeled as "impure blood" by their race and abandoned, later mostly adopted by the St. Pavlov Foundation. Those with less than 50% mermaid blood show genetic traits such as swimming ability, cold resistance, and streamlined body shape.

About that forest you're familiar with. About that companion you know so well.
Half of this newspaper page has been soaked in murky oil paint. Fortunately, the other half of the text is still faintly legible.
/lo/ - So which poor sap's up for the spot next?
Pale green characters flicker incessantly, and in a second, dozens of messages appear on the fluorescent screen at the same time. It is clear to see that life must go on.
Now, we've learned some manners in Apeiron, haven't we? Namely, to abstain from beans, never parcel off a loaf, and stay away from the white roosters on the road.
It's been so long since we last talked about these things. How time does fly! This rusty brain of mine is struggling to keep up ...
We should have waited until dawn to light the candles. The sun would have mistaken the day for night and delayed its appearance in the morning. That way, we would have had more time to talk.

Indeed. You possess a far greater understanding of the laws of nature than your ancestors. It's only natural that you wouldn't relate candlelight to sunrise. But, for the people of earlier times, there was a commonly understood connection between the two.
Did the trees not bear fruit after the Horn of Plenty was filled at the harvest festival? Did the field not wave with grain?
Does the lighting of a match not illuminate the moon?
It's human nature to try to understand the world. Of course, at that time mistakes were made, and some phenomena were attributed to the wrong causes; some theories were developed from false facts.
It was a time of symbols, you see.
The flower represented blessings and harvest, the ouroboros the eternal cycle, the hawk wit and astuteness, and the soil safety and protection.
Aside from nature, the circle symbolized protection, the triangle stability, and the triple helix ascendance, change, and the unity of mind, body, and soul.
As time went on, things became associated with one another, and more and more symbols were created.
It's not a very methodological approach.
You can see the cause and effect with your own eyes, dear. It's clear when something is related and when it isn't. If the outcome isn't what we expect, these symbols must be incorrect.
But it's not their physical form that's wrong. Physical objects never lie. It's the meaning and concept given to them that are wrong, you see.
Objects are just objects. A match is just a match, not the illuminator of the moon. An animal is just an animal; the circle and triangle are only shapes ...
Be ever so careful, dear. The fiery thirst for knowledge is blazing bright within you; be careful not to put it out.
Once, many fire thieves sat here, sipping coffee, as they tried to decipher the best angle to hold up their reeds to jam the burning wheel of Helios and steal his flame.
The gods are selfish. They're stingy with their might.
Shouldn't the gods be more generous?#Some will receive it. First come, first served.
That's easy to say when the power's not yours to give. Knowing how to share is a rare virtue. Knowing how to share knowledge is a rarer virtue still.
"How can we transfer our wisdom into mortal minds?" The gods pondered.
Can inspiration be duplicated from one brain to another? It comes and goes like a gust of wind, so what can be done?
True. I'm sure the early customers of the bakery share the same philosophy.
The line must be respected, however hungry the latecomers may be.
There are many fire thieves in the field of science—many more than the bread buyers in the bakery. Take a look at these geeks in uniforms made of aerospace materials.
Among them are arcanists in love with science who spend most of their time studying diodes and machines, and humans who are passionate about the future, always finding new inspirations ...
Elements, lightning, atoms ... Perhaps you've forgotten their counterparts in arcanum, but you must be familiar with them as scientific discoveries.

These discoveries are the milestones of progress, sweetheart. The fire thieves firmly believed that they would be able to bring about many more technical revolutions: the fourth, the fifth, the 65535th ...
Sounds like a twist to the story is coming.
Not yet, darling. We've only finished the prologue. However, there is a "but" waiting down the road.
A sudden rain dampened people's enthusiasm for the future. The floppy disks and many clever minds perished in it.
Some of the fire thieves grieved the loss. They screamed and swore to retrieve what was lost.
What about the rest of them?
They returned to primitive chaos, like coelacanths crawling back into the ocean after thousands of years of evolution. Once again, they became the proteges of arcanum.
Perhaps they made the right choice by leaving that useless science behind. Who knows?
The story of the fire thieves has only gone this far, darling. At this point, no one knows what will happen to Prometheus or what's inside Pandora's box.
Here is a well known question you must have heard: "What goes on four legs in the morning, two in the afternoon, and three in the evening?" it's so well "known" that no one finds it novel anymore.
But please do me a favor and answer me yourself.
"A human being"#Let's talk about the questioner instead.
Correct! This is the same answer Oedipus gave to defeat Sphinx. Thus becoming a hero, but also starting him on his <nobr>ill-fated</nobr> destiny.
Raise a question, give an answer. This is the most fundamental ritual. Through this, we get nearer to God.
The Sphinx, an embodiment of mercy and nobility in Egypt, was seen as a mystery to the Greeks: a dangerous being that kept secrets, and delivered the punishments of the gods.
When the question is answered, the ritual is finished, and the answerer is granted the right to reach the treasure it guards.
Yes, a ritual. Whether it is by pouring out wine; slaughtering a calf; or circling round a fire with a baby in your arms... It is an agreement; a question that demands an answer.
Every desire has a price. Whether it is paid in wine, blood, or fire, but sometimes that sacrifice is taken from you without it ever being noticed.
And the treasure you seek might be the undoing of your own desires.
Let us take a look at another question: "Stranger, what's your name?" Cried Polyphemus.
"Nobody!" Odysseus answered, and it allowed him to flee the cyclops' cave, safe and sound.
A human being and nobody, two answers that could not be more alike, yet both were bound to fate by their answer.
Alright, dear, time to call it a day. As for you? You'll get the answers you seek, you've already paid the price.
Look at this mirror, dear. There's a sizable stain on it.
It's broken.#I don't see any stains.
Yes, it is. Maybe its owner meant to break it so that the stain would be thoroughly removed.
Now the stain is gone, and the owner has a collection of little mirrors. She must have accidentally left this one behind.
Look closer, dear. You can no longer see the part that has broken off, but you can see where it once was. Right there, a sizable stain.
The owner thought the stain would be removed if she smashed the mirror. Now she has a collection of little mirrors, and the stain has gone into hiding.
A lady with great ambitions and an unconscious charm. A lady who wishes to make the rest of the world accept who she is, and has suggested that many others join her way of thinking.
Her brother, on the contrary, hopes to be taken in. In his attempt to act like everyone else, he lost an arm in a duel.
If you ask me, dear, I'd say they're very alike. Equally lonely.
The brother and sister are a mirror image of each other. She's often repulsed by the sight of him, unable to reconcile herself with all that he reminds her of.

Now, the brother has found his missing arm, along with his <nobr>long-lost</nobr> dignity. The surgery that the sister had been hoping would be done on this world has finally started. But all of a sudden, she's terrified of the incisions.
As I said, despite their differences in approach, the brother and sister are mirror images of one another.
But now the mirror is broken. I hope she can make it through the seven years of bad luck. Poor thing. There's no way around it.
A bullet is among us, right under this roof. It serves no army, no country, only peace.
The heavy rain at the end of the century dissolved and washed away many of its comrades, but it was lucky enough to survive. Its pointy end still shines silver, ready to drill a hole into its enemy.
Sadly, its bulky colleague stole its thunder in this war. One push of the button, one big explosion. There was no need for the rest of the ammunition.
Good, we saved a lot of bullets.#Good for them. They don't have to work for a while.
It seems someone has become more <nobr>budget-conscious</nobr> after working with the mathematicians.
Saving ten bullets is better than saving one. Saving a hundred bullets is better than saving ten. It's simple math.
Certainly, who doesn't want a life without the need to work? Few would hesitate to choose a life of freedom over the achievement and satisfaction of a job.
Given the short lifespan of a bullet, why would it choose anything else?
But its boss, the general, has more to think about. What are they going to do next time? Will this bullet be put to use when the rain comes again?
A big shot, dear. A wise man of the most insightful kind. You should talk to him if you have the chance.

But he's been in a gloomy mood lately. Be careful not to mention anything related to the conservative battle tactics used in 1999, the missile that would have been launched, and especially anything about the bullets lost in that battle.
He has paid a great price for the future, but you see, the future is sneaky.
Every time you think you can grasp it, it takes a step away from you, nullifying every effort you've made to get near it. Even a bullet isn't fast enough to catch up.
Then we must keep pursuing.#Perhaps bullets won't be needed in the future?
Pursuing the future. How romantic, dear. As long as we continue to close the gap between us and the future, it will eventually be reduced to zero.

But know that, as time goes by, we are only moving slower and slower in the race. Technology is regressing, and we have switched from AKs to <nobr>Mosin-Nagants</nobr>. The bullets won't be as fast as they used to be. The future is drifting away from us, and the past is catching up.
Shhhh ... Don't say such things out loud. Especially not near the general, sweetheart.
The bullets have paid a great price in order to find their way back to the future. If they hear you say they won't be needed anymore, you'll end up with quite the ammunition bill.
Alright, let's leave this bullet to itself. Solitude may help alleviate its anxiety about the future.
My dear child, look at you, you're exhausted. I couldn't be of help then, but it's ok, the "party" is over now. At least let me brush your hair, darling.
Or your hair will get all knotted, and it will hurt you when you try to untangle them.
Indeed. It happened more than once.
I'm not surprised. An old friend of ours, "knot." Often we learn our knots before we even know how to read and write.
A knot could be an obstacle that breaks the consistency of a flow, and also a reminder of forgotten things.
You can use just about anything on hand to make a knot: leaves of grass, the fur of an animal, even fallen hair ... But the sturdiest knots are tied with rope.
Knots are to be found in many stories. Signify promises, counting and measuring, an instrument of salvation and one of execution.
What else can these knots really do?
Oh, I could go on all day! The influence and power of knots can't be overstated...

It is said that it was in the cutting of the Gordian Knot that Alexander became "the Great"; just touching the <nobr>meters-long</nobr> rope provides blessings to the faithful in Belem; and tiny knots on strings can carry the history of an entire people.

The ancient Inca called it "Quipu." The intricate variations of hundreds of fabrics, colors, and lengths of strings were used to record their stories through the ages. And to think, Shakespeare only had 26 letters to create his masterpieces.
Isn't there something a bit more practical?

Just look around you: don't sailors use knots to mark depths and mend sails; or coachmen tying knots to rein their horses; and any respectable lady or gentleman knows the knots they must tie about their necks to stay in fashion.
Or consider the <nobr>knot-like</nobr> helix structure of DNA, and the changes in states of matter ... Invisible to the naked eye, these knots carry some hint at a universal law.
That there might be a string, like the Quipu, an endless rope that records in its knots everything in the world. One that can't be seen, yet there it is, everywhere, all at once.
Maybe you can tie this knot yourself. Use your hair, then form a loop, pass the end through it, and tighten it up. There you go.
I hope you keep this knot as a record of the words we shared here.

All investigators are to abandon their current tasks upon receiving this notice and return to headquarters to seek shelter. "Storm" Shelter Precautions: • We will prioritize space for the preservation of personal items that comply with regulations, but note that space at headquarters is limited—please do not bring unregistered personnel or personal items over 20 kilograms back to headquarters. Note that family members of investigators who are not members of the Foundation are also considered unaffiliated personnel. • In special circumstances, such as having to bring unregistered personnel or extra items back to headquarters to protect the Foundation's core principles, please first contact the headquarters through the nearest device with sound functionality and a dial (must have a round movable part and sound, such as a car radio), and we will respond as soon as possible. For the Foundation's core principles, please refer to the Foundation Investigator's Code of Conduct, Chapters 1 through 3. • Since the Storm Syndrome is currently irreversible, for the safety of the Foundation, returning personnel must undergo an inspection. High levels of infection will restrict your entry, and we will place you in a special isolation area until the "Storm" ends. • If you are in a critical situation and require assistance, the various rescue methods outlined in the Field Mission Evacuation Instructions will remain in effect. A fate has been forged for this purpose,
A maxim, a preconception,
A deliberate contemplation, a step taken.
Believed to be a choice.

The woodland is older than all within it.
Through passion, or reason,
Travelers grope and stumble through the branches,
Or silently tread the narrow path,
Or choose to turn away,
Stepping into the subtle unknown.

Read, the voice urges.
If now, without pursuit, close to truth,
Yet let go.

Required Materials: A square sheet of metal Other shapes and materials can also be used, observing the differences they produce is equally entertaining. Sand Flour, salt, or sugar can also be used, but be careful, they're not easy to clean once they get into those body crevices. An element of sound Yes, that's me, glad to help. You can also find any friend who knows how to sing and make vibrations, or say, dance. Working Principles: It is known that sound is produced by vibration and propagates in the form of waves, and different sounds have different frequencies of vibration, so certain sounds can produce fixed waves under certain conditions, thereby representing certain patterns. Operating Steps: First, place the square metal sheet, hereinafter referred to as the plate, on a stable and well-fixed smooth solid surface. This is to prevent phenomena such as slipping, an important step. Second, the sound element is made to contact the plate and emit sound at a specific frequency. The Scientific Computing Center has compiled the wavebands corresponding to the 26 letter shapes—you can ask Mr. Ulrich for a copy, he is a very generous gentleman. Third, observe the pattern and draw conclusions. Wasn't that simple? You can do it alone at home—try it and see what pattern your favorite music program turns into.

    Ms. Weyerhaeuser showed a high degree of cooperation in accepting her punishment. The <nobr>by-products</nobr> were processed into organic fertilizer, and the remaining fruits were distributed by the canteen at lunchtime to offset Ms. Weyerhaeuser's service activity time—the acorn bread and berry pies received quite good reviews.

    In summary, given Ms. Weyerhaeuser's excellent performance and good attitude in admitting her mistakes during this period, we believe she has fulfilled her compensatory obligations to our satisfaction, and it is recommended that surveillance and movement restrictions are lifted from Ms. Weyerhaeuser in advance. That is all.

I don't know if I'm crazy, maybe today is the end of the world, but I have to write this down—this is my duty as a journalist!

    The whole of Vienna has become an oil painting splashed with turpentine, and I'm not using that as a metaphor—literally!

    Everything is dripping with paint, and I'm no exception! Fortunately, my right hand is fine for now and I can still write.

    I thought three men fighting to the death over the pronunciation of a word would be enough to make the front page of the newspapers, but I was wrong—▊▊▊, a great war is unfolding! The boy also said, "Please let me shine your shoes, miss, your leather shoes are so beautiful." I looked at my father helplessly and angrily, he looked at the boy with a dismissive, impatient look, as if he had never spoken to him, never once kindly ruffled his fuzzy head. He was so content to enjoy his service as a person of high rank. As he said, after leaving the old and noisy house, we should say goodbye to everything from the past—the "Vingler" surname has been renewed, and we must cut off all ties with our past as peddlers.

But now all memories have turned into a bowed head in front of me, and the distance between us can no longer be measured with a ruler.

But how could a child dare to defy the authority of her father? I had to endure, and after he finished his work, I took the coin handed out by my father, secretly folded with it my own money, and gave it all to the boy.

A relatively new bronze key, indistinguishable from most ordinary keys, worn around the neck of the interviewee to become an unignorable visual focus on her person. We tried to explore the significance of the key with the interviewee, who directly demonstrated to our editor how she uses it to open and close her maintenance compartment with a swift series of motions.

A practical coat, styled like a military uniform. Though having accompanied the interviewee for many years, it still looks as good as new, with only slight wear at the cuffs and the bottom of the zipper. For the interviewee, this coat is not prized for its warmth, but more for its use as a sort of huge <nobr>"carry-on</nobr> bag," carrying multiple batteries within it for emergencies.

Every Laplace employee is notified to collect their unique ID badge after joining up, and even those in the highest position of authority are no exception. Though some are unwilling to wear their ID badge after receiving it, the interviewee clearly isn't one of them.

In 1776, the invention of the steam engine by a shipwright's son born in Renfrewshire, Scotland, which used steam as the lifeblood of mechanical labor, changed the world forever.

In 1826, a locomotive loaded with a <nobr>gas-vacuum</nobr> engine climbed Shooter's Hill, and at the same time, a piston with <nobr>self-awareness</nobr> was born.

After that, technology began an irreversible march forward, and her body bore the sum of it all—from <nobr>steam-driven</nobr> structures to internal combustion engines, then to batteries and induction motors. The glory of technology is immortal, and her body always remained young.

—Until the last day of 1999.

As soon as the first "Storm" fell, the Laplace Scientific Computing Center lost its leader. The subsequent leaders, whether in prestige or ability, were never competent enough to solve the series of problems that followed, and their subordinates faced the chaos and confusion brought about by the rapid change of power.

Someone had to put an end to it all, and to bring Laplace back on track.

The <nobr>ever-indifferent</nobr> awakened made such an observation. It took less than three milliseconds:

"The sum of all our past scientific progress does not equal one <nobr>ten-thousandth</nobr> of our future scientific progress," she said in her letter of <nobr>self-nomination.</nobr>

Laplace Scientific Computing Center

A gift from doting parents—a slightly heavy affection for most people to bear. Her most familiar friend. Made of leather and hard cotton cloth and joined with iron rivets, it is generally used for internal and external surgery or psychiatric treatment. Fortunately, the lining is soft. No one has the desire to see a clumsy child scratch themselves, or break a limb, or crack their head open. Therefore, it is indispensable.

A gift from a believer, Lorelei once used it to stop a small melee and saved him from death. In the era of war, a uniformly dyed and <nobr>brightly-colored</nobr> ribbon is considered of value. However, her mother didn't care about its value—she used it to decorate her daughter's fluffy golden hair as though awarding her a medal.

A gift, also from doting parents. At this age, most valuable items received are from this source. She asked it to capture and listen to various sounds, filling it with waves and the ocean breeze. It also helped her better meet the expectations of others—the "Little Mermaid" fairy tale they all anticipated.

Frederick Augustus I, Elector of Saxony, vanished as easily as his admired Versailles and Louis XIV, leaving behind nothing but war in Dresden. Music, architecture, paintings, even the alchemy of legend, surfaced briefly in the waters of history.

His desired splendor and ideal hegemony were fleeting; chaos took over, vying for the church's golden dome. After the infantry left the forests and riversides, the cavalry set up camp with their artillery. Chaos breeds more chaos. Just look at the people in the square.

When everyone's gathered here with nowhere else to go, you know how bad the world is out there, and Dresden has drawn the short straw. She and the wanderers she prays for are struggling in the same way—too insignificant to be noticed, drifting with the tide. The boat that would carry them to salvation has not come.

The children won't understand why, before the torrent swallows them, why the red water would seep out from people's hearts first—why different notes appear at the beginning of a song destined to end.

At that time, the people saw and recorded the following:

"I am accustomed to seeing cavalry ready for action, wounded patients, wandering refugees, like grains of sand on the beach. Artillery fire is more frequent than birds, and corpses float faster than boats on the Rhine. Everyone needed her song, willing risk their sanity for it."

"A coin intended for a wishing well, left by her parents in the square, next to a clean fountain. She hums, kicking away pebbles—with her hands still tied. Even if things were different, with these dusty hands of mine, I wouldn't dare go hold hers. She's the girl who makes people happy, after all."

"But what does she want? Those young vagabonds either end up dead or in orphanages—she's lucky to have loving parents. But she's all tied up, toiling away in the square ... Oh, I hear a group of people heard her singing, and then they jumped into the river!"

"What does she want? To be kind, to stop a small skirmish, to ease pain ... and then what? What if a bigger disaster comes?"

At that time, the parents taught their adopted child:

"Bear all pain, endure your hardships, and maintain discipline. <nobr>Self-discipline</nobr> is akin to helping others."

"Before the masses, she will lead, guide, and give blessings, for her birth was a blessing."

Lorelei: Wow, I can't believe it! You're Ms. Mouth! That means you can talk in all different kinds of ways, right? Can you sing all different kinds of songs, too?
Pandora Wilson: I'm working on that. I'm pretty good at interviews though.
Lorelei: Please ask away and I'll do my best to answer.
Pandora Wilson: I'm curious ... Where did you get the name "Lorelei from the Rhine"?
Lorelei: At first I was just me, a little pebble, then I went farther than the valley—people invited me to sing. So this is me now. People say the name fits better.
Pandora Wilson: Fits what better?
Lorelei: It fits the Dresden Elbe Valley, the fountain in the square, the crossing streams ... maybe more. People like it though ... names don't matter, right?
Pandora Wilson: Not to you, it seems.
Lorelei: Of course, rivers all have sources, but, like my mother said, we all know where they come from, but we don't need to know where they flow. I just hope that the boats can sail steadily, and that people can bathe in the water.
Pandora Wilson: That is a beautiful blessing.
Lorelei: And I wish you many blessings, my kind interviewer!

Semmelweis, busy on her journey, is stopped by a voice. The owner of the voice is a young boy, ragged but with clear eyes. He opens his palm, and a note appears before her—a list, a gift from a fellow traveler, from which she can choose whatever she wants.

The outside world is in turmoil, but here it is warm and undisturbed. The interior, however, seems a bit different from early 20th century Vienna, with wall decorations more wild and rebellious than elegant. In these chaotic times of scarce supplies, having a place to rest is good enough. Semmelweis, an eternal pragmatist, doesn't mind these details and chooses ...

Passing by a tavern, Semmelweis engages in pleasant conversation with the owner. The owner admits that in Vienna, people prefer coffee houses over taverns. To thank the only customer of the night, the owner brings out his most precious wine to treat her.
The Other Side of the Door

A door appears before Semmelweis. She touches it, feeling a liquid on the handle. It's damp, sticky, darkly hued—mottled like a bloodstain, rust, like someone's deeply suppressed, tightly sealed heart.

Semmelweis passes a record store, where someone gently lowers the needle, and time stands still—art precipitates in this moment. She can't help but stop—something is calling her, a feeling beyond words, beyond text. It roars, laughs, tempting her to break free from the shackles of consciousness—to join it, to become it.

At the end of the road stands a castle. Through the windows, Semmelweis sees flickering candles and bustling shadows. It all blurs her vision, nearly suffocating her. At that moment, a pair of thin, <nobr>stick-like</nobr> hands tightly wrap around her feet.

A horde of critters gather here, chewing on the city's heart, licking its veins, imitating the residents of Vienna, holding their own coffee gatherings underground. Semmelweis, passing by chance, stumbles into an "old critter’s" afternoon tea party.
<color=#BF7E31>"Didn't I see it at the foot of the mountain?"</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"Could it be that the critters have brought their trade to Vienna, so very far away?"</color>

Semmelweis has walked the "noble boulevards" and climbed the "foul temples," piercing through the gold leaf, glimpsing the true shadows of the city. By chance, she meets the bizarre creature again, pretending to be a "gentleman." "We meet again." "Hah, it's pinned a Goldfinch Coin to its cuff."

A page is lifted by the wind, then falls to the ground. Semmelweis picks it up, as if picking up a past, a memory, a poem that should not be forgotten. That is art—the very source of life, generously praising the era, yet ultimately, also devoured by it, torn and chewed up, spitting out only a few bones.

Several crates lean against the wall, neatly arranged, tightly locked, contrasting with the dirty floor beside them. They seem to tempt passersby—discover it, open it, and then ... find treasure or prepare to be cursed.
To the Back of the Cave

A song echoes from afar, slow then fast, harmonizing with this melody, causing the water to tremble. Semmelweis looks back the way she came, seeing only colors, just colors. In the chaos, she sees a light, a ring, bright, beautiful, strong, that can take her anywhere—places further than the future.

Gemstone rings, black umbrellas, toothpaste tubes—vintage, <nobr>avant-garde</nobr>, it's all here. Semmelweis finds a little old man in the corner, juggling coins, who pulls her into an old warehouse, eagerly stuffing candy into her hands. He's very enthusiastic, assuring her he can fulfill all her needs.

A pocket watch, abandoned by someone or something, lies by the roadside. The glass is shattered, the minute and hour hands have stopped. But does it matter? Semmelweis looks at the jostling crowd, the banners strewn on the ground—if time indeed stands still, perhaps it's better for Vienna in its current state.

Semmelweis stands before a strangely shaped fountain, subconsciously staring at the water—naturally, her reflection isn't there. She can only see a sign and a few lonely Goldfinch Coins at the bottom. "The Fountain of Fate grants the wishes of every traveler. If you're generous with the Goldfinch Coins in your pocket and ask sincerely, you might get an unexpected response. Of course, if your wish or the way you wish doesn't please the fountain, be careful—it may charge you an extra fee." "Since you're already here, why not give it a try?"

"I see an expression on your face that doesn't belong to you, my dear—draw a card! May the guidance of fate help you find peace."
A strangely dressed arcanist stops Semmelweis, inviting to divine her fortune.

It's dirty, smelly, no one wants it, and no one is willing to approach it. But at this moment, it becomes the only "object" Semmelweis can touch with her hands. After all, in this mad era, only tangible things can bring complete peace of mind.

Set in an ancient stone wall, the pungent smell of turpentine not yet dissipated, like a newborn abandoned in a ruined world. The person in the painting is hidden in the twilight, as though peering into the darkness.

Bumping, jumping, swaying, hopping, it leaves tense tracks at this untimely place.
Semmelweis doesn't care if a drunken old car shakes her to pieces—but now it's charging at her. "Using critters to power driverless cars? Quite an innovative idea."

On today's streets, many things may tug at your sleeve, be they peddlers, scammers, or troublemakers ... Semmelweis cautiously shifts her gaze, only to see several dirty little hands. "Lady, please, have a heart! You'll be rewarded!"
It turns out to be a group of begging children.

Semmelweis didn't notice this colleague first. He's in a hurry, brim of his hat pulled low. As he brushes past, he hands her a <nobr>standard-issue</nobr> Foundation tactical map catalogue.
Semmelweis takes the map but doesn't stop.

A newspaper escapes the mail package, falling into Semmelweis's hands. She is about to examine it when a passionate voice rings in her ear:
"Haha! So you're a fan too, eh? Ah, no, stupid question—anyone with a decent pair of ears would be obsessed with her. You're also hoping to watch the premiere of Tosca, aren't you?"

Semmelweis just wants to rest her feet, but as soon as she sits down on the suitcase, it begins to chatter nonstop about itself. It boasts of being made from precious mahogany, about the high value of the emerald cups, agate, and red jade within it, and repeatedly emphasizes the fact that it is currently unlocked ...

After seeing her own stone markers for the third time, Semmelweis has to admit that these alleys cannot be considered shortcuts. A "guide" appears just in time, promising the lost traveler a way out and rare treasures, all for a small fee.

Danger lurks around every wrong turn.
Semmelweis is surrounded, with three menacing faces looming over her. The leader is quirky and jocular, the henchman blunt and foolish, while one of these faces opens its mouth in an attempt to intimidate her:
"Lady, don't think for a second you're leaving with the goods—we've followed you this whole way, and it's as clear as day what you've got there."

Semmelweis is stopped by a group of individuals dressed as police officers. They claim to have received a "report of a theft" and say they must search Semmelweis—the suspect. Without further ado, they rip open her backpack, and a familiar golden pocket watch rolls onto the ground. Semmelweis has indeed seen this model in the Secession Building, but she can swear that she has not once even touched it.

A pebble, kicked by Semmelweis, rolls into an underground pool. Bubbles surface, and the sprite within asks:
"Goldfinch Coins or a trinket?" "No, I didn't throw anything in." The sprite pauses for a moment, annoyed, and shouts, "I'm asking what you want to trade for my treasure—I'm not some river god who dishes out free lunches to honest fools!"

Why is there a brick wall here? Peering through the <nobr>light-leaking</nobr> crevice, critters no bigger than a soda can bustle about, carrying bone shards, mica, and Goldfinch Coins, busily coming and going, unaware of Semmelweis's towering gaze. This is a treasury belonging to critters. "So, this little crevice is a <nobr>mini-counter</nobr>."
As the terrain rises, a sliver of the sky flows down the rock dome. The secret stargazing base is empty. Only a telescope stands here waiting for a star.
The moment she steps into the sewer, the heavy door slams shut behind her. Accompanied by gurgling water, passages diverge and converge in a place where compasses, magnets, and maps lose all purpose.

Facing her is a door, heavy as an unyielding refusal. Any rational, or somewhat rational human wouldn't contend with a solid door, but when Semmelweis turns back—the same door appears on her path. "Once again, I've wandered into the desert of reason. So, should I touch, listen, or taste now? In any case, I'll use the one I'm least accustomed to."

The rusted skywalk creaks like a skeleton struggling to rise from the grave. As Semmelweis carefully reaches the middle, the bridge suddenly begins to undulate violently—behind her, a group of critters hop and jump. The more the bridge shakes, the happier they are. "Good heavens, I don't mind you playing trampoline, as long as you don't do it here."

She appears abruptly at the side of the street, like an oil painting that is peeling. Bullet holes riddle her body as if it were a thin sheet of paper, and Semmelweis seems to see wet paint flowing out of them. A child is standing beside her.

Semmelweis merely glances at the artist, but he keenly catches her eye. "Are you interested in my paintings? This way, please, let me introduce you to some pieces that possess both artistic and commercial value!" "Commercial value? You mean to say ... "

The brown soda bottle barrels through the feet of several pedestrians, stopping only when it reaches the center of the street. Its stopping point conveniently allows Semmelweis to pick it up. The glass bottle is unharmed, only a little dusty, and the rolling has clearly shaken up some excess bubbles, which densely sway and burst within the liquid proper.

The soda churns out fine, pleasant bubbles in the glass bottle. As Semmelweis prepares to open it, something hits her hard from behind, and the glass bottle slips from her hand. This time, the soda bottle does not escape its fate and shatters.

When chaos is brewing and fermenting, it's not surprising for something minor to go off the rails—like a tram suddenly appearing at an alley without any laid tracks.
"Going against the norm basically means—we're taking a shortcut!" At least that's what the tram conductor shouts. "This actually seems like a mode of transportation worth trying."

The polite conductor asks Semmelweis her destination and reminds her that the fare she just paid was only for boarding—traveling to her destination will require another payment. "Our travel fees are calculated based on mileage, fair to all!" He tosses his newly collected coins up and down with a broad smile.

A man stands up, dressed as a passenger, but surely not just a passenger. He eyes the coins Semmelweis retracts and asks: "If you have the leisure of being able to walk to your destination, why bother wasting our time?"

"Lady, if I'd been a second slower, you would've earned the respect of those two fools." The driver leaves his cab, but what attracts Semmelweis's attention more is the animal that stands up in the corner of the carriage. Its expression and posture make its stance clear. The tram driver puts on a smug smile: "Please teach this lady the rules."

This seems like an afternoon tea meticulously prepared by a person of taste, yet it is set upon boxes no taller than a calf. Compared to the surrounding environment, it is like a <nobr>self-contained</nobr> miniature kingdom, with abundant food and exquisite utensils—everything arranged so neatly that one can enjoy a quiet, satisfying atmosphere in one glance.

Whoever sits down first becomes the master of this empty table—the invisible rule of public restaurants, which also applies here, even though there are no tables or chairs. Seat thieves and food robbers, just sitting next to the box, Semmelweis inadvertently takes on a slightly unexpected identity.

This otherworldly location is somewhat noisy. Originally, it was a place silently enduring the ravages of time, with most of its rights usurped by wild grass and moss, yet new disputes still arise. "This is definitely my tombstone!" "This one—is mine! Yours is the one on the right!" They argue incessantly, turning their gaze to Semmelweis at the same time.

"No punishment is more severe than <nobr>self-analysis</nobr>, and no imagination is more blank than the perfection that exists only in the future. And you—need no longer concern yourself—your vague shadow has already refused <nobr>self-analysis</nobr> on your behalf." In the mirror's lengthy soliloquy, Semmelweis takes the opportunity to look at her reflection—thin, but still there. The mirror continues to ask: "So, what are you willing to do for your imagined future?"
The Belly of the Starry Sky

The courtyard is completely abandoned—fences broken, walls collapsed. Before Semmelweis realizes it, she has stepped into the belly of the courtyard. When she looks back, the path she came from has disappeared, and the <nobr>ring-shaped</nobr> arcane skill aura arrives belatedly—it is the territorial defense spell used by antiquated nobles. Now, within sight, roads, plants, and buildings have all melted into a bizarre, hazy starry sky. "This illusion doesn't seem as though it is about to attack. This aligns with what I know—entrapment is the primary purpose of such spells ... conserving more resources than preset attack spells. Yes, such spells always require continuous investment, a money pit, a bottomless hole, shouldn't appear in a courtyard no different from ruins. Who needs it, and who is powering it?"

The starry sky spins around Semmelweis with its inherent melody. Semmelweis's probing fades into emptiness, not disturbing the starry sky in the slightest, like an arcanum maxim: the starry sky does not listen to the thoughts of the mediocre, fate does not accept the prying eyes of the ordinary. Semmelweis has never publicly expressed her opinion on this statement.

A kite suddenly plummets, rolling down the face of a building, scraped by its patterns along the way, and finally spreads out on the ground in complete wreckage. From the deformed struts and cotton cloth, Semmelweis recognizes it as a large box kite. "This type of kite is often used for meteorological probing, and in this era, it might also be used in adventurers' flight games. I've never taken note of where Vienna's meteorological station is, but now ... is someone conducting a meteorological detection run?" The only response to Semmelweis comes from Bella: "I presume this meteorological observer is dutiful and passionate about their work. There are still people who care about their job responsibilities, aren't there?" "Don't disturb me. Something's moving in the wreckage."

The woman seated within the tent canopy proactively extends her arm, blocking Semmelweis's path. She forcefully pushes a package into Semmelweis's hands, her voice light yet indistinct: "Tradition is always right, and insurance is against Romani tradition—it should not appear on the Romani path ... I have been guided to hand it over to a traveler about to reach their destination." The canopy and veil make it hard to see her expression, nor can one tell if she harbors any ill will. Underneath the parchment, undeniable waves of arcane skill energy pulse. It feels like a stack of documents. Semmelweis stands before the canopy and unwraps the package. A sheet of paper large enough to envelop a person flies into the air—halfway through, it curls up its lower half on its own.

Several <nobr>peculiarly-behaving</nobr> pedestrians block Semmelweis's path. Scattered around them are several wooden crates, and through the gaps between the boards, Semmelweis sees wood shavings inside. Semmelweis guesses that something fragile is placed within them, and she frowns. "Excuse me, please make way." They do not respond, only lifting their heads to reveal faces covered in oil paint. They whisper fervently, their eyes full of a desire to fight. Upon seeing Semmelweis, they charge at her without hesitation.

The street is dim and empty, and amid the wind's wailing, Semmelweis smells the scent of burning candles. It comes from a statue almost completely shattered, lying across the street—a flicker of light still burning.

The oldest form of trade, the prototype of all markets. The concept of trust sprouts and grows here, to this day—for those willing to enter the shade of trust, bartering still has its place. Verses endure for their simplicity, as are rules—leave one item, only then can you take one away.
Trading Point: Tail of the Storm

The tavern seems to have undergone a robbery: tables overturned, liquor shelves emptied, the owner is sitting alone behind the bar, deeply troubled by the loss. This is not a good time for questions, but Semmelweis won't let go of any opportunities of finding new clues. She states her business and the owner promises to help her on one condition: he needs an artefact in return.

The tavern's atmosphere is grim. The still messy tables and chairs, the empty liquor cabinet, it seems that both the tavern's repair and the red wine purchase have failed in some form. The unchanged chaos from before hardly bodes well. The tavern owner still sits alone behind the bar, his previous listlessness and anxiety replaced by a strange excitement. He draws exaggerated circles in the air with his hands, nearly hitting Semmelweis's nose. His tone is high: "Look at these! You won't regret trading with me! I've always been a man of my word!"

Roaming in the city with a whole pocket of coins is not a wise choice. These shiny little things can attract crows ... or even robbers when there's a considerable number of them. Luckily, this <nobr>arcanum-powered</nobr> stone sculpture standing at the corner of the street can help solve the problem for you ... and even yield a profit by the way. "Is this lion ... a new service of the Mane Bank?"

The lion sculpture stands at the next corner. It appears just in time—this is where you need your savings and interest. But things are not going the way you expected. "Hello, Ms. Wagner, nice to see you again! You owe us a debt of 4,600 Goldfinch Coins, and you must repay it before ... What? Withdraw your money? I'm sorry. According to our company policy, you cannot borrow any money until you repay your current loan ..."

The boy rummages around, pulling out a small gadget from the basket, he nods, signaling for Semmelweis to take it.
<color=#BF7E31>"I never expected to get this here. Thank you."</color>
All companions recover 50% HP; recover 20 Stimulus.
Semmelweis leans into the sofa, fully relaxed, curling up tightly before closing her eyes and falling into a deep sleep.
Recall a lost companion. All companions recover 10% HP.
Semmelweis looks out the window, and amidst the twisting detached shadows, she glimpses a familiar figure.

Semmelweis doesn't just see this place as a temporary resting spot. After all, there are many important matters to attend to here, such as ... reading the 'Amber Manual' she had been searching for.
<color=#BF7E31>"It contains many interesting things."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"Appendices on the sources of ingredients for arcanum potions, research on strange mechanical devices, precious herbal manuscripts, lost formulas, various anecdotes and legends, the love stories of alchemists …"</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"It's truly <nobr>eye-opening."</nobr></color>
Semmelweis finds some booklets on the shelf that can improve her arcane skill. She reads them obsessively, even making notes.
Semmelweis pulls out an oddly shaped trinket from under the bed—a <nobr>must-have</nobr> for this journey.
Obtain 30 Catalyst Essence, increase Max Stimulus.

<color=#BF7E31>"This tastes absolutely divine."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"It's been ages since I've had a red wine of this quality."</color>
Discard 1 selected artefact to obtain 1 random artefact.

<color=#BF7E31>"You once mentioned that the people of Vienna prefer coffee to wine. The reason is ..."</color>
"Because ... coffee keeps you awake and makes you optimistic. Who doesn't love discussing love, art, and the good times? Wine, on the other hand, makes you muddled and melancholic. After drinking, we're forced to confront the vast, unfillable void within us." The shopkeeper gently swirls the wine in his glass, a faint flicker of emotion crossing his face.
<color=#BF7E31>"... So, it seems I'm no exception."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"I must admit, you've made me briefly believe that listening to others' thoughts isn't entirely meaningless. Please, take this, consider it an exchange for opening my eyes."</color>
The shopkeeper reaches out and takes the item from Semmelweis' hand. Smiling, he uncorks the bottle again. Semmelweis notices a small trinket embedded there, shining like a brilliant star.

<color=#BF7E31>"It opens this easily?"</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"As it turns out, a 'door' is only closed if you perceive it to be. A 'seemingly locked' door isn't necessarily so, and there might be more than one way to get through it."</color>
Through the gap, Semmelweis sees a light, a candle's flame. A burning, dazzling flame that shouldn't belong here. The temperature rises, the scent becomes overwhelming, and she almost loses her senses. Yes, untimely interruptions always come with a price. Yet, they often bring unexpected rewards.
Discard 2 selected artefacts to obtain 2 random artefacts.

<color=#BF7E31>"It seems difficult to enter through polite means."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"Fortunately, I've never been much concerned with politeness."</color>
The door lets out a dreadful groan as a thick black mist envelopes Semmelweis, overwhelming her with immense sorrow. This emotion is evidently not her own.

Semmelweis has no interest in the stories and emotions attached to this door. She has no time to play a role that conflicts with her nature. She also has no intention of debating with the voice in her head again; it's pointless.
Enter the shop through the front door

<color=#BF7E31>"It's neither classical music nor opera; it must be some other form of musical expression."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>The melody is similar to that song, but the emotions conveyed are slightly different.</color>
With the music an energy climbs up Semmelweis's spine, embraces her neck, and kisses her lips. It is a sound unique to her, one she has long ignored. Now it has finally appeared, in this era, on this stage, clearly audible, like yesterday.
Lose 80 Goldfinch Coins, obtain 1 random artefact.

<color=#BF7E31>"Ugh ... it's them again."</color>
There is an ambush. A group of soldiers approaches her with ill intentions, but fortunately, their eyes are fixed on Semmelweis's money pouch, not on her. Meanwhile, Semmelweis has her eyes on the bags hanging from their spears.
<color=#BF7E31>"It wouldn't be a bad idea grabbing those trinkets."</color>
Enter the shop through the side door
Discard 1 selected artefacts to obtain 80 Goldfinch Coins.

The floor creaks, and a shriveled hand reaches out through a gap, blocking Semmelweis's way, as if asking for something.
<color=#BF7E31>"Are you ... an Arcanist lurking in the dark, a homeless refugee, or a stagehand pulling the strings?"</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"If I can grant your wish, what will you give me in return?"</color>
She pulls a trinket from her bag and places it in the cold extended palm. The hand opens and closes, trembling violently, and even Semmelweis can feel its joy. It gently taps the floor like an opera actor taking a final bow before retreating. But as it goes, it leaves something for Semmelweis.
All companions lose 40% HP, obtains Helmet of a Knight.

<color=#BF7E31>"The inside of the castle doesn't seem safe either."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"But right now, there doesn't seem to be any better way to escape."</color>
She pushes open the door, and in the light, glimpses many eyes. They are burning with intensity and desire, fiercer than flames, capable of crushing everything. In the midst of their gaze, an artefact lies there silently.
Discard 2 selected artefacts to obtain Helmet of a Knight.

<color=#BF7E31>"I'd rather face fears I can see than those I cannot."</color>
Semmelweis turns around. Before her stands a young woman. She wears a pair of bright red metal dancing shoes that seems fused to her very being, having penetrated into her bones and blood, compelling her to dance ceaselessly. A breeze lifts the veil from the woman's face, and Semmelweis swears she has seen her before.
<color=#BF7E31>"Is she ...?"</color>
She is captivated by that face. Just then, a group of Carbuncles dash past her, silently stealing an item from her bag. As the music ends, the woman removes her veil and places it, along with an artefact, into Semmelweis's hand.
The cold sensation around her feet goes away gradually. When Semmelweis looks back again, the castle and the hands have vanished into the thick fog, like a mirage.
Encounter a hard battle, obtain 150 Goldfinch Coins.

<color=#BF7E31>"This appears to be a different Critter. This one is more ..."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"Pretentious? Cynical? Indulged in sensory pleasure? Reminds me of many old acquaintances, hah."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"It seems to be ... 'tasting' something. Where there's food, the exit can't be far."</color>
After licking the last drop of coffee, the Critter notices Semmelweis and corners her. She has no choice but to fight for survival.
Lose 30 Goldfinch Coins, may encounter them again later.

Look, the Critter is calm and poised—it takes off its imaginary hat, bowing to Semmelweis, and kisses her hand, as if it were a perfectly mannered Viennese gentleman.
<color=#BF7E31>"Strange feeling. The Critter seems to have learned to act like a local."</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"No! D**n it ... it's after the Goldfinch Coins."</color>
Lose 30 Stimulus, the next <nobr>non-Impending</nobr> Crisis path node becomes a Discovery.

<color=#BF7E31>"There's ... a book? Does the Critter leave it, or ...?"</color>

After hearing Semmelweis's account, the <nobr>well-dressed</nobr> gentleman frowns, then relaxes. "Perhaps the story is true." Before Semmelweis ask more, he tells her a story about a human couple and their adopted little girl. How love and patience calmed the Arcanist's madness. She is not a mere victim driven by primal urges; she is in control of her own desired indulgence.
From tales of the past to the reality of today.
It is our belief that if we hope for it, it will surely come.
That sense of fulfillment, and cooing.
She is well aware of her own limits.
... Something the greater existences know nothing about.
Back then, we held on to our fairy tales with unwavering conviction.
But like all great stories, the narrative takes a sudden twist.
And now, the world will be destroyed and reborn in fire.
Greetings from the haze and debris of the phenomenal world.
Into the ditches they gently flow.
She readily offers herself as a disposable test material.
And performs countless experiments without hesitation.
She persists, regardless of the circumstances.
It is a turbulent ship, steered by a wise nihilist.
And now, he can finally rest.

An Answer in the Bottle II
It was the absolute worst thing she could find.
And so Prometheus takes hold of the sacred fire.
"This charging socket has been approved by Ms. Lucy, but every time you go, she's using it, so you have to wait a long time."
"Either be wise, uninvolved, and look on; or be practical, involved, and suffer."
She always says what she's thinking.
Do not be puzzled, those occasional abstract paintings and numerical symbols are just a friendly means of expression.
Outside the window, the endless skyline stretches forward; inside, proposals of all sizes are born.
The roar of the airship will soon be seen as a prelude to the "Rock Carnival Night."
Commemorate the past, the future, and every soul not bound by gravity.
The first invited passengers were full of praise—"By the time we landed, people were still asking if we had taken off!"
Small, medium, large; line, plane, space. Don't panic—this is just a "sensory" experience.
Equipped with the most advanced plasma guns, <nobr>high-temperature</nobr> steam pipes, and special measures for children under 12—red indicator lights and digital smiles.
From one end to the other—oh, what a long mental journey.
The Midsummer Dragon Boat Festival arrives as usual, symbolizing the prosperity of all things. A good day worth a lively parade.
A past sorrow, a simple and sincere wish. Despite the passage of time, some things never change.
Whenever weariness creeps over you, take refuge from the city's chaos and enjoy serenity.
The most innovative cruising structure of today, known for its excellent space utilization and structural stability.
The axis of fantasy, the starting point of innovation, a silver vision begins here.
In this world of all things renewed, only the "plaza" has returned to its original use.
A canvas full of infinite possibilities, perhaps the starting point of a great idea.
No matter what, we don't want the "Electric Sheep Grazing Proposal" to ruin this ingenious design.
An <nobr>out-of</nobr>-era art wave emerges here, colorful, vivid, stirring.
An <nobr>out-of</nobr>-era art wave emerges here, lively, powerful, striking the soul.
Being in a silver ocean, we need intuition, prophecy, and fantasy more than ever.
The psychological therapy of this day and age ...
Ah, you're here. I'm just organizing my observations from recent days. Look, I already have a stack of notes.
I didn't expect to meet a Mesmer here, and a "contemporary" Mesmer at that.
Although our interaction was far from pleasant ...
You know, the whole sleepwalking thing is outdated; I don't want to lie on that chair!
Sometimes, "magic" and "therapy" are just a thin line apart. Based on my own experiences, I won't deny that.
The surface of water, Orbuculum, even astrology ... I've indeed gained some new insights into identifying the inner self and helping people understand themselves.
I've heard there are also theories about dance and "healing"... perhaps my notes will grow even more.
I almost forgot, classic tales are called "classics" for a reason—evidently, the word represents a curiosity that doesn't fade with time.
For instance, your companions are clearly very curious about me.
That lady journalist with the paper bag invited me for an interview.
And Mr. Click seemed quite interested in the subject of "whether my image can be captured."
Maybe someday I'll be a legend of the city streets or a story told around a campfire in the wilderness. It's a fascinating thought in its own way.
I received a tea party invitation from ... let me see, Ms. Winnifred.
If she isn't here to discuss the quality of those arcanum armors, then yes, I do think some people are interested in "Semmelweis."
Shh ... Good day, Vertin. Are you here to listen to the song as well?
We can sit together, but you must be quiet, whether walking or breathing ...
The sound of flowing water is familiar to me; the sound of Mr. Straw comes from the animals; and then there are the sounds of woodwinds, strings; different languages ...
I could sit here listening for a long time.
At first, our languages are always not in sync.
But Mom said that one must have love and patience. And I want to say, shh ... our voices are always too loud.
Melodies flow. Each person, including you and I, are in that river.
"The Wilderness"—Is this what it is called? I have noticed that the terrain and ecosystem here are quite unique.
Any season, species, or <nobr>man-made</nobr> objects might suddenly pop up here.
From preliminary observations, I tentatively believe that the rule here is "there are no rules."
Considering your ownership of the space in the suitcase, and your connection to this place, I indeed plan to include your influence as a variable.
I will keep an eye on it, Timekeeper.
Indeed, randomness is property that exists objectively. Some people have a preference for this trait, which I respect.
But until the hypothesis is formally proven, I believe research should not stop.
I knew it, you and I are alike, always in pursuit of the truth.
You mean ... you're interested in my photo?

To be fully immersed in capturing genuine images from places nearby ... that's a dream come true for every media professional who is dedicated to seeking the truth rather than pandering to the masses.
What do you think? I've heard that sightings of cows and unidentified flying objects still occur in the wilderness.
Sounds like it requires a long wait in concealment, ma'am.
Hmm ... well, good thing I'm good at that.
The tea party awaits us. Every child can be Alice!
Of course. Do you prefer <nobr>berry-flavored</nobr> syrup, or <nobr>syrup-flavored</nobr> berries?
I haven't read fairy tales in a long time ... but thank you for the invitation, Baby Blue.
I will prepare well for this trip.
The <nobr>second-hand</nobr> supermarket is a great place; these sunglasses were less than one Aussie dollar.
Look at these sequins; I bet you can find equally beautiful things there.
Uh ... thank you, Desert Flannel. They are certainly ... shiny?
Hey, you're not being sincere, are you?
When you have matured as much as I have, you will learn to appreciate the beauty of sequins, rhinestones, and laser sunglasses.
So, listening to the ground is a useful skill. The earth will tell you where there are bighorn sheep, yak herds, or rivers.
I'm glad you think so too, little girl!
... Thank you, sir, I have gained much from our conversation.
You understand the character of flowing water, just as I understand mountains and wolf pups.
By the way, I have many heating techniques from the foothills that will surely help you!
So, what you have learned and remembered spans thousands of years?
They come from the past "6s," of which I am just one bearer.
I have also witnessed the rise and fall of several eras ... and have read fortune and misfortune in bones. But ultimately, I remain in the mountains.
So since we're both here, there's no need for me to elaborate on this experience, is there?
... And so, the evil demon king was defeated, and the swan maidens were freed. This painting tells that story, Ms. Hiss!
Oh, I see! Some of your letters look familiar, but others are like they are mirrored, more confusing than the Candlestick Festival flyers.
At first, I was also intimidated in language class, but my mom said letters are our friends. Although they sometimes look stern, we can always get along if we are patient.
Ha, that sounds like something Sherjah would say. I hope these "friends" are as easy to get along with as coffee grounds.
I'm glad you understand this, Ms. Lucy! Communicating with you about logic is quite efficient.
The combination of arcane skills, ballistic projectile calculations, and logic as a way of working makes sense. I do not understand why some people confuse foresight with "superpowers."
Oh, maybe it can be attributed to people's imagination. If you're interested, I can recommend some Disks to you.
Like "The Shining Scary Hotel" or <nobr>"X-ray</nobr> Monkey Man," or would you like to try gore films? There's also ...
I respect your interests and artistic pursuits, Mr. Joshua. But unfortunately, I have no interest in such art.
Cheers! I declare this my current favorite word.
After a whole month of ascetic life in the forest, finally—my dear, unlimited Dr. Papper!
Oh, this is not to say that your energy replenishment potion is hard to swallow ...
It's okay! I am a mature lady who knows how to listen to opinions.

I'm working on improving its taste. The preliminary plan includes adding Ead's Tongue, Phoenix Tears, and the horn of a Changeling ... Once I find the right proportions, the potion can taste just like you want, even like Dr. Papper!
Why the shocked face, Regulus? No, these ingredients are only slightly more expensive than gold, not costly at all!
You ... you must be Ms. Semmelweis. Ms. Hofmann spoke of you often.
Greta has told me a lot about you as well, missy.
She has always praised your abilities, and rightly so. Your performance during the mission was exceptional.
Thank you ... No, I'm fine. I'm just...
I'm glad I could talk to you about Ms. Hofmann ... Thank you, Ms. Semmelweis.
You're here too, aren't you, kind doctor?
Did I really hear your voice, or was it just another trick of my own hysteria? Maybe my unstable nerves are feeding me lies again.
You're not here ... Doctor ... you're not here, are you?
Ms. Sotheby, did you try the potion recipe we talked about last time?
Thank you for that potion recipe! However, I'm still missing one ingredient ...
What ingredient? Maybe I can help.
If I remember correctly ... it's "deer antler."
... Strange, I couldn't find such material in the "Arcanum Creatures Material Index."
Oh ... beautiful lady, may I have the honor of asking you about some poetry?
Are you referring to me ...? Of course, I'd be happy to! What style of poetry are you interested in?
Something like expressionism, surrealism, or confessional poetry ...
Unfortunately ... I need those that are more romantic, or rather—more favored by ladies.
First mate! Get moving, I need you to plunder more loot!
Hey, don't you dare demote me, captain!
Oh, you really understand rock! Rock is all about screaming it out!
But which song are you singing?
Hello, hello, hello. May I invite you to my party?
I know, you must want more rainbow lollipops.
Maybe it's because there are too many rainbow lollipops ...
Trust me, it's not as fun as you think.
It allows you to hear everything in the world more clearly.
Whether you want to hear it or not.
Especially, the things you don't want to hear ... those filthy secrets.
Hah! Secrets, that's exactly what I want ...
I agree with you. People pass judgment on new inventions too readily.
But that completely stifles inventors' creativity.
In the field of arcanum, this is unreasonable.
Aside from an invisibility cloak that only hides the clothes, I don't think any invention is useless.
Hey, kid, you should learn to respect your elders more.
What I mean is ... would you be interested in doing a radio advertisement?
You see, a radio with its own consciousness broadcasting an ad for Critter pets.
It will certainly deepen the concept of the "Ms. NewBabel."
I don't particularly like these ... fluffy <nobr>four-legged</nobr> creatures.
What a pity. But in fact, they are quite <nobr>well-behaved</nobr>.
When you look in the mirror, what do you see?
You don't have to answer. This is not a consultation, I respect your privacy.
This is just the sudden curiosity of a friend.
Yes, this is the first thing we see when we look in the mirror.
You always maintain yourself—this is steadfast and precious.
I really wish I had your courage ...
Oh, are you describing the phenomenon of reflection?
Or, as I have always theorized, is this garden actually a reflection of some part of your inner self?
As for me, this place has flowers and wastelands, friends, and everything to accommodate change—this is a place worth stopping by, a place that belongs to you.
If I ever leave here ... I think, when I look back in the mirror, I will see this place again.
Of course, I respect your privacy.
If you ever want to talk about it, you can come to me anytime—same as with any other topic.
We are all used to moving forward.
Because the only option is "no other option," and because things are not great, but not bad enough to stop either.
Interestingly, for me personally, it was I who chose my current situation.
Look, under the combined influence of those choices, I have come here, and I enjoy working with you.
Until our next <nobr>life-and</nobr>-death decision comes up, right?
I think you and I already have some experience in dealing with it.
I won't regret it, and through these days of cooperation, I know you won't either.
I saw my hometown, people floating in the water, people singing along with me.
I also saw my parents, they are always with me, like the water.
When we love, we will not separate, like water droplets merging.
Oh, yes, you're here too, Vertin, I won't forget you.
In the melody, on the river.
We ride on suitcases and conch shells, drifting along.
You are always here, and I am always here.
You considered my proposal to add charging stations and sensibly set them up in the wilderness, for which I am grateful.
I heard you also handled the requests of Researcher Medicine Pocket regarding walking areas and <nobr>chew-resistant</nobr> tools, as well as the suggestions for rock venues and woodland spaces.
You have become quite adept at coexisting with "differences."
This place brings together many different people. Considering the space in the suitcase, the number of people, and their backgrounds, this level of difference is even greater than in Laplace.
Differences bring conflict, but also progress. Endless conformity only leads to stagnation.
Now, I am also one of your "differences."

Huh ... What do you want? Leave me alone!
I'm not giving you the cool stuff I just scavenged, no way.
I'm off to the next junk pile! Goodbye and so long!
Looks like you want a Dr. Papper ... MY Dr. Papper, by the way.
Neither of us got to drink that Dr. Papper, and I don't understand why you attacked me. But what's done is done ...
Farewell, ma'am. I'll treat you to a Dr. Papper next time.
Ma'am, paying the fare early will get us to our destination sooner. It makes things easier for both of us ... Don't you think?
I'll give you one last chance. Give me the stuff, and I'll ask you to leave, "nicely."
I believe you, ma'am! Stop fighting, we can rebuild our trust ...
Ma'am, if I may be blunt, there's no sense in causing such a fuss over a little money. You'd be better off begging. I'm known for my generosity ...
Oh—You're, you're rich! No, no, don't retaliate, your time is too precious ...
I really wish it didn't have to come to this.
The key to victory is timely adaptation. It's time to counterattack!
Focus on the enemy's weaknesses, everyone!
I underestimated you, my former colleague. It's time for you to see the full extent of our squad's capabilities.
For the Emperor, for the Empire, advance! Advance!
Avoid that area. Come this way.
Imagine ... the ceremony after the war, my chest adorned with medals, hah!
Once again, no surrender! Fire the shells!
Capture them! Kill them! Charge! Charge!
This monster is changing tactics, it's gathering strength ... Everyone, stay alert and find cover! It's planning something big!
Rebels, the Empire's reinforcements are endless, beyond your imagination!
It's too loud ... It's disturbing the entire symphony.
Your song is like a refreshing spring, and has eased the pressure ... Thank you.
Why, Sophia? Why must we fight each other?!
I am an irrational number, an obstacle in the pursuit of Truth. I have accepted my fate, abandoned my Scriptures, and embraced the path I should have chosen.
What!? Are you making fun of my name?
Ah, it deflected my arcane skill!
Vertin, it's no use attacking 21. Just focus on 9 and 33 instead!
Start with the number that has the largest absolute value: 33!
Yes, 73, a good number. It's the 8th twin prime, the 8th lucky prime ...
... and in the same combination as 37!
But sadly, you're the 21st prime number, which makes you less than perfect. Vertin, let's start with—
... With 73, because it has the largest absolute value.
Nice choice, Vertin! You are a quick learner.
Critters eating beans and a white rooster ... These are supposed to be taboos on the island.
Is this an illusion brought on by the fog? Or a new trial ...
... No, something's not right. The flow of arcane skills on the island has changed.
I need to get rid of them first.
Is all this ... still an illusion?
What ... is this? It has more hands than all the members of a band combined!
Timekeeper, there's a gigantic creature emerging from the portal. We must complete stage two as soon as possible.
Tsk, we better finish it off before we start stage three!
Copy that. This is a critical moment. Everyone stay alert and await my command.
Is this creature changing its afflatus to match that of its attacker?
Ha, a mimic strategy. Clever. But we can also use it to our advantage.
Everyone, rotate your arcane skills! Make sure we always have the stronger afflatus! Let's teach it a lesson in improvisation!
Timekeeper, the enemy's ritual has altered the environment. Please be careful.
It has been a long time since this APPLe fell on someone's head. I assure you, this time it will not be an inspiration.
The geometry of your ritual circle is quite good, but it could use a few more triangles. I happen to have some right here. You're welcome!
Timekeeper, please allow me to assist you.
Let's rock and roll, everyone! It's show time!
Take cover. I'll send it back into outer space.
The creature is defeated, and Arcana has emerged once again. Timekeeper, stage two is complete!
Cool! Now we just have to activate it!
No. Things are going too well. Like this has been rehearsed ...
What on earth is she trying to do ...?
You're right. We've put too much time and effort into this plan to not carry it out now.
Sonetto, Lilya, Regulus, assume your positions!
It's time ... to enact the final stage.
Singing for oneself and singing for an audience ... what's the difference?
You know, while rehearsing, I found another cave structure that is even more ideal for this performance.
I'm glad ... that no one left early.
The curtain has fallen ... please stay a while and listen to this echo.
Hey, this will be a bullet exhibition. Honestly, the colorful bullets often remind me of those childhood candies I could never get ...
Ma'am, what's your favorite candy effect ... oh, I mean, bullet flavor?
Ceasefire—ceasefire! My favorite shell casing has rolled away!!
Even before we started drifting, fate had already revealed today's adversaries to us.
You don't believe in fate? Yes, a beautiful flower, how could it accept the coming wither?
You have defeated me. Unfortunately, your path is still uncertain. You don't know where you're heading.
Round Two. Someone is far from exhausted.
Someone remembers the admonition they heard when they were knighted: Never fear the enemy.
Someone admits defeat but refuses to submit to injustice.
<nobr>Y-you</nobr> again, the lady who called me a liar ...
I'm hiding here, don't come looking for me ... but don't just walk away, please ...
But, isn't it normal to protect one's own grave? Ugh ...
I've seen people like you, trying to rob us when my mom's not around ...
Take this, my mom said carrying it would bring "good luck."
The pilots are unharmed. It seems having the ability to fly prevents injuries in crash landings.
Defeat enemies to obtain the Goldfinch Coins they carry.

Eliminate the embers quickly to prevent them from growing stronger.
When the statues are gathered together, they'll cause even more trouble.
The burning stacks on the chanter might be the key to defeating them.
Without its Sturdiness, a Monstrous Cave Eagle loses its ferocity.
Critters have bad tempers, don't disturb their sleep.
Free the Fuzzy Ball Miners from their forced labor permanently.
The statues seem to be guarding something.
A gathering of Carbuncles always spells trouble.
They are inseparable, controlling their HP disparity will simplify the battle.
Never land a critical hit; they mean no harm, except to "cool you off."
Destroy their bullets, or they'll summon reinforcements.
Don't let Charred Flower Seeds hatch successfully.

Watch the state of the Roaming Wanderers.
This is a "fair" duel, taunting might ease your pressure.
Make good use of Leered to leave Shrouded Ghost with nowhere to hide.
Physical attacks seem unable to penetrate the knight's armor.
