Deary me, this place is in quite a state, isn't it? I can hardly recall a workshop messier than this one. The tools are spread all over the floor ... Quite a peculiar choice of location, don't you think?
But look at these installations ... Hmm. Well, it's not as complicated as it looks. We just need to direct the flow of the correct fluid into the bottle. Now let's see ...
Lucky for us, these still seem in good shape. All we need to do is rotate these pipes to form a path for the fluids to flow through.
Tap to interact with the pipes
Turn it to redirect the mixture to where it should go.
Look around. There must be some empty bottles nearby. Maybe they've been left in a corner and forgotten about.
Alright, nice and steady, now. Go grab it. The bottle filled with red fluid. Look how it shines.
Tap to pick up the elemental bottle.
Tap the pipe opening to insert the elemental bottle.
It's becoming more challenging, which is a good sign. We're probably getting close to the good stuff. Or maybe it's already here, right under our noses.
But we need the right key to solve the problem.
Alchemy is as esoteric and sophisticated a practice as can be, but mixing together a few fluids shouldn't be too difficult for you.
Since we don't have any other equipment right now, we might as well make use of this pipe ... Looks like an old reaction vessel to me.
Come, try it. We've got to start somewhere.
Oh look, here's a new trick.
If I'm not mistaken, this is a storage unit.
The good news is, we have more than enough materials to use. The bad news is, we have to use our brains again. All this thinking ... It never comes to an end!
Do you see those sections with the open ends? The fluids can flow through them.
It would be a good idea to use them to connect the pipes. Trust me, I'm sure it'll help.
Looks like the way we came, but it's a little different ...
These <color=#cc492f>signs</color> ... are they trying to take me somewhere?
An ethereal scorn permeates the air.
There is no option but to continue on.
The words on the wall are aiming to confuse you.
The trial is nearing its end, the <color=#cc492f>world under the light</color> lies ahead.
Examining the "Storm" is a daunting task that requires careful consideration.
That's why it's wise to collect and document every potential <color=#cc492f>clue</color> here for future reference.
Show me how you have changed since last we met.
Arcana is dangerous. We may not be able to defeat her.
But right now, that's not our goal.
Relax. I've got the whole battle plan all up here in my head!
I shall relegate captain duties to you for today, Vertin!
You have made new friends. Aye. Have they changed you?
Perhaps it's time you met my "old friends". Come; they await thy greetings.
Timekeeper! Arcana has disappeared, and monsters are pouring out of the portal she created!
Huh? She's running away!? That was quite the grand escape ...
No. I can sense her. She's still there, looking down at us through that portal.
Everyone, it's almost time. Zeno will start any minute. We need to complete our preparations as planned and force Arcana to show up.
Easy. If we finish off all her minions, there's no way she'll just stand by and watch.
The big guy up there is mine. You deal with the rest!
Trying to gain air supremacy? Not under my watch.
I'll send that outdated hunk of scrap metal crashing to the bottom of the ocean!
I will not allow the tragedy in Chicago to happen again. Timekeeper, it's time I showed you what my training's been for.
Timekeeper, I've defeated the enemy. Beginning the <color=#cc492f>preparations</color> now.
Be careful, Captain! It appears that some abraxases are being affected by the "Storm". They are attacking indiscriminately.
Alright, then don't draw their attention. Let them attack the Manus ...
Hey! We were so quiet! Why are they coming for us?!
It seems that the "Storm" cannot entirely change their instinct.
*panting* Finally got rid of them ... Now, how am I going to deal with this ...?
Timekeeper, the first <color=#cc492f>preparation stage</color> is complete!
Great! Next, we destroy the portal ...
Marvelous, Vertin. You have put on a magnificent performance.
As a gesture of gratitude, I shall bestow unto you these gifts.
She just ... showed up of her own volition?
No, something's not right. The arcane skill in that portal is fluctuating strangely ...
She's casting a ritual! Vertin, retreat!

Before starting your journey, you need to select a Tone, which determines the strength of the enemy and the amount of credits you will earn.
The higher the tone level, the stronger the enemies and the more credits you will earn.
New Noises represent special effects created under this Tone. <nobr>Higher-level</nobr> Tones inherit all the noise effects of the previous Tones.
At lower Tone levels, any characters, Psychubes, and Resonance levels that do not meet the requirements are automatically leveled up.
Once you've chosen the Tone, it's time to choose a Catalyst for your adventure. Let's go with the "Pomegranate Heart" Catalyst for this round.
Each Catalyst has its own set of initial effects.
After selecting your Catalyst, tap here to summon your companions.
In A Series of Dusks, every character has a Clamor value. The higher the character's star level, the higher their Clamor.
When summoning characters, the total Clamor of the summoned characters cannot exceed the Summon Clamor Cap.
When starting out, the Lineup Clamor Cap is equal to the Initial Lineup Clamor Cap of the Catalyst.
You can summon up to 8 companions when starting out.
When summoning companions, you can choose to recruit an assist character, who also has a Clamor value.
Moving forward is essential to reaching your final destination.
To move forward, select a node on your current path and move toward it.
During the journey, you will gain Catalyst Essence. When the Catalyst Essence, which can be thought of as a form of EXP, fills up the current limit of the Catalyst, the Catalyst will level up.
Leveling up the Catalyst will increase the Lineup Clamor Cap, grant Potential, and allow new companions to be summoned.
When summoning companions is triggered by leveling up the Catalyst, there is a fixed Clamor Cap for that summoning session.
You can choose one or more characters, but the total Clamor cannot exceed the Summon Clamor Cap.
When a Catalyst is leveled up, the Potential gained can be used for Catalyst Progression.
At each level of Catalyst Progression, you can choose to activate one of two Potential effects.
In Catalyst Progression, only the level four effects are specific to each individual Catalyst. All other Potential effects are randomly generated.
In A Series of Dusks, the total Clamor of the deployed characters cannot exceed the Lineup Clamor Cap.
Deploy a character as a combatant.
In A Series of Dusks, you can use all the Psychubes you own.
You can configure Aiders below the deployed characters to provide additional effects during combat.
During battles, the original Tuning will be replaced with Catalyst Incantations.
Using [Catalyst Incantation] consumes Stimulus. Any remaining Stimulus from this battle will carry over to the next.
During artefact selection, you can choose and keep one or more artefacts for yourself.
You have acquired a new artefact. Tap here and have a look.
In A Series of Dusks, each artefact has its own unique grid structure.
Artefacts need to be placed on the left side, in the "Layout," to take effect in battles.
Newly acquired artefacts are automatically placed in the layout.
When there's not enough space in the layout to place new artefacts, the newly acquired ones will be placed in your "stash" on the right.
You can drag an artefact to any desired position in the layout.
By cleverly placing artefacts, you can utilize their grid interactions to gain bonus effects.
Tap on an artefact in the layout to select it. You can rotate <nobr>non-square</nobr> artefacts by tapping on them again.
After completing an area, you will enter a Safe Zone. You can tap on the pieces in the zone to interact with them.
You can review artefact exchange recipes on the left side of the screen.
The exact requirements for each item are listed to the right.
After the exchange, the required materials will disappear, and you will receive the target artefact.

When the bricks crumble,
Amidst the sound of hurried footsteps,
The heartbeat of energy, orderly and rhythmic.
She still gazes,
At the distant fire that illuminates everything.
And within that fire is the ladder to tomorrow.

The moment of decision has come. Farewell, my friend.
I will forever bless tomorrow,
Hold hope in my heart for you,
And pour out all my remaining courage upon my homeland.
That shaded path, those halls, that golden circuit that bears me.

<nobr>Tick-tock</nobr>, time slips into the water;
The clouds collide and descend,
Sweeping through this fleeting moment,
All things in the world suddenly perceived.
Where is she? Where is she going?

Walking through the deepest shadows, under the intense sunlight,
She disappeared. Not behind, nor beneath.
Not in photos, nor in the mirror,
Only you see her, holding her hand.

The Potomac River flows silently.
Father, oh Father.
The grassy field and white crosses have stood for hundreds of days and nights.
I will set off, I will travel far, my wings are not yet strong, my future unknown.

On this day, Eastern people row boats, even on land! This conjures images of Viking longships. Could it signify a connection between Easterners and Vikings? The editor will continue to investigate.

Mugwort and calamus leaves, no need for dragon hearts or phoenix feathers, just common herbs. Burning them brings good fortune and wards off evil spirits—what exactly are these evil spirits? Must investigate further.

Wearing <nobr>five-colored</nobr> silk threads on this day also represents good luck. Four colors might represent the four elements, but what about the fifth color? Perhaps Easterners discovered the fifth element before Aristotle? The academic world is astonished.

On this day, Easterners wrap a special type of rice called "glutinous rice" in plant leaves, steam it, and then throw it into water. Why do they throw food into water? Find out in the next installment …

According to Eastern movies, glutinous rice is a weapon against undead spirits. Combined with warships and blessing rituals, smart people should realize—this day commemorates the Easterners' battle against certain underwater undead spirits. A terrifying truth.

This is my tenth day here. The island greeted me today with a clear morning imbued with the moist, salty breath of the sea. I woke to the cry of seabirds, realizing I had adapted to the rhythm of life here faster than I imagined: it was sunrise, and I found myself naturally reflecting on the lecture from the day before. As the teachings of the school suggest: awaken with the Star of Apollo, reflect on yesterday's deeds, and plan today's tasks.

Attracted by the gentle sea breeze blowing through my window, I decided to take a walk on the beach before breakfast. By now it was no longer a challenge to find my way through the elegantly simple white buildings built in precise patterns. I followed a sweeping curve toward the shore, wondering what function this path might serve. Soon the neat pebbles underfoot gave way to soft sand, and the cries of the seagulls mingled with the unique hissing sound of the Abraxases—I guessed they were soaring above the distant cliffs. I stepped onto the gravel, quickly becoming lost in my thoughts.

At the School of Apeiron, mornings are for strolling through the fields. Apparently, I wasn't the only one who preferred the beach for my walk. A quiet young disciple walked by, kindly pausing to touch my hand and greet me with a gesture. I smiled back, preserving the quiet moment. Not long after, two other members of the school, deep in discussion about a number theory problem, almost collided with me, so engrossed were they in their conversation. I wandered aimlessly, letting my thoughts guide my steps, contemplating my recent experiences.

"Perhaps I should stay on this island a bit longer?" I said to myself.

Of course, the only answer was the incessant sea breeze.

Unconsciously, as the cool seawater lapped over my feet, someone beside me spoke up: "You're about to step into the sea, ma'am." I recognized her hoarse, authoritative voice.

I stopped and thanked the kind Custodian. She led me to a place safe from the tides. For a moment, we faced the ocean together.

"Is it the color of wine?" The words of a poem I had read long ago came to mind, and I suddenly spoke them aloud. Please forgive me; it wasn't meant to be presumptuous. On this island, I seemed to recall all my <nobr>long-forgotten</nobr> knowledge of ancient Greece.

"What did you say?"

"Sorry, I just suddenly remembered Homer's description of the sea."

She shook her head. "No, I think it's just blue. Just blue."
—Excerpt from the column essay "The Mysteries I Know"

I remember the first time I saw a maze in a children's picture book. On the flat pages, the winding lines created complex circular, diamond, or <nobr>bird-shaped</nobr> walls. The possibility of getting lost terrified and inevitably excited my young self, and I immediately began the adventure, pencil in hand.

Of course, at the age of five, I had never heard of Theseus, the fearsome Minotaur, or the wise Princess Ariadne. Looking back now, the lure of a meticulously woven puzzle that compels one to venture within its winding walls seems like an irresistible temptation that spans millennia. Dear readers, allow me to make an irresponsible conjecture: when the genius architect Daedalus (who, according to some legends, was actually an arcanist—how fitting!) accepted King Minos's invitation to build the world's most famous labyrinth, he must have anticipated the hidden dangers of the task. Still, the opportunity to create such a puzzle with his own hands was clearly too tempting to resist.

As my loyal readers are aware, I have spent many years observing and studying those we call "arcanists." Forgive my rambling, but the above recollection of mazes is not entirely unrelated. To my knowledge, in the field of arcanum, regular shapes and lines (or "arrays") generally guide the smooth operation of spells. Proper shapes can enhance the effectiveness of arcanum, or alter and transpose its properties. Constructing these shapes as large, immovable entities is undoubtedly one way to preserve the spell.

From the labyrinths of Crete and those described by Pliny the Elder in Italy to the towering labyrinth gardens of Schönbrunn Palace, how many mazes bear the marks of arcanists? In today's society, is there still a small island somewhere like Crete that houses an unfathomable arcane labyrinth? For more insights and speculations about the arcanum, please continue to follow my column ...
—Excerpt from Notes Stained with Deep Purple Marks

According to mythology, the former ruler of Delphi was a giant serpent named Python, who occupied the local spring until he was slain by Apollo. Apollo then built his temple and made this place his base for delivering oracles. Aeschylus believed that the oracles of Delphi originated from Gaia, the Goddess of the Earth, and the legend of Python may symbolize the replacement of primordial earth mother worship with Apollo worship. Quick note: He drove away his great-grandmother's pet! What a remarkable young man. In another legend, Zeus released two eagles to the east and west to measure the earth, and the two eagles eventually met at Delphi. Therefore, a stone pillar was erected at Delphi, carried by two golden eagles, to commemorate this event that made this place the center of the earth. The stone pillar is called "Omphalos," meaning the navel of the earth. Quick note: Obviously, the king of gods needed a more accurate means of measurement ... The priestesses of Delphi were known as Pythia, and they gave oracles to the people during the Apollonian festivals. Not every question could be answered by the gods; it was up to the priests to decide which questions could be accepted. One method of judgment was to pour cold water on a goat offered as a tribute by the questioner; if the goat did not tremble, it was considered a bad omen, and appropriate rituals had to be performed immediately. Quick note: For the goat, living an extra quarter of an hour is indeed a great blessing. Tomorrow's sermon topic is set—ancient texts and traditions. Just thinking about debating with 888 makes me wish I were telling jokes to our great leader instead. In some legends, for three months each winter, when Apollo went north for purification, Delphi was taken over by the wine god Dionysus. During this time, oracles were given in the name of the wine god, intertwining the divinities of the sun god and the wine god. Quick note: "On the Worship of the Wine God within Sun God Worship," a good topic for a public lecture. At least, it looks good now—hoping that after the effect of the wine, I still think so. 37 thinks I ate too many grapes. Yes, she is a child of Hermes. I don't expect her to understand this, but I now need the spirit of the wine god ...

Considering that you've stepped through the gates of Laplace— which means there's a 95.7% chance that you're as much of an oddball as I am, and almost no one here cares about your social etiquette—I didn't originally plan to include a "relationship advice" section in this manual. I think you'll agree with me: that sort of thing is more appropriate for elementary school classes.

However, given the diversity of members here, I'm sure you don't want to unintentionally offend a potential supervisor within the first five minutes of meeting them. So here are some useful tips:

1. Honest Communication. They may not have a biological sex, they may think of themselves as a toaster, and they are a toaster. But make no mistake about it, they are still a valued colleague of ours. If you're not sure how to communicate with them, just ask them.

2. Respect Beliefs. What constitutes a life belief, and how to find them—this topic easily veers into the realm of philosophy. But generally, The Awakened often have goals or beliefs upon "awakening." I must admit that having a natural sense of purpose is something I envy. And I'm sure I'm not the only one who feels this way.

3. Understand Commonalities. Hey, since we're all oddballs, let's be real—there's no difference between a colleague who needs regular electricity or winding up, and a colleague who periodically ingests copious amounts of caffeine to stay awake. If your colleague is incapacitated by a lack of electricity, being considerate and bringing a charger is as appreciated as bringing coffee and a sandwich.

—Well, in summary, all the weirdos welcome you and hope you keep all your limbs intact during your first week at Laplace!

Attention all members of the LSCC: For your safety, please read and adhere to the following regulations. These regulations apply to all personnel entering the work areas (defined in the appendix, including but not limited to the Laboratory, the Cryptography Room, the Recovery Clinic, and the Artificial Somnambulism Room), without exception. In short, this means everywhere except the Reception and Break Room. I think we need safety regulations for the Break Room, no joke—you don't want to know what I found in my coffee last week. 1. Work Area Conduct Regulations 1.1 Eating and drinking are prohibited outside of designated eating areas. Voices from the journey ahead:

"Hey, Daniel, hurry up! Put that cartridge back in your hand or buy it with your own allowance! Don't look at me like that. Even if I buy it for you today, the arcade still has plenty of games inviting you to skip school anytime ..."

"Speaking of which, I won't ask why you can't afford this cartridge. Remember the last time you got scammed by that vendor? A mysterious ghost that helps you win 100% of the games? Pretty imaginative. Your friend is right, if you're going to play games for unconditional 100% wins, why not just play against <nobr>three-year-olds?"</nobr>

"In any case, you should know that it's your own actions that are causing you to lose your allowance. If this mysterious ghost really existed, I'd pay right now to make you old enough to apply for a credit card—then you could spend as you please. Also, for our family's sake, please don't put my number as the emergency contact at the bank."

Shouts from the shelf:

"Hey, I'm over here. Yes, yes, your pendulum is pointing at me, I'm in this box, it's covering my head!"

"You don't think so? Oh, come on, with so many used arcanum items here, everyone's mind is a mess. Of course, you'd want to find at least one—at least one that's sane—me, (hic!)"

"I don't have any problems aside for the occasional hiccup. This might be a side effect of the digestive tract splicing. That doesn't mean my feet are glued on, absolutely not. My brothers and I were born this way. Just because we're rare and not in the Critter Atlas, doesn't mean we don't exist, (hic) it's really unfair ..."

"Splicing? Some foolish people who think they're experts dismembered our poor bodies, claiming that they were exposing lies. Fortunately, I can't feel pain anymore. So, now that we've talked this much, will you let me join you? I'm much more accurate than your little stick. Eight rabbit feet bring eight times the luck. You can't miss out on that (hic), me, I mean!"

"Excuse me, are these false teeth... Ow, ow, stop biting me—let go!" 

"... So you're saying it bit me because I was feeling emotional? It's designed to punish those who break the rules? Like a disciplinary tool for teaching assistants? I thought corporal punishment wasn't allowed anymore. Wait, this is meant for parties?" 

"When the atmosphere is lively, it stores the excess and releases it all at once when things calm down ... But does it do that by biting people? Maybe you have a point, it could create some kind of atmosphere, but did my emotions just now really deserve a bite?" 

"These are the previous user's instructions? 'Due to excessive use, the internal spring has loosened. Recommended as a prank device' ... With all due respect, I have to say, I think this was always intended as a prank device, right?"

"I didn't expect to find this kind of mirror here, it's not what I was looking for right now, but—oh, indeed, the energy fluctuations from this mirror are very active. It's interfering with my pendulum ..."

"I was searching for this rare magic mirror a few years ago. Its principles are still unpublished, all the books I've found are vague about it. I tried to contact several people claiming to be able to craft magic mirrors by hand, but none of them could explain it clearly. In some old manuscripts, its usage and effects are very intriguing: it needs to be hung at a height half a head taller than the user, on a wall without metal components, for three days to take effect. Once active, its lower half is just like any ordinary mirror, without any mystical properties, but once you're about to act against your will, the upper half of the mirror will reflect your back while the lower half becomes blank."

"That means you can't face your own heart."

"I don't think I want to buy this mirror. I'm no longer fascinated by it, but I'm not sure ... Actually, I think the mirror itself could answer this question. But I guess there's no return policy here, huh? Can I sell it to a thrift store? Well, that's one way to deal with it ..."

"Oh ... Thank you, kind stranger, and your neighbor. I'll remember your advice, but I'm buying this because I'm a novice knife maker: parachute cords are a good material for handles. Sigh, perhaps I'm as clueless at the forge as I am in the wild—just an amateur. I've never heard of used parachute cords being problematic. Though a few small flaws probably won't affect the grip of the handle. Wrapping the handle with cord is already hard enough, honestly, but it's better than nothing. Think about it, if I'm hanging off a cliff, having a cord that might break is better than having nothing at all ..."

I made some coffee for these clever eggheads—enough to mend their broken souls after turning their backs on it for half their lives.
Fancy a cuppa as well? Here you go!
Regulus, it's a violation of their Scripture. We mustn't consume any beans or <nobr>bean-based</nobr> products.
Yeah, yeah, the great, sacred Scripture again! Hey! Think you can just walk away from a pirate without breaking any rules? Let's see you try!
Hah! Now you must have the beans! Or- Or- you can pick them all up!
According to their rules, I'm not to eat things off the ground... Or pick them up for that matter. Though, this mountain of beans isn't going away by itself.
Fortunately, it doesn't appear to be too stable.
An illusion of a coffee bean mountain like this is almost as cliché as a pirate with a hook for a hand.
*Soft chuckles* something like this could never hold up to skepticism.
Mankind is slow in learning new ideas.
They need new information to be explained in simple terms, using examples and analogies, or reduced to its most basic symbols and generalizations.
Eventually, once they've gotten use to the formulas and outlines,
They may just see below the surface and find the deeper essence waiting there.
What about you? What do you think is your essence?
Are you any more significant than a pile of coffee beans?
Certainly, darling. In a way, we are all a reflection of our pasts.
But is who we are a measure of our decisions, or have our decisions been decided for us long before the moment happens?
We are led by our senses, as they in turn are led by our experiences, like puppets on a string —our mind and soul can scarcely weigh in.
Do people decide to put milk and sugar in their coffee for the taste?
Or is it bitterness, that sharp sense on the tongue, that tells them it must be sweetened?
Do they even like coffee; or is it a memory of needing it to make it through the day?
Each decision we make coming from a tug on our hidden strings, strings we cannot begin to grasp for ourselves.
Only by taking out these saccharine sweeteners can we know what we're really drinking.
Ah, the mind, the soul ... But do they really exist?
A thirsty animal thinks of water and seeks out a clear spring, hunger pangs tell the cheetah to seek its prey, the fear of isolation tells the flamingo to seek the safety of her flock.
Every action we have ever taken was prompted by a natural impulse, sparks of electric current that can be tracked, observed ... predicted.
Perhaps our thoughts, desires, and our minds are only the sum of these minute reactions of cause and effect.
Perhaps none of us truly exist, darling.
We're still in a meeting. You'll have to leave from the left.
But I came in from the left. Why would I leave the same way I came in?
Oh, no. You've made a mistake! Now you must stay behind bars until you prove the four-color theorem.
Be careful not to make another mistake! Or you'll be thrown into the Gorgon Current and confined there forever.
You looked worried. Don't be! We're friends, I will defend you in court.
I will try my best to reduce your sentence to "trisecting angles with an unmarked straight edge and a compass".
I have to leave ... but not from the right. There must be a way to reverse left and right.
Mm. So then left or right can be reversed as easily as changing your frame of reference ... How can we hold people responsible for their actions when we use such malleable definitions?
We lead our lives according to these strict rules. Rules that are always changing definitions ... It's too much for this old brain of mine.
Why not simplify our definitions. To learn about the world like we were kids once more.
Let's begin with math. Could it be as mutable as left and right?
Could there be a hidden integer between 3 and 4? Is one always one, or is it just our frame of reference?
But where is it then, this <nobr>ever-lasting</nobr> truth?
Have you ever seen it, have you basked in its radiance before?
Maybe the shadows on the cave wall are our true reality. Maybe the sun is just another prop in our shadow theater?
What if the people who chose to stay in the cave were the ones who were truly wise?
Be careful with what you hold to be true, darling.
Then what? Then math itself might just as easily be toppled.
But if so, then the argument that toppled math might itself crumble, like so many coffee beans.
Whenever a doubt is raised, it too must be open to skepticism.
And so doubt follows doubt tumbling down ...
Once set in motion, you cannot escape total collapse, except to give in and find something to believe.
Timekeeper, are you leaving the banquet?
Perhaps we might go somewhere quiet, I wanted to speak with you about linear regression?
Terribly sorry, Sonetto. I really must be leaving.
Wait, perhaps a more impromptu debate? I have some fresh ideas about our past discussions, could I trouble you to help me refine them?
The "Storm" is gone. We have time to enjoy life again. You don't have to keep checking your watch or your task list anymore.
But time still is against us. And I haven't any left to spare, not even to explain myself to Sonetto.
I hate to be rude, but I need a moment of peace... If only I could turn everything silent ...
I said if you are going to stick to your plan, then you must value your time wisely. Don't get caught up in idle conversation.
Be firm in your determination, but careful not to go too far.
Otherwise your silence may be taken as a slight.
And should they retaliate, what then? That's no peace, but a silent war.
And peace will not return until one side concedes ... even if they are blameless ... Doesn't that seem unfair?
"There's no other way." Ah, how decisive young people can be.
You don't stop to ask who ought to take the blame. Or if it is right that the innocent concede to the guilty. You only want peace, and damned be the costs.
We can only hope that your snap judgements will always choose the right side, darling.
Well, well, you've already mastered your most powerful weapon.
I did warn you I'd retaliate in the same manner.
I thought you had disappeared completely. I was hoping I might talk to you about my number.
So sorry, but I really do have to leave now.

I got a very cute stuffed animal for Christmas once when I was five years old, I think. Oh, if I remember correctly, there should be an old photo! I was sitting next to the Christmas tree with snowflakes on my head and a big grin on my face. Next to me was a particularly well-behaved little bear with a tail longer than any other teddy bear's. It was incredibly cute and I took it with me wherever I went.

On every sleepless, hungry night, on every night my parents fought, on every night when the cold was unbearable, I'd hug it tightly because it was so warm and soft. As long as I could hold it, everything didn't seem so bad. It was so important to me; I always thought it was my first and last friend.

Until the day my mom held my hand and led me, nervous and fidgety, through the doors of the Velvet Restaurant.

It was then that I realized I might have something just as important as the bear in my arms—a delicious cake, a soft, thick blanket, a home that sheltered me from the wind and rain.

Today is the eighth Christmas of my life, and unlike past years, I received another carefully prepared Christmas gift. Even though I know that the bow on the wrapping paper wasn't tied by the big guy himself, I'm still very happy! He gave me a blue scarf, saying it matched the color of my eyes. Considering how pretty the scarf is, I'm willing to forgive his cluelessness in not knowing blue from green. But who asks someone what they want for Christmas next year? No sense of romance at all.

Of course, I already know what I want for next Christmas! A bigger, warmer home that can fit a bigger family, one that's even bigger than Haight Street!

"The most important thing is that I can see dozens of myself on it at the same time," the interviewee said.

The turmoil of the real world has left the hearts of the younger generation scarred and battered. They wander, seeking a refuge for their souls, only to be torn apart by the harshness of war and the vast chasm created by economic prosperity. Lost and uncertain, they pause, turn inward, and begin to focus on the self.

Fortunately, this turmoil has brought about a diverse fusion of spiritual cultures. People are drawn to each other, gathering together and finding a way to sit down again. They follow their beliefs, sharing both their inner peace and their pain, temporarily forgetting the shadows cast by material civilization. In a return to nature that is both free and innocent, they embrace equality and love. They know how to listen, are open to acceptance, and so ideas from all over the world merge and intersect, leading to a flourishing of new movements. The New Age movement has become a haven for the release of pain and confusion.

Surrounded by a circle of short white candles, Mercuria gently touches the astrolabe, listening to the stars twinkle beneath the rousing synthesizer music. Lights flicker on the stage as passionate young people expend their overflowing energy with abandon.

"You're up next! Sweetheart, do you know what they call you? Miss Heaven! Hah!"

Mercuria snuffs out the candle flame, stands up, and the crowd below fervently chants her name.

"Because this is a night worth looking forward to," she says, stepping into the roar of the crowd.

"Sara."

The gathered energy surges through the air. It is known as the Matron of the Orphanage.

"Sara!"

I forgot—it can't see me like this, so I have to...

"I'm here." I said, opening my mouth, and my eyes. I see the dust, visible in the light peeking through the crack of the door, then, the darkness, and high on the wall was a skylight, and the stars outside were dense and bright.

"Sara? Sara?"

The Matron's footsteps grow more hurried as she walks down the long corridor, up the cold, splintered metal stairs, and walks across the moldy, dusty floor. I leave the hard, uneven cement ground, brush off the particles clinging to my skin and clothes, turn the cold iron handle, and listen to the sharp, grating sound of the rusty lock.

"You're here." The Matron saw me, her eyebrows raised, pupils round, lips slightly parted. After a brief moment of shock, she quickly approaches me. She pulls me into her arms, wrapping me in her embrace, and I feel her warmth through the rough fabric she wears.

"This is not two worlds," she says.

"This is not two worlds," I repeat.

I gently stroke the Matron's waist, the place where her energy is strongest.

"Oh, my child ... you don't understand." She pulls away to look into my eyes, her eyebrows furrowed, her gaze slightly distorted, and her lips pressed together under lumps of lipstick—her energy is tense, which means she's not feeling well.

So I hug her too, wrapping my arms around her, letting her feel my warmth.

"Am I right?" I ask. "Am I in your world now?"

"No ... do you still remember what I taught you? You have to layer what you feel over the world you see."

The Matron's eyes still hold tears, her lips turned down in an expression of sadness and pain, but I don't answer her, because I see her energy is no longer tense, but full and saturated, like branches drenched in water.

I think I've found the secret to balance.

*Munching noises* I could live off of burritos forever! I love this city, San Francisco.

Didn't you mention that J's shop had changed owners? What was their name again? Lyle? Leslie?
Legers. Haight Street has seen some rapid changes lately.

Tap here to see the graffiti wall.

By the late 1960s, people were desperate to escape from the chaos of rampant inflation, wars, and scandals like Watergate. With the lyrics "Don't rock the boat" from Rock the Boat as their mantra, they decided to step off the turbulent flagship and instead ride the carefree waves of disco.

In 1977, Saturday Night Fever hit the big screen, and it electrified the City of Tomorrow along the coast. Boys threw on bright floral shirts and pointed shoes, while girls dazzled in sparkly wrap dresses or bell-bottom pants with off-the-shoulder tops. Hand in hand, they flooded the streets, all heading for the nearest disco halls.

But in 1979, die-hard rock fans launched an open attack on disco culture, leading to a notorious event—Disco Demolition Night.

Firecrackers were tossed into crates filled with vinyl records, blowing them to pieces. This 98-cent "War on Disco" ended with a decisive victory for the traditionalists. Disco, which had ruled since the late '60s, quietly faded from the mainstream under the rise of a new wave music.

But now, as we enter the final decade of the 20th century, there's a growing feeling among die-hard fans—Disco, with its undeniable energy, is making an unexpected comeback.

Whether it's house, techno, or hip-hop, it's all just disco in a new form, with a new name and a new look, spinning once again under the disco ball.

We once approached it with hope, anticipation, and a bit of caution. But now, my friends, I can't wait any longer—I'm kicking off my shoes and heading straight for the dance floor.

The good stuff is back!
From the Introduction of the Hongzhi Clinic Ledger

My name is Bruce Liu, an ordinary, unlicensed street doctor on Haight Street, hailing from an ancient Eastern land. If all goes well, I'll stay on this street until the day I can return home and reunite with my wife.

In the '80s, through skill, hard work, and sheer will to survive, we new immigrants managed to establish ourselves in this land. A few ambitious ones formed gangs, carving out new territories with nothing but our determination. They commanded respect from both sides of the law in San Francisco, but in doing so, they only deepened the poverty, isolation, and discrimination faced by the rest of our community.

As for me, a modest practitioner who played by the rules most of his life, I found myself learning the family traditions of the Italians, witnessing the extreme measures of the Brotherhood, offering good tea to corrupt cops collecting protection fees, and even picking shrapnel out of a tattooed kid's head. It made me realize—this wasn't the life I wanted.

I didn't choose Haight Street for any special reason, except that it reminded me of how people used to view Chinatown at the turn of the century—back when the elders referred to this vibrant city as "Dai Fau," or "Da Bu," meaning "The Great Port." Back then, the poor stood united and new immigrants had each other's backs. Oh, how I miss those days!

Another fellow on this street, Tang Ji, is a great example. He runs a decent restaurant here, looking after a group of "wayward" kids. One of them, a little guy named J, has become a regular of mine—first it was the back of his head, then his arm, and yesterday, his leg ... Don't get me started. Young hotheads think they're "superheroes," but in our culture, we call them "reckless fools."

Let me be clear: Bruce Liu isn't the kind of doctor you'd call a "benevolent healer." But if I'm going to keep running Hongzhi Clinic, I need to set some rules—no dealing with major troublemakers who cause harm to others, and no getting involved with gangs that send young men to their deaths for nothing.

Since the rise of the New Age movement, energy healing has become a hot topic. Despite my efforts in consulting experts and researching extensively, I still couldn't grasp the most fundamental, core question—what exactly is cosmic energy, and how does it heal us?

Therefore, I'd like to share three real-life experiences with you, dear readers.

The first time, I followed the guidelines of a popular bestseller and went to the outskirts of the city, to a valley during a full moon, where I meditated in what was supposed to be a "place of energy convergence." I almost got caught by a strange roadside shaman who tried to forcefully sell me meaningless talismans and bizarre witch doctor trinkets.

The second time, I was coerced into attending a two-week healing course on a method called "Ho'oponopono," a self-healing technique. The master claimed it could "erase the memory of the disease and deceive your symptoms ..." In the end, I gained nothing and couldn't even "erase" the painful memory of the exorbitant enrollment fee.

The third time, just as I was about to equate energy healing with mere quackery and gather evidence to conclusively label it a scam, I wandered into a tent at a market in the countryside.

A young dancer, without saying a word, was arranging a circle on the ground with candles, crystals, and some flowers and herbs. Just as I was about to leave, I heard a voice behind me: "You are lost."

"What do you mean?" I stopped in my tracks.

"Come here," she said, picking up a stone that glowed with a blue light, without further explanation.

I found myself irresistibly drawn to it, like someone who instinctively stops to gaze at the moon.

A faint vibration touched my sensitive nerves—not from the stone or anything visible, but from something far more distant, more vast, a resonance that was beyond description.

"You felt the vibrations. They're beautiful, aren't they?" Her voice seemed distant.

The heaviness and confusion in my heart began to dissipate, and a clearer understanding slowly took shape.

What is cosmic energy? It's not some miraculous force, but rather the most fundamental law of the universe—all things are made of particles, and all things vibrate.

How does it heal us? A true healer can harness the "vibrations" of cosmic energy to resonate with and enhance a person's inherent energy.

Finally, this article contains no suggestions or instructions. Consumers and healing enthusiasts are urged to consider carefully and discern wisely.

Thank you all for reading.

Charming San Francisco: Welcome and Farewell

If you've crossed the ocean to come here in this era, the first stop I recommend is the Transamerica Pyramid. From the highest point in San Francisco, you'll look down on a city that has withstood the test of time.

From the Gold Rush of the 19th century that brought people, energy, and endless possibilities to California, to the tech boom a century later in the vast Santa Clara Valley to the south, San Francisco has weathered the waves of history and still stands proudly on the West Coast.

This city, like a battle-hardened veteran, has survived countless trials—from the great San Andreas Fault earthquake of 1906 to the Loma Prieta quake of 1989, along with the ongoing power struggles and conflicts between law and order that have played out throughout its history.

Clearly, nothing can dampen this City of Tomorrow's passionate and singular pursuit of "Lady Liberty." Just as there are young people lining up all night at Ocean Beach to ride the Tilt-A-Whirl, there's also that ever-enduring golden ballroom, a relic that will never close.

Though there are the occasional unpleasant episodes, and you may feel a bit of a lull in the brief silence after the music stops, you know there's always somewhere to go on a lonely night, and this city will always welcome you.

On the other hand, it also reminds me of the funny, charming uncle from the movies. When the story reaches its climax and you're facing the choice between reality and dreams in the dark night of the soul, and everyone around you thinks you've lost it, he suddenly leans out from his worn, joke-filled couch and says, "Go for it, kid, I got your back."

You start to remember the toys he bought you as a child, the streets and bays he showed you, and how you once saw him as a comrade-in-arms, dreaming together of a great adventure in search of gold. Now, he's raising his hands to cheer you on, and throwing the biggest farewell party for your dream-chasing journey.

Friends, your best Uncle Francisco welcomes you, whether you're coming or going.

September 27, 1990, Clear Skies

    ...

    Those damn Zeno people, these had better be the last ones—Ken says the factory's almost empty.

   One month, one whole month. I'll finally be able to get a full night's sleep. Their noise has been louder than a herd of cattle begging to be let out of the pen.

    ...

    Lately, there seem to be a few more robed figures around town. Sure, some of the folks under those robes are our people—but there are also a few unfamiliar faces among them. The old guys are all huddled up in the pub praying, but the new faces are always on the move ... I should ask Ken, that old guy—he is practically no different from their most devout believers now, maybe he knows something. That stuff about Zeno, he must've heard about 'em from the black robes.

    There's been a lot of people saying "yes" to wearing the black robes lately. I caught Robert at the pub today—his lips haven't said "yes" yet, but there he was, boozing it up with them.

    ...

A conversation behind closed doors:

    "Cough ... Have you seen the youngest Smiths' girl lately?"

    "She's probably been hanging out at the bar these days. Didn't I tell you? The Smiths are all into that Order of Enlightenment stuff now, and they're pretty fanatical about it, too ..."

    "I couldn't care less about all that drama of theirs. Just saw a girl pass by who kinda looked like her."

    "I bet you caught a glimpse of something through the keyhole again. What's the scoop? Spill it."

    "Some weirdo thought he could mess around on Chisos's watch. I was about to open the door when he bolted ... The girl just kept walking minding her own business, and then that's when I saw—she had more than one shadow following her, just stretching out from nowhere ... Damn it, my eyes must've been tricking me."

    "You're talking about—'The Protected'? Right out my front door? Move over, I gotta see this ... Oh, she's gone. Guess I'm gonna hit the bar tonight and snoop around, I ... I can't believe this! 'The Protected'—right outside my front door."

The figure seen through the peephole is Ken, an earnest old friend.

    "Ha! How's that for a taste?" Ken enters with a hearty laugh, while the homeowner mutters and slumps back onto the couch.

    Ken sits down on the other side. "Don't look at me with those eyes, old friend, and put your gun away. You're just showing how scared you really are ... What am I here for? Ah, I thought you'd have figured that out by now."

    "I've just come to give you some advice," Ken says.

    "You remember, not long ago the same thing happened to me. I was looking through the peephole, not even a shadow ... I opened the door, and there was just a half-eaten apple covered in dust on the porch, my loaded bullets would've been useless."

    "I know you're wary of outsiders, but ever since I prayed for "The Sufferer," those strange occurrences haven't bothered me again. There's been plenty of weird things lately, heard you saw 'The Protected' with your own eyes yesterday? She is indeed the Smiths' little girl, fortunately, she's always been a devout little girl."

    Ken pulls out a sticky note, scribbles a few words, and hands it over. "You should at least trust your own eyes. Think it over, old friend."

—Contents of the Sticky Note— Four months Three months and twenty-one days ago, the streetlight went out. Robert climbed up to check and reported that the filament was broken. It's back on. Just a few days ago ... or was it three days, or four days ago? Hasty scribbles: 9/30/1990 20:11 - Flickers. A believer, unrobed, familiar face. Headed to the tavern. 22:47 - The streetlight came on, 3 believers (2 in black robes, 1 without) returned from the tavern. I heard the sound of a fierce wind, but the corners of their robes didn't move. 22:50 - Robert's figure flashed by the entrance window—I bet he's also peering out through the peephole. D**n it. It's been 3 minutes, and the light's still on. 23:01 - The light flickered a few times, and finally went out! Before it went out, I saw a believer (in black robes, resembling John) returning from the tavern. That way leads to John's house. When did he start wearing the robes? —Words scratched out on the back of the note— The Sufferer is engulfed in darkness, yet protects us still

Soft, hurried mumbling:

    "No ... no way. I'm not falling for those weird stories. Shadows ... just my eyes playing tricks on me, nobody else saw anything. That lamp ... nobody's changed the bulb, but it's still plugged in, so a little light now and then isn't too weird. What's up with Robert spying through his peephole? He never bothers to close his curtains, making himself completely visible to anyone passing by. He's been drinking a lot with those robed people—just what is he hesitating about?"

    "That noon sun, it really burns the eyes."

    "The clock's striking, is it twelve o'clock? My goodness. I've been here watching for two or three hours since I checked that filament ... Wait, is that fog?"

    "Oh—no, no, what on earth is that?"

    ...

    "Is that Ken? It has to be Ken! I want to join your prayer tonight, you told me there'd be one ... I think, oh, is Robert coming too? Okay, that's fine ..."

One anonymous reader compiled 23 different urban sewer predator legends she picked up during her travels and asked when I was going to write about "The Country Witch Who Turned Into a Hare." She fondly recalled how her grandmother's amusing witch stories, tinged with a touch of gentle fright, would lull her to sleep as a child.

I'd like to extend my heartfelt thanks to this reader—these contributions are invaluable to my writing, and I'll soon delve into these childhood tales. Stories of mysterious transformative arcane skills are truly captivating, and their prevalence might be more widespread than I initially thought.

As we continue with the last issue's theme, sewer legends intertwine with conspiracy theories. For example, in a tape sent in by a Mr. K from New York City, a relative of his staunchly believes that the government secretly hired a team to feed albino fish living in the sewers. February 5th

Well, ain't that odd? Pierce came back early this morning, scared out of his mind. I had never seen the kid so freaked out. He sped through town and only slammed on the brakes when he got to the front door, as if something was chasing him. That nut almost ran over Marita's little bulldog!

Only God knows what he ran into.

February 15th

The birds were chirping the whole night long. I had never seen so many of them gathered together. Oh boy, they were so noisy; I barely slept a wink.

Ruth was scared, she thought it was some kind of omen. What a joke.

Those long-beaked birdies weren't afraid of shotguns, that's for sure. I fired a shot at them, but only a few got spooked enough to fly away.

Father Morgan suggested hiring a "bird control team"—if such a thing exists in the big city, that is. But I still think we should assemble all the gun users in the town and kill all those birds once and for all, rather than scare them off.

March 27th

Had a nightmare, a very vivid one, though I can't for the life of me remember what it was all about now.

Ruth woke up scared too; I comforted her. It was just a nightmare, nothing more.

March 30th

Pierce didn't come back from Houston, but the police sure did. They said Pierce's employer in Houston reported him missing, thinking he ran off with their money.

I wouldn't put it past that sly fox.

April 10th

All night long, the birds were making that racket again. When I pulled back the curtains in the morning, I thought I was still dreaming, but it was real. There were so many birds they were blocking out the sun.

It was like a waking nightmare.

April 12th

The birds scattered.

Everyone looked kind of strange. It had been ages since I saw Marita walking her dog, and Ruth started bawling over the most trivial things. It's unnerving.

April 17th

Johnny's back in town, looking like his soul got swallowed up by the devil. I saw him running, screaming like a madman, then he just collapsed on the lawn all of a sudden, crying and begging for something to spare him.

Father Morgan came, but he had this strange look about him.

I heard what Johnny was saying. He was mumbling on and on about a "motel."

May 13th

I talked to a realtor. Yeah, it's come to that—I'm finally thinking about moving.

Why? I don't know. I guess you could call it a ... gut feeling? Maybe my mind can be eased a bit somewhere new.

Methods Through the aid of voluntary donations, the research team extracted a nucleus from a female arcanist (Genetic Mother A) and an enucleated egg cell from a female human (Genetic Mother B). The nucleus was cultivated and processed to enhance its receptivity to new genetic instructions. After injecting the donor cell nucleus into the enucleated egg cell, an electric pulse was used to fuse the nucleus with the egg cytoplasm, initiating cell division and forming embryonic cells. During this process, the ratio of arcanist to human genetic material was adjusted to be nearly equal. In Experiment No. 277, the embryo developed well, meeting the criteria for transplantation, and was implanted into the uterus of a Finn-Dorset ewe after formation. Observations 0 Months Old The subject was born through natural delivery, with 60.05% arcanist genetic material and 39.95% human genetic material, not achieving the expected complete balance, but still proving that the adult somatic cells of an arcanist can be programmed and adjusted through cloning technology. In appearance, the subject exhibits characteristics of both Genetic Mothers A and B; simultaneously, for unknown reasons, its head is highly similar to that of a Finn-Dorset, but brain development has not been affected. 2 Months Old The subject's development is slower than that of contemporary human and arcanist infants. Mild symptoms of lung infection have been found. 4 Months Old The subject's development is slower than that of contemporary human and arcanist infants, but it showed significant responses to music and human language, with consistent reactions to specific sounds. The cause of the lung infection was identified; the subject's lungs tested positive for the JSRV retrovirus, commonly found in sheep living indoors for extended periods. It was suggested that a veterinary team be brought in for consultation. 6 Months Old The subject's physical development is slower than that of contemporary human and arcanist infants, and may stop developing prematurely. Sterile room staff reported that the subject began consciously mimicking communication behaviors, as expected. Educational classes and moral guidance videotapes were initiated. The lung infection worsened, and the subject showed a strong allergic reaction to chemical fiber products. ... 10 Months Old The subject can engage in rudimentary communication, exhibiting good brain development. Multiple tests have confirmed that American country music is effective in alleviating the subject's allergic reactions, the cause of which is yet to be determined. ... 22 Months Old The subject performed excellently in communication and intelligence tests, possessing the intelligence level of a 7-year-old human child. 23 Months Old Bone tests indicated that the subject's physical development will cease completely by the age of 12.

"Who's that? Close the door behind you, old sport ... Huh? Webber, why are you back here? Haven't you enlisted yet? Those vermin are bombing the town and all the farms every day—we're all counting on you ...
—An old man who calls the motel home

"Night after night, a scratching sound scrapes across the walls of the first floor... Could it be the clawing nails of decaying zombies, begging for sustenance? Hahaha... At least it's not the debt collectors."
Local tortilla chips/Cream cheese/Mexican burritos/Whole wheat tortillas/Salted oatmeal ...
"Relax, it's all fake. A Viking would never be scared of such a silly trick ... Quit pulling my blanket!"

"First, gently tap with the back of the knife before cutting against the grain. That's the secret to properly handling meat... but this mediocre motel lacks any quality ingredients! Why on earth did they even hire me in the first place?!"
"Thirty-two bucks for a bottle of mineral water—talk about throwing your money down the drain. The thought of guzzling down that much cash every day makes my stomach churn ... Burp."
"We've received a large number of complaints about extortionate prices at a motel in Austin ... but it's in the middle of nowhere. Do you even realize how much gas it'd take to get there?"
"These charges are totally uncool, man! Every store should pay a welcoming fee to this legendary pirate captain, and provide me with all their services, free of charge!"
"I penned my magnum opus in this motel room, a masterpiece collection of poetry, but those heartless critics tore it apart ...  Ah, is it already time to pay for another night here?!"
"I've always regretted not returning this poetry collection to that guest before he checked out, but thanks to this anthology, I've become a published writer and I'm doing quite well for myself now."
"Hey, stop reading that crappy article! Let's have a 50-mile race instead!"
"If you add a dark reed pipe to the first-floor corridor, stepping on it will cause all the lights on the second floor to go out! This place is like a haunted Rube Goldberg machine!"
—A clever man with a questionable mind.
"Blonney, reckless and dumb, a typical Blondie. Always indulging herself in alcohol, beautiful clothes, and other vain pleasures."
"The pure entertainment brought by 'formulaic' approaches cannot be ignored. However, we must also consider the limitations they impose on the artistic integrity of cinema."
"Blonde girls, always standing out at school, always the talk of their classmates, known for throwing wild parties, drinking and smoking in their rooms ... Blonde girls are bad."
"Oh! What a captivating and endearing heroine!"
"Mom told me that once I break out of my cocoon, I can go find her. Today is the 365th day since she left me."
"Stay—we've got the comfiest bed, plenty of honey, and all the fruit you could ever desire. We can live together forever."
"Some people spend their lives in a cocoon. When they finally break out, they may feel like a vulnerable prey, watched by circling vultures."
"Follow the plan, just follow the plan ... One hour and five minutes to go."
"Mom, look at the huge bubble I blew! Um, Mom? Why are you floating away from me?"
"Parties are a scam—a tribute to rampant alcoholism and a complete nightmare for cleaners. Oh my God ... who threw up on the stereos again?!"

"We're all for people holding lawful parades in public places to voice legitimate demands. Just submit an application in advance, refrain from disturbing the peace, and never use arcane skills under any circumstances."

"Parties, as a form of entertainment, possess a certain duality. They often serve to relieve stress and have a regulatory role in society, but indulging in a life of constant partying can be a slippery slope—one party too many, and you may find yourself trapped in a vapid existence of empty pleasures."
"The fragments of the phenomenal world may seem insignificant, but they contribute to poor sanitation ... A schedule for cleaning the beach needs to be arranged."
"Hand, gun, handgun! Pick it up, squeeze the trigger. Bang, bang, bang! Hero, hero ... not enough bullets ..."

Irrational numbers are a set of chaotic and disorderly numbers that must be disciplined by the pursuit of truth, in order to approach the realm of rational numbers. They should not distract the wise from their search for truth.
"Tools are neither good nor bad—they are the embodiment of human wisdom. As long as they are simple and efficient, they bring about order and facts."

"I've lost count of how many times I've told Mom—I hate math! All I want is to learn how to paint or play the piano, to be an artist. But she insists that I finish today's calculus homework before anything else."
"I don't really get science and wrenches and what have you, but I do believe we should celebrate the beauty of peace and love. Sir, how would you like to buy a nice bouquet?"
"Isn't math just brilliant? It allows us to build enormous jet rockets and launch them into the sky—into the vastness of the universe! Bang! Zoom! Whoosh!"
"I-I think that giving it your all is the very best you can do. So please ... don't give up too easily!"
"Be it the Tower of Babel or the Leaning Tower of Pisa, towers are the product of our hard work, built one bucket of soil and one beam at a time ... and no one can argue otherwise!"
"Rules are essential. Everyone should follow the rules, yes ... What? I can't smoke here? Well, I don't see no sign or anything!"
"Hi there, take a flyer, please. Huh? No, I don't know what's written on it, and I'm only paid 5 cents a day. So, you want a flyer or not?"
"You should do whatever you want, even if it's just running down the street! If you wanna do it, just do it!"
"What is art? Art is the expression of ideas, art is a party everyone can join! United, we must rise up and 'take over' public squares, streets, and even police stations!"
How can we elucidate the world of art to the masses? The answer is simple—it's impossible.
"Art? Listen, kid, before you worry about that, make sure you fill your empty stomach. Art can wait."
"I don't know all that much and I certainly don't understand art, but the guests who taught me to read seemed educated enough and treated us real good ... so I think art must be a good thing."
"Unexpected, romantic encounters? Don't get your hopes up. They're more likely to turn your best-laid plans into a mess and leave you with nothing but chaos."

"Sure, gossips and secrets are intriguing, but don't be fooled by the glitz and glamor on the screen—behind it, it's not as thrilling as you might think ... I would rather have never been granted this 'blessing'!"
—From the other side of the screen
"Never take the bus. It follows a set route, you see, passing through pre-planned stops. Those eyes hiding in the grass will gobble you up the moment you get off!"
"On March 11, a motel in Austin reportedly experienced a gas leak, leading to a fire that destroyed the building. Local police have launched an investigation into the matter."

"Boletes, white mushrooms, milk caps ... there are so many kinds of mushrooms in the world waiting to be discovered. It could take you a lifetime to find them all, but unlike animals, mushrooms will always stay there, waiting for us."
"Never stay out in the open wilderness. Never expose yourself. Never make a single sound ... The dense trees in the forest are your best protection and disguise."
"A bedtime story? Honestly, I-I'm not sure ... Before the story even begins, I always ... zzz ... zzz ..."
"N-No! I don't wanna sleep! I wanna hear more stories ... Why does Mommy always fall asleep first?"

People are born here. They die here.

Texas is one wide open space. The plains stretch on forever, offering up their thick black soil to the crops and their vast pastures to the cattle. The air is dry, and the days are long and hot. Summer storms and tornadoes are frequent visitors to the ranch—visitors who leave as quickly as they come. The people here create history and have established a proud way of life, regardless of the changes in the outside world.

They're independent, tough, and rugged. They're used to hard work, to gathering around the barbecue grill, to <nobr>hand-rolled</nobr> smokes, and shotguns. They're used to local radio news broadcasts on Friday mornings and "The Tonight Show" at eight in the evening. Highways and railways are the lifeblood of this Lone Star, pumping new trends into valleys and farms. But for those who listen to old country songs, they don't give a damn to disco, rock music, newfangled outfits, or catchy new slogans.

All these new things are annoying noise. They are completely meaningless and tasteless!

—She has always thought this way. She is a true, native Texan.

"The motel owner's daughter" is a more convenient title than "the motel owner." She uses demureness and conformity to cover up and amplify the horror. This is something she has come to master.

A jingling set of keys, no different from the ones at the waist of every motel owner.
She has memorized each key and its corresponding door in the motel, like a mother knows her own children, or perhaps even better. Sometimes, the keyholes would change position or shape, almost as if a child is playing a prank. But that won't be a problem for the mother.

Wrapped snugly in a white cotton cloth, it is silent most of the time, except for the occasional wiggle or cry.
Raising this "baby" is easy for her; she gives it all the love and affection it needs. There's no doubt that she's a qualified mother—the interviewee claims, smiling.

It has always existed.

From the haunted stables and outhouses of the Middle Ages to the <nobr>ghost-plagued</nobr> castles of Gothic literature, it constantly changed forms, waiting for more visitors—more nourishment. A ship then carried it across the ocean to the flourishing New World.

In this land, there was never a shortage of legends, both old and new. It became an abandoned manor or a cabin in the woods, joyfully devouring every visitor from the wilderness, along with their screams and cries.

The 20th century ushered in a new wave of stories. No one knew exactly where they came from—a friend of a friend, a transfer student, local oddities in the corners of newspaper. Their themes vary from cars, ovens, videotapes, sewers to cities and the impending new millennium. These tales gained their own names in modern culture: urban legends. In them, it sensed something familiar—the taste of fear and the need for fear.

And so, It quietly laid its foundations in the dim morning light, growing a simple wooden porch and a flickering sign, laying down its creaking stairs. At dawn, drivers on Route 77 suddenly noticed a motel that was a little out of date.

Now the motel needed a manager, of course.

Pandora Wilson: It seems as though, more often than not, you prefer to present yourself in the role you play. What do you think role play has to do with fear?
Tuesday: Oh, role play ain't no part of fear. It's merely laying a foundation for the stories.
Tuesday: People will write the bulk of it themselves. They give it a plot and indulge in it. My role is just a guide ... a waitress guiding her guests.
Pandora Wilson: And your motel? It's playing a role too, isn't it?
Tuesday: Actors can always use a proper stage. When people step onto it, they naturally play the roles assigned to them. It is just a stage, nothing more.
Tuesday: Like how people expect to see a simple, hardworking country girl in every farmhouse, or to see multiple rooms inside a suitcase ...

During the <nobr>mid-20th</nobr> century, advances in life sciences and biotechnology opened a new realm of possibilities. The <nobr>double-helix</nobr> was unraveled, revealing a previously hidden path—the code to deciphering life itself.

No one could resist clinging on to this hope, whether human or arcanist. The term "genetic engineering" emerged in 1973, as biologists wove and pruned the strands of DNA, allowing modified results to be inherited almost without fail. Suddenly, the challenges of the past in agriculture, medicine, and basic biological research were swept away by new solutions.

Naturally, attention returned to that classic academic subject: the mutual exclusivity of human and arcanist bloodlines. This time, at a research institute in Scotland, scientists chose to take the power of creating life into their own hands, attempting to realize a dream that never came true—to balance these two bloodlines at a 50:50 ratio in a single life form.

After going through 276 failures, the 277th experiment combined the genes of a female arcanist volunteer and a female human researcher. The embryo, formed in the lab, was then transferred to the uterus of a <nobr>Finn-Dorset</nobr> ewe.

A baby girl was born, with the eye color of her human mother, a skin tone similar to her arcanist mother, and unexpectedly—the head of a sheep, the third mother.

Her DNA ratio was a delicate balance of 60% Arcanist and 40% human. While it did not achieve the desired result, the method behind her birth was enough to attract the attention of countless academic and commercial organizations.

A new miracle of life at the end of the 20th century—that's what people called her.

Her slender limbs lack any real strength, and her development was much slower than that of her peers. On the other hand, she achieved far higher scores in intelligence test than children her age.

These two facts were not particularly surprising.

This combination of genes led to an <nobr>early-maturing</nobr> brain and incomplete physical development, a risk that was already known from the very beginning—she would experience a <nobr>much-longer-than-usual</nobr> childhood until her physical development stopped altogether.

She had ethic lessons and other academic courses tailored to her special condition. She lived in a clean, sterile room, accompanied by a portable music player.

The volunteer mother visited her regularly, the researcher mother measured her data and recorded her growth, and the ewe mother stayed by her side, lapping at her fleece and nursing her.

At night, she dreamt of a soft lawn she had only seen in books and videotapes, where her ewe mother waited for her, and they roamed through the clouds together.

Dolly, this is what grass tastes like.

Dolly, you're my sweet little lamb.

Dolly, this is simply wonderful. You must go to more places, see more lawns and more clouds, just like we saw in that dream.

Pandora Wilson: This isn't the first time you've let me interview you.
Barbara: No, ma'am. I remember the day we first met.
Pandora Wilson: And before that, you'd already been interviewed so many times. It's safe to say you're no stranger to having cameras and notebooks shoved in your face.
Barbara: Indeed, people are very interested in cloning and genetic engineering, I understand that. The institute's achievements are valuable both scientifically and commercially.
Barbara: I have a lot of visitors, and no, I don't mind it at all. They're always very polite, and seeing new faces always makes me happy.
Pandora Wilson: So, is that why you chose to join UTTU? To see new faces? I think this is something our readers would like to know.
Barbara: Oh, well, that's true to some extent. I want to learn everything I can about different people and different things, just like you did through the questions you asked me that day.
Pandora Wilson: Do you ever miss the institute?
Barbara: Yes, sometimes. I'd really like to send them some postcards ... and some grass.
Barbara: I want to show them the world, through my eyes.

[A Series of Dusks: Rhapsody of the Moon] is an expansion for [A Series of Dusks]. [Rhapsody of the Moon] builds on the base game mode, introducing new gameplay elements and increased difficulty levels, requiring you to take on an even more surreal and frenzied version of "Vienna." Suite of the Moon After loading up the new expansion, the "Suite of the Moon" feature becomes available. Before embarking on your exploration, you can visit the Suite of the Moon panel and choose from a variety of "Omen" modifiers. These modifiers add challenges to your gameplay, with each one increasing the current "Indulgence" value. The "Indulgence" value serves as an indicator for the difficulty level of your playthrough. Depending on this value, you may see changes in the appearance of the moon, with each moon phase representing a different difficulty bracket that adds even more dangerous effects to your playthrough. There are five difficulty brackets, or phases of the moon, determined by the current Indulgence value: [Misperception]: Low chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Very low chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Clear Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +20%. [Illusory Sounds]: Low chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Low chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Limited Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +20%. Enemy Control Resilience +20%. [Illusory Sight]: Moderate chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Moderate chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Reduced Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +50%. Enemy Control Resilience +30%. [Illusory Touch]: High chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. High chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Majorly obstructed Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +100%. Enemy Control Resilience +50%. [Delirium]: High chance of significantly increasing Stress at the start of the round. Guaranteed to trigger Sudden Disaster. Severely obstructed Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +200%. Enemy Control Resistance +100%. Deployed characters get a decrease in Focus Chance. After completing an exploration, you will receive Shards of Shadow. These shards can be used to unlock new Catalyst incantations, Instinct buffs, or reset the cooldowns of certain Instinct buffs. If the Indulgence value is at 0, the Suite of the Moon will become inactive and no effects from Indulgence will impact you. You will also no longer be able to obtain Shards of Shadow. As the difficulty bracket of the Suite of the Moon increases, you'll be able to activate "Instinct" effects. By tapping on the broken mirror shards surrounding the image of the moon, a variety of Instincts can be chosen. The higher the difficulty bracket, the more Instincts can be activated, and the stronger their effects will be. After activating Instincts and clearing the second area, some of the Instincts will go into cooldown. Each time you clear the second area, or each area after that, these cooldowns are reduced by one round. Alternatively, you can use Shards of Shadow to instantly refresh the cooldowns. Stress in Battle After loading up the expansion, your characters will display a Stress meter while exploring. Actions taken during exploration will affect their Stress levels, which in turn will affect their behavior on the battlefield. When a character's Stress is low, they have a chance to trigger Vigilant Behavior based on their Afflatus. When a character's Stress is high, they have a chance to trigger Disorder Behavior based on their Afflatus. When a character's Stress reaches 50, they have either a low chance of triggering Focus Behavior, or a high chance of triggering Meltdown Behavior. Enemies also have Stress levels. The higher an enemy's stress, the more dangerous they become, forcing you to stay vigilant at all times. Core Content The core content is also updated—load up the new expansion to experience the following: New Catalysts: Two new Catalysts are added—the Silver Compass and the Rationality Loupe. New Path Nodes: Four new path nodes are added—Misty Domain, Into the Unknown, Perilous Encounter, and Treasure Trove. New Catalyst Incantations: Each Catalyst now has a new Catalyst incantation that can be unlocked by using Shards of Shadow. Some of these incantations can be cast by consuming Stimulus after completing certain path nodes. New Artefacts: Exciting new artefacts are added to the game. For more details, you will need to play through the new content yourself.
