A broken hourglass that cannot be turned over. Its base is inscribed with the words, "The explorer who forges ahead has dismantled the lowest rib of the starry sky and opened Its belly to millions."

A magazine brimming with Sharpodonties. In this tight space, the teeth on the coins gnaw at each other, creating an unbearable noise. Proof that there is truth in the expression "more money, more problems."

An effective life insurance policy with your name listed as the beneficiary. Although the exemptions and disclaimers seem to go on forever, as long as your goals align with the policy, enforcing these clauses won't be too difficult.
A replica of the Rosetta Stone. The three languages inscribed on it serve as a reminder that transient phenomena can never alter the essence of truth.

An effective property insurance policy with your name listed as the beneficiary. Although the exemptions and disclaimers seem to go on forever, as long as your goals align with the insurance, these clauses merely serve as a checklist for property preservation.

An invaluable treasure, with a faint song echoing within its shell. Crafted from gold and silver and inlaid with jewels, it was gifted to a pure maiden. But for her, gifts and rewards have never been necessary.
A locked nut, where the lock's significance outweighs its form. The seed's imprisonment began the moment it ripened but failed to descend into the soil.
A model ship gifted by an elderly gentleman. Even the fiercest storms and most colossal waves couldn't shake the mast of this vessel—just as nothing could rattle the gentleman's backbone.

A discarded compass. Initially, it exhibited only a minor deviation and still served as a reliable substitute for the North Star, but soon, a creeping moss overcame it, filling every crevice save for the needle.

A meticulously stuffed snake skin with dried petals and sharp thorns firmly embedded into its body. After changing hands several times, it started selecting more intelligent masters—for, upon holding it, only the wise would understand that it sees its master as an enemy.

An astonishingly effective beauty product that is still within the effective duration of its incantation. "The key to beauty lies within"—this tagline helped it win the hearts of more than half the ladies in town.
A smooth piece of amber that has swallowed a butterfly. Its wings are stuck together, still standing on its shriveled cocoon. Two simultaneous misfortunes befell this burgeoning life.
A fiercely burning mushroom. It tries to burn up everything that stands between it and survival, but there are far too many of these obstacles in its homeland.
When at a loss in battle, use your body heat to quickly incubate this egg. Yes, your enemies will ridicule you for doing so, but when the bird hatches, you will have the last laugh.
The left and right gloves have finally found each other. Overtaken by the joy of their reunion, they are now eager to share their luck with you.

A pipe that a drunken worker mistook for a plumbing part and fitted with a valve. Now, it is a phenomenal bestseller, allowing every gentleman to elegantly loosen the valve and take a deep puff—"I've never felt so full of life!"
A feather-light brooch. Its maker embedded its golden opening with tiny gems. Her movements were slow and gentle, like a devout believer returning a holy relic to its box.

This pendant of a rigid floating aircraft in flight is unsuitable for wearing. As a result, it has been hanging beneath the eaves for years, accumulating a wealth of flight experience in the local area. It is especially adept at dealing with afternoon air currents and avoiding the rain.
A hand that leads the lost back to a familiar road. They say that a man encountered it after being shipwrecked, and it led him straight across the channel. Since then, it has become a little rusty.
A custom and exquisitely made notebook from Hungary. Its cover has been worn over time. Inside are a variety of Ritual Disks, which have undoubtedly seen many battles.
A small box filled with replicas of the crests and seals of various reputable families. For those in the know, there are countless ways to maximize the value of this little box.

A projector presenting a pure and unreal dream. Through the lens, you glimpse her smiling between those doors at the edge of reality. The colors melt, merge, and surround you, lifting you higher and higher until you reach the final scene.

One of Laplace's great technological achievements, reconstructed by a boy genius. It is usually used to realize his whimsical ideas, but in special cases, it can also serve as a temporary lighting tool.

A forked weapon made from the antlers of two constantly fighting deer-shaped critters. Even after being made into a weapon, they haven't forgotten their intense rivalry—if one side hits the enemy in battle, the other side will risk breakage just to strike it itself.
If you encounter a lizard at a streetside café, don't worry—it probably belongs to a fashionable Viennese citizen who accidentally left it there. It won't pose any danger.
An arcanist once recorded the visions they observed in a realm and forged them into this armillary sphere. It was later used for astrology, divination, and even self-defense.

Go ahead and throw it at your enemies whenever you desire. The sharp thorns will make them run for their lives, and as the messenger of a certain explorer who forged ahead, its endless ramblings will probably annoy your enemies to death too.

Shimmerwings are completely invisible by the time they mature and are extremely difficult to catch without the use of optical arcane skills. In order to meet the unique preferences of Viennese nobles, they are sometimes colored with gold leaf.

This scarab lay dormant in an Egyptian elder's tomb for thousands of years. To this creature, the night is like sweet spring water. If you wear black clothes and pick it up, you will become its next master.
A group of tin soldiers ready to charge into battle. They train and rally, eager to contribute, united and brave, and terrified upon seeing the sacrifice of their allies.

Arcanists are occasionally known to make fake pendulums to sell to the uninformed—"Gaze at it, accept it, embrace it," they cry, "it will take you to the promised land!"—in reality, they are knick-knacks made from the byproducts of the materials that accidentally fall into their crucibles.
Artistic beauty aside, this delicate doll bestows the joy of completely removing one's inner defenses.
An artefact crafted from ancient agate. This vessel was born to hold all kinds of things, but all it truly holds is blood and mystery itself.
One of Laplace's many technological achievements. It teaches its user the virtues of patience—that one must bide one's time to enact the ultimate revenge.
Much older than the mute chainsaw. It is totally silent but generates a great number of sparks. Is this pure inspiration or the silent protest of the aged?
With arrows sharper than bone shards and venom more potent than any formula. It always produces some "special" surprises.
A scepter made of pure gold, symbolizing power, status, wealth, and abundance. No one knows about the red that has fused deep within it.

Recommended for use with a Silver Candelabra. It will draw in wandering spirits, attaching them to the exorcist's blade and making them the wielder's vassals. These spirits can do just about anything—provided they are willing to help you.
Dry a dragon claw bone in the sun for several days, coat it with beeswax, apply some herbal powder, and hey presto—you've got yourself a weapon that can pierce through anything.

Legend has it that whoever lifts this giant axe can bring "redemption" to the world. Throughout the ages, however, no one has ever been able to take on such a responsibility. Perhaps you will be the one.
It comes from a place farther than far, with a history longer than long. It will forever call, sing, and seek, until one day it is obliterated by time.
They only appear at night, silent and with deadly precision. When they go, they leave nothing but a faint, rusty smell behind. Then, the silence returns once again.
A cane made of pure gold, used to support the body, convey one's majesty, or perform arcane rituals ... and occasionally to knock some sense into an unmotivated youngster.
That little green parrot has used this to record many things—patient information, the latest psychotherapeutic procedures, and the stories only the two of them would discuss.
It bears an engraving of a short poem written by an arcanist. Read it aloud at your peril—after all, words are often sharper than a blade.
A glistening, clear purple liquid that allows one to see the light and peer into the darkness. It must be diluted to a specific ratio before consumption.
The fruits of the future bind you tightly, growing riper each day, their rich aroma endowing you with discerning eyes and a formidable constitution.
It has existed since this land was born. It is older than time and farther than the future. You know it. You have heard its legends, and now it finally embraces you.
More mucus, more bubbles—a single drop can spell your end. Read the safety precautions carefully before use.
Tinged with the glow of the full moon, it has become a light source unto itself, capable of awakening one from any dream, whatever it may be.

If you have a large bottle of benzoin on you, it goes without saying that you mustn't let your guard down. The more unstoppable you feel, the more cautious you should be, lest you return from your adventure with even graver injuries.

A support tool for Ritual Disks designed by Laplace's Arcane Skill Storage Department. It is used to forcibly overwrite disks with a specified incantation. Testing has shown that repeatedly writing the same incantation may enhance its strength. A small number have been distributed to be used as experimental items.
A disguised throwing bomb. Devised by a true collector to counteract the covetous nature of others. Although the acorn bomb's power is rather ordinary, it is enough to deter potential acorn thieves.

A golden cup favored by a certain noble when entertaining guests. Recently, there have been complaints of a suspicious taste residing within it. "It's sweet and fishy and sticks to your teeth and tongue. Wait, is this ..." Then he could say no more.

According to legend, those who wear these glasses can discern truth from falsehood, including the truths and fallacies of arcanum. In reality, they are just a pair of regular glasses burdened by their unwarranted fame.
A makeup box bearing traces of an incantation. It has been over-enchanted with expansion incantations, making it extremely jittery. It constantly opens and closes like a clam spitting mud into water.
A loud and flamboyant mask. Masks usually hide identities, but this one does something else: it makes the wearer unforgettable, even when hidden.

A medal cherished by generations of "true gentlemen." Normally, this medal would never leave the gentleman's side, allowing him to hold an unparalleled influence during his gatherings. "Bear this medal, and the whole world will know that you are a man of the finest quality!"
A number of buyers have found that this "big rabbit's foot" on a golden keychain does indeed bring good luck, earning it the moniker of "Super Rabbit Foot."
A pendant shaped like a hot air balloon, often mistaken for a lightbulb due to its inability to float. It is quite self-conscious of its merely symbolic role and seldom argues otherwise.
A noble girl's spotlight used to attract shimmerwings. Though they are not phototropic, shimmerwings flock to this special spotlight—even if it costs them their freedom.

One of Laplace's internal products, designed to be reliable, precise, and sustainable. It is mainly used for encrypted communication among field investigators. Due to cost constraints, there are no plans for mass production.
A typewriter used for storing incantations. Beware: Every word you type will come true. Push the wrong key, and a claw intended for your enemy might just strike you instead.
For centuries she has remained, ever contemplative, unchanging, and unceasing in her quest for progress.
A pirate bestowed her private stash upon it, along with the spirit of rock 'n' roll. Since then, it has performed night and day, seven days a week.

A locked golden box with an extraordinarily intricate keyhole—a keyhole into which no key fits unless its design is sufficiently artistic. Naturally, it has become a touchstone for the artists of the Vienna Secession.
You have obtained a scroll, its profound emotions palpable. Behold—it can probe the depths of your fears and bring you back to tranquility.

An old music box belonging to a stoic astrologer. It is so ancient that it can no longer produce a sound even remotely resembling music. She knows not its origin, just as she knows not why she cannot laugh or cry.
An outcast, ever defiant, never ceasing in its struggle. Now, its horn has been removed and presented to you, and its unyielding heart and blessings have been bestowed upon you.
A cluster of candle flames, new, dazzling, alive, and ... is there any need to say more? Its gloriousness is clear for all to see. As for what you can't see, your imagination will fill in the blanks.
A helmet passed down from a destitute composer. It is said to be destined for a spectral knight who floats above the ground. How ridiculous! Imagine a knight without a body!

A coffee pot belonging to a maid skilled with numbers. She claims the coffee brewed in this pot is more aromatic and refreshing. She also adds that, for her, no coffee is as stimulating as mathematics.
An invention born of an arcanist's whim. To maintain the balance of these scales, a goldfinch continuously regurgitates glittering coins at an incredible speed.
The goldfinch accepts your invitation, opening its sharp beak. It knows exactly what it can create and what it can destroy.

An elderberry-handled umbrella. It takes considerable effort to open, since the gem on the handle must believe you have exerted all your strength before it does so. The gem cannot tell how many people are holding the umbrella, however, so having a friend assist you is most efficient.
A golden curtain needle allegedly linked to a famous family murder case in Vienna. It ended up in the hands of a noble lady and potion enthusiast, and quickly became her new favorite item.

A gun used by the royal guard that doubles as an instrument. The designer's notes say: "Bring passion to where passion is needed most." To protect the instrument's tone and durability, the guards rarely load it with live ammunition.
You glimpse myriad emotions on the blade—love and hate, zeal and subtlety, repression and catharsis, a momentary tremor, an eternal passing. These always pierce the softest parts of us.

Invented by an arcane biologist in a moment of inspiration. To ensure the arrows hit their mark, he tied the "Super Rabbit Foot" to them. It might work or it might not—it all depends on whether the merchant's goods are genuine.
A liquid distilled from a throat-sealing poison. Handle with care and open cautiously—and be sure to consult a professional alchemist before use.
These reborn sprigs have finally taken root and sprouted. Now, she entrusts them to you, along with the countless possibilities they hold.
Pallid bones carrying all the fervor and hope of the ages. They look at you like a mother looks at her child. They will do anything to protect you.
Mucus, toxins, suspicious hues, trembling bubbles. Use this to turn absolutely any unfavorable battle to your advantage.

Grind, crush, and carefully measure the moonstone. 0.5—no, 0.8 ounces, not a mite more, not a mite less. Then add six drops of that 6 AM dew. Don't underestimate its efficacy. It is sure to make you feel happy and content.
A painkiller made of benzoin, only effective when you're not in too much pain. Don't even consider taking on more difficult tasks with only a small bottle of this stuff.

Thanks to the collaboration between the Laplace Universal Materials Enchantment Department and the Arcane Skills Storage Department, attaching Arcane Skills stored on floppy disks to items is now easier than ever.

An iteration of the One-day Winder. One wind will keep the doll moving for seven days. This model sparked protests from the Doll Rights Association. They claim that the doll's fatigue far outweighs the joy it provides.

The secret to maintaining a doll's vitality. This clockwork mechanism is blessed with arcanum—any doll can move for a full day with a single wind after acquiring such a component. "This design is a lot more convenient than just yelling at my kids to get up in the morning," one consumer remarked.

A velvet moose hand puppet. According to a criminal accused of committing multiple antique jewelry thefts, his motive was that the puppet wished to eat famous foods from history. All eleven stolen antique jewels have been recovered.

A flying squirrel hand puppet. While gliding, it accidentally spat up last night's dinner—it was a minor mishap, but the shiny stone it expelled caused quite a stir among the audience. The puppet was unfazed, however. It always knew that it had refined tastes.

A lighter waiting for a new owner. Its loose and warped windproof cover is like an old man's teeth, affecting its "expression" when lighting up. It still works, however. After all, it was found in a second-hand shop, not the trash.
A humming instrument made more portable with a string. Having spent many nights journeying the streets, the string is now old and frayed. Still, it's the loyal listener of all such instruments.
An instrument that can hum away at any time. Such instruments are not valuable, but an afternoon humming in the sun is worth a few coins, and a friend who nods along to the tune is worth a million.

A cicada wing ring inlaid with gems. The indigenous people who lived near the forest didn't show much interest in cicadas until an explorer seeking a guide offered this in exchange. His request was unusual—he wanted to go to the place where cicadas sang the loudest.

A cicada-shaped ring. Its owner tried to invent a code based on cicada songs, so he ventured alone into a forest where cicadas breed. When the end of summer came around, his friends ventured to the edge of the forest to find him and found this ring lying in the dirt.
A ticket to a masquerade ball. It can help you escape the inescapable, be it your appearance, wealth, or a persistent suitor, even if only for the duration of the ball.
Who calls your name in your dreams? Who sings you that lullaby? Baby, my baby, sleep well. Only now are you safe.

A spare item peeking out of a pocket. It holds a noble quality and a willingness to offer silent but appropriate help. Among intelligent beings, this relationship is known as "companionship." This is its goal.

The ultimate accessory for professional potion alchemists! Featuring more space, more versatile container slots, and a more comfortable fit, a famous London auction house has already bought 200 of these!
The antlers of the deer girl have finally taken root. You are amazed by the vitality within them—bright, light, and warm. You have never felt so safe.

A red dancing shoe that has lost its stage. Now, it imagines itself as a well-dressed noblewoman who is locked in a tower and unable to go out. This helps it escape most of the melancholy of widowhood.

A lone red dancing shoe. It has seen too many tears and too much bloodshed by its predecessors in the cobbler's shop. To prevent the same fate from befalling itself and its partner, it went to great lengths to ensure its partner perished in the fireplace before their first performance.
This curiosity not only helps arcanists find their way back to reality but also offers them additional blessings. Naturally, a small price must be paid to obtain it.
A gentle herb that enjoys secretly distinguishing between the types of incantations around it. Once it counts more than it can handle, it "whooshes" and grows all the thorns it can.
Pour hot tea into a cup, add three spoons of sugar, and one spoon of lukewarm milk. Oh, shall we discuss the latest poem published in Pan?

Once again, a reminder—the fairies and their scales are merely part of the product's creative concept. They are simulated using arcane projections and optical technology, and are capable of being mass produced. Of course, they protect more than just your teeth.

A spare item that unfolds like a blooming flower when taken out of your pocket. Its perfect form is proof of its friendship with its owner. It dutifully fulfills its role, longing to break its silence when it sees sauce dripping down its owner's chin.

A broken dragon toe. Modern scientific analysis shows that there is a large amount of scale debris accumulated in the cracks of the toe and that they both come from the same biological individual. It can therefore be inferred that the reason for its detachment from its owner is that the creature scratched too hard, causing it to break and fall off.
A thick black staff—though it is more like a wooden stick than a staff in size. Whenever you fail to cast an incantation, you can just throw it instead and do the same amount of damage.
Hush, be quiet—don't let your whispered breathing blow away this wandering light. When you face the darkness, you will need it.

Pour St. John's Wort oil into a glass vessel, pressurize it into a combustible canister, and ignite it with an open flame to create a terrifying yellowish-green spectacle. Those of sound mind should not attempt this procedure.
A delicate armband inlaid with blood-red gems, the ancient legacy of a fallen arcanist family. Its shining firelight dispels the gloom before you, illuminating it with the glow of faded glory.
A dull ring. The letters engraved upon it are full of scratches, symbolizing the fading of thoughts. Recite that nameless poem, for it will be your salvation.
Listen to that demonic sound that echoes in the depths of your mind—it's right. You believe it and resolutely step into the coffin.

A hammer-like pestle made of hard stone. It is used to pound the feathers and eggshells of fallen goldfinches, thus staining it an indelible gold. In ancient times, this gold was used for sacred murals.
A stone bucket often used to carry rare gifts. The bucket's holder doesn't care where they come from—they simply revel in the brief golden satisfaction.

A stone basin-like mortar. Countless goldfinch feathers have fallen into it, becoming golden dust after ceaseless pounding. If you get close to the golden bottom of this vessel, you can still hear the whispers of the birds that have been lost to it.

People often revere art and reject violence, but they are not so different. Sometimes art even relies on violence. Rather than discussing these things, why don't we guess whose gun will fire the next bullet?

A flail whose actual power does not match its appearance. The spikes cannot harm flesh, but they can make sentimental mortals experience heartbreak—like the eternal farewell of a loved one or lovers parting ways.
Originally designed as a medical tool for those plagued by hallucinations and narcolepsy. Once powered up, it is no longer just an ornament. What kind of madman would want to wear such a thing?

A yellowish tincture made by soaking oak processionary moth larvae in alcohol. It is said that the yellow saliva of a large arcane creature can stimulate the nerves and the mind. This is a herbal recreation of that substance. Clear-headed arcanists should avoid ingesting it.
For those accustomed to walking in the dark, this is better than nothing, but for those who are truly lost, it is a guiding beacon—no matter where it may lead you.

The carver of this cursed golden goblet turned into a golden snake the moment it was completed, and has been guarding it ever since. It always takes more than it gives, even knowing this will lead to its destruction.

Known to academics as "Dust Amber," this mineral is often found where carbuncles dwell. Someone once hoarded a large amount of it in their home, attempting to extract the dust buried within. But in the end, all they did was turn their home into a carbuncle nest.
This creation injures both your opponent and yourself. Simply wearing it is a grand act of determination. Who said that arcanists were weak? Now, take this!

According to an old urban legend, this painting is cursed. A wealthy man bought it for a large sum, then died that very night. On that same night, a boy who had never tasted the forbidden fruit of love met his destined one. The night was long, yet somehow still short.
A command banner woven with an arcane skill. It depicts a map pointing to safe passage. There is a small chance it will lead you down a dead end, but don't worry—it's just a flag, after all.
An automatically moving spherical compass—loyal, reliable, and best of all, free. No one cares how it works—just curb your curiosity and open it up.
Before aircraft were invented, cloud hunters drew maps on balloons and flew 800 kilograms of lightning over mountains. It was a game for the fearless.
No expertise needed—just hold, lift, and smash. It guides travelers in the fog and charts unknown paths. You'd better get used to this when you walk through the fog.
A country witch's favorite. Just add an ounce of mandrake to the pot, no more, no less, then boil the water and enjoy a carefree afternoon.
Priced at only a few Goldfinch Coins and sold by dubious shops claiming to sell genuine arcane items. "Good luck! If this one doesn't work, try another."
Priced at a few dozen Goldfinch Coins, it's currently sold in limited quantities at "Sea for Yourself," and comes with a free crystal spirit bead.

Since tangible keys can only open certain kinds of locks, one must seek the help of the intangible. The key's owner once pried open the doors of a tomb to try and coerce the spirits of the dead into doing devilish things. I hope you won't follow his path.
Placed in the trunk of an old abandoned car. Though locked, the state of the box suggests there is nothing of value inside.
Placed in the trunk of an old abandoned car. "Open it, and its contents will be yours to keep."
Placed in the trunk of an old abandoned car. What kind of person would leave their life's greatest treasure in a forgotten wreck?
No one cares how it works. Just inject a little fragrance and richness, and you will receive an unexpected joy ... probably.

A limited edition item from the "Sea for Yourself" store. It is rumored to have been stolen from the sacred flame of the Uluru Games during the event's heyday. Tempted and nourished by alcohol, the flame releases an intoxicating scent.
A handcrafted item overflowing with imagination. Just light the fuse and wait. It may not cause fatal damage, but it will certainly cause some trouble.
A dangerous attempt. Humans have long been fascinated by the abilities of arcanists and have tried many times to replicate them using human wisdom.

Newly sprouted branches tirelessly absorb nutrients until the land goes dry. Now, the remains of the young creatures that have died in the forest have become a slowly decomposing resting place for the branches to thrive on.
The ancient inscriptions on it can bring luck and protection, or plague and disease. The picker insists this is a curse tainted with venom.

A pure, black, limpid liquid with a strong bitter taste and a foul smell that matches its appearance. One often hears that "the best medicine is hard to swallow," but you're better off trusting your physiological instincts on this one.
This popular arcanist party drink doesn't rely on alcohol to evoke a primal frenzy but rather spreads honeyed joy with its thick, sweet, and sour taste. Drink up! Join the orange revelry!
A broken round mirror singed by flames and covered in deep crimson cracks. If you can't find answers in the dark, what exactly are you expecting?
An adaptive, walking floppy disk reader—a rare treasure coveted by arcanists the world over. The only drawback is that it may not be by your side when you need it.
Colorless thorns grow on vast verdant plains, drinking up all the land has to offer until the fields lose their color, and they become the only remaining feature.
A lantern with a brand new heart. Though flames tried to burn it to ashes, they ultimately became the fire that fuels its core. Even now, you can still feel its searing pulse at your fingertips.

No one is turned away from here, nor can they turn away—for there is no other option.

No matter where you come from, roads connect us all.
Where are you heading, friend? Where do your dreams lie?

To be free means to forget about the past and live in the moment. Life is filled with celebrations and moments of solitude, but they make it all worth living.
You've really got a helluva lotta land here, boss.
Folks used to fight tooth and nail for this land.
'Course not, my eyes don't look to the past.

But don't worry too much about all that. I'm right here.

Kids are out playing hide and seek and don't come home for dinner. When you finally find 'em, there they are, drifting in the lake.
This kinda thing don't happen often. Maybe I should take a walk around—see what's going on.
Forget it. I'll just do it the old fashioned way.
Your baby is simply adorable, Vertin.
It's prepared so many gifts for you—just look at these decorations, all arranged just so. It must love you very, very much.
It's called the Suitcase, is it? Well, that is quite the delightful name.
Oh?! Don't fret, sweetheart. Tuesday's Motel is a wonderful name, too. In fact, it's my absolute favorite.
I won't abandon you, my darling. You're the most precious thing in the world.
Heh. Hush, now. It can't handle too much praise.
Will you be available for a parent-child picnic soon? I have some free time coming up, and I thought it would be nice to spend it together.

Vertin, maybe all this really is your dream?
Dreams and reveries aren't quite the same. You can indulge in reveries while you're awake, too.
I think this Wilderness is the manifestation of your dreams.
It's vast and boundless—encompassing everything in equal parts.
Maybe? I DO want to see the world—witness its many landscapes.
So this could be my dream, too. But then, where are all the friends I want to make?
I want to interview more people, like you, Argus, and Tuesday.
If possible, I'd also like to make some like-minded friends.
This place sure is full of surprises, boss.
You know what this place reminds me of?
Desert's one helluva place. Loneliness, danger, death—all familiar companions in that environment.
But for a pioneer, it's a mountain of gold and silver. Same goes for this place.
Ever tried panning for gold in a riverbed? You might just strike it rich. Heh. Just kidding.
It's nice in the big city. Every day feels like a party.
All those lights make the night as bright as day, so folks can work after the sun goes down, too.
But if you ask me, nighttime's best spent with family and friends.
Gathering 'round the dinner table, chatting like this. That's what life's all about.
Vertin, have you ever encountered another version of yourself?
Walking down the street, for example, and suddenly seeing someone with the same face as your own.
Heh, it's just a little urban legend I heard from a traveler who passed through the motel.
They say that if you see your doppelganger, you'll die soon after.
But you're still alive and well. Heh, maybe the other you is the one who suffered that unfortunate fate.
No? Or perhaps you met them but pretended not to see?
It's not an uncommon occurrence. True terror is always right beside you.

Oh, Ms. Vertin. I'm sorry, I was listening to music and didn't notice you there.

Would you like to listen together?
I suppose I do have a sheep's taste in music. To be honest, these songs all sound the same to me.

Oh, please, feel free to sit a little closer. You have such a lovely scent—just like fresh grass.
If anything, the lake sees them as a nuisance.
Are you talking about the suitcase?
Your child is also quite adorable.

In the early 19th century, roads began to sprawl across America, born from a need to transport messages between states. Messages were carried by people, then by carriages, and then as the messages were carried by cars, the roads grew wider and wider. Soon, an entire system of roads covered the map.

A century later, this network had grown so large and so plentiful that they were given a new name—national highways. They were also assigned a number, like Route 1, or Route 101. But, this road, however? It refused a boring name like Route 71 or 73. Thus, Route 77 was born.

...

Call it the Great Southern Highway, the Main Street to Texas, whatever you like. The great race only happens here—from end to end, winner gets fifty dollars a mile! Let that cash prize slip through your fingers, and you'll regret it for the rest of your life, doomed to truck remorsefully along that some old road forever.

...

It may not compare to the interstate highways of today, but its charm remains. Take a stroll down this road and buy a commemorative medal, because nothing is more valuable than the joy of its memory.

What comes to mind when you think of the South? Probably the beating sun and the honest, hardworking people, right? How about shotguns and chainsaws? You need to stop watching so many movies. Chainsaws, at least, aren't a vital part of Southern life. Here are three points to remember if you want to avoid upsetting southerners:

- Many of them are hardworking and honest farmers—the salt of the earth. They're likely to work the fields their entire lives, come rain or shine. Their farms are their homes, and they're raised to be fiercely protective of them, so don't trespass. You wouldn't want someone to barge into your home, would you?

- They hold a deep connection to music, from country to bluegrass to heavy metal. Everything is welcome here, just take a look at Austin's South by Southwest music festival and you'll see it all. That being said, their standards can be quite high, and overly frivolous music might not be to their liking. For example, one should never claim that disco is true music in front of them—you wouldn't want to interrupt the flow of conversation with such a sensitive topic, would you?

- Living in vast, open spaces, "bigger is better" is the motto of the South. Big cars for long trips, huge roadside billboards to attract attention, wide hats and chunky boots to protect from the elements, and to show off a little, too. So remember, be generous. Don't say things like "just enough" or "too big." You wouldn't want to be seen as stingy, would you?

- And here's the most important point! Horror movies are all nonsense. The idea of Southern farm families being ignorant, conservative, bloodthirsty, and violent is a terrible stereotype. Never treat people based on things you've seen in the movies. You might regret it.

"That's right, the wife and I were on the road, staying at a motel along the highway," said the man in a grave tone.

"That day, I saw the strangest thing through the motel window. It was a little white sheep standing on two legs. I went out to say hello to it, and it replied! I thought it must've been a real smart sheep ..." added the melancholic woman.

"So she had this idea to take the sheep home as a pet," the man shook his head as he spoke.

"I thought it was just a sheep!" the woman exclaimed.

"So you wrapped this ... sheep in a blanket, planning to sneak it through airport security and onto the plane?" the officer responds calmly.

"That's right, officer. I thought that maybe it could keep our son company whenever we were out. We just thought ..." the man tried to bury his head between his knees.

"But who'd have thought—who'd have thought ..." tears were streaming down her face.

"Who'd have thought that it wasn't a sheep, but a little girl!" the man blurted out.

"Alright. Well, lucky for you, no charges are being pressed. Let's just finish up your statement, and you can be on your way," the officer clearly didn't want to waste any more time on this farce.

This is a cautionary tale. Don't treat animals you find by the side of the road like pets—they might just be a person.

I'm old. So old that my grandson might find me dead in bed tomorrow. Every day could be my last. That's why I've decided to write a few things down, so the priest and the kids will have something to say at my funeral.

There's nothing much exciting about being a ranch boy. I spent most of my days herding cattle and driving off cattle thieves. That's right, cowboys. But I can't quite seem to remember now. Did the name "cowboy" refer to the thieves or us ranchers? So if you're reading this and you can't figure out what I mean by "cowboy," let it be. I ain't even sure myself.

Things were different back then. There were no wide roads for people and cattle to walk on, no motor vehicles that could fit a whole bunch of cattle in them. We herded our cattle on horseback to rivers, markets, slaughterhouses, even to other states. We had to watch out for coyotes and bandits, too. But people didn't call us cowboys back then. What was it they called us? I just can't seem to recall.

It wasn't until later on that us farm boys became known as cowboys. The kids around the neighborhood used to ask me if I'd ever had a duel at high noon or tamed a wild horse. Maybe I was already going senile by then, because I had this vague feeling that I'd ridden a wild horse before and that I'd let a bullet fly under the noonday sun. But one thing's for certain: I never saw any gold. I'd hoped to collect at least a little and leave it to my kids, but I never found any to give.

Now they all call me "cowboy." Yep, "Old Cowboy Tommy," but I still feel like that might not be who I am. That's why I wrote all this. I hope that the real Old Tommy can exist somewhere in the world, at least for a short time.

Right as I sat down and ordered a drink, your Mr. Daryl started hurling insults at me.

I don't even know what the hell that is.
Anyway, Adam and the others said they were only defending themselves ...
Which is the opposite of your story. Who should I trust now?
That Red Wall of theirs. What on earth is it?
I'm the one asking questions here, not you.
What, this an interrogation? We're just having a friendly chat, aren't we? I answered a question of yours. Shouldn't you answer mine?

You've already decided who to trust, so what's the point of this conversation?

And I already said that he's claiming he was only doing the same thing.
So, until we reach a conclusion, it seems like I've got to ask the same damn question again and again.
Submit your clues to the deputy, revealing your true purpose for coming here.
Until I 'fess up and make things easy for you, am I right? Look, all I did there was ask after a girl with chestnut-colored hair and green eyes.

"'Watch out!' At that moment—she heard the driver of the car behind her lean out the window and shout: 'Get out of the car! There's someone in your backseat!' It was then that she saw there was a kidnapper hiding in the backseat, ready to attack."

"The girl gripped the bat and got out of the car, seeing someone grinning and walking toward her. Summoning her courage, she swung the bat and knocked him out cold—only to realize it was her boyfriend, returning from the gas station!"

"The girl hid the bat behind her back as she got out of the car, and sure enough, there was a man grinning as he walked toward her. Summoning her courage, she swung the bat and knocked him out cold. Upon closer inspection, his right hand was a metal hook!
And that's how the infamous Hook Hand Slasher was caught. No one saw that coming!"

Under the dazzling chandelier, they indulge in toasts, dances, and self-congratulations, whispering lip to ear in high spirits. At the end of the red-carpeted stairs, the object of their discussion finally arrives, lifting her skirt and offering a slightly apologetic smile.

    "Mata Hari! Mata Hari, my darling!"

    The rich and powerful are reduced to bumbling fools with only a coy smile. People gather and cheer, fervently chanting their hostess' name, circling at her feet, offering gold, offering jewels, offering their loyal hearts.

    Accompanying the hostess is her sister, like a shadow at her side. Whispers of this one echo through the depths of the mansion.

    The little girl who grew up in her sister's shadow rules this mansion-sized kingdom. A child accustomed to tearing apart hot roast chicken with her hands, wiping grease from her mouth with her dress, and banging her tail on the chandelier as if it were a wind chime. She roams the back garden seated on a pony, laughing uncontrollably on its back as the scent of blood from the servants' thorn-pierced legs fills the air. Gentlemen love her innocent malice, clapping to please her all the while.

    That is until a bullet pierces her sister's head. Fate reclaims all it has given, just as man was banished from paradise, and so commences the prelude to wandering in exile. Merchants and drunken paupers covet her treasures. A farmer's wife exchanges a basket of cream cakes and eggs for her jewels, a child trades a wild flower for her hairpin. Finally, her dress is covered in dust, and the ornaments on her neck and wrists are all gone, like Inanna's encounter with the queen of the underworld.

    More malicious people end up wounded by her claws. Hunters love the scent of blood, swarming in for her bounty.

    So she hides in the forest, hides in the meadows, hides in the barn. Milk and meat run across the pasture, grain fills the warehouse. She searches everywhere, but cannot find food of her own.

    "When did all this change, sister?"

    "Why are my clothes always dusty?"

    "Why haven't the mansion's servants come to find me?"

    As her claws soak in the blood of a young rabbit that's jumped out of its burrow, she feels an intense hunger, for the first time in her life.

July 13, 1943

This is my first diary entry Old Quitéria said she would <s>help me with my writing</s>

She kept laughing and said I should use punctuation but she did not tell me what punctuation is it sounds like seasoning.

Old Quitéria brought me to a place called a nursing home it is rubbish here and old too and the peoples faces are all wrinkled up and she wants me to start learning to read and do something called work so I can stay here and eat and I do not want to keep running away anyway those people cannot find me here

August 15, 1943

These "elderly" people move so slowly! Where is the thrill! They all looked at my clothes and said I must be a rich girl from somewhere far away! I told them about my past! They laughed so much! Old Quitéria didn't laugh and another didn't laugh either! The one they call the soprano! She said I was a pampered poor little thing! Fate likes to lift people up and then smash them down! I don't know what that means! But I don't like her calling me a poor little thing! Bugs are little! They are not good things they taste bad! Some even taste like dirt! So I'm not a bug! She also asked why I was not angry at the soprano I do not understand why I should be angry The soprano says bad things but she did not hurt me People who love to say good things are the most dangerous

January 4, 1944

After picking up the Morning Truth paper, I tidied up the soprano's bed. I saw many newspaper clippings under her pillow, all about the opera house. After evening prayers, I was about to take back the soprano's handkerchief when she suddenly grabbed me. She asked if I couldn't see that life was getting worse. She said I must understand that feeling, but I didn't understand what she was talking about. She said, "When your skin becomes wrinkled, you'll understand. And everyone, everyone will die without dignity in regret and ignorance." I didn't know what she was talking about. I was very scared. I thought of my sister. I don't want to become my sister.

After I put out the candle by her bed, she suddenly hugged me tightly and cried like a little girl. I copied what Quitéria does and gently patted her back. She soon fell asleep.

July 13, 1944

Old Quitéria announced to everyone that it was the one-year anniversary of my arrival at "Heartfelt Home." I was very happy because it meant there was a lot of food and no work. They said I was the star today, and I could decide everything, just like when I was at the mansion. I asked them if there were any ponies here. I wanted to ride one and let them chase me. The elderly laughed so hard their dentures fell out, but they all said they wanted to try. So I rode our "Jenny the Cow," and she trotted majestically. I rode on its back, and they chased me with their canes and wheelchairs. They fell, got up, and laughed heartily. No one helped them up. Finally, the soprano caught me. She cleverly used a bundle of hay to catch Jenny. When we got back, Quitéria scolded me, saying I could have broken their old bones. But everyone was happy, and so was I.

At night, Old Quitéria gently patted my back, but I couldn't sleep. I thought of the soprano's words. I've been thinking about her words a lot lately. I asked Quitéria if we would really just get worse and worse. She kissed my forehead and said, "What nonsense is that?"

But I promised the soprano not to reveal her secret. So I said nothing. That night, I dreamt of my old gardens, but strangely, "Jenny the Cow" was there too.

Feathers fall to the ground; the white goose in her arms is gone.

    Through the endless days and nights, her stomach growls constantly. Sometimes, she mistakes ochre stones for chunks of meat; nearly breaking her teeth on them. She licks the cuts in her mouth from the stones' sharp edges, the warm blood flowing into her stomach.

    Occasionally, she dreams of the mansion, but that was so long ago that she starts to doubt whether any of it was real or just a long dream. In the dream, she runs and jumps at her sister's banquet, tapping guests on the shoulder—they drink and toast to a bright future, but no one pays attention to her. Confused, she leaps onto the table—still, no one notices her. She's lost the ability to distinguish her memories from fantasy, and nameless grievances ignite sparks of anger within her. She raises a torch, and the mansion in her dream burns away like dry leaves until ashes fill every corner of the dream world.

    Her memories have become a collapsed ruin, past faces shattered, experiences peeling away like old paint, impossible to piece together.

    Everything returns to dead silence. When she awakens from the dream, she's in a strange and empty place—it's terribly dull, nowhere near as interesting as the banquet. She once tried to scratch words on the walls with her claws, like writing a diary. Still, she began to prefer life in this place. Because her only chance to leave has been to carry out "missions"—of course, she hates missions, the blood always sticks to her claws, and sullies her clothes. Out of curiosity, she once tasted blood, it was as bitter as lettuce, and she hates lettuce more than anything.

    This is where she learned to sing—a song her sister taught her. She's forgotten too many of the words and has no idea what dragons and zippers have to do with each other. But still, she sings it often. Every time that she does, she pictures wrinkled faces. She doesn't know why she thinks of them. But every time she does, water flows from her eyes. She tasted that water too, and it was even more bitter than lettuce.

    Her eyes, looking at the goose feathers, are as empty as a deep well.

The old geezers at the veterans residence always talk about scars, medals, and sleepless nights. Now that my battles are over, those nights have finally caught up with me.

First it was my biological father, then "Pa," and today it's "Sis" ... every night there's a ghost that won't leave me be.

No, she's no longer "Sis." What should I call her? Igor's lackey, or the rebels' watchdog?

Forget it; it doesn't matter. Let's just call her by her name.

Moldir.

Uttering those familiar yet strange syllables one at a time, a question pops into my mind, making me shiver.

—Next time we meet, will you pull the trigger ... ? Mierda! Don't ask me that! When did I become so weak and useless? When did I start depending on people? When did I start ... calling a stranger "Sis"?

... I don't know.

This black-and-white checkered room always reminds me of chess—every time I lost to Molly, Ptolemy would laugh at me for lacking a "tactical mind." The funny thing is, I never thought of them as my "brother and sister" back then.

Then came field training. My competitive streak got me a nasty cut. Molly shoved the scared soldiers aside and cradled my head in her lap. It was the hottest day of the year in São Paulo, the ground and air were scorching, and warm, moist drops hit my cheeks.

Between the shouts for a medic, I caught a hint of panic in her voice.

After that, I saw Molly differently—turns out the tough, reliable adjutant had a soft side too!

Wait ... was that sweat dripping on my cheeks back then?

04:18 AM

Molly said she was afraid of the cold, so on those rare cold nights in São Paulo, there was always someone else in my bed. She liked to call me an unquenchable crucible, and I'd joke about tossing her long hair into the fire to make a piñata ... back then, we were like real sisters. I nearly believed we were a normal family.

I know I sleep like a pig. In the middle of the night, I'd find her curled up in the corner while I hogged the blanket.

I know she didn't hate the cold as much as she claimed; she just ...

In the end, we were never normal sisters, and we could never enjoy a normal life.

Now, I've lost my identity and my siblings. I'm just "Lopera"—but who is "Lopera" anyway?

The unfamiliar sound of birds outside the window means I've finally experienced my first sleepless night. Go ahead, chirp away. I envy you simple creatures—at least you have a nest to return to after catching your worms.

In twenty-seven minutes, the dormitory door will be pushed open after three knocks, and Molly will find a way to drag me to the morning training drill.

Something warm and moist fell from my eye. It was something I rarely got to experience, at least as far as I can remember ... no, it was just something brought about by sleepiness and yawning.

... Sister, next time we meet, maybe I will pull the trigger.

The night at the veterans residence is alive with laughter, as the farewell party for Mr. Duncan unfolds as planned. Empty wine bottles on the table pile up like fortifications, as Galeno spurs the crowd on, urging Mr. Duncan to share some tales from his younger days. "Haha, that's a fine idea! Don't worry, Old Duncan might have had a few drinks, but he's not about to spin yarns just to fool you all." Mr. Duncan chuckles, rubbing the white stubble on his chin. "Whether it's pink dolphins, headless mules, or treasure maps inside giant snakes—it all happened exactly as I told you!" A barrage of adventurous stories hits the listeners like a volley of cannonballs, until late into the night, when Mr. Duncan signals for everyone to settle down. He pauses for a moment, then begins to speak slowly: "Next is a story that's not so cheerful, one that I saved for last." "I'm sure my oldest friends here remember the '1959 Lufthansa Flight Incident.' Yes, it took my whole family from me. Looking back, I was like a training dummy knocked down in the field—nothing left intact except a pocket full of medals. Two years later, in the peacekeeping forces in the Congo, I met Don Mariano Martinez. The officers called him 'rookie,' but he fancied himself the proud 'lead singer' of the military songs we sang—in his language, those two words sounded quite similar. Eventually, everyone just called him 'Lead Singer Martin.' At first, I didn't want to get too close to the Argentine, but I ended up being 'Lead Singer Martin's' roommate. He was born with the gift of the gab, his thick lips were always flapping like wet palm leaves. Back then, I was still young and foolishly thought I could quiet him down with nothing but my silent protest, but gradually he wore me down and I became talkative myself. Once we got to know each other, we often argued about football, politics, and customs, but he always followed his officers' orders. Then our lead singer's voice was forever silenced, he sacrificed himself to protect the entire unit. That's another story. As I was sorting through his belongings, I learned he came from a wealthy family and left home in pursuit of a sense of honor; two years later, I discovered in an investigation that the daughter Martin entrusted to me was also a victim of Lufthansa Flight 502. Good heavens ... that was a devil's joke! The kind no one could appreciate! Many years passed and the decorated scout retired, and was replaced by an old man wandering the favelas. Now, I look back at that word—'honor' ... Haha, it seemed more valuable than gold! For it, Martin and I gave up everything precious to us, and in the end, we still relied on it to live. Like fine wine in a bottle, you always want another glass, and another, until you find yourself drunk and face down in the gutter. Now, your Old Duncan may be about to embark on the last journey of his life. Of course, it's no longer for those pretty 'honors,' but to make good on what the kids always say— 'Got yourself some trouble? Go find Old Duncan at the veterans' home. He'll sort it out for you!'"

Cholera, malaria ... and countless other maladies, some yet to be named by the medical community, weave their way through these streets, touching everyone, human and arcanist alike. The rampant spread of disease serves as a stark reminder: in the face of death, we are all the same.

In the labyrinthine alleys of the favelas, life is a tapestry of shared hardship. Here, poverty and destitution know no boundaries, affecting all, both materially and spiritually. The root of disease may not lie here, but the sorrow that fuels the bloodshed in the streets certainly does.

People are divided by wealth and poverty, not by the extreme claims that all arcanist suffering is caused by humans. Illnesses strike both arcanists and humans, just as hunger, violence, and the ignominy of enslavement are indiscriminately imposed on everyone. The authorities turn a blind eye to the spreading racial hatred, while the Apostles Brotherhood fans the flames under the noses of the sleeping watchdogs, deepening this tragic divide to recruit followers. Gangs, like parasitic vines, thrive on the misfortunes of the favelas, waging endless turf wars, where crime is as common as breathing.

Yet, despite all this, the favelas are not the inferno people imagine.

The residents of the favelas are both passionate and frugal, poor yet generous. They will share their meager food with you, thank you with crumpled cruzeiros and genuine tears for saving their child, and yet, they will draw a knife over the unsatisfactory price of a feijoa. A person's death merely adds another silent corpse to the river, and sometimes, even the deceased's family remains indifferent.

Retired Zeno soldiers conduct charity work here, seeking alternatives to gang life for the youth: sports fields, the military, labor cooperatives ... no matter what, this is a land full of vitality. Despite the spread of crime, like the ever-flowing river beside them, their lives continue.

This hellborn ship still sails through the troubled waters of São Paulo's fate, as it did before I arrived here, and perhaps will continue to do so long after I leave.

All of Latin America suffers because of its imbalanced wealth, and is torn apart by insatiable greed. One person's poverty is another's feast, suffering nourishes happiness, like the two banks of a river, clearly divided.

Dear reader, this is the land I currently inhabit.

—A Friend from Afar
A dazzling necklace, that once belonged to an innocent heart, stolen by a young pickpocket during her wanderings and then traded for a few days' worth of food money.
"I caught that little thief. His bones were as fragile and thin as twigs, but his newly grown teeth were sharp! Otherwise, I wouldn't have let him go."
She used to comfort those childlike elders with a siren song that made them forget their pain and aged bodies.
"Sometimes, I sing, but the elders always weep, then whisper softly that it's not my fault."
Those pristine wings, however, could never, ever fly across the riverbank.
"It loved to tease us, swooping down from the eaves, landing on our heads and shoulders, as if it were a mischievous child ... "
An intercepted telegram, secrets revealed. Another bullet casing left on the execution ground.
"I ... I have nothing to do with any of this, I swear, I swear ... it has nothing to do with me!"
An ugly little wind-up figure, and nothing more.
"When I saw so many identical ... toys on the shelves and in the cabinets, I swore I'd never go in there again! Even if they were offering free candy!"
Every fallen bullet casing symbolizes a soldier's permanent rejection of their duty, honor, and the loyalty they should have upheld.
"I never thought it was a disgrace ... on the contrary, it was the most honorable task Zeno ever gave me!"
A pair of long-barreled revolvers that once accompanied sisters through countless afternoons at the shooting range—or rather, former sisters.
"This one of mine rarely won against the other one in training ... even during our last session."
Its owner has yet to come up with a more ingenious way to win. But at least it provided a little thrill whenever her trick worked.
"Anyway, isn't winning what matters? Do you really expect me to hand over control to the fickle goddess of fate?"
Relics of an old comrade, including a Zeno medal and a few letters filled with his wistful longing to see his daughter again.
"Alright, alright. To be honest, I never had the courage to open these letters until I found that drowning girl."
An ordinary-looking wrench, bursting with stories and the marks of time, just like the old craftsman it belongs to.
"Don't be fooled by its plain appearance, this here is the foundation of all my work—just as much as my calloused old hands!"
A photograph from the 1961 peacekeeping mission in the Congo, with the photographer, exact date, and location all lost to time.
"Three Brazilians, two Spaniards, one Argentinean ... you'd be surprised, but we were the most decorated reconnaissance team in the unit!"
A doctor's medical kit, containing her compassion and regrets from her past journeys.
"The root of the people's illness lies not in their bodies, but in a future they perceive as a dead end. No medicine can cure that future."
A roll of bandages, fighting back death's descent upon her patients, and extinguishing the world's light from the eyes of the doctor.
"Once you get used to the darkness, you'll find it kind—compared to the fate that took my sight."
A strangely shaped typewriter; the only weapon this doctor had in her battle with fate.
"It has accompanied me through every inch of this rainforest and beyond. We wrote together, recording it all so people wouldn't forget what had happened."
A can of guarana and a chair. We often sat like this, all day long.
Eternity#A leisurely afternoon with perpetual optimism, uncannily similar to The Tonight Show.
A Knight#The sword of Damocles hangs overhead, facing this crisis, someone advises that the best place to hide is just in the Suitcase—just in case!
Conflict, harmony, everyone's welcome and anything goes. Come, experience the music of a land consumed by its own turmoil.

Oh São Paulo, my most treasured city!
After spending so much time in all this humidity, my ropes are near to sprouting mushrooms.
As always, the first order of business upon docking is to stock up on fresh water and provisions. What say you, Captain?
... Haha. I keep forgetting, you won't be needing those now, matey.
Aye, but there is a large and well-lit courtyard here, perfect for the removal of rust and repainting. Oh, for a bit of tung oil—that'd make things all the better.
Stop right there, intruder! Put your hand in the air!
Shiver me timbers! I've gone and beached myself now. What would oI' Anne think of me offering myself up to a military officer?
You mean this hand here, eh? She's a friend of mine, and if you want me to "raise my hand," you'll be needing her consent, matey.
Whatever you are, identify yourself this instant!
No need for haste, matey, I'll tell you right now. I'll say it, right—RUN!
... Damnation, someone needs to quiet that blasted alarm.
'Tis only a small square yard. The pontoon at Nassau Harbor was a far grander affair.
You think we're lost? That's just bilge and bile.
A quick peek at the compass's jolly needle is all it takes to know all's well.
It's truly another dead end, yarr!
We made it in after all. There are weapons, rations, a brand new compass, and bottles of rum.
Oh, ol' Captain Anne's never laid eyes on the likes of this—aviation fuel!
Ships these days can take to the skies. What a sensation that must surely be!
Hush—look, a wee rascal's snuck in, but he lacks our good luck and cunning disguise.
So, then ... has the boss weighed in on the Apostles Brotherhood's proposal?
I'd stay optimistic if I were you. Things are going smoothly, but I can't give you a definite answer just yet.
Well, blow me down! Seems they're not so rough with every guest.
You should get the goods back first ... Wait, hold on.
Was this bottle part of our exchange?
I'm no plaything, I just ended up in the cargo hold by chance. You've flipped me about so much, my side's nearly sprung a leak!
Oh! You're an awakened being ... But which part is it? The bottle? The bones? Or maybe it's the pirate ship ... ?
Call me Anne Brotherhood, or Duke Dodo, or whatever you like, but don't you dare think of me as a mere pirate ship!
Well, it's a pleasure to make your acquaintance, Anne Brotherhood.
Say, I was wondering if you could teach me some pirate lingo, so I can shiver everyone's timbers at the procession.
Ahem! Well, if you're keen to listen, I do have a bounty of piratical tales to share.
But now's not a good time for old fish tales. I'm on a mission.
Why don't you come with me? We can chat along the way.
Smooth sailing on your way home!
You've been such a big help, Anne Brotherhood. Let me just go say hi to mi viejo, and I'll take you back ...
I read the report. It seems a toy boat of sorts has made its way into the warehouse.
I know you enjoy wasting your time with questionable lowlifes, but now a thief too?
Hm. It looks like we're back in hot water, Captain Anne.
That admiral's face was as sour as a lemon ... It's a marvel I made it out!
Look at that majestic river, the pretty houses, and the fishers on the pier—now that's a fitting place for a majestic ship to anchor!
Alas, 'tis a shame that it's only large enough for a four-man skiff or a canoe.
Old Duncan! Shouldn't you be out fishing instead of flapping about here?
Over there! Quick, help me catch that slippery kid!
Isn't that the mischievous scamp that sells bananas on the corner? What's he up to this time?
Someone's been breaking into houses on this street lately, and I finally caught him in the act.
Come on, let's teach him a lesson, for his parents' sake!
Aha! And the board's cleared once again! Another win for yours truly!
What say you? There's more to killing time at sea than dice and drink. Eduard the Red-Hand fancied this game, but he never bested ol' Captain Anne.
Hmm. Lady Luck is on your side today, little boat.
One, two, three ... wait, why do you only have 14 pieces off the board? We must've miscounted. I've still got a shot!
Count again, there's no mistake. I'll fetch your spectacles for you, if you want.
Spectacles won't do it, we might need a broom, or a gun maybe—didn't you see? Those Carbuncles swiped a piece!
Look yonder, a solitary young lass.
If you bring her aboard and give her a passage, some joy's most likely to follow.
Sarmatian Sea Snails! You can make a jungle camouflage potion with these marvelous little things!
If you're after their sulfurous mucus, you'd best give up now, lass—this Atlantic kind here don't make the stuff.
They're too alike to the Sarmatian Sea Snail, 'tis true—enough to give naturalists a bigger headache than a gallon of grog! Haha!
A word of caution, lass, wearing a fancy dress like that out on the wooden piers of these favelas isn't safe.
Hop aboard if you wish to keep your purse.
That day, I gave the little lass a ride.
Guess where she was headed? Hah, the Zeno base. Bad timing, to be sure.
Luckily, I ran into Lopera halfway. Before I confessed to her, she was still calling me Anne Brotherhood!
The newsboy just told me, Old Duncan got into a fight.
Who would want to fight Old Duncan?
Remember Nassib, the one who's always bragging down at the fish market? His little brat stole everything and joined the Apostles Brotherhood.
Old Duncan heard, immediately dropped his rod, and chased after the kid.
Oh, this is an ill wind to be sure. Recently, there've been too many new faces in São Paulo. It's hard to tell just who they are.
Little boat, get some help over there, quick!
Peaceful waters never rest long. Too many new faces in São Paulo lately, indeed.
First, the suspicious Manus Vindictae, then the gangs swarming the streets, and there's the Foundation's Timekeeper, like a bird fallen into the water.
It's a good thing you don't hunt pirates, Vertin. I've exhausted my supply of creative aliases.
I think ... that the authorities of the late 20th century are no longer concerned with Letters of Marque.
Of course, though, caution is a good habit to exercise.
Aye. Say, you've all the makings of a fine captain. Calm, brave, and able to spy the hidden reefs beneath the waves.
Hah, though you're nothing like ol' Captain Anne!
We'll face many enemies ahead, and I'd love nothing more than to fire off a few volleys there way. Here, you take command!
With just a few adjustments to our current situation, I'm sure we can gain the upper hand.
Ah, Captain Anne, do you remember that battle with the "Golden Emu"?
We won the day, but Helmsman Jack got himself so soaked and besotted at the victory feast that he sailed us straight into a storm.
Everything gone overnight. Even that damned Zeno base is nothing but a desolate grave.
What are you doing sighing over there? Come over here—we need a bigger boat.
Old Duncan! Where did you find so many willing hands?!
Right here in São Paulo. These brave boys live here, and they're not going anywhere anytime soon.
Someone has to stand up and teach those Brotherhood thugs a lesson.
Never have I wished more for this waterway to be wider.
Were you the one who leapt to the rescue here earlier?
This time we brought more brave lads, all eager to defend our home São Paulo's way.
But where did the Apostles Brotherhood gather all these ruffians? Hooded, soaked in black oil—many strange faces we've never seen before.
Damn, last time Lopera and I were here, there weren't this many.
Remember, don't confront them head-on! Use your wits!
Did you hear all that preaching?
They were prattling on about trials, grace, and something that would engulf the world ...
Heaven have mercy! Why doesn't the government arrest them instead of forever harrying us pirates? It's not like pirates ever wanted to destroy the world!
It's this kind of nonsense that has São Paulo's youth wrapped around their fingers.
But for an old man like me, with not many years left ...
If the world is going to be washed clean by a great flood, then I'd just like to sit on the chattering pier and fish.
I'll wait with everyone here, watching São Paulo's final moments.
Honestly, if the price of survival is becoming some newfangled greasemonger, or a greasy bottle at that ...
I'd rather sail right into a reef and call myself a wreck!
Admiral, this is all a misunderstanding!
Regarding the supplies I "accidentally" took earlier, I can pay for them in full.
Besides, I'd like to remind you, in the army ...
Zeno doesn't need advice from a thief.
Watch out, Old Duncan, they've got more reinforcements waiting in the wings!
Hah, let them try my specialty on for size. See if you can handle this new little gadget!
Stay here a few days longer, and you'll learn to sense danger early.
Are you talking about those "river cowboys"? A few potions should take care of them!
New blood, it's time to test your loyalty.
The "Sufferer" will forgive your words and deeds, ignorant little boat lady.
But this forgiveness is for you alone.
Yo-ho-ho! Ship's in fine shape, and the bones have got nary a scratch, either!
Send them to Davy Jones's locker!
I never miss—most of the time anyway.
What's a veteran without his gun?
Wow, so many things that I haven't seen.
Typhon won't give up his friends, neither will Sotheby.
Time to blow off some cannon smoke!
Ready! Anchor down! Ram the prow into their flank!
Stay put! This'll hurt longer if I miss.
Hah, my crucible really has a mind of its own.
You don't want to get on my bad side, kids.
I never get tired of this one!
As long as you hit the target!
Come on, put some power behind it!
I tripled the ingredients this time!
The enemy is coming! Everybody protect yourselves!

Does it matter? I'm all you've got. We're at war—bullets flying, wounds festering, typhoid, cholera, and all the worst of it. It's a living hell, and only fools think there's any honor in it.

Now I need you to listen. There's something you should know.
The raid on the river was a ploy, and its mastermind is an old acquaintance. As for the ones who carried it out—you already heard about them this morning.

They promised their followers they'd push south, and they did. With their supplies secured by a mysterious third party, they paraded through every town along the way, playing as "liberators" and taking out anyone they decided were their enemies.
They swelled in numbers, larger than any local gang or cult had ever gotten before.
Now they swarm across the land like a school of red-bellied piranhas. Always hungry, ready to tear apart anything that crosses their path.
Chances are they're doing fine, just like you.
Would've been nice if you caught what that little executioner and that "gold-hearted" gambler were talking about during their dice game. Guess you'll have to ask her later.
Listen, I'm not here to run your errands or play your messenger boy, so ask nicely.
There's nothing more I need to tell you. For now.
This place was once known for its inexhaustible mines, the riches of its rainforests, and its brave and passionate people. But now, the first two are gone.

Chaos and power struggles loom over the younger generation, while the rich and well-connected sit atop their piles of corpses and rubble and feast. Dining off golden plates with silver spoons, turning their noses up from the dogs at their feet.

But that gold has lost its shine and their silver spoons have tarnished, everyone can see them for what they really are. So, what now? Either the people save themselves or turn their fate over to the hands of the so-called "savior." What would you do, if it were you?
I'd save myself first.#So, why can't this "savior" save me?
That's a smart choice. Now that the carnival's over, people have to deal with more than just their hangovers—they must figure out how to save their own skins.
Most though will just run around like chickens with their heads cut off, begging for their pain to be taken away. But all they'll get is another morphine shot—nothing close to a real solution.
Fear spreads like a disease. Until an entire generation is out on the streets, hoping to find anything that will lift them out of their misery.
Who's asking the questions here, me or you? But fine, I'll clue you in a little about this "savior".
I once met a kid from Buenos Aires who told me about the "hand of god" that gave them the World Cup. He saw it as proof there was a higher power, something men should follow and seek protection from.
Maybe he had a point, I don't know. Maybe there's truly something greater out there, or maybe it's just what we mortals need to believe.

These men from the Apostles Brotherhood used to be regular church-goers just like anybody else. But faced with an opportunity to rise above their own cruel realities, they all too readily turned away.
They left their old altars and took communion with a new god. Will this new path save them? Is it worth all their efforts? I can't say.
But you wanted to know if this 'savior' can save its own. Well, I guess you've got your answer now.
Are we going to be alright?
No need to start panicking just yet. Things are still under control. Your lady friend has stepped up to solve this mess, and the veteran knows what he's doing.

This city is unlike any you've seen before. You must learn its secrets to survive—remember which street kids are from which alley and what intel they can be relied on for, learn the dates when the dealers bring their "medicine" into port, and figure out which water tanks hide the key to the local gang's safehouse.
Don't look at me for answers. It's none of my business.
A gambling game's been set up in a place unfamiliar to you. Soon, you'll be invited to join the table as well.

Hmph ... you seem to have grown quite assertive. But remember this: as a newcomer to the table, you have no privilege to make demands or probe for information unless you're looking to be targeted and isolated.

You have to lose a few rounds—pay your "entry fee." Only then can you start to learn the secrets of those at the table. The players' backgrounds, the dealer's habits, and the truth behind the highest-stakes gambler.
It's baffling to me. Why would anyone travel halfway across the world just to throw away their money?
That was a rhetorical question. But thanks for answering.
You're right; the allure of winning is irresistible, even in a game of chance. People blow on the dice, clutch a rabbit's foot, or murmur a prayer, foolishly believing they can sway the outcome.
Tsk, disappointing indeed. To think you're entangled in such empty words.
Some are so captivated by these grandiose phrases that they feel empowered when using them. Despite their vapidity, it makes them feel important.

Oh, quite the opposite. The odds are rarely equal. Your opponents could have any number of advantages stuffed up their sleeves—a larger stack of chips, easier winning conditions, or even the power to change the rules. Want a fair game? You've got to fight for it, by any means necessary.
The white suits always play it safe, carefully hedging their bets, while the black robes plot to overturn the table.
Clever? More like cretinous and atrocious.
Once the table's flipped, there'll be nothing but chaos. Who would bother to set it right again? No one.
All it takes is one lie to set off a chain reaction, and I'm afraid the butterfly effect has reached you. I have bad news. You've been betrayed.
But there's good news, too: a certain flight lieutenant appears to be more loyal to you than to the organization she swore to serve.
You know him—the admiral who was pitted against an enemy he couldn't possibly defeat. This conflict has left an incurable ulcer in his once lofty heart.
Yet, as a leader, he must remain unyielding in both body and mind.
Despite his continued victories on the front lines, he made a decision so counterintuitive that even his loyal adjutant found it questionable.
The top brass always sees things differently, I suppose.
Things never end well for traitors.#Hopefully, he knows what he's doing.
You must have heard the story of the Trojan Horse, right?

Greek soldiers sneaked past the walls of Troy inside a wooden horse. One Trojan priest tried to warn his people, but was executed by the gods themselves for doing so. Soon after, all the leaders of Troy were killed by the hidden invaders.
Being killed by your enemy is bad; being killed by your ally is worse. It was an honorless way to go.
Don't get your hopes up. He's more like a desperate patient than anything. Weary from the pain of his ulcer, and frantically searching for a way out.
In his desperation, he has clutched at an opportunity presented by none other than the Preacher herself.
Deep down, he knows he's backed himself into a corner.
Great. I'm done reading reports anyway.
I look forward to your wise decisions. We need some good news for a change.
I have some news you'll be happy to hear.
Trust me, you'll wish you had more than a minute for this. It involves a mutual friend of ours—a long-lost acquaintance you've been searching for.
Doctor, writer ... she goes by many titles, just like you and I. Sadly, in her current state, her brain capacity is limited.
It's just like after that fateful battle ended. Few survived to remember her awe-inspiring feats.
Now, this kind-hearted doctor has become a crucial part of another wicked scheme of which our dear admiral is well aware.
An orchestra without a conductor can barely play a symphony. Recognizing that missing, vital piece, the admiral seized the opportunity without hesitation.
Experience gives a veteran his scars, yes, but also a scrap of wisdom. He knew he should gain the upper hand in this one-sided gamble.
I don't know yet; there's no mention of it in the reports. I do have some speculations, however.
Those troublemakers have been focused on nothing but cultivating chaos and fanning the flames of conflict, paying little attention to the scale and extent of their intended retribution.

Now, it seems they've realized the uncertainty of this approach—drastic, volatile retribution won't get them anywhere. To reach their destination, they must forge a new path, even if it's more arduous and perilous than the last.
Your minute's up. Time certainly does fly, doesn't it?
I'll be back when there's a new development. Stay alive if you can. I'd like to keep reading reports for you.

Greetings!

By the time you read this letter, I will already be on an auto island far out at sea. Oh! Please don't misunderstand, I adore your company, especially the hallway walking parties at 3 a.m. Though I do love all parties, walking parties are a particular treat, but unfortunately, The Lady's Code of Conduct dictate that I should be sound asleep by 9 p.m. What a pity.

Also, please tell Ms. Moissan not to worry! I'm not adventuring alone; miss Vertin is also going on a trip to the legendary El Dorado. The City of Gold! Magic, gold, and even bouncing coffee beans! I can't wait to talk to the locals about potential invigorating potion recipes!

Speaking of invigorating potions, now everyone can become a brewing master! All it takes is a cup of coffee, and before drinking, add three grams of gold, and voilà, you've got an invigorating potion! I've already prepared the ingredients—the gold is on the table! And thanks to the automatic coffee drip-beast in the lounge, we're saved from the hardest part—making coffee!

And do look forward to the special gifts I'll soon bring back!

Sincerely,

Sotheby
