The Untold Stories of the Invisible College—Boyle's Impossible Flask

Perhaps you are familiar with the Royal Society, maybe you're even able to name every president. But do you know its predecessor—the mysterious scholar's assembly, known as the Invisible College? Today, we will introduce the central figure of the Invisible College, Robert Boyle, the famous alchemist, natural philosopher, and founder of modern chemistry, along with his mystical stories.

    When discussing Boyle, one must mention Boyle's Law, which states that at constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume. Boyle demonstrated this with a U-shaped tube filled with mercury. But before that, Boyle tried various devices and countless designs in his quest for a frictionless flask with a piston. He even employed arcane skills, casting an incantation of proportional scaling into a flask. As a result, the flask could indeed compress and expand objects perfectly. However, arcane skills being what they are, the object's mass would shrink with its volume, and the process would cause noticeable temperature changes. A very successful arcane skill, but a failed experimental apparatus.

    These flasks were eventually donated to the Royal Society, but it's said some ended up in private hands. So, keep an eye on the ordinary flasks around you—one of them might just be a highly convenient "Impossible Flask."

Dear anonymous gentleman,

    The Veterans' Residence deeply appreciates your generosity. Your donations have been a great help during these difficult times. We've taken to calling you Mr. Marble, after your donation of that fine marble chair. I assume marble holds some special significance for you. If you happen to see this letter, we hope that you will one day soon come through the door and accept our thanks and hospitality. I'm sure you'll be pleased and comforted by the heart-warming sights inside the home you've so long supported, and we'd love to hear the story behind the large red button you've placed on your gifted chair.

The headquarters has informed all branches that the Brazilian branch has experienced another mutiny, though specific details remain unclear. All branches are ordered, effective immediately, to recall all units and temporarily detain any personnel who have served in Brazil or were under the command of any officers from the Brazilian branch. These individuals are to remain in custody until a special agent from the headquarters arrives for inspection. Noncompliance will be treated as support for the traitors.

    The mastermind behind this mutiny remains unidentified, and discussion of the matter is strictly prohibited.

The most peculiar guest in this remote manor.
She seems unrelated or even unaware of the conflict going on in the rainforest around her. The lady-like figure licks her lips, simply craving a meal.

The little critter chasing after dust, influenced by the passion of South America.
Carbuncles are known for their adaptability, changing based on their environment and internal nature.

The critter group chasing after dust, filled by the passion of South America.
A communal, festive group of Carbuncles, they live for celebrations, parties, festivals, and endless sunshine and beaches!

Thugs active around the riverbank residential area, living off plunder.
Their true nature isn't necessarily dark—it's just that the city isn't ready for them.

Gatekeepers of the Apostles Brotherhood, also responsible for a variety of chores and busy work.

The gunmen of the Apostles Brotherhood, tasked with their unspeakable wet work.
They can appear in every corner of the city in the most ordinary of guises, indifferent to whether it's mud or blood on their hands.

Children who hang around the riverbank residential area, living seemingly carefree lives.
Youth is beautiful, blinding you from certain cruel and helpless realities.

Senior members of the Apostles Brotherhood, now retired from gang work to serve as the organization's strategists.
Though they've burnt-out their candles, they still support the Brotherhood from behind the scenes. Every organization has figures like them.

Enforcers of the Apostles Brotherhood, once stars of a certain fighting competition.
Though they may be retired prize fighters, they have long realized that no fighting technique is as reliable as a good shotgun.

Special operations combat personnel originally from the Zeno Arms Academy.
Crossing deep into enemy lines, fearless and bold, regardless of where the orders come from or where the road leads.

Regular combat personnel originally from the Zeno Arms Academy.
They are the most loyal soldiers in the unit, and as such, their loyalty is most often tested.

Combat personnel equipped with heavy firepower originally from the Zeno Arms Academy.
From fire support to frontline suppression, they wield formidable destructive power. They are the embodiment of intimidation.

Heavily armed combat personnel originally from the Zeno Arms Academy.
"No worries, just stand behind me." The most reassuring presence on the battlefield.

Frontline warfare personnel originally from the Zeno Arms Academy. 
Their role is to man stationary guns, protecting the rear of the frontline and acting as a solid defense for the team.

A Zeno officer known for his ruthless methods, despite that he cares deeply for his soldiers.
Although he lost his left eye in an arcanum accident, he remains a staunch arcanist advocate.

A body shaped by sacrifice, suffering, and flesh, bringing a moment of hope to the sufferer.
The cries of mortals turn to blood rising in their throats; fate has not shown mercy, and the heavens have not seen it.

A storm summoned from a mortal body, born from the rage of the suffering.
Listen to the howling wind—it never stops. It is as fierce as a maddened soul.

A Zeno officer, Admiral Igor's aide and adopted daughter.
Reserved and taciturn, she never hesitates to carry out her orders. Extremely capable, she handles many of the Admiral's most important tasks. In Lopera's eyes, she is a kind and gentle elder sister.

Old Patient Cobb.
The years he's spent lying in the hospital bed are as long as the wrinkles on his skin.
A secret weapon that puts patients peacefully to sleep.

A Manus Vindictae prisoner.
Wearing a mask of kindness, he has long awaited the coming night.

"Look, there's a lonely variable here. Shouldn't it be pulled into the equation and have a party with the other numbers?"
"Perhaps the perfect language will not be created by vocal chords and breath, but through logic and form. Hard concepts embedded in the universe itself ... "
"Huh ... Oh!! S-sorry, the answer is, uh, right, uhm, I guess ... C!"
"An infinite number of terms combined into one concise formula, much like the countless factors interacting in a system that ultimately causes a ball to fall. It's truly marvelous!"
"Verbal persuasion has proven ineffective, so we decided that every guideline would include a photo of a previous victim. Look, this month's accident rate has dropped by ... hmm, a full 5%!"
"Hydrochloric acid: slippery acrid taste, reminiscent of vomit. Nitric water: milder, akin to MSG and vinegar. An amalgam of lead and mercury—"
"These restraints are imposed by the cowardly upon the genius! If one is afraid of even the smallest of explosions, how can they seek the spark of progress?"
"This one, this one, and this one look fun to try ... Oh? What do you mean "prohibited?" Well, that's all the more reason to try them!"
"It looks complete, but there's still a slight deviation inside. I think I'm an ellipse."
"Everyone's heart is a picture drawn from dashed lines and dots, with gaps in desperate need of filling in."
"Hah, shape? What shape? You can't make a pile of mud into a shape!"
"Seven sides, each of different lengths, seven angles, all unequal; no axis of symmetry, neither sharp enough nor smooth enough. But I think, this is how I'm meant to be. It's fine."
"This isn't just some dusty old rock. Look closely, it's a piece of the moon I brought home."
"Shale is like a book, and this fossil's imprint tells the story of two trilobites ... Kid, that's just a metaphor, don't press your ear against the glass."
"Everything is more beautiful when she's beside me; with her a weathered old rock can look as beautiful as a statue of Venus!"
"The world is so noisy, it's no wonder some people prefer silence."
"What I can do is limited, but what I hope to do is endless."
"There are only two things that are infinite: the universe and human stupidity. And I'm not sure about the former ..."
"'Infinity' is so vast, yet it's expressed with just eight letters. Hah, language is fascinating!"
—An excerpt from a children's literature magazine
"Emergency doctors should pay attention to the quieter patients in the queue—if you still have the energy to make a fuss, odds are things aren't that serious."
"Sir, please believe me, there's no need to bring in our respiratory specialist to examine you. It really is just a common cold, really."
"That time I just hurt my foot, but ended up in the hospital hooked up to the drippers. Then my friend took too long to pick me up, so I fell asleep in the lobby ... "
"Children are so full of energy that they may not realize they're ill. It's the adults' responsibility to notice the signs."
"Don't make promises lightly. You may end up paying for it with half your life ... "
"They let me down, they took my money, my time, and worse, they betrayed my trust ... My VIP membership hadn't even expired when the club closed down!"
"Don't be so modest, good man! A borrowed cigar doesn't need to be repaid."
"Those directors promised they'd contact me for auditions next time. But it's been silence ever since ... "
"Pray you never run into them, but if you do, be able to do more than just pray."
"Why do people always avoid me? Is it because my eyebrows are a bit thick, my nose is a bit crooked, and my eyes are a bit small ... ? Do I just look like a bad guy?!"
"We spend a lot of time worrying about the dangers threatening our heads and our wallets; but consider the dangers threatening our souls—those dangers come from within."
"Aside from that, you may call me 'Mr. Wolf,' 'annoying mercenary,' or 'madman.' Really, I don't care."
"Law firms? The Foundation? Zeno? Don't count on any of those guys. We can only count on each other, on family!"
"I used to love running around, I never wanted to come back inside. Now I just want to stay home and chill all day."
"We're not related by blood, nor do we share the same last name—but we have weathered the storm together."
"Watch me closely. I will not bring shame upon my family's name!"
"No man ever steps in the same river twice, for it's not the same river and he's not the same man."
"A person cannot step into the same river even once!"
—A student of an ancient Greek philosopher
"The river's third bank? Look over there, there's a little boat made of cypress."
"To me, it seems like the rivers of your world are like a vast network of veins, I must admit I'm jealous."
"The water here is special; it's teeming with many different ideas, confusing yet enlightening ... "
"When I go for a walk, I can't help but start running ... It's the only way I can feel the wind's embrace!"
"Ladies and gentlemen, if you find any mushrooms during your cleaning, please don't touch, eat, or disturb them!"
"Hmm ... Should I use the red garbage bag, or the black one?"

Originating from the Middle East, the "succubi" race is fond of two things above all: slaughter and chaos. They achieve this via their ability to charm and captivate. Their powerful, unrestrained instincts sometimes drive them to venture into the complex and <nobr>ever-changing</nobr> human world.

The <nobr>celebrity-turned-spy</nobr> Mata Hari, as we now know, was a succubus. Her countless nights of banquets and lavish pleasures were destined to be <nobr>short-lived,</nobr> like a beautiful yet fleeting dream.

Their claws left scars. Humans came to understand the endless greed of succubi and grew fearful of them—and fear brings chaos. Eventually, Mata Hari was publicly executed. News and photographs spread everywhere, announcing an impending catastrophe that would affect all succubi.

Overnight, the succubi realm, human governments, and the Foundation all issued warrants to hunt down the succubi active in human society, including her <nobr>much-beloved</nobr> sister.

Nala Hari thus began her life of exile.

Pandora Wilson: A pile of faded <nobr>wind-up</nobr> toy fragments. Can you tell me about their story?
Anjo Nala: No! I won't! That was not a toy; it was a cage! It was a seal, with passages so narrow that I could barely crawl through their gaps.
Anjo Nala: And I could never learn how to crawl out!
Pandora Wilson: It sounds like you're lucky that you're even here talking with me now.

The End of the Privateers From the 16th to the 18th century, amid the maritime discoveries and tense rivalries, governments issued letters of marque to privateers, making them "legal pirates." However, as wars came to an end, privateers reverted back to their old ways. Most pirates would perish in fierce naval pursuits, but a few would struggle on, living a life of plunder and spoil despite being increasingly hunted. Occasionally, legends would surface of a captain who lived on after sinking to the ocean floor, or a pirate who escaped prison only to become a navy sailor, or an ancient pirate ship that hid inside a drifting bottle to avoid sinking. The Age of Exploration Also known as the Age of Great Voyages, explorers set foot on unknown lands, expanding maps of the known world. Although governments often complained about the immense financial cost involved, they quickly changed their tune when ships returned laden with gold, promoting the development of new trade routes. Ocean voyages meant adventure. Thanks to the spirit of adventure during the Age of Exploration, the world became dramatically more interconnected. The Last Dodo Extinct between 1688 and 1715. (However, a marine archaeologist who claims to have collected dodo droppings insists that a few dodos still live aboard a long-distance ocean vessel).

The captain said to cover the deck with plants to avoid drawing attention. She proudly showed off a few large birds, claiming they were probably the last dodos in the world. What's a dodo? Does it taste like turkey? The ship doesn't look much like a pirate ship anymore; more like a floating garden. I think we've lost our pride as pirates. The captain said she found what she had always wanted—it was a plain-looking bottle. We all thought she'd been scammed, as there is no shortage of conmen in Nassau. The captain told us that for things like this, you can't have any expectations. That was at least her wisdom after many years in the pirate trade. I'm not expecting much, but I do hope she can bear witness to the future for us ... ... It's all gone. I held onto a log, struggling to stay afloat, watching the fire spread on the deck from a distance. The garden is destroyed, everything is gone. Only our dodo flag is left. Damn the navy. ... ......... Whatever. I'm not going to live much longer anyway. I wonder if the captain took her away. I hope they will live on.
The Spirit of Exploration Lives On

The United Fruit Company, a U.S.-based corporation which chiefly dealt in tropical produce from poorer countries in Latin America, it possessed vast financial resources and extensive plantations, yet beneath its polished facade was a history of abuse and conflict with its workers that never stopped.

In Colombia, 1928: The oppression of the United Fruit Company sparked <nobr>large-scale</nobr> revolts. Plantation workers seized the transportation railways, expecting the company to engage in gentlemanly negotiations. However, the company instead bribed a portion of the workers to sell out their comrades.

The outcome was inevitable—there was no shortage of traitors willing to sell out their fellow workers for a few loaves of bread. After this shameful betrayal, calm was returned to the streets. The flame of resistance was extinguished. Hopeless lives drifted toward the same hopeless tomorrow, supporting the greed of some at the cost of others' misfortune.

As the United Fruit Company's expansion in Latin America continued, the region plunged into an economic depression. Low income workers coalesced into ever larger slums, and the abysmal living standards saw more and more young people turn to gangs. Latin America gradually sank into a quagmire.

Whenever she allows herself to reminisce, Lopera inevitably returns to that day.

In 1928, a little <nobr>four-year-old</nobr> Lopera first heard a sound she would eventually grow all too familiar with. She looked at her parents, at their anxious, strained smiles, and asked the kind of question every child asks.

"Are those fireworks? Is there a celebration?"

As her family traveled across Latin American countries, the days when Lopera heard those fireworks grew more frequent. Strangely enough, her parents would come home with fistfuls of money on those days, their faces always marked with anxiety and unease.

They moved into big houses, with many gifts and food, but Lopera felt increasingly estranged from her parents.

By 1936, at age 12, Lopera joined Zeno and became a soldier.

She experienced care from a "father" and "sister," warmth unlike anything she had felt before, honest familial love.

It wasn't until leaving home that Lopera understood what family truly meant.

The days at Zeno were so gratifying that they masked all her inner confusion. When the day finally arrived when she had to decide her loyalties, she was entirely unprepared.

Pandora Wilson: I must admit, I don't understand what I'm looking at.
Pandora Wilson: A wooden die made to look like any other, but always landing on an exact number. Blatant cheating.
Pandora Wilson: But do you usually show off this trick before inviting others to sit at the gambling table?
Lopera: No, usually, you need to hide everything you've got before you hit the table, because sometimes the stakes are your life.
Lopera: But this isn't one of those times.
Pandora Wilson: Could you share more of your thoughts on gambling?
Lopera: Gambling isn't very different from gunplay, sometimes you can achieve more with the right gamble than you can with a gun. But you always win more when you gamble with a gun—as long as you keep luck on your side.
Lopera: When the stakes are high and your life is riding on the chips, you feel a thrill—whether you've pulled a fast one or got caught <nobr>red-handed.</nobr> If you don't know that rush, it's because you've never bet anything worth losing.
Pandora Wilson: I see, I understand that betting on one's life is actually quite common.
Pandora Wilson: If we could move on, could you talk more about your experiences with Zeno?
Lopera: Experiences ... Once, I caused so much havoc it put Zeno into a deficit to pay for the clean up, and another time I was punished for accidentally injuring a comrade ...
Lopera: But nah, I don't really feel like getting into anything that serious. Today is just not one of those days, is it?
Pandora Wilson: Then it seems this is the end of our interview.

"This is 'Kuku,' a German Shepherd I brought back to the veteran's hospital from the trenches ten years ago." "This is 'Mira,' the rabbit. She grins when you feed her carrots!" The interviewee cheerfully introduced the inspiration behind his two patches, though the reality of them doesn't seem to match his enthusiasm.

An <nobr>arcanum-modified</nobr> weapon issued to the interviewee by the Zeno Brazil branch, intended to replace traditional tranquilizer guns.
As a blowgun, it boasts reliable performance; as a musical instrument, it can also help pass the time in retirement.

A new invention assembled from scrap metal collected over multiple days and nights, showcasing both skill and an eccentric taste.
"Living in the favelas isn't all bad; at least there's a scrapyard with a door that's always open, and they don't charge us a penny!" the interviewee says with a cheerfulness that belies his age.

Despite its lively reputation, São Paulo in the '90s was facing the melancholy and confusion that followed the end of the carnival and its own fading prosperity. Enthusiasm had faded, while the rich remained obscenely wealthy, the poor crowded into the world's largest slum.

Here, the first skill people learned was survival. Not even the basics like electricity, sewage and water facilities were regularly available, so it would flood drastically during the rainy season; infant mortality rates were alarmingly high; and hungry youths with nowhere to go would fall into gangs. Despite the gloom, the favelas continued to face a population boom.

The urban poor lived here with difficulty, yet bravely. Despite everything, they remained passionate, lively, optimistic, and ever restless. They faced the challenges and opportunities that came after hitting rock bottom with optimism and remained hopeful for an unclear future.

Perhaps they still believed that a hero would appear and bring a glimmer of life to this land—even if it was just a burst of joyous laughter.

The guys suggested I keep a diary. It's not my thing, but I'll do it to pass the time.

............

January 14th, today I saw a kid getting beaten up by a few others at the veterans' home entrance. I thought about helping, but he tripped them up with a rope and a dead knot, then made a clean getaway! Using wits to overcome adversity, he reminds me of my own childhood.

March 22nd, I received an obituary for Teo. The old man went first. How many years has it been since I met that <nobr>fresh-faced</nobr> kid in the expeditionary force?

May 8th, the TV's reporting another crackdown in some jungle, glorifying the achievements of the army. Pathetic. They completely ignore the real situation, just wantonly suppressing the resistance. That said, even if they let the guerrillas go, they wouldn't have anywhere to escape to, so it would be pointless in the end. But their will to survive and their honor won't be in vain.

June 30th, the guys said today is my birthday. I didn't even remember! I've been living here for so long now, and though it's quite comfortable, I'm always idle. I feel like I could still do more. If only I were a few years younger. Damn it, Duncan!
The Life of an Old War Dog

Mr. Duncan: This is a wine glass made from half a light bulb. It gives the wine an especially sweet kick. Here, give it a try, <nobr>ha-ha!</nobr>
Pandora Wilson: These little gadgets are interesting, but I'd rather talk about you.
Mr. Duncan: Ah, there's nothing too interesting about old Duncan.
Pandora Wilson: I disagree. You must have some glorious stories, perhaps something from your accomplishments during your military days.
Mr. Duncan: Forget it; there isn't any story there.
Pandora Wilson: Forgive me, but you don't get those medals without doing something worthy of a story.
Mr. Duncan: Take it from me—these things aren't even worth the tin they're made of. Let alone losing my wife.
Mr. Duncan: I had a comrade who entrusted his daughter to me in his dying breaths, not knowing she was already gone. What good are medals measured against the regrets they were purchased with?
Pandora Wilson: Many soldiers never receive the rewards they deserve; some call it unfair.
Mr. Duncan: So what? They'll still grow old, and life goes on. The days at the veterans' home may be dull, but at least I can still tinker with these little things.
Pandora Wilson: It sounds like you've moved on from the past.
Mr. Duncan: <nobr>Ha-ha,</nobr> I've said that to others too. I ...
Mr. Duncan: Hey, are you just trying to trick me into blabbing on about my old stories?!
Pandora Wilson: Apologies, it's just part of the interview process.

A colorful bedspread themed around the Brazilian coast, where the beach and ocean merge into a summer silhouette, originally intended for children who couldn't visit the beach.
The interviewee seems to have made a surprisingly resolute choice.

A barely usable plastic snorkeling mask, priced far above its actual cost. One of the mainstays that the street vendors hawk to passing tourists.
Not every journey goes as planned, but given the circumstances, she makes the best of it.

Once popular little trinkets in schools, they briefly became a form of currency for girls.
It's clear that the interviewee's sense of style remains rooted in a past summer, but it doesn't matter—at least they match her new bedspread.

A handmade sun hat, a <nobr>best-seller</nobr> on Copacabana Beach.
When asked about the difference between the white scenery she saw and what she read about in her books, the interviewee answers in a stifled voice while pressing her hat down until it completely covers her eyes. It reminds me of a previous interview.

A <nobr>cover-up</nobr> crocheted with colorful shells and starfish, it sways lightly with each step, sometimes making a crisp clinking sound. It was hard to get the shy interviewee to explain why she chose this outfit. Regardless, it's a unique and clever choice.

A durable, <nobr>medium-sized</nobr> handwoven straw purse, with a Bird of Paradise flower gifted by the vendor as a finishing touch. Carefully stored within are documents, notes, writing tools, special sunscreen, and a Brazilian Arcanum license.
When asked what these items were prepared for, she responds with a shy smile.

A pure white shawl with a mystical aura, intricately woven with openwork geometric patterns, serving as a doorway to ancient wisdom.
"Wearing geometry doesn't do much to inspire creativity," the interviewee calmly declares.

The finely woven fabric intertwining and extended with geometric logic, forming an almost perfect symmetrical structure. Of the naturally curved tassels, the interviewee says she could still feel some softness and flow even within the cold precision of geometry.

A pair of tropical <nobr>cave-dwelling</nobr> bird companions, primitive, mysterious, and enigmatic.
According to the interviewee, they sometimes part but never for long, they remain exactly as they were the day she arrived. Perhaps some things never change—at least she firmly believes so.

<nobr>Yellow-tinted</nobr> sunglasses bought at a local grocery store, offering no more protection than regular sunglasses. The interviewee simply feels the bright color suits the untamed rainforest better, and they weren't too expensive.

A repainted prosthetic limb with subdued colors to avoid drawing attention from rainforest friends, reinforced with cotton fabric to reduce the risk of accidents when encountering large animals.
"Hey, everything here is different from the mountains back then. I can't wait to dance with them!" Evidently, its owner has found new sources of joy.

The teeth of some carnivorous South American animal. A trophy isn't always paid for in blood; it can also be a token of friendship—or, of course, sold to local vendors for a good price when money is tight.

A common hair tie forgotten in a corner of the suitcase, with feathers that still seem to carry a trace of warm air. Though the interviewee isn't one to chase trends, her carefully considered choices succeed all the same.

A fringed shawl inspired by dense drooping leaves, exuding a subtle sheen under the sunlight. Unfolding it is like opening a page of a poem about the colorful summer.
Drifting atop the clear Sucuri River, no one cares about fashion. Fortunately, the interviewee doesn't mind, as she is here only for the water.

A warm, clear blue from the deepest part of the Sucuri River.
The indigo river bay is crystal clear, making it the perfect place for divination and extraordinary exotic sightseeing. After much consideration, the interviewee decides to simply cherish this source and remember the beautiful journey with her own eyes.

A transparent skirt, more decorative than practical, resembling waves that silently recede before dawn. The <nobr>fish-tail</nobr> design, rippling like water, was inspired by a beautiful vision of a certain oceanic race.
The interviewee mentions that she once had concerns about its origin, but no longer.

<nobr>Locally-crafted</nobr> handwoven straw sandals. Their beauty lies in the patterns created by the intertwining strands rather than any printed decoration.
"I prefer to focus on people's lives, that is where art is the most vibrant." It seems the interviewee understands art better than many <nobr>self-proclaimed</nobr> critics.

A local <nobr>vine-woven</nobr> craft, exquisite, unique, and practical. Materials like seasonal flowers and sparkling shells give it a touch of natural beauty.
There is no doubt that this is what the interviewee considers to be "art from life."

Abnormal, family Canine-form. Native to North America, constantly emits steam and smiles.

Teakettler, of the order Abnormal, family Canine-form. These small, hound-like creatures, sporting a pair of cat ears, maintain the same expression from birth to death—a suggestive, alluring smile that invites endless imagination. It's said that a mysterious creature brought back from the "new world" inspired Leonardo da Vinci's work, and it might have been a Teakettler.

They can emit a high-pitched sound similar to that of a boiling kettle, while continuously releasing a fine mist of steam. Known for their exceptionally acute sense of smell, Teakettlers have a particular fondness for the scent of fresh foliage. There have been multiple sightings of Teakettlers reported at logging camps in Minnesota and Wisconsin. To this day, the tale of "Teakettlers and fresh tea leaves" remains a popular urban legend among American lumberjacks.

By befriending these little creatures, you'll find that their thoughtful companionship and appreciation for fine tea far outweigh the value of an antique teapot.
Amphibian, family Fish-form. A mysterious, amorphous creature that inhabits waters near ancient ruins.

Abang Akus, of the order Amphibian, family Fish-form. These mysterious critters constantly change their shape and color. They are adept at hiding, gentle, sensitive, and highly attuned to the emotions of other living beings.

Abang Akus's preferred habitats are quite particular: they like to hide in the waters near ancient ruins, quietly and curiously observing every visiting explorer, even silently following in their footsteps. These critters are natural lovers of stories, be they about architecture or human. To help visitors and hear their stories, Abang Akus will even use its body to assist them in reaching hard-to-climb places. Due to their advanced shapeshifting and cloaking abilities, what most people notice is merely a flash of light or a particularly soft footstep while climbing. After the visitors leave, the Abang Akus will silently slip back into its watery home.

Due to their rarity and secrecy, Abang Akus were long thought to be fictional until Ms. NewBabel encountered one at a South Asian ruin and ascended the tower alongside it, gaining its trust. While they adore ruins in the Wilderness, they won't turn down a well-placed transparent tank with a good view.
Avian, family Bird-form. An exceptionally accurate predator, often found near human construction sites.

Tripodero, also known as the Tripod Bird, of the order Avian, family Bird-form. An exceptionally accurate predator, held in awe and veneration by hunters who roam the American countryside. Yes, this long-legged bird, whose legs can stretch far, is known for shooting mucus with perfect accuracy, knocking out its prey from way above. Its aim is impeccable, and it has a sturdy tail that acts as support, helping it maintain balance (hence its name). It typically appears near construction sites, railways, and engineering facilities, becoming the subject of folklore among the local workers.

However, despite Tripodero's formidable offense capabilities, legends tell of young railway workers who have bested Tripodero in contests, forming bonds with it and becoming exceptional hunters. Many hunters have tried to recreate this feat by seeking out a Tripodero near engineering projects, though they often either return empty-handed or are found passed out in the wilderness.
Abnormal, family Feli-form. Native to the Americas, these critters are widely distributed. Undoubtedly, they are ferocious tree destroyers.

Splintercat, of the order Abnormal, family Feli-form. These large, cat-like critters are widely distributed across the Americas, from the Great Lakes to the Gulf of Mexico, and even eastward to the Atlantic coastline. Wherever forests grow, sightings of Splintercats racing through storms are common.

On stormy nights, the rain-soaked fur of these creatures generates small lightning bolts, signaling the time to hunt. They use their solid heads to ram trees where bees nest, sparking lightning until they find their favorite honey and voraciously devour it with fresh twigs. Uninformed people often believe the fallen trees were struck down by natural lightning.

Getting close to these great cats isn't difficult; they are brave and loyal, and they love having their ears and necks scratched. You'll fall in love with their storm-cloud-like fur and the thunderous purring sounds they make. However, if you have trees in your yard, for the sake of your landscaping, be sure these fluffy creatures are well-fed before letting them in.
Abnormal, family Carbuncle. Widely distributed, suspected to have originated in Europe. Prefers to gather in groups and excels at mimicking human behavior.

Refined Groupbuncle, of the order Abnormal, family Carbuncle, is a variant of the Carbuncle species.

You are, of course, familiar with the Carbuncles, a type of critters found across the world, fond of dust and gathering in groups. They are dull, oblivious, and eat without fuss, but they are also adaptable, fond of imitation, and full of infinite potential.

The Refined Groupbuncles often appear in big cities. They are imitators of human civilization and enthusiastic socialites among critters. A Refined Groupbuncle's fine collection could astound even a true gentleman. Refined Groupbuncles spend long hours grooming each other's fur and critiquing each other's appearance. If you want to join their elegant critter salon, perhaps a shiny gift—whether an expensive gold pocket watch or a delicious yet affordable chocolate coin—can quickly help you bond with them.
Avian, family Columbidae, previously considered extinct. Said to originate from the "Wonderland." A great companion for tea parties and naps.

Dodough, of the order Avian, family Columbidae. These large, fluffy, flightless birds had long been classified as extinct, but to many arcanists, they are rare critters. It is said that the true homeland of the dodoughs is the "Wonderland", where they are friends of the Cheshire Cat, Caterpillar, and Mad Hatter, all capable of traveling freely between reality and the "Wonderland." Due to excessive hunting and invasive species, the last group of dodoughs migrated back to the "Wonderland" around the 17th century, leading human biologists to classify them as extinct.

Like other residents of the "Wonderland," the dodoughs can enlarge or shrink their bodies at will. They spend their days leisurely strolling around, having tea parties, and daydreaming. Returning to their infant form, sleeping inside an eggshell during a long afternoon nap, is one of their greatest enjoyments. Their unique "doo-doo" call can guide people through dreams to visit a corner of the "Wonderland," and perhaps it even helped inspire a certain mathematician's creation of Wonderland tales.
Abnormal, family Canine-form. Native to North America. Lively and cheerful with a great appetite. Better watch your axe.

Axe-handle Hound, of the order Abnormal, family Canine-form. Who wouldn't love this lively little dog-like critter? Well, maybe lumberjacks have a different opinion ...

True to its name, the body of the Axe-handle Hound resembles a wooden axe handle, while its head looks like an axe head, and its nose is as sharp as an axe blade. These creatures can be found in logging camps after dark, searching for their favorite food—delicious wooden axe handles. Generally, Axe-handle Hounds enjoy the company of humans, and any game a puppy loves applies to them as well. If you want to have this critter as a companion without giving up your woodworking, we suggest using a red oak handle for your axe—it's the only type of wood these hungry little critters don't like.
Abnormal, family Carbuncle. Widely distributed, often found in orchards. Gentle and juicy little creatures; you won't forget them.
Kin: Refined Groupbuncle, Carbuncle, Beastbuncle, Cartoncle.

Orangebuncle, of the order Abnormal, family Carbuncle, is a variant of the Carbuncle species.
You are, of course, familiar with the Carbuncles, a type of critters found across the world, fond of dust and gathering in groups. They are dull, oblivious, and eat without fuss, but they are also adaptable, fond of imitation, and full of infinite potential.

Orangebuncle is a species particularly skilled at camouflage, living in orchards where they almost perfectly resemble juicy, sweet fruits. Compared to their kin, they are more gentle and prefer sweet fruits and leaves. Some rumors suggest that these Carbuncles are linked to dreams. "A dream of Orangebuncles represents a call from memories," said one dream interpreter.
Avian, family Bird-form. Native to the Americas. A brightly-colored critter with only one wing. Do not attempt to capture on your own.

Pinnacle Grouse, of the order Avian, family Bird-form. This beautiful bird is a distant relative of the grouse, but its differences are obvious: it has a spiral-shaped sharp beak and only one wing, so it can only fly in one direction. Conical mountains are the ideal habitat for Pinnacle Grouses, where they circle the peaks while foraging. The feathers of the Pinnacle Grouse change color with the seasons, and it's said that their colors appear different to different observers.

The ever-changing feather colors and delicious meat (since these birds look so much like grouse, people are tempted to taste them, but when asked "Who has eaten Pinnacle Grouse?" the answer is usually vague) lead many to try capturing them, as their solitary wing gives the illusion of clumsiness. However, the Pinnacle Grouse's wing is sharper than the finest blade, and few can escape its flesh-splitting strike.
Abnormal, family Carbuncle. Widely distributed. You're certainly familiar with these little creatures.
Kin: Refined Groupbuncle, Orangebuncle, Beastbuncle, Cartoncle.

Carbuncle, of the order Abnormal, family Carbuncle, is the most typical and ancient variety of the large Carbuncle species.

You are, of course, familiar with the Carbuncles, a type of critters found across the world, fond of dust and gathering in groups. They are dull, oblivious, and eat without fuss, but they are also adaptable, fond of imitation, and full of infinite potential.

Carbuncles come in various sizes, from tiny furballs you can hold in your palm to massive furry monsters that prowl through junkyards. Many reported monster sightings have been confirmed to be Carbuncles. The most primitive of the Carbuncles have some distinctive traits: they only love dust and turn their noses up at any trendy food their relatives might fancy. As for their living environment, they prefer messy junk heaps and dark thickets. "A place that's too tidy, too bright, and with too many humans? No way. We must uphold the great tradition!" says one noble Carbuncle.
Order: Amphibian, family Fish-form. Mostly found in high-latitude regions, covered entirely in fur—don't get any ideas about that fur.

Furry Anglerfish, of the order Amphibian, family Fish-form. To survive in the icy waters of the far north, these fish-like critter have evolved to develop warm fur. They usually remain still for long periods, posing as a clump of furry seaweed while using the glowing lure on their head to attract and hunt fish. Occasionally, some Furry Anglerfish would come ashore, using their fins to crawl slowly and snack on insects for a change of taste.

Their fur is thick and warm. A century ago, ignoring the locals' warning, an explorer tried to hunt Furry Anglerfish to sell gloves made of their fur. Soon after, his entire body grew similar fur—though not nearly as beautiful as the Furry Anglerfish's.
Amphibian, family Snail-form. Native to the Baltic Sea. A large snail-like critter, slow-moving, with extraordinarily keen hearing.

Sarmatian Sea Snail, of the order Amphibian, family Snail-form. These gentle, clumsy snail-like critter have fully lost their eyesight, and their pair of antler-like, hardened forked horns have become their most sensitive organs, helping them hear everything nearby—especially strange rumors.

It is said that after the Sarmatian Sea Snails have listened to enough rumors, their horns would secrete pearl-like substances. Depending on the nature and bizarreness of the rumors, these pearls may glow different colors and shine in the dark. Through certain arcane skills, people can extract the stories contained within these pearls. Some people even raise and train these snails to collect pearls or uncover secrets. But beware: some pearls formed from certain rumors can be highly toxic, and not all stories are safe to hear.
Abnormal, family Carbuncle. Widely distributed, often appearing in the wilderness. A fierce branch of the Carbuncle species with a habit of collecting trophies.
Kin: Refined Groupbuncle, Orangebuncle, Carbuncle, Cartoncle.

Beastbuncle, of the order Abnormal, family Carbuncle, is a variant of the Carbuncle species.

You are, of course, familiar with the Carbuncles, a type of critters found across the world, fond of dust and gathering in groups. They are dull, oblivious, and eat without fuss, but they are also adaptable, fond of imitation, and full of infinite potential.

Some Carbuncles have chosen a life of savagery, with Beastbuncles being a prime example. These creatures love to collect trophies, including bones, teeth, and red ochre. They seem to have mastered the art of intimidation, wearing masks and painting themselves to show off their ferocity to enemies. However, some critter behaviorists argue that this seemingly feral instinct is just another form of imitation—who knows for certain?
Amphibian, family Crab-form. Native to low-latitude shallow waters, suitable for domestic breeding. The coveted partner of diviners everywhere.

Moon-eyed Fiddler, of the order Amphibian, family Crab-form. These rare little creatures are highly associated with the lunar cycle and tides! No wonder diviners have been flocking to these crabs since ancient times.

The markings on the Moon-eyed Fiddler's back resemble a strange human face, and depending on the tide cycle, moon phases, and the crab's physical condition, this "face" will change expressions. For experienced diviners, "crab divination"—interpreting the subtle smiles or frowns on the crab's shell—holds secrets as profound as astrology. It is said that a well-trained group of Moon-eyed Fiddlers can even replace an astrolabe, as long as they are regularly replenished with fresh seawater, and they can provide accurate guidance.

However, catching a Moon-eyed Fiddler is no easy feat. When in the water, it projects a shadow resembling a small moon, and this projection changes in a manner akin to the phases of the moon.
Abnormal, family Carbuncle. Widely distributed, commonly spotted in homes. Yes, the allure of a cardboard box is just that irresistible ...
Kin: Refined Groupbuncle, Orangebuncle, Carbuncle, Beastbuncle.

Cartoncle, of the order Abnormal, family Carbuncle, is a variant of the Carbuncle species.

You are, of course, familiar with the Carbuncles, a type of critters found across the world, fond of dust and gathering in groups. They are dull, oblivious, and eat without fuss, but they are also adaptable, fond of imitation, and full of infinite potential.

Light-blocking, private, comfortable, and secure—what Carbuncles could resist having their very own cardboard box? Some little creatures choose to become inseparable from their beloved box. If your discarded boxes are making strange noises, don't be alarmed; it's likely that some little Carbuncles have made a home inside. Getting closer to them is easy—just offer a dust-filled can. However, if you're not ready to add a new family member, you can contact Ms. NewBabel's Critter Rehabilitation Center, and we'll help find these little ones a proper home.

In that quiet home, Melania found a beautiful necklace. She remembered how her father had been secretly working on it for the past few months. Sadly, her birthday was still two months and ten days away.
In 1928, the British poet and novelist Thomas Hardy passed away. Necrologist privately noted in her diary that he was "a master of a unique form of elegy."
Mercuria moves gracefully in harmony to Voyager's music, their unspoken communication representing a level of beauty that transcends language.
Bleary-eyed from writing through the night of her birthday, Marcus notices the Sachertorte Зима left her for the morning.
In a firm tone, Sophia instructs 37 to eat more of the veggies piled on her plate.

Argus's off-road vehicle breaks down in the middle of nowhere, leaving her no choice but to hitch a ride with a band of hippies. She forces herself to sleep, avoiding their conversations and the trance-inducing sound of their psychedelic rock.
J and his friends tweak their exhaust pipes, ensuring that their rides will always leave the cops in the dust.
Enigma, going through his mundane daily routine at the lab, receives a letter from his sister detailing her recent experiences, accompanied by some mail-order publications.
In 1964, the United States started to regulate cigarette advertisements, requiring warning labels on packaging. Argus looks at the cowboy figure on the pack and shrugs indifferently.

While unleashing a flying kick at a piñata, Lopera accidentally smashes Sotheby's bottle of Glitzy Sticky Syrup #32. But thanks to the mishap, Sotheby stumbles upon Lopera's inventive snack recipes and finds a new source of inspiration.
Anjo Nala learned to make caipirinha, but one sip left Old Quitéria with a sour taste in her mouth for the rest of the day, no matter what she ate—whether it's bread, sweet potatoes, or bean stew.
White Rum and Lilya become engrossed in conversation over a steady flow of drinks. Later, they rely on the skeletal hand to steady the rocking ship on their way home.
In 1963, while The Beatles were dominating the British pop charts, Regulus hijacked half the country's radio stations to play their singles.
Mr. Duncan pieces together a disco ball from scraps of metal, and every child in the favela watches in awe as it begins to twirl and sparkle.
After realizing that Tuesday is the owner of The Eyes in the Forest, Argus takes drastic measures to prevent the book from ever entering Cristallo's room.
In 1890, Nellie Bly circumnavigated the globe in just 72 days, 6 hours, 11 minutes, and 14 seconds. She accomplished this feat with her arcanum imbued traveling bag at her side.
In 1924, Saint Petersburg was renamed Leningrad. Then in 1992, a referendum was held to restore its former name in honor of Peter the Great, and also marking the end of the Soviet era.

In 1967, in the aftermath of the Apollo 1 fire that claimed the lives of three astronauts, the Laplace Scientific Computing Center began to assist in the development of advanced fiberglass spacesuits with special coatings.
In 1980, the Yinshan rock paintings were discovered. Mercuria could sense distinct energy waves emanating from their carved symbols.
One night, Pioneer brings half a bottle of whiskey to help a lovesick chef regain his determination before serving the restaurant the next day.
In 1595, William Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet premiered. Charlie, part of the People's Troupe, is a regular viewer of this play.
Argus's visit leaves the scent of hand-rolled smokes in the stairwell. After standing there for one minute and fourteen seconds, Mesmer Jr. instructs the staff to "escort" Argus outside.
Lilya wins a drunken spar, but Su-01ве ends up with a scratch. Thanks to Mr. Duncan's expert repairs, Lilya is spared from further torment.
During recess, Blonney absently doodles a little monster. Her classmate mistakes it for a pink bunny, until it looks up and reveals its four eyes and fangs.
In 1918, The New York Times became a national publication. Barbara would often find copies of the paper among the gifts sent to her as a child.
Once again, Pioneer tries to coax Rabies's small animal companion to perch on his shoulder.
In 1971, during the historic Apollo 14 lunar landing, one of the support personnel was from the Laplace Scientific Computing Center, responsible for ground communications.
TTT's twelfth effort to connect with Sonetto is interrupted by a power surge. In the ensuing darkness, Sonneto suppresses a strong urge to use a teleportation disk and escape the scene.
In 1974, one of the most iconic Western parodies of all time hit theaters: Blazing Saddles. Argus looks back on this film with nostalgic fondness, reminding her of her youth and simpler times.
Old Quitéria finds Anjo Nala's diary in a box under the bed, only to remember that it was she herself who put it there ten years ago.
As Avgust takes a bite of hard bread, one of his lower canines comes loose. The Tooth Fairy quickly collects it and assesses the development of the new tooth.
Diggers expresses his deep respect for the Fogwalker's ideas. However, after silently looking at his watch for 10 minutes and 32 seconds, the Fogwalker finally replies that it's time to clock out.
The hand on Dikke's shoulder causes one of the new Foundation employees to freeze in shock, while Ms. NewBabel's Orangebuncle jumps around excitedly, trying to play with it.
Of the ten drinking sessions Lilya proposed to Vila, eight were turned down.
Kakania is stunned after talking to Sotheby—she too comes from a prestigious family, but she seems to be free of any inner constraints or repressions.
In 1946, the world's first electronic computer, ENIAC, was created. The LSCC was one of the first to have access to it, and was the only organization that did not use it for ballistics calculations.
By 9:00 a.m., Windsong is already sipping on her morning vodka with a lemon twist, claiming it as her secret to unlocking inspiration.
Anjo Nala performs the Colonel's poem for the elderly, exploring themes of love, death, war, silence, and an elusive "homeland" that is both close and forever out of reach.
A chance meeting between Eternity and Ms. NewBabel quickly turns into a delightful conversation. After an hour and 32 seconds, Tennant also joins in the exchange.
In 1957, the influential American astronomer and astrophysics pioneer Russell passed away. The Computing Center presented a bouquet of flowers in honor of his contributions.
Balloon Party tried to decorate Lilya's ride with balloons and lights. An epic 30 minute chase ensued.

In 1943, a hole spewing lava opened up in a cornfield in Parícutin, burying the village and marking the birth of the Parícutin volcano. It quickly became a point of fascination for arcanists around the world.
37 and John Titor engaged in a discussion that no third party could possibly comprehend.
Matilda proposed a challenge to Sonetto, offering her Orbuculum as a bet for the top spot in the upcoming test. Sonetto pondered whether she should purposely get a few questions wrong.
In 1987, the light from SN 1987A reached Earth. Recently, Regulus has been working on a telescope that can observe the remnants of the supernova.
An-an Lee cooks up a barbecue using energy from exorcised spirits and invites Sonetto to join her. Sonetto declines, citing pressing work commitments.
While working as a dishwasher, J noticed a child sneaking into the kitchen to scavenge for leftover bones and decided to buy him a burrito.

A tug-of-war between Ulrich and Enigma over the usage permissions of the lab saw Ulrich repeatedly securing it with a code, only for Enigma to repeatedly crack it. After this constant back-and-forth, the lab became accessible only to the two of them.

Mr. Duncan flips through an old photo album with the elders at the veterans' residence. When he gets to a certain page, he can't bear to turn it, so he excuses himself to continue inspecting the wheelchairs.
In 1972, the U.S. launched the Jupiter-bound spacecraft "Pioneer 10," which carried a gold-anodized aluminum plaque bearing a message from humanity. The message was designed, in part, by the LSCC.
In 1994, Nirvana performed their last gig in Munich. Regulus "borrowed" an album from the Foundation, and Sonetto "helped" her clean up the paperwork afterward.
Ezra's delicious pickled crab mushrooms were such a hit, he saved a jar for Sonetto while she was out in the field. In return, she gave him a guide on selecting the perfect mushroom coffee.
In 1900, Sven Hedin unearthed the ruins of the ancient city of Loulan. Among the ruins, he found a shard of pottery etched with an incantation.

Along with the snails, Flutterpage included some food from home in her delivery for the "witch." As she chased Flutterpage away, Willow opened the jar to find a delicious serving of creamy mashed potatoes inside.
Although Vila often asks the Tooth Fairy to take care of the children, she couldn't quite understand the purpose of collecting their baby teeth.

While stealing from a kitchen, Kimberly is stopped in her tracks by the sound of a child crying in hunger. Despite her own rumbling tummy, she leaves a jar of stewed potatoes and half a chicken for the child to eat.
Barbara and Argus spend an entire day listening to country music together.
Druvis III remained perfectly still in the quiet forest all day. A blue-winged bird, mistaking her for part of the scenery, landed on her finger.

After losing to Argus in a game of roulette, Lopera reluctantly honored the bet and followed An-an Lee's instructions to make a set of Yin-Yang 3D imaging lenses that could see ghosts. She wore them for the rest of the day.
Willow remained completely impervious to Tennant's flirtatious advances. The result was a failure of epic proportions.
Bkornblume bought a whole package of Lübeck marzipan and took one for herself. As she was walking, she ran into Sonetto and offered her the second piece.
In 1991, computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee introduced the concept of the World Wide Web to the world, coincidentally on the same day that TTT was celebrating her birthday.

Desert Flannel transformed Poltergeist's bedsheet into a glittering spectacle adorned with rhinestones and plastic flowers. Mercuria, arriving to help Poltergeist with an energy healing session, paused at the door and briefly thought she had been teleported to a San Francisco nightclub.

In 1932, the photography industry mourned the passing of George Eastman, the inventor of Kodak cameras. Click, a loyal user of Kodak products, has always regarded them as the gold standard in the camera industry.
Despite spending a whole afternoon and drinking almost half a case of Dr. Papper, Regulus and X still couldn't figure out Melania's "Acey."
In Lopera's dream, someone asked her who she was pointing her gun at. After waking, she decided to erase the dream from her memory.
Flutterpage stepped into Willow's home for the first time and immediately noticed her glistening gold medal.
A motorcycle shop owner offers J a helmet as a token of thanks for putting down some trouble. J picks the blue one but pauses, unsure of his sister's current preferences.
In 1966, The Sound of Music wins Best Picture at the 38th Academy Awards. On that same day, Charlton sneaks Pickles into the cinema for the first time, tucked inside his bag.
Flutterpage lingered at Willow's doorway for an hour, twenty minutes, and thirty seconds, counting the leaves whisked away by the wind as she listened to the clanging of metal against the floor.
Try as she might, Yenisei just can't figure out the nature of the lake water stored in the suitcase.

"Balloons, Cartoncles, tape, and plenty of creativity—these are the reasons for the safety regulations updates."
"Please remember to check the lost and found board regularly—especially the pictures. We often struggle to identify the official names of these creations."

Children love bright colors and sweet scents, so Orangebuncle makes an ideal playmate—as long as you're okay with juice splashing on your bed sheets.

"Business cards, a smile, and just the right amount of persuasion—they can always touch the deepest part of your heart, revealing needs you didn't even know you had."

"At this eloquent tea party, the tea leaves selected by the Teakettler were unanimously praised by all the connoisseurs. It is reported that the Critter Center is working on bringing them to market."
"No one is more suited to the stage than Teakettler. It does not need a script, nor rehearsal. It is always smiling and smiling, from the rise of the curtain till the end of the play."

Abang Akus? Not catchy enough. Tripodero? Too hard to remember. How about ... Sarmatian Sea Snail? Snail Radio?

Moon-eyed Fiddlers? Not bad. With some clever packaging, they should fetch a good price.
I think I'll go ask an old friend of mine.
See if they can help these staff members find a more suitable new home, heh heh.
Freshly fallen, blood-soaked, and covered with drool ...
It looks like my collection is about to grow again.
I gave Ms. NewBabel a jar of special "candy" as a token of my appreciation.

Oh wow! Patterns I've never seen before, with a beautiful tail and powerful hooves!
Aha stop! Your feathers are tickling me. You're trying to make friends with me, aren't you?

This reminds me of the time Sophia and I searched for all kinds of natural geometric shapes.

Wow, there are so many mysterious creatures here! A multi-legged beast with a human face on its back, a large Carbuncle dressed in a tuxedo ... I've never seen them before!

People often say that critters don't have the social manners fit for artistic gatherings, but in my opinion, you are undoubtedly a well-mannered gentleman.
This Axe-handle Hound seems to be interested in my arcane wand.
What's the matter, little one? Would you like one of your own? Let me craft an arcane wand that even a critter can use.
I remember the Critter Center guide mentioning your aversion to red oak. Don't worry, I'll choose the perfect wood for your wand.
The Moon-eyed Fiddler, a critter that influences the lunar cycle and tides. Pour out a cup of seawater, and it will come.
There are still many mysterious phenomena beyond the island, and what I know is far from comprehensive.
The pursuit of knowledge is a virtue. We must continue our studies, starting with this peculiar face.
Let's see here, there's workshops, more workshops, and some kind of lounge—ha, who'd waste their break time watching silly movies anyway?
You ought to build a racetrack, and bring in plenty of chew toys!
Lemme have a taste here... Hm, beef-flavored? A bit bland, but not bad.
Send three dozens to my lab! And put it on the Critter Center's tab! We need it for our collaborative research, of course.
The kids love outdoor art classes, whether they are observing sunflowers in the garden or watching seagulls at the harbor.
Different creatures never fail to spark their amazement and joy. And of course, they also love having free time.
When it comes to critters, I believe we should conduct similar activities, introducing the kids to these little creatures.
This will promote understanding and change, starting with ourselves and passing on to the younger generation.
I will make sure to suggest this idea to Ms. NewBabel.
Axe-handle Hounds love forests, Pinnacle Grouses fly around mountain peaks, and Furry Anglerfish prefer cold climates.
Your Wilderness provides a home for each of these critters, catering to their individual needs.
I believe this is because they are under the care of someone like you.
You have a deep understanding of each visitor's differences and treat them with equal acceptance.
I eagerly look forward to our continued cooperation. The future lies in our united hands.
During field exploration, critters are our reliable partners.
On the tundra, it is often more likely to encounter one of these mischievous friends than a human.
For me, that is perfectly fine—they don't need you to put on fake smiles during negotiations, and they treat all academic theories with equal indifference.
After all, Kikituks only care about whether your boots and toes are tasty or not.
If you happen upon a kind-hearted Ijiraq and share a sip of vodka, it might just keep you warm under a deerskin cloak.
So, I tried to use a mirror to reflect an Abang Akus.
In the mirror, it emitted a soft glow, and changed the shape of its body—identical to its form outside the mirror, yet somehow different.
The psychology of these creatures is a peculiar subject; I wonder if one day critter psychology will be considered as absurd as electroshock therapy.
But wasn't psychoanalysis just as crazy when it was first proposed?
Regardless, I sure want to give it a try.
We were taught Critterology in class, and I memorized all the textbook descriptions.
But touching them with my own hands is entirely different.
You remember the notes, right? "Abang Akus has a smooth, elastic texture, slightly sticky and damp ... "
Today, I noticed how incredibly soft it is, almost like a cool scarf.
I have a strong desire to learn more. Will you join me, Timekeeper?
The swinging automatic feeder, the crackling bouncing ball ... No, I've already used those ideas five years ago.
Do you have any other interesting suggestions?
For example, we could add a button to this thing here, "When the Splintercat wags its tail, an arcanum insect parade will appear in the Wilderness!"
Oh, don't worry, I'll make precise calculations for its range and scale.
What's that? You've had enough of strange insects?
Crabomancy is indeed a unique branch of divination, but in my opinion, the role of the Moon-eyed Fiddler is overrated.
Nothing compares to the clarity and sharpness of the Orbuculum, certified by the great Ms. Matilda herself.
Clear your mind and touch the surface of the crystal with your fingertips, and it will reveal the inner world of the seeker.
That's far more worthy of interpretation than what's on a crab shell!
The new trial seems successful. I think it's time to update that old guidebook and remove another page from it.
Confidence, encouragement, and anticipation—these surprises will come true, just as the Timekeeper predicted.
Through the use of divination and her natural talents, Ms. Bouanich achieves success once more!
I see! You're also a fan of the tale of Typhon conquering the Auto Island, aren't you?
This sample here deserves observation ... and research funding!
We should commence the experiment immediately and find the variable that leads to progress.
You enjoy my songs, don't you? I have plenty more where that came from, and even more after that ...
Fascinating, let me see what you've learned ...
You've got such a spacious suitcase, Master.
I wish that ugly toy were half as roomy as this, so I could shape myself however I like and do whatever I want.
It's so spacious here that I can easily find a spot to sing without disturbing anyone.
You're so considerate, but I'm fine like this. Staying in human form makes me feel at ease.
As for when I'm sleeping? ... That's a bit like snoring. Nobody wants to snore, but it's hard to control.
Sometimes I wonder if I should expand my knowledge of advanced alchemy. It might come in handy in times of need.
There's quite a few skilled arcanists around here. Do you have any good alchemy mentors to recommend, Vertin?
Sotheby ... She does seem capable of concocting anything, but her methods are way too expensive for me.
Still, her tricks for hiding things are impressive. How can she fit so many potions into one dress and still move about freely?
Regulus? An alchemist? All she ever talks about is rock and old pop music. I thought she was just some kind of music enthusiast, always up to no good.
... Now that you mention it, she did introduce herself as a genius alchemist when we first met.
That means APPLe must be one rock star of a mentor, huh?
Yesterday morning, I put extra oil in my hair, and three people called me Karson before the day was over.
If this keeps up, I'll start turning my head whenever I hear "Karson." That won't do.
What's Karson usually like? I'd hate to start imitating someone I don't even know.
Forget it, bad influence on the kids.
Maybe I ought to try a more hip hairstyle; this mature look isn't doing me any favors.
Do you think I'd look younger if I grew my bangs out to cover one of my eyes?
I just met that so-infamous "Rock Pirate." She's far more audacious than I imagined.
Not even I would dare to cross the Royal Navy, but she was wreaking havoc on the Thames without a care in the world!
You should never underestimate the younger generation.
A misunderstanding? Impossible. I have a keen eye for distinguishing between liars and truth-tellers.
Her confidence was unmistakable. The stories of her causing mayhem on the Thames seemed plausible, especially the part about drinking pepper straight with water for fun.
Sometimes, it feels like I can still hear the ticking of the winder, and the suffocating grip around my neck never loosens.
It was unbearable, so I did everything I could to please each new master.
Murderers are drawn to dangerous women, while children seek out nurturing sisters. And then there's Manus Vindictae ... They were a chaotic mess. I've never encountered anything like them.
As for the current me ... Is this the real me, or am I still shaping myself to your preferences, Master?
Oh? Then what do you like?
Maybe I can make a few changes ... based on my own thoughts and ideas this time.
A life like right now is already great! I have the freedom to live without harming others, a comfortable bed to sleep in, the ability to sing my heart out, and guaranteed food.
Even if this life is shaped by your will, I'm more than happy to play along for you.
Want to play a game, Vertin?
One of us stands and falls back, while the other catches them.
No, you're the one falling. I'll be the one catching you.
I trust you completely, so there's no need to test my trust in you.
Ha ha, no need for bets or tricks this time; it's just a fun little game.
Although, if we want to make it more exciting, let's bet on our mutual trust.
A suitcase like this couldn't be made with conventional craftsmanship alone. Arcanum is truly amazing.
But what happens if someone bothers us while we're all inside the suitcase?
It's a pretty attention-grabbing piece of work, after all. Curious kids could easily cause some mischief if they stumble upon it.
Aha, Old Duncan is always on the lookout for these types of problems.
I've got an idea—what if we attached a hot air balloon to the suitcase?
That way, when no one is watching, it can quietly float away to the safety of the sky.
Just remember to tie it to a rope so it doesn't drift off too far during the night.
This suitcase is a real treasure. How much can it hold? Can anyone enter without your permission?
Having a flask that can shrink an entire ship is already amazing, but this suitcase seems to do even more.
No, I've moved on from the seafaring life.
But it's true that this suitcase could do so many incredible things—like dodging cannon fire or even creating a sanctuary for dodos.
Haha, the worth of treasure is determined by the beholder. How true that is.
I'll never trade it with you. This bottle was left to me by Anne, afterall.
Try not to scare the others.
He insisted on using refined language.
Was there some kind of misunderstanding?
This isn't exactly part of my preferences.
What kind of life do you want?
You got another big score in mind?
I think the shrinking bottle is better.

The Bumping Gumball Machine mixes the best elements of two Gumballs to create a mixed Gumball.
Mixed Gumballs are a great way to lure in and attract new critters.
Please note that mixed Gumballs can only attract new critters of the same type involved in the mixing, or their variants.
Tap here to add a Gumball to the mixing.
Tap here to preview the flavors of this mixing attempt.
Critters lured in by <nobr>high-quality</nobr> Gumballs will grow more during training.
Mixing gumballs of different qualities makes it easier to attract common critters. However, rare critters seem to have more selective tastes.
Use Entwined Winders to activate the Bumping Gumball Machine.
When mixing rarer Gumball flavors, additional Entwined Winders are needed.
Now pick two of your favorite Gumball flavors, mix them together and see what happens!
Lopera, you have entered the rainforest.
The dense foliage in the rainforest makes it easy to get lost; every step requires careful consideration.
Each move costs stamina, so make sure you reach your destination before you run out of energy.
Let's start by heading due east.
Each new location has its own unique set of events.
Choosing different solutions will lead to different outcomes.
Some events can be resolved by crafting the right item through the use of alchemy.
Your alchemy is not perfect, so if you don't get the item you want, just try a few more times.
Proceed with caution and carefully check everything on your way to your destination.
The rainforest is filled with peril; test your bravery here and see how far you can push yourself.
In this place, thoughts outpace actions. Each action and incantation <color=#cc492f>resolves immediately</color> when played.
Now, try your hand at defeating this Carbuncle. See what it's like.
In this place, chaotic memories form a protective barrier around our enemies. Those with Memory Shells <color=#cc492f>take reduced damage</color>.
When a Memory Shell <color=#cc492f>is attacked</color>, it loses stacks. Once all stacks are depleted, the shell is destroyed.
Once a Memory Shell is broken, the truth will be revealed and the enemy will enter the [Truth Exposed] status, greatly increasing the damage they take.
Incantations of a <color=#cc492f>stronger</color> Afflatus and incantations of a <color=#cc492f>higher rank</color> will help break through Memory Shells more effectively.

A new mechanic is introduced in the Memory Palace—<color=#cc492f>swapping</color> characters. When a Backup or Substitute character's <color=#cc492f>Moxie is full</color>, they can be swapped into battle. Note that "Backup" and "Substitute" mean the exact same thing in this playmode, they're just different terms.
Breaking a Memory Shell will <color=#cc492f>increase the Moxie of Backup or Substitute characters</color>. So, go ahead and destroy the Lordbuncle's Memory Shell.
It's time for the marvelous Matilda to enter the field.
The swapped in character will <color=#cc492f>immediately cast their ultimate</color> without consuming AP.
Tap to substitute out Eagle and substitute in Matilda.

Everyone holds desires,
within their hearts, within their letters.
Please, grant me true affection beyond words and actions,
with that gentle smile, those rusted dreams.
I would live for this.

Solitary bird, leaving the nest, 
have you ever dreamed
of skies crossed, of forests gathered?
Sunset, oh sunset, what you shine upon
is neither the way home nor a homeland.
Where lies the rainforest to rest?

One day, we will rise to the transcendent kingdom,
escaping, sooner or later, this painful phenomenon.
But until that day, go forth to prove it,
this icy, sweet hypothesis on the cone.

A crimson gift from a friend,
a burden too heavy to accept.
Joy and sorrow be abandoned; yet the ache,
retains in the heart, a soft murmur.
