Welcome to Old Duncan's Trinket Shop! Before you start perusing, tell me, what are you looking for?
If there's something you need, just let me know. I can piece it together for you.
Or did you come here just to see me? I should have a piece of candy here for you ... Hang on, this is a nut.
Use your imagination! Everything has its uses; for instance, this can prop up a table leg.
Here's some tactical adhesive for you. It works wonders when you want to shut the mouth of someone chanting an arcane skill.
Add a pair of wings and a gate key to the biting box here, and watch—it can fly!
A masterpiece! Don't ask me how I put it together; some things just happen in a flash of inspiration.
Ah, a memory you'll never forget ... When you live long enough, you're bound to have a few.
Oh, no, no, this one's much too valuable. Why don't you just take it with you instead? Less risk of wear and tear.
Look at this adorable bunny! You like it? Sadly, I'm not a magician; I can't pull it out of a hat or anything. But I can make you a glowing bunny lamp if you're interested.
Sometimes you can barter for things you could only imagine. You'd be surprised what you can do with a few old parts—like this here.
I think you've got enough to prop your table up to the ceiling by now.
If it's stuck, use oil. If it's falling apart, use adhesive. You can never have too much.
You really love collecting little trinkets, don't you? You've almost cleaned me out here!
No worries; you can take all these masterpieces with you. I've already saved their blueprints.
There's no such thing as too many spare parts. Bring as many as you like. I'll take care of them.

Location: Near the "Nascence" Factory Report: A wild critter was caught stealing [Item Divination Rods] produced by the factory! Comment: Ah, is it looking for cardboard boxes? This type of carbuncle does seem to lack a sense of security. Resolved: I offered it an unlimited supply of cardboard in exchange for labor, and it gladly accepted.

Location: Near Greencage Studio Report: A small critter was found with a mouth full of [Slender Horn Shards]! Comment: Could it have escaped from the [Cranking Gumball Machine] ... ? Resolved: I assured it that its horns were already beautifully adorned and didn't need any further decoration.

Location: Near the Alchemic Abode Report: A pastel-like critter was found bouncing and repeatedly hitting the [Coward's Nightlight]. Comment: Strange in terms of its aggressiveness, method, and target. Resolved: It seemed to think the nightlight, with its orange glow, was one of its kin. I removed the scarecrow's hat, revealing the lightbulb underneath, and it drooped its leaves in disappointment and hopped away.

Location: Near the "Nascence" Factory Report: A turkey-shaped critter was attacking a [Good Luck Can]. Comment: Dodoughs are relatively rare critters, usually of a calm temperament. What could the [Good Luck Can] have done to offend it? Resolved: It found the image of the dodough on the can unflattering. I assured it that we would redesign it based on its own likeness, and it agreed.

Location: Near the "Nascence" Factory Report: A group of larger critters was fiddling with a set of [Auto-Writing Pens]. Comment: It's normal for a group of Refined Groupbuncles to take an interest in cultural customs, but for them to attempt to create something of their own is unprecedented. Unresolved: They consider beautiful handwriting an essential gentlemanly trait, but as none of them can read, they've asked me to judge their handwriting contest. However, due to the automatic nature of the pen, each of their handwriting looks exactly the same.

Location: Near the Alchemic Abode Report: An enraged critter was attacking a box of [Light-as-Air Gummies]. Comment: Splintercat? Could this be a repeat of the dodough incident ...? We seriously need to consider redesigning the packaging for these products. Resolved: It didn't think the [Light-as-Air Gummies] packaging was ugly, but it felt that the image of the splintercat on the package was invading its territory. This packaging clearly has issues beyond style.

Location: Near the Flamespark Workshop Report: A small critter was dangerously playing with [Misty Bubble Ball]. Comment: An incredibly rare teakettler! Please tell me you didn't scare it off. Unresolved: All I remember ... is its ambiguous smile ... inviting me to play with the balls. We need stricter supervision of these goods and protective eyewear for our patrol team.

"Seriously, why does this project need so many live specimens? And if they're really necessary, can't they be shipped here a bit later instead?"

"Relax. Ever since you found out how much these Fiddler Crabs cost, you've been stressing out. If you ask me, the death of that last one was just an accident. It's not like you purposely skimped out on apples and forced them to gobble up one of their tankmates, right?"

"Eh, oh well, that's all in the past now. Check out these watertanks separating and holding the crabs now. Didn't spend a dime on them! How's that for a bargain?"

"Not bad. Where'd you get them?"

"I made a bet with a vendor. We disagreed on who the winner would be for a few events, so we settled it with a wager: if I guessed all the champions correctly, I wouldn't have to pay a single cent for them."

"Which events did you bet on?"

"All of them."

" ... So you're saying that you guessed every single champion correctly, just to win a few crab tanks?"

Test Item: Blaring Fanfare (Referee Equipment - Batch Two) Test Site: An open field (the fog is too dense to see in detail, but there are no nearby residential areas) Test Results: 1. All sample devices produce sound normally, with their quality and loudness meeting referee equipment standards. 2. Aside for two testers who got lost during the "Long-Distance Listening" phase and couldn't report the results in time, all procedures and results have met test standards. Note: The blaring fanfare is incredibly loud. It was thanks to them that the two lost testers found their way back. The fog's been exceptionally thick lately, and there's a risk of getting lost when venturing into unfamiliar areas. This test site might have been a bit too remote, but at least it didn't cause the public to think the event started early, unlike the last time. The mountains of complaint letters sent to the committee sure saved them a fair amount of coal that time—thankfully, this round's testing concluded smoothly.

"Go ahead, try putting the key in the lock ... Aw, the door actually opened? Alright, make a note of this: the Obfuscation Incantation on Door 819 has failed. What a pain in the rear." 

"Huh? What do you mean? Should I not have opened the door?"

"It's fine. You just don't fully understand how this competition works. These winged keys are supposed to fly straight to their designated doors, but in past events they were flying around aimlessly like flies, right?"

"Y-Yes? Does that have something to do with ..."

"Exactly. It's because of the Obfuscation Incantation. When they can't find their door, they panic and behave erratically, similar to what we saw during the competitions. But this time it went straight to the door, so I was hoping it wasn't because of its pessimistic nature or something. But now, I'm starting to feel a little pessimistic myself."

Conversation at work: "I heard the funding for these stones was tough to get from the Foundation." "Yeah?" "Of course. They say it took seven or eight reports to the Foundation before they finally agreed to fund it. They claimed that adding decorations to the venue would attract more people to buy front row tickets, especially with the popular floor ritual." "So that's what all that fuss was about. The person who kept giving us orders, were they from the Foundation? They seemed quite pleased with these stones." "Well, they certainly look the part." "Guess even the bigwigs at the Foundation have questionable taste if they think these tiny stones are impressive. They don't even reach my shoulders! Placing them in such a large venue takes away any sense of grandeur. It's just a cheap imitation of the Stonehenge." "You get what you pay for, I guess. With only seven or eight reports, we can't expect towering stones; maybe if we wrote seven hundred reports, we'd get the real deal."

Work Description: Review the weight of equipment used for the [1500-Meter Weighted Run] project. Importance: High (heavily crossed out, later handwritten) Very Low!! Work Record: 1. Just to reiterate, this job is completely pointless if I can't catch the people who have been sneaking in to feed the sheep. 2. I strongly urge the committee to thoroughly investigate this situation. Using a gold-dyed sheep as a weighted object is a long-standing tradition, and unauthorized feeding should not be seen as an act of kindness. If the sheep does not maintain its specified weight, it will significantly impact the fairness of the preliminaries. To whoever is reading this report, I don't care who you are—if you don't take action, you are just as indifferent to the integrity of the competition as those rule-breaking buffoons. 3. The excess weight was removed by shearing today. Honestly, if we cannot stop the unauthorized feeding, I suggest another shearing 30 minutes before the start of the competition to ensure proper weight. I can guarantee that it will not delay the start of the event. Regards from a skilled sheep shearer.

A non-biological (?) species often sighted in areas devastated by war. "The defeated cheer its arrival, while the victorious flee in terror. The artillery always seems to target the side that is winning." Perhaps it seeks to challenge the strong, or perhaps it simply seeks to prolong the conflict.
"When night falls, the flames of civilization will be extinguished by its presence; not a light will remain." We finally found this victim's lighter in a pile of bullet casings.
"Day and night are meaningless; you will spend the rest of your existence in a bunker." As long as you stay inside, this should not be a problem for you ... What was that, a blackout?!

After an enemy takes an action, if an ally's HP is below 40%, Medicine Pocket casts the incantation [Breaking · Alchemy Ware] once (can trigger once per round). After Medicine Pocket takes an action, Medicine Pocket gains Healing Done +10%, stacking up to 40% this way.

▩0%s Enhancement: At the start of each round, switches between [Breaking · Break Time] and [Breaking · Exorcism Time] statuses. When entering the [Breaking · Exorcism Time] status, all allies gain rank +1 to their incantations. When entering [Breaking · Break Time], all allies gain a Shield with (their own Max HP x30%) HP for 2 rounds.

▩0%s: [Circle of Life] Enhancement: DMG Heal +10%, Leech Rate +10%, and DMG Bonus +20%. Druvis III gains an additional DMG Bonus +1% for every 100 ATK she has. Druvis III gains an additional Penetration Rate +50% against targets in the [Petrify] status. At the start of odd-numbered rounds, all allies gain 1 stack of [Breaking · Gradual Shift].

Enemies under the protection of Memory Shell gain Final DMG Taken Reduction +20%.

    Memory Shell decrease in stacks after being attacked. 1-target attacks reduce 2 stacks, while mass attacks reduce 1 stack. Stronger Afflatus interactions, high rank incantations, and ultimates further increase the number of stacks reduced.

    When Memory Shell is reduced to 0 stacks, it is shattered, causing that enemy to enter the [Truth Exposed] status with a penalty of Final DMG Taken Reduction -70%; and whenever that enemy takes Genesis DMG, all Backup or Substitute characters gain Moxie +1.
The carbuncles are busy collecting scraps of paper, while the young succubus is sharpening her claws.
These carbuncles recover Moxie very quickly. Try to keep them from casting too many ultimates.

Reluctance is the antithesis of devotion.
Why not follow the example of your peers? Start by not covering your ears when they roar.
The stacks of Memory Shell on enemies fluctuate randomly. Prioritize attacking enemies with fewer stacks.
Look at the Foundation's lackeys, they're exhausted! We look much better than they do, at the very least!
Focus fire and break the enemy's Memory Shells, don't give them a chance to rebuild stacks.
Win in 15/11/8 rounds to gain Challenge Points +100,000/200,000/400,000.
If the number of hits taken is less than 25, gain Challenge Points +10,000 for each additional hit avoided.
Repetitions, over and over again. We are still like children, searching for enlightenment through Her teachings.
Avoid "stimulated" enemies and focus on attacking enemies that haven't taken any stimulants.
She shall lead us through the rain, washing away all the impurities from our past.
Try to break "Razor" Captain's Memory Shell each round, but focus on eliminating his allies first.
As it turns out, nothing can be trusted unless it's promised by She herself.
Make sure there's an enemy with a broken Memory Shell each round, and prioritize attacking the Winged Cat.
As time passes, information begins to degrade. This is especially true for memories, particularly the joyful ones.
Break Memory Shells at the right time to stop enemies from casting ultimates and stagger their timings.
The moths are truly amazing, but their perception is limited by the reality they can see with their eyes.
Break all enemy Memory Shells each round. Fully deplete their Contingency Shields before they prime up their big attacks.

Once the moths have left my mind, I feel like my sense of self has become dull, uninteresting, and empty.
I can't wait for my next adventure to fill this void.
Even though Gravel Carbuncles die after casting an ultimate, still try to defeat as many as you can each round to avoid their powerful attacks.
Attack enemies in rapid succession to overwhelm their defenses.
Try using attacks of a stronger Afflatus to break the enemy's Memory Shells.
Breaking the enemy's Memory Shell grants Moxie to Backup or Substitute characters. Swap in a Backup or Substitute character to unleash a devastating blow.
Enter the Critter Ensemble to unlock

The scratches on the back of my hand still sting faintly. How am I supposed to discipline this new arrival? I heard she's a succubus and needs special treatment, but I don't know anything about succubi. Does she eat bread?
Enter the Snow Cathedral to unlock

The Guiding One is gone, and all we're left with is a preacher who has suddenly appeared. The "Storm" didn't take us to a brighter past, and now we must abandon it for an unclear new ritual. Perhaps we've failed, and this biting cold is our punishment.
I have a question, but who can answer it?
Enter the Secluded Lair to unlock

The believer who went to San Francisco has returned, and I have so many questions for him. How are the others doing? Can we still operate under the guise of the Order of Enlightenment? Who is the beautiful woman who brought him back? And why on earth is he holding that ugly, bizarre tin toy? If only the man could still talk.
Parse the first 3 pieces of intel to unlock

That voice, it echoes endlessly in my mind. Her promises have all been empty—I can't see any of the beautiful visions of her promised era. But when she calls my name, her voice is so gentle. So, I suppose my name must be ...

Prolonged exposure to the moth-attracting environment has started to cause severe mental disturbances. To ensure my personality remains intact, I am halting this phototaxis study for now and compiling an interim report.

The succubus has been incessantly searching for a child's toy like some kind of destructive six-year-old. I knew those enchanting tales of Mata Hari were false; the succubi don't possess any of that supposed innate charm. What I need right now isn't the determination of a strong man, but a full set of scratch-proof equipment.

That succubus has already ruined three masks and shredded three rolls of bandages. Can't she control her claws? I need to speak with the honorable apostle. Since she's still refusing to join us, we can't just let her stay here unchecked.

Ms. Grace certainly lives up to her title of apostle—she actually managed to tame that succubus with nothing but an unremarkable wind-up toy. Now that they've gone to Texas to check on the ritual's progress, I can finally rest ... maybe even study the different types of wind-up toys.

Not even Brazil's humidity is as suffocating as Zeno's clinging presence. The Apostles Brotherhood won't last much longer. Where's that succubus? At the very least, she should be fulfilling her role as an enforcer by now ... What's she doing in the courtyard? Is that a turkey?! Zeno—they're coming! I need to find cover immedia-

"Don't worry so much, friend. How could the Guiding One die?" My companion strolls through the snow like a carefree Siberian pony. "She's so powerful and wise—surely she has her reasons."
His response is hardly satisfactory.

"She is simply bearing our suffering in our place. This is just a step toward transcending her mortal body. When the day comes, she will be reborn from the depths and bring about a new order. For now, all we have to do is gather materials for the new ritual."
His lengthy speech, as always, still does not explain why I'm hauling volcanic stones in this frozen wasteland.

I can't understand what the disciples and believers are thinking, but I do envy them. While the believers are simple-minded, they're fearless, and the disciples have no sense of self, so they have no worries. While I tend to my wounds, they devote themselves to their faith. Maybe they're the ones who have truly passed the trials, while I am just a failure.

If this continues, my confusion will inevitably overwhelm me. Perhaps it's time to put my faith to the test. Whether I succeed or fail, at least I'll be able to follow the Guiding One with conviction.

"Kill! Kill, kill!"
Well, at least he's still spirited. I'd bet Matheus gave him an order to kill before fleeing. Better stay away—both the weapon in his right hand and the toy in his left look painful.

The beauty who brought that believer back came to see him again. Her care for him is truly meticulous. Each "kill" is followed with a round of tender consolation. But I see right through her; it's clear that woman has ulterior motives. What could he possibly give her in his state? That ugly tin toy in his hand? This whole thing is in poor taste.

Ms. Grace visited us in person! She shook each and every one of our hands! I have to say, there's quite a bit of difference between the apostles—Matheus would never have greeted us this way. Oh! Even the fellow who always yells "kill" was moved enough to extend his hand!

The one who kept yelling "kill" is dead. Perhaps his mind was so occupied with that single word that he failed to notice the cliff edge beneath him ... Sorting through his belongings was such a hassle. His prized tin toy—where did it go? It's nowhere to be found. Maybe he didn't bring it with him today.

Names mean nothing to me. I am merely a believer. The rising rain tore through my era, and this mask taken from a corpse became my salvation. The lady in the mask knows my sins, and she accepts me without hesitation. This voice is my only shelter now.

Humans took away our names, merely referring to us as arcanists. This rain is the tool through which their sins will be washed away. All should be as it is—yet the Preacher claims that the rain is a mistake ... O, great Guiding One, is it as she says? If so, then let us correct this mistake and return to the promised era.

People call us the Apostles Brotherhood. We follow in the footsteps of the Sufferer, bearing pain to save humanity. But humanity is ignorant and stubborn; there must be an angel to guide them. Like this lady's gospel, under her guidance, we have learned to seek common ground despite our differences, and the Apostles Brotherhood will share the glory with Manus Vindictae.

That beam of light appears so radiant. The secret I need might lie within it. But where are my wings? How can these ugly limbs take flight? And where is the guidance of my antennae ... Oh, I'm not a moth; I am only a person.

Most Manus Vindictae followers don't understand succubus ecology. Their primary sustenance isn't bread or adult humans. They feed on human desires and emotions, consuming human foods like turkey as a substitute when emotions are scarce.

The confirmation of Arcana's death dealt a major blow to Manus Vindictae. As a result, they have altered some of their objectives. Their main aim has shifted from accelerating the "Storm" to preparing some kind of ritual, the exact purpose of which is unknown. However, based on the intel provided by Moth, it is speculated that the ritual will be held somewhere in a high-latitude region. High-latitude areas will be prioritized for investigation.

Manus Vindictae's lower-ranking members have failed to recognize the significance of a contract object to a succubus. The victor's control over a succubus is absolute, but this is often overlooked in the process of multiple contract transfers. The most recent known holder of the contract object was the apostle "Ms. Grace," who brought it to Texas, USA.

As for supplementary information on this intelligence, corroborating with Zeno's report on the Tuesday's Motel investigation, the contract object was indeed found among Officer Stefen's belongings at the time. Admiral Igor never sent it back to the headquarters, however. When the Timekeeper was investigating Stefen's death, a thorough search of his belongings revealed no sign of what should have been a very conspicuous contract object, leading to the assumption that the contract object was placed among Stefen's belongings after the Timekeeper's departure.
Colonel? Everyone? Where are you all, and where is this place?
Is this a dream? A dream from my past?
... It should be fine. Old Quitéria is right here by my side, everyone else must be here too.
It's so dark—but this nightmare should be over soon ...
This is such a strange dream, yet everything here feels so familiar.
And this voice—it sounds so warm, so nostalgic ... Who could it be?
There's mud everywhere; I'd better watch my step ...
The soldier's caught sight of my silhouette, I'm sure of it.
He knows about my sister, and about my fears and desires.
He promised that he wouldn't tell anyone, and I desperately want to believe him.
But why do I keep getting the urge to break his neck?
Let's take a break here and rest for a bit.
That voice—it's been guiding me this whole time, I think.
But I just can't remember whose voice it is.
This dream is so long. Am I really still not yet awake?
I can't see a thing. It's as if I'm in a cramped, murky maze.
I'm so hungry. How long have I slept? My body feels so heavy. Why can't I leave?
What's this? The path is blocked off.
Hmm ... No, it's too heavy; I can't move this.
Come here, child. Perhaps I can help you.
Who are you? I don't recognize you, but ...
Your voice is familiar, like an echo from a long-lost memory ...
That's not important right now, child. Focus on moving that obstacle in your path. It is the manifestation of your fears.
I can calm your mind, but you must be the one to overcome it. Only then will it temporarily lose its form.
And avoid pursuers at all costs. If they catch a glimpse of you, they'll chase you mercilessly.
The slower beasts fall right into these traps. You, on the other hand, seem to be more cunning than they are.
I am not the naive prey you imagine, ripe for your slaughter.
It doesn't matter what you think; there's still a hefty bounty on your head.
Either give up or try to outrun my bullets. Pick one.
It doesn't matter what you do, the result will ultimately remain the same.
Please stop, or you I might end up hurting you.
You're not as weak as you pretend to be. So, this is who you really are—a dangerous and powerful demon.
I have no desire to harm you, but if you continue to push me, I will not hesitate to break your neck.
Let's put an end to these meaningless threats. It is simply our duty to hunt and catch our prey.
Hold it right there, lady; this is a routine inspection.
What? No ... I ... I just want to leave this place in peace.
Hmm? That face. You're that girl on the wanted posters!
Don't move! Stay where you are! You're under arrest!
No, please! Go away! I don't want to go with you!
I'm just trying to live my life. Why is everyone so determined to catch me?
I can't take this anymore. I want to tear them all apart.
No, child. You can't give in to that animalistic urge, or you'll end up living like a wild animal.
But I didn't do anything wrong. Why do I deserve to be treated this way?
Some people will be afraid of you, yes, but others will understand you and like you. They'll want to hear your singing and stay by your side.
So calm yourself, child, and try to change, try to become a new person.
Of course you were only bluffing.
Are you here to lock me up too? Put me in a cage?
The St. Pavlov Foundation has issued an arrest order for succubi. I'm just following orders.
But why? I haven't done anything wrong!
There's no need for us to use force in this situation. I kindly ask that you comply, Ms. Succubus.
I am most sorry that things have come to this. Please, come with me now.
Stay calm, child. We both know that you can do this.
I feel much better because of you. Thank you.
Go on. Keep going and escape from this place.
Stop right there! I won't let you escape that easily!
You're making a mistake! Even if you catch me, no one's going to pay you a reward!
Don't lump me in with those lowly bounty hunters. This is my official duty.
I told you, you'd get hurt.
I underestimated you, and I underestimated the power of a succubus.
You are far too dangerous to be kept alive.
Are you really willing to die for a stupid bounty!?
This is no longer about bounty. It is about duty.
Over here, child. Follow these directions, they'll see you to safety.
Take advantage of the chaos and head south. You'll be able to lead a peaceful life there.
A peaceful life? Will I be as wealthy and carefree, just as before?
No, you won't be wealthy; you might even have to work. But you just might gain something you never had before.
Go, child. You'll see when you get there.
And finally, my work is done.
There are even more of them than before. Looks like I need someone to help me.
Follow the gunshots in the rainforest and collect alchemic materials along the way.|You've reached the favela, where you may find Sandro, according to Rodrygo.
Better go back into the rainforest and continue to look for Sandro.|You've reached a jungle swamp. You may find some good stuff in the deserted cottage by the lake.
Meet your companions from Zeno and continue to chase after the gunshots.|You've reached a remote manor. The target is right ahead.
Once again you've returned to the rainforest, a place that never disappoints.
Your toe bumps into a hard object hidden in the grass. It's a battered, antique handgun that looks like it's been chewed on by a dog. Perhaps this is a stroke of luck.
A cup of cold cappuccino sits on a decaying tree stump. It's an overly distinct, and rather bewildering, clue.
A shepherd with a bow, hunting for his lunch in the rainforest. He claims his father is with the Apostles Brotherhood.
After a burst of chaotic gunfire, birds scatter wildly through the jungle. Though a rare sight, it only makes finding your way forward more difficult.
A colorful bird's nest catches your attention. You're always sidetracked by eye-catching things, but who wouldn't be?
A street performer attempting to set up shop in the rainforest catches your eye. You have reason to believe his stable life is reliant on the charity of his rainforest friends.
A cunning fox resembling Musae III is offering you a good deal.
In a shallow pool, a fierce crocodile blocks your path, poised to attack.
A tripodero stands in your way. Instead of wondering why the most precise hunter in the wilderness is in the jungle, you should focus on avoiding getting knocked unconscious.
A poisonous swamp lies ahead, too dangerous even for the fittest Zeno soldier to cross. For you, trusting your instincts may be the best choice.
An open suitcase hangs from a branch on the riverbank. It's filled to the brim with cash—a tempting sight for anyone.
You originally planned to buy green propolis in São Paulo, but the beehive in front of you will make a worthy substitute.
Distant gunfire should serve as a decent landmark, but the echoes in the forest are simply overwhelming. Hope you have good hearing.
Two Zeno traitors are lying in ambush in the grass. You aren't their target, but once you meet their gaze, the game is on.
A Zeno supply point, now deserted thanks to the rebels. You can take anything you want and not need to file a single piece of paperwork.
A swamp filled with piranhas—more threatening than if it were toxic.
A half-constructed old tram station, left abandoned due to lack of funding.
A retired hunter has set up a shooting range in the rainforest. It's a paradise for gun enthusiasts. Ready to outsnipe the scruffy guy beside you?
A broken radio. Perhaps it's worth fixing to gather some intelligence. Information is crucial in a dangerous place like this.
After a long period of exploration, you're exhausted. Time to consider your next steps.
You stumble upon an Apostles Brotherhood hideout. Will you show mercy or earn some easy military merit? The choice is yours.
In a dilapidated courtyard stands a small tree laden with ripe berries. Whether they're edible or not is beyond your knowledge.
An armed adventurer runs up from behind you. He says he's being chased by a vicious crocodile and pleads for your help.
A Laplace environmental monitor sits in a house, visibly out of commission.
A forest hunter, admiring your bravery, wants to share hunting tips with you.
Several tooth fairies that have yet to take up residence in a jar. They're a valuable material, but capturing them is no easy task for the untrained.
A soaked Mother Goose nursery rhyme book lies by the pool. Picking it up stirs up memories you'd rather forget.
"I've got some news that'll cheer you up," says the amateur information dealer, hoping to peddle rumors of dubious origin.
A set of rusty dog tags, one bearing a coin-sized bullet hole. Clearly, a nasty battle took place here.
A smuggler poisoned by a yarara lies dying in the house corner, still clinging to his now-useless treasures.
A broken-down off-road vehicle sits outside the house. If you can get it running, your journey will be much smoother.
Some smugglers' supplies sit abandoned in a corner of the house. Better store them properly before they spoil.
A set of handcuffs specifically designed to restrain arcanists. It's adorned with Eastern patterns. It seems it crossed the sea through the hands of smugglers.
You arrive at an abandoned shelter, which once provided refuge for a family, or so you believe.
A diligent mother hen is teaching her chicks how to fly by pushing her eggs from her branch. If they don't smash when they hit the ground, they're a good kid.
A birdkeeper collapses from hunger on a favela street. His beloved "children" seize this moment to gain their long-wished-for freedom.
A woman in Foundation field gear approaches you. It seems she needs help—likely struggling with her task.
A riverside pirate gang's house bears the sign "House of Misfortune." Clearly, they never wondered where this misfortune came from.
A scrapped tractor and plow lie in the corner, along with a foul-smelling skeleton. Something happened here.
A violinist from the favela invites you to listen to her impromptu performance. Her dream is to perform on the stage of São Paulo's music hall.
A vendor at the market recognizes you and starts hawking his trinkets. He hails from a village you're familiar with.
A booklet resembling a Brotherhood registry. Perhaps this will lead you to their headquarters.
A local food store serving traditional dishes. An ideal resting spot on your journey.
The charred remains of a house destroyed by a fire many years ago. Now it's a haven for tropical animals.
A group of river pirates gambling on a raft. They are unaware of your presence.
A collapsed advertising sign that reads "Happy Paradise." It and the surrounding junk have become a playground for local children.
A monkey on the roof is throwing small stones at you. What can you do? It's only a monkey, after all.
Two foreign tourists are strolling through the favelas of São Paulo, carrying all their valuables with them. You decide to show them some of your local hospitality.
You capture a child eager to join the Apostles Brotherhood. His fate rests in your hands.
Everything here brings back memories you'd rather forget. But the past holds both good and bad—always remember that.
The antique gun suddenly misfires. Aside from the slight injury, you're mostly just surprised at its sudden activity.
The gun misfires as it hits the ground, detonating like a concussion grenade and scattering the nearby wildlife.
You regret this impulsive act almost immediately, and now you've paid the price. You don't want to see coffee again for a week.
After careful consideration, you conclude this is merely a cup of cold coffee. Don't be discouraged; at least you've gained some unexpected insight.
It doesn't matter who the child's parents are. Right now, you're just going to enjoy a meal with an honest youngster.
You drive the shepherd away. Given his background, you're not sure whether his arrow would hit the prey on the head or somewhere less appropriate.
Your ruthless act brings a silence to your surroundings. You strain your ears, finally figuring out where the gunfire’s coming from.
The jungle is no place for a stroll. Take this time to learn, and be more careful next time.
The nest contains the scraps of the devoured kin of the avian critter that built it. They may make for decent alchemical ingredients.
Admiring the scenery is enjoyable indeed, even if it's of no help to your journey. But you already know this.
Clearly, this friendly merchant has picked the wrong place to set up shop. Your charity is already helping him tremendously.
His jungle friends take offense at your rudeness and launch an attack on you.
The fox expresses its gratitude for your generosity, leaving a few worthless trinkets behind before vanishing into the depths of the jungle.
There's no such thing as a kind-hearted fox. You learned that from the fairy tales you read as a kid.
The bullet does its job, but your reaction was slower than anticipated, leaving you slightly wounded.
The bright light temporarily blinds the crocodile, allowing you to escape the pool safely.
The tripodero is an excellent hunter, but luckily, you're even better.
Turning your back on a hunter is never a wise move. Fortunately, you manage to escape relatively scot-free.
You're always prepared, once again allowing you to overcome the obstacles in your path.
Despite losing some time, you trust your instincts were spot on.
You're certain this box is full of counterfeit money, which isn't very useful to you right now. You trade it to a riverside merchant for some useful items.
Several pirates jump into the river, yelling as they struggle to save the bait. It seems you've dodged a bullet—though you were never truly afraid in the first place.
You've paid a small price, but luckily you were prepared for the worst—after all, this isn't your first time getting stung.
You always manage to achieve your goals using your arsenal of cunning tricks, even if it costs you some time.
You successfully discern the right direction. This will be of great help in your following exploration.
Always remember this lesson: never ignore any clues in the rainforest, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem.
Your aim is as accurate as ever.
You seize the opportunity to escape—best not to waste time on trivial matters.
Everyone knows this isn't your style, but this trick works every time.
Did you really think the rebels wouldn't clean this place out before leaving? The heat and fatigue of the rainforest must be affecting your judgment.
Most of the supplies are gone, but the storage room deep in the facility still holds some useful items. It's certainly better than nothing.
The careless rebels left evidence behind in their reports. This should help you on your journey.
You fire several bullets at the moving targets in the swamp, quickly taking care of the dangers in front of you.
Rather than risking your life by confronting the piranhas, a detour to their keeper might be a wiser choice.
Some poor soul lost in the rainforest stumbled into this swamp, his rotting corpse now a marker of the surrounding dangers. Don't let this act of "kindness" go to waste.
You find a few beds. It seems someone's made this place their home.
You turn to unconventional methods to clear out the outpost, and your hard work yields rewards—you come across some usable alchemy materials.
A vagrant returns. He tells you about his begging exploits for the day and hopes you can help him out. Clearly, things didn't go well for him.
"Test your aim; only $20 a round—no Cruzeiros ... and you have to use your own bullets." ... The shopkeeper's demeanor makes you want to shoot him instead.
The rainforest is never short of lurking threats. Fortunately, customers are often inclined to help the shopkeeper out of kindness. You use this as leverage to gather some intel.
You stand there, watching the hapless plump sheep miss their shots, all the while planning to fleece them in a bet.
Your crucible can create many wonders, but precise mechanical parts aren't among them. Perhaps you've overestimated your cunning?
You may excel at gambling and shooting, but fixing things has never been your forte—in fact, you're far better at breaking things.
A swift kick does the trick—an impressive makeshift repair. Now you can move on.
The rainforest is a cornucopia of food. As a skilled hunter, you won't need to worry about going hungry.
A vehicle could save you precious time. Even finding a wheel would be better than trekking through the rainforest on foot.
You fire up the crucible and toss in everything you've got. You don't know what you'll need, but it never hurts to be overprepared.
You should rest first. The road ahead is still a long one.
Your special bullets melt all the lethal weapons inside. Your enemies have no choice but to surrender.
You resist the urge to break in and quietly leave. You don't like to waste your time on trifling matters.
Dull colors are edible, bright colors are poisonous—testing these old suppositions with your mouth was obviously an unwise choice.
You are unwilling to take unnecessary risks outside the gambling table, so you let them become alchemy materials to be used in your crucible.
Your little creation saves the day. This is one incredibly lucky fellow, since your willingness to help is as unpredictable as a roll of the dice.
The crocodile shows no interest in you, and you don't intend to disturb its happy hunting. Who knows, perhaps you'll come across some decent adventuring gear later.
Clearly, repairing machinery is not where your strength lies, but tinkering with random things is something you can handle.
You have no interest in the eccentric schemes of the computing center in the rainforest. You're more concerned with the cocoa beans that fill their machines.
Watching your impressive marksmanship, the hunter's expression sours as he realizes his overconfidence may have been just a tad too much.
"You honestly think the things you caught while hunting are worth my time?" You scoff at the suggestion and leave.
The tooth fairies are more agile than you thought. After a brief struggle, all you manage to snag is a small portion of the loot they stole. This entire escapade was barely worth it.
Rather than blindly attempting to capture them, perhaps you should try communicating with them amicably. Maybe they'll reveal the secrets of the rainforest to you.
A gaggle of ferocious geese surrounds the pool, eyeing the delicious treasures in your pocket. Luckily, you came prepared.
You will no longer allow the trivialities of the past to cloud your mind. There are more important matters to focus on right now.
Being penniless is not something you want to grow accustomed to. Luckily, the other party is willing to accept your "junk" as payment.
You rarely play by the rules. "I'm not so good with words, so how about you talk to my gun?"
Since there's no chance of them to return to where they belong, it would be best to let them to rest here for now.
You don't know where they came from, but you can help return them to their rightful place.
You leave something he may find of use, and in return, the supplies are yours to take. A few goods for a life is more than a fair deal.
From a scientific standpoint, using poison to fight poison is not logical, but he has no choice but to try his luck.
"You're a hell of a lot luckier than I am!" The thing that flew out of your crucible saves the smuggler's life. He wishes to thank you properly.
The car is miraculously fixed, but what else are you expecting? It still doesn't have a battery or gasoline. There's no way you can get it running.
After several attempts, you come to the conclusion that it would be better to take it apart and throw it into the crucible than cling on to any expectations of it actually working.
You'd rather take a risky bet at the gambling table than try to fix this.
The compressed food inside is by no means delicious, but it'll fill your belly. Besides, you're used to the taste.
You find the radio in the house and inform Zeno to send someone to retrieve the supplies. This took a little longer than you expected.
There's no need to feel bad about leaving them behind; they are not the primary focus of this journey after all.
Thoughtless actions often lead to negative consequences, but fortunately luck is on your side. Good thing you have the other hand to help you remove the handcuffs.
It's too heavy. You realize it was a mistake to try to catch fugitives with it, and abandon the idea. Fortunately, it's not too late.
It's much too heavy, and with its excessive size, it won't fit into your crucible. You decide to let it remain here forever.
It's a dusty family photo. What could have happened for them to leave without taking it with them?
Didn't you once have a stuffed animal like this? Was it a little crocodile or a little beaver? You know these are trivial memories of the past now.
The clock's hands are frozen at 2:18, capturing a moment in time forever. Perhaps it's waiting for its owner to return.
You don't want to disturb anything. For those caught in the "Storm," these remnants might one day become cherished memories.
All the eggs crash to the ground, and the hen leaves in despair. You find some useful items in the empty nest.
You stop the hen's madness. Even a trickster like you can't stand such an absurd scene.
You offer him a meal. After gobbling it down, the birdkeeper stands up, gives you a small token of thanks, and sets off to find his children.
You hesitate, knowing how precious this freedom is. You once longed for it too.
Tracing back your histories, you both work for the same goal or organization. You have no reason to turn down her request.
You have no fondness for those bureaucrats in plaid uniforms. At this moment, you have no intention or desire to lend her a hand.
Without breaking a sweat, you deal with the pests—along with the stench in the room.
The stench wafting from the door crack is suffocating. You curb your curiosity and move on.
You don't find anything useful and decide to leave.
Gathering evidence isn't your specialty, but you manage to do a sufficient job of it. In the end, you realize that it's just an unlucky soul who lost his life in some unfortunate accident.
How could anyone refuse such a warm invitation? Despite losing some time, you can't help but feel much cheerier.
You've never had much passion for music, so you offer her a small trinket as an apology and leave.
Rather than leaving, you opt to buy some trinkets to reciprocate his kindness. It's been a while since you felt such warmth from strangers.
Clearly, this is not the time for shopping or catching up.
This stack of useless papers and the false information they contain can't slow you down.
The Brotherhood's tricks successfully deceive you. It is not easy to find your way out of the favela, and it has already taken up a considerable amount of your time.
The food is by no means tasty, but it does help ease the hunger.
Past experience tells you this place isn't a good choice, and the empty seats confirm it.
Though the chef speaks highly of his dishes, you find their uniqueness a little hard to swallow. You generously offer a recipe of your own.
You fail to find anything useful, but it was still quite an interesting experience.
The charred remains of the house eventually collapse, but fortunately, no harm is done. The animals will have to find new homes.
A rare scenic spot on your journey. How long has it been since you last had a proper rest?
Your participation elevates the intensity of the gambling. As expected, things devolve into a chaotic farce, but you walk away with significant gains.
Though you would like to join in, you have more important matters to attend to. See? Showing a little restraint now and then isn't so hard.
The gambling chips catch your attention and quickly make their way into your pocket. Just as you knew they would.
You try to get information from the little scamps, but favela dwellers aren't the easiest folk to deal with. Fortunately, you know how to handle them.
What starts as a peaceful conversation turns into a "fierce battle." Luckily, you know how to handle the little rascals.
The ringleader tries to extort you, but after seeing your "fireworks," they all flee in terror.
It's no more difficult to deal with them than any other thugs you've faced in the past.
Impatience overcomes you, and you fire a few shots to drive it away.
A clever monkey never refuses a glass of delicious juice. Now you can make it pay.
You guide your two newly made friends, fending off hoodlums along the way. You even offer them some tasty delicacies from the area. This isn't like you at all!
After a brief exchange, you become impatient and leave without looking back.
As expected, their flashy outfits attract some unwanted attention. Fortunately, you were prepared for this and help chase away the uninvited intruders.
Zeno's people take the child. You pray he makes better choices once he's calmed down.
The child's made-up story moves you, and you decide to let him go—who knows, maybe he is telling the truth.
The choice is his to make, and you must respect it. At least you can offer him a bit of help toward his journey.
The favelas aren't all junk and despair; there are also certain sights worth seeing. You know this better than most.
The roadside vendor's pot emits a tempting aroma. You know there's no guarantee it will live up to its promise, but you don't mind trying.
You know you're no different from any of them. Bullets, bets, and luck—that is all you can count on these days.
You doze off in a corner. The people here never pay much attention to what others are doing, as long as they're not wearing anything valuable, that is.

London Air Pollution Auto-Detect Cleaner Research Notes

Improved Suction Device - Third Test Unsuccessful again. Not surprising—a mere cleaning device cannot possibly hope to replace the role of the Fogwalker lineage. Amplifying the family's Arcane Skill may hold some promise, but ... we've only three weeks left. Truth is, my goal is not to solve the unsolvable mysteries of the industrial era—I simply need to ensure that breathable air is available to all for the event's duration. That means faster filtering, broader reach, larger capacity—just for a short period of time, not forever. Arcane Skill Boosting Device - Fourth Test I could be off the mark on this one. Boosting the potency of arcane skills showed very limited effects. This line of thought failed to meet expectations, miserably so. It was a bloody waste of time! Air Pollution Purifier - First Test Thanks to the St. Pavlov Foundation for their ritual inscription techniques, the device works! I was on the right track, somewhat. The Fogwalker's Arcane Skill may be irreplaceable, but this essentially doubles the number of hands we've got. By inscribing incantations onto a device like this, it's like having a duplicate of myself, working in tandem with me. Sadly, I'm not capable of supporting more than one of these, and the purification efficiency is still subpar ... Air Pollution Purifier MK. III - First Test A complete catastrophe! I'm a fool, an idiot, a nincompoop! Curse it, curse it! Advanced Air Pollution Purifier - Third Test What an astounding discovery by the Foundation! I've never heard of enchanting arcane skills onto everyday, ordinary items before; their developments in this area are revolutionary. Though I lack the expertise to perform true enchantment, following their instructions to combine specific tools has improved my Arcane Skill's integration into the device! And by integrating components of human technology ... I've achieved success! I shall name this creation the "London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier." London Air Pollution Auto-Detect Cleaner MK. III - Seventh Test Phenomenal! Maintaining the purification output puts an extraordinary strain on me, but at least it is sustainable for several hours. I pray that tomorrow's demonstration goes off without a hitch.
Unofficial Work Logs (Not Suitable for Formal Submission)

Note 1

It's hard to say which is more miserable—the pea soup in the air or the pea pudding on my table.

I didn't finish today's report concerning the Fogwalker. He wasn't in his office, and I only happened upon him while wandering the streets at dinnertime. Trying to find someone in the fog is the worst game of hide-and-seek imaginable. The Fogwalker is piecing together a device he claims to be some sort of smog filtration machine ... I hope he doesn't truly believe he can handle all this fog on his own.

Note 2

Almost had my leg smashed in by a car. An Uluru leaflet dive-bombed my face, and with the Foundation uniform on, I couldn't get cross about it and tear the thing up.

HQ sent new tasks. Annoying. Frankly, under these circumstances, it feels inevitable that the London qualifiers will be canceled.

Note 3

Never thought I'd be drafting up paperwork to get the qualifiers canceled so soon. I'm oddly excited about the whole thing.

Note 4

Yes, it's all so strange. Everything here contradicts what we've managed to preserve in our records. But so what, why couldn't it have just been recording errors, bad recording practices, or outright falsified data that were passed on to us?

Meanwhile, I'm choking on coal dust that is falling as heavy as snow and putting up with a colleague who keeps getting lost in the fog. A stellar job experience.

Note 5

It's done, though there's a heap of follow-up work ahead. Honestly, I'm hoping that magnificent contraption will actually succeed. That way all these decorations won't go to waste, the tourists and athletes won't have wasted their time, and I won't have wasted all my pre-drafted paperwork.

Waste, waste, it was all a waste ... but I suppose things could have been so much worse.

Though the research has faced setbacks and failed to resolve the pressing issues of the Uluru qualifiers, we greatly appreciate the open-minded approach and collaborative spirit exhibited by your department. Without your material enchantment technologies and the protocols for incantation inscription, progress would have been far more limited. As indicated in earlier communications, we are committed to sharing the outcomes of this joint research endeavor in both mechanical engineering and arcanum studies. Although the device has not yet achieved its intended results, we will honor this commitment. As per standard collaboration practices with the Foundation, since your team provided only technical support while all material sourcing and manufacturing were conducted by us independently, the physical device will not be included in the shared materials. However, we will share its design concepts, manufacturing data, and complete test records. ... Please accept our heartfelt gratitude for your continued cooperation. Should you require clarification or wish to discuss this matter further, please do not hesitate to reach out. Yours sincerely, Arthur Fog London Atmospheric Clean-up Committee Office

Post-Qualifiers Prospects: Setting Out Beneath Clear Skies

Following the Uluru London Qualifiers, 32 athletes from Britain, competing in 18 different events, departed for Australia aboard an Imperial Airways flight this morning. The weather was exceptionally clear with fresh air and no visible smog. Imperial Airways personnel commented that it was "an exceedingly rare occurrence, an ideal omen for their momentous journey."

    Reports suggest that the rare clear skies may be related to the "Fog Monster Incident" during the qualifiers. Many claim that Willow's floor ritual routine banished both the fog and the phantom beast, while skeptics argue that the Witch staged the entire event, using a sinister spectacle to manipulate public sentiment. Others have even claimed to hold insider knowledge indicating this to be part of a century-long conspiracy orchestrated by the British government ...

    Whatever the truth of the matter, the Uluru qualifiers have brought tangible benefits to London. Hospital admissions for respiratory conditions have dropped by 60%, with many residents reporting easier breathing and air quality "reminiscent of centuries past."

A spectator trying to stay away from the crowd.

A sharp-eyed visitor at the Uluru Fair.

A gladiator setting out on a new journey.

A group of gentlemen, striding proudly together.

Not your everyday sightseer.

A traveler zooming by.
Her exhaust fumes left a lasting impression—some tourists even mistook it for one of the local attractions.

A timekeeping bird so round that it looks like it swallowed a clock.

Birds that chirp like the ticking of a clock's second hand.

When the smog thickens, threatening to consume the light,
Who shall stand firm? Who shall charge forth? Who shall raise their voice?
Who shall become the flame bright enough to cut through the haze?

The divine flame,
The cutting edge,
Relentless footsteps that press forward.
Puppets, insatiable in their thirst for victory,
All now encased within its confines.

What is the worth of gold, or a medal's weight?
Our aspirations soar far higher than this.
Yet so often they are shackled by such constraints.

Flutterpage, Liberti, Little Miss Why.
Why so many names, oh my.
And still, I wonder, why ask why?

"Don't be afraid. They are neither ghosts, nor fairies, nor the boundless unknown. They are the air we breathe, the memories we hold ... our souls."
"Is this it? This plain old thing is supposed to be my soul?! I was supposed to shine like a star, for all to see! There's definitely been a mistake somewhere!"
"Tartness—mentioned three times, apricot yellow—mentioned twice, paper and leather—also mentioned twice ... Thank you, I'm not concerned with the shape of my soul. This data will suffice."
"I'm trying to commune with my soul but I haven't heard anything at all. Could it be because I'm already a spirit ...?"
"Who among us is truly free? We are all bound by these frail bodies and limited perception, in a world that is far too narrow."
"Heh, if you make the cage beautiful enough, they'll forget they're trapped inside."
"I'm not trying to shock you here, heh ... but the truth is, I picked up most of what I know now ... from in there."
"Hunker down between these rickety iron bars, and all the troubles of the world fade away in no time. If this isn't bliss, I don't know what is."
"We rushed to the peak, necks stiff from looking up, but the only thing we saw was a passing plane."
"Mister, you've got it all wrong! The thief's over there—quick, he's getting away!"
"And as the clock strikes twelve, our adventure begins! Wait—there are fourteen names on the list, so how are there fifteen people here?"
"While most long-limbed creatures are limited by the night, there are certain beings that will always find you in the darkness. Bats, snakes ... and restless human infants, to name a few."
"Integrity is an invaluable treasure—not only does it yield wealth, it can earn you loyalty."
"For Sale: the invisible dragon in my garage. Fair price, honest seller."
"Always stay on your toes! Even the most honest-looking businessman might very well be leading you straight into a Ponzi scheme!"

"The craftsmanship and unique texture are just the tip of the iceberg—this is an entirely new art form—the material's fragility is key to its aesthetic charm! What do you mean? No, it's not just a shoddy knock off!"
"Side by side, we journeyed on, overcoming every obstacle before us, but at some point, I found myself walking alone ..."
"Is there some place you've always longed to be? Heh, where I am now is exactly the destination I dreamt of in my younger years."
"If only these confused youngsters made plans before setting off on their journeys of self-discovery, they wouldn't end up piling more work on our plates."
"Every river finds her course to the sea, and the seas themselves intertwine. Aye, which is why on the ocean there's really no such thing as being 'gone' or 'sailing far past the horizon.'"

A popular hat choice in London's hat boutiques, worn by many ladies at the time of the interview. However, it was the interviewee who truly made it iconic.
Sometimes, it is not the outfit that defines the individual, but the individual that defines the outfit.

This long cloak, once all the rage among women for its unique collar design, continues to be a favorite for the interviewee long after the trend had been forgotten.
Its hem strategically conceals her legs from the side and rear, sparing her from unwanted attention.

Built to suit the interviewee's body and habits, this prosthetic boasts flexible joints and an almost perfectly lifelike weight and appearance, making it a genuine work of art.
Nevertheless, the interviewee describes it as "an ugly, awkward fire poker."

The 1921 treaty marked the attainment of Ireland's long-sought independence. The shadows of conflict faded, and a compromise that most could live with was put forward. However, opinions remained divided.

While some believed the compromise to be just the first part of a larger plan, others considered it an outright betrayal of freedom. The debate over peace seemed to have no end in sight.

And so, the poor, innocent black swan, entrusting her faith to peace, danced gracefully that day.

Her misjudgment took everything from her—her family, her dreams, her home ...

Leaving only a stiff, clunky prosthetic as compensation.

"Poor lass ... you're so young, and yet ... Be sure to come to me if you ever need anything, alright?"

The old woman across the street looks at everyone with pitying eyes, but after losing her son in the war, how could she spare any sympathy for anyone else?

"I'm not your daughter. Save your energy for yourself."

...

"Afternoon, miss, we live just down the street. We're getting married in a week—would you like to come?"

A new couple? Everyone else is struggling just to get by—and they're inviting a stranger to their wedding, of all things?

"A wedding? You'd be better off saving that money for your rent."

...

"Shh ... quiet, the witch is here—watch out or she'll put a curse on you."

"She curses anyone who gets too close to her—just look at Mrs. Kate and the Jameses!"

Utter foolishness, but it's not like I care—as long as they leave me alone.

"Your lives are already cursed with misery anyway, with or without me."

Pandora Wilson: It's been a long time since you were out on the field. What's going through your mind right now?
Willow: Honestly, I am bored out of my mind.
Pandora Wilson: Oh, that's unexpected ... I thought you'd have deeper feelings than just boredom.
Willow: Were you expecting lofty dreams of glory? Or for me to speak of a burning desire for victory? Only a child would waste their thoughts on such trifles, and I curse anyone who gives a damn about them—may they never get what they want.
Pandora Wilson: I didn't mean to bring up any of those topics, but you make thought-provoking points all the same. So, what do you really care about when it comes to performing? 
Willow: There's a particular person I want to watch my performance.
Pandora Wilson: Would you care to tell us who that is?
Willow: Charlotte. Charlotte O'Hagan.
Pandora Wilson: So, this is about proving something to yourself? And to her?
Willow: Who knows? I just want to dedicate this dance to her, and wish her all the best of health.

The interviewee sifted through the scraps of fabric and selected several pieces that she liked best before turning them into hair ornaments.
Sewing was a skill most children learned in her time, though the interviewee's proficiency in it was decidedly below average.

The interviewee's trusty <nobr>Y-shaped</nobr> metal rod. It serves an array of functions, depending on the user's creativity.
According to the interviewee, she has been banned from using it indoors and in tight spaces, due to past incidents.

The interviewee's best and only pair of boots, which her sister handed down to her after her sister received new shoes for her birthday.
The interviewee enjoys the loose fit and sense of freedom these oversized boots offer, and plans to wear them for a while longer until they eventually fit snugly.

In a family of limited means, it makes perfect sense for children to assist with housework and lightening the load for the busy adults. When the household income falls short of supporting the entire family, children were often encouraged to do other work to supplement their parents' earnings.

However, after the Industrial Revolution took the children out of their homes and into the factories, problems began to surface.

This problem plagued Britain from the late 18th century and well into the 20th, only to be definitively resolved by the Children and Young Persons Act of 1933.

Yet, for some families, this resolution came at a price, how was the Grove family supposed to make ends meet when children were no longer allowed to work in factories?

"How about being a knocker-upper? You'll at least earn your lunch money that way."

"It's not a bad little job, runnin' around the city, meeting all kinds of people, and knockin' on their windows. It's better than polishin' shoes, anyway."

"You know what? You've actually got a very important job. Without you, how can people 'spect to get to work on time?"

She's at it again, same old nagging. Better get comfy.

"Sleeping in on workdays is bleedin' awful. You get the whip and a pay cut and all. No wages, no bread, and if you've got no bread, you'll starve, then you'll have to eat bugs and the like."

What's she even on about? She's doing my poor head in ...

"I know, love, you're all over the place with questions right now—why this, why that, why get up so early? Can't we have a cheeky lie-in? When all you get for your day's work is a measly loaf, you can't help but wonder why in God's name the bakery charges so much for it."

I get it now. She's the one who's confused.

"Sorry, can't say I know either. But I reckon there's an answer somewhere, right? If not, why do the grown-ups never ask?"

Sorry, little one. I see you're in a muddle, but there's not much I can do about that.

"So, you'll wake me up tomorrow too, right?"

The day's done, little one. Time to close your eyes.
"Night-night, Ollie. See ya tomorrow."

"Cluck, cluck."

Pandora Wilson: Considering your age and your era, it's no small miracle that you've managed to retain such an unspoiled and innocent outlook on life.
Flutterpage: Mum and Dad keep bangin' on about it, tellin' me to grow up quicker, but I ain't quite figured that out yet—feels like I'm still just doing it one year at a time.
Pandora Wilson: I assume they're talking about growing up mentally, not physically.
Flutterpage: I reckon someone oughta put the secret to growin' up in the papers for the whole world to know.
Pandora Wilson: That's quite an interesting concept, and one I'd certainly never considered before. Perhaps we can start a column on it—"The Secret of Growing Up."
Flutterpage: Well, how about I go first and let you in on me own little secret, too.
Pandora Wilson: I have no doubt it's something brimming with creativity.
Flutterpage: How's about I share the secret of flying with you! It's well easy, honest!
Pandora Wilson: For the safety of our more impressionable younger readers, we may have to keep this next part between you and me.

Mr. Fog purchased this item from the same millinery he got the interviewee, and later gifted it to him upon his awakening.
The woolen fabric could possibly hold some form of kinship with the interviewee.

The interviewee purchased this genuine leather saddle at his own expense, having it <nobr>tailor-made</nobr> to fit his hobby horse, making it look very much the part of an extravagant plaything.
"A real ranger needs a real saddle!" the interviewee declared, even though his horse isn't a real horse.

Though this hobby horse was buried under a pile of toys in a London shop, it still managed to find its way to the interviewee.
Not only does it allow him to live out his dream of becoming a ranger, but it has also made him incredibly popular with London's children.

The early 20th century was an era of turmoil. As Australia continued to honor its cavalry's heroic deeds in the war, a thread of wool sailed across the Indian Ocean, passed the Cape of Good Hope, and crossed the Atlantic, bringing the legacy of pure Australian wool to a fedora hat in Great Britain.

His memory of the past is hazy, as a gentleman's hat can only observe the hats of others. But that particular day stands out vividly in his mind—a sea of fedoras and casquettes all around him, the rhythmic rise and fall of a clenched fist, and a white cloth overhead.

The white cloth then floated downward, gently resting on his head ... or more specifically, on the head of the gentleman wearing him.

"Our battle has only just begun!"

Indeed, it was in that moment that the words above made sense to him, and he realized—this is a battle, one that had just begun, and one that would never end.

Somewhere on this planet, there exists a beautiful land of red soil—a place teeming with life, where water flows, grass grows, and wool is plentiful. Yet, despite its tranquility, ambitious souls constantly eye the peaceful lives of its inhabitants.

That was until a courageous rider appeared—a brave member of the Rangers dedicated to restoring justice and equality to the people of the red land!

With the precision of an eagle and will of iron, he and his steed rode as one. He made his name known to all ...

"I am ... Brimley!"

...

"Now, I hope you all leave here today with no doubts in your hearts. This outcome is exactly what I had hoped for, both as a spokesperson and as a ranger."

Brimley concluded the press conference in record time, despite straying from the script. His opening words left a lasting impression on everyone present, including himself.
Once a Ranger, Always a Ranger

Brimley: It's truly an honor to be interviewed by UTTU today—not just as a spokesperson but also as a hat.
Pandora Wilson: And what a hat you are. Everyone knows how skillfully you handle the press, so I think I might actually manage to get a decent interview this time.
Brimley: Too right, you will. Keeping the populace pleased is part of a ranger's responsibility, after all.
Pandora Wilson: It's not rare to see people flip between different personalities when finding themselves in different situations, but you always seem to remain true to yourself.
Pandora Wilson: Do you cling on to your ranger identity, even when the job at hand doesn't call for it?
Brimley: Bloody oath! Whether I'm out there fighting for the underdog, staring down a bushfire, or scribbling away on the perfect speech—I'm a ranger, and I always will be!
Pandora Wilson: I'm glad you're finally speaking off-script. Now, let's get to the heart of who you are as a ranger—no holds barred.

One of the velvet hats that were à la mode among the ladies of London. In a city where trends change like the weather, knowing which hat to wear for the right occasion is an essential part of a lady's education.
"Just to be clear, the feather on this hat isn't a critter feather as the shopkeeper claimed. It's a plain old ostrich feather," the interviewee commented.

A handy set of tools for bow and arrow maintenance, with the dual purpose of making a lady's belt appear more beautiful and elegant.
The interviewee praised its functionality—in fact, she was quite intrigued by the idea of adding more arcane implements.

The crafting of a fine longbow is as complex as the crafting of a ritual wand. In terms of material selection, both require similar attention to detail.
With her deep knowledge of oak, the lady was immediately drawn to the bow. After a brief touch of the wood, she realized—the bowyer had once studied under her family, as she could hear the faint whispers within the beech.

A professional set of fencing gloves, offering durability and the perfect balance of softness and firmness.
The gloves feature the image of the interviewee's favorite animal, evoking memories of her time in the East. No wonder her unorthodox technique bears the hallmarks of many different regional fencing techniques.

A simple headband, ideal for sporting events. A "gentleperson" must always maintain their image. The interviewee emphasized that, beyond its practical use in fastening her long hair during duels, this headband also plays an important role in allowing her to bow elegantly to the ladies upon achieving victory.

A rapier used in fiery duels. This ancient arcanist sport imposes few restrictions on weapons, instead challenging players to navigate the delicate balance between beauty and fragility.
The interviewee made this rapier with her own hands, using carefully selected materials and expert craftsmanship. It reflects her confidence, making a bold statement while showcasing her mastery in balancing risk and reward.

Made from cutting-edge experimental materials, this equipment incorporates metal inlays and rivets to meet the rigorous demands of competitive use. However, with her powerful military physique, the interviewee seems unconcerned with the details of her gear.
This upgraded developer prototype, used by the interviewee as a racing weight, bears an Oxford Street sticker—provided for free by the event organizers as a commemorative souvenir.

The interviewee prepared this <nobr>custom-designed</nobr> tricolor IDM 5100 soft power cable set specifically for this trip. When asked why this setup was chosen for an outdoor competition, the interviewee offered us only an undecipherable string of letters as a reply.

Official attire for the judges of London's aerial events. While the sunglasses may not offer the same level of protection as specialized goggles, their anti-glare properties are unmatched. "And more importantly, they're the coolest thing on the court!" remarked the interviewee's pirate friend.

Originally designed for long-range hearing tests, this arcanum device now serves as a starting gun for referees. The interviewee noted that its rhythmic whirring is loud enough to scare off any critters lurking in the stadium.

This leather waist pouch, made for referees, stores various arcanum items and features a side compartment containing a glass bottle filled with strong liquor. Despite its high-quality craftsmanship, the interviewee seems to regard it as a single-use item, if past usage habits are anything to go by.
