This town is alive, like a rushing river of desire.
Let's dance in the streets, one more time.
Find a spot where you're closest to the sky, then challenge gravity to a duel.
That annual fervor, so hard to quench—even in the fog, it blazes just as fiercely.
The trains head out on their routine hunts and return with carriages of coal and provisions, feeding a city always hungry for more.
At the crossroads in the heart of the city, where crowds and chaos reign, even the god of love's arrow can miss its mark.
Ships spew a white trail of steam, floating, rising, and blending seamlessly with the city sky.
This is where light and fire burst forth before surging to every corner of the city.
A leisurely day begins with a nod to another fellow gentleman.
You don't need to look up to know that today is a beautiful day.
In and out and around the mist flows, like blood pumping through the city's veins.
Do you see the city breathing? It's there in the paper mill, and the power plant too.
A river which pays the price for the development of civilization.
A river which witnesses the lives of those who walked along its banks.
While machines have brought prosperity to the city, they have also brought smog.
So, you've got yourself a suitcase that can hold an entire army. You can change the scenery in here and even conjure up a few candy houses whenever you fancy? Not to shabby, I suppose.
But let's have a gander at who's living here ... A child, another child, there's ... a lunatic ... funny.
Right, let's be honest, now. It's not like any of this is really worth making a fuss over.
It's not like anyone else gives a damn, anyway. And as long as you're not bothered, it's nothing to lose sleep over.
I suppose I should take a leaf out of your book on this one.
Well, you certainly don't strike me as a witch.
No darkness, no indifference—you're young and responsible to a fault. You'd make for a terrible witch.
Oh, don't even bother trying to console me, I can't stand that sort of thing! It'll only make me say something even nastier.
Sometimes, in London, you'll see people takin' to the streets, all kinds of people shoutin' about how important it is for kids to be in school.
Did you ever go to school, Vertin? What do they make kids do there?
Skippin' ... I know all about that. Whenever I've got a question with no answer, I usually just fly off somewhere else for a bit.
Or I'd hide. Hidin' always does the trick. I can shove my head in the laundry basket, and the grown-ups'd think I'm just a heap of dirty clothes.
Your clothes are too tidy for that, so I s'pose it's not really an option ... but you could still give it a go—it's actually really comfy in the laundry basket.
I bet they've got a lot of really important jobs at school, ones that only little kids like us can do.
Probably as important as bein' a knocker-upper, right? Else, why would all them kids be so keen to go?
Me? I'm all grown up now! No school for me, that's what Dad says, anyway.
Crikey, you've got some top-notch rangers here. Wouldn't hurt to start a proper rangers' club, if you ask me.
I'd be top dog, of course, but who do you reckon should take number two? A true ranger's always up for a bit of advice on matters like this.
That "mighty king of wooden steeds," eh? You can't deny he's got one hell of an impressive mane, and those eyes—phwoar, true grit if I ever saw it.
Any ranger worth his salt would be chuffed to ride that one. On the other hand, the thing looks more like a steed than a rider, eh?
Ha! That young fella, he's got the makings of something great, no doubt!
The lad's got guts on that bike, I'll give him that, and he's certainly got the ranger tone down!
I'm teaching the lad everything I know.
You're not quite there yet, mate. You might not be a ranger, but you've definitely got what it takes to be the club's top sponsor—the big cheese who calls the shots!
Naturally, if you're keen on giving riding a go, I can show you how it's done.
The first step's easy, mate—all you've got to do is plop me on your head.
It seems like you're always at it, coming and going, and when you do return, you look like you've been to hell and back.
People like you don't last long in this world, you can mark my words.
What are you even trying to prove? That you're so courageous you don't even fear an early demise?
Don't be daft. A handful of years after you've kicked the bucket, not a single soul will remember you.
Or you could live like a spineless coward, endure all those sneers, and perhaps, one day, something good might come your way.
When death comes knocking, it'll be too late. So, make the most of the time you've got, while you still can.
(She follows you around, not a word spoken).
I haven't had any work to do since I got here, and it's left me with far too much time to spare.
From what I've gathered, the most popular job around here is bein' one of your lackeys, so I'm still learnin' the ropes.
No, you don't need to pay me—this job's interesting enough on its own.
(She spreads her arms, flaps them like wings, and takes off like a bird).
Blimey, the weather here is as temperamental as London's.
I reckon I spent too long under the Aussie sun ... nearly forgot what this kind of weather feels like!
That's right—London's fog, its streets, and all those old mates ... especially Fog. Before I even realized it, he'd become Old Fog, became a hero long before I had the chance.
Speaking of which, since I've got Oliver looking up to me in a way, maybe I should find a more subtle way to get him to call me "Uncle Brimley."
A real ranger never complains about the weather! Come rain or shine, it's all part of the ride, mate!
And don't forget about maintenance—when you're out riding in the rain, it's all about keeping your trusty mate polished and waxed.
...? Hello? A flood of energy just obscured my vision. Is that you, right there?
So, you weren't trying to hide ... This energy—this *is* you, isn't it?
No need to worry, I'll keep my distance ...
From right here ... I can finally see your true presence.
It's just like I've always said—those high-and-mighty suits? Can't trust 'em for a second.
They're totally out of touch with our struggles, our worries, and our dreams.
If we want a peaceful future, it's something we gotta create, with every step we take!
You're chasing big dreams, pal, and I've got your back on that.
A "pal" who's down to support the arts! Now that's a real pal! Ready to jump in with both feet and go all the way with me?
I was thinking of filling the Foundation brass's office with bubbles, just to shake things up a bit.
Dude ... Stir up the hornet's nest like that and everyone's gonna get stung. How about we go do something a little more practical?
You could lend a hand to A Knight with his armor, and hey, maybe pick up a bit of art along the way—the art of hammering steel.
Oh my ... Just what am I seeing right now?
Why in the world would you dress yourself like that?
You got it—everything I'm wearing is second-hand. Fashion doesn't come for free, Mr. Model.
Poverty is certainly no picnic ... it does limit one's wardrobe choices, but I'm not talking about managing your finances here.
A lack of confidence is far worse than poverty could ever be, my dear.
Be confident! You're pretty enough without all these gaudy embellishments of yours.
Especially those rhinestones ... Whatever compelled you to encrust every piece of jewelry you're wearing with those things?
Ain't you an adorable little puppy? Come here, darling. I've got a treat for you ...
The puppy is very happy to play with you.
I always thought it'd be nice to have a little doggie around the motel, but not everyone's comfortable sharing their space with an animal.
You know, darling, pets and children don't always mix well. A guest once confided in me that her child, in a fit of jealousy, placed their pet in the microwave just to get her attention.
I suppose there ain't no way to avoid these sorts of things from happening, is there?
<... It seems this horror story takes the idea of "hell is other people" and extends it to include pets.>
The puppy does not understand why you are trying to scare it.
What the hell are you doing over there?
N-Nothing! I just ... I saw you, ma'am, and ... I suppose ... it's just an old habit ...
I-I didn't steal anything! I'm just ... a little nervous, that's all ...
Ain't no need to fret, missy. We ain't living in those days where they'd string ya up for just lookin' the wrong way.
Ain't nobody around here gonna mess with you, and I can tell you ain't done nothin' wrong.
Y-Yes, that's right ... but ... please, allow me to stay away ...
Your gun ... it ... it makes my heart race with fear ...
Mr. Nick Bottom, I'm so glad you agreed to my interview request. Thank you!
No need for thanks! When I'm on stage, the spotlight never fazes me.
Now, there might've been a hint of a personal motive behind me scheduling this interview ...
So, if you don't mind me asking—what's it like to have a donkey's head?
It's brilliant! Vegetables taste more delicious than ever before, I'm always full of energy, and my mood's all the better for it!
What matters most is, with this mask on, she might still remember me from that day.
Right, a mask just as lifelike as yours.
I-I don't have any spare change! Please leave me alone!
I was thinking of calling up Mesmer Jr. and Marcus to play a game of Perudo. You should join us.
I-I don't think so ... I'm not the best at games like that ...
Don't worry, it's easy. I'll show you how to play!
Can you at least ... give me some time to prepare ...?
I need to put on a new sheet, see if the snacks are still good ... and ... I need to mentally prepare myself for all this ...
So ... you go wherever you want, with people flocking to you and showering you with love and attention, and you don't even have to worry about being hunted down?
Maybe you could share your secret with me? That way, I won't have to starve.
Most people are wolves in sheep's clothing. They're all very dangerous, but it's simple enough getting through it all.
The first step is to play innocent, act weak, and get them to drop their guard.
Do I truly have to? I've done enough of that in my time ... Any other tips?
In that case ... just share your secrets with them, no matter how insignificant or grand. In exchange, take theirs, and make them forget yours.
Well, my master already destroyed my secret ... I don't need to beg for a contract anymore.
Well, it looks like you've got the hang of it, anyway.
Sometimes, you just have to accept the fact that age catches up with you. Like recently, whenever it rains, my back and waist start acting up.
Regular care is the key to avoid rusting away. Someone makes sure to oil himself regularly, and that is why, even without legs, he is still quick on his feet. Ha-ha.
Hmm, guess I'm overdue for an oiling too ... Any recommendations?
Verily, to preserve a joyful heart is the most noble of self-maintenance practices. Pray, do you understand why one should heed the advice of the porcupine?
It is because they are always sharp and to the point.
*the satisfied laughter of having told a good joke*
So, that bottle of yours can just resize whatever's inside it?
So ... what you're telling me is that it's holding way more water than it looks?
Aye, the water in here's enough to float a proper ship, lass.
If I were you, I'd just fill that bottle with vodka.
Once, I just poured rum in here, and by thunder, it nearly had me capsized for good.
I took to mixing my rum with water after that. Rum's a fine thing, but overindulgence will have you sailing straight into a storm.
That's a shame. I just thought I'd found the perfect drinking buddy.
Well, who do we have here? I never thought I'd see the sacred flame of Uluru outside the stadium.
My, Charlotte, it's been a while, hasn't it? You've grown so much.
You still remember me? How flattering.
I have a good memory—children are always counting on me as a source of wisdom. Not to mention the fact that you're the youngest Floor Ritual champion in history.
Hah! And being the first disabled athlete makes me all the more memorable, doesn't it?
Disabled? Oh no, my child. The Uluru Games are for everyone.
It doesn't matter if you have four legs, three, or only one. Look at me—no legs whatsoever.
You look just like a little version of Mr. Fog.
I suppose calling me "Little Fog" wouldn't be entirely unwarranted ... Do you know my father?
I lent Mr. Fog a hand with his work—probably the most important work I've done, alongside wakin' folks up, that is.
What's wrong? You sound like you got a right bad toothache! Reckon you do? I could have a word with Ms. Tooth Fairy for you, she's brilliant at sortin' out tooth troubles.
No, I'm simply lamenting ... lamenting the fact that even a girl of your age must already concern herself with work.
*sigh* ... I'd wager the conscience of London's government was buried by coal ash long ago.
Mr. Brimley! Thanks a million for helping us with the journos last time!
A mere trifle, miss—hardly more effort than a quick flick of the brim.
Yay! I guess that makes us friends now, eh? Let's shake hands!
... This isn't very ranger-like of me, but I think I'll have to decline on this occasion ...
Oh, right, you have no hands! No worries, I'll go for your coat, or maybe the brim of your hat! You wouldn't get offended, would you?
Taking offense isn't the problem here ... It's just that, if I shook your hand, I could end up catching fire, and I'd prefer to avoid that, being as flammable as I am.
Reflecting what's around us won't help us learn the truth. We must cast our gaze further into the distance.
I couldn't agree more. It's important that we listen closely and broadcast voices from beyond.
Just as the speed of radio waves aligns with that of light, I believe we'll have many more topics to discuss.
Did you arrange for someone to give you a dusting today? I wonder if I could share that service ...?
Should someone owe me coin, hindering my timely payment of the king's taxes, would you defend me, or would you side with our esteemed sovereign?
I shall ensure the debtor repays what they owe you in line with the law, then see to it that you pay your taxes as the law demands.
Ah, but what if he claims that if he pays me back, he won't have the coin to pay the sovereign's tax in due time? What shall we do then, Your Honor?
Esteemed elfin, I offer you this coin—grant me the power to achieve world peace on my own terms.
If I could do that, I'd have made world peace happen all by myself by now! And do you really think world peace can be bought with just a coin?
Not just that! Are you planning to fix the world yourself, or are you hoping a wish can do it for you?!
S-Sorry, I guess I was just trying vent and let all that frustration out ...
The Flaming Boxer, The Ice Cream Debate, The Suitcase's Magical Voyage, The Warden's Childish Game ...
So many photos ... are you sure you want me to have them?
I capture these moments and share them with those who can't see such things with their own eyes ... people like you.
Thank you so much! I'll cherish these photos forever!
Aloha! Konnichiwa! Finally got a chance to use that nifty greeting I learned! Hah! What's on your mind, miss?
Oh ... You are from Hawaii, yes? I have always been interested in Hawaii ...
Glad to hear that! Hawaii is an amazing place—sunshine, beaches, and plenty of coconuts! You're always welcome to drop by!
But I don't have any family there, so I'm not sure if I can ...
Don't worry! We're all family—ohana! When you come, I'll show you around!
That sounds wonderful! I will send my photos over before I go! I wonder coffee shops are like in Hawaii ...?
Oh, hello? Were you calling me just now?
You must always be wary of wolves—they could be lurking in the shadows.
I appreciate your concern, but surely we must be safe here in the Wilderness, right?
Never let your guard down. One must stay alert.
You're really worked up about this. How about a piece of candy to help you relax? It's got a refreshing mint flavor.
*slowly backing away* Forgive me, but I'm still on mission ...
It's alright, Lisa/Louise are good girls. We can wait for you.
After that, we can play forever, and ever, and ever ...
I'm sorry, but I have to leave right now! *hurrying away*
You live on the other side of the screen?! How's that even possible?
Honestly, I'm just as mystified. This is my biggest secret, and it's still a mystery to me too.
That's incredible! Talk about being camera-ready, twenty-four-seven! Besides, you are hands down the most photogenic person I know!
I wish I could be more like you ...
Cheer up! From my perspective, you're the one living on the other side of the silver screen!
It's funny, isn't it? Our whole lives more or less revolve around being crammed into a tiny screen!
You've got the look of a real cowgirl about you—one fit to ride even my saddle!
Consider yourself lucky—not just anyone gets to ride the mighty king of wooden steeds!
Why not? What's the matter? Don't you have confidence in your riding skills?
Hopping on you? I reckon that would make me seem a mite immature, don't you think?
So, what does the DUU-DUU-BELL-BOO eat once it's left the atmosphere?
Uhm ... Err ... I think ... if I remember correctly ... it's either grass or ... wait, no, wheat?
Grass in space? I didn't see any of that when I was up there.
I ... W-What I meant was, I never saw anything like that in any of the documents!
I see ... well, a-actually, it's because they, uh, ruminate—yeah, you know, they chew their food again!
Sometimes, they'll touch down, eat way more than their body weight in wheat, and then zoom off again!
And that's where crop circles come from!
Indeed, the wind blows softly today, a most auspicious time to spread one's wings.
After this brief interaction, I am even more convinced of your literary prowess. I shall leave you to your peace for now, and return at another time.
You're the one in charge of handling inheritances, huh?
That's me. Are there any "future matters" that require my attention?
Nothing too serious, just need a small favor.
If I kick the bucket before my pals, be sure to hand my stuff over to them.
What kind of "stuff" are we talking about?
I've got a whole stash of ice cream hidden in the freezer under the bed.
Do you think I'm a witch?
I'm not ready to die just yet.
Bad weather can make people nostalgic too.
All I can remember is the bad weather.

Flowers bear fruit, and beasts give offspring's way.
With eyes of fire, pierce through the cloudy maze!

During a certain period in history, the term "Big Smoke" became a "celebrated" moniker for London, drawing some curious travelers to its streets. However, from the 17th century to some time later, the essence of a visitor's experience in London hadn't changed much. Especially for those who chose to visit in winter, the dense fog often obscured the city's sights. By the 19th century, however, this fog had become an integral part of London's "charm," so much so that some curious visitors would feel their trip incomplete without a glimpse of the dense—and not always white—mist.

The shift in public perception, where disappointment gave way to "pleasant surprise" under the same foggy veil, was an intriguing one. This change was fueled, in no small part, by art: painters flocked to the city in winter to capture the fog-laden Thames, and novelists used the mysterious haze as the stage for detective dramas. As these works gained popularity, people naturally embraced the combination of fog, water, and the ancient cityscape, viewing the smog as an essential element of London's appeal.

For London residents, however, the smog was anything but romantic. This mix of stagnant water vapor and industrial pollutants became known as "pea soup" in the 19th century. Anyone breathing the air could tell that the name was far from complimentary. Yet, this wasn't enough to raise significant alarm—pollution alone wasn't enough to halt the relentless march of industrialization. It wasn't until London, the great coal-burning engine, was brought to a standstill by the Great Smog of 1952, choking the city for five days, that effective legislation began to take shape.

...

Today, as the "Storm" seems to hurl the world backward in time, I've had the privilege—or misfortune—to witness a yellow fog as thick as pea soup with my own eyes. It hovers among towering smokestacks, its texture, stench, and the reflexive gasp I stifled upon opening my window all testify to its harm. I recall reading a poet's description of it: "Like a secret something that adds beauty to everything."

What a strange, yet profoundly poetic, form of praise!

Now, before setting out on my field mission, I must hurry to claim a high-filtration mask—surely the only thing capable of making my journey remotely pleasant. Considering the absurd traffic accidents that occur in such fog, I might also need to fashion a reflective vest. A soft disk enchanted with an illumination arcane skill should also suffice. However, to penetrate this fog, the incantation will have to be exceptional in its potency.

I have no doubt that one or two researchers would eagerly pursue the challenge of developing such a device. Knowing them as I do, I'd bet all my personal files that were lost in the "Storm" on it, ha.
"Evolution of Uluru Traditions in the 20th Century"

"Standardization is a necessary process for sustainable development."

Though the chief overseer of the Foundation's Uluru Committee has never engraved this phrase onto her sleek walnut desk, anyone who has interacted with her knows it is her guiding principle.

With her approval, her assistant provided me with extensive materials. Since the Foundation officially took charge of the Uluru Games, this assistant has been by her side, driving and witnessing a series of transformative innovations.

"Without a doubt, for the wider Arcanist community, the Uluru Games are a glorious and ancient tradition. From bedtime stories for children to street games and even professional pursuits, they originate from Uluru, revolve around Uluru, and ultimately nurture Uluru in return. Fueled by people's spontaneous enthusiasm, the games have thrived to this day. Yet, the overseer was among the first to recognize the potential risks threatening its legacy."

The assistant recounted their initial encounter with the overseer: "In my youth, I witnessed a young participant nearly lose their life due to lack of safety regulations. I gathered similar cases and called for attention to fairness and safety in the games—and soon received a response: an invitation from the overseer to work together. I still remember her words during our first meeting: 'Competitive sports should be the seed of peace, not the breeding ground for danger'."

"It was only after working with her that I realized a standardized arena was merely the first step toward a renewed Uluru Games. Surely you remember the uproar when high-risk events were suspended for the first time? Critics lambasted the decision as destructive to Uluru's traditions. But amidst the storm of public opinion, the overseer remained steadfast, believing that only by ensuring the athletes' safety could the Uluru flame burn on.

"Please understand, the overseer has no intention of letting these traditional events disappear. Over recent years, several events have been reinstated with revised rules, and others are being revitalized with a combination of modern science and arcanum, transitioning into entertainment formats to preserve them. Our first experimental project, the Puppet Arena, was recently launched, and we eagerly await everyone's feedback."

At the end of our conversation, the assistant whispered, "She might appear stern and lacking in passion, but the overseer harbors a deeply held wish: that one day, 'arcanum will become a source of joy for all Arcanists'."
"The Witch's Silhouette: Dances, Rituals, and More"

Dance is a ritual form understood by most Arcanists and even humankind at large. However, opinions differ on the source of its arcane power: "Anyone with a witch's lineage is born with it." "They use some ancestral salve, like a flying ointment." "Invisible demons guide them." "Surely they were kidnapped by fairies as children! My mother swears that's the story of every witch she's ever met."

To unravel this mystery, I joined the "Source" Arcanum Research Expedition and visited the hometown of Ms. Charlotte O'Hagan.

Surprisingly, the area still retains an Iron Age charm and simplicity. Fairies are openly visible and interact with humans, enlisting their help to build homes, wage battles, or play card games. In return, they offer magical treasures or sage advice. "We don't mind sharing our roof with mister spirit over there," said one family. "He knows how to keep meat fresh, so our herring always sells best on the street."

When asked about ritual dances, locals guided us to a clearing with massive stones arranged in a circular formation, complete with standing pillars and lintels—nearly identical to the setup in Ms. O'Hagan's training hall. "Usually, it happens on May Day or at the start of winter. Everyone holds ribbons or short sticks and dances in circles around the stones. Gradually, the numbers grow, but you can't tell who has joined—fairies and sprites like to disguise themselves and mingle!" One guide demonstrated some steps, claiming they were "taught to my great-great-grandfather by a fairy." Interestingly, parts of the dance mirrored Ms. O'Hagan's movements. However, all it did was attract a flock of birds.

Another villager shared a more modern adaptation: "Nowadays, most villages prefer to light two bonfires in the square. If you want protection, walk between them—the smoke and flames will ward off evil. For good fortune, you need to dance around them. Remember, clockwise only! Mischievous fairies might try to confuse you!"

...

At the end of our investigation, we sought Ms. O'Hagan's personal view on such floor rituals. Her response was succinct: "I have no stories to tell."

The Uluru Games have officially begun! Dear readers, surely you wouldn't want to miss the thrilling match between the British and French teams or Caroline Bartley's elegant dance performance while still snoozing away, would you? Knocker-uppers are offering special services during the Uluru season. Here's our list of top recommendations:

Mr. Hans: ★★★★★
A beloved figure in Dalston and known as the "living Big Ben," Hans is also a volunteer for this year's Games. With twelve years of experience as a knocker-upper, he's never made a mistake. His lively knocking rhythm is sure to energize your entire day!
Price: 8 pence a week.

John Ritchie: ★★★★★
Taking advantage of the Uluru Games, the "Crafty" John Ritchie has joined the ranks of knocker-uppers! During the Games, just tell him your favorite athlete, and he'll knock on your window 30 minutes before their match begins.
Price: 8 pence for the entire Games.

Mrs. Smith: ★★★★☆
Everyone knows about Mrs. Smith's pea-blowing talents. Even last year's shooting champion was amazed by her precision and power. Each morning, you can wake up to the satisfying sound of dry peas gently tapping against your window, without fear of them breaking the glass.
Price: 6 pence a week.

Flutterpage: ★★★★☆
Floating through the streets or perched on your balcony at dawn, this petite messenger provides a delightful alternative to sticks and pea-shooters. For a mere 6 pence, she will chirp like a sparrow at your window and deliver the morning news, free of charge.
Price: 6 pence a week.

Oliveira: ★★★☆☆
The ever-creative Oliveira seems to have drawn inspiration from the Games. Will it be a starting pistol? A referee's whistle? Or perhaps a silver arrow landing on your bedside table? Oliveira won't reveal his latest knocker-up methods to keep the surprise. His techniques are certainly effective, as long as you don't mind a bit of a shock first thing in the morning.
Price: 6 pence a week.

Dear Lily,

I'm sorry I haven't written to you in the past two weeks. The opening of the Uluru Fair has kept our family even busier than we expected. Athletes and tourists are everywhere now, filling Cross Street with a cacophony of accents. Aunt Martha says even pickpockets would be overwhelmed by the chaos here.

With the preliminaries officially underway, the shop will surely leave me with no free time at all. But I haven't forgotten our promise, and I'm sending you a local's guidebook to ensure you have a wonderful time at the fair—keep this letter with you, and you'll enjoy it to the fullest!

First, avoid vendors claiming they're officially registered with the fair's report list. This is a new fair for Uluru, and any claim of registration is bound to be false.

Second, always bring an umbrella in London, unless the Floor Ritual events manage to conjure up some rare sunshine. If you forget, look for Bernard's umbrella shop, near the florist with the antler decorations at the street corner. But here's the trick—look across from it! Down the alley, there's another umbrella shop. The prices differ by five fold, but the products are identical. In fact, both shops have the same owner!

When you reach Cross Street, you must try the "Fortune-Telling Ice Cream." The man's cart may not be the newest or most eye-catching, but wherever the Orbuculum on its handle goes, it draws a crowd. For just 2 extra pence, the vendor will predict your favorite flavor. If he gets it wrong, you'll get a free ice cream. It's the best deal ever! Too bad I've never managed to get a free one—he must either be a fortune-telling master or an ice cream genius, because I love every flavor he picks!

You mentioned wanting to buy a tea set in London. The porcelain shops on Cross Street aren't anything special, but I recommend a shop east of the square. Its sign reads "Herbal Specialties," but inside, it's filled with consigned tea sets. Mrs. Winston, a connoisseur of elegant tea sets, would surely be delighted to help you find a unique one.

Mom's calling for help, but I have to finish with this—Mom and I have reserved a great spot for you at the restaurant, complete with a bouquet. Guess what kind of flowers they are! I've also prepared mashed potatoes, pudding, and fish and chips for you. I can't wait for your arrival!

With love,

Monica

The long-extinguished sacred flame has once again been kindled in the ancient arena of the Uluru Games, bringing Australia's stories to a close. Now, your brief respite also comes to an end, much like those dreaded moments when you have to leave your vacation behind or linger in bed instead of facing the day.

Embrace the waves and set foot onto the deck of the "Free Breeze"—don't forget, you still have a mission to fulfill. 

Navigate the treacherous winds of the sea, and in the distance, Ushuaia awaits you, Timekeeper.

The ultimate cruise party!

No matter where you're from, what you do for a living, or what troubles weigh on your mind... you are welcome aboard the "Free Breeze"! Let's leave those mundane files, heavy burdens, and dull conversations behind and rejuvenate ourselves! Waves, sunshine, fine wine, and music! Come aboard and discover what it truly means to embrace life's essentials!

Worried about tickets? Don't be! A free-spirited ship charges its fare freely—Australian dollars, arcane materials, or any treasured item you deem valuable. Come aboard, and let's meet the remarkable passengers who will make this voyage unforgettable!

July 30, Wednesday
Still vomiting ...

I heard that Mr. Antonio has recently become enamored with a cruise ship orchestra—how curious. Oh, he's not some romantic artist, nor does he have a collection of fine treasures at home. He's an accountant—yes, the accountant for La Vie Française—a cautious, even slightly old-fashioned gentleman. Neither he nor his wife are particularly knowledgeable about music, and they seldom attend concerts.

Mr. Antonio gets seasick! He made quite a spectacle of himself on the ship ... Yes, he certainly lost his gentlemanly composure there, the orchestra on board completely captivated him. It was an exceptionally unique orchestra with a truly extraordinary musician ... That's how Mr. Antonio described it, darling. Hard to believe, isn't it? Who knows, maybe his seasickness was making him hallucinate?

In any case, Mr. and Mrs. Antonio have set sail again, on the "Dream Expedition." And Rusty's come back, hasn't he? That's a good boy, Rusty.

The nights on deck are eerily quiet. Once the orchestra retires for the night, only the sea breeze, the melting ice, and the dizziness remain.

To endure such unbearable discomfort for the sake of these performances—this is not something he would have done in the past. On sleepless nights, with the wind howling across the deck, the preparations before the voyage now seemed trivial. He had practiced balancing on a waterbed, simulating the ship's motion, but never imagined he would still lose his balance on an actual ship.

He waits for the sunrise, for the final performance, for the return journey. Then, the days ashore will come—sitting in an office, counting coins that aren't his, staring at a life so predictable it seems to stretch to infinity.

The delayed sunrise at sea stirs unease, along with a faint curiosity—what would it be like if it delayed further, or if eternal darkness took its place?

Thankfully, the sun eventually rises.

Excerpt from "A History of Arcane Ethnicity"

...

Due to the reclusive nature of the Nukutais, our knowledge of this enigmatic people comes only from the sparse accounts of a few trading ships that had contact with them and the legends from neighboring societies.

...

In the folklore of coastal civilizations in the South Pacific, there are often tales of Shell People or Hermit Crab People. These beings, dressed in shells and living in the water, are depicted as otherworldly ocean emissaries or guardians. They offer advice and guidance to the protagonists in these stories or help those lost at sea.

...

With the Age of Exploration, the veil over these mysterious figures was lifted, and a small island named Nukutaeao, known for its production of mystical and esoteric crafts, became a topic of intrigue among adventurers in taverns. Consequently, the intrusion of explorers and trading ships seemed to weary the Nukutais, and records from that period show they gradually vanished from the pages of history. They employed some form of arcane skill to conceal the island's exact location, ensuring their homeland never appeared on any official map.

...

Today, with advancements in maritime technology and increasing global communication, it is only a matter of time before the island of the Nukutais is rediscovered. The author can only hope that this inevitable encounter will not bring undue harm to the Nukutais, wishing that they can integrate into the global community through peaceful and friendly exchanges. May the final chapter of this Age of Exploration conclude with harmony.

Evaluator's Comments:

Alright, enough with the charade. The only thing in this document that she actually provided herself is this photo! I'll let her join the research group as a formal researcher, but she will not receive any benefits until she personally fills in all the blanks on this form.

—Ulrich

"The topic of this brainstorming session is: How did this 'Pioneer' manage to cross the 'Storm' and continuously send information to the Earth's surface?" The ferrofluid flows freely in his glass tank.

"Is it possible that this is just a prank? Like a cipher game created by one of us, accompanied by fake photos and data ..." An indifferent researcher shrugs.

"Then go and write a detailed report on who you think is pulling the prank, one every week, until someone confesses to being behind it."

"That's an abuse of power!" The researcher, who intended to remain silent, slams the table. "Alright ... I have a thought. The 'Storm' rewinds people into disappearance, but some things that inherently exist longer might not be completely reversed. This 'Pioneer' could be some kind of man-made satellite that regularly sends data, and the 'Storm' rewinds it to an older version, but doesn't affect its operation."

"We've already experienced time periods as far back as the beginning of World War I; no man-made satellite should even exist at the time."

"I've got it! It's aliens! Aliens are crossing the 'Storm' and sending us some kind of signal! It's not surprising at all that they have technology immune to the 'Storm' among their advanced space tech, right?" A researcher with a fanciful imagination raises his hand.

"Damn it, we don't have time to verify baseless hypotheses such as these!"

"The man-made satellite theory might just be a reasonable hypothesis. Maybe the internal structure of the satellite just happened to form a knot-like structure? Many of the satellites launched by Laplace have adopted arcane techniques, theoretically capable of activating the immunity spell." The researcher, feigning seriousness, rests his chin on his hands.

"That's a good direction, but your reasoning is too idealistic. Let's proceed on the premise that there exists a satellite capable of gaining immunity to the 'Storm' and investigate further, regardless of the principle behind all this. Now, everyone, spread out and check every satellite in Laplace's history. If this hypothesis is confirmed, it could be another significant breakthrough in our 'Storm' research."

Serres Common Names: Pig-toothed Ray, Anchor Fish, Deep Bass Disc, Hammerhead Ray. Back home, we call this thing a Sea Bat. That's not right! Sea Bats are a different species and they definitely don't smash your portholes at night! Classification: Subclass: Aquatic Primal Critter, Order: Oceanic, Family: Ray-form, Genus: Flying Ray. In my opinion, it should be classified as a bird. Distinctive Features: Broad wings, long tail, a pair of clawed fins, and curved ivory-white fangs. Hey, I just thought of a business idea! Could we pass these fangs off as ivory? Serres typically live in groups and feed on large fish, seabirds, and drifting debris. While they may look similar to Olitiau, their behavior couldn't be more different. While Olitiaus are generally non-aggressive, Serres are known for their fondness for challenging creatures larger than themselves—including sperm whales, baleen whales, megalodon sharks, and passing ships. Sometimes, they even mistake protruding rocky outcrops and coral reefs for foes. When a Serres spots a ship, it leaps from the water, attacking the vessel with its sharp wings and calling upon its companions. They seem to have a competitive nature; each Serres strives to soar higher and leave deeper marks on its target. Stay away from the windows. You never know how deep their wings can slice. Despite their large numbers, Serres communicate through a single method: sound. They can produce a wide range of calls within the 10-180Hz frequency range, ideal for underwater communication, and they can sense each other's vibrations through their wing membranes. The best way to deal with Serres is to disrupt their hearing. Shouts, bangs, and music can confuse them, while enough volume can physically irritate their auditory systems, causing them to flee in discomfort. Now that's more like it! My former captain tried using anti-Olitiau measures against them, which is why he's my "former captain."

According to the Timekeeper's statement provided to our personnel, the recent hijacking of the "Free Breeze" was orchestrated by Ms. Grace, a member of Manus Vindictae. Her involvement included the abduction of the Nukutais and persuading passengers to wear Manus Vindictae masks. Considering this, an upgrade in our risk assessment for Ms. Grace may be necessary, along with issuing a formal warrant for her arrest.

Additionally, with assistance from Regulus, a member of the Timekeeper's team, Researcher Ulrich of Laplace was able to complete his 'Artificial Storm' experiment on the "Free Breeze". Regulus's record was identified as an immune material, however its overall efficacy is weak, providing only a minor delay in the onset of Era Sickness, and critically lacks reproducibility; none of the copies of the records show the same level of efficacy. "Walk, walk, through the dense forest, around the streams, toss aside your shoes, undo your buttons, ponder in the wind, and dance under the moonlight."

"Your body transforms into a werewolf, a helmet materializing atop your head. With your transparent noggin, you can breathe even in the vacuum of space. You tilt your head back and let out your first howl beneath the full moon."
"If humans were to develop wings, would they still yearn to fly toward an imagined future?"
"Oh, my dear friend, on this long journey, what I fear most is not the tasks, paperwork, or police, but the lack of wine, jazz, and companionship."
"Hold tight to the helm, don't lose sight of your direction, and never forget where you are headed."
"Some people think all they need to do is say 'Ahoy, matey,' and just like that, they've become a true pirate."
"At sunset, fish leap out of the water. I throw my harpoon, and there in the once-clear waves, I see a blood-colored sunset."
"Living on the sea isn't easy. You have to leave everything behind and head towards the unknown, just as we did back then, right, Anne?"
"Ha? Would anyone really listen to that noisy, unsophisticated racket?"
"We can sleep in other people's parked cars at night, and earn pocket money by delivering newspapers during the day. Wait and see, one day our names will be on an album cover."
"They call you a vagrant, a clown, a good-for-nothing, unworthy of the stage, but don't bother caring about a single word because their brains are too small to hold even an extra note."
—Article one of the rock 'n' roll act
"Is life really anything more than a moment on the stage? [After all, each and every script must eventually reach its final page, and then the curtain falls.]"
"Take a deep breath, look up, don't blink, and wipe the sweat off your hands. When that curtain rises, you'll own the whole world!"
"I'm tired of staring at that gray ceiling, unable to see the moon, tired of everything. But standing here, as I lift my hands, I start to think maybe I can touch the stars."
"A few coins can buy a smile, which is much more precious than anything else I've ever seen."
"Put on the sunglasses, smooth out your wig, adjust the microphone to just the right spot. What's the theme for tonight's performance? Oh, this rockin' APPLe believes that won't matter much."
"On a moonless midnight in October, I fly alone over the city, wanting to escape. No one can catch up with me."
"Before dawn, I caught a star trying to escape gravity."
"He was amazing, swaying day and night with that guitar. In the end, not even death could separate them."
"I don't agree with the noisier parts of rock music, but I have to admit that every time I switch to their station, this flower seems to show its best state."

Wrapped in the embrace of her brother and friends, Fatutu wears a new necklace woven from red tree fruits as her people sing birthday songs for her. |The loud confetti and unfamiliar birthday melodies of the outside world still confuse Fatutu. As the leader of the Nukutai grows another year older, the hibiscus flower in her braid stays fresh, and she still holds hope for her new home.

An outfit prepared for female musicians of the "Free Breeze" crew. Due to the outstanding solo performance of the interviewee, the crew prepared her a unique uniform befitting her role as the ship's music star.

A composite instrument combining features of the violin, flute, euphonium, and other instruments through the "Astrictus" incantation. Known as "a most captivating gadget," "the eternal pearl of the 'Free Breeze'," and "the maestro of music" ... the interviewee used it for solos and gained numerous accolades.
It is rumored that this incantation originated from a renowned luthier family in Cremona, the birthplace of the violin. This background sheds light on the performer's extraordinary musical talents.

A souvenir in the shape of a ship's wheel, accentuated by silk ribbons in oceanic colors, given to every guest boarding the "Free Breeze."
The rules state that crew members should not ordinarily purchase or wear items intended for passengers. However, as part of a promotional stunt, the previous captain gifted this special item to the interviewee, in recognition of her role in the ship's publicity efforts.

Cremona is a world-famous haven for violins. Every day, its streets are filled with pilgrims who eagerly discuss music theory and gather to perform out of their deep devotion to artistry and craft of the violin.

Yes, the violin can be magnificent—until its sound saturates every day, every place, every room, and every dining table discussion. The child who once adored the violin began to lose her passion, her eyes drifting toward the broader world of musical instruments. However, to parents who were famed luthiers and players, anything else was only a distraction.

The family's arcane skill brought them accolades and opened doors with their innovations. But their rebellious child used that very skill to combine all the instruments she had secretly collected, creating something strange, beautiful and new. With this creation, she boarded a cruise ship bound for destinations unknown. Just like countless other children who ventured far from home, she left without looking back.

To this day, the girl from Cremona who boarded the "Free Breeze" continues to sail across the oceans of the world.

Bagpipe Musicians from Scotland define it as a reed aerophone, capable of producing a brilliant and resonant sound by inflating its bag. I think it's perfect for a grand, high-pitched entrance! However, its tone is rather pitched and can easily become monotonous. Irish Tin Whistle A six-holed flute with a fipple mouthpiece, known for its continuous sound that produces rich overtones. Its unique and complex timbre is fascinating. But it suffers from a limited range and volume, leaving it unsuitable for performances on a cruise ship. Euphonium A quintessential low-register instrument! It boasts an impressive lower range, and I adore its deep, mellow tone. Unfortunately, it can't reach higher notes, causing it to occasionally blend into the background during performances. Violin With its wide range and beautiful tone, the violin is a captivating instrument. Its rich variety of sound is delightful to all who hear it—unless, of course, you've been forced to play it since childhood. ...

Barcarola: A talking mouth?! Where did you come from? I'd love to hear your story!
Pandora Wilson: I believe it would be best to keep our interview focused on you, Ms. Barcarola. You're the one that people want to know. 
Pandora Wilson: I was hoping you might share your experiences as a musician on the "Free Breeze."
Barcarola: Oh, right! Of course! Well, it was a wonderful experience. I still think of my time aboard fondly. During the day, I'd spend my time listening to our guests' stories, and if there happened to be a luncheon or tea party, then I would join them as we savored new dishes from around the world together.
Barcarola: And in the evenings, I would perform brand-new compositions based on their requests and experiences of the day, I admit I miss basking in their applause.
Pandora Wilson: That sounds absolutely sublime, what a shame that your ship is gone.
Barcarola: The "Free Breeze" may be gone but I'll never stop performing. In fact, we could even play together!
Pandora Wilson: I'm afraid I'm not much of a musician.
Barcarola: Don't worry, even the sound of a whistle or melodica can become part of a wonderful performance. I'll help you!
Pandora Wilson: I appreciate the encouragement, although I must insist against it.
Barcarola: ... Oh, scusami! I didn't mean to be too forward, I just love sharing music!

Handcrafted accessories made from white hibiscus flowers indigenous to Nukutaeao. The Nukutais utilize a special technique to preserves these flowers, which has made them popular among visitors during their Merchants' Fair.
The flowers symbolize purity, resilience, and eternal life. However, the interviewee seems unaware of this symbolism.

A necklace crafted from various marine shells, each one intricately inscribed with hieroglyphics, except one, the furthest to the left.
The Nukutais consider these shells sacred, wearing them as amulets throughout their entire life. The inscriptions symbolize their emotional journey and most significant moments. Thus, the number and neatness of the inscriptions reflect the wearer's age, experiences, and soul.

A mysterious totem inked on the interviewee's arm, which seems to lack deeper significance.
The Nukutais, skilled at living in harmony with nature on their secluded island, use stone powder as paint and their bodies as canvases to create unique designs.

The island was sinking.

Few noticed the dotted archipelago drifting in the South Pacific. As the merchant ships sailed away with the final tides before sunset, taking with them tropical fish and Nukutai handicrafts, they left behind an ever-submerging cemetery and a coastline battered repeatedly by storms. Nukutaeao is but a tiny dot in the ocean, a place that might be erased from the map with a swipe of a finger.

Masked figures reached out, stating, "We are born in the wrong era."

The tumultuous waves repeatedly affirmed their foresight. For the first time, those who lived their lives alongside shells argued intensely. The elders, shaking their heads, stubbornly ignored the signs, while the young discreetly covered the cracks in their shells, discussing an era-defining revenge and their planned escape.

The debate stretched until dawn. When the stars faded into the morning light, the new chieftain led what remained of their tribe from the vanishing island onto the "Free Breeze".

She said the Nukutais had no choice left.

"The world outside is filled with hate and war." The shells passed down from our ancestors tell us how frightening the world outside Nukutaeao is. Wicked witches hide in ancient caves, Nakarua serpents often conjure colossal waves on the seas, and roaring monsters and giant birds lurk on every island. Nukutaeao is peaceful and serene, while disputes are ever-present outside. "The outside world is full of cunning, evil people who will hurt others easily." What I've seen on the "Free Breeze" is quite different. People sing and dance, and they're masters of fascinating performances. The brave sit on small boats drifting with the waves, spreading "peace and love." Every night, under the watch of the Southern Cross, the passengers sleep peacefully. They seem no different from us. "We are born in the wrong era." The outside world isn't as bad as we heard, and people aren't as evil as we imagined ... Are these people truly the right targets for our vendetta?

Pandora Wilson: You are certain to be the subject of great curiosity in agreeing to this interview. So little is known about your homeland.
Fatutu: There's a reason for that, the "Veil of Nothingness" cast by our ancestors, it hid Nukutaeao from the outside world.
Pandora Wilson: So, prior to now, you never had any contact with the outside world?
Fatutu: No, we did, our people would periodically welcome traders to our land and invited guests to come and experience our island.
Pandora Wilson: That does make me curious, what kind of goods do you have to trade?
Fatutu: Pickled red snapper, sundried hala fruit ... Oh, and we use a special technique to preserve hibiscus flowers, the accessories we make from them are always very popular.
Pandora Wilson: Considering all that happened, I'm surprised that you seem so positive about the "outside world."
Fatutu: ... We Nukutais have always been hospitable. Even aboard that cruise ship ...
Fatutu: Ah, but I noticed that the guests on that ship seemed to love and yearn for the sea. That's quite different from our people. I wonder why they don't miss their homes and friends?
Pandora Wilson: Perhaps it's because they don't have a home like yours.

A tri-cornered hat with feathers that tremble slightly, as if harboring a mysterious will of its own.
It appeared on an ordinary morning, bringing the interviewee a distant call, an unexpected voyage, and an extended duty.

A piece of dead coral, heavy on the shoulder, like the fingers and bones of the departed. The interviewee explains that at its core, it is a flower, its life is marked by transformation and sedimentation until it reaches its final form—a bloom that will never wither.
And so, she continues to cherish it, holding it delicately.

A fossilized turbo, with distant wind sounds and untold whispers filling its shell.
"It was salvaged from a deep sea trench, murmuring love, regret, and wishes. Until these whispers cease, I shall keep sailing."

A thin, transparent piece of silken fabric with a pearly sheen, complementing the colorful glaze of the shells. 
After observing the entire process of customizing a performance gown, the interviewee kept this small remnant, believing it to hold some fleeting inspiration, far too precious to be discarded.

A silver-plated brooch, reflecting the fabric's hue of the evening dress, shimmering like water ripples in the mist.
Sea stars are flexible and simple creatures that perceive everything through their bodies without relying on eyesight.
Much like the owner of this accessory.

A handheld censer filled with hot coals and frankincense, provided by Eurybia, the sponsor of the "Midnight Smoke Show." It's used to present incense to the guests.
"It's one of our best brand events from our 'Ocean' series. Through her performance, our fashion philosophy of 'spirituality and self' has been perfectly embodied."

A custom fur shawl made primarily from the winter fur of domesticated critters, hand-trimmed and collected by the lady herself. It also incorporates spider silk, synthetic fibers, and ornate feathers left by Dodoughs in the wilderness. No animals or critters were harmed in the manufacturing process.

Accessories produced by Ms. NewBabel's Critter Center for formal pet occasions.
Although popular belief holds that the critters' compliance is due to arcane incantations, the designer asserts that the comfortable, lightweight materials and the love in their hearts are what truly make the difference.

A cherished evening dress worn by the interviewee on significant occasions. She spent her first earnings on this gown to step onto bigger and further stages. Now, she takes it out of her wardrobe once again.

Red seafarer rain boots issued to the crew of the cruise ship.
Made from PVC with steel-plated soles, they protect the little sailor against punctures and erosion as she rushes across the deck, continuing the hunt in the post-storm sea breeze.

A slender shotgun disguised within a meticulously folded umbrella, all in an effort to avoid alarming passengers.
Until the trigger is pulled, few would ever imagine a hunter's silver bullet to fly out instead of an umbrella cover.

Silver bullets specially constructed to be fired underwater.
The interviewee indicates a knot on the carrying strap: "The previous one had been worn while crossing the atoll. Now, it is kept as a memento."

Parrots are often held to be divine messengers, capable of conversing with both humans and gods through their gift of speech. However, the stylist adorned the interviewee with the feathers not as a testament to her skills but to endow this elegant attire with a touch of passion and courage.

An imported fan made from sandalwood with ribs carved in Baroque patterns adorned by the thinnest silk, favored by Europeans.
When unfurled, it gently wafts out a delightful fragrance capable of soothing guests, lifting their spirits, and helping them find "peaceful awareness."

A brooch of metal and glass, shaped like wings, taken from a dusty box and polished anew.
The hostess of the salon acts like your closest friend while maintaining the perfect distance, much like this brooch, just above the heart, but never piercing the skin.

There's nothing there, you think to yourself, not even my own shadow.
But then, perhaps there is something. As you stroll through the hall beneath the moonlight, you find a note.

Semmelweis stands before a strangely shaped fountain, subconsciously staring at the water—naturally, her reflection isn't there. She can only see a sign and a few lonely Goldfinch Coins at the bottom. "The Fountain of Fate grants the wishes of every traveler. If you're generous with the Goldfinch Coins in your pocket and ask sincerely, you might get an unexpected response. Of course, if your wish or the way you wish doesn't please the fountain, be careful—it may charge you an extra fee." "Since you're already here, why not give it a try?"

"Please come in, they eagerly await your arrival."
Following the voice, Semmelweis steps inside. The windows reflect her silhouette, and a serene melody flows through the air. She is momentarily bewildered: are these artefacts mere illusions woven from sound, or are they tangible reality?
The hall is empty, she is greeted only by transparent display cases.

Though unique, the collection is not entirely unfamiliar.
Semmelweis searches her bag and finds it—an artefact she collected earlier, one also imbued with melodies.
Semmelweis examines the exquisite exhibit with care. They seem both real and illusory, as if from another time and space, beckoning her to reach for the melodies that seems to surround them.

Nowadays, a commotion on the street is hardly surprising. A gentleman, holding a pistol, is seeking someone to duel on his behalf—his injuries do not mar his elegance but rather add a touch of tragic heroism to his demeanor.

Semmelweis is not skilled in this art, but her courage far exceeds her opponent's. The crowd erupts in thunderous applause, surging towards the victor, eager to lift her up—as if driven mad by the word "victory."

"Madam, your psychological condition requires immediate attention!"
Semmelweis finds a new lifeline. However, after a long conversation at the clinic, she realizes that the doctor has mistaken her for another patient.
The doctor continues a monologue, ignoring any explanations. Semmelweis decides to play along to get away.

A group of Refined Carbuncles snatched Semmelweis's communicator, but a buzzing flash came at the right moment, scaring them into dropping it in the middle of the street before fleeing.
Semmelweis picks up the communicator and reads the Foundation's message: "All squads status report, do you require assistance?"

Hadn't she just been here? The studio is empty, but Semmelweis recognizes the roses on the table—the lingering arcane energy is familiar to her.
"Why ...?"
Bullets. Black mist. The fresh water droplets on the petals.
Semmelweis falls into deep thought.

<color=#BF7E31>"It opens this easily?"</color>
<color=#BF7E31>"As it turns out, a 'door' is only closed if you perceive it to be. A 'seemingly locked' door isn't necessarily so, and there might be more than one way to get through it."</color>

"Fugue of Reflections" is the latest expansion for "A Series of Dusks." This expansion adds a new ending to the base game and introduces character-exclusive artefacts known as [Acoustica]. More characters will rise to prominence in the pre-Storm Vienna. New Ending You don't need to have the expansion loaded up to experience the new ending, but you do need to have completed the [A Wish Granted] ending. Explore Vienna to see how to unlock the new conclusion. [Acoustica] Artefacts With the expansion loaded up, you can acquire [Acoustica] artefacts during exploration. These artefacts represent exclusive power ups for certain characters, and require the character to be in specific party positions to activate their effects. You can enhance Acoustica artefacts by meeting certain conditions. By meeting all enhancement requirements, an Acoustica artefact becomes [Fully Enhanced]. Based on how many fully enhanced artefacts are in your layout, additional [Harmonia] buff effects can be triggered, further strengthening your team. Completing the final path node of the Ring Road and defeating the [Impending Crisis] battle guarantees you one [Acoustica] artefact, prioritizing those exclusive to your current companion. You may also find Acoustica artefacts during exploration. [Current Characters with Acoustica Artefacts]: A Knight, Eagle, Voyager, Spathodea, Sonetto, Ms. NewBabel, Lilya, Lorelei, An-an Lee, Lucy, Jiu Niangzi, Anjo Nala, Lopera, Willow, Flutterpage, Barcarola, Charlie, Regulus, Druvis III, Matilda, 37, J, TTT, Semmelweis, Eternity, Medicine Pocket, Centurion, Sotheby, Melania, and Pickles. Tougher Battles With the expansion loaded up, enemy stats are increased. During an [Impending Crisis] and the final battle, you will also gain three powerful special incantations. Once used up, however, the enemies will become significantly stronger. Base Content The base content has also been updated with the following: New Path Node: The [Tuning Hall] path node has been added. New Combat Mechanics: Some battles can now include extra detrimental incantations that are added to your hand during combat. New Artefacts: [Acoustica] artefacts and [Fabled] quality artefacts have been added. More content awaits your discovery.

The combination of toughness and softness, an object of graceful motion. Dancers use it to sketch rainbows for the gods, and the gods reward them with applause and glory.
There might be a thousand ways to fold a paper bird, but only the style taught by childhood friends can carry wishes high into the sky.
A freshly composed, unperformed piece of music, imbued with the hopes, sorrows, and longings of its creator. One corner, once soaked and now dried, bears tiny crystallized grains of salt.
As long as you wear it, you can swagger onto any theater stage, and perhaps even earn some unexpected and anticipated applause.
Another form of music. Classical, lyrical jazz, or rock? Only the vibrating stylus of a record player can truly understand.
Grow, be incinerated, and then grow again. The oak etches the ebb and flow of arcane energy into its rings, just as life captures each twilight intertwined with joy and sorrow.
A bright and proud crystal orb. The user will soon notice that uttering the phrase "Who is the most powerful crystal orb?" significantly raises the accuracy of the divination.
Both a clever enigma and a subtle truth. Some are captivated by it for life, while others take one glance and flee in terror.
An incredibly advanced mode of transportation, a toy for the daring. Riding it across cobblestone streets, all worries vanish, leaving only a heart-pounding, exhilarating thrill.

Go ahead and place your bets. You know, even if you lose everything, you can always bounce back, because this is the last chip you carry around your neck.
Meticulously prepared with the freshest, most precious ingredients, and catalyzed by whimsical ideas. Take a sip, it definitely does not taste like Dr. Papper.

In the Suitcase, you can meet people from all corners of the world. Their words, actions, and experiences each have a unique rhythm.
Just like how the world has countless different instruments: hurdy-gurdies, ouds, bagpipes, launeddas ...
When these unique instruments come together, they create ever-changing new melodies.
Yes ... Take, for example, the cello, saxophone, and harp. Each has its own charm when played solo.
Of course, the violin isn't bad either. Its wide range and beautiful tone make it a natural favorite ...
But I prefer playing ensembles, Like the performances on "Free Breeze," where the waves and the wind join in, now that is music that's truly irreplaceable!
Yeah, exactly. We could also hold a concert in the Suitcase together!
Will everyone come? Bring your instruments, a hand drum, a maraca, even a leaf ...
It's a bit like Nukutaeao here; we're surrounded by water, though there, the sea breeze blows, and the surface of the water often mists over.
At dusk, we would kick cocoball on the beach together. Fishing boats would dock, and the sun would set and rise.
There are many strange rooms here. Sometimes, I forget where I've been.
I want to ask them for directions, but many people don't seem to care where they are ...
There are many other things as well ... but I'm sure I'll find a way to deal with them!
Yes, strangers often come by, wandering like me, looking around, sometimes getting lost.
But back during the trade seasons, we entertained many guests as well. I imagine it was a bit like when we first met.
Just like back then, we can trade things we need and help each other out. After all, we're now living on the same land.
The wilderness is peaceful. Every now and then, we need to let our ears and hearts rest—but just for a little while!
It's also a place for solitary thinking, just like that old church in Cremona.
Wandering through familiar places, that's something I used to do too.
The same instruments, the same performances, everyone saying the same things ... None of it was bad, really, but I couldn't stay trapped there any longer.
So I took my "Crackling Box" and wandered, eventually finding my way here.
Well, I'm constantly thinking of new compositions and performances, imagining sounds and instruments I've yet to see.

I tried writing in the sand by the water's edge, matching the words on the shells with the new ones I've learned.

Only the Nukutai can understand these words, as these shells record all of our emotions and experiences.

Playing solo has its charm, too.
By ensemble, you mean performing together?
How are you settling in here?
Is it a lot different from the island?
I walk around here pretty often.
These words are incomprehensible to me.

Don't lose hope! The Foundation and the LSCC have been working hard to overcome the "Storm," and we've never been so close to achieving it!
Yes! Our research on the "Storm" is on the verge of a breakthrough—one that will benefit everyone!
Come on, guys! Do you REALLY want to plaster one of those things on your face? You'll never be able to eat again—or listen to music!
Blimey, what kind of life would that be?!
Don't waste your breath on these lapdogs! They're all bark and no bite!
The civilians have calmed down, Timekeeper.
Take a moment. I'll deal with the rest.
No, Sonetto, this crisis is far from over.
Good grief! How many passengers are on this bloody thing?!
Ms. Grace deliberately led us here to the deck ... but why?
Timekeeper, the fog is thickening by the minute. The low visibility might hinder our ability to use arcane skills.
As suspected. Our attacks can't reach her from this distance.
Please allow me to spearhead the assault.
Is Ms. Grace inside ...? No, this power feels more complex than any person—and much more dangerous.
Timekeeper! The cocoon is affecting the masked guests somehow—look, they're writhing in pain!
We have to act fast—finish this before more civilians fall victim.
Why, Ms. Grace? They've already given their souls over to you ... Why do you insist on taking their lives, too?

Ha! A bit of maths is nothing to this brilliant Captain!
Don't be nervous. That touch earlier was just an accident.
Can you communicate in English? Hello?
... Looks like I need to start studying waveforms.
Wait, it seems the signal is not properly connected.
I need to guide the signal to the <color=#ffb892>receiver</color> first. Apologies, but I need to make some adjustments to you, miss, sir or ...
Alright, there must be components here to help me adjust the signal ... like these <color=#ffb892>deflection plates</color>?
Various <color=#fb7d09>interferences</color> will block off all signal transmissions.

Interesting ... the output is a little different this time.
I should probably summarize some of the recurring waveforms; otherwise, they'll just be gibberish to me.
Who let a carbuncle in here? Oh, this is going to be fun!
Catch it, everyone! Quick, get it!
First to catch it gets this string of sausages!
Damn it, who's running around in the corridor?!
... Back to summarizing—it's not hard, but some of these signals are too weak for my liking.
Fortunately, I borrowed a few <color=#ffb892>signal amplifiers</color> from the engineering team ahead of time. Best put them to use.
When there are multiple receivers, all devices must be activated to obtain information.
Signal amplifiers can boost signal waves and split them into two separate waves.
Use deflection plates to direct the signal waves to the amplifier's input and see it in action.
... That's the long and short of it.
For all of you, identifying the initial patterns should be a simple task.
The real challenge lies in how to deal with the chaotic parts—the ones without any pattern.
I ... I'll do my best to understand.
It's all down to the team! Once you're all proficient enough, we can expand to larger-scale statistical work.
I've identified one set of signals from the previous work—<color=#ffb892>the decryption Key</color>.
It can control the <color=#ffb892>shielding switch</color>, disabling the <color=#ffb892>shielding device</color> to unlock more pathways for receiving signals.
<color=#fb7d09>The decryption Key</color> is a special decrypting signal; on its own, it cannot activate the receivers.
Connect the decryption Key to the shielding switch to turn it off.
After the shielding switch is off, the shielding device blocking the signals will be disabled.
Signals can disrupt each other; an existing signal will take priority and block any new signals that cross into its path.
Place a component here to block off this signal, giving priority to the one on the left.
Use the interference component to block other signals and give the Key priority, allowing it to extend into the shielding switch.
Honestly, this feels more like physical labor than mathematics.
The more forms and patterns we organize, the more possibilities arise.
... And the more options we have to sift through in the end.
Most data cryptography involves this kind of process.
Just think of it as a little game to relax with after work, rather than a physical job.
That way, even if we discover this is just an elaborate years-long prank, we won't suffer too much disappointment.
This signal is being interfered by many shielding devices. Let's hope we've got enough key signal transmitters.
The letter in the upper left of the icons shows the correspondence between shielding devices and their respective switches.
Make good use of the signal amplifier to boost the signals and decrypt the devices.
If this is truly a satellite signal receiver, we'll need to use this new perspective to solve the issue.
Exactly. It's about as valid as your "Awakened hypothesis," don't you think?
Assuming it was built based on the LSCC's aerospace engineering standards, its encryption methods should have discernible patterns.
We can extract information fragments and cross-reference them with existing encoding standards.
Then, we can iterate through all possibilities ...
Perhaps we need to keep existing encoding standards in mind, and manually adjust the shielding device's decrypting sequence to something workable.

The notes and strings of home play only old tunes.
Young notes struggle to break free from the cradle,
Yearning to be as free as the sea breeze, to roam and wander.
Dearest ones, do not worry, do not grieve,

From the viscous depths of night, I see you,
My family, my kin,

Now I lift you up,
Caressing the texture of words, inhaling the scent of sea salt.
I cannot find, I fear, I cannot find the true you.

Forgetting tedious rules,

That tin toy controls the succubus ... ridiculous! It looks like junk from a flea market! If I'd known, I would have guarded it with my life! Hopefully, I won't be blamed for losing it. A devout believer like me shouldn't face such an end.
The journey doesn't stop, can't stop. Our destination, the Promised Land, still lies far ahead. Is our home actually at the end of this? Are we drifting further away? I remember my home was ...

The moth-attraction experiment mainly induced strong homesickness. To end my uncontrollable crying and depressive symptoms, this phototaxis research will be temporarily concluded. I will start compiling the summary report as usual.
Nukutaeao? The island swallowed up by the sea? I read about it in the newspaper. How is that linked to our fate? Oh, right, that was something from the "past." So, now that island should still exist.

I remember ... it was in a tucked away in the corner of the newspaper, a dilapidated wooden boat carrying "the last of the Nukutais." It was only mentioned once, followed by bold headlines of new maritime discoveries. Hey, a bunch of arcanists suddenly appearing out of nowhere—who else but us would care?

Humans are insatiable; you hide to avoid conflict with them, yet they see it as the natural order of things. All of this is for the sake of those new arcanists. The sooner we can make their island well known, the sooner they'll learn of humanity's malice, and we can avoid the worst case scenario.

Lady Grace, elegant and merciful Lady Grace, such benevolence should not be bestowed upon humans for mere show. Those human boiler operators, along with their captain who shields them, should be sent to the depths of the sea, to mark the beginning of our new kin's journey. A transaction? They don't deserve it. Well then! It's time to set sail! Load another shovel of coal into the boiler!

The sound of shattering, followed by scolding from above—new materials are needed. The heart is too soft, the spine lacks strength, and the skull is unstable. There must be a perfect material capable of holding a life through its entire lifetime ...

The clangor of drills, the new collaborators are too noisy, interrupting my meditations. They haven't even undergone the trials; why allow them to roam freely... Is there no peace even at the world's end? Hopefully, Lord Forget Me Not will stand firm against their leader.

The gulls are calling, but there's no sound of boats cutting through the waves. Perhaps the promised ship won't come after all. I had been pessimistic, but it's still disheartening not to have more compatriots join us. I hope Lady Grace, at least, brought back sufficient supplies.

Silence. Not even a whisper of wind. What else can I do? Since Lady Grace brought back some shells, why don't I ... Teeth? Yes, teeth might work. Strong, enduring. If my life ends here, my teeth might ...

Lord Forget Me Not seemed to have said something to Ms. Grace. It's unusual to see a hint of anxiety in her usually serene smile, but I'm sure I didn't misread it. Ms. Grace, the graceful and composed Ms. Grace ... Have you made some mistakes as well?

Why am I guarding the cold storage? Everyone else is guarding the engine room or the lower cabins. How could the cold storage be of use in our future tasks?

What's that? It's for storing Ms. Grace's collection?

Oh, that makes sense. May she be in good spirits.

Welcome to the cold storage, new friend. Sorry, but the ice cream has been moved out. You can take a rest here for now. Ms. Grace in her wisdom wants to document everyone's past, even the most foolish stories. Perhaps it's just her love for collecting, I can't say for sure. Nonetheless, it means everyone has the opportunity to be remembered. Isn't that marvelous?

I once had the privilege of seeing Ms. Grace's collection. Every piece is a work of art, meticulously preserved and each with its own story. Yes, Ms. Grace remembers them all, even those who would have been forgotten by society. So, wipe away that frown. Once we reach land, she will remember us and carry us forward on our path of devotion.

What is a home really? The land? The house? Or the people around you? It's a complicated question, but if I had to choose, I'd pick the people. You can find a new land, your house can be rebuilt, but every shell's pattern is unique. Wherever they go, I will follow.

Home? Home is full of suffering. I might as well set it ablaze. Is it my fault I was born an arcanist? Take me anywhere, it's better than staying here in misery. Even if I fall to my death on the way, at least it's my choice.

Home no longer exists. Only by staying close to my loved ones can I gain some warmth. My future is filled with suffering, and my shell will bear many scars. When I die, my legacy will be a tale of sorrow. How will my descendants learn about happiness from such memories? Please, take us back to the past. Let the children experience happiness at least once, so they won't lose their way.

Filthy, filthy. I'm at the doorstep of home but can't open the door. My hands are covered in blood. Touching the doorknob will anger my mother. Please, give me a small basin of water so I can wash my hands clean and step over the threshold with a smile.

Manus Vindictae has leveraged the information gathered from crossing the "Storm" to present Ms. Grace as a prophet, thereby earning the trust of the Nukutai people in this era. According to internal records, the Nukutais, displaced by rising sea levels, were meant to be contacted and properly resettled by our branch. It may be time to reconsider our strategy of passively awaiting era events to unfold, to avoid such incidents in the future.

From birth, the Nukutais will receive a shell which, through special arcanum rituals, records their entire emotional journey. This is how they described it during previous consultations. They take pride in passing on shells filled with beautiful memories to their descendants. In essence, the Nukutais' "Spirit Shells" carry an arcanist's lifetime of emotional fluctuations, making them excellent carriers of arcane energy, and a prime target for Manus Vindictae.

Ms. Grace, who carried out Manus Vindictae's plan to win over the Nukutais, is suspected of being directly under the command of Mr. Forget Me Not and linked to the earlier incident involving the transfer of Ms. Kimberly's contract item. Given her numerous malicious actions in the "Free Breeze" incident, which had a profound impact on all parties involved, it is recommended that she be added to the wanted list.

The exact goal of Manus Vindictae remains unclear, but since Ms. Grace took over "Free Breeze," there have been multiple unusual sailing records. Based on the findings from this research, it is suspected that Manus Vindictae is stationed in a region even further south. Australia has already undergone comprehensive checks during the Uluru Games. It is now recommended that subsequent searches focus on South America and South Africa, particularly in regions like Chile, Argentina, and the Republic of South Africa.
