Listen up, rookie. Since I'm your instructor, I need to make sure you don't embarrass me out there.
Did you review the basic operational guidelines for Los Angeles Arcane Affairs Officers before taking this job?
Yes! First, all police operations must remain within Los Angeles's administrative jurisdiction.

Second, we must develop practical and cohesive plans, procedures, and strategies to reduce arcanum-related crimes and behaviors, improve the quality of life for citizens, and maintain harmonious relations between humans and arcanists ...

Administrative Procedure 311-09: In civil disputes involving arcanum, mediation should be prioritized to minimize the impact of arcanum-related factors, provide citizens with professional guidance, and avoid actions that could escalate conflicts.
… Oh, great, a model student response.
Administrative Procedure 320-05: In criminal cases involving arcanum, Arcane Affairs Officers in the vicinity should provide assistance whenever possible, minimizing harm to citizens …
With that painfully by-the-book response, you might as well join Internal Affairs. Heard they love that kind of stuff.
Let's keep it simple, remember—big or small, whenever arcanum is involved, it's up to us, the "arcane cops," to handle it.
But don't worry too much; more often than not, the small stuff outweighs the big stuff.
Understood, Instructor Poitier. Should I recite the rest?
The rest? Nah, you sound like you've got that covered—
On the topic of injury and death compensation ...
Rookie, where's your chameleon comms? Lost it?
I think I still have it ... look, right here. It's just gone into camouflage.
Maybe Qiangliang showing up scared it into hiding.
Qiangliang? That electric tiger of yours? The one that lives in your phone?
This old brick phone was the relic I used during my first summoning of Qiangliang. It became the token of our bond.
When I use this phone to call Qiangliang, it will answer.
Wild! It's like something straight out of those TV shows.
But using a phone for rituals? I thought rituals from your side of the world would be more …
... Traditional? Like those dancing shadow puppets you've got?
That's an excellent guess. Previous generations of summoners in my family did use shadow puppetry to call Qiangliang. But that was centuries ago.
Oh? So, does that make you a once-in-a-century kind of genius?
… Not really. I was just lucky that the phone is a more convenient method than shadow puppetry.
There it is—you're still humble as ever, princess.
Can you summon Qiangliang again? I owe it a thank you for the help earlier.
I wouldn't recommend it. Calling Qiangliang without a good reason might make it angry, and …
Great. We've hit a dead end. Just what exactly did we miss?
Maybe we should go over the items in Loggerhead's bag again.
Loggerhead … seriously? She packed all these film reels, but somehow missed the most important one!
Look at this. Was she planning to open a video store? So many movie reels!
Hey, Liang, these ones are in Chinese, right?
… Yes, ma'am. That's The Qimen Fighters. Here's Ms. Vampire, and Troubled Lunatics.
Classic Hong Kong films, but it's unclear if these were Loggerhead's collection, or gifts from Director Noire.
Good grief. Do we need to watch all of these? We don't have that kind of time.
No, I don't think so. These are just regular film reels, and their stories aren't related to our investigation.
Ha! I almost forgot you used to sneak around and watch movies behind your parents' backs. Your knowledge is broader than I thought.
So, other than C07, which one here's your favorite?
Ugh, dull as ever. I knew it.
But … if we wrap this up quick, you should watch Ms. Vampire. It's a hallmark of Hong Kong arcanum films.
We've gone through the bag, but the missing reel isn't here.
Perhaps it's time for us to try something else.
Yeah, let's hear what our big-shot director has to say.
So, what happened next? After I passed out, how'd you manage to drive off the Nightpiercer?
… We didn't drive her off. She left when she heard the sirens from the reinforcements you called.
Chief Elden arrived. Director Noire used arcane skills to control her puppets and guide them to you. That allowed the medics to reach you and Ms. Scott in time to get you to the hospital.
Sounds like we owe her a big thank you.
… Sorry, Miss Poitier. I couldn't stop Ms. Qi Xing. She took the Reunion of the Three Swallows …
Don't beat yourself up, kid. No one expected the Nightpiercer to show up like that.
How are Scott and Pug Dog holding up?
Pug Dog's been caught and is in custody. Ms. Scott is stable after emergency treatment, but she hasn't regained consciousness just yet.

Doctors believe her coma, like those other victims, was caused by Reunion of the Three Swallows. The department has officers guarding her, but until the case is solved, we can't expect her to provide any useful information.
As for Director Noire … Sorry, I should've informed you earlier. She's the one who tipped me off about the illegal arcane artifact deal.
Though she participated in the deal, her honesty, cooperation, and her lawyer's efforts convinced the department not to pursue her case further.
Tch, typical of Hollywood. A director can go from criminal to collaborator with just a few words.
We should talk to her again—about Ms. Qi Xing and about that reel … Maybe there's more she hasn't told us.
You know, I've shared so many of my stories with you. Why don't you tell me some of yours?
Directors are always on the lookout for good material. I'm curious about your past.
They say you're a once-in-a-generation talent, the one who summoned Qiangliang—the Xiandao Beast that hadn't answered the Liang family's call in 300 years.
… That was all just a misunderstanding.
The day I summoned Qiangliang, I learned its name and glimpsed its memories.
Centuries ago, Qiangliang was gravely injured during its last summoning and has been recovering ever since. That's why it hasn't answered the Liang family's calls.
I just happened to summon it when it was finally healed. My family thought Qiangliang chose me, so they placed high expectations on me.
… But I'm no chosen one. I was just lucky.
Does your family know about this?
… I did not want to disappoint them.
"That morning, we lay amidst the ruins, and sis handed me a bottle of beer. Suddenly, I understood—I already had the whole world. I just hadn't bothered to look."
… You're right. If we cut out the chaotic, corrupted footage, this could be a great film.
That line—it's so Teresa. A house can be rebuilt, and the gaps between friends can be mended. She always loved life.
It's hard to believe, especially after seeing this. A Teresa like this would never have taken her own life.
Miss Vigil, thank you. Her creation being restored to its original form is something I'm truly grateful for. And it's all thanks to you and your team.
About Qiangliang … I'm more sorry than you can imagine. This wasn't my intention, but ultimately, my selfish behavior caused this to happen.
If there's anything I can do to make amends …
There's no need to feel guilty, Miss Qi Xing. Purging the ghost plague is part of Qiangliang's and my duty.
I know that you really liked those movies … I must have really let you down, eh, kid?
… I won't lie. I was a little disappointed.
But it doesn't matter, C07 is still my favorite character, and that will never change.
Wait a moment, Qi Xing. Before you and the officers leave, Miss Liang and I need to confirm one last thing.
There's something in your testimony that's been eating at me. Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying that you're lying. The Vigil's interrogation experts confirmed that much.

But even you probably noticed—the sequence of events that led you to become the "Nightpiercer;" you stole the reel, and caused the incident in Chinatown, but your motives seem … inconsistent. I feel like I'm missing a piece to this puzzle.
It's almost like the memory gaps affecting Loggerhead. But your expertise in arcane skills surpasses hers. Perhaps you can recall something.
I'm sorry. I really don't remember …

I only recall how it all began. I got word that Reunion of the Three Swallows had found its way out of Foundation storage and into the black market. I even got into the secret auction for it through some intermediaries but, unfortunately, I didn't have the dough.
So I asked myself, who else out there could be as fixated on that reel as me? The answer to that was obvious.
That's right. You're a public figure. Following you to Los Angeles wasn't difficult. I tracked down your intermediary, Pug Dog, and for a bit of cash, I got the time and location of your deal.
I see. So, the "friendly advice" Pug Dog gave me back then was about you. What a guy—zero professional ethics.
That night, my only objective was to take the reel from you. The question of who stole it from the Foundation wasn't something I even bothered to think about. But …
At the very last moment, a sliver of sense kicked in. It was a close call, but I managed to hold myself back. I think there was a moment when I really intended to kill that poor staffer, Miss Scott.
… But I don't understand why I felt that way. You know the rest.
The player that placed us here …

Although I don't usually keep a journal, I had to record today's encounter—I met the great Miss Matilda Bouanich!

I still remember that summer. My mother lectured me for an hour before we left and then another hour during our journey. I thought I was following her instructions perfectly: I was dressed perfectly neat; my greetings were memorized word-for-word. But the moment I met the Bouanichs, I froze solid, too nervous to say anything. Even adults can get stage fright, so how was it fair to give her own daughter the cold shoulder for it? A smile or a pat on the back from mother was all I needed to finish my greeting without fumbling.

Thank goodness for Lady Beryl. She saw what happened, and her gracious words salvaged the situation. I didn't disappoint my mother after that. I'm sure of it because the rest of my memories of that visit were pleasant—Lady Beryl's warm smile and Matilda's energetic chatter. Matilda could be as noisy as she liked and still win her mother's approval, how I envied that so much.

But Lady Beryl … for some reason, I can't remember what she looked like. Now I understand Latham's frustration. Being Matilda's mother, I could imagine a matured, refined version of Matilda—minus the childish energy and, oh right, without the hooked nose, that's my mother's trait.

This letter was tucked inside a folder of interrogation records, it appears to have been exchanged silently between two Vigiles agents during an interrogation. The two distinct handwritings reflect their unspoken dialogue:

"She's tight-lipped about it."

"But she seems unaware that we've already figured out everything."

"Fascinating, like a mouse in a lab experiment—arrogant yet clueless."

"There's still one thing left to figure out: how exactly did she learn to crack the anti-theft arcane seal?"

"All her lies and disguises fall apart under scrutiny, but she hasn't given up a single clue about this. Even our artificial somnambulism couldn't uncover anything …"

"Could it just be sheer dumb luck?"

"Disappointing. I've taught you better—never rely on million-to-one coincidences. Always consider the more plausible scenario."

"You mean … she's being controlled by someone else? And they've erased her memory, so she can't betray them?"

"Exactly. That slippery merchant gave up Scott, but there's no way a minor employee could pull off something like this. Rejoice, we've hooked a big fish."

"So … we're letting her go?"

"Yes, but not without loosening her strings first."

"Understood. I'll notify Mr. Pedra. I trust he'll ensure Miss Scott feels completely at ease after some … subtle adjustments."

"Good. You're a reliable assistant, Billy."

The second writer seemed about to reply but left only a hesitant pen stroke.

A groundbreaking communication device and a symbol of status during the early economic boom. A treasured birthday gift from a relative, it carried heartfelt greetings despite its bulky size. Today, the "brick phone" serves as a unique sanctuary for a special companion, accessible only by its owner.

Crafted from tireless dedication, unwavering discipline, and a deep belief in justice, this uniform symbolizes the wearer's commitment.
"My actions must never betray the honor of the Vigiles." Though spoken softly, these words resonate with conviction.

A totem, a responsibility, and a legacy. When thunder roared, this mask was passed to its young inheritor, fulfilling the ancestral wishes of countless generations. The wearer diligently maintains the mask three times a week, keeping it pristine and free from dust.

On the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month, under the turning stars at year's end, a ritual must be performed to banish plague spirits, ensuring the renewal of life. Officials gathered in the palace, guards lined the stairs, and peasants, merchants, and craftsmen presented offerings. Even passing sages paused in reverence.

"Let Zhenzi prepare. Commence the banishment."

The eunuch recited incantations, and the Zhenzi responded in unison. Under watchful eyes, the Fangxiangshi brandished shield and spear, performing a solemn dance to summon the Xiandao Beast and dispel all evil spirits. 

This year, however, something was different. Though the chief minister declared the ceremony complete, the Xiandao Beast lingered. The Fangxiangshi, clad in black and red robes, now bore white hair and furrowed brows.

The beasts growled lowly by his side as he spoke: "The lineage of the Fangxiangshi ends with me. You must carry on the duty."

The Zhenzi exchanged astonished glances, realizing their leader had entrusted them with the mantle.

Qiangliang let out a low growl. On this day, the chief minister and each of the Zhenzi took on a new surname, pledging to defend the people in the name of their respective Xiandao Beast.

A pair of exquisitely crafted wooden puppets, inherited from the interviewee's father. Under their master's control, they are dedicated actors and obedient assistants. They are also the reason for the interviewee's frequent appearances in tabloid rumors.
"They've been 'working with me' for years," the interviewee joked, "but there's no contract term, and their salary isn't guaranteed."

A budget-friendly padded shoulder coat chosen unexpectedly by the interviewee. Despite its affordability, the structured design and prominent shoulder pads remain an iconic Hong Kong style.
"This coat is practical. Look, with these shoulder pads, Aa Sing can sit on my shoulders comfortably," the interviewee explained.

A modified tungsten spotlight mounted on the interviewee's wheelchair, enabling the director to light a scene and shoot at any moment.
According to the interviewee, its most practical use is illuminating dark paths at night.

A New Wave!

In the 1970s, Hong Kong drew nourishment from a booming economy. Meanwhile, the term "New Wave" was no longer novel in Paris but became a rallying cry for inspiration on this distant shore.

No one knows exactly how this movement started. While the streets buzzed with the influence of Shaw Brothers' dramatic, operatic martial arts films, a new generation of creators began to focus on a different side of the city. Lugging heavy 16mm film cameras through neon-lit streets, they captured gritty yet striking imagery.

They wanted more people to see their films! They yearned for bolder content on the silver screen! Their passion fueled their creativity, blending violence, folklore, and arcanum into stories filled with romance, absurdity, and tragedy. Their works captured the clash between people and their times, leaving an enduring cultural legacy.

Amid this wave, the film Muddle emerged, marking a significant milestone for its creator.

Detective C07 Shatters Box Office Records! The holiday movie season has ended, with Detective C07 dominating the cinemas with its thrilling fights and comedic moments. This outcome was a forgone conclusion for the C07 series, but the film's ending has sparked heated debates. It's reported that lead actress Qi Xing is scheduled to appear at the upcoming film festival in a week, sharing behind-the-scenes stories with her fans. —Silver Screen New Weekly: Lunar New Year Edition Hero Films Without Heroes By Anonymous Years ago, when C07 first premiered, we were thrilled to see that heroes didn't have to be glorified, untouchable elites. Heroes could also be cheeky and humorous, like a friend who loves to show off. But as the series continued, with larger budgets and grander productions, its original spirit seemed to fade away. Watching the latest installment of Detective C07, all I felt was disappointment. Is this still the Detective C07 that championed justice? Is this still the same filmmaker who gave us Muddle? —World Film Review New Art Trio's Midnight Clash: What's Keeping Ms. He Pleading? Late last night, reports surfaced of a heated argument at the home of New Art Company screenwriter He Rijun. At around 2 a.m., cameras captured Ms. Noire and Ms. Qi Xing leaving together, their expressions suggesting the disagreement was far from resolved. By 8 a.m., Ms. Qi Xing announced she would not attend next week's film festival. Following this, director Noire declared that there would be no further installments for Detective C07. Though no official explanation was given, the incident undoubtedly signals a major shift for New Art Company. Stay tuned for updates. —Harbor Daily

Sticky notes filled with to-do lists, pinned alongside a Foundation badge on the interviewee's chest.
Film cannot capture every corner of memory, but the marks left by handwriting embody the wisdom of someone battling amnesia for years.

Film rolls specially modified by Laplace, significantly differing in material, color, and weight from standard ones. These rolls are vital for the interviewee to form their daily memories and maintain a sense of identity.
The specific technology Laplace used to achieve this function has been buried within the vast "memories" of the interviewee. After searching fruitlessly for an hour, they declared it to be classified.

A durable crossbody bag used by the interviewee to store her "memory rolls," charging cables, and other essentials. Evident signs of wear suggest it has endured countless challenges. The interviewee remarked that anyone who can carry this bag might consider entering a weightlifting championship.

In the 1820s, people discovered the phenomenon of persistence of vision, making horses endlessly gallop on spinning strips of narrow paper.

In the 1870s, twelve cameras were aligned to capture exposure in one-thousandth of a second, stitching photographs into moving images.

By the 1880s, numerous inventors using varying methods but identical ingenuity created the tools of cinema. Paper reels, mirrors, lamps, hand-drawn frames at sixteen per second, and supple celluloid film … Audiences handed over their nickels in exchange for comedic tales told through fragmented scenes.

Inventions continued. Twenty-second clips became three-minute shorts, and shorts turned into longer films. What came next? Athletes, trains, dogs, or the sea? Eager eyes watched intently, unaware that a small piece inside the projector had awakened.

Gears pulled perforations, and film glided smoothly through her body, narrating an endless silver-screen world. Alongside the people ahead of the projector, she too marveled and anticipated each frame and every scene.

Brewing Coffee: A sudden warmth, a daze, an urge to sing. That feeling is surprisingly similar in humans. "Daily Meal": Fullness, increasing fullness, dizziness, countless small boxes, white noise, clinking sounds. This stomach is too small; one packet is never enough for most people. Soup Dumplings:Steam almost instantly fogs up the lens! The whole meal is spent wiping it off. Did you manage to eat them in the end? 35mm Special Film: Sour, astringent, a friction-like texture, the salty taste of silver halide, like the instant you open a tin can. Next time, try a horror movie and let me know what it tastes like. Keychain: Cold, sweet metallic taste—not as sweet as lead sugar, lively and dense collisions, mixed with a hint of rust. So you swallowed the keychain and then went looking for it everywhere?! Cheeseburger: Sticky, noisy, energizing, dizzying. This is one of the best items on the Foundation's cafeteria menu! If you don't like it, give it to me! Foundation ID Card: A serious voice, information, a plastic taste similar to film, layers of secrets. That matches my expectations. Sidebar Note: This must be Scott secretly writing in my notebook. Sidebar Note: How different can a cheeseburger and soup dumplings really taste? I need to ask her next time we meet.

Pandora Wilson: Hello, Ms. Loggerhead. Loggerhead: Hello! Sorry, I don't remember your name. If you'd like, just hang tight while I project my memory reel from the past three days ... Pandora Wilson: No worries, this is our first meeting. Pandora Wilson: As an awakened born within a projector, you must have witnessed countless great films. What are your favorite ones? Loggerhead: Oh, it would definitely be a black-and-white silent film! The texture of silent reels has a unique charm, always taking me back to the "Silver Screen Era"—everything was new, vibrant, and every new work was a groundbreaking marvel! Pandora Wilson: You just mimicked one of Chaplin's classic gestures. Loggerhead: Absolutely, he's my favorite actor and director! Modern Times, City Lights ... The marks of an era, the dignity of the little people, all captured in exaggerated comedic conflicts. Oh, I wish I could compete in a Chaplin impersonation contest! - 30 minutes later - Loggerhead: Oh no! This note says there was an interview scheduled for 10:20, and I'm already half an hour late. I have to go ... Pandora Wilson: Doesn't your note mention your interviewer's name? Loggerhead: No, that's stored in a memory reel I didn't retrieve. Pandora Wilson: ... I'm your interviewer.

The frame is made of slender bamboo ribs and decorated with peonies and orchids. Draped in silk and illustrated with scenes of the four seasons, it is designed to be carried on the shoulder.
After the shoot, the interviewee made a request: "May I take this lantern back with me? If it's hung under the tavern's eaves, I'm sure it will brighten the day of every customer who sees it."

Gold threads run through jade beads, hammered into an accessory for a goddess in a painting, imbued in order to warm the shoulder and neck. When asked about the ruby's origin, the interviewee removed it for closer inspection—it turned out to be just a drop of red paint caught by her wooden puppets.

A chased copper ewer with a slender neck and circular base, gilded all over, reserved for entertaining esteemed guests during festivals. The interviewee often shares drinks with visitors until dawn, waking up as if from a dream.
As for what they see in their dreams, accounts differ, but all claim they've wandered into a painted scroll.

The fan bears embroidered intertwining branches, with tinkling tassels that shield against the sun, wind, and dust, while concealing many secrets. Frequently used as a token of love, the fan's giver and recipient remain known only to a matchmaker who ties their names to a red thread.

A gold lock adorned with pearls and red string knots, said to bind two hearts together, ensuring they never part. The interviewee accepts all requests, and a glimpse reveals countless names etched densely on the back—even the names of a pair of Critters.

A thin and flexible red thread symbolizing all the connections and ties in the world. The interviewee uses it for a kind of string game, weaving intricate patterns between her fingers.
She kindly asked if we'd like to learn this ancient game, but for the sake of our readers' love lives, we politely declined.

Hair styled like clouds, adorned with an awe-inspiring lotus, though the coiled silver snake deters many from starting a conversation.
When asked why the lotus throne hides a transforming snake, the interviewee smiled and whispered, "Hush, don't tell—it's something you shouldn't have seen."
Jade and silver beads form a shimmering web that sways with every step and passing breeze. It gathers the worldly loves and hates of each believer, as well as their briefest glimpses of fear.

A jade-green vial brimming with life, with lush willow branches and nectar sweet as honey. "Why mind the trivial details of appearances? For now, just savor its sweetness," the interviewee urged. "Come, don't be afraid, it's well-behaved."

A wing-shaped headpiece crafted from feathers, thorns, and wrought iron, adorned with neatly arranged raven feathers, glowing in deep blue and purple hues. Alongside her cherished staff, it will witness prosperity returning to the forest.

A black wooden staff spiraling upward with hawthorn thorns entwined around it.
Legend has it these thorns were prepared for an ancient full moon ritual. Offering it true devotion could earn nature's blessing—though only the interviewee knows if this is true.

Crows perch on thorny branches, neither arriving nor leaving.
"What do their hoarse voices foretell?"
When asked, the interviewee merely smiled without answering.

A seemingly ordinary bamboo scroll that has accompanied the interviewee through countless days and nights. Within it, she records her experiences; both simple and complex; light and weighty alongside the fleeting emotions etched during its carving.
Ruyi Scepter of the Green Moon

"I've wandered through magnificent mountains and rivers, growing accustomed to the cycle of seasons. What remains unchanged is the eternal moon above and the jade-carved object in my hand," the interviewee remarked.

A veiled hat imbued with moonlight.
At night, the interviewee lifts the thin veil to admire the moon shattered in rippling river water.
"It's here, and that's all the perfection I need."

A shadow puppet shaped like a lantern, crafted entirely by the interviewee—from material selection and coloring to assembly and calibration. Its intricate surface and harmonious colors reveal her meticulousness, patience, and passion for drama.

No one knows what the interviewee's purse contains.
"The world is filled with countless stages, each performing countless dramas. Surely, you can see this purse couldn't possibly hold all the stories I've seen."

"What did you see, what did you hear? Here lies a play crafted just for you, and as long as you're here, the curtain will never fall."
The interviewee always wears a mask, regardless of the genre of the play, yet he understands better than anyone how the drama will end.

The Teller Machine - Bright as Day
Any protagonists eager to see the parade should find a good spot early!
As the lights begin to shine, the year's mysteries will be revealed within.
"These mystical creatures from the Far East are masters of transformation and bring fortune to those they meet."
Rumor has it this landmark's design was inspired by a Critter that starred in a famous festive film.
The moment it was raised, the neighborhood's spirit found its form.
"People need dreams, here is where we build them."
Never napping, never slacking, forever watchful.
One rises, one sinks, but nothing can stop their inevitable reunion. Before scooping it up, be mindful of the filling inside.
Through the cold winter, a warm yet harmless fire blooms atop the trees.
Raise the oars, climb the mast, higher and higher—do you see it? The dream left adrift upon the sea.
The wind, intent on its course and destination, unwittingly set the millstone into motion.
The branches stretch to catch the golden rays of the May sun. Pick up your flower basket and don't forget the steps. It's time to celebrate.
During the Dushuo Festival shopping rush, few leave this place empty-handed.
Wherever wanderers go, the scent of tangerines, roasted delicacies, and saltpeter follows.
The brightest stars of the century all find a place here.
"I saw it with my own eyes. They use their feet to push off one another, and then just like that, they can fly!"
It's said that, occasionally, arcane creatures of myth blend into the festivities, enjoying the celebration alongside the crowd.
Under the mighty pines of the West Coast, lanterns and candles mark the beginning of a new year.
Wherever we are in the sphere, we revel in the same festive cheer.

"I try to treat everyone in the Wilderness with kindness, and they return that kindness back in equal measure. It's a pleasant feeling. But I later realized—the more I treated them well, the less I had on me, whether it was food, dust, or even my Sharpodonty.
But it doesn't matter. I have so much, far too much. I don't mind at all."
Some prefer to wander alone through the Wilderness. That's fine—after all, there aren't any man-eating Critters here. At least, not yet.
"Somewhere in the Wilderness, there must be others—humans or Critters—who know the feeling of solitude."

"Studies show that as long as there's a habitable forest environment for them, Splintercats can migrate to it, crossing oceans like passing tempests, heading straight for their destination. This explains their widespread presence even in the most remote corners of the world."
"If you're out of ideas, try seeking inspiration from Abang Akus. Its ability to transform might just surprise you."

"Moon-Eyed Fiddlers shed their old shells at specific intervals. You can make all kinds of crafts with their shells, or stir-fry them with sea salt as a crunchy delicacy, you can even wear them as masks if you're going to a masquerade."
A children's picture book, covered in crayon scribbles, was left forgotten in a corner of the Wilderness. Inside are dozens of illustrations of NewBabel Center's Critters and exactly 127 blank pages.
"Please don't gossip with Dodoughs. They'll get so caught up in the chitchat that they can dehydrate and collapse from exhaustion. It puts a huge strain on our critter health management system."
"Carbuncles learn to communicate with other critters by mimicking and adapting. They have an impressive aptitude for social learning—despite seeming a little clueless."

"As tea parties become more frequent, reports suggest that Refined Groupbuncles and Dodoughs are socializing more. People have witnessed them mimicking human behavior—greeting each other, serving drinks and even exchanging business cards."

"If you're destined to be different, you'll need to find a new way of life—and a critter companion like no other."
—Excerpt from Ms. NewBabel's Critter Rehabilitation Center Official Brochure
The Curious Wilderness and Its Mischievous Children—Written by children who love critters.
Tripod birds? With bodies like that, I can already imagine how hilariously awkward they must look when they walk.
… No, no. What if they're unexpectedly agile? What if they're masters of gymnastics—doing handstands and spinning moves? Never mind, I don't care.
… Why are you looking at me like that? I'm not going to demonstrate it for you. Go bother someone else.
Dodoughs wear suits. But why suits? Are they going to a tea party? Would they take me along?
How do Furry Anglerfish walk on land? Do they have legs? What do they eat?
Can Moon-Eyed Fiddlers laugh? Do they cry? Can I make funny faces at them?
I want to say hello to every critter here. Can I stay? I won't be a bother—I'll find a job.
A Splintercat! I heard they're full of energy, sometimes headbutting trees and even causing lightning strikes. But now that I see one up close … they're pretty cute.
Huh? It's spinning in circles, purring like thunder … I think it's about to summon a storm. You'd better run.
Me? Don't worry. Compared to a real ocean storm, this little squall is nothing, just another instrument in a symphony of sounds. In fact, I think I might incorporate it into my next melody.
A Moon-Eyed Fiddler, this one really does look like a face doesn't it? I never expected to see one here ...
No, the Nukutai are quite familiar with them. Back on the island, we would use them to predict changes in the tides.
I'm not quite as good an artist as my elders, but I can weave you a trinket from its shell.
Consider it a thank-you gift for letting me stay.
Hey! I'm training for a run. Wanna join me?
Oh, I'm not running alone—I'm racing against … huh? Where's Pinnacle Grouse? It was just beside me!
Haha, it's too fast! One blink, and it's gone!
One day, I'll catch up. And when I do, I'll be able to punch as fast as it moves!
Hello, you look interesting—like a dancing snake I once saw in a dream.
I heard you can change form freely, taking any shape and color. If we become friends, we could do so many things together.
You're like a kaleidoscope, or maybe a Rubik's Cube. I want to see more of your transformations!
I think letting Critters live in the Wilderness is a great idea—it's great for scout training.
But keep an eye on those Carbuncles. They learn fast, and I worry they might cause trouble.
Here's a little secret—the LSCC actually keeps a few Carbuncles for research. One time, they broke out and busted up an entire lab, and we got an unexpected holiday …
This … this is classified information! Please keep it secret, okay?
This guest … ah, no, haha … It's just dressed like a tea house patron, so I instinctively—
But since we have the chance, let's host a tea party! I just happen to have a poetry book a guest gave me.
"Cherry blossoms at dusk, from now on, fade into the past."
Hmm … it doesn't seem very interested. Did I read it wrong?
Tripodero is said to be a great hunter. Hmm … I don't know about the open plains, but in the rainforest, they wouldn't stand a chance.
You see, the jungle is dense with foliage and teeming with creatures.
Being a good shot isn't enough. You have to use your every sense and skill in the jungle to be successful.
Luck plays a part too … Nevermind, I don't really want to think too much about it.
You're inviting me for afternoon tea? Haha, I'd be delighted. It's an honor. Let me check my pockets for something fitting for the occasion …
Alas, all I have today is this rather crude pistol. My apologies for the lack of decorum.
Oh, don't worry—it's only for … unusual situations. Fortunately, today isn't one of those days, haha.
Oh, little Furry Anglerfish, do you like my little conch?
The fuzzy ball on your head glows, and my conch glows too … under the right conditions.
I guess that makes you two alike—but that doesn't mean you can hide it in your fur, understood?
Aloha! Hello, Axe-handle Hound! Out for a stroll?
Whoa! Why are you gnawing on my bow?! That's not okay!
I heard Axe-handle Hounds don't like the taste of red oak. I guess I need a red oak bow!
Hey! My dear Teakettler! It's so great to see you!
What? You're thirsty? Alright, let's find some water …
Oh no! You can't milk it! Even if you could, it wouldn't be enough for you!
And besides—it's not a cow … Yeah, it's not a cow! Its name is DUU-DUU-BELL-BOO!
Hey, what are you staring at? You want something from me?
I get it—you want to play with Maleficent and Tonika, right?
How about we make that bowtie-wearing APPLe the target? First one to knock him down wins! Haha!
Mr. Dodough, are you also interested in this History of Critters?
I'll turn up the lantern so you can see better.
No, no … It's best to stay quiet while reading, no more of that "Doo-doo" sound, okay? …
Huh?! Stop! Books are not for eating!
The sounds of the Wilderness are often hard to catch, but radio waves are everywhere.
Is it a malfunction? Or is there a stronger signal causing interference? I don't understand.
… Forget it. Take it easy. The other side of the monitor isn't picking up anything. This rare moment of silence is worth appreciating.
Maybe tonight I'll finally get a good night's sleep.
Another Wilderness patrol is complete, ma'am. Awaiting your orders!
Ms. An-an Lee seems to always call you that. Would you prefer we called you sir?
Or maybe Captain, Team Leader, Commander, Boss?
Accidents happen. Daily precautions are essential, ma'am.
I just saw a kid trying to jump off a five-story tower, claiming he could fly.
Luckily I was there, or it would've been a tragedy.
This place is amazing, don't you think?
Spacious, quiet, with fancy backdrops, and you can even adjust the lighting and weather on command. Do you think I could use the space for a few days to shoot a film?
Oh wow, you're really generous! I'll make sure to save you a front-row seat for the premiere.
No, I want you to guest star in it—as the guardian deity of this place.
You've got a point. I had so many ideas, but so often they vanish before they go anywhere.
I've never had access to such a fantastic location before. My reputation must be growing.
Maybe you could help round up a few more actors, then all we need is a good script and we could produce a blockbuster here that would put Hollywood to shame.
W-What's going on? Who are you? Where am I?
Vertin? Timekeeper? I remember. Say, could you please prepare a warm, dry, spacious room for me?
Don't worry, my memory of meeting you for the first time has been stored in the safest place I can think of.
You know, it's nice to be able to forget certain emotional moments, just so I can experience them again. I guess that's one of the few perks of forgetfulness!
Hmm, I see. But isn't the scenery changing a bit too quickly around here?
Look at this, it's only been a few days, and the scenery doesn't match what's in my reels at all. Why is that?
Ma'am, there's a call for you.
Yes, it's from Qiangliang. It specifically asked for you.
It says thank you for your care during this time.
You want me to relay messages in the future? But Qiangliang prefers to tell you directly.
Basically, it means "Thanks for looking out for me lately" …
Hmm ... If I'm being honest, what you've been through could be made into a great film.
Oh, no, I don't plan on putting you on the big screen. Your story is already complete as it is. Adding unnecessary details would ruin it, and I don't do documentaries.
Besides, your story isn't over yet … Have you thought about how it should end?
A happy ending is great, I love happy endings.
You don't seem convinced? Oh, come on, trust me. I really do want every character to have their own happy ending.
But writing a great happy ending can be even harder than writing a tragedy, so I'm still working on it.
An open ending sparks the most discussion.
Hollywood doesn't like that style, though. They insist that every story must have a clear and definite conclusion.
But I think if the journey is exciting enough, the story doesn't need an ending to define it.
You're standing right in front of the camera! How about striking a pose?
We're filming a talkie. You can speak, Timekeeper.
It'll be fine! We can just dub over the audio in post to match the movements of your mouth.
Actually, the folks at the Foundation and the LSCC love doing this. Sometimes they ask me for silent footage of our superiors so they can dub over it.
As for what they say … I forgot! Completely and utterly forgot! Really!
I think so! After all, the camera is my eyes, and the film is my brain—the only difference is my "brain" can be shared with others.
So as long as I respect personal privacy, I wouldn't say it's a violation really.
And actually, I have an advantage over regular people in this!
Because the moment I take out the film like this … all the secrets I've seen are erased from my memory!
A perfect success requires thousands of careful rehearsals. Don't stop now.
Based on my calculations, we have met our expectations. We did it.
You never know whether a small action now might lead to unexpected results in the future. Keep smiling.
Hmm—clearly, you're much smarter than a frog. Do you want to be the next prince?
The desolate wilderness is no different from a silent forest. We should listen together to the wind passing through.
Shhh—keep it quiet. Revealing secrets always leads to trouble.
Essence stands above all else. Your existence is a testament to that fundamental truth.
Some Critters are both wise and powerful. Yes, I do believe that's true.
I'm glad you've changed. But no matter how much you change, you'll always be yourself.
Not bad, I like it! Keep going.
Now's the moment—raise your hands and make some noise!
Would you like to see my crucible performance too?
If my eyes aren't mistaken, you're becoming more and more refined, more and more radiant.
Best not to wish for too much, my friends.
Yes, you can collect these, just like how I collect badges.
Aloha! I'd love to learn more of your language!
Relax, they don't mean any harm. Just make sure they don't bite too hard.
Are you going to dance along with DUU-DUU-BELL-BOO too?
You don't need to call me ma'am.
It's safe here, no need for patrols.
What kind of film are you shooting?
Can you take it for me?

Again and again ... you don't know when to quit, do you? Just like me when I was young.
I wasn't wrong about you, after all.
All our countless choices have led up to this moment.
But not all of those choices were made willingly. No, some of us had no choice but to fight over scraps in the dark corners of society.
This time though, it is my choice, my own will. And I'm fortunate to have you playing opposite me.
I can see it in your eyes—you're not playing the role of a hero or an officer; you're yourself and nothing less.
What about you? Is playing the role of a murderous villain really what you want?
The answer to that is yours to find out, little Vigil.
A word of warning: don't leave your friends stranded. Their lives are in your hands.
Only fools rush in, little Vigil.
Oh, it seems you know how to take care of your friends.
Get the camera rolling, Noire. At last, I'll get the ending I always wanted.
Looks like there's no stopping you.
In that case, I'll make you stop!
You've left your friend stranded. Heh, now their strength is mine.
Oh, another addition to my collection. Soon, you'll all be tucked away in my film reel.
What a pity, little Vigil. You gave a poor performance.
It seems I expected too much from you.
Stop this futile resistance and face reality ... No matter how hard you try, you can't change the past!
No, little Vigil. This isn't my curtain call ... not yet.
Oh no, *cough cough* … Officer, this thick fog is making my head spin! It reeks from those stinky, clumsy oafs!
Damn it, they've all scurried behind those crates! Well, go ahead, what are you waiting for?!
Don't listen to this lunatic, officer! If it weren't for her "little devil" constantly provoking my children, they'd never have stepped into her filthy yard!
Alright, alright! Sir, ma'am … Please, stop arguing!
Step aside a little … I'll give you both a satisfactory answer.
I need to move those crates first … Otherwise, these Munchalos will just keep circling around them.
There was something I read in the "NewBabel Critter Training Guide"—Munchalos become extremely drowsy after intense activity. Looks like it's time to put that to the test …
Alright, sir, please bring your pets and come with us. The police station will handle further processing as needed.
Oh … My sweet babies! Daddy's taking you home right now!
Something … is coming out of his body?! Watch yourself, rookie!
What is that …? It seems to be some kind of ... non-corporeal specter?
No, that's not right … I don't sense any ghostly aura around them.
According to Eastern records, they're entities that bring calamity, disease, and malevolent curses … But this time, astonishingly, these Ghost Plagues have taken on human form.
… I don't know why yet, but something must have triggered their transformation.
My duty, alongside Qiangliang, has always been to drive out these Ghost Plagues. It's time to put an end to this disturbance!
Waaaah! Why are you chasing me?! The hamster's over that way!
I need you to cooperate! Stop right there!
Oh …! Officer, watch out! Don't run through the corridor like that, you almost knocked me over!
Whew, I need to be more careful … Keep my arms and legs in check, avoid hitting civilians, and stay clear of all this equipment.
Uh … is something the matter, officers?
You seem to have overheard our conversation. Was there anything in it you might know about?
We welcome any leads you might have, and even offer a reward for helping solve the case!
No, no … I-I didn't hear anything. This is all happening so suddenly. I have urgent business to attend to. Please understand, officers …
There's no need to worry, ma'am. You seem a bit flustered. Here, why don't you come sit down, and we'll have a nice chat?
Yes, I'm sure there's a way we can be of help to each other.
What are you doing in my room?! This is a serious ... um … criminal offense!
Get out of my room, or I'm calling the police! The phone—it's right here in my hand!
No need for that. I am the police.
W-What?! You—you're that Vigil from the hospital!
I was sure I had shaken off <size=30>this <size=25>person …</size>
Umm ... So what do you want with me?
I think you already know the answer to that.
Listen up! In the first scene, you're a martial arts apprentice in Chinatown, cornered in an alley by a group of thugs.
You're an outsider here, trying to avoid trouble, so all you can do is curl up and take the beating.
Eat this! Don't you know what "hand over the money" means?! You wanna suffer?
Hey, stick to the script, Vigil! I'm only giving you one warning!
Get off my set! You're not welcome here!
Good, good … Second scene. You've had enough. You're humiliated and furious, ready to fight back.
Get it together. No more looking weak—show me your anger.
Now, you get up from the ground, not to prove yourself, but to tell them that whatever you've lost, you're taking it back!
What are you afraid of?! She's just a crippled runt.
Don't bite off more than you can chew!
But how ... She doesn't have the reel anymore, how can she still summon these monsters?
She's been deeply corrupted … The Ghost Plagues have latched onto her. She didn't summon them—they were always lurking within her.
Get away! Stay back! This isn't over!
I haven't made her acknowledge me … I still have a plan, I still … still …
Her mind is starting to unravel already … Poitier, we have to take her down now!
Good ... very good. I've been waiting for this moment.
The time has come for you to uphold your duty, Miss Vigil.
I won't hold back, Ms. Qí Xīng.
No, wait … Don't let your guard down, kid! She's not down yet!
What ...!? This power, it doesn't look like it's hers …
I didn't bring any tissues, princess. So if you start crying, you'll have to wipe your nose on your new uniform.
Alright, let's see if I'm up against a powerless little girl, or a real challenger.
I will go easy on you.
Oh, alright, stop, stop! We … or at least I acknowledge you now!
Good. Looks like she wasn't just all talk.
Sorry, I did my best to restrain myself ...
Phew ... If this had kept up, we'd have been exhausted before the real suspect even showed up.
Don't be afraid, child. Here, stand behind me.
Stay calm, everyone. This is just a new parade performance.
I can feel it … The source of these "malevolent spirits" is nearby.
Tsk. Not you two again. What do you want? Get lost!
Hah, you really think … we were just waiting around for you to save us?
Enough talk, Tony. Chen won't be able to hold them off for long. The effect will wear off soon.
Hah, don't worry about it … After he's dead, we can make up whatever story we want.
Tsk … Chen, quit wasting our time and hurry up!
I #*&$ will take back what's mine …
Chen is like a rabid dog … He's out of control! We need to fall back!
Sifu, you look much better as a human …
Sorry, but this is the last time.

Higher, better than life itself.

Then she said: Cut—

"See? I told you your stupid plan would get us all killed."

"I don't recall you ever voicing a single objection to my meticulous plan. If I'd known you were such a coward, I would've left you to drown in the nonsense those lunatics call literature—until your brain burned to a crisp!"

"At least that way, I wouldn't freeze or starve to death, you pathetic fool."

"Oh? So you'd rather rot in that cold cell, waiting for them to toss you some suspicious pills just to survive? I'd rather take my chances!"

"Whatever. It's useless anyway. No one escapes this cage. In the end, we'll all die here ..."

Comala, originally a local sanatorium, was built in the early 20th century in Ushuaia, Tierra del Fuego. In the 1970s, the facility underwent a comprehensive transformation, incorporating advanced European concepts brought by the National Foucault Studies Association.

Today, Comala features a groundbreaking panoramic architectural design that allows inmates to see across the entire facility from their individual wards. Though referred to as inmates, they are largely free to engage in various forms of entertainment within shared spaces. The facility's staff places complete trust in their self-discipline, choosing not to intervene in any of their personal interactions or even organized gatherings.

To ensure comprehensive security, a central watchtower was constructed to provide surveillance and protection while reducing the psychological burden of constant observation on patients.

Every inmate is guaranteed the best possible treatment, with the goal of full recovery and reintegration into society—just as Comala promised.

I am overwhelmed with anguish, and neither sorrow nor fear can ease this pain, even for a moment.

That day, the National Foucault Studies Association and the masked ones came to my door and sought my wisdom. The former brought forth a concept, attempting to research its feasibility, while the latter presented a parable, revealing something of the past and the future.

I searched tirelessly for an ultimate answer but to no avail. I memorized the colors of every pigment yet failed to paint the landscape. I felt lost and stuck. They called me by the wrong name, and I could not discern their true desires.

You are me, but not entirely. Now, I am about to perish, as an incomplete illusion.

<i>Yes, I am in paradise. My heart races, unable to speak.
It feels as though I am finally reaching my true happiness,
Just as we reunite and dance together.<i>

I've never watched a full film. The loving couples in films are like angels in a poem, stirring my heart with longing. That night, sleep eluded me, and I kept the lights on.

A mouse ran in. It wasn't afraid of me, but I feared it might chew up my poems I'd written on the scrap notes.

I threw some crumbs on the floor. The little creature crept over, picked up the pieces, and began to nibble. I reached out my hand, and it slipped through the door crack, vanishing from sight.

It probably went back to its cigar box.

"I sell dice. Interested?" Asked the street vendor.

I indifferently replied, "I've got plenty of dice in these filthy pockets of mine. Every night, I use them to win a few mugs of ale at the tavern to keep me warm. My point is, I'm not exactly short on dice."

The vendor paused for a moment, then leaned in. "I don't just sell ordinary dice. I bet you've never seen one with twenty faces." She pulled out a beautifully crafted die made of hard paper, with thirty neatly aligned edges.

"Try it," the vendor said, handing it to me, as if offering a random stone she'd picked up by the roadside.

I casually rolled the die. The first roll landed with 6 on top. The second roll was 13, the third was 4, the fourth was 17, and the fifth again was 6 ...

I had rolled it far more times than there were faces, yet still hadn't landed on every number. Frustrated, I emptied my pocket of all its coins and bought the die.

From then on, I rolled the twenty-sided die every day, hardly ever leaving my house. The tavern had long since removed me from their regulars list, yet I still never landed on every number.

It should have been a miracle, but instead, it became a cage that made me lose my way.

A new friend has arrived at home, and everyone's too busy to help …

Fixing up the temple, setting off firecrackers, making calls … I'm busy too, because I'm the "inheritor" and need to bond with our "new friend," Qiangliang. No one has time to guide me. According to Mom, I have to figure it out on my own. I guess it's because they don't dare to talk to Qiangliang—but I do. It'll be fine, I'll manage somehow.

I know how to entertain a new friend. It's not hard. I remember everything Mom and Dad did when they had guests. First, hospitality means serving tea! I made tea, prepared a fruit platter, and even brought out my precious crispy noodles and burger candy… Sure enough, Qiangliang was very interested in the crispy noodles!

It looked at me, and the little snake on its tail looked at me too. It must have never eaten this before. I showed it how—crushing the noodles in the bag, sprinkling the seasoning, and pouring them onto a plate. I also shared my favorite way of eating them: a bite of noodles, a bite of candy, salty and spicy followed by sour and sweet, all the flavors mixed together!

But in the end, the crispy noodles were wasted. Qiangliang blew the crushed noodles everywhere. Luckily, I cleaned up the house before Mom and Dad got back. Next time, I need to prepare a deeper bowl!
Today, I played a really fun game with Qiangliang …

I've always wanted to play hopscotch with my classmates, but I've always had to hurry home to practice my arcane skills. Now that I have Qiangliang, I don't have to play alone! As soon as Mom and Dad left, I invited Qiangliang, and it didn't turn me down.

Qiangliang is really big, so I had to draw the squares even bigger. It took four whole pieces of chalk. There were lots of old roof tiles near the temple waiting to be replaced, so I picked up a bunch of sturdy ones. That way, even if Qiangliang accidentally stepped on them, we wouldn't run out.

I showed it the rules—hop on one foot, hop again, then both feet … Jump to eight and back. The squares were huge—I jumped as hard as I could, but I still kept stepping on the lines. Looks like I need more practice if I want to play with Qiangliang. It couldn't recite the chant either, so I promised to chant for it when it jumped. Friends should help each other.

When it was Qiangliang's turn, I threw the tile for it, but when it landed, the thud was so powerful it shook the ground! Good thing I found a quiet spot—otherwise, we would have been caught.

But the biggest problem was that Qiangliang never learned how to hop on one foot! I tried teaching it again and again, but it just tilted its head and stared at me. In the end, I had the little snake on its tail throw the tile for me instead. It seemed to enjoy that, so it looks like this will be our own version of the game.
Dad has me doing some new training. It's not as exhausting as before, but I keep failing …

My coordination with Qiangliang is not going well, but it's not its fault. I should've realized that Qiangliang can't speak or even read.

That won't stop me. Whenever Grandpa took me fishing, I would draw while waiting for him to catch a fish. Grandpa would guess what I was drawing, and he'd always get it right. We can do the same. I'll draw out the actions so Qiangliang can remember them. That way, with just one signal, we'll be in sync.

I drew a little person and a big cat to represent us, showing that it's time to strike together! Then I drew a fist to signal that we need to get ready, an outstretched index finger to mean we're attacking, and an open palm to mean stop. After practicing the signals for a while, Qiangliang understood it! This method is perfect, and we'll definitely get it right next time we practice.

……

……

……

Dad said Qiangliang and I can't rely only on gestures, that would be lazy … Gestures should be supplementary, and I need to communicate with Qiangliang without using words or movements at all. Dad always says I don't think things through enough, but how can I improve when I can barely sort out my own thoughts, let alone understand what Qiangliang's thinking ...
Dad said the temple is all fixed up, and we need to choose a good day to hold a ceremony …

This time is different from before, Dad said I have to host it. Now that Qiangliang is here, it's my responsibility. I've memorized the procedure, practiced the dance steps, and rehearsed my lines over and over again. But when Dad checked on me tonight, he said my expression wasn't firm enough, and my movements lacked strength.

There are still two days left—I can practice many more times, but I also have school and homework during the day … I can do this. Still, I feel so nervous …

If only I could be like Qiangliang. It always looks so mature. I don't fully understand what maturity means yet, but I think I must be like Qiangliang—silent, yet everyone knows it's powerful and capable of anything.

No one else knows how badly Qiangliang was injured before—that's why it slept for so long, until I woke it up …

Qiangliang is still waiting for me. By now, it could've gone back into the phone to rest, but it's staying here with me. I should stop writing and practice some more. If I mess up, everyone will be disappointed.

I'll recite the incantation one more time before I practice.
