"Come in, come in! Unless you'd rather freeze into an ice sculpture out there." He seems to mean well.
A dual-toned brushstroke, a hint of scarce yet precious vitality.
A blizzard is coming. The town is the only refuge. You'd best get there soon—or never leave at all.
The frozen sea no longer bears ships, and the snow-covered lighthouse stands an empty shell.
Roaring through endless white days, then falling silent in sleepless nights.
An unfamiliar world, capable of raising previously unexamined propositions and opening up new perspectives on the universe.
"Transcendentality" … or perhaps … this pursuit that exhausts all things …
It is everything in the universe, the sum of all inquiries. It is truth, an existence beyond words.
It … cannot be reached, cannot be touched.
Shadows in the mind, phantoms that linger day and night.
They argue endlessly, filling every corner of my mind with the chaos of reality.
They just won't let me stop and think …
Vertin, please, find me a job here!
Anything—cleaner, bookkeeper, critter breeder in a factory … even a deckhand!
Oh, and if it's paid daily, even better—I swear I'm not implying you'd delay my wages.
Hmm? Well, of course, writing doesn't exactly put food on the table, does it?
Otherwise, I'd starve to death before I even finished my novel, haha …
But don't worry about me. I'm used to this kind of life. I'll manage just fine!
You're trying to offer me a stable environment where I can write without worry, aren't you?
Indeed, as long as one lives, new and interesting things will always arise …
You never ask me questions, and you never waver.
You're always like this—no doubts, no hesitation, moving forward with absolute conviction.
What binds the prisoner, why the forest lies in shadow, who dwells beneath the mask …
No, these questions are meaningless. They are not yours to ask.
Only you may ask what's in your heart—I need not say a word.
Do you seek nothing? Is everything already meaningless to you?
No, you are not omniscient, but you accept your ignorance and pursue answers regardless.
That is why you are so different from everyone else. That … is good.
Perfect, Vertin. You came just in time!
I was just writing the opening scene of a character based on you. Your arrival is sure to inspire me even further!
"Vertin stood before me. With the entire Wilderness contained in this little suitcase, our meeting was bound to happen sooner or later. And so, the story began … "
Yes! This is exactly the scene I need!
… "Vertin brushed past me, walking toward the stone steps, passing through the pure white door, leaving the Wilderness behind. I had missed the perfect beginning."
The path of literature is always guided by eurekas and chances … Whatever the case, your arrival has given me new thoughts. Thank you, Vertin!
You don't need to do this.
This is exactly why I'm here.

I've adapted Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas into an entirely new tabletop RPG—no need to understand it fully, you and your companions in the suitcase can all join in. Wait, Vertin, why the grimace?
Remember, each player takes their turn in a clockwise fashion. If you wish to share secrets, you may pass notes to one another.

The first time I encountered tabletop games was at a poetry reading. The professor was reciting a long, tedious narrative poem when a friend, whose name I no longer remember, leaned over and asked, "What's your character's stats?"
No, Vertin. Don't talk to me right now ... it's your turn. Stay in character and focus!
Shall we continue the last game? Don't worry, I've saved our progress. We can call Joshua and Jennifer over and start anytime!
Give me the right number of tokens, please. But … are you sure you want to buy this now? Oh, nothing, it's totally up to you!
"The cowboy says to the coachman: 'If we follow those cattle, maybe we'll find the shadows we lost.' " So, what's your next move? Will you follow them?
We've been through this loop a few times now. Is there anything you'd like to describe? How exactly are you taking the item? What's going through your character's mind?

"The fog ahead thickens, and even the whistling can't help them orient themselves. In the distance, the vague outline of an ancient temple emerges." We've now arrived at Templo de la Metáfora. Stay quiet, and watch out for monsters and traps.

Clear goals, well-placed monsters and traps, scaling rewards, distinct character setups, and a rule system that allows for every possibility … I made sure that Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas was simple enough. So, what exactly makes it so hard to understand?
"The wind carries a whisper like an ancient poem through the fog." How do you plan to investigate that old stone platform?
Of course, I won't just tell you outright—it's all part of the metaphor. The clues are hidden in the previous lines. Think carefully …

"The old man's eyes light up with joy. 'My god, it's you! You've finally arrived—the ones who set everything in motion. I've waited for you for an entire century!'" Now, to touch the core of Templo de la Metáfora, you must solve a riddle.
This is a great treasure discovered in the "Laberinto de Símbolos." Its greatness lies in the fact that it is a part of us—a fragment, a symbol.
Congratulations! You've obtained your own "Golden Fleece." Relax, it's just a metaphor—it's got nothing to do with Jason or Medea.

A perfect rabbit—it has self-awareness, its actions are unpredictable, and the results it brings always weave a story.
Hmm? I think … this is the essence of Visceral Realism …
This item is incredibly rare, a gift left to you by the Gaucho Rider of 1975, a legendary cowboy from Sonora. Make good use of it.
Thank goodness, we've finally gotten past the cowboy and coachman bit ... Ahem. Now, quick, come with me—our grand adventure carries on!
This tale isn't solely about the cowboy and the coachman—it's about us as well. Honestly, is that so difficult to grasp?
Okay, the temple chapter is finished, but the story is far from finished.
I didn't expect you to loot the place clean. From what I saw, it was like putting sugar cubes next to an anthill.
You've taken every last item from the stone platform. This might be a bit of a spoiler, but you won't be able to collect anything else for now.
Well… that's certainly one way to go about adventuring … But you really should think about the hints I gave you, Vertin!
Actually, these items aren't part of the metaphor—okay, I did say, "everything is part of the metaphor," but these items really aren't!
I'm beginning to wonder … if exchanging items is what excites you most about the game?
Hey, I get that spending all your indicators at once is a common rookie mistake, but as the game master, I strongly suggest saving a few for the next part!
Excellent work! You now have all the essential items with you!

Hang on … I think you're misunderstanding something, Vertin. Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas is not a game focused on base-building and combat … You don't need to set up fortifications in the village!
Another night passes, and now every villager is armed with a brand-new weapon and ten bottles of healing potion. The village walls have also been raised to ten meters tall …

A month ago, I graduated from Leningrad University and was assigned to work at the Plesetsk Cosmodrome. This launch base is a major joint project between the government and Laplace, and today is my first day on the job. I made sure to put on a brand-new pair of leather shoes and even ironed my suit. The building is magnificent, and the lab is fully equipped with all the latest technology—far more than I ever expected in my scientific career. My team leader, Andreas, seems to be a kind man. He told me there aren't too many rules here—just remember to wear your gear during safety inspections.

The base has pretty good meal subsidies, generous leave policies, and even holiday bonuses. Our whole team gets together to drink vodka every Friday night! If we're lucky, they'll even invite a nearby circus to come and perform ... Honestly, it's nothing like what I had imagined, but all the more reason to do my best to get the job done.

Once winter sets in, the nights here become unbearably long. Back in Leningrad, I used to keep a few potted plants indoors to help lift my spirits. But here, my only option is to try my luck with the neighboring botany team. They're running a preliminary experiment to observe how plants grow in zero gravity by culturing sunflower explants.

I "bribed" Alyosha with a few bottles to look after a potted sunflower I picked out. He also promised to, if their experiment succeeds, hand it over for me to bring back to my dorm.

[Crossed out] My sunflower has turned completely moldy! Alyosha said he doesn't know why and that he'll start over with a new batch. He must've secretly used the clean bench for some other experiment and contaminated these materials! What an idiot!

[Crossed out] Another Foundation branch staff member is coming to the base. I heard he enjoys tinkering with little gadgets. Hopefully, he knows a thing or two about growing plants—then he can have my vodka instead.

I ran into a problem at work—a matrix calculation I've been stuck on for two full days. Andreas suggested I ask the materials team leader next door for help. He said she's brilliant at math and once helped the propulsion team optimize their advanced model—something they'd been struggling with for three months.

According to Andreas, she's the only one on her team. A rather unusual organizational structure. I've also heard her research is ... extraordinary, so extraordinary that it has no staff, no recognition, and, most importantly, no funding. Yet it sounds like she's willingly wasting her time there.

Well, I suppose there will always be people who waste their time on unfunded, seemingly pointless research. I remember hearing about this even back in university—like the one studying the flight dynamics of oak processionary moths, or the one trying to ignite a lamp kilometers away using optical arcane skills. Researchers like that usually end up obscure and unknown for their entire lives.

In any case, I plan to ask for her help tomorrow. Still, I admit, I really hope I don't end up in such a miserable situation.

Today I overheard the geography team talking about anomalies they've discovered in magnetospheric activity. I've always had terrible luck with auroras—I seem to miss them every time. Turns out there really is something unusual going on. Hopefully, they'll get to the bottom of it soon and give us a proper aurora forecast.

But they've barely started—the first step is placing observation instruments, and even that is still in its early stages. At least they've brought in a ley line researcher to help set things up. Poor girl's not even stationed at the base …

If I really want to see the aurora, I'd better just spend more time outside and hope for the best. After all, increasing the sample size is a key part of any research—I refuse to believe my luck can stay this bad forever!

Who knows, maybe I'll even run into that ley line researcher, Windsong. If she's willing to share a bit of her data with me ...

Someone forgot to turn off their record player. There's been faint music echoing through the lab hallways all morning—indistinct and constant like bees hovering near your ears. After a while I finally managed to catch the lyrics:

"The stars shine bright across the night,
I ask the void, what's past the light?

A voice calls out, my heart beats fast:
Will you stay still or rise at last?

I'll pack my things without delay,
And chase the stars that guide my way."

...

My team leader lost his patience before I did. He stormed out of the lab, searched around, and finally shut off that damn thing off. Thank goodness. Silence at last.

Good morning, my fellow mentally deficient friends. For once, I woke up in peace. I must say, this place is far more comfortable than the outside world. Want a piece of pie?
I can't go on … My legs … I can barely feel them! They've swollen into two stiff lumps! I didn't join the Order of Enlightenment for this kind of suffering!

"Thank you for bringing Ms. Urd here. On behalf of Manus Vindictae, we appreciate your assistance. Your accommodations in Antarctica are ready. I assure you, the tea you'll be served is of the same quality as what Mr. Forget Me Not enjoys."

Since Warden Tartuffe's transfer, the authorities never contacted Comala Prison again. And ever since Manus Vindictae's involvement, operations here have temporarily been placed under Merlin's supervision. Welcome to Comala Prison. For any inquiries, please leave a letter in the mailbox at the entrance or call the number listed below.

This moth-luring experiment was a complete success, with no significant psychological abnormalities observed. It's presumed that I've grown accustomed to this work environment. I will now proceed with the usual summary report.

This is Murphy's, and this is Bugsy's. Take them, and don't forget to thank Henry. He chose to wear the mask so you could have these pills and food to keep your free literature alive. Praise be to his selfless commitment.

When you see one human, there's likely forty more beyond your sight. I know, I know, they're all the property of the Administrators, and we have a deal with them—no slaughter without cause in prison. But isn't our hatred for humanity reason enough? Is it not?

Good morning, Murphy, Bugsy. You two know the rules better than I do. Henry's traded goods are running out. Who's next to wear the mask? Poetry isn't going to fill our stomachs. Does no one really want to follow in Henry's footsteps?
Ah, time to say goodbye. Why are so few of you willing to come? Since when did you all become so opinionated? Fine, an extra participant in the ritual is always welcome. Follow me.

I get it now. From today onward, I am Manus Vindictae, not the Order of Enlightenment. Names don't matter, but when do I get to operate outside? Zeno's forces are still enforcing martial law? Why me? I haven't even done anything to provoke them!

And now you're telling me the Zeno faction in Brazil is on our side? They almost killed me back there! Just who are we, what are we supposed to be doing? Until I get some real answers, I refuse to—what? A cruise trip? Fine, fine, I'll put up with this a little longer.

The lead, she's up there socializing in the banquet hall, while I'm shoveling coal in the boiler room?! This isn't the cruise experience I signed up for! I can't balance a pilgrimage and shovel coal at the same time like the others!

Following this endless pilgrimage, I have finally reached the world's end. Sigh, maybe the real treasure was the hardships we faced along the way. Now, my journey ends in this prison—entering this cage is my escape from the world's cage ... Wait, what!? Now we have to go even farther south?!
"Yes, the prison we're heading to is fascinating—a place where no one is truly themselves. As for the warden ... I know him well. You can stay as long as you like; I assure you, he won't interfere."
"There's nothing more to be done. Just let things take their course. This display cabinet … I'll keep it for myself."

"You lost Ms. Urd? What a disappointment. You want me to give you a chance to 'make it right'? No, we don't tolerate failure here. You will get nothing but punishment. Meanwhile, I will search for Ms. Urd myself."

"Thank you for your concern, but I'm fine. It's just a minor side effect from the arcane skill. And here we are—watch your step. The path ahead is treacherous. We're about to climb a mountain that isn't known to anyone"

Regarding your question—whether I have contacts within the Foundation or Laplace. I do answer some researchers' inquiries from time to time. No need to speculate, Ms. Grace. This does not count as espionage.
Regrettably, I'm not the warden of this prison. If you want to know more about Manus Vindictae's past, perhaps Merlin can tell you.

No need for irrelevant questions. I'm sure you've already pieced together a rough idea of who I am. Years ago, I crossed paths with Mr. Forget Me Not during a brief stint researching the Fountain of Youth. That's all there is to it.

Ms. Urd has left. As per our discussion, Merlin did not stop her and even managed to hide her movements from Manus Vindictae. But ultimately, she made her own decision—to head for Antarctica and seek her own fate. This is something neither of us can change for it may be the will of fate itself.

I have a grim suspicion—Urd may have chosen to side with Manus Vindictae. According to the moth's intel, she went to Antarctica of her own accord to join them. At the very least, it seems she's come to some kind of understanding with them.

There's no doubt that Manus Vindictae's headquarters is in Antarctica. That would explain why, even after dismantling so many of their hideouts, we've failed to make a real dent in their numbers. It's reasonable to assume they have some way of withstanding the "Storm," which only functions in Antarctica—and their deployment there likely exceeds anything we previously estimated.
The movements of the Zeno rebels remain unclear. Unless they have taken no action after defecting, they must be preparing for a large-scale military operation.

This experiment showed significant noise and signs of possible self-dialogue, limiting the amount of usable data. Preliminary speculation points to an anomaly in the moth's condition—or perhaps an undetected issue with my own health. Regardless, I request that this situation be reported to the appropriate authorities.

Balloon Party ties a bunch of balloons onto Rabies. Rabies gently shakes its body, producing creaking noises that sound like laughter.
In celebration of World UFO Day, aliEn T once again tells everyone inside the Suitcase about the time he met DUU-DUU-BELL-BOO.
While Ms. Radio is broadcasting the morning news, Kanjira notices Punji nestled on Hissabeth's head.
Yenisei and Name Day stand side by side in the Wilderness, gazing silently at the distant river.
Argus takes Barbara for a ride, the two of them listening to country music all day long.

Lorentz Butterfly's latest papers and letters arrive as scheduled. Ulrich reads them carefully as always, but halfway through he finds the rest mangled, with pages twisted, smeared, and marked with the unmistakable chaos of Medicine Pocket.

Marcus asks about the core riddle of Templo de la Metáfora. Recoleta realizes she's completely forgotten. It's hard to remember, after all, when you've written 103 novels since arriving in the Suitcase.
The first touring exhibition of Ms. NewBabel's Critter Center at the SPDM Library concludes successfully, and Teakettler's proposal to serve as the library's guide is now under consideration.
Pioneer joins Mercuria's meditation session for the first time. Just because he's a mannequin, that doesn't mean he isn't interested in meditation.
On reopening day at the popular Laplace Museum ice cream shop, Medicine Pocket tosses what would've been their 101st complaint about the snail eyeball-flavored beans.
Aleph receives a letter from Recoleta, along with the third edition of The Turquoise Serpent Club.
Two days after the ice cream shop's reopening, 37 sends 10 crates of ice cream and a letter to 6 via Critter Express. Fortunately, none of it melts.
In 1930, the first FIFA World Cup was held in Montevideo, Uruguay. To commemorate the occasion, J and Pioneer organize a Suitcase soccer (football) match, with Dikke as the referee.
With help from Balloon Party, Flutterpage flies across the entire Wilderness, scattering paper planes carrying various wishes to the Critters busy at work below.

During the final penalty shootout of the Suitcase soccer (football) match, J accidentally shattered the Tooth Fairy's jar. It took him two whole days and the cost of one tooth to gather the scattered fairies back.
The Indisputable Board Game has become popular inside the Suitcase and, after some tweaks, no longer limits the number of players.
Satsuki shares funny stories from her days working at the teahouse. That night, Baby Blue dreams a whole new kind of dream, one that carries the sweet scent of cake.
At cocktail parties, Eternity always keeps an eye on the one who offers her a "Bloody Sunset."

During lunch break, Black Ibis takes Liang Yue to an authentic Chinese restaurant. There, they bump into Loggerhead ordering the same spicy pepper soup, "Hu La Tang," and Matilda, who's crying from the heat but still loudly insisting she's fine.
The sequel to the "Spring Elfin Special," filmed entirely by ONiON, airs today.
Recoleta tells Cristallo the story of the cottage with a blue roof and a disturbingly real dream about a ring-shaped prison.

Noire and Blonney talk all night about the latest movie release. Blonney successfully convinces the director to shoot her suspense script about vintage cars and gentleman Critters, with Jessica making a special cameo.
In 1881, the International Gymnastics Federation was founded in Belgium, inspiring the earliest pioneers of the Floor Ritual program.
Tennant invites Eternity for a ride. She happily agrees and brings her longtime friend Ms. NewBabel along.

Darley Clatter proposes celebrating today as the "Suitcase Carousel Festival." With support from Barcarola, Balloon Party, Baby Blue, and sponsorship from Sotheby, the festival—together with the Twist Ball—is officially added to the Suitcase's event lineup.
Semmelweis receives seven "Gruß an Aachen" and one blank card.
37 and An-an Lee watch Good Will Hunting together. Before the protagonist even appears, 37 has already solved the professor's math problem, leaving An-an Lee with an awkward smile.
Musae III and TTT meet for the first time, and TTT offers a secret for five Musae Coins.
Regulus proposes forming a band inside the Suitcase. Tentative members include Lorelei as lead singer, Voyager on violin, her good friend Kiperina, and Barcarola on just about every other instrument.
Aleph, Merlin, and The Idealist, all masters of metaphor, are also invited to join Regulus's band as lyricists.
Kiperina and Voyager lie side by side in the Wilderness, quietly chatting. A shooting star streaks across the sky, but neither manages to make a wish in time.

How long has it been since we last spoke? The long tug-of-war with the cold drained all my energy. Only today did I manage to warm up enough to dip my tail in ink and write to you.

Sylvie is doing well. Maxime and Alexandre always help her think in parallel, and Monique, as usual, keeps things under control at critical moments. Serpentes has been showing more and more signs of thought lately. I think it's only a matter of time before he speaks. Hélène is sleepier than ever, staying in heated rooms around the clock.

As for Chantal and Pierre, they're the same as always.

And me? I didn't just hibernate. The local literature has filled the gaps in my collection that Sylvie once ruthlessly discarded.

The Melusines were deeply moved by these authors' vivid portrayals of suffering and death, yet even within the darkest themes, the authors' exploration of new paths brimmed with vitality, dreams, and a defiant sense of romanticism.

Whenever I read the literature to her, her memories become unusually vivid, and she recalls one line in particular with striking clarity from Pasternak's February: "The truest verses arise by chance, tempered in the fire of pain."

Of course, there's no way to verify this and Sylvie would never admit it, but I believe she's the most romantic in our family. Or maybe the second-most. After me. I wish you were part of the Dubois family too. That way, you'll truly understand what Sylvie's memories feel like when she sees a shooting star.

I truly hope we can talk about all of this someday. Maybe after Sylvie's little challenge is complete, you could visit Plesetsk. I promise Sylvie and I will both be warmly waiting to welcome you.

Your dear friend,

Estelle

Cepheus learned a wonderful way to live.

Cepheus moved quickly. And so, it fell hard. After that, it donned a metal shell.

Inside that metal shell, the ghost of Cepheus witnessed countless beautiful moments—

A near-eternal hearth being lit. Man-made stars launched into the sky. Earth's songs reaching beyond the Solar System.

But it all vanished in the rain. Its dreams ended.

And Cepheus felt regret for the first time. It realized, perhaps, that it didn't really know how to live after all.

Cepheus believed itself to be a guiding pointer for millennia to come, leading the way for ten thousand years. But in truth, it realized it didn't even understand the road to the next hundred years. It couldn't even light the paths of the Southern Hemisphere.

What happened to Cepheus afterward? It returned to the space base and continued its research for the sake of those still living.

As many of you have read in academic journals, the theoretical feasibility of teleportation incantations is not determined by distance.

However, the farther the distance, the more interference factors there are, and to this day, we still don't know exactly why. Thus, long-distance teleportation has always been considered the realm of pure fantasy.

However, during the extreme conditions just before the "Storm," we gathered a vast amount of arcane energy fluctuation data from outer space to the Earth's surface.

After repeated cross-analysis, we finally discovered a stable arcanum waveform capable of anchoring teleportation incantations. My teammate, she gave it a misleading name—"Pulsar Waveform." I suppose that was her way of being poetic or something.

...

Yes, I hear some of you murmuring that this is purely experimental, lacking theoretical proof and impossible to replicate. That's true. But the fact is, over the past few weeks, we've tested it repeatedly. As long as you simulate this waveform near the destination and there's enough arcane energy, you can achieve teleportation with up to 95% accuracy.

...

That's all I wanted to share today. I believe that one day in the distant future, with a complete theoretical framework, teleportation could become a field that outpaces aerospace itself. But even now, what we've uncovered is a stable, practical technology—perfect for food delivery.

"This is the sea? It's so much more beautiful than I imagined ... It's a pity I can't bring it back to look at under the orange light of my bedroom, or lie in my mother's arms while I watch it."
"You will drift far, carried by energy ... Is this a journey, or a return home?"

"After a ten-hour drive, I finally arrived at the forest locals call the 'Source of the Stream.' Passing through layers of mist, I finally saw its true colors. Dear readers ... are those dolls tied to the trees?!"
"Maybe finding a cause worth devoting yourself to is its own kind of solution. Since there's no place to return to, you just keep moving forward. That way, the road ahead always stays wide."
"More often than not, all we can do is make the patients as relieved as possible. Beyond that, there's little we can do. It truly breaks my heart."
"It's not just about creating sweet memories. It's also about comfort—a way to recall the carefree days buried deep in your mind."
"Miss Fortune Teller ... your grip is a bit too strong. Please don't pull my fingers toward the letters you want. Just give me a few candles for health, that'll be enough."
"Pain is personal. As much as we might empathize, we can't truly feel another person's suffering. It can't be compared, nor is it elevated or degraded by any objective condition."
"Of course I had to draw it! Or else it might have exploded in my head! ... It must exist. I need to see it, touch it, and have it praised in the real world!"
"Wait, how much did you say it costs? That much?! For just this one?!"
"You look gloomy and spiritless. Stick this on, and that feeling will be all gone. Pay first though, no free trials! But ... since you're a pretty lady ..."

"If you're going to turn your passion into a career, you have to learn how to compromise with reality. But that doesn't mean letting people walk all over you. Every compromise is a stepping stone toward earning greater creative freedom."

"He's the greatest jazz vocalist in the world! Look, he even autographed this for me! He knows me! I saw him wave at me from the stage once! Such a wonderful voice ... He deserves a bigger following!"

"Sometimes I still seem to hear the cheers and songs we sang on the beach ... Truth may be gone, numbers may no longer matter, but that's not the only reason he became our leader. I think I'll still follow him."
"Music is what brings people together. It sweeps away sorrow and brings hope. Even Carbuncles appreciate it—I mean, who wouldn't?"
"Your question is indeed valuable. My conclusion is ... that my staffs need an alarm loud enough to wake them and tough enough not to be smashed against the wall."
"Seeing him lying there in a pool of blood—it was disgusting, but in a way, it was also a relief. I stopped having nightmares after that day."

"Just look at this lush, green land of mine! You can feel the abundance in every breath of air. Come summer, the Carbuncles will be swarming like crazy because they know a good thing when they see it!"

"Today is just a continuation of yesterday. Maybe a few of my cells have died and been replaced, but that doesn't mean I've been reborn in any meaningful way. Physically and mentally, I'm the same as I was. Anyway, is there anything to eat around here? I'm famished."
"To be born anew, just the thought is enough to set some imaginations running wild. But from my personal experience ... be careful. You might lose yourself in the process."

The LSCC maintained its cutting-edge spirit. Employees turned offices into gaming arcades; bookshelves were crammed with the Global Catalog, Tumbling Stone, and neatly printed cognitive enhancement research papers.

Laboratories in Palo Alto were lit all night, bright enough to dull the stars overhead. What did it matter? Compared to those great advances of the era, everything else was just dust in the wind.

In a small apartment, nine pairs of eyes fixated on the scrolling numbers. The machines, the theories, the roaring processors, and glowing monitors never commented on themselves, nor did they incite any religious awe. When parents spoke about personal computers, they praised them for making communication easier, weaving the world closer together.

Yes, this was the reality she and her siblings chose to pursue.

A swatch of searing, burning color, pinned to the collar as a symbol of resolve.
Though the interviewee received it long ago, careful preservation has kept the fabric crisp, showing little wear even now. People often say it carries the same sentiment as hope.

A measuring instrument crafted from brass, infused with a trace of arcane metal to make it lighter and easier to carry.
Long ago, it sowed the seeds of Ley Lines, from which the path now unfolds.

A mark that has accompanied the interviewee for many years, sometimes giving off a glow, but most often it remains quietly dim. Some say it is the manifestation of their arcane skill.
Others, in more fanciful tales, call it dust that chose to stay behind on the blue planet.

This is the vibrant eighties.

New things are everywhere. Volga drivers roll down their windows to grab a Pepsi from roadside vendors. A little bear plush sits quietly on a shop counter, watching the crowds wave their goodbyes. Inside the circus tents, the shows go on as scheduled. Troupe members deliver just the right amount of thrill and excitement to the audience, then relieve the lingering tension with hot meals after the curtain falls. She rests safely inside this eggshell of a world—beyond it, chaos and the human condition churn.

Her troupe loves to share stories with her during their breaks. Night school classmates eagerly bring her news and gossip. Myths, legends, and ongoing events in the real world tangle together like the warm, rough knots in a bear cub's fur. Not every story actually happens, but every single one overflows with hope for the future, enough to make you forget the frostbite in your fingers, the endless lines, the long journeys and exhaustion.

There is an ideal here. A yearning for a steadier, safer life. If you can reach the cosmos, what pain or death could ever defeat you?

That's why she keeps stepping onto the narrow wire again and again, chasing a higher vantage point.

Higher than that taut wire. Higher than the waving flags.

High enough to look down on this glass sphere of a world—until everything on the ground blurs together, and nothing seems separate anymore.

Kiperina: You're right, Ms. Pandora Wilson.

Kiperina: But they always end up missing something. There's always some piece I just can't capture.

Kiperina: … I did try. Mr. Name Day taught me how to use it, and Ms. Mesmer Jr. reminded me about it, too.
Kiperina: They were right. The images created by machines aren't quite the memories I live through.

A metal companion that grows alongside children and follows them deep into the earth. Its blade once caught the firelight of life. The original silver scabbard is rarely displayed and is more often repurposed as a carving knife. The use of an object depends on the person, and this one proves that well.

A handmade trinket kept out of habit. Sometimes gifted to children or friends, or briefly placed somewhere as a marker. Occasionally used as a vessel for arcane skills during assignments. The interviewee simply refers to it as a consumable.

Once a simple bone ornament, later decorated as it passed through generations. To the current holder, it carries a heavy burden of expectation.
Left by the eldest sister to the youngest, passed on as a keepsake to their brother, and finally turned into a farewell token—leaving an unseen bruise on the third child. In the end, it is fortunate not to have ended up abandoned in some drawer.

If the snow mound can collapse once, then it can collapse again. And again.

Change and upheaval teach people to keep their distance from unreadable prophecies, only to push them further into the current. A few manage to keep hold of the reins of their horses, tempering their lives for the sake of another unreadable, elusive word: freedom.

To the children struggling to get by, the wild hares darting through the woods mattered more than the occasional news from town. Back then, "a life adrift" was just a phrase, it carried no weight and held no meaning for them. There were so many languages and words to name the world before them, yet not a single one could describe the world as it was. Long before they could make sense of what was unfolding around them, he and his siblings had already seen how the fire came to an end.

"What do you see, Lyonya?" his brother asks, mimicking ataman-like solemnity. He sets down his knife and buries the half-carved wood in the snow, staring into the distance.

The eyes of the birch trees gazed back in silence. The snow reflected the blinding light of the sun.

"Nothing. Just snow."

It was just an endless, eternal field of snow.

This vessel is destined for the stars, but before that, it has spent a long time admiring their glow.
The steles stand silent, towering in the bitter cold.

So here you are, calling out to the cosmos, hoping the vast unknown will serve up an answer unbounded by gravity.
To the naked eye, the water in the Wilderness looks very clean. However, there is no evidence that it is suitable for sustaining life ...
Vertin, have you ever observed signs of fish in the rivers and lakes around here?
Just Abang Akus? Ha, never mind—as if a snake could make hors d'oeuvres out of something that size.
You know, Vertin, one of us has been thinking about catching some fish in the Wilderness for a snack.
… If there were any. So there's no need for you to worry. Now, it's just me watching over my own little fish, making sure they don't get snatched up.
Hear that? If even Vertin hasn't seen them, they're probably not in the area.
That's right, it turns out one of us decided that lake fish might make for a tasty treat, and by the time I realized it, he'd already been sneaking out for several nights ...
All's well that ends well, I suppose. You can stop fretting over fish that may not exist, and I can stop losing sleep over him sneaking off.
I've been observing these critters … Have you noticed? They're constantly picking out friends for themselves.
They're quite amiable when with their chosen friends, but a few of the Carbuncles can't help but start brawling the moment they see each other.
No ... that's not it. This is simply a matter of personal interest.
These critters always remind me of the little creatures I once cared for … especially when they dart after specks of dust in those little clusters of theirs. Such carefree little things.
I was just wanting to confirm ... does Ms. NewBabel need any help? I might be able to lend a hand.
I'm flattered, but ... who could possibly manage a thing like that out here in the Wilderness?
I've only managed to recognize a handful, so I'm tracing their paths and studying which companions they choose.
It reminds me of how I learned about the stars as a child. You need to start off with the ones that stand out most, and soon the whole constellation begins to take shape ...
A touch of patience is all they ask ... and all they ever really need.
I've noticed the snow in the suitcase vanishes quicker than one might expect. It melts right along with the ever-changing weather.
The weather here is wildly unpredictable, yet strangely, I've never come across a single tale or rumor about weather phenomena inside a suitcase.
Because this kind of uncertainty and change often serves as fertile ground for myths and legends, people will go to great lengths to find patterns in what otherwise defies understanding.
Storytelling is our oldest method of making sense of the unknown, and the simplest ...
And I've certainly crossed paths with my fair share of storytellers here, in this suitcase of yours.
Now that's not really something I'm good at. As you know, I just have a knack for collecting stories.
How about a change of topic? I was wondering ... do you know how Han Zhang's been lately?
This episode of Approaching Arcanum is almost at an end, and as tradition dictates, no show is complete without ...
A lucky audience member! Hey there, Vertin!

Oh, right … we haven't technically built up any traditions yet. After all, this is our very first episode, so calling it a "tradition" is a bit premature. We'll need some empirical evidence before we can make that claim!
Stick around for the next show, and the one after that, and soon enough, talking about "tradition" and saying "as tradition dictates" will become a tradition in itself.
Yes, this is the part where we introduce you to our listeners ... and offer our sincerest thanks.
Although this wasn't the smoothest of shows, and in the end, we only managed to air it over the radio, you've stuck with us through thick and thin.
So we came to one conclusion—that if anyone deserves the title of our inaugural lucky audience member, it's most certainly you!
Timekeeper, I've heard the students at the SPDM hardly ever get to see the outside world before graduation.
Was it the same for you?

Does that mean you've never been to a circus before? Did you ever sneak out after school with your classmates, just to squeeze into a big top tent like sardines, passing around a single piece of chocolate ...?

Not that I ever had any experience like that, I only meant that I think most schoolchildren share a moment like that at some point. I used to see kids just like that ... before I became part of the show myself.
From then on, I was in the spotlight. There's no time to watch from the crowd when you're preparing for a performance. I had a job to do, and I had to do it right.
I heard about it from a Laplace researcher, and it made me wonder ... perhaps you've never seen a circus performance before?

I used to think circus performances were quite common, and that laughter and gasps were a regular part of the shows. But it turns out that, in different times and places, things aren't always like that.

That's why I'm preparing a performance here in the Wilderness. It won't be very polished, and it certainly won't be as good as the shows we used to put on, but I want to relive a piece of the past that once brought joy to so many people ...
I want to share that joy once more. Will you come to see it?
Ah, perfect timing. I believe you may have dropped this.
It rolled into the little space between the sofa and the rug. I just happened to catch sight of it.
Happy to help. Your suitcase is such a peaceful little haven, and in my experience, people are more likely to misplace things in the places they feel most at home.
I wouldn't really call it wisdom or anything like that, just a personal feeling. There aren't many places in the world where you can truly feel at ease, but your suitcase is definitely one of them.
That wasn't my intention, but thank you for your generosity.
I don't usually treat lost items as collectibles. I wouldn't want my storeroom looking like a lost-and-found. Kidding, of course.
So you've taken on one of Ms. NewBabel's requests?
You mean you can tell every Carbuncle apart?
Why don't you cook up a story.
Thanks, I was just looking for this.

Day One For polar explorers, the romance lies in challenging the last great unknown. McMurdo Sound, on the northwest edge of the Ross Ice Shelf—this is the heart and launch point of Antarctic expeditions. Yes, we've arrived. Day Three At Mack's shout, we all stepped out of camp and saw auroras in broad daylight. Even in the coldest place on Earth, it was a rare and beautiful sight … but no, something about it felt wrong. Day Seven We've lost two members … We still don't know what happened. The sun is gone from the sky, though it should still be daytime. … Something is wrong with this place. Day Twelve? It's fine. We're close to the coast. Any passing ship will see us … and my distress signal. Day ……………… Do not seek the truth. Do not go deeper into Antarctica. Do not proceed!

Available Equipment for Polar Environments Due to Antarctica's harsh climate and extreme conditions, standard expedition tools, such as compasses, are often ineffective. Prior to landing, ensure essential specialized equipment is prepared, including diesel generators, snowmobiles, and radio transmitters. Conduct a complete inventory check in advance. Simone: I do not know much about chess, but I've heard that brute-forcing through opening moves isn't a practical way to play. Lucy: Perhaps. When searching for the right path, systematically going through all possibilities is still the best approach. Simone: But this is just an exhibition match. I am not a professional chess player—the notion of winning or losing this match holds little significance for me. The same goes for the vice president. We've lost track of Igor and his forces, but it's confirmed they've reached the interior of Antarctica.

Based on the final intelligence reports we received, their likely encampment is far from the Ross Sea landing site—hardly an ideal position for an ambush or interception. From both a terrain and a strategic standpoint, it seems more like a location chosen for a swift retreat.

Currently, we have no way of discerning Admiral Igor's true intentions. For now, however, it's clear that his forces will not pose the primary threat when the Zeno Expeditionary Force launches its assault on Antarctica.

The "Mother Spirit" is a deity worshipped by certain communities within the Arctic Circle. According to legend, after she casts endless sunlight over the North Pole, she falls into slumber at the edge of the Antarctic, awaiting her next awakening—a cycle that brings eternal day to the north once more. In regions where this myth is told, the "Reindeer Festival" emerged. During the festival, youths compete in reindeer handling, and the year's champion becomes the Mother Spirit's chosen, marking the occasion by sounding the great drum in praise of the sun, raising the proudest banner, and declaring a victory that flutters in the wind. It is said that a lost child who passes through the Mother Spirit's body glimpses her soul and receives a piece of "good news" powerful enough to change the course of their life. ■ Preliminary assessment: This is most likely a fabricated local myth with no credible value for further reference.

... I believe our history is woven by two opposing forces: order and chaos—the latter can also be called "defiance" or "liberty."
These twin impulses live in every human heart. And as nature dictates, these impulses often harden into faith. Those who champion both order and liberty will forge groups, spilling blood for their creeds. This war has raged since rise of the first cities.
There is one force that resists invaders, wicked rulers, and fanatics that would burn civilization to ash. As for proof, let me think ... consider the Borgias, yes ... There must have been a soul, or some souls who served as Liberty's blade, ending lives of those tyrants. Those souls surely embodied the very ideal of free will.

Fear tames men like sheep, making them flock willingly to familiar causes. Fear forges scattered strength into a solid whole.
Thus, for sacred order, we need to spread fear wisely and harness its power.

March ■■ Good heavens! I never thought linear perspective would be so hard to learn. I asked plenty of dumb questions, but Uccello answered all of them patiently and kept encouraging me. Father said I needed more practice too. March ■■ The lords kept throwing out new ideas, but Uccello always managed to talk them down. The fresco is getting more and more lively and artistic ... It is an honor to witness the birth of a masterpiece. March ■■ Following Uccello's advice, everyone tried that magical paint, including the most stubborn ones among us. I hope these days never end. April ■■ We are being dismissed. My skills have improved over these last few days. Uccello generously shared his paint with us before he left. The story is coming to an end. We have to leave the painting unfinished ... I've put away the paint, but its odor remains in my mind.

[Southeast Corner of the Room] Piles of a sand-quicklime mixture, a bit of carbon dust, several nails and punched paintings. Just some leftover materials they didn't use. Worthless to me. [East of the Room] Two carving knives, several brushes, and a piece of glass. Nothing worth taking. The glass looks like some kind of lens. Dried Paint They didn't seal the paint can with beeswax! What a waste ... A dozen letters and several intact paintings. Finally, something worth taking. I can make a new manuscript and name it Mystery of the Frescos or Wonders of Florence ... No, I need a more eye-catching title. [North of the Room] Scaffoldings. Collapsed. Messy carvings: a group of dancing human symbols, their meaning is unclear. Is this a signature? I bet the scaffoldings were broken by the ones who were fighting.

People enjoy speaking with her, eager to hear her advice—after all, age brings wisdom, doesn't it? Of course, Deimos would disagree, and this elder harbors no fondness for the young chosen one either. Still, fear has a way of enforcing obedience.

A Kephallonian Cultist of Kosmos.
Violence is a simple language that anyone can understand. In the Eagle Bearer's second homeland, many seek control over the vineyards and harbors. This gang leader, also a skillful sailor, appears to have considerable backing—not just from the local people and animals.

A Kephallonian Cultist of Kosmos.
The palace of Ithaka has long attracted treasure hunters, drawn by the legendary riches of epic heroes. One such team, led by this man known for training pincer-swinging helpers, is no different—they even rob travelers on the road. As one bard put it: just another petty villain lacking originality. Still, it seems powerful figures have taken notice of his findings—and now seek to win him over.

A Delphic Cultist of Kosmos.
This Pythia has delivered prophecies faithfully for years—well, mostly faithfully. A slight tweak to the divine words here and there—what harm could it do? It's all in the name of maintaining order. She remains, of course, a trusted and respected Pythia.

A Delphic Cultist of Kosmos.
This regular patron adores the Delphic theater. He funds costumes and props, organizes rehearsals, and encourages young actors. In return, the stage becomes his eyes and ears.

The clues point to a Cultist of Kosmos in Delphi.
Control isn't always enforced through violence. With the help of loyal followers, Kostas knows this god-blessed land like the back of his hand. Few have seen his face; some rumors even exaggerate his appearance. But as his eyes are picked off one by one, his reign draws to a close.

A Spartan Cultist of Kosmos.
A typical mercenary—blunt, ruthless, and battle-hungry. After the Cult extended an olive branch, he found new "joys" in life. Now, you can speak to him in the only language you both understand.

A Spartan Cultist of Kosmos.
This Spartan commands considerable local prestige—insightful in military matters and earnest in public affairs. Yet in some areas, he refuses to tolerate dissent—such as how a hero's statue should be sculpted.

An Olympian Cultist of Kosmos.
This patron is especially popular among those who come to Olympia dreaming of becoming professional athletes. He scouts promising young talents and trains them for the Cult of Kosmos. Lately, he's been trying to recruit a newly arrived lyre player—who, as it happens, is also an exceptional bookworm ...

The clues point to a Cultist of Kosmos in Olympia.
Alecto has the charisma a leader needs—or at least the volume. It makes his speech feel blessed by the gods. Once an Olympic champion, he later found perfect harmony with the Cult.

The clues point to a Sage of the Cult of Kosmos.
A climactic figure found in every heroic saga: cold, powerful, proud and exactly the battle you've been waiting for. The Sage remains confident in his strength despite you having cut away his wings. Go on, defeat him now. Your journey won't end here.

A massive arcane sea creature spotted near Kephallonia.
Vaguely human in form, she emits high-frequency vocalizations resembling human speech—though local sirens insist she lacks true intelligence and operates purely on predatory instinct. Strongly advised: do not peer beneath her skirt.
Note: Possibly an anomaly resulting from observational redundancy; continued monitoring recommended.

Colossal arcane creatures roaming Delphi.
Terrestrial, massive in size, slow-moving, omnivorous, apparently still growing. Highly attuned to ley energy; when contacted with such energy, they gain strong self-healing abilities.
Hmm, what could we learn from its mythology?
Note: Possibly an anomaly resulting from observational redundancy; continued monitoring recommended.

A colossal arcane creature spotted in Olympia.
Terrestrial, with a humanoid face and multiple limbs, it carries dangerous venom throughout its body—its tail being the most toxic. Difficult to classify within existing arcane zoological frameworks. Beware the blue poison—thick, oozing, flowing blue poison.
Note: Possibly an anomaly resulting from observational redundancy; continued monitoring recommended.
She scours through the tomes, absorbing the light of wisdom. Now, at last, she understands that the knowledge she should worship lies elsewhere.
His works are just like his character—solid, faithful, and stainless.
"The Truth"never lies. A fact that doubters find out before uttering a single word.
When night falls, people hear wings flapping in the sky—not from common bats, but from its shadow.
She's said to be a descendant of Medusa. Whoever looks straight into her eyes would see only death.
Coral fragments and pieces of shipwreck cling to her chain. Her breath reeks of decayed fish.
Its roar can shatter clay pots, and its mouth can ... Well, you don't want to know where the captives are.
He never sleeps, literally. The sailors swore they had seen him standing still on the deck when a storm struck, as if he was an unmovable rock.
Some said he was abandoned at a mass grave when he was a child, yet he survived. Others believe he sought shelter from the God of Corruption.

Gleaming gold, dazzling and impenetrable, sculpted with ideal musculature and covered in intricate, dense engravings. At first glance, it seemed fit for the noblest of men—until the interviewee interrupted to correct us: only the most fearsome deserve to wear it.

Its blade bears traces of ancient forging techniques, hinting at a gift from the gods—bestowed upon a warrior who could not be defeated. To face it is to divide the strong, who rejoice, from the weak, who wail.

A triangular shard which embodies Pythagoras' theorem through the combination of precise angles of point, line, and plane—a work of geometric perfection. More crucially, it affirms its bearer's "identity" in a subtle but authoritative way.

"Decades ago, a small group of people gathered around a theory. They believed it could be used to control the space. To them, the world moved between two forces: order and chaos."

But some among them fell too deeply into chaos. From that descent, the Cult of Kosmos was born.

Wearing masks, black robes, and the image of a serpent that devours all, they made no effort to hide their ambition and greed. They claimed to desire order, but sought to build it through war—an order that served only themselves. And so, the Greek world was plunged into endless conflict.

To prolong the war, they orchestrated an event in 446 BCE. Within the smoke-filled temple of Delphi, a trembling, feverish female voice delivered a sentence upon a newborn boy:
"To prevent Sparta's fall, the child must fall first."
Bound by the divine will of the oracle, the Spartan Gerousia left the family no choice. One rainy night, the infant was cast from Mount Taygetos.

Though he survived the fall, his descent through life never stopped. As if swallowed by the serpent itself, he no longer belonged to his family—or to any place under the Sun.

A rare find, well-concealed, no finger sacrifices required. Enhanced through visionary refinements, the Hidden Blade became the assassins' deadliest implement. We remain fascinated by its design and have requested a prototype sketch from the interviewee, hoping to understand how it achieves both deadly precision and aesthetic grace.

A rugged cloak for a seasoned assassin—lightweight, weathered, and resilient. The interviewee shared that it shielded its wearer from Florence's sudden summer showers, and kept blood from staining his robes the instant the blade struck.

When asked about this artifact's origin, the interviewee paused, visibly moved, and shared its story with heartfelt emotion. They requested anonymity upon publication. To respect their privacy, we offer this excerpt:
"On the night before his execution, a father entrusted a family heirloom hidden in a secret chamber to his son. The young boy, in a panic, rushed home and put on the assassin's robes passed down to him. Years later, he finally understood—that night, his father had already made up his mind to pass on this ancient legacy."

Like many who live through great eras of history, the people of Renaissance Florence rarely grasped the weight of the age they inhabited.

They were preoccupied with the price of wool, the exchange of florins, and adding the last brushstroke to a mysterious smile. Unknowingly, they shaped a new reality—one where an ancient idea bloomed once more from the shadows: that mankind is born free.

This idea, a fragile spark at first, inspired countless souls to rise in its name. It carried the ancient struggle into the modern world, tinting the war between Assassins and Templars with a vivid shade of Florentine red.
At the heart of this conflict stood the Auditore family. One generation. Two. Three? Only their successors know the final count.

But whatever the number, the world remains in balance.
After centuries of bloodshed, the sun over Florence still shines with the same generosity, warming saints and sinners alike. This city, instinctively tilting her left cheek toward tradition, can't help but glance to the right, gazing toward a brilliant, uncharted future.

What remains of the legendary Spear of Leonidas. It hums with energy, awakened by a mystical power. Its whispers are faint, elusive—perhaps only the interviewee truly understands what they mean.

In 480 BCE, King Xerxes I of Persia led a massive invasion into Greece. At the narrow pass of Thermopylae, King Leonidas of Sparta and his 298 Spartan warriors—joined by a handful of soldiers from other city-states—used the terrain to hold back an army that outnumbered them many times over.
Leonidas and his men fought fiercely for three days, withstanding wave after wave of Persian assault, until they were finally overwhelmed and fell where they stood.

The war has long since passed, and the legend now rests in the verses of wandering epics. And the hero's broken spear, preserved through bloodlines, lives on in its passing.

Decades later, in Lakonia—briefly spared from the tides of war—a descendant of Leonidas was born and raised. A spirited girl, trained in Spartan discipline by her father, a respected general of the polis. Her mother had bestowed upon her that legendary broken spear, forging in the child both the art and spirit of Sparta.
But one rainy night, to the sound of her mother's wails, that very father cast his daughter from the cliffs.

Perhaps it was Tyche's mercy. The fall did not deliver her to the underworld, but instead marked the beginning of something else—a legend. She stood, lifted her eyes, and there it was: the broken spear that had fallen with her, resting quietly under the moonlight.

And so, it finally met the moment to fight for its master again.

The following passage was recorded by Vertin and others, attributed to an Athenian bard. According to the bard, it tells the tale of a mercenary known only as "The Eagle Bearer":

Tell me, Muse, of the legendary mercenary,
The western wind that swept across the wine-dark sea, ever wandering,
Who met many people and city-states, their cunning and guile,
And through the vast oceans and the forests of the gods,
Endured endless suffering in body and spirit,
Seeking kin, seeking home.
Goddess, daughter of Zeus, sing us her tale.

She once walked the soil of Phokis, where Apollo's priestess
Altered her prophecy for her.
When the west wind reached Attika,
The Athenians welcomed her with joyous feasts.
Winged words carried her to Lakonia,
Where she stood before the king of Lakedaimon,
And her arrival forced him to face a dark fate.
As he turned to flee, a spear pierced his chest.
The king collapsed, his armor clattering against the stone.

Time flowed on, and the end came as it does for all.
By the will of the gods, she found her way home,
Returned to Sparta, though peace still eluded her.
When she was back in her mother's arms, the gods rejoiced,
All but one—the distant god of fear,
Son of Ares—held fast to his spite
Against god-like Kassandra,
Until she stood once again before the cliff where it all began.

Kassandra: ... Sorry, I shouldn't have stared at you for so long. Could you repeat the question?
Pandora Wilson: No problem. You're actually one of the few interviewees who aren't too curious about me. Even Arcanists sometimes struggle to let that curiosity go.
Pandora Wilson: Back to the topic—do you still feel anything like longing, nostalgia, when you think of Sparta?
Kassandra: I was a Spartan once, but that was a long time ago. Once you learn to survive on your own, you stop holding on to the past.
Kassandra: Though, there are exceptions.
Pandora Wilson: Could you tell me about one of those exceptions?
Kassandra: When you see ... someone you've longed to see but also feared the day you would. Especially when they're so tied to your past.
Pandora Wilson: Someone from your past ... Was it your family?
Kassandra: They'll always be my family.
Kassandra: Even after they threw me off a cliff.
Pandora Wilson: Even if they raised their swords against you?
Kassandra: That was their choice. Not mine.

A golden fruit shimmering with an arcane glow. The interviewee readily admits it comes from Laplace's arcane materials warehouse.
"Oui, it's actually a Fruit of Good and Evil. I painted it together with my siblings. If it looks familiar to you—that's right, I modeled it after the images in the archives.
It's my new project: myth interpretation!"

An ancient crown discovered by the interviewee amid some ruins on the Petrified Islands. Her siblings adorned it with the fresh leaves of spring.
Wearing an unidentified relic—especially one suspected of carrying the traces of arcane skill—might seem reckless. Yet when speaking about it, the interviewee and her siblings express disappointment: the crown feels as if it was calling out, adapting itself to its new owner when she put it on, but aside from its unusually perfect size, there seemed to be no other effects.

A soft, iridescent gown crafted by the skilled women of Lesbos and Chios.
The history of the Gorgon may be as long as these islands themselves. To explore the subtopic "Origins of Myth," the interviewee and her siblings spent a long time traveling around the region. She admits that convincing the local Daughters of Artemis to lay down their bows was the hardest part of the research.
"But it was worth it—I witnessed a rare ritual. Be sure to read my new paper!"

A heavy yet supple fabric, sturdy enough—hopefully—to withstand the chill of the underworld.
In Athens, the interviewee commissioned her favorite verses to be embroidered in gold thread onto this garment. It cost her a small yet painstakingly saved fortune.
But she believes it was worth every coin: wherever she travels, even along the dark banks of the Styx, poetry will be there with her.

An ancient instrument said to carry the love of a mythical poet in its strings.
To chronicle the departed with pen and paper once felt too vast a task—too easy to lose oneself in the palace of details. But when the interviewee heard the lyre during the Dionysian festival, it dawned on her: perhaps the strings, too, are a way to remember.

A treasured emblem of honor, adorned with fresh leaves and ancient gems, which the Athenians believe carry the beauty of poetry.
The interviewee unexpectedly received this offering when she was playing the harp in the Acropolis, along with an invitation to play the role of the underworld's poet—a prospect that terrified her. Not every listener believes the epic she sings—a tale of pursuit—is drawn from real life, but the people love it all the same.

A rare treasure dredged from the seafloor. Her sisters once held honey and poison alike, adorning the temples of witches and sea gods. But the interviewee prefers to scoop fresh spring water with it instead, turning it into a remedy for pain.

A light and flowing textile said by the interviewee to be in the style of the Sirens.
She never expected to meet distant kin in this age. She paints the moment of reunion, and in return, she receives a Greek-style vocal lesson—along with this veil, light as a sea breeze.

A silver-and-shell hand ornament that gives off a curious chime when tapped.
Many myths describe her people as wielders of mystical powers—singing enchanting songs, brewing strange potions, or raising towering waves of vengeance. She doesn't deny there's truth in some of the tales, but to her, these hands are most powerful not for destruction, but for what they create.

A high-quality crystal lens. Clear vision reflects a clear mind—essential for any philosopher, especially an apple steeped in ancient Greek thought.
Besides, a sharp view helps with the dizziness that comes after one too many glasses of wine.

A fruit painted in hues that echo through the classical era or a muse to Renaissance masters—call it what you like.
"This is a total accident," says the interviewee. He fully understands the Athenians' obsession with him—though they confused it with a different, more famous fruit.
Comedy and tragedy, the interviewee says, are merely two sides of the same leaf.

A splendid sash that shines like the golden sparks of inspiration in a scholar's mind.
The interviewee received it in a modest Athenian home, at a gathering where there was an abundance of poetry, debate, theater, and wine. The interviewee woke groggily in a bundle of soft cloth, clutching a gift from an Athenian philosopher—a token in memory of an everlasting friendship.

A treasure from the field, holding golden grains and plumes in radiant bloom.
"Everything in fashion is cyclical, just like the seasons," says the interviewee. Her horn-shaped pouch holds seasonal harvest, captured forever in solidified precious metal.
This sparks rumors—is she expanding her bizarre product line? She answers only with a smile.

The color-shifting gemstone earrings are said to come from a gem workshop in southern Greece.
The dazzling light of these gems shifts with every angle, like the never-closing eyes on the tail feathers of a goddess's favorite bird.
"Oh, darling, when we talk, you can look into the pair of eyes you like."

Every queen should have her own crown, and this one is no exception.
Gold, turquoise, and malachite are carefully carved and set onto a headband, like twelve stars. Work takes its own time—no matter how the myths and years pass, the laws of the seasons do not bend to human will. This is one unchanging thing in a hundred years.

Assassins can move between rooftops and the ground without using a ladder.
Most enemies cannot move between these two terrains at all, while some can by using a ladder.
Each tile can hold up to 4 enemies.

Towers are located in the middle of 4 tiles. Assassins can climb them at the cost of AP to enter the Stealth status, gaining immunity to enemies' search.
Enemies cannot climb towers.
Haystacks and Rooftop Gardens are hiding spots open to Assassins in the Stealth status. They also provide immunity to enemies' search.
If there are enemies in an alert tile, Assassins entering this tile will be Exposed.
Assassins cannot use Assassin Skills in water tiles.
New enemies are spawned from the spawn spots every round. Their number will further increase when the alarm sounds.
Assassins must enter the area or use a skill to learn information about it.

If an Assassin is Exposed during an enemy round, the alarm will sound, increasing enemies' Detection and causing the spawn spot to spawn more enemies.
An active alarm will reset as long as no Assassins are exposed in 2 consecutive rounds.
When on a tower, tap on the adjacent Haystacks to perform the Leap of Faith, which allows Assassins to move there without consuming AP.
Assassins automatically enter the Stealth status when in an enemy-free tile. While in this status, they can perform Assassination to kill enemies.

When detected during an enemy search, Assassins enter the Exposed status, drawing enemies to move towards them.
Enemies attack Exposed Assassins in their round.

When changing from the Exposed status to the Stealth status, Assassins leave a trace on their current tile, towards which enemies will continue to move.
The trace only disappears when any enemy reaches it or 2 rounds after it is generated.
When in the Stealth status, Assassins can perform Assassination against enemies in the same tile, killing them directly.
When in the Stealth status and on a tower/rooftop, Assassins can perform Air Assassination against enemies in the adjacent tiles, killing them and moving to that tile simultaneously.

When Assassins attack an enemy, they have to fight all the enemies in that tile.
When in the Stealth status, Assassins' attack automatically becomes Ambush, which increases their Critical DMG in battle.

When there are multiple Assassins in the same tile, they can launch a Joint Attack, which starts a battle involving all the Assassins and enemies in that tile.
When in the Stealth status, Assassins' Joint Attack automatically becomes Joint Ambush, which increases their Critical DMG in battle.
When in a hiding spot, Assassins can perform Hidden Assassination against enemies in the same tile, killing them without leaving a body and obtaining their items directly.

When an Assassin's HP goes to 0, they enter the Downed status and cannot conduct any operations.
Other Assassins can use items or skills to heal them.

Enemies become bodies after being killed. Assassins can hide them when there are no enemies around, after which they may obtain items.
When an enemy moves to a tile with bodies in it, the alarm sounds.
One incident is triggered at the start of each round, causing a variety of impacts and deciding enemies' movement direction if no Assassins are being Exposed.
When no Assassins are being Exposed, enemies move in the direction decided by the incident of the round; otherwise, they move towards Exposed Assassins.

Enemies start a search when Assassins move to their tiles or when they move to Assassins' tiles.
When there are multiple enemies, each of them starts an independent search. Assassins become Exposed if detected.
When exposed Assassins move away from enemy tiles, half of the tile's enemies will chase them to the current tile if possible.
In an enemy round, enemies start a battle involving all the enemies and all the Exposed Assassins in the same tile if there are any.
Enemies in the Stationed status stay where they are.

... This place could use more haystacks. Especially under buildings tall enough to poke Zeus in the eye.

Timekeeper ...? Sounds like a god's name.

I alone am worthy of the name "Deimos."
... Why not? Heh, how typical among the ignorant. Once you have claimed a name, you have to embody it.
Reaching above your station, refusing to bow to us ...

This place is free of conspiracies, violence, and oppression.

Our goal here has been achieved.
Quitting is not an option for Assassins. It's like a mark burned onto our bodies ... and our souls.
I am and always will be an Assassin, but sometimes, I can use a break like this.
Such a peaceful moment under the sun ... It reminds me of the old days in Florence when everything had yet to happen.
I believe you understand that feeling, Vertin.
Vertin, you said you were interested in the mercenary lifestyle, huh?
Get up early before sunrise, arm yourself, and wait for your creditors at the door.

Well, I always go with the latter.
Good. I'll send Ikaros to wake you up tomorrow.
Make sure to train your arms and legs in advance. Maybe then you'll be useful when a debt collector comes knocking at my door.
Save your strength and get some rest. Don't over sleep.
If you're here to negotiate on her behalf, you have my answer.
You know who I'm talking about—the mercenary with a broken spear, my "sister."
Leave her before you regret it ... You stand no chance against me.
You're a smart woman and I'm willing to bet you know who would win in a contest between us. Make the right choice.
There is only one way to survive, and that is ...
Apparently, you need someone to tell you what to do ...
I hope you have enough sense to make the right decision.
How does it compare to Florence?

I'm only here for a chat, and I speak for myself.

Behold, this worn yet even glow of memory,
Plunging with a "plunk" through the crimson clouds.
The evening bell summons recollections from the grave,
Turning to white doves—weightless now, no longer burning.
And I wait, for its tireless, infinite returns.

Circling, wings spread toward rosy-fingered dawn,
Striding, leaping, sailing to the wine-dark sea.
Clutch the helm, raise your voice in song,
Till sirens climb your blade,
Summoning the first dream that stings you.
