Slipped on broken ice? Don't panic. You might've just found the ruins' entrance.
Watch all chapters of "In Her Own Reflection."
Moving beyond the illusions of homeland, you're guided onto a path both real and cold.
Watch all chapters of "A Moment on the White Expanse."
A soldier's duty, the virtue of restraint, and a sister's choice.
We plan to replace these jarring alarms with more melodious tunes.
Employees complain that they can no longer listen to their favorite songs without flinching.
You've grown accustomed to handling emergencies, both physical and psychological.
Truth be told, doesn't it seem like we have an unreasonable number of lab incidents?
Your fondness for Critters rivals only your devotion to the competition.
These little ones have too much energy, so best keep your hat out of the line of fire.
Firewood is scarce in Antarctica, but guess what? We've got plenty of brain cells to burn!
They say you should shun evil deeds and embrace all that is virtuous.

Complete the Level I achievements in Reunion Once More, Expedition Guidelines, Hardship Behind the Gate, Rescue Operation, Desensitization Plan, Vanguard Commendation, Sticker Enthusiast, and A Good World.
Your fate spins like thread on a spindle, one more turn, then another ...
A game so simple it breeds self-doubt.
Clear on [Fundamental Computation] or Higher Difficulty.
What a thrilling battle—or was it?
One "interesting" experience is more than enough ...
Equip 2 Thought Fragments to any Mind Circuit.
Can't we come up with some solutions without these?
Equip 3 Thought Fragments to any Mind Circuit.
Or is this just feeding our weird collector's obsession?
Alright, first it was weird symbols. Now it's weird objects.
You're telling me combining them actually works?
What am I, a census taker now?
Go fetch my analyzer. I'll settle this with that critter!
Bring any resource x4000 back to the Silver Sanctuary.
Reports from the logistics department always say the same thing: insufficient supplies and self-reliance required.
Bring any resource x8000 back to the Silver Sanctuary.
"Turning Trash into Treasure" is a Laplace project now?
Bring any resource x20000 back to the Silver Sanctuary.
Let's see what we've got today ... a baseball bat, bottle caps, and ... Neutron Cola?
We are the ones who found all those supplies. Why are they being "rewarded" back to me?
Feedback: Suggest Musae III add a quick exploration function.

Complete the Level I achievements in The First Step, The Lighthouse's End, The Key of Wisdom, Exponential Growth, United Beneath the Banner, The Demon Hunter, The Scavenger's Handbook, and Easy Rider.
We have witnessed the first umbrella's invention. And now it's time for us to step into the rain.
Excellent! Now I have three penguin guards.
I'll be sure to ask their names to include them in the acknowledgements section.
Ah, I see his trail—just ahead.
Let's hope this squirrel is reliable.
He's by far the smartest squirrel I've ever met.
I should talk to him about the record later.
He may have some unique insight on the matter.
I forgot to tell him that my carrier fluid doesn't freeze below -80°C.
But considering the potential for metal to turn brittle in extreme temperatures, I'd better move fast.
Starting transmission to the Timekeeper. Let's hope nothing goes wrong—ah, flux.
Time to think outside the tank. Maybe I can rig a radio antenna kite ...
Forget it. Nothing will work in a Force 8 Antarctic gale.

Several distant barks echo,
but the direction is unknown.
There is nothing left to feel but cold stone and the frost-hardened earth.

Something's wrong here. Attune to the sounds, the scents, the shifting wind,
And that faint residue of arcanum.

Viscous liquid seeps into every crack between the stones,
The scent of blood hangs heavy, demanding caution.
A path shaped by what I know and what I once only dreamt. At least it's tangible enough for now.
The darkness is drowning all sense of direction. Still, there's a guiding hand lingering in it, or perhaps just an instinct ... I should follow it.
Loose moss tumbles with the quietest rustle.
The snow blocking the way comes crashing down.
A wind blows here, cold enough to pierce through bone.
Calling the Timekeeper, this is Ulrich ... Damn it, the Foundation's communications are barely getting through.
What's up? Lost contact with yer pals?
Lieutenant Moldir's intel about the ritual is critical. I have to report it to the Timekeeper as soon as possible.
But the blizzard's too heavy, and the mountain's too tall. We need to find a location suitable for our shortwave radio ...
No sweat, partner! Just leave it to me! So what kinda spot we lookin' for?
Electromagnetic waves get absorbed and reflected by terrain. Direct waves give off stronger signals than reflected or diffracted ones.
So the fewer the obstacles between us and the Timekeeper's team, the more likely we are to make contact.
Of course, the state of the ionosphere still affects a few ... Sergeant Fairchild? Are you listening?
... Huh? 'Course I am! Bright-eyed and bushy-tailed as ever. So, ya need a clear spot facin' the city ruins, right?
Then you folks do yer thing, and I'll scout on up ahead. Keep yer peepers open for my markers!
No response, but there are no issues with the signal. The Timekeeper must be busy.
Dontcha worry! It's all clear ahead. Ya can holler for yer pals any time ya like!
I'll admit that you've got a knack for science. If we make it back alive, I wonder if you would consider joining the Laplace Scientific Computing Center?
I'm certain my colleagues would have no issue in accommodating another unusual arcanist.
Shucks, I'm flattered! I'd be keen for a visit, but I'm afraid I done already sworn my loyalty to Lieutenant Moldir!
Gonna scout on ahead now. Save yer lecture for later! Keep movin' and try not to let yer brain freeze through!
This spot looks good. We've got a direct line of sight to the city ruins, so the signal should carry.
Dontcha stop now! It's dangerous here. We gotta keep movin'.
Dangerous? We're the only ones here, and the slope is quite gentle. The avalanche risk is less than 0.5%.
I need to establish communications. This intel must reach the Timekeeper—now!
But Mr. Ulrich, dontcha smell that? Air's dusty. Somethin's lyin' in wait for us!
The Timekeeper's in danger. If we lose this comm window, the next one won't come easily.
You two go on without me. This risk is mine to take.
But boss, that ... goes against my orders ...
Relax. Just hand me the thermos. I'll know when to hide.
Look, I get yer worried about yer pals—but this fancy radio of yers just ain't worth it.
The equipment isn't my concern. See? I have backup units. All it takes is a little paperwork at Headquarters.
Now wait just a dang minute! What if YOU fall off next time?
Fine, fine. Since ya got the patience for all them Foundation forms, we'll take it low and slow. Just follow yer guide, we'll make it work!
But every step we take this way takes us farther from the Timekeeper—compared to Manus Vindictae, we're moving at a snail's pace ...
Never thought I'd wish penguins could fly.
Funny ya mention it—back in Florida, these fellas did take a couple flyin' lessons from a tripodero.
'Course, furthest they ever got was the other side o' the creek! Haha!
Now go on and tell me some more 'bout those "shortwaves" and "bouncy signals"—yer guide'll find just the spot for ya!
Double-time now! I don't wanna see no more nasty surprises!
She has no part in this operation.
So you have other plans for her? She's quite durable—a useful "piece" indeed.
Yes, she's brought many interesting whispers from the dark, hasn't she?
It's a pity moths don't last long in the rain.
I've already passed the ritual intelligence on to Vertin. They'll need her assistance to reach it.
Just "Moth" alone? Please, allow me to deploy an elite squad to assist.
Your team's never made contact with the Timekeeper before, have they?
Heh ... she always has preferred a softer touch.
That won't be necessary. This isn't combat—some doors require only a light touch to open.
And our moth needs a light to fly to.
This will likely be her final delivery.

Mr. Forget Me Not entrusted me to deliver the Fountain of Youth to the sanctuary and to assist you with the ritual preparations. This is my first time having the honor to enter this holy place, Apostle Animus.
Oh? So the "ever-noble" Mr. Forget Me Not deigns himself above such tasks now, does he?
It's not my place to question his affairs, Lady Apostle.
... But when I last saw him, his condition was concerning.
*scoff* More likely the result of incompetence than the price of brewing the immortality elixir.

This was his most sacred charge. No matter his state, he ought to have crawled back to the sanctuary himself and groveled at the Mother of Resurrection's feet. To eschew pilgrimage over mere flesh wounds ...
I see you wear no mask. Don't tell me he sent an untested follower to deliver ritual materials?
I've pledged my faith to the Inculcator of Arcanum, Lady Apostle. I am blessed.
You ARE an apostle. Pft. First that red-haired fraud, and now a near-total stranger! How many more vermin must the Mother of Resurrection's gifts be squandered on?
No matter. I do not expect the likes of you to contribute anything meaningful to the ritual.
You'll follow my orders. Whatever title Forget Me Not gave you, remember who rules this sanctuary.
As you will it, Apostle Animus.
Ms. Sophia ... You can't build a faith on hatred.
You and Vertin—you've witnessed the phenomenal world shatter time and again, have you not? Tell me, how do you navigate the Emanation?
We shelter who we can. The Timekeeper—the Foundation—took in Regulus, 37, and many others. Ms. Sophia, you—
And yet you must let go of kin and friends, treading over the corpses of untold more besides. You turn a blind eye to the suffering wrought by the "wheel of birth" ...
Because your little ark is simply too small to carry them all.
We ... Manus Vindictae is not the answer! They only bring more suffering! More strife!
Is that not the world's true face?
... The wise reach the far shore, the lucky gasp for air as they cling to whatever they can find, and the rest struggle in the whirlpool below.
The Manus are killers! Do you really want to drag even more people into that whirlpool?!
Even if no hand disturbs the sand, the tide will eventually rise to erase all marks. Or have you found another answer?
"The fragility and impermanence of sand is precisely why people strive for something eternal" ...
Sacrifice is agony, yes, but I and those beside me walk this path because it is the right one.
... I see you've already made up your mind.
Let's see how these "geniuses" handle the "Storm."
Don't worry, a beating won't hurt much—after all, you're just a pawn now.
This is only a drill—remember your real objective here! They're not actual lives ...
Good. Strict adherence to protocol is the fastest way to "crack" the code.
Seems you've completely forgotten the Laplace Emergency Protocol for the "Storm."
Laplace simulating Laplace. Eccentrics imagining eccentrics.
Staying in the box might be no different from being outside—both endure the "Storm" again and again.
My advice? Actually use that ferrofluid floating around in your tank and think harder. Don't be stupid.
If you can prove it'll be safe after it's unlocked, I'll lend a hand.
And how exactly could one prove such a thing BEFORE they unlock it? Researcher Adler, since when has Laplace opted to employ such elementary paradoxes against its employees?
Don't touch what you shouldn't. You should know that by now, after all the years you've spent here.
But if we followed that rule, we never would've raised our umbrellas against the "Storm" now, would we?
... If I told you what was down there, would you be able to walk away?
Hypothetical answers demand verification. You know this better than I.
If you crack the combination, you'll find—nothing?
Every second counts, Adler. We never know when the next "Storm" might hit. Time has never been our ally.
Besides, this isn't your lab. Disputes require votes under emergency protocols.
Majority rule? You forget those opposing you aren't just statistics. I, for one, have always been in the dissenting minority.
Someone has to play devil's advocate.
I'll honor the committee's decision. At least we can agree on that.
Regardless of the outcome, when Musae III complains, at least I won't be called your accomplice.
Also, why do alarms always come with Critters?! Is that some kind of rule?
We'll settle this at the vote. But remember that opposition is always a valid choice. Those against you aren't just statistics on a sheet.
Wise choice. Now bury the sandbox, turn around, and focus on your project.
Where are your scientific ethics? You're a disgrace to the title "Researcher"!
That's not ethics—that's the curiosity that kills lab cats.
From my perspective, our research outweighs aiding these randomly generated pieces.
Agreed, Researcher Adler. But this is also a chance to demonstrate Laplace's humanity.
I've had enough complaint letters accusing my humanitarian efforts of being exploitation in disguise.
Fine. You'll receive another one soon enough.
Hey Ulrich, were people complaining about you again? Was it for making them work non-stop? Or forcing them to drink coffee every four hours?
Neither. This time, he's obsessively caring for people he thinks need help while completely ignoring the true objectives.
Humanity? Compassion? Are you sure we're talking about Ulrich? Not some ... uh, other ferrofluid in a glass jar?
Oh, sorry. I didn't mean to interrupt your research. I'm just here to submit last month's budget report. Carry on.
Right, the "Storm." This little toybox is about to change all your pieces into grinning, wide-eyed Critters with an approaching "Storm."

And here you are still busying yourself with a pawn—who, after being reset so many times, has finally started to realize that something is wrong with this world—in an attempt to find a solution to the "Storm."
I believe it could be a route to finding a solution.
Listen, Ulrich, what we need to do right now is finish this emergency manual so when the real "Storm" hits, we can minimize the damage.
Instead of doing what you're supposed to and studying this damn box to find ways to stop the rain, you're happy to loaf around and listen to them sing praises over your "humanitarian spirit."
If you really care about "humanity," then why aren't you listening to the growing voices of dissent?
You're gonna get even more complaints than me the way you're at each other's throats.
We're just having a civilized debate.
Not sure a "civilized" debate ends in one party yelling at the other in their mother tongue.
Anyway, I didn't come here to watch you argue. I was just, uh, passing by to submit our budget report.
Did you have fun on your little trip? Maybe you should transfer to the Foundation's dispatch team. Then you could do something in every pre-"Storm" window.
And you can focus on saving everyone you want to save instead of hyper-fixating on your half-baked compassion here.
But the truth is right in front of us.
Ha, why don't you move instead? Anyway, keep it down. Next time, I might have to join in too.
It's one of my few sources of entertainment.
I never knew you had this side to you, Ulrich.
Ahem ... At least the real APPLe doesn't know about this.
Stop provoking those hooligans. I never knew you were so belligerent.
I doubt anyone actually buys her nonsense.
Our brilliant cryptography lead is so linguistically gifted that he can now communicate with animals.
I might need to reevaluate your professional competence.
Congratulations—you actually kept your head clear.
Be glad you've always worked at Laplace.
A soldier and an Awakened attacking a whole camp? Ha!
A mathematics game from the East.
This simulation box has certainly made you bold.
Is this some special brand of humor?
Why isn't the defendant Medicine Pocket?
If you're this "kind" to every simulated character, this simulation won't last long.
This is obviously a trap. You should know ... Scheiße, fine.
A mysterious ore, gently nestled in clay. Used in Insight and Resonance rituals for characters. Also usable as a material for crafting advanced materials.
Electricity pulses through him as he notes calculations on the scratch paper. Climbing a mountain is no more difficult than deciphering the Voynich manuscript.
If you want to be a fluffy Robin Hood of the city, you better prepare your paws for scorching summer asphalt.
"Is the abyss scary? Yes, it is." The girl answers her own question, "But, no matter what, I'll keep heading into it. Because that's where my answer lies."
There is no way back, child. Let the pain push you forward, and do not be afraid, for there will always be someone by your side.

Down, down, descend the stair,
Step down, I say, to the devil's lair.

The mad often speak the truth.
I strain my eyes into the abyss, but darkness is all I see.
All she wants, is to stand in the light forever

Go and seek the Golden Fleece. In the land of endless peace.
Blood and tears become one, as she weeps in the dark.
When, with blood, the disordered threads are soothed, fate shall reclaim what was once eschewed.
The flood of time will take us all, but pray, let me find my own stream.
The Other Bank of the River
Go to the other ferry, back to the mouth of the River Tiber.
On the never-ending relentless march through time, the future will come again.

The promised flood has come, submerging birds and fish in the past.
Yet the silent and steadfast wade into the tide,
Moving upstream toward answers and the future.

At the path's end lies only emptiness—
The river bends back, yielding to old memories.
Yet still, my friend, we keep on marching forward.

"No, there was a woman's voice spelling letters, but it made no sense. MYDA, SEVA ... She also said something quite creepy." "Did you record it?" "Only got a few clips. Here, listen." "Mike, Yankee, Delta, Alpha ... *static noise*" "Sierra, Echo ... Victor, Abandon ... I'm the only one left ... Am I really the only one? No, I-I can't give up, no ... *static noise* Run away!" The First Tale When he arrived in this world, the child received the Mother Spirit's first blessing. He stopped crying as a sunbeam fell on the pillow. Through his tears, he saw Her gifts: golden rays warming his hands, white cloths softly swaddling his body, and fresh air breezing into his lungs. A single life is all we are given; thus, the Mother Spirit taught the child to cherish. The Third Tale The child gripped a bow, leaving deep footprints in the snow. It was his day to hunt. But this land hadn't seen any trace of birds or squirrels for ages. The long-absent spring was growing fainter with every passing year like a distant myth. Finally, the child took down a doe just before sunset. Closing those watery eyes glowing with innocence, his weary hands shakily splitting the flesh, he recognized that this was the Mother Spirit's second blessing. Staring at the frozen, fragile branches, the child knew it was time to go south. The Seventh Tale The sun fell into the moss-covered plains, its once eternal fire frozen by the ice. Fish drowned in the waters, sinking to the riverbeds where they transmuted into swords. Coffins creaked open. Shriveled fingers clawed at passersby, seeking redemption. The child trudged across the land, his blood and cotton wool forming scabs over the surface of his skin. His fingertips, first ravaged by chilblains, were then abraded by hoes and pickaxes. Only his vocal cords remained alive to pray to the Mother Spirit. Please rewrite the laws of this world. Please grant us a new spring. The Ninth Tale The lost child received the Mother Spirit's third blessing. In the farthest south, the child passed through the Mother Spirit's body and knocked upon the gate to Her soul. A sense of warmth he hadn't felt for a long time enveloped him, making him Her child once again. Cradled in the Mother Spirit's arms, he heard the last message. Many, many years later, when the earth was again dotted with trees and flowers, the child's children sat around the campfire, begging for tales of the Mother Spirit. "I embraced Her and She enlightened me. That was a great gift," he said, "Her great gift."

The early 20th century—the glorious age after the Second Industrial Revolution. Electricity, new technology, a complete system of knowledge—and a fire to "turn the world upside down."

In 1909, an American explorer cut through the sea ice at the North Pole, giving the hesitant a firm slap on the back: Get going, dreamers ... conquer the unknown! Dig through every inch of snow, and carve your name into the bones of the Jurassic!

From Ushuaia, from Sydney, from Wales, from Bergen—teams raced toward the last uncharted continent.

One after another, they braved the wind and snow, planted flags at the South Pole, charted every edge, and declared human sovereignty over the outermost frontiers.

And from the bottom of the earth, they shouted together, "We have solved the last mystery!"

A well-used notebook, stuffed with receipts, stubs, and coupons. "Things to do once I've saved up!" ① Trip to Kangaroo Island. I need rest, rest, lots of rest! I gotta forget that fast-food kitchen ... the spilled sauces and those endless dishes! ② Ride a hot air balloon. Honestly, I've always wanted to see the city from above. I rush around every day looking for work, but never actually see it—maybe up there, I'll finally have the chance! Note: Don't forget Plappy!

A child once claimed to have had a dream like this.
In the dream, there was a real yet bizarre little town, filled with twisted, fantastical buildings that came together like an endless labyrinth.
As he tried to escape, he met other children in the same situation. They spent forever searching, but could never find the way out. When the stars and moon rose, the last of their strength had left them.
Then, from down the road, came a melody.
"I wanted to know who could play music that beautiful, so I walked over ... but I only saw a white corner of a robe and a giant rabbit—how strange! Why was it so big?"
"We followed the music, and somehow we really made it out—it's so bizarre! I think a kind bard found us and led us out of the maze."

On a bustling street in Munich, she rode a penny-farthing for the first time. The oversized wheel was hard to control, leaving crooked tracks in her wake.
But mastering this old-fashioned device wasn't so hard ... it only took a little practice.
Gears clicked precisely. The evening breeze brushed her cheek. Gazing into the golden dusk, she forgot the sound of rain for a moment—the rain yet to come, the rain already gone, the rain that always kept her on edge.
This was a stable new world. The family gem on her chest no longer weighed on her thoughts. She gave a faint smile.
Maybe one day, everyone will be free to ride the streets with her. And sunlight will fall as if the rain never existed.

A river connects all friends. Passing old ones, meeting new ones ...
"So, the farther I go, the more friends I'll make." Under the clear moonlight, a girl hugged her pillow, counting fingers, murmuring, "I have to remind them—the ground beneath the bed isn't a lawn, it's water. When we talk, tie down the anchor, or the bed will float away ..."
Moonlight sparkled across the river, brushing her cheeks. She slowly closed her eyes.
"And when rowing, paddle from one side only ... then I can spin in place and make up a story about a river fairy."
The waters keep flowing, carrying a curious heart and a new dream.

Faster, higher, further, rock climbs into the stratosphere!
"The days of braving open seas to dodge capture are over! The great Captain Regulus declares a new golden age of music! World tour routes, 3,000 feet in the air. We will soar to new heights! Our one and only mission; to share the glory of rock'n'roll with the world ... A music festival in the sky AND on land ... dig it! The highest-altitude concert in history!"
*ahem* "APPLe completely understands how the Captain feels. Still, it may be best to keep the music down at night. Even if there's no police presence in suitcase, the folks here are sometimes more dangerous than any old copper."

Samba comes from Bahia, Brazil. It's warm, cheerful, and full of life.
"Samba Sphere" includes several classic samba songs. Sputnik loves the rhythm and bounce. So she bought a samba outfit based on the game's cover art—where a cartoon monkey wears samba clothes.
She's still spinning nonstop in the disco hall. Even in San Francisco, you can feel that East Atlantic Brazilian vibe.

Punch, kick! Roll, counter! Win—or go again! Fighting games offer a different kind of freedom from real life.
"Super Warrior: Howls in the Night" leads the genre. Even when they're outside of the arcade, fans mimic their every move, and the characters' outfits have become a trending fashion. If you don't know about them, you're out of the loop.
But not all trendsetters know the game inside out. "Because I fit the role" is reason enough ... quick reflexes, playful attitude, and the pay's good too. If the cosplayer suits the role, sometimes the role suits the cosplayer just as well.
"Catgirl! Catgirl Niruya, over here!" With a shout, the girl hopped onto a rooftop, chasing two colorful butterflies, disappearing down the other side.

"Giga Girl! Brave hero of justice, Giga Girl!"
This was gaming's golden age. When video game heroes were kids' idols. Top of the charts: Digi-Hero Giga Girl.
"She can leap 10 meters in a single bound! Charge up her fists for a lightning punch! Giga Girl's awesome—I wanna be just like her!"
At Laplace, the staff decided to perform a Christmas miracle. Old toaster ovens became metallic helmets. Vacuum tubes became transforming gloves. They even used secret tech to build real rocket backpacks. Turns out, most researchers are just kids at heart.
When the child put on the gear she'd wished for, her favorite digital hero stepped into the real world.

In the late 20th century, the hit series "Private Detective" launched a new game: Mystery Numbers. Fresh arcade cabinets popped up everywhere, sparking conversation across town.
"Hey, guess what? I saw the real 'Mystery Man'!"
Rumors spread about a visitor to a particular Aegean island. He looked just like the game's star: a tan trench coat, a metallic mask, a hidden past, and a name marked by a single letter.
According to an anonymous Foundation employee, someone suggested he clear up the rumors—but he refused. That refusal only added to the mystique, just like the original game. To this day, this "urban legend" is still a fan favorite.

TTT is wondering why people run the moment they see her.
She doesn't think she looks scary, so it must be something else that's startling them. Why do horror movies always use TVs as a motif?
Maybe it's because there's a type of character that can naturally appear on-screen, talk to whoever's on the other side, and not raise any alarm.
A weather reporter? A shopping channel host? Or maybe she could pretend to be a super hacker?
As she trails along the wires, a video order system at a drive-in diner catches her eye.
"This is it! A drive-in diner server! Friendly pink uniform, roller skates weaving through parked cars, decadent desserts, and always serving from the other side of the glass!"
"I'll have a Big Max."
"One extra-large milkshake."
"A Big Max, no mayo."
Well, at least this time, no one is running away screaming.

"You want me to act in a local tourism promo? Sorry, my weekends are fully booked."
The girl waves politely, smiling as she turns down the eager talent scout, just like she always does. But then she calls out to the retreating figure.
"Wait ... there's a party I might be able to cancel."
She reaches into her bag and grabs her dream-filled notebook. Maybe it's time to make better use of opportunities that fall into her lap. "Fine, I'll model and act. But I'll be directing and editing it myself. Deal?"
Grindhouse, mill films, B-horror flicks ... she adores them all. But she's never been satisfied just playing the pretty, textbook girl in front of the lens. Maybe this is her shot to shatter the cliché.

What makes a good hat? Size. A big hat keeps the sun and dust off your face, and in rough terrain, it even helps protect your head.
What makes a good pair of boots? Size again. Thick soles make the worst trails feel like sidewalks. Heavy leather keeps in heat and blocks out the cold. Tall heels lock into stirrups, and wide shafts shield your legs.
Big hat. Big boots. Big catchphrase. A trusty horse named Silver. Congratulations, now you're a true Lone Rider.
"I think I get the message behind this ad. The Lone Rider is mature, stoic ... and driven by a sense of justice for all. That's what makes the character shine."
The director's eyes light up.
"This kid was born to play a cowboy!"

"You're all top psychiatrists at this facility, what's your read on the patient's condition?"
"Based on her case history, I'd recommend a more conservative approach. A relaxed environment where she feels free—ideally tied to something familiar—might help stabilize her."
"What about jazz? The era matches hers, it's broad and diverse, and the lyrics are improvised. With all those rhythms guiding her, she could sing freely, without rules. That might help her reconnect with herself."
"I'll contact the Foundation branches in Chicago and Austin. They'll coordinate the logistics. We'll need to assign someone to accompany her. Let the winds of the Windy City carry her, and maybe she can enjoy some Texas bluebonnets along the way."

January 21st, Copacabana. Crowded.
I ... don't like summer. Never liked the beach either. There are always so many beautiful girls there. Seeing them makes me think about my freckles ... my crooked knee. Maybe, I should just keep it covered up ...

February 3rd, overcast. Still crowded.
A new sheet! Or ... I guess it's a beach towel? It's a bit short, might not cover my leg. But who left this towel here? Did someone give it to me? It's nice, though I think the pattern's too eye-catching ...

February 9th, clear skies. People didn't leave until after midnight.
While I'm wearing that towel, I almost feel like ... I'm one of those girls. It's strange.
Sometimes the tide brushes against my leg. It softens in the water. Maybe it likes that wet, weightless feeling ... Should I try something bolder ...?

A crumpled application form. Application: Ma'am, thank you for this opportunity ... but I was just doing my job. I really don't deserve to be invited to the Rio de Janeiro branch for a special presentation ... Processing Note: Investigator Marcus, no need to worry. The Rio branch has already prepared a grand beach party for you. Application: A beach party ...? Uh, ma'am ... I might need some time to mentally prepare ... Final Decision: You've been reading books about beaches and seashells lately, haven't you? Aren't you at all curious what those shells look like in person? At Copacabana, you can study them up close. Maybe even do a bit of crafting. Don't worry, it's a vacation. Application: Alright ... Ma'am, I'll do my best!

"I think I've found a new Fibonacci sequence! On the way to the spring, I came across a strange flower the locals call a sunflower. Its head holds two spiral patterns, coiling in opposite directions, perfectly interlaced."
"And not just sunflowers; I saw it in cacti, and even typhoons. It's a whole new form. The phenomenal world has so many ways to express the same principle."
"Eventually, everything in the phenomenal world fades. No matter how its appearance shifts, its core remains the same—time. That means all phenomena are finite ... even my little jar. But for now, the sequence exists perfectly in these flower heads. That's the wonder of the phenomenal world: even in its limits, it never stops showing us more possibilities."

In the early 20th century, Manaus flourished thanks to rubber. Workers tapped the trees, trading milky-white sap for gold. Their wishes came true. Wealth flowed in from the forest along the Amazon. Labor brought harvest, and finally, the children at home no longer had to go hungry.
Along with the riches come tourists by the thousands. They come to marvel at the miracles of the rainforest: pink dolphins, macaws, and whispered tales of the Curupira.
An expedition truck imported from distant Punjab rolls into the jungle.The explorers find jaguar tracks in the swamp, study the patterns on its fur, watch how gracefully it hunts. They narrowly escape a python's belly, slipping free with a flash of quick thinking.
The forest looks on in silence, just as it has always done.

A weathered glass bottle, clearly used.
Record: Collected from the Oka River during the spring flood. At this time of year, the water is thick with voices. Even if you submerge completely, you won't find any clear direction ... Too much listening leads to delirium and confusion.

A brand-new pot, its rim decorated with patterns typical of Marajó Island.
Record: Collected north of Marajó. The road there is winding, but full of surprises. The forest canopy blocks out the sky, and inside live all sorts of wondrous creatures—brightly colored parrots, birds with massive beaks, and herds of water buffalo ... The flowing water here always points its direction clearly. It makes you think of loud, passionate things. In St. Petersburg, you'd rarely find water like this.

Colors mean different things to different cultures.
Rio de Janeiro is a city painted in bold strokes. People travel across the world just to see it for themselves. The locals love bright colors because they're full of life. They remind people that it's still worth hoping for better days.
"Where I'm from, in Rayashki, purple used to mean nobility and dignity. In the pre-industrial age, its main source was the juice of murex snails, rare and difficult to extract. So it became a privilege of the old aristocracy. But here, purple often symbolizes sorrow. And when paired with yellow, it's considered a bad omen."
"Only red is the exception. In our culture, red almost always stands for one thing: unwavering courage and passion."

A FIERY DUEL
A dueling event where contestants must choose certain fragile items as weapons. Each item must be between 4 and 30 inches long. Grip style is up to the contestant.
During the match, only these weapons may be used to strike. Anything else counts as a foul. Valid hit zone: torso (above the belt). Points are awarded for hits. Highest score wins; bonus if your item doesn't break.

Note: Contestants may not distract each other through gestures or speech that causes blushing or shyness.
Addendum: Dating your opponent after the match is also forbidden!

In the late 18th century, Winged Key Archery became an official event in the Uluru Games.
It all began with an arcane artefact: the Winged Key. Its instinct to seek out keyholes caused all kinds of unnecessary trouble. First played in Yorkshire over a wager. An Arcanist claimed he could, in the split second before the key reached the lock, fire a silver arrow through its hole and pin it to the door.
To test their skill, ten keys and ten locks were prepared. The game was on. Though the Arcanist only managed to hit one rusty key and lost spectacularly, the game nonetheless became a popular pastime, and it's been played ever since.

"This journey is by invitation only." Route: Easter Island–Bermuda–Atlantis Easter Island: An island stuck in the past, with no future. Civilization left behind wonders on its soil. Boarding note: For your safety, do not speak to the crew without permission. Bermuda: The birthplace of countless legends. Experience a firsthand miracle among its infamous tales. Boarding note: If you hear anything late at night near Dance Floor C, don't panic. The crew often host midnight shows; it seems they had a love for karaoke ... back when they were alive. Atlantis: Final stop: Poseidonia, the crown jewel of the Atlantic. Boarding note: Do not feed the crew. The cruise will not be liable for the consequences of failing to heed this warning! The dance floor on Deck C is packed from wall to wall.
Disco music kicks in, and the spotlight lights up the center. It's showtime.
Smoke drifts from a jellyfish-shaped censer, dancing to the girl's gestures, shifting into strange and wondrous shapes.
The crowd watches, silent, until the performance ends.
There is no applause.
"... I saw my mother," one woman mutters blankly. "She left me when I was just a child ... I never expected to see her again ... let alone like that ..."
"If my son had lived ... I think he'd look just like that now," says an old man, voice trembling.
The audience are lost in thought. Onstage, the girl snuffs out the censer. Her figure fading away with the smoke.
"A kind of healing. That's what travel is for." That is the girl's answer when the salon host asks her why she performs.

Everything here is different from what she once knew.
The masts tower like ancient trees, and every undercurrent feels like the breath of some beast. But that's fine. A skilled hunter adapts to any terrain. And she has her shotgun. Passed down from her mother's mother, now it rests in the hands of the last daughter standing.
Night falls. The velvet sky begins to drop. Lights dim, the noise fades. She's finished her shift, but doesn't head to her quarters. The night isn't over yet.
She picks up the silver "umbrella" and looks up at the full moon overhead.

A late-night salon. The hostess speaks with her guests.
"Doctor, how do you do it?" A young woman leans forward, curious. "I didn't say a word, yet you seem to know everything about me ... as if you've been beside me all along."
"All outward signs," the hostess replies, "are part of who you are. I only say what I see."
Before her words finish echoing, an older woman can't help but voice another question. She's been holding it back, clearly, for some time.
And so, the salon gives way to another flowing, layered conversation, peppered with the occasional quiet laugh.
Every seemingly random dream is shown to have a meaning far beyond imagination. Reflected in art, it could be a gecko on a clock, a lobster on a telephone, or a green apple suspended in front of your eyes.
Restrained and professional. Typical Laplace dress code.
Chaotic and desperate. Typical Laplace working style.
Go and explore, for the snowfields are out there.
Go and pursue, for the "unknown" is out there.
She had her doubts, but for the sake of the majority, she remained silent.
The only way through is forward; there is no turning back.
On the scales of life, there lie pinecones at one end and acorns on the other.
Sometimes, a well-ended adventure tastes sweeter than any nut.
I am willing to be the pioneer.

The wise man declares, "A circle is perfection." The world laughs, "So is an ellipse."
At the ideal starting point—of creation, of vision, of victory!

A handwritten manuscript, unsigned
"Hmm ... I've never actually raised an animal before, but if I want to be a knight, I'll be needing a horse. A good horse can do a lot, it can break through encirclements, improves speed (though I don't have much need of that; for me, wandering is part of both life and writing) ... More importantly, I'd have another reader. Horses are sensitive creatures. I could read my drafts to it!"
<a section scribbled out>
"I've decided to name her Bernardah. That's a good name. Every time I read her a new story, she gently nudges my hand with her damp nose, just like when she's asking for more alfalfa."
Weightless among the ruins of the past, falling becomes the way forward.

A performance log, recorded by a circus member

"She'd never performed on top of a castle before. The situation was far worse than we'd expected ... Years of sun and wind had left the bricks brittle. The cracks were filled with yellowed root systems, roots that somehow acted like glue, just enough to hold the whole thing together."
...
"When I told her all of this, our little trapezist became even more set on performing. I asked her why. She didn't answer. She just looked toward the castle's battlements, where a tiny flag was fluttering."
...
"The castle stood there, almost merging with the sky. I followed her gaze. The top of the castle was higher than any height she'd performed from before, like a sword piercing the clouds. Is that what had her so entranced?"
A crown can't be split, so we crowned another.

An old diary, written by two hands with near identically clumsy handwriting
April 27
Today Dad gave me a birthday present. A chess set. I love it!
Today Dad gave me a birthday present. A chess set. I love it! But Lisa, do you even know how to play chess?
That doesn't matter! Louis, it's just a game, just like all the others we used to play!

April 29
Lisa won!
Louis won too! I love my friends. This way, I get double the joy!

April 30
Lisa got a gift from Louis! A queen's crown!
Louis got a gift from Lisa! A king's crown! Lisa picked it out herself. Louis loves it!

Three sisters make their home in the wilderness. Known as the greatest of "sculptors." Their garden is filled with stone figures so lifelike that they could humble even Pheidias himself. Though rumors persist about petrification spells being the true secret to their art.
The youngest of the Gorgon sisters is deeply loved by the older two. During springtime, she patiently untangles her sisters' serpentine locks by the babbling brook. Managing living hair proves challenging when each strand fights back. All in preparation for their "Rite of Spring" dance, where those same snakes help by counting out the beat with their hiss, keeping each movement of their performance perfectly in time.
As Medusa's head went flying through the air, her last thoughts may well have drifted back to one of those spring days.
Hissabeth will never know. But she finds some peace in knowing her own head is still where it belongs.

The ocean's daughters live on a barren stone island, untouched by human hands.
To fill their endless days, they sing with voices that captivate all living creatures. Though people call these haunting voices dangerous, the sirens pay no mind. After all, they have seen and braved all the perils of the sea.
When Vila enters their world for the first time, curious eyes follow her every movement. With voices shaped into a perfect harmony, the sirens invite her to share a song from Rayashki.
She sings a song unlike anything they've heard before—mightier than any storm. One by one, their voices join hers until their little island resonates with an impromptu choir.

"Why did Orpheus look back?"
No one can truly say, and the question remains unresolved. Marcus has spent a great deal of time trying to understand it.
"In The Symposium, Phaedrus sees him as someone who held back from loving completely. In contrast, Georgics paints a picture of the gods using him for their own entertainment. He managed something no other mortal had, yet still couldn't avoid the path laid out for him. Maybe what we call free will might really be the very thing that locks us into fate."
"Some say he turned because of his longing for his love. Others think he was caught up in his own vision of romance ... I still can't decide which makes more sense."
"But think about it. If you suddenly heard the voice of someone you lost, how could you not turn around? Whether it was a friend from the orphanage, a ghost from the Flannan Isles, or someone like Madam Hofmann ... who could truly keep walking without looking back?"

This is the season of abundance.
Ears of golden wheat bend low, soon to meet the farmer's scythe. Across the fields, a river of browning husks flows toward the horizon where it meets the soft blue of the evening sky.
The earth is the first mother of us all. She feeds everything that lives, her rivers marking lines across her surface like gentle wrinkles, and her hills forming the graceful curves of her lips. Pomegranate trees sink their roots deep into her soil and grow strong with life.
Eternity follows this golden trail. She bends to collect brightly colored stones from the sandy soil, astonished to discover such breathtaking beauty. This kind land offers more than gold and minerals. It gives every creature a place of calm and belonging.

What kind of influence could an apple really have?
Some tales speak of it as the fruit that grew on a tree of knowledge, offering wisdom to humankind. In other myths, it stands as the most iconic symbol of Eden, said to create illusions and shape human thought. It is believed to hold the accumulated wisdom of ancient scholars, opening doors for future generations—though a few have used that same knowledge to bring about catastrophes.
"Naturally," Mr. APPLe concludes, "this APPLe believes such stories are nothing more than rumors. In daily life, apples are perfectly harmless. Our qualities are limited to being refreshingly juicy and reasonably knowledgeable, and that is all there is to it."

Mr. APPLe and Jiu Niangzi get into a deep discussion about the winemaking process, which—unexpectedly—draws Mr. Duncan's attention. Suddenly, Lilya appears out of nowhere, volunteering to be the first taste tester of the final product.

Buddy Fairchild and Pickles enter into an increasingly deep conversation about melting glaciers in Antarctica. By the end of it, they both agree that global warming is a far more urgent issue than agonizing over the philosophical debates about nihilism.
During Willow's check-up at the Laplace Rehab Center, Mesmer Jr. steps in to help, going through the entire process without saying a single word to each other.

After tasting the chili sauce from Liang Yue's homeland, Centurion becomes completely hooked. She offers a lot of money for the recipe but gets turned down, so she decides to travel abroad to find out how it's made.

Ulrich's attention is continually taken by the presence of a fly that no one else can see. It is only after a heavy rain cleans his glass tank that he realizes that it was just an illusion the entire time.
After losing the speed contest against Nautika, Darley Clatter promises to share his prized carrot supplies with Nautika in recognition of her victory.
Avgust's stories about his homeland deeply move Moldir, filling her with sadness and respect for people she has never met before.
As Marcus lies down to sleep, her mind is flooded with the formatting errors in the report she turned in, keeping her awake until morning.
Pioneer reveals a new suit tailored especially for Mr. Duncan, and as they began the fitting process, Ms. Sotheby walks in. A familiar name begins forming on her lips before she catches herself.
When Loggerhead goes to Aleph with a question about how to preserve long-term memories, she receives only silence in response.
An-an Lee and Horropedia share their honest thoughts on Blonney's latest experimental thriller. The next day, all their popcorn is gone, with only a few strands of deer hair left behind.
Shamane carefully carves a piece of wood into what resembles Jiu Niangzi's wooden doll. But despite his best efforts, she immediately sees that it's just a lifeless copy.
Regulus volunteers to test-drive the jet-powered wheelchair X designed for Noire. Afterwards, doctors at the Laplace Rehabilitation Center note that a rare "one of two cases medical incident."
At Eternity's grand dinner party, J isn't allowed in because of his casual clothes. He only gets through the door after borrowing a tie from Pioneer to match the dress code.
Lucy, looking around and seeing that every charging port in the Suitcase is taken, longingly thinks of all the unused chargers sitting back at Laplace.
Flutterpage asks Oliver Fog to borrow an umbrella for another try at testing her umbrella-parachute idea.
Pioneer suggests some nice-looking quick-dry bedsheets to Poltergeist, but Poltergeist politely turns him down because the sheets don't have the right "eyeholes" in the exact places she wants.
Melania and Kanjira become good friends after competing to secretly grab the last Dr. Papper from the fridge.
At Buddy Fairchild's request, Click takes a photo of him with his penguin squad. In return, Buddy gives Click his stash of age-old nuts, which might not taste very good anymore.
The group of "gourmets" living inside the Suitcase all agree that Ezra's homegrown edible mushrooms are especially delicious.
Thanks to Mercuria's suggestion, Barcarola gets introduced to "disco music." As soon as Mercuria starts dancing, Barcarola picks up her instrument and joins in without hesitation.
Argus loses badly in a bet with Centurion and has to hand over ten full jars of Picrasma Candy as the agreed payment.
Heavy rain leaves Hissabeth's snake siblings with colds. She loses sleep due to their constant sneezing.
At a charity auction dinner, Sotheby buys a field investigator's last rusted bullet, paying ten grams of gold for it.
The gentle sound of Getian's flute playing falls from high in the trees, drawing the attention of both Rabies and a flock of birds. They gather below, curious about this unusual music.
Thanks to X's latest adjustments, Pickles's translation device can now fully understand social situations. For example: "The user is making friendly but meaningless sounds."
Though Fatutu, who was personally trained by Regulus, scores the highest in the motorcycle safety test, her mentor shows no sign of pride.
Liang Yue plays a ping-pong match against Madam Z, losing by just a small margin. As the others leave, the two stay behind to keep practicing until the sports hall shuts down for the night.
After watching J's forging techniques, A Knight presents his sword. Holding it in silence, J sighs and finally admits that his own skills could never create such an indestructible weapon.
Though Avgust wins Buddy Fairchild's sledding contest, the real winner is Pickles, who gets his prize: a full crate of heavy canned dog food.

While doing research in the library, Tennant comes across records showing that the Tavernier family once owned a very rare gemstone. She stays up all night going through the archives to try and track it down, but her search turns up nothing.
In a conversation about death and destruction, Necrologist and Charon both agree on one thing—they both represent the beginning and the end.
Dikke and Sentinel end up in a disagreement after a discussion on "punishment"—which shows how differently they see the topic.

Ms. NewBabel's Critter Rehab Center launches a new type of food for domesticated Critters and places test samples inside the Suitcase. That night, Regulus and Buddy Fairchild accidentally try the product without reading the label and give positive reviews.
Charon notices that Poltergeist's clothing style closely matches his own, but maintains proper boundaries by not inquiring about it, while Poltergeist equally chooses to remain silent on the matter.
La Source helps Druvis III water the trees and feels a rare happiness in making someone else's wish come true.
In her efforts to maintain order among the children in the Suitcase, Eagle takes on the role of "captain." She's so effective that the nighttime fridge raids are put to an end.
After Bunny Bunny compliments the farm's cows, the nearby aliEn T becomes unusually curious.
After once again comparing battery charging speeds, power stability, wear rate, and storage methods, Lucy weighs on their pros and cons before deciding to stick with the batteries she has.

After going through friendly discussions and "negotiations," TTT decides to satisfy everyone's demands by setting up four TVs to play children's programs, news, documentaries, and commercials all at once. The result is everyone watching in eerie silence as the noise has become too chaotic for anyone to hear anything clearly.
Pioneer easily takes first place in the "red light, green light" game without any effort.
​Windsong and Kaalaa Baunaa find common ground in their study of ley lines and astronomy and decide to write a research paper together. Windsong quietly hopes their paper won't be rejected.
Click shows the battlefield photos he took, and Charon touches them gently, as if he can still smell the sulfur and earth in the pictures.
After hearing Charon's story, Diggers gives him a gerbera daisy.
With encouragement from Dikke, Cristallo joins the children's soccer game inside the Suitcase—as a fair referee.
Sentinel pulls out her last sealed military ration from her pocket. She takes one bite before drinking four or five mouthfuls of water.
At dusk, Fatutu meets 37 on the beach. After talking, they decide to take a walk on the beach together. When they make a pinky promise, both remember many things about the beach.
Loggerhead forgets to set the oven timer correctly, which causes thick smoke to fill the kitchen. Bunny Bunny then gives her a long-term"kitchen ban."
Sweetheart agrees to star in Blonney and Loggerhead's new film. Even though it's unpaid, she enjoys acting in the absurd horror movie.
As Matilda describes the scene, Sentinel slowly rebuilds the image of Place Saint-Michel in her mind and starts to miss the cafés there.
After enjoying dozens of days in the sun, Flutterpage gets a healthy tan and creates a deeper bond with Leilani.
Anjo Nala gives up on cooking after burning her fifth chicken, simply because she can't take another bite.
Following a deep conversation under the stars, Desert Flannel offers Sputnik a part-time role she'd been considering.
Because of a clock malfunction, Oliver Fog leaves work 2 minutes later than usual. He carefully records the time as evidence for use in future time-off claims.
After tasting sushi made by Satsuki, An-an Lee comes up with a creative fusion idea that mixes in roast goose flavors.
During the rainy season, Sonetto picked up and helped an injured frog. When she lets it go, she notices that her hands no longer shake like they did in the past.
On this day in 1959, the Antarctic Treaty was signed. "Fluffy Duke," "Scarlet Titan," and "Brother Jake" are always in high spirits on this day.
Charlie played both Napoleon and Napoleon III on stage, both of whom were crowned on this historic date.
In December 1910, neon signs made their commercial debut. It would take another half-century before mirrored disco balls lit up the night.
Windsong could never thank Sotheby enough for her nutrient potion "Lady No. 500," which kept her going through the long winter field survey.
In 1930, All Quiet on the Western Front was released. Many years later, Charon sat alone in Noire's screening room and watched it in stoic silence.
In 1957, Vanguard TV-3 managed a heroic 1.2 meters before falling back and exploding. Sputnik reportedly offered her condolences.
A rare arcane bacterium was identified. Reports suggested that the colder the environment, the faster it feeds on food.
After discovering that it really took 500 experiments for "Lady No. 500" to succeed, Windsong's desire to meet her investor intensified.
In 1968, the computer mouse was introduced to the public. Before that, X had his own experiment with pointing devices using a bowling ball as the trackball.
In 1957, Illiac Suite, the first score ever composed entirely by computer, was completed. John Titor showed great interest in it, while Barcarola felt it lacked a human touch.
The Statute of Westminster was enacted on this day in 1931. Australia, along with many other Dominions, thus became an equal, separate, and independent nation within the Commonwealth.
On this day in 1901, the first radio signal was successfully transmitted across the Atlantic Ocean. Even today, the thought of this achievement still excites Ms. Radio.
Let flowers bloom in the cemetery; a powerful memory of all those who were taken from us.
Nautika's joining the field survey significantly reduces travel expenses. A change that greatly pleases Windsong.
Lorelei shows Vila her little conch. Together, the two enjoy a peaceful moment of listening to the calming sounds of the ocean.
On this day in 1773, 342 chests of black tea were hurled into the sea. This also marks the day that the sirens in Boston Harbor were able to sample tea from Wuyi, China.
On the first day of Saturnalia, Druvis III conjures an evergreen tree at the children's request.
Ulrich quickly steps in to prevent some Laplace employees from using 32K memory disks to commemorate the release of the IBM 7090, pointing out how utterly inefficient and impractical the idea is.
Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol was first published on this day in 1843. Oliver Fog knows the story very well.
Marianne found Rabies sitting on a branch of the evergreen tree. They shared a quiet moment together, listening to Flutterpage giggle as she tried to take flight from another branch.
It's the Winter Solstice. Liang Yue made the most of the day by having dumplings for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

On this day in 1983, China introduced its first self-designed supercomputer, Yinhe-1, to the world. Madam Z sent a card to a classmate who contributed to its development, expressing her happiness for their achievement.
Moldir was puzzled at how Lilya managed to fly a broom in such rough condition. Mr. Duncan told her that maintenance is about keeping it in the air, not restoring it to perfection.
On the last day of Saturnalia, Shamane made small sculptures made of evergreen wood for everyone. Buddy Fairchild was happy to help him gather the raw materials using his front teeth.
Inspired by an ad from another soft drink brand, Regulus persuaded Jessica to pull a sleigh as she gave away cans of Dr. Papper.
The warmth radiating from Ulu kept Punji warm and active through the winter.
Flutterpage has been happy to help deliver letters between two pen pals living in the Suitcase, even if the trip only takes about 30 seconds.
The movie The Exorcist was released in theaters in 1973. Blonney strongly disapproved of the director firing guns during takes to get real reactions from the actors.
Pavia immediately gave up his plan to toughen himself for blows when he found out Spathodea would be his practice partner.
On this day in 1924, Edwin Hubble announced the discovery of the Andromeda Galaxy. Sometimes, Voyager can be seen looking in its direction.
With the catchy tune of Love Me Do looping in the background, Vertin had an undisturbed, quiet day.
