And when the person before you once again asks for Critters as "Storm" samples, you find yourself rethinking again.
Samples. Or punching Critters. Did you really punch one?
The researcher twirls in glee and wants to give you a reward.
But the samples still fall short. You'd never hit one more than needed. Too bad the researcher plans to step into the "Storm" himself.
Critters may be cute, but they're basically pests—just like this one!
He stumbles in a daze, murmuring faintly: "So that's it ... I get it now ..."
Rumor says the return rate is 100%? Maybe?
He tells you a welcome party is being held for new investors.
Go join the welcome party. Have a great day.
"Shocking investment scam: a con artist disguised himself as a successful entrepreneur. So far 20 victims and a huge amount of money involved ..."
You got all your funds back, with interest and even some compensation.
Only fists can deal with a scumbag like this.
The investment was real. I got double my investment back!
I'm gonna tell all my friends and family to invest. Missing this would be a shame!
Rumor says the return rate is 100%? Really?
Trade "gold coins" for one of three treasures. Signed below: Musae III.
The machine starts shaking violently. With a loud noise, three prizes are ejected from the bottom.
You seem to have broken the machine. Probably time to leave.
You're from Laplace? Oh! Then you must be able to help me!
I need dragon grass, stabilizer, and APPLe's green branch. I'm sure there's plenty of it in the Laplace warehouse! Could you spare me some?
What a beautiful day. Thank you!
Let's see ... stabilizer first, then dragon grass, and finally APPLe's green branch ...
Whoa! *cough-cough* Looks like something's wrong with APPLe's green branch. How odd ... why is there such strong arcane residue on it? Did you use it for something?
Looks like we'll have to gather the ingredients again. Either way, thank you! Please, take this. It's a reward from Typhon.
A bounty of materials! Oh? And Mr. APPLe?
Wise and juicy Mr. APPLe, might you spare the time to help me for a moment?
Let's see ... stabilizer first, then dragon grass. Now, Mr. APPLe, it's your time to shine.

Perfect! The potion's ready!
How can I possibly thank you? Oh, I know! Take this—a reward from Typhon.
Potion for sale, no scams here!
An Awakened? Is there something I can help you with?
I used to hang from it until I fell from the tree.
A girl in a formal dress studying potions? Why, she's my captain's most generous patron. I'll help you. Give me a moment.
You're right. Though I promised my captain I would wait here, I suppose a short break wouldn't do any harm.
Hey, what are you doing?! Why are you taking out the rope? I won't back down!
To avoid being turned into apple juice, he ran away in frustration, leaving a twig behind.
After staring at you helplessly, a few whimpers serve as an answer.
It seems disappointed in you. Maybe we need a translation device.
The puppy's friend is lost. Have you seen them?
If you see them, please tell the puppy he is waiting here.
The puppy thanks you for helping him. Please take this.
It looks cautious. In this case, a little food might help it open up.
Wendy is drawn to the food and follows closely behind.
It seems to have forgotten you already gave it food and lets out a "coo coo coo" sound. Maybe it wants more.
This pilot sits on her battle broom and whistles as you approach.
The pilot didn't expect you to ignore her and shouts, "Hey!"
Your repeated silence has upset the pilot. She rushes over and says, "Hey, hold on a second!"
I'm a Zeno pilot. I keep order around here, but we're freezing our butts off. You got anything warm? Like that stuff ...
There's a Crates Gang Camp nearby. I bet they've got some! Can you cover my post while I grab it? Or maybe you could "borrow" some for me?
Of course, Zeno always helps others.
So? Did you get the stuff?
Ha! Great, just what I needed.
The camp's Crates Gang eyes you warily.
Hey! You! Don't loiter here. Move along!
Wrong password! All units alert! Intruder!
Here to swap shifts? What's today's password!
Burp. That's mine, yeah, my wallet. Here's the password. Take it.
It seems to be signaling you to follow.
Kind stranger, can I have some money? My dog is all I have now.
You're so kind even in the apocalypse. Take this.
He's about to attack the Crates Gang base and invites you to join.
You decide to be a lone hero.
In the last fight, I took an arrow to the knee.
Even if it heals, I probably can't fight again. I may have to retire ...
Your camp needs gate guards. Maybe he's a good fit.
With you onboard, this mission will go smoothly. I might even get promoted!
One guy at the table says, "Kid, we're short one player. Want to join?"
Your turn to draw. You've got 3 cards to play. Which one?
You're suspicious. Lifting the tablecloth, you find they're cheating.
You don't know why, but somehow you persuaded them.
For cheats like this, some physical persuasion is required.
She's shocked you spotted her and looks scared.
She's shocked you found her again and looks even more scared. She runs once again.
She seems to have given up running.
She begs for mercy and leaves something behind.
The pond sparkles and seems to ask, "Want to make a wish?"
A bag has appeared out of thin air.
A lady walks out from the pond, furious over your repeated wishes, and pelts you with coins.
Maybe the pond once had a use, but now it's been eroded by the "Storm."
The monster followed your wish straight to you.
Generosity is a virtue, especially in the apocalypse.
After gobbling it down, the beggar thanks you and asks for more travel funds.
He thanks you repeatedly and leaves behind some luggage he can't carry.
He stumbles away cold and hungry, leaving some discarded things behind.
My friend! We meet again. Do you remember me?
You gave me food and lent me money to get home.
Thanks to you, I reunited with my family. Here's a gift I prepared for you. Please take it.
Too bad—he can't remember anything about himself.
The man is in pain but recognizes the photo. It shows him and his son, who was taken by a red-skinned monster after the plane crashing. So memory didn't die. It was just ... unavailable.
He thanks you for helping him recover his memory. He heads out to find his son and leaves you something.
Treasure. For you. Money. For me.
Looks like this building is a courthouse. Inside, there's an audience forming. The judge has called for the defendant.
Perhaps you do need judgment, but not today, and certainly not now.
The defendant takes the stand. The charge is "stealing beans."
Somehow you're in the defense seat. And you shout out loud.
The judge suggests you read some law books.
The whole court bursts out laughing, but you know the reversal begins here.
After a debate, the judge rules: "Guilty! The defendant is sentenced to 48 hours of silence. Effective immediately."
Your extensive funding seminar experience helps you catch loopholes. You win a "not guilty" verdict.
The defendant is grateful and wants to give you something.
Strange, hoarse noises come from the receiver. It keeps asking if you're leaving.
All you can hear is a low growl. You catch a few words: "run ... "
This place offers peace for thinking, just like a toilet.
Resting in the phone booth, your muscles and lactic acid finally make peace.
The funny thing is that this phone booth became your haven in the "Storm."
Rock music blares from a floating hot air balloon. Staff are fed up and ready to shoot it down on your command.
Someone put a record player on the balloon. At least you got a record.
The balloon floats higher, out of range. But the volume never drops. Reminds you of a coworker, maybe soundproofing should be solved next.
No way that thing gets approval to play again. What now?
If it can't be moved, just leave it be. A lucky surprise for someone else.
I'm sure Enigma would love this.
"Oi, you blockheads! These are limited edition!!" A strange girl bursts out, her face red from yelling at the team. You know her, but you know it's not really her.
Your mate has great taste, at least—but these are mine. If you want, I can bring you some other records next time.
Your actions violate the LSCC Safety Management Regulations. I'm afraid we'll have to temporarily restrict your movement.
Hah! A pirate's ship may be sunk, but she'll never be captured!
A flash explodes from her fingertip. When the light fades, the self-proclaimed pirate is gone.
A play is worthless without an audience. Would you like to see this masterpiece?
At first, it's a drop of rain you can barely see, from the sewer, from a rubber sole, from milk about to be poured out. It pooled, unnoticed. An era ended. Some survived.

All the explosive news converged on this day at the Remit Cup pavilion.
Speeding rock pirates, spotlight-hungry artists, camera-shy sheepdogs ... and the world-class thief who dropped onto the center stage.
Don't step into the forest. Don't disturb the forest. Don't leave the forest. The forest knows everything you do.
Let's see what other good shows await.
Tradition and thought, truth and chains, on a faraway coast, new stories are still being written. Turn the page with them.
As a traditional sport is about to be revived, rumors fly through the streets. How will the millennia-old fire and her companions reignite the sacred flame?
As the sea swallow soars through dark clouds, as sunflower seeds sprout, as the steel beast roars once more, a new world awaits them!
You still think that last one was more fun.

A famous arcade machine from the 90s, 60-in-1 model. Before the "Storm," machines like this could be found everywhere: arcades, malls, even convenience stores. Now, it's hard to find even in the Foundation's reserves.
Two little pixel guys jump and flip to fight off aliens.
The ultimate duel—Wind, Forest, Fire, Mountain!
There's still time left. Who knows if this machine will still be here next time. One more round?
Break's over. Time to get back to work.
There's still time left. Who knows if this machine will still be here next time. One last round?
Why is there ... a toilet here? Thank you, Musae III, for your thoughtfulness!
A startled voice comes from inside: "Who's there?"
Oh, it's Ulrich. You scared me. I'm not slacking off, I was just ... thinking through some problems.
Yes, of course, yes. Let me jot it down.
The thinking pays off. A sheet of calculations slides out from under the door. But its owner can't move, thanks to a spontaneous sciatic nerve misfire. He asks you to pass the report to a colleague.
The person inside is shocked: "Hey, don't do that!"
They start begging: "Wait a second! I'm coming out!"
Thanks to your persistence, the stall finally opens. Turns out, it was a Laplace researcher hiding inside.
Alright, but I can't get up just yet. If you've got time later, come back for me.
Maybe it's the "Storm Syndrome" that makes him think there's actually a toilet here.
"Wuuugh ... blegh!" Something bursts out of the stall. Whatever it used to be, it's now completely immobile.
Your dry sense of humor shows. The researcher stays silent, seems it's the only way he knows how to cope.
Roger that. Thanks for the help. Here's a little something for your trouble.
"No math! No math!" someone screams, as a man gets dragged into a cave.
You feel it's time to explain what respecting personal choices means.
It's just class, like quitting an addiction. Once you're past withdrawal, you'll be fine.
His eyes are blank, like he barely escaped with his life. He mumbles incoherently, his words slurred.
"You let him go? Then you can study in his place," the blue-haired girl says.
Clearly, theory is the superstructure, strength is the base. If you want to sneak past her, you'll pay for it.

"Answer this: What's 20 times 6?"
Apparently, the girl thinks a simple math question is enough to test you.
She's impressed with your math skills. After chatting about her plans for the sloppy guy, she gives you a few gifts.
Messing up that question totally ruined his credibility. Looks like you'll have to study in his place.
This person looks familiar, but in a way more hopeless than before.
Don't bother him. Just grab whatever's nearby and move on.
A weak little flame that looks like it could go out at any second. Only some burnt wood chips remain.
Your encouragement doesn't help. The flame still looks like it'll die any moment.
Your comfort doesn't work either. The flame still looks like it'll die any moment.
Lying on the wooden plank, she quickly regains her strength. Now recovered, she tells you the sacred fire has gone out. Perhaps finding the backup flame is the only way to restore it.
You arrive at the altar. The massive brazier hinting at the flame's former glory. Faintly etched on it is a single word: "Reincarnator."
It seems she threw a fit from being lit the wrong way, but either way, the flame is burning now. She's safe for the moment.
The flames rise high. When you look back, she's embracing the Reincarnator.
The Reincarnator before you looks like they're waiting for someone to help.
I need to light the altar and save my friend ... but I can't control my power. Will you come with me to the altar?
The road to the altar is dangerous. You'll have to protect her.
A black-haired girl asks you for help. She was here traveling with a friend, but they ran into a guy with a knife. Now they're gotten separated.
You decide to turn on your detector, only to be hit with an immediate burst of alarms. Either it's broken, or you have good reason for not believing this sob story.
The group arrives at the lighthouse. If you had to describe it, it's a textbook horror movie setting.
Split up and get picked off one by one?
After searching for a long time, only one photo catches your eye. Inside the dusty frame is the same girl from before. Looks like you shouldn't have trusted her story.
Just as you're about to subdue the girl, a crowd rushes out from every corner of the room, all carrying film equipment. Turns out you were right, this really is a horror movie set.
You worried the set might interfere with your experiment, but convincing people is a hassle. Luckily, there are still some salvageable supplies here.
Their design skills are genuinely impressive. Maybe their talents shouldn't be limited to sets?
Thank you for your help. Here's a token of appreciation!
So this is what "A just cause enjoys abundant support" looks like.
Maybe they needed the supplies more. Or maybe we just needed a real challenge.

Splitting up took a toll. Just as you're about to subdue the girl, a crowd rushes out from every corner of the room, all carrying film equipment. Turns out you were right, this really is a horror movie set.
We got separated in a giant lighthouse. Shouldn't be too far.
A strange painting: day looks like night, the earth looks like sky. But looking at it brings an odd sense of calm.
You reach out and touch the frame. A strange feeling washes over you.
Thanks to this mysterious artwork, the Researchers' Resistance against the "Storm" seems to have increased.
A rundown monastery stands resolute. Not a common sight inside the toybox, but still more fitting than an outhouse, right?
Though abandoned, dismantling this building will yield a large amount of resources.
For the Awakened, this is just mimicking what they've seen. But maybe because it's too utilitarian, the prayer goes unanswered.
You've tried enough. The best option now is to dismantle the place and collect the resources.
Maybe try a different pose and give it one more shot.
Still nothing. Time's almost up, try one more time, or break it down?
Maybe these Awakened have been right to pray. A strange device appears before you.
Supply signals are scattered everywhere—part of an emergency simulation. Since you've found one, start calling for support.
Safety comes first. Stocking up on meds is critical to keeping everyone alive and completing the mission.
Another person means another set of hands. With the current manpower shortage, any help is vital.
Send this batch back first to make room for more scavenging. Even if we don't get back in time, at least we found something.
It's not a lot, but only a fixed amount of supplies is available. Only catch is ... you've got to file the request yourself.
A watchtower of sorts, though what it was meant to look out over is unclear. Maybe climbing it will help you scout the terrain.
Good. Now the surrounding area can be considered mapped.
We've got more pressing matters to handle.
Come have a look. I'm sure there's something you'll like.
A sword in a rock. Classic. Pulling it out doesn't make you a hero, but it does get you free drinks.
It's free, might as well try.

You pull it out with ease. The tavern keeper immediately declares you a hero, who takes it as their responsibility to help others. Though soon you realize it wasn't destiny that made you pull the sword out, it was the barkeep.
As a hero, I accept this responsibility. What quest do you have for me?
Instead of titles, you'd rather he honor the reward first ... but he goes right on assigning the quest.
A simple delivery. A letter to a kid who hasn't been home in two years.
Not what I expected, but sure, I'll handle it.
Turns out that delivery was just the start. The kid wants help gathering some stuff.
I've got other things to do.
Then the Demon Monarch showed up out of nowhere.

A researcher from Weapons R&D stops you and asks for resources to build a massive weapon capable of taking down large targets. Ever since the Ultimate Answer Act was passed, these requests have become routine.
We've got some spare materials. Good luck with the project.
We're short on supplies ourselves. Sorry.
I always rely on the kindness of strangers. Thank you.
You saved me. I think this is the start of a beautiful friendship.
Some birds aren't meant to be caged. Their feathers shine best in the light of freedom.
Hey! That outfit ... is there some kind of party nearby?
Is there something that can pierce through any wall?
The power of science is amazing!
Strange rumors going around lately. You heard anything?
Is there a thing here called a "Royal Cheeseburger"?
Even the crows can't be bothered to come out and complain about today's weather. Care for some hot soup?
Need a break? There's always room by the fire for someone with stories to tell.
I love the smell of gasoline in the morning.
Roads? Where we're going, we don't need roads.
Forget today's troubles. Tomorrow's a new day!
I can't take it anymore. I'm leaving this damned place!
You're back? How's the outside today?
Don't forget to calibrate the timer before every expedition.
I know my knee's injured, but do we really have to bring it up every single time?
Hello, how can I help you?
Those noises beyond the barrier ... Are we safe?
It's been three days without supplies. What should we do?
Would you take me in? Thank you so much!
That uniform ... Are you from Laplace?
Lost contact with HQ. Initiating emergency protocol. Personnel satefy prioritzed.
The "Storm" is coming. We need to evacuate fast.
Thanks for the invitation. I hope I can help.
Are you collecting data too? Ah, never mind. It doesn't matter anymore.
The sample parameters don't match standard models. Recalibration needed.
We'll observe the arrival of the "Storm" until the very last second.
Hey! Wait! Do you have the research equipment I need? Can I join you?
Researcher? This area's not safe. Be careful.
Hello, Awakened. This is the Zeno army. The road ahead is dangerous. Stay safe.
First mission, and I run into this ... What rotten luck.
You're saying ... you have a sanctuary ? Of course I'll join you.
Sir, care for a newspaper? The "Storm" is coming!
That's right. They say the "Storm" will wash everything clean. If I were you, I'd hide fast.
Too bad I need to make money.
Buy a paper and you'll know everything. Once I sell out, I'll have enough to buy a ticket to the shelter.
Yes, the "Crates Gang" has a Storm shelter. All it takes is enough money to get in.
I'm curious. Why aren't you even a little scared, knowing the "Storm" is coming?
If that's true, I could provide intel long-term. But ... I've got family, so ...
Thank you. You truly are a good person!
Laplace? Why would someone from Laplace leave the tower? I thought you were all bound to your labs ...
I remember her. She used to work at our Foundation's office, helping civilians.
But I'm not sure now. We're severely short-staffed, and the [Crates Gang] just ambushed us.
The [Crates Gang] has taken over the area. We request assistance from Laplace as per the Foundation Aid Act.
Once we retake this place, we'll help you find that girl.
Looks like the Crates Gang has fled. I also have some intel you might need.
Not really. Just heard refugees talk about sightings in the [Velvet Forest].
Thanks for your help. Anything else?
You've done a lot. I'd be glad to join.
The name Laplace seems well-known around here. Everyone you meet knows of you.
Just like your name, frailty seems to be a Laplace employee stereotype. She doubts your strength deeply.
Strength brings responsibility and trouble. To her, you seem powerful, which means you should be able to fix her problem.
Clearly, hashing out everything in a place like this runs counter to everyone's stereotype of Laplace Employee. Maybe invite her to the tower for a proper talk.

Hello, Laplace. If you can help us with a few issues, we'd gladly assist you. 
We've lost contact with one of our soldiers nearby, and our communications are down.
You scientists can probably fix that, right?
Communications are back, but he says the situation's urgent. Can you check it out?
Thank heavens. They were telling the truth about reinforcements! Dying together is better than dying alone. This way. Watch out, they're on high alert.
The Crates Gang got their hands on some weapons. If we don't deal with them, evacuation here's going to be a mess.
But where do they have left to go ...
You came, just as I calculated.
Yes, the "Storm" is coming. And this world is a simulation, isn't it?

A girl mentioned it once, but I didn't believe her. Now all the data points to that answer. It explains so much. I know you're not the leader of this world, but clearly, you have an important mission.
That's Laplace, alright! Come, I've got something to show you.
Scattered papers all point to one thing: the "Storm" is coming ... exactly when predicted.
That lady hoped we'd unite in the face of crisis. Instead ... this is what we got.
But now you're here. Maybe we really can be saved.
Is this your first time here? Or do you ask me that every time?
I'm just a researcher, like most folks in Laplace.
Don't worry, I won't start wondering whether we count as people. I'll leave that to philosophers. I just want to fix the "Storm."
My research here is done. Next step: find a solution.
There's always a way. If not this time, then next time. Sooner or later, I'll solve it.
Of course. But may I ask some questions? I'm curious how Laplace outside this box sees us.
Would you give your life to stop your world's "Storm"?
Can I solve all this on my own?
How do you people out there see us?
I see. I will go with you.
Understood. Goodbye, Laplace outsider. I'll continue my research here.
You watch the Critters digging in the sand from inside their coconut shells. Once they start setting up shop in them, you finally hit the bottom.
A combination lock? And Musae III's message: "Congrats on reaching the end of the world."
Maybe unlocking this will reveal the whole truth, and help you survive the toybox's trials ahead. The "answer" is too tempting for any researcher.
But what if it's Pandora's box? You could be trapped in the toybox forever, or become the next Crates Gang until a kind colleague opens it again.
Your companion outside clearly disagrees with using an unorthodox method to complete a mission that may determine Laplace's fate.
Your ferrofluid shudders at the crossroads. This is a critical decision. Everyone's waiting for your answer.
Will you open the lock? Time's running out. The alarm following the message now echoes across the beach.
The alarm following the message now echoes across the beach as enemies gather.
There seems to be some secret here waiting to be uncovered ... or perhaps it's just waiting for the right person.
A tower that can shield from the "Storm"? How much is the ticket?
A woman told me about it. At first, I didn't believe her, but then she said a bunch of things only I would know.
She got so many things right that everyone started believing her.
She told us she'd stay in the [Darkened City] to help more people. Maybe you can go check it out.
You Laplace people should understand the "Storm" better than I do, right?
It's true that an ordinary person shouldn't know about Laplace. But it's just bad luck, these memories cling to me like stains on my clothes. The "Storm" can't wash them away.

Maybe it's a curse. I died during the chaos and got buried deep underground. I mean, like four or five meters deep. But somehow, that kept the "Storm" from affecting me. When I woke up, everything had reset.
At first, I was terrified. But slowly, I realized that while this world keeps going through the "Storm," I still remember everything.
They walk into the "Storm" again and again, and the world gets turned upside down each time. It's like a game, where the player keeps resetting the save file ... and I'm a corrupted save left behind.

With every reset, I've tried everything. I've sought help from Arcanists, from the Foundation, from Zeno, even from the Crates Gang. But no matter what, I can't change this world. I can only help others as best I can.

Until you showed up, I didn't get it. Why would a group of Laplace folks be out here collecting resources and attacking the Crates Gang? Your combat power is way beyond what Laplace is know for. Or is everyone who falls from the sky like this?
I hope you can help more people. If these resets are inevitable, then maybe the more people survive the "Storm," the closer we get to a solution.
There's a Zeno camp in the [Howling Snowfield]. I took shelter there during the last "Storm." You can seek them out if you need help.
I get where you're coming from. Maybe you'll find what you need in the [Howling Snowfield].
I knew you outsiders must be the type who'd go around looking for quests.
Have you sent staff to the [Dusky Badlands]?
I met a Laplace researcher there during the last Storm. Maybe you should go check it out.
While you were gone, I thought about my "uniqueness."
Maybe I'm not the unique one ... maybe it's where I was buried: the [Serene Bay].
Where I was buried, there were waves and the smell of seawater. After being buried there, I started remembering things. Maybe we should go take a look.

63616e20796f752068656c70206d65207265747269657665207468656d3f.
(Translation: Can you help me retrieve them?)
A Critter sniffs a stack of documents and looks like it wants to swallow them whole.
The Critter gave up the data and fled.
The mission says we're a two-person team, but three people showed up at the rendezvous point.
You quickly realize that someone who isn't from Laplace has snuck in. To find them, you'll need to use your big glass brain.
The person in front of you claims to be the designer of the staff dormitory. Might be worth hearing his testimony.
At first there was only one Dormitory. As research progressed, we could build more.
Each Dormitory can house up to five assistants.
The person in front of you claims to be the designer of the Assembly Square. Might be worth hearing his testimony.
The Assembly Square is used to propose and announce Ulrich's resolutions, with a limit of two announcements.
Each time, you can choose one resolution out of three to propose. Whether it gets approved depends on the Assistants' voting results.
The person in front of you claims to be the designer of "Lucy" the Trailer. Might be worth hearing him out.
The trailer stores collected materials. Each item takes up weight, so don't go over capacity.
Assistants met during exploration can also board the trailer. They don't count against the weight, so bring as many as possible.
So, did you figure out who the imposter is?
I knew it was him! Thanks for your help. Here's a token of our gratitude.
He's not the imposter. The panicked researchers don't even have time to deal with you.
Hey! Heard the rumor? Heavy snow ... "monsters" appearing.
Monsters? We don't usually call unknowns "monsters." Maybe this needs some digging.
Definitely not a Critter! A snowy monster is supposed to be white!
Your sharp observation confirms the creature isn't a ghost. You feel a little disappointed.
After a tense standoff and attack, you find it's just a Tooth Spirit. Amid your colleague Enigma's mocking laughter, you move on. Good thing you don't have teeth.
A snowman, built from the laughter and joy of children. Maybe not the answer you wanted, but at least it'll make the kids happy.
A Critter senses your presence and takes a combat stance.
Back off, fishbowl-head. We're just "collecting" a bit of comfort tax. Don't stick your nose in.
The thugs flee in a panic.
They don't speak your language, but you and Enigma are language experts. You'll figure something out.
Insults, with their unique facial and body language, remain universally understood, just like now.

As an Awakened, people expect you to "understand non-human speech," like how computer geeks are expected to fix everything. But you always disappoint. The Critters probably think your gestures are hilarious and wander off.
The Critters can't grasp the idea of "wait and see." They just see you staring blankly at them. Thankfully, the kind little things don't mock you, they even keep trying to talk.
You decide to mimic their movements. After all, first contact usually starts with body language.
Did they get it? No one knows; they all just bolted. Aren't there any glass-brained Critters in the world?!
Us, locked in the box, but, no like.
Boss say, here, grab people, all bring here!
Glass brain, lure boss, boss get beat, we go home.
Give you, beat boss, but don't beat us.
A deceived Critter shrieks. No need to lie to yourself, it's just cursing.
Only one researcher is in the tower, logging data endlessly ... don't say he's lonely. He's not.
Oh! My god, someone actually came here.
You're into space stuff too? I really want to go to space!
Yeah, it's always been my dream to look down on the world from space!
I built this observatory myself! And I even got a signal from outer space!
Come on, let me show you!
You look at the screen. The so-called "space" signal ... looks very familiar ...
The researcher eagerly awaits your response.
You mean I live in a toybox? And the space signal came from your world?
Oh! That's fun! No need to be careful, I'm not discouraged. My job is to explore the unknown. Space? Your world? All unknown!
I'll keep researching. Maybe one day I'll meet you in your world! Here, take this little souvenir.
Oh wow, thank you for recognizing my work!
Here, let me share my research with you.
You know them like plants know the sun or fish know seaweed. Fixing it is no big deal.
"Flock" ... though you haven't seen any sheep since entering the box, but there might be some wool scattered about—if you're lucky enough to find.

Yes, because a maze can be seen as two sections divided by the correct path. Follow the edge of one, and you'll inevitably reach the exit.

Please, have a seat! Would you like a cup of coffee? I found some in these supply crates.
Canned food or vegetable packages? Fuel or batteries? We'll need to balance weight against calories.
Please, don't be afraid. Those wailing sounds outside are not the Mother Spirit's wrath, only the cold wind howling through the stone walls ...
Antarctica is like a distant yet familiar dream. I've learned so much about it, yet after stepping onto this continent, everything still feels new and mysterious ...
Thinking of chipping off a piece of rock? Too bad, it's actually synthetic.

These cans expired twenty years ago? N-not a problem! As long as they aren't dented, I'll eat anything!
Take a file with you. It's always important to keep your ice axe sharp.

Supplies are low, but we can ration them—the coarse salt from the mandrake can be used to make soup and we can use the packaging for kindling.
Let me do a final check and make sure nothing useful gets left behind ... Alright, time to try our luck at the next tent.
All set. At least we won't starve, get lost, or freeze solid from the wind ...!

I can't wait to run the lab tests. This could be revolutionary!

Strange rumors have emerged from the western front. Soldiers speak of a humanoid gargoyle—its petrified arm unable to be penetrated by bullets, its gaze driving men to madness. Even in darkness, none escape those piercing eyes or the headshot that follows. They call it "a lone devil cast out for defying the gods."
Given that gargoyles live in groups, these rumors remain unverified. Yet after millennia guarding church windows, these gargoyles are gradually becoming the embodiment of fear and despair in soldiers' accounts.

Nicholas is a thirty-two-year-old veteran. He said he fought tooth and nail to get his kids into school because he never had the chance.
On the battlefield, he led us in charges, retreats, patrols, and night watches. He scrubbed the "new recruit" immaturity off us. But during break time, he'd squeeze between us high schoolers like the most eager student, begging us to teach him how to read and write. "Gotta write my wife more than just 'I'm safe,'" he'd say. We loved teaching him.
At that supply crate with the kerosene lamp, we were his teachers. But step outside the trench? We became fledglings under his wings.

— Rossel

The squad come upon signs of Andrea and his reconnaissance team.
Something shimmers between the far-off ice columns. Is it just snow-blindness ... or a miraculous species unknown to science?

The object turns out to be a long-abandoned flashlight.
Its pale glow tracing a lonely path. The snow ahead is marked by discolored patches of dried blood that break its uniform whiteness.
The map leads them to a battered pack, wedged between the rocks, likely mere moments from being buried by the snow.

After a brief rest, the squad sets off once more.
A signal breaks the silence, crackling through someone's radio.
The fractured electronic pulses echo a single location again and again.

Moldir's squad comes upon a lost detachment of Igor's forces.
Having run out of food and water, they teeter on the edge of total physical collapse.

The squad reaches the spot mentioned in the note to find a lake stretching out before them.
Perhaps due to the unknown ritual mentioned in the note, the lake remains unfrozen.
From the still lake, three penguins soon emerge, accompanied by several leaping fish.
The Steep Path to the Peak

The squad discovers a temporary supply point belonging to Manus Vindictae.
It rests at the mountain's foot, buried beneath a heavy covering of snow, it looks ready to collapse under the weight.
Moldir locates a lake in Manus Vindictae territory. Could it serve as a chokepoint if rigged with traps?

The lake's surface doesn't appear to be evenly frozen.
Moldir marks the weak points, deciding to give Manus Vindictae a little surprise.
The trap is set. Now, they only need to lure the Manus followers to the lake.
Lured by the frozen fish scattered by the penguins, the Manus disciples follow the footprints laid by the squad, taking the bait—hook, line, and sinker.
The snowstorm rises once more. To keep the outpost secure, the squad must stay alert to the shifting weather.
Recent reports from the observation point show irregular blizzard patterns. It is now closing in on the squad outpost.
Meteorological scans show the blizzard front is still distant from the summit, but wind speeds here are higher than across the plains. In two hours, the storm will arrive.

The blizzard finds the penguins first, then through the white curtain, come Manus Vindictae stragglers.
This may be a rare opportunity for the squad to trap those "masked creeps" where they stand.
As the blizzard begins to ease, Moldir and the reinforcements emerge from the fading snow.
The path ends here, and before them lies only a steep icefield. The squad must now push through the worsening blizzard.
The squad continues along the narrow path and reaches the summit. This grants a great vantage point, but the terrain is perilously steep.
Moldir's squad establishes a "squad outpost," a lure in plain sight, upon the ice.
From the new observation point, the blizzard's route and coordinates can be tracked with pinpoint accuracy.
As the storm lifts, the Manus followers find themselves with a cliff at their backs and the squad blocking their path ahead. They have nowhere left to run.
Antarctic weather is unpredictable. With night falling, the squad must decide to either set up a temporary shelter, or continue their journey.
During their rendezvous with Andrea's team, Moldir's squad acquires intel linked to David's whereabouts.
Moldir and her squad reach the first temporary supply post, but it can only shelter a limited number of people.
Moldir's squad arrives at the second temporary supply post, where everyone can be safely accommodated.
The blizzard returns. Contacting their remaining teammates now becomes a matter of the utmost urgency.

Inside the tent, they find a tattered note.
Duty pulls them onward, as investigating the note may prove to be a pointless distraction.
The note claims to lead to a hidden temporary supply point. Moldir must now decide whether to investigate.

The squad finally arrives at the supply post. Amid broken canvas and scattered gear, they discover a message from David and a transceiver adorned with pinecones.
However, to contact headquarters, they'll need to switch to an encrypted channel known only to a few.

A group of penguins close in on the squad, drawn to the frozen fish in their supply crate.
Buddy Fairchild proposes an intel-for-supplies exchange with the penguins, yet the fish remains an essential resource for the squad.

The squad once again runs into the penguins who asked for their frozen fish.
"They say they've seen the Fluffy Duke," Buddy Fairchild translates.
Duke Fluff makes contact with Sergeant White Gloves, and it is revealed that he is the one escorting the Igor's detachment back to base.

I don't know you.#This scenery is bleak.

The stench of rust and burnt flesh is quite unbearable.

But the entire world is in ruins now. I have nowhere else to go.
And it seems you're stuck here with me. You poor sap.

I hope that rusty old thing holds SOME kind of secret—to saving the world, or ending this war.
Maybe then, you can take on another career before you die. A watchmaker, perhaps.
The war will end one day.#I have reasons to continue the fight.
I've nothing more to say. Would you kindly leave me alone for a while?
I have no tea or snacks to offer. I can't even recall what they taste like.
Go on. Savor the war. There'll be another after this. No need to worry about things going exactly as you'd like.
Look at these boys. They left home with puffed chests and confident smiles on their faces—
Thinking they'd go to the front, pull a few triggers, kill a few enemies, and come back as heroes.
But when their feet hit the soil, they turned "pacifist," it seems, wounding their own hands rather than their enemies'.
Their mothers should have begged them to stay, not waved their handkerchiefs to see them off.
They made a misjudgment.#They had no choice.
Soldiers follow orders, officers give them, higher-ups make them, parents send their children off to die ...
And not one of them will bear the weight of their "misjudgments." Only the dead must answer.
Really? You think death is the only option?
What could possibly be the point in that?
Don't tell me you believe there's GLORY in dying on the battlefield? The thought makes me sick.
Look there—at the lifeless body lying flat in the mud.
He couldn't even muster the courage to flee, so he bribed a fellow soldier—a man he barely knew—with three cigarettes to surrender with him.
He died—killed in a moment of pure, senseless hatred. And the other lived—saved by a flicker of mercy.
Where should his mother aim her grief? At the officer who changed his mind just a moment too late? Hah!
The officer will be pardoned; they'll say he, too, was a victim of this endless, miserable cycle of hatred.
So tell me—please, tell me—to whom this rage should go, and I will take this kitchen knife and plunge it into their heart!
I'm afraid I only have turnip stew to serve you. I will add a few sausage scraps to your bowl, however.
Here. Now go. It's best you leave before another battle breaks out.
Is there something else you want from me?
You know what? Since you're so fond of visiting ... take the chair you're sitting on.
Even through the coldest winters, that chair was spared the fire. Perhaps it was meant for you.
Ah, yes—a tragedy to serve such a dish to such an honorable guest, but I'm afraid I have no tears left to shed to season the thing.
If this farce had ended sooner, perhaps I'd have treated you to a feast—
Bacon, beef stew, pretzels, mashed potatoes, sauerkraut, and a tankard of beer, of course.
But the big men in the army disagreed. They valued shiny medals on their chests over food on their people's tables.
Right. Since you insist on staying, I will go to the market and see what I can find.
Sit here for a while longer, if you like. Prepare for a lifelong stay, even.
With any luck, this place will become your grave by the time the next farce ends.
Their masters remain quiet ... for the most part. And you know why.

What do you mean, "I know why"?#You sound like a soldier I know.

... Mein Gott, ████, as I write this, it finally dawns on me: I've always known why he refused them after all. I just never thought anyone would have the courage to make that choice.

My Dearest Cousin Ladislas,

How oft thou art in my prayers. I trust with all my heart that Italy hath already begun to feel as home unto thee. I am told the folk there are warm of spirit and generous of hand; I can well believe thou hast found many a kindly friend upon thy path.

Marianne and I do prepare for a journey into Austria, and our hearts are full of longing. For there lieth, as thou hast spake so oft, the very heart of the new art. I yearn to lift mine eyes unto the golden tracery crowning the Secession Building, whilst Marianne doth dream of wandering through the galleries and little shops of the Wiener Werkstätte. We have set our minds also upon the Karlskirche—Fischer von Erlach's great Baroque church. They say its nineteen stained-glass windows shine as jewels and its nave holdeth a majesty not soon forgotten. Should any sketches from our travels serve thy studies, it would delight me to send them forth.

Our past words dwell yet within me. Marianne telleth me ever of the new age dawning—of electric light supplanting the gentle glow of candles, and of the darkness of our nights fading away. Yet, dear Ladislas, I still feel the nearness of the old ways. This age of machines hath left many unsettled and without refuge; soon they shall crave a quiet place wherein to kneel and seek God's comfort and counsel.

Then do I call to mind thy words, and my heart is moved—that our prayers must rise above the clamour of industry. And so do I begin to dream, with thee in my thoughts, of a church for this new century, yet still a haven for the soul. Though our cousin smileth at such fancies, her words have sown new imaginings in me, and I have begun to set them down in drawings. Mayhap to raise such a place would take ten, even fifteen years; yet it comforteth me to picture thee by my side when the time cometh, helping to bring our vision to life.

Thou art ever in my thoughts and ever in my prayers.

With all my love,
Agnès

A Recent Report on Manus Vindictae​​

Reports continue to arrive from across the globe concerning arcanists operating under Manus Vindictae (a complete list of names and locations can be found in the attached appendix). These individuals have been gathering in coordinated cells, their training evident. Given the efficiency and precision of their attacks against human military forces, it is no longer accurate to call them merely an "organization"; they are, in effect, an army. Each morning I open what feels like ten thousand urgent messages clamoring for my attention, with still more pleas for reinforcements. Our office has been working without pause. Fatigue has dulled even my anger; nothing surprises me anymore—not even reports of skirmishes between warlords in the eastern territories. At times, I am tempted to reply that they needn't fret; east or west, it makes little difference. The entire world is sliding into chaos. ... The contingency plan drafted by Creius has now been submitted to the committee for review. It addresses the escalating threat posed by Manus Vindictae. Should they succeed in building a large-scale regular force—or if their attacks continue to spread disorder—the proposal urges the Foundation to form its own standing military rather than rely on Zeno. Creius sets forth what he claims is the most efficient approach: recruiting and reorganizing both human and arcanist soldiers already at the front. This is madness. Does he intend to make the Foundation a rival to every government on earth—an entity viewed with still deeper suspicion? Creius has always been radical, but war elevates such voices. He shows no concern for how the world might react, arguing instead that "we live in an age the Storm could erase at any moment, so we are not obliged to heed their protests." Only recently would such words have been unthinkable. His position is plain: if Manus Vindictae declares open war, governments will have no choice but to align with the Foundation. Yet should we follow his plan, we begin the most perilous of games.

████,

It has taken me a long time to write this letter, though my mind has never ceased its vigilance.

You know, as well as I, that I have spent my life mastering the concealment of intent, approaching even the unknown with a scholar's patience. You know, too, why I have worked to prevent conflict—not from idealism, but because I have seen what war truly leaves behind, long before the Foundation, long before the "Storm" rose.

My principles have often led me to aid or forge alliances with adversaries. I have long sought to create a balance between humans and arcanists. I firmly believe that Force is a tool, nothing more, and its misuse brings only chaos. While we may bear a fraction of the consequences, ordinary lives carry the rest. I have acted with care, and for that I have been called a Dove—a label I dismiss. My concern has never been for titles or comfort, only for what must endure.

Zeno's defection is largely credited with the rise of the Hawks. Committee members, wary and distrustful, sought to establish a military force directly under Foundation control. Meanwhile, the "Storm" has transported us back to a time dominated by warfare. Creius's philosophy runs contrary to our values and the traditions that preserve a fragile equilibrium. His contingency plan would not only threaten security but also collapse it. Should we provoke governments, forsake our mediating role, or coerce allegiance—how could the Foundation survive the "Storm", Manus Vindictae, or the world itself?

And yet ████, I cannot deny that Creius has succeeded—though his triumph chills me more than it reassures.

Hill 299 is secured. Eight divisions have been withdrawn from the frontline trenches. Soldiers untrained against arcane assault survived where they would otherwise have perished. Nearly one hundred thousand lives were spared. All achieved under the shadow of his contingency plan. None can dispute the effectiveness of his actions—but effectiveness is not wisdom. The currents he has unleashed will embolden the reckless. Those who were once cautious may now lean toward the Hawks. The balance we have preserved hangs by the thinnest of threads.

Wishing you all the best.

Marsha

Soldier with an exceptional throwing arm.​​
His skills might once have made him a star pitcher; now they're used for a deadlier sport.

An infantryman clutching his rifle.
Compared to the overwhelming power of artillery barrages, their lives fragile as a wisp of air.

Machine guns are swifter and more flexible than heavy artillery.
Once its tripod touches the ground, you pray you're nowhere near its lethal arc of fire.

A soldier with a flare pistol.​​
In war, intelligence can be a lifeline or a death sentence. Bringing commanders glory, or ruin.

An armored vehicle rolling through the battlefield.
A mounted machine gun on top indicates that it's built to more than withstand enormous punishment.

An uncontrollable fear.
Surging from a place of raw primal instincts.

An imagined representation of mortality.​​
It remains intertwined with fear until one learns to transcend death itself.

A fragment of war.​​
The smoldering ruins reveal countless contorted faces, their hatred and grudge persisting long after their bodies have turned to ash.

An agent of deprivation, a harvester of death.
It claims the right to deprive millions of their lives, ultimately offering them all to death.

An overwhelming tide of grief.​​
There's no use distinguishing between wails and sobs. The sorrow has already submerged us all.

The long buried forms of the fallen.
Though they no longer know who they are, their lifeless form still mimic human movements.

A pilot surveying craters and trenches from the sky.​​
She feels deep down that her existence shouldn't be defined by creating such devastation.

An officer stationed at her post, awaiting instructions.​​
Wait for victory, for defeat, or simply for all this to be over.

An executioner stands ready to enforce discipline.​​
Her revolver was meant for those who violate orders, yet now she finds herself uncertain.

A scout conducting his patrols atop his mount.​​
Carrying his ideals of justice, he rides, perhaps hoping to mend this wounded land.

A veteran who has removed his uniform.​​
Though nearly disconnected from past military discipline, he fiercely clings to his sense of honor.

A regular infantry.
​​Loyal and disciplined, but inflexible.

Heavy weapon specialists, equipped with devastating firepower.
Excellent at providing both fire support and frontline suppression. Their overwhelmingly destructive force makes them the embodiment of deterrence.

Heavily armed soldiers.
"It's going to be alright, get behind me." Their presence alone raises the morale of the frontline.
The moment he squeezed the trigger for the first time, he felt a flood of power wash over him, exhilarating, intoxicating and impossible to forget.

A lazy reinforcement soldier, dismissive and unreliable.
He insists that what the sentry saw was "Just a bear."

A diligent sentry.
He firmly believes what he saw was, in fact, definitely not a bear.
He has seen glorious battles and thunderous applause, but now, there is no more music. Yet the effects of what he will experience next will be more real than anything before.

Steadfastly believing that the old order will endure.
They still have something to protect, and will defend it with unbreakable devotion.

Agents laboring tirelessly for war.​​
Perhaps they've all become infected by war's relentless fever.

An insidious and chaotic war machine.
An embodiment of war and death, no one knows if it really exists or if it's a product of fear-filled delusions.

This land has thrived before,
And shall thrive again in days ahead.
But why, oh why, does it lie weeping today?

Beetles make their way across the scorched earth, their feelers trembling.
Where tin cans were buried by the barracks, wildflowers now grow.
Morning dew forms on rifle barrels, reflecting the faint glow of fading stars.
Ah, life continues, just as it always has, just as it always will.

At ease, attention, then back to the bloodshed.
The gunfire fades into a future cloaked in silence.

A body weighs more than a shell, yet a name becomes lighter than the dust.
Death moves among them without making a sound,
Granting the same eternal stillness to both body and dust.
All have sinned, and must pay their dues.
All have sinned, and must pay their dues—I stand counted among them.
I shall stand as watcher, as sentinel.
I shall stand as watcher, as sentinel, as a shield against the dark.
All wickedness shall be judged—and none shall go unaccounted.
Youth's dreams die here, on a hopeless path.
Youth's dreams die here, on a hopeless path, soldiers' eyes stare hollow and lifeless.
With their final cries, a hard-earned wisdom was shared.
With their final cries, a hard-earned wisdom was shared—savor the peace.
Until all bear it in their souls, war can never be forgotten.

Until the bombs fall.

Smoke drapes itself over memory, dark-red blood seeping through until everything turns a sallow gray. Under the cover of night, a trembling soldier lights a cigarette, its glow a small, defiant red. He hesitates before lifting it above the trench, waiting for the crack of a bullet.

Hands slip over his eyes. Murmured words in the dark melt fear into stillness, stillness into rapture. Terror leaves him at last.

He is back in a sweeter time: drums pound like hearts around him, hot drink scalds his throat. He spins and spins, ignoring the blood on his hands, shutting out the hoarse cries that break from his own mouth—clinging to this perfect instant.

Gunfire?

Stories are told of a soldier who placed such a poppy behind their ear for a nap. He dreamed of dim figures roaming the field around him—wandering aimlessly, faces open as if to wail but never making a sound.

Dark rain clouds gather over Europe.

Under that heavy sky, exhausted young men trudge forward like columns of ants, mechanically obeying their orders. At the word, they rise from their shelters, throwing themselves by the thousand into tempests of steel.
In shattered moments between the blast and before their screams, their bodies broken apart, and their last thoughts hanging on the warmth of summer and home.

Then something rises from the broken parts of a man. From above, it sees other young soldiers crying in pain on the battlefield. It watches as new bodies are pulled up from the line only to soak the next barrage of bullets. It sees charred trees and lifeless streets. It sees a mother's gaze fixed on the path where her child marched off to war. It passes children and the elderly huddled in abandoned fields. Then—at last—a white figure that moves calmly through the burned land, accompanied by a black horse.

The soul observes as this white figure lifts a body onto the horse's back. It watches them as they make their way through battlefields and fierce combat, leaving that hellish place for places still green and good. There, the figure takes each body and buries it in cold ground.

Where have all the young people disappeared to? The soul continues floating upward, dissolving into the thick white fog that now covers everything.

Dark clouds still hang over Europe. Countless raindrops form and begin to fall. And from that ground soaked with sorrow, tiny green shoots push their way through.

Throughout cosmic evolution, how many quests for truth have unfolded?
The geocentric model believed Earth stood motionless at the universe's heart, with all celestial bodies moving according to the theory of epicycles and deferents, each following its own path.
When Copernicus introduced his heliocentric model in 1543, its elegant simplicity challenged established powers who rejected it despite later historical vindication.
Generations of thinkers have knocked on the world's door with questions. They pursued answers through struggle, only to find each solution birthing new mysteries. Science and civilization have interlocked, evolving together to this day.
Inside the glass tank, the ferrofluid swirls in configurations that mimic possible cosmic structures.
Every question ultimately requires an answer, even if obtaining it means enduring endless self-torment—someone must shoulder this burden.

This place is far from barren. Instead, it is alive with laughter, music, and noise of all kinds, likely from a lively party.
The laughter comes again and again with one voice. The young speaker clears her throat. "At this wonderful moment ... oh, wait."
She adjusts her lopsided vine-woven wings. The fuzzy guests don't object, and neither do the "newlyweds" she casually left on the tree stump. The ceremony starts again—music plays, the couple enters, and the blessing angel clears her throat once more: "At this wonderful moment ..."
This time, the wings stay in place. The guests chatter excitedly, tossing handfuls of petals, while a few rush forward to get closer to say congratulations to the newlyweds.
"Nice and orderly, please. It's time for the next part of the story. Let me see ..." She passes the newlywed on the left to a fuzzy guest's waiting mouth. "On their wedding night, the groom's belly was ripped up ..."
Yet create their own hell through the barrels of their cannons and guns.
Gunpowder and flowers, echoing with the thunder of forged steel.
Shadows of life, memories of death, a lone walk along the Styx.
When the spring winds blow, their last embers of sorrow are swept away.

"She's gone. 3 months have passed since her last letter." As Flutterpage hurries down the steps, she hears an old woman speaking into the house. She hesitates, glancing back at the tilted mailbox with its noticeable crack—the reason the elderly woman often waits for her by the door.
Stamps are always in short supply during the war, and empty mailboxes have become the norm. Flutterpage had witnessed this quiet disappointment too many times. After a brief pause, she gently knocks on the door, presenting a primrose to the disappointed woman.
"Is this for me? How kind ... thank you, dear." Leaning on her walking stick, the woman steps outside the house. "I'm waiting for news—the kind that blooms like this flower."
Flutterpage lifts her gaze curiously. "You mean ...?"
"War lingers like the coldest winter. May peace arrive with the spring."
"I think I get it. When spring comes, I'll make sure you're the first to know—you can bet on it. Good news travels quick as anything on the wind ... and deliverin' is what I do best."
His past quest has ended, yet hope still beats deep within his chest.

This armor is designed to make a knight unstoppable on the field, forged by the Foundation's newest smith. When telling A Knight about the gear, J pulls out a thick stack of denied supply requests. "That last piece took 80 mithril bars! Hope our pals in 'Razor' Squad ain't too jealous—this set here is one-of-a-kind." Though someone notices J lacks even a hint of remorse.

Thanks to the infusion of powerful arcane metal, this armored shell provides enough protection for his high-risk solo missions. Though J always insists he prefers working with a team, when danger strikes, he consistently chooses to take the brunt of it himself, ensuring safer paths for his fellow teammates.
When A Knight asks about his reasons for making this armor, J simply smooths out the wrinkles on a blue ribbon, grips an old badge tightly, and suddenly poses an unexpected question: "Do you believe a new age is coming?"
The Wax and Wane of the Heart
Though the moon waxes and wanes, her heart holds true.

The moon hangs high in the night sky, uneasy, restless, and ever-changing.
She arrives by Death's invitation, moonlight draping over her like a delicate veil. Along twisting paths, she lingers near the windows of those destined to die.
No matter how lost or scared people feel, they cannot stop her visit—just as the dying cannot turn Death away, just as the moon must cycle through its phases.
Her song always comes before the funeral dirges, weaving through final words and confessions to create each lament anew. Some who study arcanum believe this is a sacred mourning ritual, perhaps tied to the moon's arcane influence on madness. Semmelweis, however, offers a different view: "Could it simply be an illusion born from the fear of death?"
The morning starts with encouraging news from the home front.

Beep, beep, beep ...
Ms. Radio is still unaccustomed to her new coating, yet much like her lingering distaste for relaying today's news.
Fresh reports of conflict and violence emerge daily, accompanied by the shriek of gunfire and thunder of explosions; the blood of the fallen runs like a wine-red river. Yet she does her duty. Critical intelligence awaits transmission; each piece may be the one that proves decisive in shifting the war's momentum.
This conflict demands victory—only through triumph can tomorrow arrive for all.

​​Here, nothing seems related to war, yet everything is.​
The watchers are now the watched.
With weapons raised, we speak as equals.
Each and every sin weighs the same.
Confess—even if no ear will ever hear it.
Prayers stretch out, reaching for a salvation that never arrives.
No regrets, no fear—only the hopeless finality of fate.
To fight again like carefree children at play.
In the end, we are drenched in suffering, blood, and tears.
As the skies clear, we climb the hillside to gaze at our distant home.
That wonderful place we can never go back to.
Run free, dream bold, leave doubts for another day.
"Abandon all hope, ye who enter here."​
There is deception hiding in the Bloody Sunset, with power to separate true diamonds from their imitations.
People move through an age of conflict, holding tight to their beliefs.
This war cannot be escaped—yet every soul prays for the moment when peace at last catches up.
Dawn Rises over the Kill Zone Survey Stage
Pray, for the kind will be rewarded and the wicked will be punished.
Green vines now grow along its barrel, its burned black iron covered in blossoms.
Creak—creak—The giant waits for the knight's arrival and the traveler's homecoming.
Day after day, year after year, befriending rats and dodging gunfire.
A simple fried onion is all it takes to awaken the lion within us.
These are golden peaks shimmering in emerald waters, and here new life emerges from devastation.
The red horse of war circles around aimlessly until the pale rider takes it home.
Apologies, I ... did not know you were there.
Is there something that you needed?​​
It is strange to feel nervous.
But given some time, there may be some peace to be found talking with you in this little world.
Even now, even like this, a roll of thunder causes muscles to seize and snap to attention—the reflexes of a soldier do not fade.​​
Things might feel a little awkward, but I want you to know I really appreciate you, Vertin.
You've created a peaceful space here, and it will be both a duty and an honor to protect it.
Thoughts come slowly and often wander.
This place is quiet. A fitting place for souls to rest.
Please tell me you aren't about to grab a shovel ...
That was not what was intended. It was only a notion, a stirring thought.
These are seeds meant to find this earth and grow.
They'll provide shade for those who lost their tomorrows.
I'm just enjoying the sunshine. It is a welcome respite from the grim smoke of the battlefield.
If it were possible, I'd bring every one of my fellow soldiers here to see this place.
Tell me, Vertin, have you ever traveled all the way to where this sea meets the horizon?
A common mistake—you're thinking of vampires. Our kind has always cherished sunlight.
Sunlight represents justice. Nothing wicked can escape its glow.
It is good to be in a place where nothing is destroyed without reason.
Only documenting what is here—all the companions to be found, you included.
Day after day, everything is documented.
From death springs new life in abundance.
You may pick one if you like; there is no harm, and they return soon after.
Just satisfying my curiosity, that's all.
Glad that you like this place.
My mistake. I was under the impression that Gargoyles couldn't stand sunlight.
That flower on your chest, Charon ... I've often wondered about it.

After returning from Antarctica, the tenth "Storm" has brought Team Timekeeper to an entirely different 1920 than they knew, one that does not match the history books.
Dressed in a rough approximation of a soldier's garb, Charon collects his fallen comrades across the battlefield. One warm thought burns under his cold skin—that the war may soon be over.
Ceasefire negotiations have hit a standstill. Military representatives, each convinced of their inevitable victory, have created a deadlock, until an unexpected bullet finds its mark ...
A young medic finds herself surrounded by unidentified troops in the forest. Outgunned and outnumbered, a mysterious sniper rescues her—then begins asking her questions.
The medic, the soldier, and the sniper all converge at the graveyard. But the assassin shows no hostility—she's simply come to mourn.
The sniper, known as "Sentinel," shares critical intelligence about Manus Vindictae. Meanwhile, "XII" Squad arrives in the now deserted Montpaix.
Two deserting soldiers flee toward the other side's trenches. Their commander, lost in a red haze of madness, orders them gunned down. Charon steps in to halt the slaughter.
Amidst silent graves, the Major slowly returns to himself. His recovery leads him to Montpaix, where he shares vital intelligence with the Foundation.
Guided by this information, Marsha and "XII" Squad's "Beagle" scout an abandoned village, only to find themselves caught in an ambush from an armored vehicle.​​
The Sentinel's timely intervention destroys the enemy vehicle. Yet in the chaos, enemy soldiers slip away, sparking a desperate pursuit across the Windmill Plain.
A battle from the past, a bloody clash that two soldiers survived. They once fought each other for a cause neither believed in. Now all that remains is memory.
Sentinel arrives at the Gargoyle Monastery with Marsha in tow—a rare place of shelter for what few kin she has left.
"XII" Squad receives critical intel delivered by Marsha, immediately sharing it with the delegates. Peace at last is on the horizon ... or is it?

Officials pour into Montpaix, gathering for the planned armistice. The soldiers at the front, digging into fresh deliveries of humanitarian supplies, are already celebrating. Certain that the war will soon be over ...
Charon arrives at the cemetery to meet with his old commander and comrades in arms. Both of them know that this will be the last time.
The end of this war was not as foretold, and so the peace they had longed for is greeted with great unease.
A beautiful horse gallops across the meadow under the shadow of the windmill, carrying Marsha and Marianne on his back. A moment of fragile beauty away from the horrors of war.
Manus Vindictae forces strike the safe zone. Turning the site of the armistice into one of violence and slaughter.
Manus forces launch their assault. Human soldiers, unequipped to face arcane skills, buckle under their relentless attack. Thankfully, "XII" Squad's captain already seems to have a plan.
Charon emerges from the underground passage. He makes no attempt to stop Sentinel—but he laments as she proceeds that these are the gates of hell.
Sentinel proceeds deeper into the underground fortress. Above ground, the captain of the "XII" Squad scans the battlefield looking for some kind of turning point.

Fighting side by side with the "Demon," Sentinel destroys Manus Vindictae's bunker.
She resists the "Demon," despite its promise of power. Every move and every defeated foe falls by her own will.
Gargoyles seldom change, yet they've known nothing but upheaval. As long as the fires of war burn, Sentinel feels unable to truly return home.
The Hawks have gained power, the Storm Reformation Act has been amended, and there's new intel on Urd ... a tangled mess of factors now threatens to shake the fragile eastern front.

While the assassination in the safe zone is regrettable. Based on current findings, we've determined there were no failures in our security protocols. Still, we intend to pursue the suspect and further study their methods so that we can improve safeguards to prevent future incidents.

The ominous boom of artillery rolls again beyond the horizon.
Once more, we can't tell who is attacking or defending. And we never know whether a stray shell will fall on our heads and blow the whole place to bits.
That war's miles away, but I swear the chaos and gunfire sound like they're right here in my ear.
 ...
Kinda hungry. Think I'll get some hot onion soup.

There is an unspoken cause of death for officers on the battlefield: killed by their own men.
There are many reasons. If morale is low, some troops may turn their anger on the brass. Deserters get caught and lash out to survive. Far too often, an officer barks out a seemingly suicidal order, and his men turn their guns on him instead.
Facing the extremes of war, this kind of treachery can feel not just excusable but entirely human.

Even in modern times, knights in heavy armor still march onto the battlefield. Forming solid lines, holding back wave after wave of enemy assaults. With arcane skills, they support the front lines.
Until the day comes when artillery fire swallows the field whole, they remain the best protection for foot soldiers.

That monastery hasn't seen use in ages. There's a war going on outside, and the place doesn't even have a proper roof.
But sometimes the smell of warm pastries drifts out from inside, along with whispers.
I couldn't hold back my curiosity, so one day I snuck in using a bit of my clumsy arcane skill.
I saw a statue there of a crying girl, so lifelike, more vivid and beautiful than anything I've seen from so-called master sculptors.
That evening, when I got home, I was scolded by my father. He told me I shouldn't use arcane skills I hadn't mastered yet and that if I wasn't careful, I could bring disaster.

Investigation into the News Media Montpaix is to be the site of the armistice signing, yet it was also the place where Colonel Hirschfelder was assassinated. Some "safe zone." Is there really any reason to come here again? I guess sometimes all you need is a good name, a story, a symbol. "Peace built on bloodshed." "Someone gave their life for this day." "This place carries the people's hope for peace." I can already imagine the headlines. Either way, I won't complain about an end to the war. Guess I'd better think of a headline that's not too cliché.

My Dearest Coline,
I don't even know how to feel writing this. The front has gone quiet, and the higher-ups are about to sign an armistice. The war's ending. I should be coming home to you.
That's how it was supposed to be.
But I haven't been able to sleep. Night after night, I hear the shelling in my dreams. I see men in black masks and uniforms storming our trenches, slaughtering us.
I jolt awake every time, and can't fall back asleep. One night ... I don't know why ... I ran.
I'm a deserter now. I may never see you again. I'm not even sure how I'll get this to you. But however it is delivered, know that it holds all my love for you.

Someone once said that war is diplomacy at its worst.
The shift from war to peace is never linear. It spirals, doubles back, filled with contradictions. It's a lot like how diplomacy works.
Everyone's hoping for the armistice to be signed. But maybe once this war ends, new battles will start elsewhere. Old flames might be reignited by human hands. Maybe nothing will change.
Even so, when I look at these dying soldiers lying in their beds, I feel we still need to believe that true peace will come.

What did I see?
The sky was blood red. The ground was covered in stakes like grave markers. The rivers ran with thick, crimson sludge. Was that really just mud?
No comrades, no enemies, only me, trapped in this horrific mire. Oh ... and the Demon in the distance. And that shadow hidden in the dark smoke? That ominous face? Did you see it? No, of course, you're not here.
This is the battlefield. This is my war. But what exactly am I fighting?

A filthy, torn-up doll lies abandoned in the corner of the monastery. None of the Gargoyles ever paid it any mind, yet it was packed with the rest of their luggage.
It'll never again be some little girl's favorite toy. But maybe it'll find a new home, on a windowsill in the sun.

At first, the children were excited. They knew about fireworks but had never seen any. The first day, it seemed almost like a show.
But then it continued for a second day. A third. And more. The booming never stopped. And as the booms crept closer and the ground began to shake, their voices went from wonder to irritation to fear.
Then the sounds stopped. All the sounds stopped. 
There were no voices asking about fireworks. 
No voices left to ask.
