"Who went with you to the chapel?"
"A few young guys and one of the housewives from the next village. She keeps complaining there's no food and that she can't go home. I wouldn't exactly call them devout."
"... I see. For humanitarian reasons, St. Pavlov Foundation will provide some emergency aid to civilians affected by the war. Do you have any requests?"
"Ah ... food. My prayers have been answered once more."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

So far, we still haven't fully understood Manus Vindictae's activities in the Antarctic, nor the impact of the "Flood." Given the current situation, we require a more detailed and complete report from someone present during the event.

To: Rational Ferrofluid

"Field reports, experiment reports, budget forms, overage slips, fuel bills ... I've written so many reports and signed my name more times than I can count. I wish someone cared how I feel ... but considering how important communication is, maybe there really are key things missing from my reports."
"Once I submit this last one, I think I'll go sit in a different vessel for a while, just to reset and get back in the work mindset again."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

The Foundation is optimistic about the future of Artificial Somnambulism. To provide better logistical support for Team Timekeeper, we hope to receive a technical report summarizing all relevant experiments carried out on them so far.

To: Paranoid Researcher

"Seems like even the Foundation has a sense of humor, wanting to get their hands on Artificial Somnambulism ... It's a diagnostic method at its best, a scientific technique to evaluate mental health. It doesn't have much to do with what arcanists deal with. The fact that they even want this tech just proves how bad things have gotten out there. But I'm not handing over any report. Why? Simple, I don't care for irrational arcanists."

From: Z

The Hawks are inclined to intervene in this war through military means, which will inevitably involve recruitment. We need to act before they do and identify arcanists who could strengthen the Foundation's show of force. We cannot allow this war to escalate unchecked.

To: Top Prodigy

"Mr. J from Haight Street is ... gutsy, I do believe he would accept such a mission. Ms. Flutterpage could be a skilled messenger. While Ms. Radio would be adept at picking up signals from the battlefield ..."
"It seems that Madam Z wants to make contact with these arcanists before the Hawks get to them, so they don't end up fueling the flames of war. This is all part of the internal power struggle within the Foundation. For the Timekeeper's sake, I should probably keep this quiet."

From: Irinei

Manus Vindictae is plotting to cause unspeakable chaos and war in this era. To oppose them, we need to form an army of our own. I believe your convictions will lead you to lend us your strength.

To: Knight of Haight Street

"To be honest, I didn't feel much connection to the Foundation at first. But they are doing the right thing, and it's where Paulina once chose to go ... Working with them is a hundred times better than brawling with scummy gangsters in alleyways."
"My Bowie knife's greatest purpose is to slit the throats of Manus Vindictae and to help folks when they need it. So if this job means protecting the innocent, count me in."

From: Pedra

Given the threat posed by Manus Vindictae, the front urgently needs arcane items capable of countering them. We hope we can put aside our differences and work together again.
We'll arrange to deliver the payment to your designated location in the coming days.

To: The Ageless Merchant

"The Foundation's back with another big order. I was going to turn them down because they're hard to please ... but the person in charge this time seems like a reasonable gentleman. I think this will be an interesting deal, hehe."
"As for these 'Arcane-Blocking Helmets,' they only said they needed to 'block arcane skills,' they didn't say 'how many times.' So this batch should meet their expectations. As a gesture of goodwill, I'll just take a deposit this time."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation, Logistics Department

Immediate need for more personnel! We urgently need bold, brave, and fearless folks to deliver letters from the rear lines to safe zones near the front! These include family letters and classified military mail, which are extremely important!
Generous rewards offered.

To: Odd Errand Kid

"This job's kind of hard, but also not that hard. Just like walking the streets of East London, I can hide in the bushes to dodge bad guys or climb to the rooftops to avoid wild beasts. I need a bigger backpack. A really, really big backpack, because I've got to carry lots and lots of letters. I'm supposed to take them to a place called the "safe zone" ... Oh, will there be a big cart to take me there? Then at least I can nap on the way."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

The situation on the front is grim. But to develop countermeasures and preserve these records for the future, we need someone to organize and archive the current footage.
We recommend close cooperation with the war photographers on the frontlines.

To: Zealous Investigator

"Maybe I should stop joking about being an 'obsessive nerd' because they've started treating me like one. Isn't organizing files something for the office clerks to do? Why'd they give it to me ... Oh, I get it. They just can't handle all the bloody, gruesome stuff. Makes sense! A logical job assignment! Now I'm actually looking forward to seeing what that ghostly guy can do."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

The Foundation hopes to stay as informed as possible on front-line developments, so we need a large amount of real-time visual data. After much deliberation, we've decided to assign this task to you.
Given your physique, we believe this won't be too difficult.

To: Ghost Photographer

"... The shooting conditions on the Western Front are dreadful. Poor lighting, and so much mud—it will affect the quality of the photos ... The only good part is the lack of sunlight. It doesn't hurt my eyes."
"Bombs are dropping everywhere. Screams and curses constantly ring in my ears ... I need to protect my camera so I don't miss a good moment."
"... Hm? My health? Don't worry. It's ... not important."

From: "XII" Squad

Innumerable radio signals are transmitted from the front every day, but due to the technological limitations of this era, we're unable to receive all of them.
We request that you lend your talents to help us receive as many as you can, especially any distress calls from soldiers!

To: A Certain Radio

[Bzzzzt—]
"Tuning, tuning ... There are so many messy signals at the front. I need more time to sort and receive them. But I'll do my best."
"Also, please, please promise me that you won't try to boost my reception by trying to swap my batteries. It only makes things worse. Remember that these tasks should be handled with patience."

To Lt. Lopera,
Zeno HQ has received your field mission request. However, due to the current instability on the Western Front and your prior record, we are unable to approve it.
As circumstances allow, we will assign you to a future mission. In the meantime, you are ordered to take care of those circumstances.

"They used to fall over themselves to send me out, and now they won't even let me leave? What the hell are those Zeno pencil-pushers thinking ... Dammit ... Father and Moldir are still out there, and they've left me behind ... No matter what, I have to find them and get some answers."
"What else am I supposed to do ..."

From: Laplace

The Foundation has recently acquired a batch of arcane items via trade, but due to a lack of proper communication, the delivered items failed to meet expectations. We have reallocated these items to Laplace in order to enhance their effects.
Given the time constraints, we'll send additional support staff to assist. Early delivery is desired.

To: Strange Machinery Expert

"I can only express remorse that this situation occurred. Rather than excoriating the merchant, I can't help but think this is a result of Foundation bureaucracy."
"Back to the main issue, portable arcanum-blocking equipment, tough and durable ... a tricky challenge, but I can add some fun ideas. Like a three-button control panel, and a top hatch on the helmet that opens to release a pair of doves ..."

From: Laplace

The arcane items under development must be simple in form and easy to use. To prevent the machinery expert from inserting his trademark eccentricities into our final product, we need a professional to oversee the design and ensure timely delivery.

To: Tech Expert

"4f6e2069742e" The following is a full translated response from John Titor via IDM5100: "This is a simple task. It's no harder than developing IDM5100. The only concern is that this wearable device wasn't supposed to be invented until 1920. Our results might carry additional risk. If Laplace has fully assessed that and found no issues, I'll accept the task."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

To track the movements of Manus Vindictae, per the request of the captain of "XII" Squad, the logistics department has dispatched a package of wartime radio parts and paint to the front. Please perform any additional custom modifications as needed and continue your signal reception task.

To: Radio in Wartime Outfit

"All I did was install a special antenna, and now my reception has massively improved ... It looks like the Foundation has impressive technical capability. I've learned something new again."
"Now then, let me test things out ... Field News Flash: Still annoyed by this gloomy weather? Try Umbra Co.'s latest umbrella ... Uh, I still need a bit more time to calibrate, so please don't mind me ... Oh, the paint job? That's to match my identity as a 'field radio.' Once the job is done, I'll return to the War Room. Don't worry."

From: Irinei

Given the chronal chaos, we hold no expectations for Zeno's military capacity, but we must still assess their actual remaining forces.
Our end goal is to maintain an army under the Foundation's command.

To: Cadet Under Review

"Aloha! Anyone there? I'm here to deliver the report! Hmm? Is someone there? No one? Really, no one? Where do I hand this report in? Let me see ... Hmm ... What does it say here? Do I deliver it to the Secretary's Office? Or maybe the Internal Affairs Department? Or maybe the front desk? Hey, I got it! I'll just leave it right on the steps by the door, so that way anyone coming in will see it first thing! Hah, that's that! Nothing to stress over. Mission complete!"

From: "XII" Squad

We've confirmed the presence of Gargoyles on the battlefield. We lack solid details on their taxonomy. We request that you travel to the old monastery they inhabit and use your arcane skills to "read" the area and gather more information.

To: Foundation Agent

Marcus activates arcane skills and enters the world of reading "Reality is like a book. Everything can be read if you know how ..." "Spilled tea. Crumbs from a cookie dropped on the floor ... signs of life. They lived here, their eating habits no different from humans." "Flakes of skin like stone, one of their traits ... Is that blood? No, marks left by prolonged kneeling." "A weeping statue? So realistic ... no more than that, it was once alive!" "... Seems as though I have a long report to write."

From: Pedra

Following the recent attack, frontline soldiers captured several loitering individuals near the safe zone. Their testimonies confirm that Manus Vindictae was involved.
Please deliver this report to our representative at the safe zone.

To: Loyal Scout

"Good morning. I'm Eagle, tasked with delivering this report. It's from Foundation HQ and contains further details concerning the recent incident."
"Um ... yes, I'm a Scout, currently stationed with Lorenz—I mean, Laplace."
"... Y-you want my ID? I-I'm sorry, I don't have it right now. But ... please contact Mr. X at Laplace. H-he can vouch for me ..."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation Logistics Department

After reviewing recent tasks, we've made the decision to formally hire you as our official messenger.
Your first task will be to distribute mail and critical information to civilians near the frontlines.

To: Foundation Courier

"A new job, ay? How much are you payin'? And exactly where am I goin'?"
"People look so happy whenever they see me. They gather around, waiting for the messages I've been carryin', and then the smile as they open 'em up, like those people I used to wake up for work."
"The grown-ups at the Foundation call me a "carrier pigeon," guess they mean it funny-like, but I think it suits me."

From: Z

With battles still raging all over, we would request that Ms. Bouanich perform a reading to see how the present situation will unfold.
No matter the result, we believe that there can still be a peaceful future for this era.

To: Star Investigator

"Hmph! The Foundation once again returns to the astounding talents of Star Investigator Matilda Bouanich. But of course! A vision from the best, the most brilliant Matilda ... Huh? There is nothing ... N-no! It must be because the Orbuculum's a bit cloudy ... Zut! Let's try again."
"The Eastern Front is too far, I am afraid I cannot see much of anything yet. As for the Western Front ... something odd seems to be happening within some hilltop fortress? Perhaps Manus Vindictae will appear there ... It seems someone else's arcane skills are interfering. That is all I can see for now ..."

To Ms. Recoleta
Our editorial team is once again honored to receive your submission. We must say this new piece differs significantly from your past work, filled with sincere reflections on war and peace. We find it deeply thought-provoking.
After the war ends, we hope you'll visit us to discuss future publication.

"Huh? I submitted something? I don't recall ... Could it have been that short story I sent to Vertin? I'd just drafted an early novel concept and wanted her feedback ... Did I send it to the wrong place? How ..."
"They actually liked that draft ... Well, first drafts are always the best and the worst ... Please forgive me. In any case, that's not a draft fit for publication!"

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

There's a large amount of <s>junk</s> on the battlefield left from a recent encounter. Please head out and recover what you can. It may help us analyze the progression of the war or, at the very least, assess potential soil contamination.

To: <s>Junk</s> Collection Expert

"This place reminds me of life before the Foundation. Back then, the streets were filled with strangers. No one ever tried to connect; we'd just avoid glancing at one another and walk on."
"War feels a lot like that. Everyone's tense, dreading the day, worried that it might be their last. Their faces dull, anxious about tomorrow, tired, and hungry."
"But in places like this, scrap and trash become useful. No need for fancy titles. What matters is the story they tell about what happened here."

From: Former Knight

I hope you'll pardon my unsolicited letter. I understand that you are a psychotherapist who uses arcane skills to treat patients. The front has many soldiers suffering from shell shock, and innocent civilians have been affected as well. I believe they need your help.

To: Idealistic Doctor

"I remember reading about a great war in a book I borrowed from Marcus. Is this the war? It feels even crueler than what I've read ... So many people trapped in the gloom, with no path forward."
"The 'Storm' brings chaos, but war is a man-made disaster. If my treatment can help even a little, I'll gladly offer it."

From: "XII" Squad

We've heard you've accepted Commissioner Irinei's mission to deliver a "declaration of force." Before that, we'd like you to head to the Windmill Plain and discreetly locate a former knight. As a "fellow knight", we trust you'll complete this task with ease.

To: "Wolf Knight" of the Foundation

"This wide plain is so lovely! You'd never see this kind of view in the concrete jungle of Haight Street. Still, this terrain isn't ideal for motorcycles. Better find this 'lady knight' quickly and head back. If I do get spotted, let's just hope she won't be startled by the gear I'm wearing."
"Oh right, formality's sake: May the peace be with us, haha."

From: Irinei

Reading through the Zeno cadets' reports, it's clear our current forces aren't enough to face Manus Vindictae. Though some commissioners are hesitant about deploying animal-based units, in desperate times, they may be our only option for certain special missions ...

To: Animal Friends

"Would you look at that! Who woulda thought the Foundation would turn to squirrels and penguins in their time of need? What d'ya figure they want? A couple of tactical assault penguins guarding office doors? Or maybe they need a rodent to get the lowdown on classified intel? Heck, I just barely survived an Antarctic flood, I reckon I don't need any more crazy experiences before I turn twelve!"
"... Hold on, ain't nobody told me the Foundation was offerin' unlimited peeled chestnuts, pine cones, and vet services in return! L-let me think on it ..."

From: Laplace

Due to the influence of arcanum from Manus Vindictae's forces, a peculiar fungus has sprouted near Hill 299 along the Western Front. Researchers are en route. Please be prepared to receive new samples.

To: The Wrecker of Laplace

"An arcanum-affected fungal strain? Sounds fun. I'll need a full setup: iron stands, Petri dishes, distiller, temperature-controlled bath ... and a whole room to fit it all in. But where can I get one ...? Oh—Adler's old room is still empty. Perfect. From now on, that's my lab. Approval? I just approved it."

From: Laplace

The fungus found near Hill 299 seems to share arcane properties with the black algae previously discovered in Antarctica. Please proceed with caution as you collect samples.

To: Fungal Researcher

"The air is really humid, and the soil's damp too ... Under these conditions, mycelium grows faster. Looks like I can find a lot of the species mentioned in the report. But it hasn't rained recently. Why's the environment like this? Could it really be from arcane interference? If so, is this a side effect of the incantation?"
"Ugh ... no time to space out. This place is still dangerous. Best to finish quickly. Medicine Pocket is waiting on my samples."

From: Pedra

Manpower on the frontlines is stretched thin. We need all hands to support present operations and stop Manus Vindictae's schemes.
Also, an outstanding payment needs to be delivered; please handle it en route to the front.

To: Guest Teacher

"Given my current role, this task shouldn't fall to me. Still, I understand the Foundation's predicament ... My capabilities are quite limited at times like this, but ... Ahem—'A blessing in disguise,' as they say. If I'm to act as a courier, this won't be too hard, and who knows, maybe I'll find some rare Western European porcelain on the way ..."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

We understand you are no longer an employee of the Foundation, and we have no grounds to force your cooperation. But if there is any hope to end the conflict and expose Manus Vindictae's conspiracy, we find ourselves in need of your keen investigative skills and the talents of your people to gather intelligence on the frontlines.

To: Former Investigator

"Looks like the supplies meant for the frontline troops didn't make it in time. They wouldn't come to me unless things were really this dire."
"... Heh, the frontlines, huh? Seems like a place to enjoy a feast ... Er, no, that's a bit rude to the soldiers. I should bring some chocolates. Neptune brand's supposed to be good ... I'll head out as soon as the evening permits. No need for my colleagues to see me off."

From: Irinei

The war is over. What people need now is a solemn ceremony to mark the arrival of peace. To meet that need, and to affirm the Foundation's presence and stance, we ask you to draw on your experience and help prepare this ceremony.

To: Chief Representative

"If this were just another defense line parade, all I'd need is the ceremonial uniform, practiced steps, and enough drills to commit it to muscle memory ... But this time is different. This ceremony declares the power of the St. Pavlov Foundation to the world. The expectations will be stricter, and the process more complex ... I wonder if my old parade notes might still be of help ..."

To Ms. Regulus
We have received your complaint regarding the treatment of the Timekeeper's team. Objectively, they already have full operational authority and logistical support from the Foundation. The Storm Act will also be further amended. We will not be processing your complaint any further.
After the Foundation's Logistics Department dismissed her complaint, the enraged Regulus blasted rock music in her room for an entire day while cursing nonstop to vent her frustration.

To Madam Lucy,
Long time no see; hope you're enjoying your vacation. Given where you are, I'm sure you've heard whispers of the situation on the Western Front.
I know you're under no formal obligation, but I'd like to hear your thoughts on this war. Let's call it a casual conversation between "old friends."

You knew I was on vacation and sent this letter anyway ... I cannot grasp your reasoning.

If I happened to be recharging, I might very well have missed your letter entirely. A message not received cannot be replied to, which means the sender wastes time and energy. Perhaps even more should they need to rewrite and resend a new letter to get a response.

Even so, you are asking for the opinion of an "old friend" who stepped off your "chessboard" long ago?

I am afraid I am not extensively versed in warfare or strategy. And I fail to see what scientific benefits exist in testing the unknown variables of war one by one.

Yet, as a courtesy for an "old friend," I will consider giving you a more in-depth response later.

The following is a report compiled by Foundation administrative staff. Upon returning from Antarctica to Foundation HQ, the Timekeeper underwent a special psychological test conducted by Ms. Mesmer Jr. The results showed no abnormalities. Afterward, the Timekeeper learned from Madam Z that the 10th "Storm" in Antarctica had transported everyone to a different 1920. In this new era, a war that should have long been over is still raging. The Foundation refers to the event as a "chronal distortion," and two internal factions have since emerged: the Dove Faction, which favors diplomacy, and the Hawk Faction, which believes in fighting fire with fire.

Upon hearing Lilya was being sent to the Eastern Front, the Timekeeper and Sonetto came to see her off. When the topic of the Dove-Hawk dispute came up, Lilya expressed disinterest, then invited Vertin to join her, longing to see the vast eastern grasslands with her own eyes.
Currently, the Timekeeper's team is grounded, but due to recent shifts inside the Foundation, she may be able to win them more operational rights.
Outside the office, the Timekeeper meets the captain of "XII" Squad, Creius, for the first time. He seems interested in establishing deeper cooperation.

With the Western Front stabilizing, revisions to the Storm Reform Act are now underway. Thanks to recent events, the Hawks have gained influence and strongly support expanding the Timekeeper's team rights and budget—an advantage for her.
Back at HQ, Creius meets the Timekeeper again and reveals he holds intel related to "Urd," piquing her interest.
Sonetto delivers Lilya's contact info. There's trouble brewing on the Eastern Front too.

"Foundation, parley, Hirschfelder ... today." A young woman in a grayish blue soldier uniform enters the forest outskirts of the Montpaix safe zone. The soldier waiting there grows suspicious and confronts her, only to be killed instantly. He carries a map pouch containing intelligence and, most importantly, an arrival time. Exactly what she came for.

"We chance to meet again, young chevalière?" The soldier in a grayish blue uniform arrives at Charon's cemetery. Gravestones now mark the once-disordered ground, giving it the feel of a true "cemetery"—stones placed by her hand. She stands before a monument, head bowed in prayer, ignoring the barbed questions of the woman beside her. Finally, she lifts her gaze and meets Marsha's wary eyes.

"And perhaps ... on that day when peace finally comes, you will return to us?" Under the cover of night, the soldier called "Sentinel" walks into a forest where her fellow Gargoyles await. Ladislas, a male Gargoyle, worries about her recent "crime" and fears she's falling into darkness. After a tense conversation, "Sentinel" enters a petrified state to rest. A soft voice reaches her ears. In this dreamlike state, she speaks with an unseen person. Her voice then turns soft and gentle.

"Even if this war was, as you believe, a divine punishment, the people have suffered enough." After the battle, Marianne brings Marsha to the Gargoyle Monastery. Her kin welcome Marsha kindly, except for her cousin Ladislas, who reacts with fear. As tensions rise, Marianne hands Marsha a key lead: proof of Manus Vindictae's collusion with military higher-ups on both sides. This evidence is the reason they came.

"All is well. You may stay—so long as you do not lie." As the armistice nears, Marianne returns to the monastery. Ladislas, disillusioned by how the war defied prophecy, kneels at the altar in regret and refuses food. Marianne tries to speak to him, but he only offers silence in return. Later, Marsha returns, bringing food and vital intel from the front. After exchanging updates, the two decide to take a walk through the Windmill Plain.

"If I must sin to fulfill my sacrifice, then so be it." Guided by the "Hound" Yermolai, Marianne arrives at the Hill 299 fortress to execute Creius's plan. Before the bunker's door, she encounters Charon emerging from a cloud of poison gas. He questions her intentions, but to Marianne, her own sins mean little compared to the suffering of others. She will not stop here.

"I'm sorry, Agnès." The "Demon" bombards Marianne with illusions—the dead, fallen comrades, and Marsha. It tries to lure her into corruption. But Marianne holds firm. Every choice up to now was her own. The Demon has nothing to do with it. Amid vivid hallucinations, she drives her bayonet into the "Demon." She will bear all the sin herself.

"Tell my father I will not return ... until the true conflict is brought to an end." Marianne returns to the Gargoyle Monastery. Her father arrives to share their family's plans for the future, including moving to Paris. He also explains the truth behind a past incident affecting their kin. Marianne says nothing, but she has already chosen her path. Not to Paris. To the next battlefield.

"The name you see there doesn't belong to this war any longer." Charon sees it as his duty to collect his fallen comrades and handle their burials. As the war intensifies. Bodies pile up. With his horse, Andreas, missing, the work grows harder. His superior sends him to the safe zone to fetch a package, and so he makes his way to Montpaix. There, Charon meets a Foundation medic named Marsha. She tells him of a nearby hill that could serve as a graveyard and offers to take him there.

"There was no ill intent. The ways of this war do not fall upon your shoulders." Led by Marsha, Charon arrives at the hill she spoke of. Curious about her past, he prepares to ask, but she reveals it first: she was once a knight fighting in the war. Charon apologizes for his careless words. Then the two part ways.

"I ... don't want you to see what lies beneath ... Please, look away." Charon returns to the trenches. On watch, another soldier spots two deserters from the enemy's side approaching. Charon suggests letting them in—reasoning that they do not wish to fight. However, Major Braun suspects a trap and orders them shot. He's on the verge of madness, even threatening his own men. In desperation, Charon releases something called "Terror" from within himself, and Major Braun collapses.

"I am in no position to stop you ... from walking through the gates of hell." Charon follows the cloud of death to the trenches near Hill 299, where he faces Sentinel. The poison gas seems not to affect the grave digger, as he shuffles forward. He understands why Sentinel came, but has no intention of interfering. Though he may not want to see more death, he can feel the difference in this new battle. And death does not make a distinction between arcanist and human. As they part ways, he leaves Sentinel with these words: "I feel a deep sadness for you."

"Your war is over, Paul." The front grows quiet. Soon, there are no more souls to guide. With his task complete, Charon buries the last of Paul on the hill beside his friends. His horse Andreas returns, joined by "Blackbird" Merel, who chooses to accompany them. Brought together by fate, the three now form a small fellowship. Their journey leads them toward the Eastern Front.

"I ... can't tell you what to do, Eberhard." Paul and Eberhard were classmates before joining the army together, friends before they were comrades. They supported one another through the horrors of battle and shared each other's sorrow as their friends fell around them. Their connection only grew stronger. After waking from his terror, Eberhard loses the last of his strength. As the past comes flooding back, in that moment, he forgets his pride as an officer and reaches out to Paul with desperate hands. But the figure he reaches for isn't fully Paul anymore. Charon has lost the ability to see what lies ahead for those who survive, and he has no power to change the course of fate. Still, he chooses to stay with his friend, holding on to the hope that even such a small act might shift the direction of the war.

"With best regards. A dead man." Carrying Herr Mühlenberge's letter addressed to Class 3, Paul steps towards the graves where Eberhard waits for him. They talk about the past, and for a time, Paul finds memories he long thought lost—bicycle rides in the chill of winter, shared boredom and passed notes during Latin classes, their days at school. As Paul reads out the letter, the boys cannot help but laugh at their professor's rambling phrases and all-too-familiar quotes attributed to long-dead men. In that moment, Eberhard lets go. Paul promises that he will write back to Herr Mühlenberge. After their goodbyes, Eberhard leaves the graveyard. The reply will not come easily. Its words, together with a single gunshot, will write the final chapter for their story ... and for the people who lived it.

"Victory lies ahead, ready for the taking!" Major Braun commands the front, burning with determination to destroy the enemy once and for all. His faith in this coming victory borders on manic. There is no reason in his words, only fire. After delivering his speech in the trenches of the second company, he drops down from the firing platform and leads a further cadre down the line. It appears that keeping morale high has become the commander's most essential task.

"That was an order, soldier. You are to shoot that foreign devil." Two enemy deserters approaching their trench have raised the tension in the line to a fever pitch. Though the men agree that they should let them in, Major Braun rages, insisting their surrender is a ruse. He orders a soldier to open fire on them, eventually raising his pistol to aim at his own men. Charon makes his appearance with near moments to spare before there is further bloodshed, though when his efforts to sway the Major fail, he is forced to reveal his face, spreading a strange mist that fills the men nearby with terror. When the mist dissipates, Major Braun lies on the ground unconscious. Though the remaining deserter is brought to safety, the spectacle ends on a somber and bitter note.

"Just as it always was ... hm ... Well said. Farewell, mein Freund!" Eberhard is calm, as if the madness that once consumed him has vanished completely. There among the gravestones, he and Paul start to recall old times. The old memories flooding back—as they talk about the town they grew up in, their lessons, and the teacher who had taught them both. When their conversation reaches the topic of that teacher, Eberhard gives Paul the letter he has been holding. It was written by the head teacher for all of their graduating class. The two of them are the only ones left to read it. The quiet of this place does nothing to bring Eberhard peace. Each name etched in stone around them marks the sinking depths of his guilt. He asks Paul to write a reply to their old teacher, then tells him that he needs some time alone. And so he walks away from the war and says goodbye to his friend. Returning only to fill an empty grave.

"I'm Nurse Marsha." Marsha, a medic from the Foundation, runs into Charon as he arrives at the safe zone to collect a personal package for his commander. During their talk, Charon raises concerns about the lack of proper burial places for fallen soldiers. After hearing this, Marsha recalls a spot just outside the safe zone. The two decide to go there together.

"Wait, you know Hirschfelder? Do you have any idea who shot him?" As Marsha heads back toward the safe zone, she receives a cryptic message about the assassination that has taken place there: the shooter may still be in the same woods she is walking through. She watches the surroundings closely as she makes her way back to town, but before she can get far, she is ambushed by armed soldiers with no clear allegiance. Brave but outgunned, just as things turn for the worse, a series of precise shots takes out her attackers. Marsha looks up and spies a sniper high above in the trees, rifle still raised. She cannot help but make the connection that this shooter may be the very sniper that she was warned about. Yet their brief conversation leaves Marsha with more questions than answers.

"You seem to mourn the dead, but you don't realize how far you've set us back? We were nearing a ceasefire." The mysterious sniper arrives at the graveyard to pay her respects. Afterwards, she responds tersely to Marsha's questions. As they exchange words, Charon expresses a growing concern about his commander's well-being. The discussion between the three of them ends without any clear resolution.

"Wait, Sentinel!" Marsha survives the surprise attack launched by Manus Vindictae, but the shock and blood loss leave her struggling to stay conscious. Once she manages to steady herself, she attempts to follow "Sentinel." What she finds is a desperate soldier from Manus with no way out, preparing to end his own life, and not far from him, "Sentinel" lies wounded, her stony body scarred with multiple gunshots.

"But that battle is long over. You and I are no longer enemies." Injured from the fighting, the two young women find a quiet spot in the forest to rest. Marsha confirms that the two of them had once been on opposite sides of a battle. She explains that after their fight, she stopped serving her Order and eventually joined the Foundation, choosing a new path as a medic dedicated to saving lives. In response, Sentinel reveals her true name, Marianne. Confiding in Marsha, who seems different from what she has come to expect from people connected to the Foundation. Although she still has doubts about the organization itself, Sentinel makes the choice to offer Marsha her help.

"I'll come find you after you move. How does that sound?" At the Windmill Plain, the two finally find the chance to talk not just as soldiers but as ordinary people. Marianne shares her dream of one day running a clothing shop in Paris. Marsha admits that she will likely be reassigned soon. But a sudden burst of Marsha's radio ends their brief repose. A message calls her back to the front without delay.

"Feel free to call on me if you find yourself in need, Timekeeper." Walking through the Foundation headquarters corridors, Creius, the captain of the "XII," has his first encounter with Vertin. He had heard of her before the mission to Antarctica and is now seeking the chance to speak with her directly, hoping they might work together. He seems especially drawn to her unique role as the "Timekeeper." After their brief meeting, he receives a report from one of his squad members, Yermolai—about unusual activity from Manus Vindictae. Creius quickly orders his team into action, though he is unable to join them until his field request is officially approved.

"So, you're asking me to share the result of my investigation to root out the rotten apples in your army." With authorization granted by the Foundation, the "XII" proceeds into the abandoned Montpaix safe zone to carry out their investigation. Although most of the valuable assets have already been removed, they are still able to reconstruct several crucial clues from what remains. During this time, the field medic Marsha meets with Creius and passes along information regarding a mysterious informant and the presence of the Gargoyle sniper. These revelations significantly narrow their search for the assassin's identity. At the same time, Georg, a representative from the Inter-Factional Committee, arrives secretly just beyond the boundaries of the active search zone. In a private exchange with Creius, he voices his concerns about the growing control of Manus Vindictae over the military. Hoping to pave the way for upcoming peace talks, Georg asks for Creius's assistance in uncovering credible proof that links Manus to direct involvement in armed forces.

"We'll dig up whatever they have buried." After hearing what Eberhard revealed in Montpaix, Creius contacts the higher-ups at the Foundation. The verified signs of Manus's involvement in military affairs lead him to report the secret visit made to him by the head of the Inter-Factional Committee. He pushes the leadership to move forward with the suggested plan for launching renewed peace talks. However, in order to truly persuade the decision-makers, his squad needs to secure more concrete evidence than Eberhard's words alone.

"I need someone coordinating the defense of this town should the Manus attack." Following up on the intel provided by Eberhard, Creius orders his squad to begin sweeping the specified locations. Among them, an abandoned village is marked as a key target, and "Beagle" Paravyan and Marsha are assigned to investigate it. Meanwhile, "Blackbird" Merel is tasked with holding the rear at Montpaix, positioned to intercept any sudden attacks that Manus might attempt. An unspoken question lingers on Creius's mind: is Merel a trustworthy squadmate, or is she still unready to stand on her own?

"Follow me. We're going to the front lines. You can fill me in on the details on the way." Creius, now serving as the Foundation's frontline commander in Montpaix, feels no sense of relief even with the armistice on the horizon. The investigators sent to Hill 299 failed to report in and have not responded to any attempts at contact. It's clear that something dire is happening there. His suspicions are confirmed the moment the first shot is fired, as Manus soldiers launch a sudden attack on the safe zone, nearly overpowering the Foundation's security team. But as the situation reaches a breaking point, Yermolai arrives and eliminates both the enemy commander and the attacking troops. Thanks to his timely intervention, Creius is able to reach the front and assess the situation.

"Not the Foundation's plan. Not yet, at least. This is my course of action." Creius reaches the front, accompanied by Yermolai, Sentinel, and Marsha. After taking command and organizing medical aid for the wounded, he briefs Sentinel on his plans, though the Gargoyle remains doubtful of him. The underground fortress at Hill 299 serves as Manus Vindictae's key stronghold, pinning at least 8 divisions of human soldiers within their trenches. Though brave, the soldiers on the front are inadequately trained to face arcane troops. In order to relieve the pressure on their lines, Creius plans to utilize Sentinel's abilities as a Gargoyle to help destroy this powerful fortress.

"It's time the Foundation took action and built an army capable of crossing the 'Storm.'" Enemy assaults pound the front relentlessly. Creius manages to convince the human forces to join together under Foundation command as he coordinates defensive maneuvers from the trenches. With few resources available, the soldiers are forced to hold their ground and hope for reinforcements that may never arrive. At this crucial moment, a long-awaited communication finally comes through. Irinei, acting on behalf of the Hawks, conveys a strategic agreement to Creius. He commits to rallying the Foundation's support and handling the political challenges involved in Creius's plan. In return, Creius must ensure the loyalty of the troops on the front and work out ways to overcome their desperate situation.

"The Manus fortress at Hill 299 has been destroyed!" Sentinel's operation succeeds. With the Foundation's support, the troops begin to withdraw from the front, though many must be carried due to injury and others seem lost in their own minds, as if struggling to process both what has happened and what is happening. Yet despite all the hardships of this final moment, each soldier breathes a sigh of relief as the guns, at last, fall silent.

Led by Captain Creius, Foundation Squad "XII" arrives at the abandoned Montpaix safe zone to begin their investigation. The squad consists of many former elite operatives from the Vigiles Bureau, their specialized skillsets proving crucial to the covert investigative missions on the Western Front.

"Beagle" Paravyan and Marsha from the"XII" arrive at the abandoned village to carry out their search mission. Combing through the area, they engage in a conversation about their fellow squad members and touch on parts of Marsha's past. The mood stays heavy throughout their exchange. Just when they are about to conclude the fruitless search, they are ambushed by an armored vehicle.

Acting on Creius's command, "Hound" Yermolai from the "XII" heads toward Hill 299 to look into the disappearance of fellow squad members and keep an eye out for Manus activities.
Unlike the rest of the squad, Yermolai's speech is often sarcastic, revealing a noticeable lack of respect for his captain.

Just as Manus Vindictae forces begin their attack on the besieged Montpaix safe zone, "Hound" Yermolai arrives on the scene. He eliminates the enemy commander and drives the Manus forces back. With the immediate threat neutralized, Yermolai and Creius move toward the front.
Yermolai's investigation reveals that Manus Vindictae has formed an army. Although the exact locations of their troops are still unclear, it is confirmed that a particularly threatening group is centered on the fortifications around Hill 299, their sudden appearance raising the stakes of the conflict.

Sentinel is entrusted with the vital mission of destroying the fortress at Hill 299, with the seasoned "Hound" Yermolai leading the way through terrain he knows well. 
Upon arrival, Yermolai hands over a set of explosives along with a map and shares all the intelligence gathered about the structure's layout. The outcome of the entire operation now depends on Sentinel's ability to carry out the plan.

"Hound" Yermolai makes it back to the trench command post, where he updates Creius on Sentinel's actions. Given how bleak things have become, he voices doubt about the Gargoyle's chances of pulling through. Still, with no better options left, all they can do is hold the line and place their hope in her.

"Beagle" Paravyan follows Charon's horse, Andreas, to the graveyard, confirming the animal has no ties to Manus Vindictae before preparing to leave.
Just before heading off, he casually brings up "Blackbird" Merel, another "XII" Squad member, and is told that she is still alive. On learning that she has been deliberately avoiding Foundation searches, he reacts with quiet concern rather than surprise.
It appears that even her fellow squad member sees Merel as someone who struggles to manage on her own and as someone they genuinely feel the need to worry about.

"... Anyway, I was just worried that something bad might've happened to you, like what happened to ..." "Blackbird" Merel of "XII" Squad, the guard who once escorted Ulrich to Antarctica, is now tasked with maintaining security in the safe zone. When Marsha returns from her operation and reunites with Merel, the real weight of the moment lies not just in their safe reunion but in the crucial evidence Marsha brings with her—proof that could bring about peace.

"Please, Mr. Charon. Come with us. We could really use your help." Merel spots Charon getting ready to leave the safe zone and manages to persuade him to join the supply convoy by offering half of her chocolate. Her duty at the front involves distributing humanitarian packages, including cakes, sweets, sausages, and beer, to all soldiers equally, as a symbol of the expected truce. It is clear that Merel is far more comfortable with this kind of task than with fighting, and it raises the question of whether she was ever truly cut out to be a soldier in the war.

"If you need that kind of help ... maybe we can travel together?" With Charon's help, Merel successfully avoids being found by "Beagle," though she's a little annoyed when he lets it slip that she is still alive. She has determined to leave the Foundation, yet has no clear idea of where to go next and wants nothing to do with Manus Vindictae. Charon seems to be the only person she can truly rely on. In the end, Charon agrees to go with her and promises to help keep her hidden from the Foundation's watch. For someone worn down by war, it is the first time in a long while that she feels a sense of safety.

"No matter then, I am on your side." While Team Timekeeper remains barred from field missions, Lilya, serving as Zeno's lieutenant, receives a direct order from Admiral Somme to deploy alone to the eastern front. Unlike the slow, entrenched battles of the western front, the eastern front poses more complicated and unpredictable challenges. With no interest in factional disputes and little left to do at headquarters, Lilya is, in many ways, the ideal choice for the task. Before setting out, she asks Vertin which side she stands with. But regardless of the reply, Lilya's response remains firm and unchanged: "No matter then, I am on your side." That steady loyalty is what makes her the one person Vertin can fully rely on, no matter the situation.

"From the looks of it, I think it's the ... rebels." "I've been on a mission on the Eastern Front, under the direct orders of Admiral Somme." "Guess what I found *static*, капитан? A *static* Zeno outpost without *static*." "From the looks of it, I think it's the *static* rebels." "I can tell *static* in more detail. Call me back as soon as you can." Lilya's transmission cuts. Concerned that Lilya could be in danger, Vertin prepares to take action.

The Antarctic "Flood" has shifted the timeline back to the year 1920, triggering heated discussions within the Foundation over how to respond to Manus Vindictae's activities. However, internal disagreements are making it difficult for the group to reach a clear decision.
Inside the office, Constantine and Z brief Vertin on the strange situation—a warped version of 1920 and a drawn-out war that no longer matches any known history. They suggest that the cause might be linked to the newly emerged "Storm" or perhaps connected to Arcana's unexpected resurgence.
Although the true source of timeline disruption remains uncertain, the Foundation now aims to end the prolonged warfare and stabilize this altered era.

The assassination in Montpaix has been a serious blow to the Foundation's global efforts. Many nations have withdrawn from the peace talks in response. Inside the Foundation, the Hawks are now calling for increased military preparedness to confront Manus Vindictae through force if necessary.
To get to the bottom of the crisis, an on-site investigation is essential in order to gather key information. This critical task has been entrusted to Creius and the highly skilled members of the "XII."

Eberhard's recorded words following his recovery become a key piece of evidence, revealing how deeply Manus Vindictae has embedded itself within military structures over time. Given the shifted timeline, the group's unusually swift mobilization hints at possible interference from Arcana, whose resurrection may be affecting this era.
In an effort to turn the situation around, Creius informs Foundation's higher-ups about the secret visit by a representative from the Inter-Factional Committee who is working toward a peaceful solution. If they can use this connection to expose how military leaders have been cooperating with Manus Vindictae and present that information to pacifist governments, it could give peace negotiations a much-needed boost. However, they must first secure stronger evidence to support their claims.

During "Beagle" and Marsha's investigation in the abandoned village, they uncover signs that Manus Vindictae may have access to unexpected military capabilities and could be forming their own army. Irinei, representing the Hawks, agrees with this conclusion and suggests forming an army controlled by the Foundation along the western front. In contrast, Pedra from the Doves strongly opposes the idea, arguing that such aggressive action would be dangerously short-sighted.
Constantine brings the unproductive debate to a close, stating that current protocols will remain in place until solid evidence confirms these concerns. However, the Foundation must begin preparing contingency plans in case a full-scale conflict does become a reality.

The actions carried out by "XII" Squad are shaping the situation in a way that supports the Foundation's goals. The Inter-Factional Committee representative who secretly met with Creius has started using the intelligence gathered by Marsha to challenge the military leadership. Once the pacifist political parties take power, an armistice will surely be signed in Montpaix, the very safe zone where the assassination once took place. Yet, when Creius raises certain concerns, Vertin begins to wonder whether Manus Vindictae may have been working with the Foundation during the peace talks that are doomed to fail from the beginning, possibly as a way to draw attention away from their true aims.
Despite the ongoing uncertainty, the coming peace has now become the most important goal of all.

A soldier slips past the Foundation's surveillance and makes his way into the forest outside the safe zone. It is clear he is carrying out a secret mission, with orders tied to suspicious objectives.
When he arrives at the planned meeting point, he does not find the ally he expected. Instead, he comes face-to-face with a woman radiating murderous intent. The encounter ends quickly, with the soldier fatally struck before he has a chance to defend himself. The attacker then retrieves the pouch he had been carrying.

Soldiers who seem to be with the unlucky one who was killed have been hiding in the same forest, though their exact mission remains unclear. Their cover is broken when they unexpectedly cross paths with a medic, leading to a sudden firefight.
Although they are equipped with SMGs that give them an edge in firepower, their tendency to only watch what's directly ahead makes them easy targets for a sniper.

Manus Vindictae has clearly formed its own army and is now fully prepared for combat. While "XII" Squad members "Beagle" and Marsha are investigating the abandoned village, an armored vehicle carrying a group of Manus soldiers launches an ambush on them. A conflict is about to break out.

Sentinel's attack destroys the armored vehicle, forcing the surviving Manus soldier to flee. In a panic, he kills his wounded teammates before making his escape. To him, Sentinel seems like an unstoppable monster. His weapons do nothing against her, and running is the only way he might survive.
He makes it to the Windmill Plain and briefly reunites with a fellow soldier, but Sentinel catches up quickly. His companion is taken out almost immediately.
With no way out, he keeps shooting, but his bullets have no effect on the gargoyle's body. Exhausted and hopeless, he falls to his knees, mutters ominous invocations under his breath, then ends it all with a final shot to his own head ...

Thanks to the documents Sentinel gave to Marsha, world leaders now know about Manus Vindictae and what they're trying to achieve. Refusing to be manipulated, the nations at war begin to reopen peace talks, guided by the Foundation. The end of the conflict finally seems possible.
But Manus doesn't seem ready to give up so easily. Creius believes their recent involvement in a doomed mission might be a distraction. If he's right, it means they're working on something else at the same time—something far more important.
At the same time, a "XII" Squad recon team sent to Hill 299 has stopped responding. Manus Vindictae's secrets may be hidden there.

The Manus officer, who had been hiding in plain sight while posing as an assistant to political delegates, finally makes a move. As world leaders gather in Montpaix to sign the armistice, the officer seizes the opportunity and calls in a sudden military strike. In an instant, Montpaix turns into a battlefield.
Caught off guard, the Foundation's security team struggles to respond. Manus Vindictae quickly takes control, aiming to stage dramatic scenes that can be broadcast across the world. Their goal is to spread their beliefs and ignite more wars, all to usher in what they claim will be a glorious new era ruled by arcanists.
Just as the situation worsens, "Hound" from the "XII" arrives in time to cut the attack short. Even so, Manus Vindictae still has plans in motion.

Troops from Manus Vindictae continue to flood out of their fortress at Hill 299, launching attacks on positions held by soldiers from both warring sides. Having little experience fighting enemies with arcane skills, these soldiers are unable to fight back effectively.
As their defenses begin to fall apart under the pressure, it seems more and more likely that Manus Vindictae will win and spread the conflict even further ...

The battle at the front shows no sign of stopping.
Each company suffers losses, only to be filled again with new recruits. Most of them arrive with no idea what war is really like, bringing along heavy bags from home as if they were heading to a school trip instead of a war zone.
Their training begins the moment they arrive. They have to learn how to live in the trenches, how to communicate under fire, and most importantly, how to recognize different types of artillery using only sound.
Soon, enemy shells begin to hit their position. These recruits will have no shortage of chances to learn; they likely won't stay the same for long.

The new armistice will be signed in just seven days, but soldiers are still stationed at the front until the official papers are signed.
Replacement troops keep arriving while kitchen teams work hard to prepare meals for those in the trenches. Medical facilities are overwhelmed. Soldiers with serious injuries that cannot be treated at the front are sent to the rear, and those who cannot be saved wait for burial teams.
Although everyone looks forward to going home, the war continues until peace is officially confirmed.

With the armistice nearly signed, all fighting at the front has come to a stop. Soldiers just need to hold out a few more days in the trenches before they can start heading home.
The sudden quiet across the battlefield feels almost unreal.
This uneasy calm is broken when Foundation staff arrive with humanitarian rations. Soon, the trenches come alive with cheers as soldiers pass around beer and sausages, raising their glasses in joyful toasts that, for a moment, push the horrors of war to the back of their minds.
Now, everyone waits with hope for the peace that's about to come.
"Auf den Frieden! (To peace!)"

The sudden crack of cannons breaks the calm, a sound the veteran immediately recognizes with a heavy heart.
Though the scheduled ceasefire hasn't officially begun, with peace nearly within reach, who would order an attack? Before this question can be properly considered, the sharp whistle of incoming shells is followed by explosions that quickly reignite fighting across the entire front.
Packed personal belongings are destroyed in the blasts. Soldiers still recovering from hangovers fall before they fully understand what's happening. Pouring from the Hill are masked attackers dressed in black combat gear.
This is when human forces confront Manus Vindictae's troops in direct combat for the first time.

Through the efforts of Creius and the "XII," even former enemy human forces now fight side by side, working together to build a shared defensive line against the advancing Manus troops. For the first time, rival human groups put aside their animosities to face a common enemy as one.
All they have to do now is hold the line with everything they have, waiting for the right moment to break through the enemy's defenses.

The great retreat begins.
Sentinel has taken down Manus Vindictae's fortress at Hill 299. With the loss of this key high ground, the enemy can no longer hold their position at the front. Human forces now begin pulling back.
They successfully hold the line. Those still able to walk move ahead slowly, while medical teams carry casualties toward the aid stations. No injured are left behind—whether ally or former enemy—as everyone follows Foundation personnel across no man's land toward safety.
They're going home.

October 11, 1920. The Timekeeper and the team returning from the Antarctic are put through a special psychological test. During this process, the Timekeeper learns that the tenth "Storm" has led them to the wrong version of 1920, where a war that should have ended is still going on.
This "chronal distortion" causes growing tension within the Foundation. The Doves push for peaceful approaches, while the Hawks argue for armed action. It results in a tense deadlock between the two factions.
October 18, 1920. Fighting continues to spread along the Western Front, and tensions keep rising.

October 19, 1920. The Western Front is still caught in constant fighting. In the trenches, Charon works tirelessly, dragging the bodies of fallen soldiers. But the brutal fighting and the disappearance of his horse, Andreas, make the task even harder. Peace talks are making real progress and could bring the war to an end by winter, but Charon's commanding officer remains focused on achieving complete victory.
While on a mission to collect a personal package for his commander in Montpaix, known as a "safe zone," Charon meets a young medic. At the same time, a brutal and one-sided massacre begins to unfold on the outskirts of Montpaix ...

October 19, 1920. Amid the chaos of war, various factions move behind the scenes. Marsha, once a knight and now serving as a medic, offers help to Charon. At the same time, Lilya, the Barents witch, is sent to the Eastern Front under new orders. Meanwhile, the captain and the members of "XII" Squad from the Foundation have already started their secret missions.
In the heart of the conflict, inside the Montpaix safe zone, where peace talks are held, the military delegate is killed. The fragile ceasefire is thrown into doubt.

October 19, 1920. After parting ways with Charon, Marsha heads back, and a message from an unknown contact reaches her. It delivers the startling news that the military delegate involved in the peace talks has been killed, and signs point to the assassin possibly hiding in the same woods she is now walking through. Before she can react, Marsha is suddenly surrounded by a group of unidentified hostiles. In a twist she doesn't expect, she is rescued by a sniper who then admits to being the one who carried out the assassination.
At the same time, the Foundation gets ready to send out their newly assembled "XII" Squad to uncover the truth behind the assassination.
October 20, 1920. The day following the assassination, its impact ripples through every corner of the battlefield.

October 20, 1920. The war continues, heavy gunfire pounds the front lines without pause. Far from the chaos, in a quiet graveyard, Charon, Marsha, and the mysterious sniper cross paths unexpectedly. Tension rises, but Charon steps in and stops a confrontation. Thanks to him, the sniper is able to finish mourning, hinting that this visit was only meant for that purpose.

October 20, 1920. At the graveyard, the medic and the sniper known as "Sentinel" face each other in a tense standoff. During their exchange, the name Manus Vindictae surfaces, hinting at deeper ties. Both the fallen military delegate from the peace talks and Charon's commanding officer seem to be linked to this situation.
At the same time, in a deserted safe zone, the captain of "XII" Squad holds a secret meeting with a representative from the Inter-Factional Committee. Two important pieces of information come to light—the sniper is in fact a Gargoyle, and Manus Vindictae is slowly building power within the military.

October 20, 1920. The soldiers on the front lines show incredible endurance, persisting in harsh trenches where they eat wheat bran and drink from muddy puddles. Despite these conditions, they sing out loud with high spirits and even show compassion to enemy deserters. However, one commanding officer begins to act violently and without reason, once even pointing a weapon at his own men. To stop the situation from turning worse and to save the commander, Charon is left with no choice but to use Terror to bring the officer back under control ...
A brief calm returns to the trenches, and Charon's actions offer a sign of humanity amid the war.

October 21, 1920. Eberhard and Paul were drafted into the army at the same time. They fought side by side, grieved for lost comrades, and held on to the belief that only victory could make their suffering worth it. Now, Eberhard recovers from terror with Paul's help, his war fervor slowly fading. With heavy hearts, they decide to head toward Montpaix.
The information Eberhard shares gives the Foundation higher-ups and the captain of "XII" Squad key insights into how Manus Vindictae operates, helping them prepare more effective plans.

October 21, 1920. On the captain's orders, members of "XII" Squad quickly spread out to several key locations to look into the movements of Manus Vindictae. Among them, a member known as "Beagle" teams up with the medic and is sent to scout an abandoned village.
Their search turns up nothing of value, with no solid clues to follow. As they discuss what to do next, a Manus armored vehicle suddenly opens fire, catching them off guard.

October 21, 1920. "Sentinel" destroys the Manus armored vehicle. Its crew flees in a panic. Amid the chaos, one soldier manages to escape to the Windmill Plain, only to find "Sentinel" still closely pursuing him. Hopelessly, the soldier ends his life with his last bullet.

October 21, 1920. As the fighting briefly dies down, the sniper and the medic take a moment to talk. It becomes clear that they once fought on opposite sides of the war. But as they begin to understand each other's honest views, the sniper shares her real name with the medic and gives her a personal promise of support.

October 21, 1920. News from the battle-scarred village reaches Foundation headquarters. Higher-ups believe that Manus Vindictae is building its own army. This discovery quickly sparks sharp disagreement over how to respond.
At the same time, the sniper brings the medic to the Gargoyle Monastery. There, she hands over carefully collected evidence dating back to 1918, which reveals ties between Manus Vindictae and senior military officials. However, her actions are met with opposition from some Gargoyles, who remain split over whether to push for peace or stay out of the conflict entirely.

October 21, 1920. Most members of the "XII" complete their assignments and return, with the medic quickly handing over the gathered intelligence to the captain. Using tactical data provided by the sniper, the Inter-Factional Committee's representative now believes they hold enough leverage to push for a ceasefire. However, during the captain's careful questioning, Manus Vindictae's deeper plans are unexpectedly revealed to the Timekeeper.
Even with these discoveries, the possibility of peace now takes priority over all other concerns.

November 1, 1920. With clear evidence in hand, world leaders are now removing military officials found to have ties with Manus Vindictae. The global situation is moving toward a formal ceasefire and a true path to peace.

November 9, 1920. International delegates gather in Montpaix, preparing to officially sign the armistice within the next 48 hours.
Meanwhile, on the front lines, "XII" Squad member "Blackbird" guides Charon through the trenches. They come bearing humanitarian packages for soldiers on both sides. As troops from opposing factions come together to celebrate the coming peace, Charon feels suddenly out of place and slips away from the gathering. He has somewhere else to be.​
November 10, 1920. Paul reaches the graveyard, carrying Eberhard's package. Both of them know this will be their last time together.
November 10, 1920. The medic returns to the monastery with an update from the front. Some units have already begun to pull back, and the rest are preparing to leave after the armistice is signed.

November 10, 1920. A black horse wanders onto the scene. The former knight turned medic, decides to take her new sniper friend on a wild ride across the untouched meadowland.
After this brief taste of freedom, both are called back to their duties.

November 10, 1920. The final steps for the signing ceremony seem to progress smoothly until Manus forces launch a surprise assault on the safe zone. Though initially successful, "XII" Squad member "Hound" arrives and takes down the enemy commander and forces Manus Vindictae to retreat.
Though the situation in Montpaix is taken under control, Manus troops begin to make attacks across the front. Their sudden offensive scrambles the squad mates of the "XII" leaving many out of contact.

November 10, 1920. Facing reckless assaults by Manus forces, human troops from both sides of the front manage to stem the tide but are being slowly whittled down.
In a private exchange, "XII" Squad's captain shares an audacious plan with Sentinel. He intends to seek her help in taking Hill 299 from Manus Vindictae.

November 10, 1920. Guided by "Hound," the sniper fights her way through Manus soldiers and reaches the underground passage of Hill 299. She plans to get to the ammunition depot and destroy Manus Vindictae's key fortress.
Yet as she opens the door, Charon appears dragging a dead man behind him. Before he leaves, he warns her that she's "walking through the gates of hell."

November 10, 1920. The sniper moves deeper into the fortress.
On the battlefield, the captain of the"XII" pulls off a rare achievement by bringing together former enemy human factions to stand united against Manus Vindictae. The leader of the Hawks also delivers welcome news: the Foundation agrees to back his "frontline contingency plan." Now, all that remains is to hold the line long enough for the sniper to finish her mission.

November 10, 1920. Deep inside the fortress, the sniper is faced with countless visions, but she pushes through them with sheer determination and succeeds in destroying the stronghold at Hill 299.
With the mission completed, soldiers on the front begin their planned withdrawal. The war between human factions on the Western Front officially comes to an end.
November 11, 1920. Marianne returns to the Monastery. The sudden and unexpected peace leads the Gargoyles to begin re-thinking their future.​

November 11, 1920. Charon is reunited with his horse, Andreas. Beside him is "XII" Squad member "Blackbird," who, tired of living with constant danger, decides to leave with him.
Back at the Foundation, the Hawks gain ground as the Storm Reformation Act enters a new phase of revision. The captain of the "XII" meets with the Timekeeper, leaving behind hints related to "Urd."
At the same time, Lilya delivers vital recon reports from the Eastern Front, introducing unexpected new developments.

November 18, 1920. The St. Pavlov Foundation sends investigators to assess the conditions of civilians in former war zones, and plans to deliver a range of humanitarian support in the aftermath of the war.
November 20, 1920. Relief work continues smoothly on the Western Front. At the same time, the Foundation turns its focus to a different battlefield where "Razor" Squad and Lilya are active.

Once a vibrant tree—its branches arcing toward the sky, leaves dancing in the wind, with ants thriving in the shelter of its roots.
Until someone sets fire to rotting leaves at its base, thick smothering smoke billowing from the all-consuming flames that devour all that grew there.
Flame, O flame—beneath your dance, the sweetest sap bleeds! Drink it, devour it, destroy it!
The first ant senses the heat too late, the fire scalding its feet. Too small to run, it is consumed in an instant.
The second ant flees, scrambling down from the tree. Sap, meat, and colony—all forgotten in the scramble!
The third ant sees the fire burn. Oh, how it roars—glorious, golden! Lost in the blaze's glare, it surges into the heart of the flame. Longing to be golden forever!
A deluge falls from the heavens, washing over the great tree and the ants below, coming as if a savior.
The rain patters over the curled, charred body of the first ant. The trickling water pools and lifts the blackened thing, yet it does not move.
The second ant dashes toward the rising water; relief fills its mind, believing itself spared ...
The third ant rages madly as the golden light dims and fades, forgetting the agony of the fire from mere moments before.
Fire scorched only the surface—bark, chitin, and skin—but water seeps below, and soon they come to curse it.
Puddles of murky water ripple over sodden earth. The ants huddle beneath the cover of bladed leaves, longing for the warmth of the sun.
They shiver in their flooded nest. Until one, still black with char, whispers. "The fire would have saved us if it had only burned brighter ..." And others cry out in agreement.
Though the rain yet falls, the ants emerge—from the nest, from the grass—toward the smoldering wood, in search of some remnant of the flame.
And at last, in a bleak crevice, they find an ember burning. Cradled there in wait for the end of the rain, so that it might set the world ablaze.
They gather around the fading spark, each waiting for another to act. It cannot find purchase on the soaking wood. But the ants, yes, the ants are dry.
As once they served queen and colony, now they serve the flame. Mindless, heedless, they throw themselves in to feed its hunger until it burns anew.
The first goes, then the second, and the third. A flicker rages up against the dark sky, burning to spite the downpour. Each ant cheering as if the victory was their own.
Until at last, one ant recalls the world before the flame and how they had once feared the fire before the flood.
A thousand of her sisters rise as ashes from the flame only to settle in the cold, wet mud.

Do we really have to hold our book club here? I have a bad feeling about this.

It's not that I'm afraid to die, it's just that ... this feels like an unnecessary risk. We're just reading books. We really don't need to immerse ourselves like this.

I was told our next meeting would be held in a golden field. It sounded glorious. Now I feel like a fool. Can someone tell me where exactly this golden field is?

All I've seen are destroyed houses, upturned dirt, and filthy puddles.

Alright, that's enough. I can't stand this place anymore!

Today, a shell—AN EXPLOSIVE SHELL!—landed so close to me I could almost touch it!

They promised it would be safe!

​​"Hey, what's that you've got there?"​​

​​"Just some letter I found in a crater up ahead. I was about to take it into the dugout over there."​​

​​"It's only a single page. No name, no address, nothing."​​

​​"I tried reading it for clues, but it doesn't seem to be of any help."​

My dear child, this may be the last thing I ever do for you. I know we all must do our part, but still, I prayed they would never call up your name.

Young men dream of war—of valor, sacrifice, and patriotic speeches. Of glorious tales of conquest and victory to share when they come home.

They dream of marching side-by-side, dressed in gallant uniforms, swaggering down streets to admiring gazes.

Of course, they idolize those uniforms; how could they not? The military designs them with that very purpose in mind, so that foolish boys will dream of wearing them.

They dream of wearing them on dates when the war is over, but always when the war is over.

They never dream of the trenches, the rats, or the bullet that comes as their first and final kiss. Or that their uniform may come a size too large and patched with bloodstains where some other dreamer spilled his guts.

Have I scared you? I hope so. If nightmares could slaughter those dreams, I'd gladly send one to you every night.

Honor is only a word, one left unspoken on a thousand dying lips.

It was only ever a dream, packed like gunpowder into burning hearts of youth, to be spent like so many bullets. 

Please, child. I beg you not to go.

Dear readers,​​

People have their own ideas about this war. There are all kinds of records circulating, some real and some fake, each one more dramatic than the last because the papers always want new and shocking "truths" to report. But I refuse to waste time on things that will eventually be examined from every angle. Instead, I want to look beyond the typical explanations and think about how this war really started and where it may lead.

For ordinary people like us, it was only in the final weeks or even days before the fighting began that the reality of it began to set in. It felt like any other peaceful sunny afternoon until, without warning, there were soldiers in the streets and conscription notices plastered on every wall.

Years later, trapped in a maelstrom, we can still look back from the quiet center of the chaos and remember how calm the summer afternoon was before the war. The contrast burns in me like a hole in the pit of my stomach.

Of course, everyone looks back on the past with longing. In our minds, we still see champagne, outdoor cafes, grand theater performances, and the endless optimism of the World's Fair.

Just by remembering those things, we can't help but smile sadly at what's been lost.

The well-known historian Orwell, an arcanist, once wrote: "No noble airs could ever redeem these vulgar, flashy streets." How well those words describe our lives before the war. Now we eat butter substitutes and bread made from bran because the real wheat and butter have been sent to the front lines, though the bread usually arrives molded-over and hard as tack; the butter rife with maggots and fit only for rats. But we've gotten used to it, we stiffen our necks and tighten our belts another notch.

Because deep down, everyone still believes that when the war ends, we'll go back to living the way we used to.

I can't believe she actually wrote that down!​​

And they call her a great writer? Let me make one thing clear. I'm not any kind of saint. This whole thing boils down to a simple question of who will be the first to stop. Today I told that young soldier the same thing I'll tell the men on the other side of the trenches tomorrow. Real soldiers? Does anyone really want this war? What do you know about their last offensive? In just three months, the casualties hit two million three hundred thousand. Do you understand that number? And yet here we are arguing over who fired the first shot. Does it even matter in the face of a number like that?

I'm tired of reading these essays full of dramatic proclamations and so-called profound revelations. Writing is the easiest thing to do. With just a few lines, you can turn a young man being sent to his death into a hero or a tragic figure—his home destroyed, forced to take up arms, yet still clinging to kindness and gratitude. A few drops of ink to sum up an entire life. That's much simpler than what I do, wasting my breath arguing with people who refuse to listen.

But I won't give up. And I'm asking others to join me. To everyone in the book club, ask yourselves this: Why are you reading in the middle of a war zone? To experience something for your next writing project? Or to let the sound of explosions spark your creativity?

No. It's to make you see the real flesh and blood behind those beautifully crafted words. These aren't just descriptions—their young lives cut brutally short, families left with nothing.

I hope this piece makes you think.

Take care as you put the empty shells away. This too is a kind of burial.​​
Old metal can always find a new purpose. But one can only hope it won't be reforged into another instrument of war.
When casings first fall, they're often so hot that they can burn patches into the soil. Yet soon enough, they cool and are swallowed up beneath it. In that way, they are much like soldiers.
I wish to never see this many spent shells again and to never again see a war like this.
It is worth the cost. On the battlefield, such things are rare ... if they exist at all.
A gust of wind was all it took to sweep it away.
Take these bullet remnants and turn them into something useful. Live your life. While we still have tomorrow.
Red is blood, crimson and hot. But it can be more; it can be the bloom of a flower on a sunny day. Go see the flowers.
We've run out, and we've no idea when or if we will restock. When things become scarce, we learn to appreciate them more.
The only thing I've seen go quite so quickly was the last shipment of cigarettes.
I am only a walking corpse who will soon have nothing left.
