106#Along the Don River#Along the Don River
Even before gun barrels, the falcon's hunt never misses.
A fiddler crab trying to live on the steppe—perhaps a new evolutionary possibility.
An affliction lurking beneath pain, kindling rage and death, spreading through fired bullets.
Thank god you woke up before the next round of surround-sound "alarm clocks" went off.
Here we witness how wildfire ignites.
Her spine divides darkness from light.

Stories of salvation—in snowfields or behind ash wood planks.
The mercy in these stories is all the same.
Past sins press against the back of his skull, demanding answers. Not just today.
Those farewells left unsaid—let the music carry them far away for me.
This is the tale of an unyielding fortress, built of iron, gunpowder, and stone.
Those who crowned themselves kings, who dared carve their names into history—all that remains is this "crown."
May every bell ring for something other than farewell.
Travelers whose only desire is the road itself, forever preparing to leave tomorrow. And tomorrow. And tomorrow.
An endless memory, flowing toward past, present, and distant shores.
Farmers enjoy unchanging days and nights, unaware the world beyond the high walls has long since changed.
Wind sweeps across barren plains, carrying away every trace of color and life.
Hoofbeats come riding the wind, bringing news of hope.
Quiet has returned within the crumbling fences. Neither the herdsmen nor the herd looked back toward their homes.
... Coffee itself isn't rare. Making it well—that takes skill.
Brew it too long and it turns bitter and harsh. Too short, and it's bland as snowmelt.
It reminds me of wartime. The days when we would lap up fallen snow just to quench our thirst.
People who leave the battlefield—if their minds aren't filled with new things ...
What they see when they close their eyes is only guns, blood-smeared faces, and campfires flickering in the night.
Not entirely. Too much coffee makes people more awake.
In the end, I always find myself holding a cup, inviting whoever's still here to share a drink ...
This teacup was a gift from an orange-haired girl with a blue ribbon.
She told me that every afternoon, she'd gather her friends for tea parties out on the plains.
Perhaps someday I'll join those children at their tea parties ...
The weather here is always changing.
Just now it was clear—suddenly storm clouds are gathering and the wind's picking up.
Could you give me a hand? Please take that kettle of hot water to the lounge.
Recently, Ms. NewBabel asked me to help care for the "overly energetic" sleepless Critters out on the plains.
So I added some sage to the Drowsy Sheep Tincture.
Thank you. You've been a great help.
But please, keep the kettle away from the Teakettlers.
Otherwise they get too excited and start spraying steam everywhere, like a pot boiling over.
Ms. NewBabel always says perhaps I'm a natural-born Critter tamer ... because I can sense shifts in their emotions faster than anyone else.
The communication device is the most honest thing on the battlefield.
It never pretends to be brave, never lies. It simply relays what it knows, faithfully.
This is a song Moldir used to love playing on the dombra.
"Oh golden summer, you've lingered too long."
"We lift our cups to the dwindling days. "
... I can't quite remember the rest.
Back then, my comrades always asked me to keep the beat for them.
They kept singing even when snowflakes landed on their faces—
"Will be carried by ravens back to the steppes."
The air is always freshest after it rains.
Like earth, dew, and grass mixed with a hint of benzoin.
That silver-haired girl who loves meditation gave some to me recently.
It helps ease the pain of the wounded.
But at night, when I'm alone with all kinds of pain ...
I use it to help me sleep sometimes.
Muddy puddles in the trenches, bloodstains, mangled bodies, and those who collect them.
Rain passing through forests, drumming on armor with a crisp sound.
Horses resting under trees, nuzzling me gently. Makes me very nostalgic.
Are you learning how to make coffee?
I hear ... a song? The melody sounds sad.
I hear ... a song? Did you used to sing?
Does the rain remind you of anything?

Now that we are almost at the end of this tale, this is a reminder before the curtains come down and a note of appreciation in return for your listening ear and generosity. May both of us look back on this fondly as I look forward to the next chapters of your story.

Watch out for his channeling effects.
He's a monster now, rotten to the core ... Father, we need support from the Flying Witches!

We need to trust our allies if we want to win this fight.
I think his attacks are weakening!
You sure? It feels even colder than before! Did we really end their weather ritual?
A contained winter now broken free—unleashing the formidable power of nature.
Shake off the cold and stay focused! The fight's not over!
Who should my squadron help during the next attack?
Help is on the way. Coordinate with them.
The flying witches are coming to help. Hang on, everyone!
All troops, break formation! Air support has arrived!
We're taking severe casualties! We need immediate aid!
Requesting air support! God ... we need a miracle.
Those machine guns are keeping Krutov well covered. They must be taken out as soon as possible.
Those machine guns are aimed at the Cavalry Corps. We need to do something to keep our allies safe.
Fiddler crabs are usually found along the coasts of the Baltic Sea and the Mediterranean; they're favored by diviners in those regions.
There's no way one could have made it all the way from the sea to here!
Listen, keep your eyes on the target, and fire as soon as you hear the command.
Wait, it's the Foundation's comms we're talking about ... Scratch that; we'll use a "flare" instead.

Yeah, yeah ... take your time, fledglings.

Clue Summary Mr. Creius' letter mentions there's information on Urd hidden in Bereggrad on the Eastern Front, which is also where Lilya lost contact with the Foundation. To investigate Urd's whereabouts and ensure Lilya's safety, Team Timekeeper must head to the Eastern Front.

Clue One: Mr. Creius arranges for Ms. Marsha to meet Team Timekeeper in Tamarovka. The Timekeeper confirms that Lilya is safe and receives assistance from Vice Admiral Burakov, the commander of the Zeno Cavalry Corps on the Eastern Front.
Clue Two: Igor has critical intelligence regarding Urd. He will share it if the Timekeeper and the Cavalry Corps agree to work with his Gryphon Legion to confront Krutov's army together.
Clue Three: In the Amber Room, the Timekeeper finds some information that is hard to understand. It seems she wants to go back there after the war ends ...

Clue Four: The Timekeeper does not uncover more details about Urd or the vessel ensoulment experiments in the Amber Room, but she and Igor reach a mutual understanding. She believes that as long as their goals align ... or do not conflict, she can trust him.

Clue Summary A former Zeno admiral, Igor defected during the São Paulo incident, taking his forces to join Manus Vindictae. After the Antarctic incident, he separated from Manus Vindictae, causing a split with his close ally Krutov, who continues to work with the Manus. Igor proposes forming a cooperative alliance with the Timekeeper and Vice Admiral Burakov to stop Krutov's forces.

Clue One: Throughout their conflicts with Krutov's army, the Cavalry Corps remains on the defensive. Blinded by his hatred, Ptolemy worsens the situation. Igor, however, sees something on the battlefield that gives him a slight advantage.

Clue Two: Using intelligence obtained at the cost of Gryphon soldiers' lives, Igor learns about Krutov's movements. Igor uses his arcane skill to teleport himself and his soldiers into the heart of the enemy formation, confronting Krutov's army directly in a final battle.

Clue Three: After the final battle, Igor and the Timekeeper seem to return to the Amber Room in secret. According to the Timekeeper, Igor hopes to establish further cooperation with her and has shared crucial intelligence about Krutov.

Clue Summary Ms. Marsha was once a knight of the Hochland Order and later became a medic for the Foundation, moving from battlefield to battlefield. After the battles on the Western Front ended, she joined "XII" Squad under Mr. Creius. She is currently escorting willing fighters to the Don River region to support the Eastern Front. Under Commander Ivan's direction, Ms. Marsha stations her team in Tamarovka, where she unexpectedly finds Merel, who has deserted her squad.

Clue One: Before the siege begins, soldiers from Krutov's army infiltrate Bereggrad to seize supplies. Ms. Marsha rushes to the hospital to protect the children inside, but she encounters an enemy assault and sustains serious injuries.

Clue Two: After the situation on the Eastern Front calms down, Ms. Marsha receives a message from "XII" Squad. She learns that Mr. Creius has already made thorough preparations for Merel, and now her job is to escort her back to the Foundation.

Clue Summary Lilya follows Admiral Somme's orders and heads alone to the Eastern Front on a mission. She discovers some possible traces of the Zeno rebels. However, due to a suspected equipment malfunction, she loses contact with the Foundation before she can relay any specific details.
Clue One: While on the Eastern Front, Lilya follows the Zeno Cavalry Corps under Vice Admiral Burakov's command. After delivering her intelligence, she remains on standby at the camp.

Clue Two: When the Timekeeper arrives on the Eastern Front, she makes contact with Lilya and brings good news: the Foundation has formed the new Flying Witches, who will soon arrive on the Eastern Front.
Clue Three: Lilya temporarily leads the newly formed Flying Witches. She gets a new Su-02ве, allowing her to carry out missions while her old Red-38 is out of commission.

Clue Four: The rites set up by Manus Vindictae in the Don River basin are the main cause of the Golden Famine. After forming a tentative alliance, Igor provides the coordinates of these rites. Lilya leads the Flying Witches to locate and destroy them.
Clue Five: After the final battle, Lilya considers executing Igor herself but is persuaded by his confession, deciding to give him another "chance."

Clue Summary Vice Admiral Ivan Ivanovich Burakov, commander of the Zeno Cavalry, comes from the Don River basin. With the region suffering from the Golden Famine, he leads the Cavalry Corps to protect local residents from bandits. Vice Admiral Burakov was once one of Igor's subordinates and has some understanding of his arcane skill. Based on Lilya's report, he suspects that the "bandits" might actually be Igor's rebels.

Clue One: Vice Admiral Burakov is surprised by the personnel and intelligence the Timekeeper brings but seems somewhat disappointed to learn she is not there to investigate the Golden Famine. Nevertheless, he promises to assist with the Timekeeper's operations.

Clue Two: During negotiations with Igor, Vice Admiral Burakov discovers that the bandits are not just Zeno rebels but Krutov's army working with Manus Vindictae. He recognizes the value of Igor's proposed alliance but still feels hesitant about dealing with this former-colleague-turned-traitor.

Clue Three: To ensure peace in the Don River region, Vice Admiral Burakov decides to cooperate with Igor to jointly counter Krutov's army. This decision goes against orders from the Zeno Command Center, and he is prepared to face a military tribunal for it.
Clue Four: With the Gryphon Legion's assistance, the Cavalry Corps achieves victory on the Eastern Front. As a result, Vice Admiral Burakov begins to let go of some of his suspicions toward Igor.

Clue Summary Colonel Sabina Sternova, chief of staff of the Zeno Cavalry Corps, is known for her military acumen and unwavering loyalty to Vice Admiral Burakov. She previously submitted reports to the Foundation regarding the famine issue in the Don River basin, but no significant progress has been made. Colonel Sternova infers from Lilya's report that the weapons used by the bandits are not something they can acquire independently, strongly indicating Manus Vindictae's support.
Clue One: After the war, Colonel Sternova plans to leave the Don with the Cavalry Corps for the next battlefield.

Clue Summary Sergey is a soldier locally recruited by the Zeno Cavalry. He comes from a village in the Don River basin with a long family history of military service. After unusual climate conditions cause crop failures, he joins the Zeno Cavalry to hunt down local bandits. He has an optimistic nature.

Clue One: After the city's disturbances are quelled, Sergey's squad begins pursuing a patrol team from Krutov's army but falls into an ambush set by a Manus ritualist, resulting in the capture of the entire squad.
Clue Two: Sergey lives through the final battle. He later decides to follow Igor and joins the Gryphon Legion.

Clue Summary Moldir is Igor's adopted daughter and Lopera's older sister. Like Ptolemy, she is loyal to her father, but she is much calmer and has a better understanding of long-term consequences. During the Antarctic incident, she successfully escaped and returned to Igor's forces. During the war on the Eastern Front, Moldir is carrying out missions in other regions on Igor's orders.

Clue Summary Ptolemy is Igor's adopted son. He believes that his father's actions are justified and works tirelessly to achieve Igor's goals. In the outskirts of Bereggrad, he acts as Igor's messenger, delivering messages to the Timekeeper and Vice Admiral Burakov.

Clue One: During a past assassination attempt, Ptolemy lost his left eye while protecting Krutov. When he learns the truth behind the attack, he becomes blinded by revenge, leading to poor judgment in battle.

Clue Summary Mr. Creius previously served as a liaison for the Foundation's military department and is now the captain of the newly formed "XII" Squad. His accomplishments on the Western Front earned him more support within the Hawks. Madam Z deduces that this is a key reason he could obtain intelligence about Urd. Mr. Creius shares the intelligence he has with the Timekeeper to facilitate cooperation between them.

Clue One: For some reason, after the Western Front battles ended, "Blackbird" Merel deserted the "XII" Squad and did not return to the Foundation. Mr. Creius knows she fears him and is avoiding her former squadmates.
Clue Two: Upon learning of Merel's desertion, Mr. Creius forges a "secret order" assigning her to the Eastern Front to investigate the Golden Famine, preparing for her eventual return to the squad.

Clue Summary According to information sent by Ms. Marsha, "XII" Squad's "Blackbird" Merel left her squad during the war on the Western Front and subsequently disappeared. Perhaps her experiences in Antarctica made her desperate to escape the war. Merel meets Mr. Charon on the Western Front. To evade the Foundation's search, she travels with him as his companion.
Clue One: While escaping from Perevoznaya, Merel accidentally falls into a river. After Sergey fishes her out of the Don, she stays temporarily at the Cavalry camp.
Clue Two: Later, Merel follows the Cavalry Corps to Tamarovka, where Ms. Marsha, also a member of "XII" Squad, discovers her. Merel can get help from her, if she does not run again.
Clue Three: Hearing the "secret order" from the "XII" Squad, Merel realizes she will not face punishment from the Foundation but will still have to rejoin her old unit.
Clue Summary A ritualist of Manus Vindictae commands Manus soldiers and manages prisoners of war within Krutov's army. Her true name and genuine purpose for cooperating with Krutov remain unknown.

Clue Summary Mr. Charon is an Awakened who works as a gravedigger on the Western Front, putting fallen comrades to rest. After the war on the Western Front, he travels with Merel and his beloved horse Andreas.
Clue One: After becoming separated from Merel in Perevoznaya, Mr. Charon is captured by Krutov's army.
Clue Two: Before the war starts, Mr. Charon endures horrific torture at the hands of Krutov's soldiers. His bound and mangled body is sent to Bereggrad as a declaration of war.
Clue Three: Thanks to the efforts of Ms. Marsha and Merel, Mr. Charon recovers. He is currently recuperating in Bereggrad.
Clue Four: After the war, Mr. Charon bids farewell to Ms. Marsha and Merel, then continues on his journey with Andreas.

Clue Summary Mr. Irinei fights to increase the Hawks' influence within the Foundation. He firmly believes that establishing a Foundation army is essential to overcoming the unfavorable situation caused by Manus Vindictae and regaining the initiative. The Doves disagree with the Hawks' radical approach, leading to two opposing voices within the Foundation. They work together on the surface, but each side acts for its own goals in secret.

Clue Summary Madam Z has helped the Timekeeper many times, making her one of the few Foundation officials to earn the Timekeeper's trust. Madam Z doubts Mr. Creius's reasons for reaching out to the Timekeeper. She fears the Hawks plan to pull the Timekeeper to their side, or even force her hand. Nevertheless, she trusts the Timekeeper's judgment and approves her mission.

Clue Summary Krutov was once a subordinate under Igor. By working with Manus Vindictae, he has built his army's power in the Don River basin and become a local warlord. Interested in his arcane skill, Krutov wants Charon to serve his army.
Clue One: The main reason Krutov and Igor split was a difference in their ideologies. Krutov despises Igor and wants to destroy the Gryphon Legion in Bereggrad.

Clue Two: Before the battle begins, Krutov tortures Charon and sends his mutilated body to Bereggrad, using his deathly aura to injure the Cavalry Corps' morale. Krutov wants to kill Igor and prove his worth to Manus Vindictae.

Clue Three: Even while he served under Igor, Krutov had big ambitions. He once staged an assassination attempt on the Gryphon Legion to achieve his own goals, making him an enemy of Ptolemy as a result.

Clue Four: On the final battlefield, Krutov undergoes the mask trial, covering the whole field in a harsh winter. However, under the assault from Lilya and the others, Krutov is ultimately defeated. He uses the Manus ritualist's rite to escape Tamarovka, vanishing without a trace.
The Enemy Who Took His Eye

November 20, 1920. Eastern Front, Don River region. A Zeno Cavalry Corps detachment conducts a routine patrol and engages bandit forces along the way. While pursuing the fleeing bandits, the unit unexpectedly discovers a suspicious camp.

November 20, 1920. The patrol unit returns to the Cavalry Corps encampment. The lieutenant in command reports the existence of the suspicious enemy camp to the cavalry commander. Judging by their weapons, the commander suspects they are Zeno deserters or possibly connected to Manus Vindictae.

November 21, 1920. Following orders from higher command, the Cavalry Corps is dispatched to garrison the Eastern Front and guard against Manus Vindictae activity. However, the unexplained phenomenon known as the Golden Famine, along with sightings of suspected Zeno deserters, causes the situation to deteriorate further.

November 25, 1920. A Cavalry Corps conscription officer attempts to enlist new soldiers in Perevoznaya, upstream along the Don, but the village is attacked and looted by bandits, forcing the recruits into combat.
November 25, 1920. A refugee escapes the attack and flees Perevoznaya but accidentally falls into the river. She is later pulled from the current by young cavalry soldiers.

November 26, 1920. After the Foundation approves the field operation request, Team Timekeeper arrives at Tamarovka on the Eastern Front and meets up with the Cavalry Corps. The Timekeeper also brings news of the newly formed Flying Witches.
November 26, 1920. The Timekeeper gains a general understanding of the Eastern Front and receives the commander's assurance that the Cavalry Corps will assist her operations in the region.
November 26, 1920. The Cavalry Corps departs Tamarovka. As they approach Bereggrad, they discover that the route into the city is under Gryphon Legion control.

November 26, 1920. After contact is established via a Gryphon Legion messenger, the Timekeeper, the Cavalry Corps commander, and the Gryphon Legion admiral meet beside the steppe river for a three-party negotiation. The admiral seeks to broker a joint alliance.

November 26, 1920. Nightfall. During talks by the steppe river, the Gryphon Legion admiral is targeted in an assassination attempt by a Cavalry Corps messenger. The attempt fails, and order is eventually restored.

November 27, 1920. After the two armies reach a cooperation agreement, the Cavalry Corps enters Bereggrad and forms a joint front with the Gryphon Legion to confront the bandit forces and Manus Vindictae troops entrenched along the Don River basin.

November 27, 1920. Team Timekeeper begins an independent operation. During the operation, Bereggrad comes under a sudden enemy assault. Bandit troops use aerial bombardment as cover to infiltrate the city but are met with coordinated resistance from the allied forces and local militia.

November 28, 1920. In the aftermath of the attack, Bereggrad's civilians buy into enemy propaganda and begin calling for the surrender of the Gryphon Legion admiral in exchange for the city's safety. The admiral judges that remaining in the city is untenable and proposes that the allied forces withdraw to their camps to seek a way out of the impasse.

November 28, 1920. The allied forces formulate a plan of operations against the enemy. Before the operation begins, the cavalry commander decides to allow soldiers whose homes are nearby to return briefly to visit their families.

November 28, 1920. Nightfall. The Cavalry Corps soldiers who had left all return to camp. The Cavalry Corps completes its assembly and, under the call and leadership of its officers, marches out toward the battlefield.

November 28, 1920. The Cavalry Corps begins rapid maneuver operations, leaving Zeno Command Center temporarily unable to track its exact movements. These coordination duties are temporarily assumed by Team Timekeeper. Information regarding the Cavalry Corps is relayed back to Zeno Command Center through the Timekeeper's contact with the Foundation.
November 29, 1920. The Cavalry Corps departs Bereggrad. Security within the city and care for the wounded are left to the remaining Gryphon Legion units and local militia.

November 29, 1920. Enemy soldiers infiltrate Bereggrad's hospital, attempting to seize medical supplies and children with aptitude for arcanum. Militia members and Gryphon Legion soldiers thwart the enemy's plot.
November 29, 1920. A Cavalry Corps detachment pursues enemy forces into the upper reaches of the Don River but runs into an ambush and is captured in its entirety.
November 29, 1920. In support of the Cavalry Corps' operations, the Foundation's Flying Witches conduct a special mission along the outer perimeter of the Don River basin.

November 30, 1920. Contact is lost simultaneously with both the front-line battlefield and rear-area towns. The Flying Witches are ambushed during their return, while enemy movements remain unclear. The allied forces face the prospect of a complete collapse across all fronts.
November 30, 1920. The Gryphon Legion admiral returns to Bereggrad to confirm troop casualties.

November 30, 1920. A Gryphon Legion soldier obtains intelligence at great personal risk and transmits it to the allied rear. Using this information, the Gryphon Legion admiral formulates a plan of action and prepares the allied forces for a counteroffensive.

November 30, 1920. The Gryphon Legion admiral uses his arcane skill, instantly transporting the allied forces to the decisive battlefield in an attempt to stall the enemy advance and disrupt their supply lines.
November 30, 1920. The allied forces and the Flying Witches launch alternating assaults, routing the enemy's main force. The Cavalry Corps continues pursuit of the retreating enemy.
December 1, 1920. The fighting on the Eastern Front comes to an end, and the Golden Famine is resolved. The residents of the Don River basin stand on the threshold of postwar peace.
December 3, 1920. A member of the "XII" Squad arrives in Bereggrad to escort a teammate who deserted during the Western Front campaign back to the Foundation.
December 3, 1920. The Timekeeper secretly returns to the Amber Room and reaches a renewed cooperative understanding with the Gryphon Legion admiral.

December 3, 1920. The Cavalry Corps receives orders from Zeno Command Center and prepares to depart for its next destination. Some young local cavalrymen choose to join the Gryphon Legion. Both the war and its soldiers withdraw from the Don.

December 8, 1920. Team Timekeeper returns to the Foundation. According to the Timekeeper's report, Manus Vindictae continues to operate covertly across multiple regions, requiring sustained investigation. If necessary, regional branches are to be contacted for support.

The Foundation establishes contact with Zeno Cavalry Corps and confirms Lilya's safety. In addition, Team Timekeeper's field operation request is approved, and the Timekeeper and Sonetto prepare to depart for the Eastern Front.
Team Timekeeper arrives at Tamarovka on the Eastern Front and meets with Lilya, officers of the Cavalry Corps, and other personnel.
The Timekeeper accepts Igor's proposal and enters a mysterious facility known as the Amber Room to pursue leads related to Urd.
The Timekeeper loses consciousness inside the Amber Room. Upon awakening, she finds herself brought up from underground by Sonetto. At this time, Bereggrad is under enemy aerial bombardment.
The Timekeeper exchanges information with Igor by the steppe river regarding the Amber Room and Urd, then returns to the Cavalry Corps camp.
During the Cavalry Corps' combat operations, the Timekeeper assumes responsibility for part of the communications work. From midnight onward, all contact on both sides is cut off.
The Timekeeper makes a second secret visit to the Amber Room and reaches a certain understanding with Igor.
With objectives on the Eastern Front achieved, Team Timekeeper prepares to depart and return to the Foundation.

According to the Timekeeper's report, no further information regarding Urd or the "Vessel Ensoulment" experiments is obtained from the Amber Room on the Eastern Front. Continued monitoring and investigation remain necessary.

"AZP-37 Automatic Anti-Aircraft Gun. It's Zeno." Lilya leads a Cavalry Corps detachment on a patrol along the Don. The unit comes under bandit attack en route. After successfully repelling the enemy, Lilya pursues the fleeing bandits and unexpectedly discovers a suspicious camp.

"There is a possibility we're ignoring here: Igor's rebels." Lilya leads her unit back to the Cavalry Corps camp and reports the encounter to Commander Ivan. After a brief discussion, they reach a conclusion: the enemy is likely either Zeno rebels or forces affiliated with Manus Vindictae.

"Then you'd better learn how to get your speed up to 240 in 5 seconds." The Foundation's newly formed Flying Witches are temporarily placed under Lilya's command. Alongside this assignment, she is issued a new Su-02ве flight vehicle for operational use.

"Never had a bad one." Igor gives Lilya coordinates for the rites established by Manus Vindictae in the Don River basin. As long as the Flying Witches can dismantle these rites, the Golden Famine can be brought to an end.

"Igor is not a man to be trusted. Don't let your guard down for even a second." The Flying Witches arrive at the wasteland northwest of Bereggrad, the location of the first rite. Lilya does not trust Igor. After carefully confirming there is no trap, she successfully dismantles the rite.

"... Stay alert. I'll check this out myself" The second rite is located near a mountainous area northeast of Perevoznaya. Lilya maintains a high level of vigilance. However, having spent too much time at the first site, she does not hesitate for long this time and swiftly destroys the rite.

"We're looking at a defensive ambush here. Alpha One, Alpha Two—blow them to kingdom come!" The third rite lies on the western side of the upper Don. Unlike the previous sites, it is guarded by a small number of Manus Vindictae soldiers. The Flying Witches eliminate them all.

"Now's no time to be relaxing. Stay sharp!" The Flying Witches reach the mountainous region southeast of the Don and successfully dismantles the fourth rite. As the operation progresses smoothly, some members begin to lower their guard, but Lilya issues a timely warning.

"We'll bring her home once the battle's over." The Flying Witches arrive at the coordinates of the final rite and finds the area empty. As confusion sets in, the unit is ambushed. One member is shot down, and casualties are sustained.
"It's Krutov—I spotted the bastard! Let's blow them to hell!" The Flying Witches spot Krutov and his forces on the battlefield below and launch an aerial bombardment.

"I see them, Sergey! Stay back!" Following Sergey's signal, Lilya identifies Krutov and the ritualist attempting to escape and immediately launches another bombing run. Krutov ultimately escapes, but as the final rite, his withdrawal from the Don River basin marks the end of the Golden Famine.

"I said it before, I'll say it again. I will personally escort you to the judgment seat." As the Cavalry Corps celebrates its victory, Lilya quietly leaves the camp and goes alone to the steppe riverbank, where she finds Igor by himself. She intends to carry out her own form of extrajudicial justice.

"Got you!" Under Sternova's arrangements, Marsha makes use of an abandoned house in the village to set up a temporary medical station. While cleaning and organizing the place, she unexpectedly apprehends Merel, a fugitive member of the "XII" Squad.
"Who's next?" The village's young cavalrymen clash with the locals over the bandits. Marsha steps in and shuts the dispute down.

"I suppose I'll have to give it a try." Charon, tortured beyond recognition, is delivered to Bereggrad as a declaration of war. To save his life, Marsha uses her arcane skill to sever her fear of death and walks toward him alone.

"It won't be an easy task, but it'll soon be over." Charon's condition leaves Merel overwhelmed with guilt. As Marsha observes his state, she urges Merel to steady herself. The two then work together to administer emergency treatment.

"Hey, have you ever heard any stories about knights?" Marsha risks her life to protect the children from Manus Vindictae soldiers who infiltrated the hospital. By the time reinforcements arrive and drive the enemy back, she is already gravely wounded and slips into a coma.
"I'll soon return to the Foundation headquarters. I look forward to hearing from you." Marsha entrusts a hastily written letter to a teammate, asking him to deliver it to her friend, Sentinel.

"Even all this way away ... there's still fighting?" After leaving the Western Front, Merel travels with Charon to Perevoznaya on the Eastern Front. The village is suddenly attacked by bandits. While fleeing the village, Merel becomes separated from Charon, falls into the river, and loses consciousness.

"... I should never have forced you to take me with you in the first place ..." Charon's ordeal weighs heavily on Merel. After the Cavalry Corps marches out, Merel remains in Bereggrad to continue caring for him.

"I hope I see you again, Charon ... I'll miss you too, Andreas." A member of the "XII" Squad brings word that Merel will not be treated as a deserter but must return to her unit to receive punishment. She accepts the decision and bids a solemn farewell to Charon and his beloved horse, Andreas.
"In the end, I have a mother again. That is enough for me." Commander Ivan invites the Timekeeper and her companions to his home in Tamarovka to share a meal prepared by his "mother."

"You taught Krutov well, Igor. Old-fashioned, but effective." Krutov's scheme of sowing discord turns Igor into the target of widespread blame. Ivan orders his men to quell the unrest within the city while considering the timing of the Cavalry Corps' withdrawal.

"To protect our home and kin. That is why I stand with Igor's rebels." Facing the current situation, Ivan chooses to defy orders from Zeno Command Center. He persuades Sternova to place the Cavalry Corps' rear under Gryphon Legion protection and jointly oppose Krutov's forces.
"Now!" With the aid of Igor's arcane skill, Ivan leads the Cavalry Corps in a sudden thrust into the center of the battlefield, launching a surprise attack on Krutov's supply lines.

"We're withdrawing anyway. Why risk the two weeks?" After receiving news that Perevoznaya in the upper Don has fallen, Sternova reports to Ivan. When she learns that Zeno Command Center has ordered the Cavalry Corps to withdraw from the Don River region, her patience wears thin.

"I'll take my leave of you now. Commander Ivan's about to rally the troops." At night, Sternova conducts pre-battle mobilization alongside the commander in the camp. To defend the Don, they lead the Cavalry Corps toward the decisive battlefield.

"Argh, it hurts. *whimper* I'm never going to walk again ..." During a routine patrol, Sergey is shot and wounded. Despite his complaints, the injury is not serious. After resting briefly, he ignores his comrades' attempts to stop him and heads to the river to catch fish.
"Too bad I only caught YOU today, huh?" While fishing by the river, Sergey pulls the unconscious Merel from the water and looks after her for a while.

"Wait, am I seeing things? Why are there so many people outside the city?" As the vanguard of the Cavalry Corps, Sergey advances at the front of the column entering the city. As they near Bereggrad, he realizes the road ahead is blocked by a force bearing the banner of the Gryphon Legion.

"I'm sorry that this is the way we meet again." Igor leads the Gryphon Legion to the outskirts of Bereggrad and sends a messenger to contact the Cavalry Corps, arranging a three-party meeting with the Timekeeper and Ivan.

"I'm letting it go, and so are you." During talks by the steppe river, Igor is targeted in an assassination attempt by a Cavalry Corps messenger. Although Ivan persuades his men to cooperate with the Gryphon Legion, some remain dissatisfied with the decision.

You allowed yourself to be blinded with hatred, Ptolemy." Igor personally returns to Bereggrad to confirm the status of his missing units. He discovers that Ptolemy, acting on impulse, issued a faulty order that led to the complete annihilation of an ad hoc tactical squad.
"It's been a long time, Krutov." Using an arcane skill, Igor teleports the allied forces into the heart of the battlefield, launching a surprise assault on Krutov's army.

"No mortal can transcend eternity, Krutov." Igor uses himself as bait, enabling Ptolemy's strike to land true against Krutov. Cornered, Krutov accepts the trial of Manus Vindictae and releases the power he has amassed as the final rite.

"I've committed many crimes—I will not run from them. I will be ready to surrender my life when the day comes." By the steppe river, Igor calmly submits to Lilya's "judgment." After his confession and Ivan's intervention, Lilya changes her mind and decides to spare him for the time being.

"Your 'shadow of death' means nothing. What I need is a precise prophecy." Krutov receives a report from the ritualist that a group of prisoners has been captured. Among them is Charon, an Awakened. Intrigued by Charon's arcane skill related to death, Krutov seeks to make use of him.

"A pity you have to go. It's rare I meet someone worth more than a few words of conversation." Charon refuses to yield to Krutov's proposal and threats. Krutov abandons the idea of keeping him and makes other arrangements.

"If you refuse to scratch my back, don't expect me to scratch yours." Krutov and the ritualist clash over the terms of their cooperation. After a heated argument, the ritualist compromises, and Krutov tacitly allows her to deal with the prisoners in her own way.

"They're going to cut us off! Third company, stop those riders at once!" As Krutov's forces advance near Tamarovka, they are suddenly ambushed by the Cavalry Corps, teleported into the battlefield by Igor's arcane skill. Realizing Igor's intentions, Krutov immediately orders his troops to counterattack.

Facing the growing strength of local bandits, Zeno Cavalry Corps is clearly outmatched. Their immediate priority is to recruit young riders willing to oppose the bandits and replenish their ranks as soon as possible.
A Zeno conscription officer enlists new soldiers in the village.
After a brief period of rest, the Cavalry Corps departs Tamarovka and begins moving upstream along the river toward Bereggrad.

The Cavalry Corps encounters the Gryphon Legion stationed outside Bereggrad. Opinions among the young cavalrymen differ regarding the Gryphon Legion admiral, branded a "traitor," and the army under his command.
The Cavalry Corps commander reaches a cooperation agreement with the Gryphon Legion admiral. The Cavalry Corps formally enters Bereggrad and establishes its garrison within the city.

Following enemy air raids, resentment toward the Gryphon Legion admiral spreads among the city's residents, triggering unrest. The Cavalry Corps commander orders evacuations and reassurance measures to prevent further escalation.
On the eve of departure, the Cavalry Corps soldiers receive orders from the commander: those who can return home and back within half a day are permitted to visit their families.
To defend their homeland, the remaining young Cavalry Corps members choose to embrace the risk of death and follow their commander into the coming operation.
Before the Cavalry Corps arrives, the Gryphon Legion has already moved secretly to the outskirts of Bereggrad, occupying the key routes into the city.
The Gryphon Legion sends a messenger to the Cavalry Corps stationed near Bereggrad, seeking to arrange a private meeting between the two sides' senior leadership.
Enemy squads exploit the chaos to infiltrate the city. The remaining Gryphon Legion soldiers engage the enemy and protect the civilians.

A Gryphon Legion detachment is ordered to infiltrate the woods outside Bereggrad to gather intelligence on the enemy commander. Their route is exposed, and the bodies of the fallen soldiers are later returned by the enemy.
One survivor from the destroyed detachment successfully infiltrates the enemy camp and delivers crucial intelligence to the Gryphon Legion admiral, completing his mission in his final moments.

Local bandit forces move toward the Don River tributaries and prepare to encamp along the riverbanks. Cooperating with unknown forces, they plan to carry out an arcane operation involving arcanists in the Don River basin.
The ritualist within Krutov's army conducts experiments linked to Manus Vindictae using captured prisoners.
At dawn the following day, Krutov's forces dispatch bombers to carry out an air raid on Bereggrad, while ground units infiltrate the city amid the chaos.
Manus Vindictae soldiers within Krutov's forces infiltrate Bereggrad once more, attempting to seize medical supplies and children with aptitude for arcanum.
The Manus ritualist notices that the rites set along the Don are being destroyed one by one. Combined with reconnaissance reports from Krutov's army, they prepare to intercept the forces responsible.

The Foundation receives Team Timekeeper's application for a field operation to the Eastern Front. Considering the current conditions in the region and the importance of Team Timekeeper, the Foundation decides that "XII" Squad will assign personnel to provide support. The newly formed Flying Witches are also deployed to the Eastern Front to assist the Cavalry Corps' operations.

According to communications from Zeno Command Center, the Cavalry Corps stationed on the Eastern Front defied withdrawal orders and chose to cooperate with the Gryphon Legion in opposing Manus Vindictae forces. Should they succeed, this may yield long-term strategic benefits. For the time being, the situation is to be closely observed.

Based on contact with the Timekeeper, she personally supports the cooperation between the Cavalry Corps and the Gryphon Legion. In practice, Team Timekeeper's operation also receives intelligence support from the rebel admiral. However, the Timekeeper states that only "initial operational objectives" have been achieved and that she is unable to withdraw from the Eastern Front at this stage.

According to further communication from the Timekeeper, the Flying Witches are currently dismantling the rites established by Manus Vindictae across the Eastern Front, acting on intelligence provided by the rebel admiral. This operation is expected to resolve the Golden Famine affecting the region. During the Cavalry Corps' operations, the Timekeeper will also assume responsibility for part of the communications between the Corps and Zeno Command Center.

The war on the Eastern Front concludes with the victory of the Cavalry Corps and the Gryphon Legion (former Zeno rebels). From the Foundation's perspective, this outcome aligns with its strategic objectives. However, the potential consequences of extensive contact with rebel forces warrant continued attention. Team Timekeeper's mission is deemed complete.

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

"XII" Squad member "Hound" reported that the two sides recently experienced some minor friction in the Luxembourg area. Although the situation ended peacefully, we request clarification on your objectives to avoid misunderstanding your position.

To: The Elusive Gargoyle

"The Foundation is being overly sensitive. I am merely extinguishing the approaching flames."

"To avoid further complications, allow me to make this clear: when my actions align with the Foundation's objectives in the future, I am willing to offer my assistance, provided I am not obstructed and necessary intelligence is shared."

"These are the rules I established with 'Hound.' You are free to confirm them with him."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

The Eastern Front is currently experiencing crop failure due to the Golden Famine. We seek professional knowledge regarding plains agriculture, or insights from specialists with long-term experience living and working under such conditions.

To: The Optimistic Scarecrow

"Purrr ... purrr ... Ra ... Rab ... Rabies ... "Fields ... fields ... dr ... dr ... drought ..." "Water ... water ... pour ... water ... Plant ... crops ... crops ..." "Bad people ... Bad people ... Ah! Ah! Ah! Ah ...!" This oral report has been transcribed into an audio signal and forwarded to Laplace Scientific Computing Center. John Titor has been commissioned to attempt interpretation.

From: Foundation Staff Member

While we have obtained advice from an agriculture specialist, we lack the short-term means to resolve the Golden Famine. If the Foundation were to invest sufficient resources into the Wishing Spring, would it be possible to improve crop conditions on the Eastern Front?

To: The Spring Elfin

"So someone important in the Foundation believes you can buy wishes just by dumping gold coins or candied fruit into a spring? Well then, why not carry those sweets to the fields where nothing grows, so people can actually fill their bellies?"

"My little jar only holds spring water, so if you're hoping for a miracle, go find that guy who lives inside a golden lamp!"

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

We have received the Timekeeper's application for a field operation to the Eastern Front. Given the current instability in the region, we have reservations about deploying her team and request your assessment.

To: The Chief Assistant

"According to the Timekeeper, this operation aims to obtain intelligence related to Urd. Our source is currently confidential, but if the Timekeeper deems the operation necessary, I will respect her judgment and accompany her."

"The situation on the Eastern Front does pose risks, but we can seek support from the local Cavalry Corps. I will also fulfill my duties as the chief assistant and ensure the Timekeeper's personal safety."

From: Zeno Command Center

Reports from the Cavalry Corps stationed on the Eastern Front indicate the emergence of bandit forces of unknown origin. In addition to attacking villages and seizing supplies, they have been abducting children. You are requested to establish a listening post in the area and gather as much intelligence as possible."

To: The Eavesdropping Expert

"I've set up a listening post in a mountainous area downstream, far from any settlements. Even in such a remote area, enemy patrols are still visible. They wear black uniforms and operate in small squads along the lower river. Behind them, I hear more complex signals—their scale may already be beyond estimation."

"Given their size and range of movement, the Cavalry Corps should devise a thorough plan before taking action."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

The newly formed Flying Witches have been deployed to the Eastern Front. As this is the unit's first time operating newly developed equipment, we request comprehensive technical support and logistical coverage from Laplace Scientific Computing Center.

Recipient: The Hanged Man's Alchemical Platform

"A bunch of broom-riders just got new toys, but they still haven't paid the remaining upgrade and maintenance fees. What? The Foundation's footing the bill? That's wonderful! I hear Lilya's leading them—she once smashed Mesmer Jr.'s window, you know. Honestly, if they fly their brooms straight through all Laplace's windows, that would be hilarious. I'd even offer them free maintenance."

From: Laplace Scientific Computing Center

Our "troublemaker" has completed adjustments to all logistical equipment required by the Flying Witches. Given their instability, on-site operations must be reassigned to other personnel. We look forward to seeing what you can do.

To: Team Management Expert

"When Medicine Pocket returned the brooms to the Flying Witches, they kept muttering things like, 'Remember to come back and smash Laplace's windows!' Utter nonsense. I can understand the LSCC's concerns—who knows what they might have done to those brooms. There's no helping it. This sort of thankless work falls to me. I'll treat it as a business trip. I'll get overtime pay when I'm back, so it's not all bad, wouldn't you agree?"

To Moldir

I will lead troops to the Eastern Front with Ptolemy. Now that Krutov is no longer under control, I must settle this matter personally. You are to remain at headquarters and oversee troop management across all regions. I will also make good use of the report you brought back regarding the Timekeeper.

Igor

"Judging by Father's tone, he intends to settle matters with Krutov. I should have gone to the Eastern Front as well, but since this is Father's order, I will carry it out to the best of my ability."

"He also mentioned the Timekeeper in his letter. After what I experienced in Antarctica, he seems to have formed his own opinion of her. Father likely possesses intelligence that could be of value to her, so the two may be able to reach a certain level of cooperation."

From: Zeno Command Center

The Cavalry Corps is currently stationed in Bereggrad. We wish to understand public sentiment toward the Corps in order to adjust our deployment strategy. Considering our future developments, we will also require the support of local militia.

Recipient: The Ghost Reporter

"As commissioned, I took photographs throughout the city. Most people are unwilling to appear in the same frame as soldiers ..."

"Many of the photos are filled with resentment and unease—this is a serious issue for the Cavalry Corps. A small number, however, show people carrying on with spirit, fully convinced the war will come to an end. You may prefer the latter."

From: Zeno Command Center

Public opinion in Bereggrad has turned against the Cavalry Corps, particularly after yesterday's air raid. Civilians are now directing their anger at the troops stationed in the city. We request that you arrange theatrical performances to soothe unrest.

To: The Frightened Playwright

"Wh–What? There's still a war going on outside, and I'm supposed to put on a play here? The city was just bombed—if the performance bombs too, won't they take it out on me? Wh-What should I do ...?" The stage lights come up. The performance begins. "From ancient times to the present, tyrants and violence have never been able to strip people of their right to joy. Not even war, not even blazing battlefields ... That's right—raise your voices! Cheer for the tyrant's inevitable downfall!"

From: Zeno Command Center

A castle owner on the Eastern Front has opened his estate as a refuge for officials and other parties seeking peace, drawing hostile attention. We request that you infiltrate the castle under the guise of a maid and discreetly protect key individuals.

To: The Skillful Bunny Girl

"Oh? A secret mission for little ol' me? Satisfying guests is my specialty, so playing a maid should be no problem at all! But how do I protect these guests of mine? If I spot a bad guy, how do I deal with him? Hmm ... well, when the time comes, I'll just give them a smack, right? Hehe!"

From: Zeno Command Center

Supplies on the Eastern Front are critically low. We require an experienced individual to formulate an optimal plan for gathering materials and crafting tools, ensuring civilian livelihoods and sustaining supply lines for the Cavalry Corps.

To: The Nimble Veteran

"Quero cair duro aqui—Zeno still remembers old Duncan! Back when I was stuck in the Sanatorium, I used to think someday a big shot from Zeno would come asking for my help. Life sure takes strange turns."

"Right, back to business. When supplies run short, you improvise, and you get your hands dirty. As long as you can push through, that's a win. My rule is simple: 'If it works, use it!' Hahaha!"

"Hold on, let old Duncan jot down some bright ideas ... What? You're hoping for something more scientific and reliable?"

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

According to reports from Zeno Command Center, the Eastern Front is suffering from a severe shortage of medical professionals. Given your past experience and record, we request detailed and reliable recommendations.

To: The Roaming Doctor

"I only tend to people's teeth. I am not a general physician. Seeking my advice is not a wise decision."

"In wartime, frontline medics possess far more practical experience and skill than I do. Ensuring their personal safety alone would already be an effective solution. I will also do my best to leverage my connections to put Zeno in touch with trustworthy doctors."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

The Foundation is secretly planning an important meeting to discuss post-war matters on the Western Front and affairs concerning the Eastern Front. In light of your professional performance in Montpaix and our current cooperative relationship, we request that you discreetly scout the venue and assess its security.

To: The Allied Assassin

"... This is the venue chosen by the Foundation's superiors. To a Gargoyle born in darkness, this is a grand and extravagant setting. From a security standpoint, it has surprisingly few blind spots. If the Montpaix agreement had been signed here, I might not have succeeded."

"As a secret venue, it is sufficiently secure. Still, if given the choice, that ruined church on the Western Front would make me feel safer."

From: Flying Witches Liaison

The intelligence provided by Igor has proven accurate—except for the final site. The flight unit has sustained casualties, and the location of the last rite remains unknown. We require external support.

To: Western Mercenary

"Oh? A big commission from the Foundation. If you're looking for someone, give me a personal item belonging to the target. If you're hunting arcane rites, fragments will do—anything marked with the rite. Soil, scraps of paper ... blow it to bits, doesn't matter. Let me take a look ..."

"This is—are you sure what you're looking for is a 'rite'? From where I stand, this 'rite' seems to have grown legs. You've got a real problem on your hands."

The fighting on the Eastern Front is over. Ptolemy and I are still alive—for now. We defeated Krutov's forces, but he escaped. There is still much to be dealt with. Once arrangements are complete, I will contact you again. Communication Record Destroyed

"Father's operation has concluded smoothly at last. From his tone, however, it seems they will not be leaving the Eastern Front anytime soon. In the worst case scenario, if Zeno suddenly turns its guns on the Gryphon Legion, I believe Father has already made preparations."

"Before our next contact, I must quickly inventory the remaining supplies at headquarters and accelerate the tasks assigned to field operatives. As for fieldwork ... this rare joint operation only leaves me hoping Ptolemy does not create trouble for Father."

From: Marsha

Please accept my apologies for this abrupt message. The war on the Eastern Front has claimed many innocent civilian lives. I have learned that you are a caretaker of gravestones. I therefore wish to commission you to come to the Eastern Front and work alongside one of our Awakened to prepare proper rites for the fallen.

To: The Necrologist

"I tend to gravestones, and I also fulfill their wishes. The dead and their gravestones are not the same thing, and a necrologist's involvement may not align with the wishes of the deceased. If you already understand this, then I will accept the commission."

"I have heard of the battlefield gravedigger from the Western Front—so he is an Awakened ... Perhaps, like me, he is skilled at listening to the voices of gravestones. I look forward to meeting him."

From: Z

The military department has received confirmation that "Razor" Squad has arrived in the Don River region on the Eastern Front. Please report on "Razor" Squad's operations to date and outline subsequent plans.

To: "Razor" Squad

"The fighting along the Don has subsided. Next, 'Razor' Squad will focus on civilian evacuation and postwar relief, and will complete intelligence sharing before the Cavalry Corps withdraws. As for matters prior to our arrival in the Don River region, ask the knight from the "XII" Squad. She can report on our behalf as well."

"That said, we should have submitted regular reports on our actions and status ... Has the liaison been slacking off again? The Foundation really ought to consider reforming its staffing structure."

From: Irinei

The Timekeeper has gone missing on the Eastern Front. Even the chief assistant has been unable to determine her whereabouts. This appears to be an independent decision on her part, but given her cautious nature, she should have left an emergency contact method. If you have any information, please make contact on our behalf and instruct her to report back to the Foundation as soon as possible.

To: The Potion Alchemist

"I do not like that bearded gentleman. He is not a friend to the Timekeeper or myself. Still, as a lady, I cannot refuse a gentleman's request. I will help."

"This is an 'Automatic Communications Cylinder.' There is one in her suitcase as well. Simply press here and it will—oh? How strange. The cylinder says she is not within communicable range? I now formally apply to the Foundation for permission to travel to her current region. She may be in trouble, and as a lady, I cannot stand by while a friend is in peril!"

To Ms. Bunny Bunny

The war on the Eastern Front has concluded, and your guard assignment at the castle is complete. You may withdraw via the evacuation route prepared by Zeno Command Center. Payment will be issued shortly. The castle owner's evaluation of your performance is as follows: flawless.

—St. Pavlov Foundation, Military Department

"These past days have been unbelievable! Back in the village, I'd never seen such luxurious tableware or such soft, elegant beds. Every meal and cup of tea was of the highest quality—I could barely resist sneaking a bite just from the aroma alone! But, being the finest maid there is, I did not eat the guests' meals."

"Besides my maid duties, I even caught a few bad guys! Everything went smoothly, so I guess that means I can finally relax now!"

From: Vertin

I wish to commission you to study the effects of soul transfer on the human body. I would like concrete information if possible, such as its impact on the brain and internal organs. I believe this may be achievable with the aid of Artificial Somnambulism.

To: Mesmer Jr.

"My old classmate has brought me another headache. This troublesome bond dates back to our school days, and I have no intention of avoiding it—especially since she has prepared such an excellent room for me. That said, if she could reduce my workload—say, by getting injured less often during field operations and requiring fewer examinations—I would be most grateful."

"This time the issue is 'soul transfer.' I am not sure what she intends to do with such knowledge. Artificial Somnambulism may allow for the transfer of memories, but the aftereffects and risks cannot be reliably assessed."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

From our current assessments, we have successfully thwarted Manus Vindictae's actions on the Eastern Front. However, it is evident that the Eastern Front is not their ultimate objective. Our intelligence remains insufficient, and we urgently require any potential sources that may help break the deadlock.

To: The Crystal Merchant

"Manus Vindictae's movements are difficult to predict. I understand why the Foundation is so anxious, but I cannot fulfill your request at present ..."

"Not long ago, a friend holding an official position within the French government mentioned something intriguing. Their investigation team discovered unusual activity in regions beyond both the Eastern and Western Fronts—possibly the work of arcanists. They may be nothing more than coincidences, but they could also yield unexpected results."

From: St. Pavlov Foundation

The crystal merchant has provided several location leads. On-site investigation reveals broad forested areas with no obvious anomalies. We believe expert analysis is required to identify any hidden traces.

To: The Wandmaker

"The vegetation within these forests has been affected by arcanum. The soil's breathing rhythm and the flow of its aura are faster and more erratic than usual. This is a finely constructed ritual, capable of burying its surface traces deep underground. Yet forests cannot truly assimilate artificial traces. Given time, the forest will absorb and digest the ritual's influence, and its true form will inevitably reveal itself through the growth of plants."

"It has been a long time. How is everything going at the Foundation?
There is nothing left to do on the Western Front, so I accepted a commission and came to the Luxembourg region. Unexpectedly, 'Hound' is here as well. I initially thought he was pursuing me, but once I put a gun to his head, he became quite obedient. I set a few rules with him: as long as he does not interfere with me, I will provide assistance—just as we did on the Western Front.
I intended to have him pass along this letter, but I prefer to avoid excessive involvement with the Foundation. Perhaps we can meet and talk someday. I hope you remain safe."

"Recently, I led a field medical unit to the Eastern Front. The plains are barren, yet the weather remains warm—far too warm for November along the Don.
Something feels deeply wrong. Commander Creius informed me that the Timekeeper will also be arriving and asked me to prepare to receive her. The Foundation sending the Timekeeper personally suggests critical intelligence is at stake. Given the abnormalities here, perhaps she will be able to resolve them. I will fulfill my duty and ensure her safety."

Bandits are everywhere outside the village. Wheat will not grow, and the heat is unbearable. Is this really November? This morning, the sound of thunder, or perhaps roaring winds, came from across the river. When I looked up, I saw several enormous birds the likes of which I had never seen before. It sent a chill through me I cannot even describe.
The villagers say they intend to fight the bandits and reclaim the grasslands of their ancestors. But I am just a refugee who fled here. I must find a way to leave this godforsaken place.

Medical supplies in the town are utterly insufficient. We can only prioritize the critically wounded, as we do not have the capacity to treat those with minor injuries.
The shortage of personnel is just as severe. Then there was that ... unusual patient, brought in tied across a horse's back. I do not know whether he could even be referred to as a man—I am not even certain he was a patient at all. If not for the young woman in armor stepping in, I might have collapsed alongside the soldiers myself.
As a medical worker, I find this deeply distressing.

I was granted half a day off, so I went home.
The window of our earthen house was open. Mother was cooking—borscht, dry bread, and a plate of potatoes. We never cook this much food. I think she knew I was coming back and made extra.
Mother said Ksenia came by yesterday. She left me a small wooden box and told me to open it only after I had gotten rid of the bandits.
When the war is over, I will propose to her.

Mother says the bandits flew a massive plane over the city and bombed it. Awful people, through and through. The church roof was destroyed—looks like gatherings will have to be held in the square from now on.
Misha was practically bouncing with excitement. He says he has never seen such a huge aircraft before. Alek wanted it to crash into the open field ahead so we could turn it into a secret base.
I thought about fixing it instead—taking Mother with me and flying away, somewhere we would never have to fear bandits stealing our food again. That would be better.

We caught those bumpkins on horseback in no time at all. Ridiculous, really. They have no idea what Manus Vindictae is capable of—the ritualist will make sure they suffer properly.
Having said that, this mask is a nightmare to wear. I can barely see at night, and the constant whispering makes it impossible to sleep ... The black liquid leaking from it—whether it is water or oil, I cannot tell—soaks straight through the uniform. Everyone washes their clothes in that river. At this rate, the water will turn black sooner or later.

Dear Mother and Father,

I did it! I passed the selection trials for St. Pavlov Foundation's new unit—I actually made it! It turns out it's a flying witches unit. Can you believe it? I get to ride a flying broomstick and soar through the skies, just like that—free as the wind.
Oh, and they are still preparing my service number. I promise I will give it everything I have and make you all proud!

Your daughter, Arya

Kampev was sent to a rear hospital to recover after being shot in the lung. I still owe him fifty rubles. He hasn't once pressed me to pay him back.
Demyan lost an arm in an explosion. At the time, he was in the trench, getting ready to bring bread and drinks to the others.
The admiral passed me a condolence letter. I want to return to the front and keep following him. I want to drag this leg of mine to visit Kampev and Demyan. I miss those good old days.

A government official in black-and-white checkered clothing showed up in the village. He says he is a specialist sent by the higher-ups to handle postwar matters. Everyone in the village thinks he's just being nosy.
The people from Zeno say the famine is about to end. The village plans to plant potatoes—potatoes as big as a person. Then they will hollow one out, turn it into a sich, and shove that "specialist" inside to stop him from snooping around.

From: Dennis
Location: Kraków
Mission Objective: Identify candidate sites suitable for use as a secondary base.
Mission Brief: Kraków is an old city, packed with complex historical structures. Its layout favors defense, but the buildings' structural integrity still needs assessment. It has been added to the shortlist.

Personnel: Kiel
Location: Jūrmala
Mission Objective: Rescue hostages.
Mission Brief: The operation encountered heavy resistance, but the hostages were rescued successfully with no casualties. Some of the rescued expressed willingness to join our forces and may be considered as reinforcements.

Zeno's screwed things up, yet again. They'd already issued a withdrawal order, so how did it still spiral into a full-blown war? I heard the Cavalry Corps even teamed up with the rebels—none of it makes any sense.
Because of them, the supply transfer reports, resettlement problems, and equipment-usage logs ... we're now fighting a different war: a war on paperwork.
I wish the resettlement department would move faster and find some poor chump with an arcane skill perfect for sorting files to come help us.
Yesterday I ran into a Zeno soldier who'd just come back from reporting in on the Eastern Front. He leaned in and told me as quietly as he could: Igor's troops might be active out there, too.
You mean the Zeno rebels? The cleanup work in São Paulo isn't even finished yet—are things really about to blow up again on the Eastern Front?

I can't figure out what anyone would want in a place where people are barely getting enough to eat ... I hear Team Timekeeper has also submitted an external assignment request for the Eastern Front. Maybe something big really is going on out there ...
Shh! It's Commander Creius. Drop it. Time to get back to work.
The crops still won't grow. At this rate, I don't think any of us are making it through this winter ... or autumn.

If you ask me, the first thing we should do is guard our own grain stores. Bella said she spotted a suspicious figure hiding behind her fence, but when she grabbed a hoe and chased after them, they were already gone.
Probably drifters. There are refugees wandering around everywhere these days ... You think they'd steal grain?
Who knows. Bella also swears she saw a giant river crab lurking behind her warehouse, like it was sneaking grain from the granary.
A river crab? Stealing grain? Out here on the plains?
Load everything onto the cart. Once it gets dark, we'll hurry to Bereggrad and sell all our goods.
Are you out of your mind? Those refugees from the east say Bereggrad is packed with soldiers right now. They're fighting in the city.
Idiot. Food is scarce everywhere—especially for the army. We take this into the city, hike up the price, and sell it all to the military. They'll buy every last bit.
And you're not worried about catching a stray bullet on the road?
That's exactly why we leave at night. If we pull this off, we won't have to worry about winter anymore.
... No wonder everyone calls you "Mad Mark."
Thank you for tuning and maintaining the equipment. I can receive signals from much farther away now, and far more clearly.
I only handle "on-site after-sales support," but as long as everything's working smoothly, that's what matters.
Doing occasional fieldwork has its merits: it lets you see the outside world and how it's changing.
You're right. Maybe we'll even make a few new friends ... Speaking of which, I happen to have a disc with a recording of Voyager playing violin. Want to give it a listen?
There are ten minutes and thirty seconds until the next battle report comes in. We've got plenty of time to take a short break.

Eastern Front, Don River region. A Zeno Cavalry Corps detachment conducts a routine patrol and engages bandit forces along the way. While pursuing the fleeing bandits, the unit unexpectedly discovers a suspicious camp.

The patrol unit returns to the Cavalry Corps camp. The lieutenant in command reports the existence of the suspicious enemy camp to the cavalry commander. Judging by their weapons, the commander suspects they are Zeno deserters or possibly connected to Manus Vindictae.

Following orders from higher command, the Cavalry Corps is dispatched to garrison the Eastern Front and guard against Manus Vindictae activity. However, the inexplicable Golden Famine, along with sightings of suspected Zeno deserters, causes the situation to deteriorate further.
A Cavalry Corps conscription officer attempts to enlist new soldiers in Perevoznaya, upstream along the Don River, but the village is attacked and looted by bandits, forcing the recruits into combat.
A refugee escapes the attack and flees Perevoznaya but accidentally falls into the river. She is later pulled from the current by young cavalry soldiers.

After the Foundation approves the field operation request, Team Timekeeper arrives at Tamarovka on the Eastern Front and meets up with the Cavalry Corps. The Timekeeper also brings news of a newly formed Flying Witches.
The Timekeeper gains a general understanding of the Eastern Front and receives the commander's assurance that the Cavalry Corps will assist her during operations in the region.
The Cavalry Corps departs Tamarovka. As they approach Bereggrad, they discover that the route into the city is under Gryphon Legion control.

After contact is established via a Gryphon Legion messenger, the Timekeeper, the Cavalry Corps commander, and the Gryphon Legion admiral meet beside the steppe river for a three-party negotiation. The admiral seeks to broker a joint alliance.
Nightfall. During talks by the steppe river, the Gryphon Legion admiral is targeted in an assassination attempt by a Cavalry Corps messenger. The attempt fails, and order is eventually restored.

After the two armies reach a cooperation agreement, the Cavalry Corps enters Bereggrad and forms a joint front with the Gryphon Legion to confront the bandit forces and Manus Vindictae troops entrenched along the Don River basin.

Team Timekeeper begins an independent operation. During the operation, Bereggrad comes under a sudden enemy assault. Bandit troops use aerial bombardment as cover to infiltrate the city but are met with coordinated resistance from the allied forces and local militia.

In the aftermath of the attack, Bereggrad's civilians buy into enemy propaganda and begin calling for the surrender of the Gryphon Legion admiral in exchange for the city's safety. The admiral judges that remaining in the city is untenable and proposes that the allied forces withdraw to their camps to seek a way out of the impasse.

The allied forces formulate a plan of operations against the enemy. Before the operation begins, the cavalry commander decides to allow soldiers whose homes are nearby to return briefly to visit their families.
Nightfall. The Cavalry Corps soldiers who had left all return to camp. The Cavalry Corps completes its assembly and, under the call and leadership of its officers, marches out toward the battlefield.

The Cavalry Corps begins rapid maneuver operations, leaving Zeno Command Center temporarily unable to track its exact movements. These coordination duties are temporarily assumed by Team Timekeeper. Information regarding the Cavalry Corps is relayed back to Zeno Command Center through the Timekeeper's contact with the Foundation.
The Cavalry Corps departs Bereggrad. Security within the city and care for the wounded are left to the remaining Gryphon Legion units and local militia.
Enemy soldiers infiltrate Bereggrad's hospital, attempting to seize medical supplies and children with arcane aptitude. Militia members and Gryphon Legion soldiers thwart the enemy's plot.
A Cavalry Corps detachment pursues enemy forces into the upper reaches of the Don River but runs into an ambush and is captured in its entirety.
In support of the Cavalry Corps' operations, the Foundation's Flying Witches conduct a special mission along the outer perimeter of the Don River basin.

Contact is lost simultaneously with both the front-line battlefield and rear-area towns. The Flying Witches are ambushed during their search for the rites, while enemy movements remain unclear. The allied forces face the prospect of a complete collapse across all fronts.
The Gryphon Legion admiral returns to Bereggrad to confirm troop casualties.

A Gryphon Legion soldier obtains intelligence at great personal risk and transmits it to the allied rear. Using this information, the Gryphon Legion admiral formulates a plan of action and prepares the allied forces for a counteroffensive.
The Gryphon Legion admiral uses his arcane skill, instantly transporting the allied forces to the decisive battlefield in an attempt to stall the enemy advance and disrupt their supply lines.
The allied forces and the Flying Witches launch alternating assaults, routing the enemy's main force. The Cavalry Corps continues pursuit of the retreating enemy.
The fighting on the Eastern Front comes to an end, and the Golden Famine is resolved. The residents of the Don River basin stand on the threshold of postwar peace.
A member of the "XII" Squad arrives in Bereggrad to escort a teammate who deserted during the Western Front campaign back to the Foundation.
The Timekeeper secretly returns to the Amber Room and reaches a renewed cooperative understanding with the Gryphon Legion admiral.

The Cavalry Corps receives orders from Zeno Command Center and prepares to depart for its next destination. Some young local cavalrymen choose to join the Gryphon Legion. Both the war and its soldiers withdraw from the Don.

Team Timekeeper returns to the Foundation. According to the Timekeeper's report, Manus Vindictae continues to operate covertly across multiple regions, requiring sustained investigation. If necessary, regional branches are to be contacted for support.

For victory, glory, who could have known
What you've set ablaze are but innocent bones?
Beliefs you held the day before have turned to ash and nothing more.
Within the depths of your despair—what flame is it that fights for air?
A flickering blossom of fire so red
Quietly lighting the path of the dead.

Perhaps the underworld is home to endless night.
Perhaps the Don is the Acheron by daylight.
Death itself watches with unblinking eyes,
Its empty gaze present as each comrade dies.
Atop black horses, the living cross the riverbed.
Don't hold regrets. Don't turn your head.
For the past is beyond redemption.

Fleeting world, fleeting world, how the good days fade apace.
Friends and kin, old and new, have vanished without a trace.
If each meeting merely preludes farewell, then let me play for you till dawn.
Though bygone days hold too much grief to tell, my heart, like a river, flows on.
